Arrange the following stages of the scientific method in the correct sequence:
A. Experiment
B. Observation
C. Hypothesis
D. Question
E. Analysis
F. Conclusion
o: B, D, C, A, E, F
D, B, C, A, F, E
B, C, D, A, E, F
C, B, D, A, E, F
0.x: The sequence is observation, question, hypothesis, experiment, analysis and conclusion. Replication and peer review follow these stages.
0.tq: Fix the first two stages and then place testing, analysis and conclusion in order.
xs: The sequence is **Observation → Question → Hypothesis → Experiment → Analysis → Conclusion** (B, D, C, A, E, F) — option **(1)**.
Observation comes first and raises a **question**; a **hypothesis** is then tested by **experiment**.
**Analysis** of results precedes the **conclusion**.
xa: After the conclusion comes **replication/peer review**.
**Theory** = well-tested explanation of **why**; **law** = description (often mathematical) of **what** always happens, e.g. **Newton's laws**.
⚠ **Trap:** a theory does not "become" a law.

xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: science is **empirical, testable/falsifiable, reproducible, systematic, self-correcting**.
Statement 2 is correct: **pseudoscience** claims scientific status but **cannot be tested**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **reproducibility** is one of the defining features of science, not inconsistent with it.
xa: Per astrophysicist **J.V. Narlikar**, **astrology** has **not** been considered a science (**UPPSC 2018**).
Scientific method ends with **replication/peer review** after the conclusion.
⚠ **Trap:** a **theory** does not "become" a **law**.

Science is **empirical, testable/falsifiable, reproducible, systematic, self-correcting**.

1.s: Which pair of monomers forms Nylon-2-Nylon-6?
1.x: Nylon-2-Nylon-6 is made from glycine and aminocaproic acid and is biodegradable. Nylon-6,6 uses hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid.
1.tq: Recall the monomers of each nylon.
n: Nylon-6 is formed from caprolactam. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 30-33]
Melamine-formaldehyde is formed from melamine and formaldehyde. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 30-33]
Glyptal is formed from ethylene glycol and phthalic acid. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 30-33]
Nylon-2-Nylon-6 is formed from glycine and amino caproic acid. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 30-33]
xs: **Nylon-2-Nylon-6** is formed from **glycine and amino caproic acid**, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Caprolactam** forms **Nylon-6**; **ethylene glycol and phthalic acid** form **Glyptal**.
**Melamine and formaldehyde** form **melamine-formaldehyde** resin.
xa: **Nylon-6,6** is formed from **hexamethylenediamine** and **adipic acid**.
**PHBV** is formed from **3-hydroxybutanoic acid** and **3-hydroxypentanoic acid**.
**Terylene** is formed from **ethylene glycol** and **terephthalic acid**.

n: Polypropene (PP) is formed from propene (CH₃–CH=CH₂). [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 30-33]
Natural rubber is formed from isoprene (2-methyl-1,3-butadiene). [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 30-33]
Neoprene is formed from chloroprene (2-chloro-1,3-butadiene). [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 30-33]
Nylon-6,6 is formed from hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 30-33]
xs: The correct match is **a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv**, so option **(2)** is correct.

**Neoprene** → **chloroprene**; **Nylon-6,6** → **hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid**.
xa: Natural rubber is **cis-1,4-polyisoprene**; isoprene is **2-methyl-1,3-butadiene**.

Match List-I with List-II.

(a) Vitamin B1
(b) Vitamin B2
(c) Vitamin B7
(d) Vitamin B12

List-II
(i) Riboflavin
(ii) Cobalamin/Cyanocobalamin
(iii) Biotin/Vitamin-H

1.x: B1 is thiamine, B2 riboflavin, B7 biotin (vitamin H) and B12 cobalamin, giving a-iv, b-i, c-iii, d-ii.
1.tq: Recall the chemical names of B vitamins.
n: Vitamin B1 is chemically called thiamine. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin B2 is chemically called riboflavin. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin B7 is chemically called biotin. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin B7 is also called vitamin H. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin B12 is chemically called cobalamin. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin B12 is chemically called cyanocobalamin. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
xs: The correct match is **a-iv, b-i, c-iii, d-ii**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**B1** → **thiamine**; **B2** → **riboflavin**.

xa: B1 deficiency: **beri-beri**; B12 deficiency: **pernicious anaemia**.
B7 deficiency: **skin disease**, **hair fall**.

1.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Vitamin B2 deficiency may cause cheilosis, glossitis, dermatosis and digestive disorders.
Vitamin B5 deficiency may cause paraesthesia and burning sensation.
1.x: Option C is incorrect: pellagra comes from lack of B3 (niacin); B5 deficiency causes tingling and burning feet. The B2 symptoms are right.
1.tq: Recall the deficiency disease of each B vitamin.
n: Vitamin B2 deficiency causes cheilosis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin B2 deficiency causes glossitis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin B2 deficiency causes dermatosis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin B2 deficiency causes digestive disorders. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin B3 deficiency causes pellagra. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin B5 deficiency causes paraesthesia. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin B5 deficiency causes a burning sensation. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
xs: The incorrect statement is "**Vitamin B5 deficiency causes pellagra**", so option **(3)** is the answer.
**Pellagra** is caused by deficiency of **B3 (niacin)**.
**B5 (pantothenic acid)** deficiency causes **paraesthesia** and **burning sensation**.
**B2** deficiency causes **cheilosis**, **glossitis**, **dermatosis** and **digestive disorders** — correct.
xa: **B6 (pyridoxine)** deficiency: **anaemia**, **skin problems**, **muscular twisting**.
**B1 (thiamine)** deficiency: **beri-beri**, **neuritis**.
All B vitamins are **water**-soluble.

1.s:
Assertion (A): Vitamin K deficiency may result in increased clotting time and bleeding.
Reason (R): Vitamin K is involved in blood clotting.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
1.x: Both are true and R explains A: vitamin K is needed to make clotting factors, so lacking it slows clotting and causes bleeding.
1.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: Vitamin K functions in blood clotting. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin K deficiency increases clotting time. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin K deficiency causes bleeding. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
xs: **Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Vitamin K** functions in **blood clotting**, so its lack causes **prolonged clotting time** and a **bleeding tendency**.
xa: Vitamin K is chemically **naphthoquinone** and is **fat**-soluble.
**Vitamin C** deficiency causes **scurvy** and **bleeding gums**.
**Vitamin E (tocopherol)** has **reproductive** and **antioxidant** roles.

The kidneys maintain ionic balance. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 55-56]
The kidneys maintain acid–base balance for pH regulation. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 55-56]
Urea is formed in the liver. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 55-56]
Urea is filtered by the kidneys. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 55-56]
xs: The incorrect statement is "**Urea is formed in the kidney**", so option **(2)** is the answer.
**Urea** is **formed in the liver** and only **filtered** by the kidneys.
The kidneys lie on **either side of the vertebral column** and maintain **ionic** and **acid–base balance** — correct.
xa: Urea is the **main nitrogenous waste** removed by the kidneys.
Urine pathway: **kidney → ureter → bladder → urethra**.
Normal urine: about **1.5 litres per day**, **pH** about **6.0**.

Fullerene is used in drug delivery, lubricants, catalysts and nanotechnology.
Graphene is mainly used as a fuel and reducing agent in iron extraction.
Graphite is used as a pencil 'lead' and as a dry lubricant.

Diamond is used in cutting, drilling and grinding tools. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 23-26]

Graphite is used as a dry lubricant. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 23-26]

Fullerene is used as a catalyst. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 23-26]
Fullerene is used in nanotechnology. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 23-26]
Graphene is used in electronics. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 23-26]
Graphene is used in composites. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 23-26]
Graphene is used in sensors. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 23-26]
Graphene is used in future flexible devices. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 23-26]
Coke is used as a fuel. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 23-26]
Coke is used as a reducing agent in metallurgy. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 23-26]
Coke is used in iron extraction. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 23-26]
Diamond is used for cutting and abrasives in industrial applications. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 23-26]
Graphite is used in lubrication. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 23-26]
Graphene is used in electronics and nanotechnology. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 23-26]
xs: The incorrect statement is "**Graphene** is used as a fuel and reducing agent in iron extraction", so option **(3)** is the answer.
**Graphene** is used in **electronics**, **composites**, **sensors** and **future flexible devices**.
**Coke** is the **fuel** and **reducing agent** in **iron extraction**.
Diamond (jewellery, cutting tools), fullerene (drug delivery, catalysts) and graphite (pencil leads, dry lubricant) are correctly described.
xa: **Graphite** is also a **moderator in nuclear reactors** and an **anode material** in **lithium-ion batteries**.
**Diamond** is used in **glass cutters** and **heat sinks**.
**Activated charcoal** is used in **gas masks** and **water and air purification**.

1.s:
How many of the following are used in electronics and nanotechnology?
I. Fullerenes
II. Carbon nanotubes
III. Carbon black
IV. Hydrocarbon monomers
1.x: Two are used in nanotechnology: fullerenes and carbon nanotubes. Carbon black goes into tyres and hydrocarbon monomers into plastics.
1.tq: Recall the nano forms of carbon.
n: Fullerenes are used in electronics and nanotechnology. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 23-26]
Carbon nanotubes are used in electronics and nanotechnology. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 23-26]
xs: **Only two** — **fullerenes** and **carbon nanotubes** — are used in electronics and nanotechnology, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Carbon nanotubes**, **graphene** and **fullerenes** are used in **electronics and nanotechnology**.
**Carbon black** is used in **ink**, **paints**, **tyres** and **construction**, not nanotechnology.
xa: **Fullerenes** are also used in **drug delivery**, as a **lubricant** and a **catalyst**.
**Graphene** is used in **composites**, **sensors** and **flexible devices**.
**Coke** is a **reducing agent** in **iron extraction**.

1.s: Carbon black is used in which of the following?
1.x: Carbon black (lampblack) is a pigment in paints, inks and tyres. Graphite serves reactors and batteries, and diamond glass cutters.
1.tq: Recall the uses of carbon black.
n: Carbon black is used in paints. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 23-26]
xs: **Carbon black** is used in **paints**, so option **(3)** is correct.
Carbon black (**lampblack**) is used in **ink**, **paints**, **tyres** and **construction**.
**Nuclear reactor moderators** and **Li-ion battery anodes** use **graphite**; **glass cutters** use **diamond**.
xa: In **tyres**, carbon black is a **reinforcing agent**.
**Activated charcoal** is used for **water and air purification**.
**Coke** is a **fuel** and **reducing agent** in **metallurgy**.

1.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Sodium benzoate is used in soft drinks, acidic foods and fruit juice.
Propionic acid or sodium propionate is used in stored grains, cheese and milk.
Boric acid is a commonly preferred modern food preservative.
Sodium metabisulphite is used in jams, sauces and pickles.
1.x: Option C is incorrect: boric acid is an old preservative, no longer preferred because it is toxic. Sodium benzoate, propionates and metabisulphite are current preservatives.
1.tq: Discriminate old from modern food preservatives.
n: Sodium benzoate is used as a preservative in soft drinks. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Sodium benzoate is used as a preservative in acidic foods. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Sodium benzoate is used as a preservative in fruit juice. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Sodium metabisulphite is used as a preservative in jams. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Sodium metabisulphite is used as a preservative in sauces. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Sodium metabisulphite is used as a preservative in pickles. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Propionic acid and sodium propionate are used as preservatives in stored grains. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Propionic acid and sodium propionate are used as preservatives in cheese. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Propionic acid and sodium propionate are used as preservatives in milk. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Boric acid was used as a food preservative in older practice. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
xs: The incorrect statement is that **boric acid** is a preferred modern preservative, so option **(3)** is the answer.
The notes list **boric acid** only as an **older practice**.
**Sodium benzoate** (soft drinks, fruit juice), **propionates** (stored grains, cheese, milk) and **sodium metabisulphite** (jams, sauces, pickles) are correctly matched.
xa: Sodium benzoate is **C₇H₅NaO₂**, code **E211**.
**Sorbic acid / potassium sorbate** act against **yeasts and moulds** — cheese, cooked foods, pickles.
**SO₂** preserves **dried fruits** and is used in **winemaking**.

xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i**, so option **(2)** is correct.

1.s: Which of the following acts as an antibacterial preservative?
1.x: Formic acid acts as an antibacterial preservative. Aspartame and stevia are sweeteners and fructose is a natural sugar, so none of them is an antibacterial preservative.
1.tq: Recall the role of each additive.
n: Formic acid acts as an antibacterial preservative. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
xs: **Formic acid** acts as an **antibacterial preservative**, so option **(4)** is correct.

xa: **Sorbic acid** and **potassium sorbate** act against **yeasts and moulds**.

1.s:
Assertion (A): Monosodium glutamate is a flavour enhancer.
Reason (R): Monosodium glutamate provides umami flavour.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false

1.x: Both are true and R explains A: MSG gives the savoury umami taste, which is why it enhances flavour.

n: Monosodium glutamate is a flavour enhancer. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Monosodium glutamate provides umami flavour. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
xs: **Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A**, so option **(1)** is correct.

1.s:
Consider the following statements:

II. Boric acid, potassium permanganate and iodoform are antiseptics.
III. Phenol and chlorine are disinfectants.
IV. Bleaching powder and formaldehyde are disinfectants.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
1.x: All four are correct: alcohol, iodine, H₂O₂, boric acid, KMnO₄ and iodoform are antiseptics, while phenol, chlorine, bleaching powder and formaldehyde are disinfectants.
1.tq: Discriminate antiseptics from disinfectants.
n: Alcohol is an antiseptic. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Iodine is an antiseptic. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Hydrogen peroxide is an antiseptic. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Boric acid is an antiseptic. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Potassium permanganate is an antiseptic. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Iodoform is an antiseptic. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Phenol is a disinfectant. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Chlorine is a disinfectant. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Bleaching powder is a disinfectant. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Formaldehyde is a disinfectant. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
xs: All four statements are correct — **I, II, III and IV**, so option **(1)** is correct.
I: **alcohol (ethanol)**, **iodine** and **hydrogen peroxide** are antiseptics — correct.
II: **boric acid**, **potassium permanganate** and **iodoform** are antiseptics — correct.
III: **phenol** and **chlorine** are disinfectants — correct.
IV: **bleaching powder** and **formaldehyde** (**strong**) are disinfectants — correct.
xa: **Garlic** has **natural antiseptic properties**; **crystal violet** is an antiseptic.
**Hydrogen peroxide** is used for **wound cleaning** as a **germicide**.
**Methylphenol** is a **surface** disinfectant.

o: Chilli powder — Brick powder or Sudan dyes
Milk — Water, detergent, urea or starch
1.x: Turmeric may be adulterated with metanil yellow or lead chromate. The peritoneum is a dialysis membrane, not a turmeric adulterant.

1.s: Which of the following correctly describes food irradiation?
o: It is identical to food adulteration.
It uses only magnetic fields to reconstruct food images.
It always increases the need for chemical preservatives and refrigeration.
It uses ionising radiation to destroy harmful organisms without altering nutrition substantially.
1.x: Food irradiation uses ionising radiation to destroy harmful organisms without altering nutrition. It can reduce the need for chemical additives and refrigeration.
1.tq: Select the option that combines the process, purpose and consequence correctly.
xs: **Irradiation** uses **ionising radiation** to destroy harmful organisms **without altering nutrition** — option **(4)**.
It **cuts** (not increases) the need for **chemical additives and refrigeration** — option (3) is wrong.
It is not adulteration, and reconstructing images by magnetic field is **MRI**.
xa: **Radiolytic products** cause **negligible chemical change**.
**DAE** has installed **25 food irradiators** in **PPP mode**.
Gamma rays extend shelf life of **potatoes and onions to 8 months** without cold storage.

1.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Department of Atomic Energy has installed 25 food irradiators in PPP mode.
2. Gamma rays can extend the shelf life of potatoes and onions to eight months without cold storage.
3. Irradiation necessarily requires refrigeration after treatment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
1.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Irradiation can extend shelf life without cold storage, so statement 3 is false.
1.tq: Check the numerical facts and reject the reversed preservation claim.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: **DAE** installed **25 food irradiators** in **PPP mode**.
Statement 2 is correct: **gamma rays** extend shelf life of **potatoes and onions to 8 months** without cold storage.
Statement 3 is wrong: irradiation **cuts the need** for refrigeration.
xa: Under **PM Kisan Sampada Yojana**, MoFPI funds irradiation units: **16 approved, 9 operational (Aug 2025)**.
Irradiation destroys harmful organisms **without altering nutrition**.
**Radiolytic products** cause negligible chemical change.

1.s:
Consider the following statements about food fortification:
1. Salt is fortified with iodine.
2. Oil and milk are fortified with iron and folic acid.
3. FSSAI marks fortified food with the '+F' logo.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
1.x: Statement 1 is correct: iodised salt. Statement 2 is wrong: oil and milk get vitamins A and D; iron, folic acid and B12 go into rice. Statement 3 is correct: FSSAI's '+F' logo. So '1 and 3 only' is right.
1.tq: Rice = iron, folic acid, B12; oil and milk = vitamins A and D.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: **iodised salt**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **oil and milk** get **vitamins A and D**; **iron, folic acid and B12** go into **rice**.
Statement 3 is correct: FSSAI marks fortified food with the **"+F" logo**.
xa: **Fortification** = adding **micronutrients**.
⚠ Fortification adds nutrients; **adulteration** adds inferior/harmful substances.
**Irradiation** preserves food **without altering nutrition**.

1.s:
How many of the following industrial applications are correctly matched?
I. Graphite — electrodes and batteries
II. Diamond — cutting and abrasives
III. Activated charcoal — purification
IV. Carbon black — reducing agent for iron extraction
1.x: Three pairs are correct: graphite for electrodes, diamond for cutting and activated charcoal for purification. Coke, not carbon black, reduces iron ore.
1.tq: Discriminate coke from carbon black.
n: Diamond is used in cutting, drilling and grinding tools. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 23-26]
Diamond is used as an abrasive. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 23-26]
Graphite is used in electrodes. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 23-26]
Graphite is used as an anode material in lithium-ion batteries. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 23-26]
Coke is used as a reducing agent in metallurgy. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 23-26]
Coke is used in metallurgy as a reducing agent for iron. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 23-26]
Activated charcoal is used for purification. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 23-26]
Activated charcoal is used for water purification. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 23-26]
Activated charcoal is used for air purification. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 23-26]
Diamond is used for cutting and abrasives in industrial applications. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 23-26]
xs: **Only three** pairs are correctly matched, so option **(3)** is correct.
I: **graphite** → **electrodes** and **lithium-ion battery anodes** — correct.
II: **diamond** → **cutting** and **abrasives** — correct; III: **activated charcoal** → **purification** — correct.
IV is wrong: **coke**, not carbon black, is the **reducing agent** in **iron extraction**; carbon black is used in **ink, paints, tyres**.
xa: **Carbon black** (**lampblack**) is a **reinforcing agent** in **tyres**.
**Graphite** is a **moderator** in nuclear reactors.
**Coal** is used as a **fuel**.

1.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Imaging technique)
a. X-ray
b. CT scan
c. MRI
d. Ultrasound

List-II (Principal characteristic)
i. Strong magnetic field and radio waves acting on hydrogen nuclei
ii. High-frequency sound waves and echoes
iii. Ionising electromagnetic radiation
iv. Computer reconstruction of many X-ray images into cross-sections

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
1.x: X-ray uses ionising electromagnetic radiation; CT reconstructs multiple X-ray images; MRI uses magnetic fields and radio waves; ultrasound uses sound waves and echoes.
1.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes with mismatched principles.
xs: Correct matching: **X-ray – ionising EM radiation**, **CT – computer reconstruction of many X-ray images**, **MRI – magnetic field + radio waves**, **Ultrasound – high-frequency sound waves and echoes** — option **(1)** (a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii).
In X-ray, **dense tissue (bone)** absorbs more — useful for **fractures, chest**.
**CT** gives cross-sections but a **higher radiation dose**.
xa: **MRI** acts on **hydrogen nuclei**; **no ionising radiation**, good for **soft tissue**.
**Ultrasound** uses sound above **20 kHz**; no ionising radiation, so used for **foetal development**.
Ultrasound also detects **liver, heart, kidney** problems (**APPSC-GS 2022**).

1.s:

Reason (R): Ultrasound uses high-frequency sound waves and does not involve ionising radiation.

o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false

1.s: Which process is used for desalination of sea water and purification of water by removing ions and bacteria?
1.x: Reverse osmosis pushes water through a membrane against the osmotic gradient, leaving salts and bacteria behind, so it desalinates and purifies water.
1.tq: Discriminate osmosis from reverse osmosis.
n: Reverse osmosis is used for desalination of seawater. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 48-51]
Reverse osmosis is used for purification of water. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 48-51]
Reverse osmosis removes ions from water. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 48-51]
Reverse osmosis removes bacteria from water. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 48-51]
xs: **Reverse osmosis** desalinates seawater and purifies water, so option **(1)** is correct.
In reverse osmosis **external pressure** on the **concentrated side** moves solvent from **high to low** concentration.
It **removes ions and bacteria** and is used for **desalination of seawater**.
Plain **osmosis** moves water the other way — **low to high** solute concentration — so it cannot purify water.
xa: **Plant roots** absorb water by **osmosis**.
Osmosis occurs through a **semipermeable membrane**.
An **RO purifier** applies pressure **against osmosis** to push water through the membrane.

xa: In **reverse osmosis** solvent moves from **high to low** concentration.
Uses of reverse osmosis: **desalination** and **water purification** — removes **ions and bacteria**.

The older unit of conductance is mho. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
xs: **Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A**, so option **(2)** is correct.
A: **conductance** is the **reciprocal of resistance** — **G = 1/R** — true.
R: the **older unit** of conductance is the **mho** — true, but a unit name does not explain the definition.
xa: SI unit of conductance is the **siemens (S)**.
**Conductivity** = **σ = 1/ρ**, unit **siemens per metre**.
**Resistance** unit **ohm**: **1 Ω = 1 V/A**.

1.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. A fuse uses the heating effect of current.
II. Fuse material should have a low melting point.
III. A fuse is connected in parallel with the device.
IV. A fuse melts when current exceeds its rated value.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
1.x: I, II and IV are correct: a fuse uses the heating effect, is made of low-melting wire and melts at excess current. III is false because a fuse is connected in series.
1.tq: Recall that protective devices are in series.
n: The working principle of an electric fuse is the heating effect of current. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
Fuse material is a low-melting-point alloy. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
A fuse melts when current exceeds its rated value. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
A fuse is placed in series with the device or circuit. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
xs: Statements **I, II and IV** are correct, so option **(3)** is correct.
I: a fuse works on the **heating effect** of current — correct.
II: fuse material is a **low-melting-point alloy** (**tin-lead**) — correct.
III is wrong: a fuse is placed **in series** with the device or circuit, not in parallel.
IV: it **melts** when current **exceeds its rated value**, breaking the circuit — correct.
xa: A fuse melts **immediately** during a **short circuit**.
It gives **overcurrent protection** — **prevents damage** due to **excess current**.
**Household wiring** has a **main fuse** and **individual circuit fuses**; some appliances have **built-in fuses**.

1.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Equivalence Principle is applied in General Relativity.
Statement B: The Equivalence Principle is used for GPS corrections.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
1.x: Both are true: the equivalence principle is the basis of general relativity and is used in GPS time corrections.
1.tq: Recall the applications of the equivalence principle.
n: The Equivalence Principle is applied in General Relativity. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
The Equivalence Principle is used for GPS corrections. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
xs: **Both Statement A and Statement B are true**, so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Equivalence Principle** is applied in **General Relativity** and in **GPS corrections**.
xa: **Doppler Principle** is applied in **radar speed guns** and **medical ultrasound**.
**Uncertainty Principle** is applied in **electron microscopes**.
**Pascal's Principle** is applied in **hydraulic lifts, brakes and presses**.

1.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Conservation of Angular Momentum explains an ice-skater’s spin.
Statement B: Conservation of Angular Momentum explains planetary orbits.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
1.x: Both are true: a skater spins faster when pulling the arms in, and planets speed up near the Sun, because angular momentum is conserved.
1.tq: Recall examples of angular momentum conservation.
n: The Conservation of Angular Momentum explains ice-skater spin. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
The Conservation of Angular Momentum explains planetary orbits. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
xs: **Both Statement A and Statement B are true**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Conservation of Angular Momentum** explains the **ice-skater spin** and **planetary orbits**.
xa: ⚠ **Conservation of (linear) Momentum** explains **recoil of a gun** and **rocket propulsion**.
**Conservation of Energy** applies to **roller coasters** and **pendulums**.
**Archimedes' Principle** explains **buoyancy** and the **floating of ships**.

1.s:
Assertion (A): Antiseptics are applied to living tissue, whereas disinfectants are applied to non-living surfaces.
Reason (R): Disinfectants are toxic to tissue, while antiseptics are safe for living tissue.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
1.x: Both are true and R explains A: antiseptics are gentle enough for living tissue, while disinfectants are too toxic and are used only on objects.
1.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: An antiseptic is applied to living tissue or skin. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
A disinfectant is applied to non-living surfaces. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Antiseptics are safe for living tissue. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Disinfectants are toxic to tissue. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Antiseptics are used on living tissue. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Disinfectants are used on non-living objects. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
xs: **Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Antiseptics** are **safe** for **living tissue**; **disinfectants** are **toxic** to tissue, so they are used on **non-living objects**.
xa: Antiseptics: **hydrogen peroxide**, **iodine**, **iodoform**, **boric acid**, **potassium permanganate**, **crystal violet**.
Disinfectants: **phenol**, **chlorine**, **bleaching powder**, **formaldehyde**.
⚠ **Ethanol** appears in both lists — antiseptic and disinfectant.

1.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Main function of kidney
(b) Kidney and blood pressure
(c) Site of urea formation
(d) Urine pathway

List-II
(i) Liver
(ii) Long-term blood pressure regulation
(iii) Kidney → ureter → bladder → urethra
(iv) Filters blood and forms urine
1.x: The kidney filters blood and forms urine, regulates long-term blood pressure, urea is made in the liver and urine flows kidney → ureter → bladder → urethra, giving a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii.
1.tq: Recall the facts about the kidney.
n: The main function of the kidneys is to filter blood and form urine. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 55-56]
The kidneys regulate blood pressure over the long term. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 55-56]
Urea is formed in the liver. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 55-56]
The urine pathway is kidney → ureter → bladder → urethra. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 55-56]
xs: The correct match is **a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii**, so option **(3)** is correct.
**Main function** → **filters blood and forms urine**; **kidney and blood pressure** → **long-term regulation**.
**Urea formation** → **liver**; **urine pathway** → **kidney → ureter → bladder → urethra**.
xa: Kidneys also maintain **water balance**, **ionic balance** and **pH**.
**Dialysis** is recommended when the **kidneys fail** (**APPSC-GS 2019**).
**Haemodialysis** uses a **machine filter**; **peritoneal dialysis** uses the **peritoneum** as membrane.

1.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The kidneys remove metabolic wastes and toxins.
II. The pH of urine is approximately 6.0.
III. Urea is formed in the kidneys.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
1.x: I and II are correct: the kidneys remove wastes and toxins, and normal urine is slightly acidic, about pH 6.0. III is false because urea is formed in the liver and only filtered out by the kidneys.
1.tq: Recall where urea is made and urine's pH.
n: The kidneys remove metabolic wastes and toxins. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 55-56]
The pH of urine is approximately 6.0. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 55-56]
xs: Statements **I and II** are correct, so option **(1)** is correct.
I: kidneys **remove metabolic wastes and toxins** — correct.
II: urine **pH** is about **6.0** — correct.
III is wrong: **urea** is **formed in the liver**, only **filtered** by the kidneys.
xa: Average urine volume is about **1.5 litres per day**.
Kidneys handle **long-term** regulation of **blood pressure**.
**Dialysis** removes **wastes** and **excess water** from blood when kidneys fail.

1.s: Who was associated with the discovery of Vitamin A?
o: Frederick Gowland Hopkins and Casimir Funk
Elmer Verner McCollum and Marguerite Davis
1.x: Elmer McCollum and Marguerite Davis discovered vitamin A in 1913. Lind linked citrus with scurvy and Funk coined "vitamine".
1.tq: Recall the discoverer of each vitamin.
n: Elmer Verner McCollum and Marguerite Davis are associated with Vitamin A. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 42-43]
xs: **Elmer Verner McCollum and Marguerite Davis** are associated with **vitamin A**, so option **(3)** is correct.
**James Lind** showed **citrus fruits cured scurvy**; **Umetaro Suzuki** extracted **aberic acid** from **rice bran**.
**Hopkins** gave **accessory food factors**; **Casimir Funk** **coined "vitamine"**.
xa: McCollum also **helped discover** **vitamins B and D**.
Funk developed the **vitamin concept**.
Suzuki's extract was a **water-soluble micronutrient mixture**.

1.s: Elmer Verner McCollum, credited with the discovery of vitamin A, also played a key role in the discovery of which other vitamin?
1.x: McCollum, who co-discovered vitamin A in 1913, identified vitamin D in 1922 as the anti-rickets factor in cod-liver oil. Vitamin C was isolated by Szent-Györgyi, and vitamin E was found by Evans and Bishop.
1.tq: Recall McCollum's work on fat-soluble factors: A first, then the anti-rickets D.
n: Elmer Verner McCollum helped discover Vitamin B. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 42-43]
Elmer Verner McCollum helped discover Vitamin D. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 42-43]
xs: McCollum also helped discover **vitamin D**, so option **(2)** is correct.
The notes credit **Elmer Verner McCollum** with **vitamin A** (with **Marguerite Davis**) and helping discover **vitamins B and D**.
xa: Vitamin D is **calciferol**; deficiency causes **rickets**.
**Casimir Funk** **coined** the term "**vitamine**".
**Hopkins** gave the concept of **accessory food factors**.

1.s:
Consider the following statements:

I. Red blood cells are the most numerous blood cells.
II. White blood cells are the largest blood cells in size.
III. Basophils are the most abundant granulocytes.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
1.x: I and II are correct: RBCs are the most numerous blood cells, and WBCs are the largest in size. III is false because neutrophils, not basophils, are the most common granulocytes.
1.tq: Discriminate neutrophils (most) from basophils (fewest).
n: RBCs are the most numerous blood cells. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 10-14]
WBCs are the largest blood cells. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 10-14]
Neutrophils are the most abundant granulocytes. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 10-14]
Basophils are the least common granulocytes. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 10-14]
xs: Statements **I and II** are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
I: **RBCs** are the **most numerous** blood cells — correct.
II: **WBCs** are the **largest** (and the **fewest**) — correct.
III is wrong: **neutrophils** are the **most abundant granulocytes**; **basophils** are the **least common**.
xa: Basophils are also the least common **WBCs** by **percentage**.
**Erythropoietin** from the **kidney** drives red cell formation.
**Vitamin B12** and **B9** aid **red blood cell formation**.

1.s:
Consider the following statements:

II. The testes produce sperm and testosterone.
III. The ovaries are located in the pelvic or abdominal cavity.
IV. The ovaries produce ova, estrogen and progesterone.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
1.x: All four are correct: the testes in the scrotum make sperm and testosterone, and the ovaries in the pelvis make ova, oestrogen and progesterone.
1.tq: Recall the location and products of the gonads.
n: The testes are located in the scrotum. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 47-49]
The testes produce sperm. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 47-49]
The testes produce testosterone. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 47-49]
The ovaries are located in the pelvic or abdominal cavity. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 47-49]
The ovaries produce ova. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 47-49]
The ovaries produce estrogen. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 47-49]
The ovaries produce progesterone. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 47-49]
xs: All four statements are correct — **I, II, III and IV**, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Testes** lie in the **scrotum** and produce **sperm** and **testosterone**.
**Ovaries** lie in the **pelvic or abdominal cavity** and produce **ova**, **estrogen** and **progesterone**.
xa: **Placenta** produces **chorionic gonadotropin**.
Pituitary **FSH** and **LH** are tropic hormones.
**Adrenal cortex** also secretes **androgens**.

1.s: Which of the following is associated with Conservation of Momentum?
o: Recoil of a gun and rocket propulsion
1.x: Gun recoil and rocket propulsion conserve momentum: the forward momentum of bullet or exhaust equals the backward momentum of the gun or rocket.
1.tq: Recall the applications of momentum conservation.
n: The Conservation of Momentum explains recoil of a gun. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
The Conservation of Momentum explains rocket propulsion. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
The Conservation of Momentum explains recoil of a gun. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
The Conservation of Momentum explains rocket launch. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
xs: Conservation of Momentum explains the **recoil of a gun and rocket propulsion**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Hydraulic lift and syringe** follow **Pascal's Principle**, not momentum conservation.
xa: **Conservation of Angular Momentum** explains **ice-skater spin** and **planetary orbits**.
**Conservation of Energy** applies to **roller coasters**, **pendulums** and **power generation**.
**Bernoulli's Principle** explains **lift on an aeroplane wing**.

1.s: What is the optical action of a burning glass on sun rays?
1.x: A burning glass is a convex lens that converges sun rays to a point and can ignite paper.
1.tq: Recall that a convex lens converges light.
n: A burning glass converges sun rays. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 64-76]
xs: A burning glass **converges** sun rays, so option **(3)** is correct.
A **burning glass** is a **convex** lens — it **converges sun rays**.
xa: A convex lens is also a **magnifying glass** — a **virtual magnified image** with the object within F.
A **concave** lens **diverges** rays — used in spectacles for **myopia**.
A convex lens has **positive** power.

1.s: What is the SI unit of resistivity?
1.x: Resistivity is measured in ohm-metre (Ω m), since ρ = RA/l. Ohm is for resistance and S/m is for conductivity.
1.tq: Discriminate resistance, resistivity and conductivity units.
n: The SI unit of resistivity is the ohm-metre (Ω m). [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
The SI unit of potential difference or voltage is the volt (V). [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
The SI unit of resistance is the ohm (Ω). [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
The SI unit of conductivity is the siemens per metre (S/m). [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
xs: The SI unit of resistivity is the **ohm-metre (Ω m)**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Ohm (Ω)** is the unit of **resistance**; **volt (V)** is the unit of **potential difference**.
**Siemens per metre (S/m)** is the unit of **conductivity**.
xa: Resistivity is also expressed in **ohm-centimetres (Ω cm)**.
**Conductivity** is the **reciprocal of resistivity** — **σ = 1/ρ**.
**Conductance** = **1/R**, unit **siemens (S)**, older unit **mho**.

The SI unit of conductance is the siemens (S). [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii**, so option **(2)** is correct.

**Conductivity** = **1/ρ**; SI unit of **conductance** → **siemens (S)**.

1.s: Hydrogels find application in which of the following groups?
o: Contact lenses, wound dressings, diapers and drug delivery
Solar cells, transformers, magnets and satellites
Brake fluids, cement, glass and steel
Tyres, batteries, optical fibres and semiconductors only
1.x: Hydrogels are water-absorbing polymers used in contact lenses, wound dressings, diapers and drug delivery.

xs: **Hydrogels** are used in **contact lenses, wound dressings, diapers, drug delivery** — option **(1)**.

Diamond is used in heat sinks. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 23-26]
Graphite is used as a moderator in nuclear reactors. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 23-26]
xs: The correct match is **a-i, b-ii, c-iii**, so option **(2)** is correct.

1.s: India's own satellite-based navigation system is known as
1.x: NavIC is India's own satellite-based navigation system and supports location-related services.

xs: India's own satellite navigation system is **NavIC** — option **(4)**.

1.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Soap is harmful to delicate clothes.
All older detergents were readily biodegradable.
Detergents are suitable for delicate clothes.
1.x: Option C is incorrect: many older detergents had branched hydrocarbon chains that bacteria could not break down, so they were non-biodegradable and caused foaming in rivers. Soap is biodegradable and harsh on delicate clothes.

n: Soap is harmful to delicate clothes. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 59-61]
Detergents are suitable for delicate clothes. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 59-61]
Soap is generally biodegradable. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 59-61]
Some older detergents are non-biodegradable. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 59-61]
xs: The incorrect statement is "**All older detergents were readily biodegradable**", so option **(3)** is the answer.

xa: Soap solution is **alkaline** due to **hydrolysis**; detergent solution is usually **neutral**.
In **hard water** soap gives **poor lather**; detergents give **excellent lather**.

1.s: Buna-S is formed from which combination of monomers?

2.s:
Consider the following statements about India's S&T policies:
1. The Scientific Policy Resolution, 1958, adopted under Jawaharlal Nehru, was India's first comprehensive S&T policy.
2. The Science and Technology Policy, 2003 was issued under Manmohan Singh.
3. The Technology Policy Statement, 1983, issued under Indira Gandhi, stressed technological competence and self-reliance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
2.x: Statement 1 is correct: SPR 1958 (Nehru) was the first comprehensive S&T policy. Statement 3 is correct: TPS 1983 (Indira Gandhi) stressed competence and self-reliance. Statement 2 is wrong: STP 2003 came under A.B. Vajpayee; Manmohan Singh's was the STI Policy, 2013. So 1 and 3 only.
2.tq: 1958-1983-2003-2013-2020 = Nehru-Indira-Vajpayee-Manmohan-Modi.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct, so option **(1)** is correct.
1: **SPR 1958** under **Jawaharlal Nehru** was India's **first** comprehensive S&T policy — correct.
2 is wrong: **STP 2003** came under **A.B. Vajpayee**; **Manmohan Singh** issued the **STI Policy, 2013**.
3: **TPS 1983** under **Indira Gandhi** stressed **technological competence and self-reliance** — correct.
xa: ⚠ **1958 – 1983 – 2003 – 2013 – 2020** = **Nehru – Indira Gandhi – Vajpayee – Manmohan Singh – Modi**.
**Draft STIP 2020** is India's **5th** S&T policy, with **bottom-up** consultation.
**STI 2013** made **innovation** central — "**Science, Technology and Innovation for the People**".
SPR 1958 came during the **Second Plan (1956-61)**; **DRDO** was formed the same year.

2.s:
Arrange the following policies in chronological order:
A. STI Policy
B. Scientific Policy Resolution
C. Science and Technology Policy
D. Technology Policy Statement

xa: The **Draft STIP 2020** (Modi) is the **5th** policy.
SPR 1958 came during the **Second Plan (1956-61)**.
STI 2013 added **innovation**; STP 2003 joined **science and technology**.

2.s: Which of the following statements about national science and technology policies is correct?
o: STIP 2020 preceded SPR 1958 and was the second national policy.
SPR 1958 was the fifth policy, whereas STIP 2020 was the first.
SPR 1958 was the first national science and technology policy, whereas STIP 2020 was the fifth.

STIP 2020 stressed **Atmanirbhar Bharat**, **open science**, **gender equity**.

2.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly represents the broad approach of the Draft STIP 2020?

Centralised, top-down and closed research governance

xs: **Draft STIP 2020** was **decentralised, bottom-up**, aimed at **self-reliance** (**Atmanirbhar Bharat**), **open science** and **gender equity** — option **(3)**.

xa: STIP 2020 is India's **5th** national S&T policy, under **Narendra Modi**.
Vision: India among the **top three scientific superpowers** in the coming decade.
**Open Science Framework**: **"One Nation, One Subscription"**, **FAIR** data, **INDSTA** portal.

2.s: Which one of the following was NOT an outcome of the Draft STIP 2020?
2.x: Atal Innovation Mission was not an outcome of STIP 2020; it was set up by NITI Aayog in 2016 as a separate initiative promoting innovation among students. ONOS and RIEF were associated with the draft policy proposals.
2.tq: Use the separate-initiative trap: identify the programme established outside the policy.
xs: **Atal Innovation Mission** was NOT an outcome of STIP 2020 — option **(1)** (**BPSC 2025**).
**AIM** was set up by **NITI Aayog in 2016** as a separate initiative promoting innovation among students.
**ONOS** and **RIEF** were outcomes; open science was part of its **Open Science Framework**.
xa: ONOS was approved by Cabinet in **Nov 2024** (about **₹6,000 crore**).
**NITI Aayog** also publishes the **India Innovation Index**.
Exam angle: "which is **NOT** an outcome/objective" of a given policy.

2.s: Which of the following correctly describes the leadership structure of the Anusandhan National Research Foundation?
o: The Minister of Finance is its President and the Minister of Education is its sole Vice-President
The Prime Minister is its President and the Ministers of Science and Technology and Education are Vice-Presidents
The Principal Scientific Adviser is its President and the Cabinet Secretary is its Vice-President
The President of India is its President and the Prime Minister is its Vice-President
2.x: The Prime Minister is the President of ANRF, while the Ministers of Science and Technology and Education are its Vice-Presidents.
2.tq: Use the constitutional-style office hierarchy to discriminate between authorities.
xs: **PM = President**; **S&T and Education ministers = Vice-Presidents** of ANRF — option **(2)**.
The **PSA** chairs **PM-STIAC**, not ANRF.
xa: ANRF is statutory under the **ANRF Act, 2023**.
About **₹36,000 crore** of its funds is expected from **non-government sources**.
The **RDI Fund** runs through a **Special Purpose Fund** in ANRF.

2.s: Which of the following is a role of State Councils of Science and Technology such as APCOST?
o: Issuing national patents and regulating all Union laboratories
Framing state science and technology policy, providing research grants and popularising science
Serving as the statutory governing council of ANRF
Determining India’s Global Innovation Index methodology
2.x: State S&T councils frame state S&T policy, provide research grants and popularise science. They do not perform the national statutory functions of ANRF or NITI Aayog.
2.tq: Apply the state-level institutional role to the functions listed.
xs: State S&T councils **frame state S&T policy, give research grants, popularise science** — option **(2)**.
**APCOST** = **Andhra Pradesh Council of Science and Technology**, under AP's **Environment, Forests, Science and Technology** department.
ANRF governance and **GII** work belong to national bodies (**PM-led ANRF**, **NITI Aayog**).
xa: APCOST gets support under DST's **State S&T Programme**.
AP angle: **DST-STI Hub** at **SPMVV, Tirupati** for **SC/ST women** (3-year project, **Jul 2026**).
Tamil Nadu's council works on translating academic research into use.

2.s: APCOST functions under which department of the Government of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Industries, Commerce and Information Technology Department
Higher Education and Skill Development Department
Environment, Forests, Science and Technology Department
2.x: APCOST works under the Andhra Pradesh Environment, Forests, Science and Technology Department.
2.tq: Use the department-name distinction to avoid a neighbouring-department trap.
xs: **APCOST** works under AP's **Environment, Forests, Science and Technology** department — option **(4)**.
APCOST = **Andhra Pradesh Council of Science and Technology**.
xa: It gets support under DST's **State S&T Programme**.
State S&T councils **frame state S&T policy, give research grants, popularise science**.
AP angle: **DST-STI Hub** at **SPMVV, Tirupati** for **SC/ST women** (**Jul 2026**).

2.s: Which of the following correctly describes the distinctive feature of the STI Policy, 2013?
o: It limited scientific activity to government laboratories
It was India's first national science and technology policy
It added innovation as a central component and aimed to place India among the top five scientific powers by 2020
It removed innovation from the science and technology framework
2.x: The STI Policy, 2013 made innovation central and set the objective of placing India among the top five scientific powers by 2020.
2.tq: Identify the defining addition and the associated target year.
xs: **STI 2013** made **innovation central** and aimed at India among the **top five** scientific powers **by 2020** — option **(3)**.
India's **first** S&T policy was **SPR 1958**, not STI 2013 — option (2) is wrong.
It added innovation rather than removing it, and backed private R&D and **PPP** structures.
xa: ⚠ **top five** by 2020 = STI 2013; **top three** in the coming decade = **STIP 2020**.
Target: raise share of global publications from **3.5% to over 7%**.
**Quadruple** papers in **top 1%** journals.

2.s:
Consider the following statements about the targets of the STI Policy, 2013:
1. It aimed to raise India's share of global publications from 3.5% to over 7%.
2. It aimed to double the number of Indian papers in the top 1% journals.
3. It sought to enhance private R&D and create new PPP structures.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
2.x: Statement 1 is correct: 3.5% to over 7%. Statement 2 is wrong: the target was to quadruple, not double, papers in top 1% journals. Statement 3 is correct: private R&D and new PPP structures. So '1 and 3 only' is right.
2.tq: STI 2013: publications 3.5% to 7%, top-1% papers x4.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: raise share of global publications from **3.5% to over 7%**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the target was to **quadruple**, not double, papers in **top 1%** journals.
Statement 3 is correct: **enhance private R&D**, new **PPP** structures, high-risk innovation.
xa: STI 2013 aim: India in the **top five** scientific powers **by 2020**.
GERD target: **2% of GDP**, with private sector **matching** public spending.
New tools: **"small idea-small money"**, **"Risky Idea Fund"**.

2.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the STI Policy, 2013:
1. It proposed intervention in about ten high-impact sectors.
2. It sought to use modern science to advance traditional knowledge.
3. It assigned agricultural research and development policy to the STI Policy rather than ICAR.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
2.x: The 2013 policy envisaged direct STI intervention in about ten high-impact sectors and the use of modern science for traditional knowledge. Agricultural R&D policy was left to ICAR, making statement 3 incorrect.
2.tq: Identify the reversed institutional responsibility in the third statement.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: ~**10 high-impact sectors** for direct STI intervention.
Statement 2 is correct: **traditional knowledge through modern science**.
Statement 3 is wrong: agricultural R&D policy was **left to ICAR**.
xa: STI 2013 also set up the **Fund for Innovations for Social Inclusion**.
Theme: **"Science, Technology and Innovation for the People"**.
Publications target: **3.5% to over 7%** of the global share.

2.s: The Defence Research and Development Organisation was formed by merging which of the following?
o: TDE, DTDP and the Defence Science Organisation
2.x: DRDO was formed by merging the Technical Development Establishment, the Directorate of Technical Development and Production, and the Defence Science Organisation.
2.tq: Test the formation history through the exact component organisations.
xs: **DRDO** was formed by merging **TDE, DTDP and the Defence Science Organisation** — option **(3)**.
It was formed in **1958**, the same year as the **SPR**.
**DST, DBT, CSIR** and **DSIR, SERB, ANRF** are civilian S&T bodies, not DRDO's constituents.
xa: SPR 1958 came during the **Second Plan (1956-61)**.
**SERB** was later subsumed into **ANRF**.

2.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with the STI Policy, 2013?
o: Risky Idea Fund — support for high-risk innovation
Fund for Innovations for Social Inclusion — socially inclusive innovation
One Nation, One Subscription — STI Policy, 2013
Small idea–small money — support for small innovative ideas
2.x: One Nation, One Subscription is associated with the Draft STIP 2020 and was approved in 2024, not with the STI Policy, 2013. The other three were associated with the 2013 policy.
2.tq: Catch the cross-policy substitution by matching each instrument to its correct policy period.
xs: **One Nation, One Subscription** is from the **Draft STIP 2020**, not STI 2013 — option **(3)** is wrongly matched.
**ONOS** was approved by Cabinet in **Nov 2024** (about **₹6,000 crore** for 2025-27).
STI 2013 did bring **"Risky Idea Fund"**, **"small idea-small money"** and the **Fund for Innovations for Social Inclusion**.
xa: STI 2013 targeted ~**10 high-impact sectors** for direct STI intervention.
It left agricultural R&D policy to **ICAR**.
ONOS sits in STIP 2020's **Open Science Framework** with **FAIR** data and **INDSTA**.

2.s: The vision of the Draft STIP 2020 included making India:
o: A regional scientific power only by 2050
Dependent on the top three foreign research systems
The sole scientific superpower within five years
One of the top three scientific superpowers in the coming decade
2.x: The Draft STIP 2020 envisioned India becoming one of the top three scientific superpowers in the coming decade and proposed a people-centric STI ecosystem.
2.tq: Identify the precise ranking and time horizon rather than accepting an exaggerated claim.
xs: **Draft STIP 2020** aimed at India among the **top three scientific superpowers** in the coming decade — option **(4)**.
It also sought a **people-centric STI ecosystem** under **Atmanirbhar Bharat**.
xa: ⚠ **top five** by 2020 = **STI 2013**; **top three** = **STIP 2020**.
Target: **double FTE researchers, GERD and private share of GERD every 5 years**.
Funding: **STI Development Bank** — corpus fund for long-term strategic areas.

2.s:
Consider the following statements about funding proposals in the Draft STIP 2020:
1. It proposed a National Research Foundation with hybrid funding from private capital and CSR.
2. It proposed an STI Development Bank to provide short-term consumer credit.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
2.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the STI Development Bank was a corpus fund for long-term strategic areas. So '1 only' is right.
2.tq: STI Development Bank = long-term strategic funding.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: **National Research Foundation** with **hybrid funding** from private capital and **CSR**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the **STI Development Bank** is a **corpus fund for long-term strategic areas**, not consumer credit.
xa: The NRF idea took shape as **ANRF** under the **ANRF Act, 2023**.
STIP 2020 target: **double** FTE researchers, GERD and private share **every 5 years**.
**Strategic Technology Board** links strategic departments.

2.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the principal GERD-related target associated with the draft Science, Technology and Innovation Policy, 2020?
o: To raise GERD to 2% of GDP only once by the end of the Tenth Plan
To double the number of FTE researchers, GERD and the private share of GERD every five years
To maintain the existing level of GERD for five years
To eliminate private-sector participation in research funding
2.x: The draft STIP 2020 proposed doubling full-time-equivalent researchers, GERD and the private share of GERD every five years.
2.tq: Use the distinctive repeated-doubling target to identify the policy.
xs: **STIP 2020**: **double FTE researchers, GERD and private share of GERD every 5 years** — option **(2)**.
**2% of GDP** by end of **Tenth Plan** was the **STP 2003** target — option (1) is wrong.
xa: STI 2013: **2% of GDP** with private spending matching public.
GERD was **0.84% of GDP in FY 2023-24**; earlier about **0.64-0.65%**.
The national aim is still **2%** of GDP.

2.s: The DST-STI Hub at Sri Padmavati Mahila Visvavidyalayam, Tirupati, is associated with which focus?
o: Shared high-end instruments for MSMEs in urban clusters
Patent filing activity and global innovation rankings
Sericulture, agriculture and livelihoods for SC/ST women
2.x: The DST-STI Hub at SPMVV, Tirupati focuses on sericulture, agriculture and livelihoods for SC/ST women through a three-year project.
2.tq: Apply the location-specific institutional detail to identify the project focus.
xs: The **DST-STI Hub** at **SPMVV, Tirupati** works on **sericulture, agriculture and livelihoods for SC/ST women** — option **(4)**.
It is a **3-year project** (**Jul 2026**).
Shared high-end instruments for **MSMEs** is the job of **SATHI**, not this hub.
xa: **APCOST** works under AP's **Environment, Forests, Science and Technology** department.
STIP 2020 stressed **women, marginalised and LGBTQ+ inclusion**.

2.s: The Scientific Policy Resolution, 1958 was introduced during which Five Year Plan?
2.x: The Scientific Policy Resolution, 1958 came during the Second Five Year Plan, which covered 1956–61.
2.tq: Place the policy within the correct Five Year Plan period.
xs: SPR 1958 came during the **Second Plan (1956-61)** — option **(2) Second Five Year Plan**.
It was India's **first** comprehensive S&T policy, under **Jawaharlal Nehru**.
xa: Same year **DRDO** was formed by merging **TDE, DTDP and the Defence Science Organisation**.
It resolved to **"foster, promote and sustain"** science.
It set up **national labs and institutions**.

2.s:
Consider the following statements about GERD targets in India's S&T policies:
1. The Science and Technology Policy, 2003 aimed to raise GERD to 2% of GDP by the end of the Tenth Plan.
2. The STI Policy, 2013 aimed at GERD of 2% of GDP with private spending matching public spending.
3. The Scientific Policy Resolution, 1958 set a GERD target of 1% of GDP.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
2.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: SPR 1958 (and TPS 1983) had no numeric GERD target. So '1 and 2 only' is right.
2.tq: Numeric 2% GERD target first appears in 2003; 1958 and 1983 had none.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: **STP 2003** — **2% of GDP** by end of **Tenth Plan**.
Statement 2 is correct: **STI 2013** — **2% of GDP**, private sector **matching** public spending.
Statement 3 is wrong: **SPR 1958** had **no numeric target** (nor did **TPS 1983**).
xa: Reality: GERD reached **0.84% of GDP in FY 2023-24**, a **15-year high**.
Critics: the **2%** GERD goal was **missed under every policy**.
**2026 recommendations**: GERD to **2%** within **4-5 years** via the private sector.

2.s: India's Gross Expenditure on R&D (GERD) reached what share of GDP in FY 2023-24, described as a 15-year high?
2.x: GERD reached 0.84% of GDP in FY 2023-24, a 15-year high. About 0.64-0.65% was the earlier level, 2% is the national target that every policy has missed, and 1.2% is not a recorded level.
2.tq: GERD 0.84% (FY24) vs 2% target.
xs: GERD reached **0.84% of GDP in FY 2023-24**, a **15-year high** — option **(2)**.
**0.64%** was roughly the earlier level (about **0.64-0.65%**) — option (1) is outdated.
**2%** is the national aim, never reached — option (4) is wrong.
xa: **STP 2003** aimed at **2%** by end of the **Tenth Plan**; **STI 2013** at **2%** with private matching.
**2026 recommendations**: **2%** within **4-5 years** via private sector.
Draft **National Health Research Policy, 2026**: health-research spending from **0.024%** of GDP to **0.072% by 2037**.

2.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. PM-STIAC was set up in 2018 and is chaired by the Principal Scientific Adviser.
2. The Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser was created in 2009.
3. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam was the first Principal Scientific Adviser.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
2.x: Statement 1 is correct: PM-STIAC, 2018, chaired by the PSA. Statement 2 is wrong: the PSA office was created in 1999. Statement 3 is correct: Kalam was the first PSA. So '1 and 3 only' is right.
2.tq: PSA office 1999 (Kalam first); PM-STIAC 2018.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: **PM-STIAC** set up in **2018**, chaired by the **PSA**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the PSA office was created in **1999**, not 2009.
Statement 3 is correct: the first PSA was **A.P.J. Abdul Kalam**.
xa: PSA = chief S&T adviser to **PM and Cabinet**.
PM-STIAC framed **nine technology missions** (**Oct 2018-Jan 2019**).
**ANRF**: PM = President; S&T and Education ministers = Vice-Presidents.

2.s: Which of the following statements about ANRF is NOT correct?
o: It provides strategic direction for research and innovation.
It pools public and private research and development resources.
Its entire proposed ₹50,000 crore funding for 2023–28 is to come from non-government sources.
It subsumed the Science and Engineering Research Board.
2.x: The proposed funding is ₹50,000 crore for 2023–28, of which about ₹36,000 crore is expected from non-government sources; therefore, the entire amount is not expected from non-government sources.
2.tq: Find the incorrect funding-composition statement rather than the incorrect institutional function.
xs: Statement (3) is NOT correct — of **₹50,000 crore** (2023-28), only about **₹36,000 crore** is expected from **non-government sources** — option **(3)**.
ANRF does give **strategic direction**, **pools public and private R&D** money and **subsumed SERB** — options (1), (2), (4) are correct.
xa: **Ease of Doing R&D in India report (Aug 2026)**: ~**80%** of ANRF funds go to **IITs**; slow approvals.
ANRF: **PM = President**.
ANRF Governing Board finances projects at **TRL 4** and above.

2.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the institution with its role or establishment detail?
o: DST — established in 1986 as the parent department of CSIR
DBT — established in 1971 as the nodal department for science policy
DSIR — established in 1985 and functioning as the parent department of CSIR
CSIR — established in 1971 as the Department of Biotechnology
2.x: The Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR) was established in 1985 and is the parent department of CSIR. DST was established in 1971, DBT in 1986 and CSIR in 1942.
2.tq: Start with the sure institutional-year pair and reject swapped departments.
xs: **DSIR (1985)** is the **parent department of CSIR** — option **(3)**; its Secretary is **DG of CSIR**.
**DST** was est. **1971** and is the nodal science-policy department — option (1) is wrong.
**DBT** was est. **1986** — option (2) is wrong.
**CSIR** was est. **1942** — option (4) is wrong.
xa: **PSA** office created **1999**; first PSA **A.P.J. Abdul Kalam**.
**PM-STIAC** set up **2018**.
**CSIR and DBT** are India's lead agencies for **BRICS S&T** (**Mar 2026**).

2.s: During India’s chairship of BRICS science and technology cooperation, which two organisations act as India’s lead agencies?
2.x: CSIR and the Department of Biotechnology act as India’s lead agencies for BRICS science and technology cooperation during India’s chairship.
2.tq: Identify the correct pair of lead agencies rather than a general policy body.
xs: **CSIR and DBT** are India's lead agencies during India's **BRICS** chairship — option **(3)** (**Mar 2026**).
**CSIR** (est. **1942**) runs under **DSIR**; **DBT** was est. **1986**.
xa: **DST** (**1971**) is the nodal department for science policy.
**ANRF** is statutory under the **ANRF Act, 2023**.
**PM-STIAC** is chaired by the **PSA**.

2.s: Which organisation is the nodal agency for improving India’s Global Innovation Index rank and also publishes the India Innovation Index?
2.x: NITI Aayog is the nodal agency for improving India’s GII rank and publishes the India Innovation Index.
2.tq: Identify the agency from its paired ranking and index functions.
xs: **NITI Aayog** is the nodal agency for India's **GII** rank and publishes the **India Innovation Index** — option **(2)**.
The **India Innovation Index** 3rd edition (**2021**) was released on **21 Jul 2022**.
xa: NITI Aayog hosts the **Atal Innovation Mission** (**2016**).
The **National Innovation Council (2010)** was under **Sam Pitroda**.
**ANRF** pools public and private R&D money.

2.s:
Consider the following objectives of the Science and Technology Policy, 2003:
1. Promotion of research, innovation and technology transfer.
2. Sustainable development and poverty alleviation.
3. Improvement in quality of life.
4. Optimal utilisation of existing physical and knowledge resources.
Which of the objectives given above were associated with the policy?
2.x: All four objectives were associated with the Science and Technology Policy, 2003, including the optimal utilisation of existing physical and knowledge resources.
2.tq: Check whether the apparently less prominent fourth objective is also included before choosing the complete combination.
xs: All four were **STP 2003** objectives — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4** (**UPPSC 2008**).
Objectives: **sustainable development, poverty alleviation, quality of life**.
Also: **research, innovation and technology transfer**, and **optimal utilisation of existing physical and knowledge resources**.
xa: STP 2003 was under **A.B. Vajpayee**; it brought **science and technology together**.
It aimed to raise **GERD to 2% of GDP** by end of the **Tenth Plan**.
STP 2003 stressed **investment in R&D**.

2.s: The National Innovation Council, established in 2010, was associated with which of the following?
o: A.P.J. Abdul Kalam and the management of defence production
Sam Pitroda and the promotion of inclusive innovation
The Principal Scientific Adviser and the regulation of higher education
NITI Aayog and the preparation of the Five Year Plans
2.x: The National Innovation Council was established in 2010 under Sam Pitroda, with inclusive innovation as its goal.
2.tq: Pair the body with its chairperson and distinctive objective.
xs: The **National Innovation Council (2010)** was under **Sam Pitroda**, with **inclusive innovation** as its goal — option **(2)**.
It was the vehicle of the **Decade of Innovation (2010-2020)**.
xa: It promoted **state and sectoral innovation councils**.
The first **PSA** was **A.P.J. Abdul Kalam** (office created **1999**).
**NITI Aayog** publishes the **India Innovation Index**.

2.s:
Consider the following statements about the Open Science Framework of the Draft STIP 2020:
1. It proposed 'One Nation, One Subscription' for pan-India journal access.
2. It proposed that publicly funded data be made available under FAIR terms.
3. One Nation, One Subscription was approved by the Cabinet in November 2024 with about Rs 60,000 crore for 2025-27.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
2.x: Statement 1 is correct: ONOS gives pan-India journal access. Statement 2 is correct: data under FAIR terms. Statement 3 is wrong: the outlay was about Rs 6,000 crore, not Rs 60,000 crore. So '1 and 2 only' is right.
2.tq: ONOS: Cabinet Nov 2024, about Rs 6,000 crore for 2025-27.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: **"One Nation, One Subscription"** for **pan-India journal access**.
Statement 2 is correct: publicly funded data under **FAIR** terms.
Statement 3 is wrong: Cabinet approved ONOS in **Nov 2024** with about **₹6,000 crore**, not ₹60,000 crore.
xa: Open science portal: **INDSTA** (Indian Science and Technology Archive of Research).
ONOS and **RIEF** were outcomes of STIP 2020.
⚠ **Atal Innovation Mission** was NOT an outcome of STIP 2020 (**BPSC 2025**).

2.s: Which of the following correctly states the 2026 recommendations concerning research and innovation funding?
o: GERD should reach 2% of GDP within four to five years through greater private-sector participation, along with creation of NISPG and Vigyan Nidhi
A National Institute for Science Policy and Governance should be abolished and fellowships decentralised
GERD should remain below 1% of GDP and public funding should replace private funding
The target is to double GERD within one year through the existing fellowship system only
2.x: The recommendations called for GERD to reach 2% of GDP within four to five years through the private sector, proposed NISPG, and suggested a unified fellowship called Vigyan Nidhi.
2.tq: Match the recommendation package rather than isolating one proposal.
xs: The **24 May 2026** recommendations: **GERD to 2% of GDP within 4-5 years via private sector**, plus **NISPG** and **"Vigyan Nidhi"** — option **(1)**.
**NISPG** = **National Institute for Science Policy and Governance** — to be created, not abolished.
**Vigyan Nidhi** is a **unified fellowship**.
xa: **RDI Fund**: **₹1 lakh crore** to boost private R&D.
GERD reached **0.84%** of GDP in **FY 2023-24**.
Criticism: **2%** GERD goal missed under every policy.

2.s:
Consider the following statements about the Research, Development and Innovation Fund:
1. It has an approved size of ₹1 lakh crore.
2. ₹20,000 crore was provided for FY 2025–26.
3. It is intended to boost private research and development.
4. It is operated through a Special Purpose Fund in the ANRF.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
2.x: All four statements are correct. The RDI Fund has a ₹1 lakh crore size, includes ₹20,000 crore for FY 2025–26, promotes private R&D and operates through a Special Purpose Fund in ANRF.
2.tq: Test the fund’s size, annual allocation, purpose and institutional channel together.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**RDI Fund**: **₹1 lakh crore** to **boost private R&D**.
Approved **1 July 2025**; **₹20,000 crore** for **FY 2025-26**.
Run through a **Special Purpose Fund** in **ANRF**.
xa: Duration: some notes say "over **six** years", others **seven** years (**Feb 2026**).
**ANRF** funding: **₹50,000 crore** over **2023-28**.

2.s:
Consider the following statements about the draft National Health Research Policy, 2026:
1. It is the first unified health-research framework, prepared by the Department of Health Research.
2. It proposes a two-tier governance structure.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
2.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the draft proposes three-tier governance. So '1 only' is right.
2.tq: Health Research Policy 2026: first unified framework, three-tier governance.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: the draft **National Health Research Policy, 2026** (**Department of Health Research**) is the **first unified health-research framework**.
Statement 2 is wrong: it proposes **three-tier governance**, not two-tier.
xa: Target: public health-research spending from **0.024% of GDP** to **0.072% by 2037** and **0.15% by 2047**.
Criticism: the **2%** GERD goal was **missed under every policy**.
GERD reached **0.84% of GDP in FY 2023-24**.

2.s: Which of the following correctly describes INSPIRE?
o: Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research; it draws young talent into science from school awards to PhD fellowships and faculty posts
Institute Network for Science and Professional Research Education; it provides shared instruments to MSMEs
Innovation Support Programme for Research Equipment; it upgrades departmental laboratories
Indian Network for Scientific Promotion and Research Excellence; it provides only university publication grants
2.x: INSPIRE stands for Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research and covers a continuum from school awards to PhD fellowships and faculty posts to attract young talent to science.
2.tq: Use the full-form-and-purpose combination to reject swapped institutional functions.
xs: **INSPIRE** = **Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research** — it draws young talent from **school awards to PhD fellowships and faculty posts** — option **(1)**.
Shared instruments for MSMEs is **SATHI**; departmental lab upgrades is **FIST**; publication-based grants is **PURSE**.
xa: **SAIF** — regional centres for high-end instruments.
**FIST** covers **universities and higher educational institutions**.
**Vigyan Nidhi** was recommended as a **unified fellowship** (**2026**).

2.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I
(a) SATHI
(b) FIST
(c) PURSE
(d) SAIF

List-II
(i) Grants based on research-publication performance
(ii) Regional access to high-end analytical instruments
(iii) Shared professionally managed S&T infrastructure
(iv) Laboratory and infrastructure upgrading in departments
2.x: SATHI provides shared infrastructure, FIST upgrades laboratories, PURSE uses research-publication performance for grants, and SAIF provides regional access to high-end instruments.
