xs: **Science Express** was an exhibition train of **DST** with the **Vikram A. Sarabhai Community Science Centre, Ahmedabad**, first flagged off in **2007** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Later editions: **Biodiversity Special** and **Climate Action Special**.
The **2003–04** exhibition on wheels was **Vigyan Rail** (DST, not CSIR); the **2015** school programme is **Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan**.
xa: ⚠ **Vigyan Rail** = DST, not CSIR (UPSC 2005 trap).
**NCSM** (formed **1978**) is under the Ministry of Culture, not DST.
**IISF** is an annual science festival begun in **2015** (New Delhi).

6.s: 'Vigyan Rail', a science exhibition on wheels run in 2003-04, was organised by:
o: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research
6.x: Vigyan Rail was organised by the Department of Science and Technology (DST). CSIR is the classic trap (UPSC 2005). NCSM (Ministry of Culture) runs science centres and mobile exhibition buses, and the Ministry of HRD ran the Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan, not the science trains.
6.tq: Science trains (Vigyan Rail, Science Express) = DST, not CSIR.
xs: **Vigyan Rail** (2003-04) was organised by the **Department of Science and Technology** — so option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ **CSIR** is the classic trap (UPSC 2005).
**NCSM** (Ministry of Culture) runs science centres and mobile exhibition buses; the **Ministry of HRD** ran Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan.
xa: **Science Express** — DST exhibition train with the Vikram A. Sarabhai Community Science Centre, first flagged off **2007**.
**Vigyan Prasar** (**1989**) and **NCSTC** are also DST bodies.

6.s: The India International Science Festival (IISF) is best described by which of the following statements?
o: An annual festival begun in 2015 in New Delhi, organised by the Ministry of Science & Technology and the Ministry of Earth Sciences with Vijnana Bharati
An annual exhibition organised by NCSM under the Ministry of Culture since 1978
A school science congress organised by the Ministry of Education since 2015
A biennial festival begun in 2007 by DST alone
6.x: IISF began in 2015 in New Delhi and is organised by the Ministry of Science & Technology and the Ministry of Earth Sciences with Vijnana Bharati (VIBHA).
6.tq: Match the festival with its start year, place and complete group of organisers.
xs: **IISF** is an **annual** festival begun in **2015** in **New Delhi**, organised by the **Ministry of Science & Technology** and **Ministry of Earth Sciences** with **Vijnana Bharati** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**NCSM** (formed **1978**) is under the Ministry of Culture; **Science Express** (DST) first ran in **2007**.
xa: VIBHA = **Vijnana Bharati**.
**Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan** (Ministry of HRD/Education) was also launched in **2015**.
The **National Children's Science Congress** is run by **NCSTC** (DST).

6.s: ICMR-SHINE, a science and health outreach initiative, is intended primarily for which group?
6.x: ICMR-SHINE, expanded as Science & Health Innovation for the Nextgen Explorers, is an outreach initiative for students of Classes 9–12.
6.tq: Use the target-group distinction to separate school outreach initiatives.
xs: **ICMR-SHINE** is an outreach initiative for **Students of Classes 9–12** — so option **(2)** is correct.
SHINE = **Science & Health Innovation for the Nextgen Explorers**.
xa: It is run by **ICMR** and the **Dept of Health Research**.
Its **2nd edition** concluded in **Aug 2026** (16 Aug 2026).

6.s: Which of the following is NOT associated with the National Innovation Foundation?
o: Festival of Innovation at Rashtrapati Bhavan
National Biennial Grassroots Innovation and Traditional Knowledge Awards
VIGYANOTSAV quiz for National Science Day
6.x: The National Innovation Foundation conducts or is associated with the grassroots innovation awards, IGNITE and the Festival of Innovation at Rashtrapati Bhavan. VIGYANOTSAV is associated with National Science Day outreach by NCSTC.
6.tq: Find the one programme belonging to a neighbouring institution rather than NIF.
xs: The **VIGYANOTSAV quiz for National Science Day** is NOT an NIF activity — so option **(4)** is correct.
VIGYANOTSAV is part of **NCSTC**'s (DST) National Science Day outreach.
NIF's competitions: **National Biennial Grassroots Innovation and Traditional Knowledge Awards**, **IGNITE**, and **Festival of Innovation (FOIN)** at **Rashtrapati Bhavan**.
xa: NIF grew out of the **Honey Bee Network** (Prof. **Anil K. Gupta**).
NCSTC's National Science Day outreach reached over **6.35 lakh** people.

6.s: Vigyan Dhara is best described as:
o: A DST umbrella scheme merging three schemes relating to capacity building, research and innovation
An autonomous body for grassroots innovations under NITI Aayog
A radio network operated by IGNOU
A single television channel for school education
6.x: Vigyan Dhara is a DST umbrella scheme merging schemes concerning S&T institutional and human capacity building, research and development, and innovation, technology development and deployment.
6.tq: Identify the umbrella-scheme concept rather than a communication channel or institution.
xs: **Vigyan Dhara** is a **DST umbrella scheme merging three schemes** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The merged areas: **S&T institutional and human capacity building**; **research & development**; **innovation, technology development and deployment**.
It was approved by the Cabinet in **Aug 2024**.
xa: The grassroots-innovation body under DST is **NIF**, not under NITI Aayog.
The FM radio network of IGNOU is **Gyan Vani**; free DTH educational channels = **SWAYAM Prabha**.
**Vigyan Prasar** (DST, **1989**) runs **India Science**.

6.s: The National Innovation Foundation-India was set up in March 2000 with the support of:
o: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research
6.x: NIF-India was set up in March 2000 with the support of the Department of Science and Technology and functions as an autonomous body of DST.
6.tq: Use the parent-department trap to identify the institutional sponsor.
xs: **NIF-India** was set up in **March 2000** with the support of the **Department of Science and Technology** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is an **autonomous body of DST** (UPSC 2015 statement 1 is correct).
xa: NIF grew out of the **Honey Bee Network** of Prof. **Anil K. Gupta** (SRISTI, IIM Ahmedabad).
Base: **Gandhinagar/Ahmedabad**, Gujarat.
Mandate: scout, support and spread **grassroots technological innovations** and **outstanding traditional knowledge**.

6.s: Which of the following best describes the mandate of the National Innovation Foundation?
o: To scout, support and spread grassroots technological innovations and outstanding traditional knowledge
To regulate all patent applications in India
To operate national educational television channels
To conduct advanced research exclusively with foreign institutions
6.x: NIF's mandate is to scout, support and spread grassroots technological innovations and outstanding traditional knowledge. It is not mandated to conduct advanced research exclusively with foreign institutions.
6.tq: Reject the wrong-activity trap by identifying the institution's actual mandate.
xs: NIF's mandate is to **scout, support and spread grassroots technological innovations and outstanding traditional knowledge** — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ It is **not** about advanced research with foreign institutions (UPSC 2015 statement 2 is wrong).
Educational TV channels are run by others (e.g. **SWAYAM Prabha**, Ministry of Education).
xa: Competitions: **National Biennial Grassroots Innovation and Traditional Knowledge Awards**, **IGNITE** (students' ideas), **Festival of Innovation (FOIN)** at Rashtrapati Bhavan.
**STIP 2020**: grassroots innovators to be helped with **IPR/patent filing** through higher education institutes.

6.s: The National Innovation Foundation grew out of the:
6.x: NIF grew out of the Honey Bee Network, associated with Prof. Anil K. Gupta, SRISTI and IIM Ahmedabad.
6.tq: Link the institution to its origin network and reject unrelated science platforms.
xs: NIF grew out of the **Honey Bee Network** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The Honey Bee Network is linked to Prof. **Anil K. Gupta**, **SRISTI**, **IIM Ahmedabad**.
**SWAYAM Prabha** is a DTH channel group; **ISCA** is a science association (**1914**); **VIGYANOTSAV** is an NCSTC National Science Day quiz.
xa: NIF-India was set up in **2000** (March) as an **autonomous body of DST**.
Base: **Gandhinagar/Ahmedabad**, Gujarat.

6.s: The Raman Effect commemorated by National Science Day was discovered by C.V. Raman in:
6.x: National Science Day commemorates C.V. Raman's discovery of the Raman Effect in 1928.
6.tq: Use the year attached to the commemorated scientific discovery.
xs: C.V. Raman discovered the **Raman Effect** in **1928** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**National Science Day** (**28 February**) commemorates this discovery.
xa: **National Mathematics Day** — **22 December**, birth anniversary of **Srinivasa Ramanujan** (declared **2012**).
NCSTC uses National Science Day for outreach — **VIGYANOTSAV** quiz, science kits — reaching over **6.35 lakh** people.
Raman also founded the **IASc** (**1934**, Bengaluru).

6.s: National Mathematics Day was declared in 2012 to commemorate the birth anniversary of:
6.x: National Mathematics Day commemorates Srinivasa Ramanujan's birth anniversary. It was declared in 2012, his 125th birth year.
6.tq: Distinguish the scientist associated with Mathematics Day from those associated with physics and technology.
xs: **National Mathematics Day** commemorates the birth anniversary of **Srinivasa Ramanujan** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It falls on **22 December** and was declared in **2012**, his **125th** birth year.
**C.V. Raman** is honoured by **National Science Day** (**28 February**).
xa: National Science Day marks the discovery of the **Raman Effect** (**1928**).
Raman founded **IASc** (**1934**).

6.s: Which one of the following pairs of day and date is correctly matched?
6.x: National Science Day is observed on 28 February, marking C.V. Raman's discovery of the Raman Effect (1928). National Mathematics Day is on 22 December, Srinivasa Ramanujan's birth anniversary. The first two options swap these two dates, and 11 May is not Mathematics Day.
6.tq: 28 Feb = Raman (Science Day); 22 Dec = Ramanujan (Maths Day).
xs: **National Science Day — 28 February** is correctly matched — so option **(3)** is correct.
It marks C.V. Raman's discovery of the **Raman Effect** (**1928**).
**National Mathematics Day** is on **22 December** (Ramanujan's birth anniversary); options 1 and 2 swap the dates.
xa: Mathematics Day was declared in **2012**, Ramanujan's **125th** birth year.
National Science Day 2026 events at **VIT-AP** were addressed by ex-ISRO chief **A.S. Kiran Kumar** (**1 Mar 2026**).

6.s: Vigyan Prasar is an autonomous organisation under which of the following?
o: Department of Science and Technology, Ministry of Science and Technology
Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Human Resource Development
6.x: Vigyan Prasar is an autonomous organisation of the Department of Science and Technology under the Ministry of Science and Technology. It was set up in 1989 at New Delhi.
6.tq: Use the parent-department trap by distinguishing DST from the Ministry of Education.
xs: **Vigyan Prasar** is an autonomous organisation of the **Department of Science and Technology (DST)**, **Ministry of Science and Technology** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was set up in **1989** at **New Delhi**.
⚠ It is **not** under the Ministry of HRD/Education (UPSC 2005 trap).
xa: Vigyan Prasar runs **India Science**, an Internet-based (OTT) science channel.
**DD Science** (daily one-hour slot on DD National) and **India Science** were launched together on **15 January 2019**.
**Vigyan Dhara** (Cabinet, **Aug 2024**) is a DST umbrella scheme merging **3** DST schemes.

6.s:
Consider the following statements regarding DD Science and India Science:
1. DD Science is a one-hour daily science slot on DD National.
2. India Science is an Internet-based science channel run by Vigyan Prasar.

xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is the answer.
Statement 1: **DD Science** is a **one-hour daily** science slot on **DD National**.
Statement 2: **India Science** is an **Internet-based (OTT)** science channel run by **Vigyan Prasar**.
Statement 3: both were launched together on **15 January 2019** by the Union Minister for Science & Technology.

7.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its full form and target group?
o: SEATS — Scheme for Early Attraction of Talents for Science — school students
SHE — Support for Her Education — doctoral researchers
AORC — Assured Opportunity for Research Careers — only school students
MANAK — Million Awards for National Academic Knowledge — university teachers
7.x: SEATS means Scheme for Early Attraction of Talents for Science and targets school students. SHE is Scholarship for Higher Education, AORC concerns doctoral and post-doctoral careers, and MANAK concerns school students in Classes VI–X.
7.tq: Full-form trap using familiar-looking but incorrect expansions.
xs: **SEATS — Scheme for Early Attraction of Talents for Science — school students** is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
**SHE** = **Scholarship for Higher Education** (not "Support for Her Education"), for top-ranked UG/PG science students.
**AORC** is for **doctoral / post-doctoral** researchers, not school students.
**MANAK** = **Million Minds Augmenting National Aspiration and Knowledge**, for Classes **VI-X**.
xa: INSPIRE is a **DST** flagship launched in **2008**.
AORC = INSPIRE **Fellowship** (PhD) and INSPIRE **Faculty**.

7.s:
Consider the following statements about INSPIRE components:
1. SHE stands for Scholarship for Higher Education.
2. SHE supports top-ranked students in undergraduate and postgraduate natural and basic sciences.
3. AORC includes the INSPIRE Fellowship and INSPIRE Faculty programmes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
7.x: All three statements are correct. SHE is the higher-education scholarship component, while AORC covers research-career opportunities through INSPIRE Fellowship and INSPIRE Faculty.
7.tq: Component-scope statement testing with a look-alike expansion trap.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is the answer.
Statement 1: **SHE** = **Scholarship for Higher Education**.
Statement 2: SHE supports **top-ranked students** in **UG/PG natural and basic sciences**.
Statement 3: **AORC** covers the INSPIRE **Fellowship** (PhD) and INSPIRE **Faculty**.
xa: ⚠ SHE is NOT "Support for Her Education".
INSPIRE Fellowship 2025: **653** doctoral fellowships, **65% female**, ~**31%** former SHE scholars.

7.s: The INSPIRE component 'MANAK', aimed at school students of Classes VI-X, stands for:
o: Million Minds Augmenting National Aspiration and Knowledge
Million Awards for National Academic Knowledge
Mission for Advancing National Aptitude and Knowledge
Model Awards for Nurturing Aspiring Kids
7.x: MANAK = Million Minds Augmenting National Aspiration and Knowledge, for Classes VI-X (age 10-15). The other expansions are made up; 'Million Awards for National Academic Knowledge' is a common wrong guess.
7.tq: MANAK = Million MINDS (school ideas), not awards.
xs: MANAK stands for **Million Minds Augmenting National Aspiration and Knowledge** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is aimed at Classes **VI-X**, aged **10-15**.
xa: Other INSPIRE components: **SEATS**, **SHE**, **AORC**.

7.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Ramalingaswami Re-entry Fellowship — Indian life-science and biotechnology scientists abroad — DBT
VAJRA — Overseas scientists, including NRIs and OCIs — SERB/ANRF
J.C. Bose Fellowship — Active senior scientists recognised for excellence — SERB/ANRF
PMRF — Women scientists returning after a career break — Department of Biotechnology

ANRF schemes: **PMECRG**, **Prime Minister Professorship**, **National Science Chair**, **N-PDF**.

7.s: Which one of the following is NOT a scheme or initiative associated with the Department of Science and Technology in the material listed?
7.x: The Ramalingaswami Re-entry Fellowship is a DBT (Department of Biotechnology) scheme for Indian life-science and biotech scientists abroad who return, so it is the odd one out. INSPIRE, Vigyan Jyoti and the Nano Mission are DST schemes.

xs: The **Ramalingaswami Re-entry Fellowship** is a **DBT** scheme, not DST — so option **(1)** is the odd one out.

**INSPIRE** (**2008**) and **Vigyan Jyoti** are DST schemes.

7.s: Which of the following is NOT a component associated with NIDHI?

It is run by **NCGTC**.
NIDHI's components include **PRAYAS**, **Entrepreneur-in-Residence**, **Seed Support System**, **Technology Business Incubators**, Accelerators and Centres of Excellence.
xa: NIDHI is a **DST** initiative of **2016**.
**Fund of Funds for Startups** — **SIDBI**, **₹10,000 crore**.

7.s: Which one of the following schemes is intended for meritorious girl students studying in Classes 9 to 12 and is implemented with the Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti?

xs: **Vigyan Jyoti** is for meritorious **girl students of Class 9-12**, with the **Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti** as agency — so option **(2)** is correct.

**GATI** is an institutional gender-equity charter; **CURIE** supports **22 Women PG Colleges**; **WISE** is for women scientists.

**WIDUSHI** = senior women scientists in **interdisciplinary** S&T (APPSC-G1 2024).

7.s:
Consider the following statements regarding WISE-KIRAN:

2. It particularly supports women scientists who have experienced a career break.
3. Its programmes include WISE-PhD, WISE-PDF and WIDUSHI.

xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is the answer.

Statement 2: it supports women scientists, esp. those with a **career break** — re-entry and advancement in STEM.

7.s: WIDUSHI, associated with WISE-KIRAN, is intended primarily for which of the following groups?
o: Women scientists seeking their first extramural biotechnology grant
Senior women scientists conducting interdisciplinary research in science and technology

7.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: SERB-POWER — Women researchers in academic and R&D institutions

8.s:
Consider the following statements about the Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF):
1. It derives its legal basis from the ANRF Act, 2023.
2. The Union Minister of Science and Technology is the ex officio President of its Governing Board.
3. It subsumed the Science and Engineering Research Board (SERB).
How many of the statements given above are correct?
8.x: Statement 1 is correct: ANRF rests on the ANRF Act, 2023. Statement 2 is wrong: the Prime Minister is the ex officio President of its Governing Board. Statement 3 is correct: it subsumed SERB. So only two are correct.
8.tq: ANRF: Act 2023, PM as President, SERB subsumed.
xs: **Only two** statements (1 and 3) are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
1: ANRF rests on the **ANRF Act, 2023** — correct.
2 is wrong: the **PM** is **ex officio President** of its Governing Board.
3: ANRF **subsumed SERB** — correct.
xa: ANRF is custodian of the **₹1 lakh crore RDI Fund**.
ANRF schemes include **MAHA-EV**, **SERB-SURE**, **JC Bose Grant** and **Ramanujan Fellowship**.
**Criticism:** funding shortfalls followed the **SERB-to-ANRF** transition.

8.s: The ₹1 lakh crore RDI Fund is associated with the ANRF through a:
8.x: ANRF is the custodian of the ₹1 lakh crore RDI Fund through a two-tier Special Purpose Fund.
8.tq: Combine the fund amount with its institutional mechanism.
xs: ANRF is custodian of the **₹1 lakh crore RDI Fund** through a **two-tier Special Purpose Fund** — so option **(4)** is correct.
ANRF was set up under the **ANRF Act, 2023**; the **PM** is ex officio President of its Governing Board.
xa: ANRF **subsumed SERB**; funding shortfalls followed the transition.
ANRF schemes: PMECRG, **MAHA-EV**, MAHA MedTech, AI-SE, PAIR, **SERB-SURE**, JC Bose Grant, Ramanujan Fellowship.

8.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the two Quantum Test and Reference Facilities in Andhra Pradesh?
o: 1S at SRM University-AP and 1Q at Medha Towers, Gannavaram
1S at IIT Hyderabad and 1Q at Amaravati Secretariat
1Q at SRM University-AP and 1S at Medha Towers, Gannavaram
8.x: The 1S test bed is at SRM University-AP and the 1Q facility is at Medha Towers in Gannavaram.
8.tq: Separate similar facility codes by matching each code with its precise location.
xs: India's first Quantum Reference Facility test beds: **1S at SRM University-AP** and **1Q at Medha Towers, Gannavaram** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Option 4 swaps the two.
xa: Opened on **14 April 2026** (**World Quantum Day**).
Components from **TIFR, IISc, DRDO, IIT Bombay**; built with **Qubit Force/Qubitekk**.

8.s: The foundation stone of the Amaravati Quantum Valley was laid at which of the following places?
8.x: The foundation stone of the Amaravati Quantum Valley was laid at Uddandarayunipalem.
8.tq: Use the location-based direct-recall method and distinguish the foundation site from associated facilities.
xs: The foundation stone of the Amaravati Quantum Valley was laid at **Uddandarayunipalem** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Acharya Nagarjuna University** hosts NIELIT classes; **Medha Towers, Gannavaram** hosts the **1Q** test bed.
xa: The Valley has **50 acres** under NQM, with two **18-storey towers** (**₹1,205 crore**, L&T).
AP plans to train **4.5 million** people in AI and quantum.

8.s:
Consider the following statements about incentives and human-resource development in the Amaravati Quantum Valley:
1. Technology firms in the Valley are eligible for 100% exemption from stamp duty and registration fees.
2. Andhra Pradesh plans to train 4.5 million people in artificial intelligence and quantum technologies.
3. The exemption applies only to registration fees and not to stamp duty.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
8.x: The policy provides 100% exemption from both stamp duty and registration fees, and the plan includes training 4.5 million people in AI and quantum technologies. Statement 3 incorrectly excludes stamp duty.
8.tq: Split the paired financial terms and identify the statement that reverses the scope of the exemption.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — so option **(1) 1 and 2 only** is the answer.
Statement 1 is **correct**: **100% stamp duty and registration fee exemption** for tech firms in the Valley.
Statement 2 is **correct**: AP plans to train **4.5 million** people in AI and quantum.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: the exemption covers **both** stamp duty and registration fee.
xa: Quantum Computing Policy: **50+** proposals, **7** approvals.
IBM will **train 1 lakh youth** under the Feb **2026** MoUs.

8.s: The NIELIT Quantum and AI campus at Amaravati is being established by which Ministry, with classes scheduled to begin from September 2026 at which institution?
o: Ministry of Science and Technology; SRM University-AP
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology; Acharya Nagarjuna University, Guntur
Ministry of Education; Andhra University, Visakhapatnam
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship; IIT Tirupati
8.x: The campus is associated with the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, and classes are scheduled from September 2026 at Acharya Nagarjuna University, Guntur.
8.tq: Use the 'which ministry and which institution?' two-part discrimination method.
xs: The NIELIT Quantum & AI campus is by **MeitY**, with classes from **Sept 2026** at **Acharya Nagarjuna University, Guntur** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Campus: **8.5 acres**, **₹730.70 crore** over **5** years.
**SRM University-AP** hosts the **1S** test bed, not NIELIT.
xa: A **NIELIT Quantum AI deemed university** was among the **seven MoUs** (Feb **2026**).
**PanIIT Summit** on deep tech: **Vijayawada**, **3 Oct 2026**.

8.s: Which State became the first in India to have a dedicated quantum computing policy and aims to be among the top five global quantum hubs by 2030?
8.x: Andhra Pradesh is the first State with a dedicated quantum computing policy and aims to make the Amaravati Quantum Valley one of the top five global quantum hubs by 2030. No such policy is recorded for Karnataka, Telangana or Tamil Nadu.
8.tq: First quantum policy = AP (Amaravati Quantum Valley).
xs: **Andhra Pradesh** is the **first State with a dedicated quantum computing policy**, aiming for the **top five global quantum hubs by 2030** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Its Quantum Computing Policy drew **50+** proposals with **7** approvals, and gives **100%** stamp duty and registration fee exemption.
xa: India's first **Quantum Reference Facility** test beds opened in AP on **14 April 2026**.
Foundation stone at **Uddandarayunipalem**.

8.s: India’s bioeconomy was valued at over which amount in 2024?
8.x: India’s bioeconomy was valued at over US$165 billion in 2024.
8.tq: Recall the exact scale figure and distinguish it from public-sector mission outlays.
xs: India's bioeconomy was over **US$165 billion** in **2024** — so option **(3)** is correct.
This is cited under the **Bio-E3 Policy** (**2024**).
xa: Bio-E3 = **Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment**.
Budget 2026-27: **Biopharma SHAKTI**, **₹10,000 crore** over **5** years (biologics, biosimilars).

9.s: J.C. Bose was a pioneer in microwave and millimetre-wave radio research and used which of the following components?
9.x: J.C. Bose pioneered microwave and millimetre-wave radio research and worked with a coherer and a galena semiconductor detector.
9.tq: Match the scientist’s research area with the characteristic apparatus associated with it.
xs: J.C. Bose used the **coherer and galena detector** (a semiconductor detector) in microwave/millimetre-wave radio — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **crescograph** was his plant-growth instrument, not a radio component.
xa: He worked at **IACS**, Kolkata.
Honours: knighted **1917**, **FRS 1920**.
Area: **plant physiology** and **radio/microwave physics**.

9.s: Which one of the following is a book written by J.C. Bose?
o: The Mathematical Theory of Black Holes
9.x: The Nervous Mechanism of Plants was written by J.C. Bose. His other listed works include Response in the Living and Non-Living and the Bengali science-fiction work Niruddesher Kahini.
9.tq: Distinguish the scientist’s own book from works associated with other disciplines or authors.
xs: **The Nervous Mechanism of Plants** was written by **J.C. Bose** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Chromosome Atlas of Cultivated Plants** was co-authored by **Janaki Ammal**.
xa: Bose also wrote **Response in the Living and Non-Living** (**1902**).
He wrote the Bengali science fiction **Niruddesher Kahini**.
⚠ Tagore's **Visva-Parichay** (**1937**) was dedicated to **S.N. Bose**, not J.C. Bose.

9.s:
Consider the following statements about J.C. Bose:
1. He showed that plants respond to stimuli like animals.
2. He founded the Bose Institute, Kolkata, in 1917.
3. He formulated the theory of thermal ionisation of elements.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: Statement 1 is correct: Bose showed that plants respond to stimuli, the 'plants have life' idea. Statement 2 is correct: he founded the Bose Institute in Kolkata in 1917. Statement 3 is wrong: thermal ionisation (the Saha equation) is Meghnad Saha's work. So the answer is '1 and 2 only'.
9.tq: J.C. Bose = plants have life + crescograph + Bose Institute 1917.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — so option **(2) 1 and 2 only** is the answer.
Statement 1 is **correct**: J.C. Bose showed **plants respond to stimuli like animals**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: he founded the **Bose Institute, Kolkata** in **1917**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: **thermal ionisation** (the Saha equation) is **Meghnad Saha**'s work.
xa: Bose invented the **Crescograph** to measure plant growth.
⚠ **Saha** = thermal ionisation + Damodar Valley plan.

9.s: Srinivasa Ramanujan worked at Cambridge with which mathematician?
9.x: Srinivasa Ramanujan worked with the British mathematician G.H. Hardy at Cambridge.
9.tq: Identify the collaborator from a set of scientists connected with different fields.
xs: Ramanujan worked at **Cambridge** with **G.H. Hardy** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Amrit Lal Sircar** invited C.V. Raman to IACS; **P.M.S. Blackett** guided **Bibha Chowdhuri**'s PhD; **D.M. Bose** worked with Bibha on cosmic rays.
xa: **1729** is the **Hardy-Ramanujan number**.
Ramanujan: born **22 December 1887**, Erode (TN); died **1920**; **FRS 1918**, Fellow of Trinity College.

9.s: The number 1729 is popularly known as the:
9.x: The number 1729 is known as the Hardy-Ramanujan number.
9.tq: Recognise a famous numerical association rather than a date or institutional fact.
xs: **1729** is the **Hardy-Ramanujan number** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It recalls Ramanujan's collaboration with **G.H. Hardy** at **Cambridge**.
xa: **22 December** = **National Mathematics Day**; **2012** = **National Mathematical Year** (**125th** birth anniversary).
Ramanujan: **FRS 1918**.

9.s: The Raman Effect was discovered by C.V. Raman on 28 February 1928 at which institution?
o: Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science, Kolkata
9.x: C.V. Raman discovered the Raman Effect on 28 February 1928 at the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science in Kolkata.
9.tq: Link the exact date of a discovery with its location and institution.
xs: Raman discovered the Raman Effect on **28 February 1928** at the **Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science (IACS), Kolkata** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Raman Research Institute** (**1948**) and **Indian Academy of Sciences** (**1934**) were founded by him later; he was IISc's first Indian director.
xa: Raman worked at IACS outside office hours while in the **Accountant General's Office**, Calcutta (from **1907**), invited by **Amrit Lal Sircar**.
IACS was founded in **1876** by **Mahendra Lal Sircar**; **150th anniversary in 2026**.
Raman Effect = change in **wavelength** of light when it scatters.

9.s: The Saha equation was formulated by Meghnad Saha from his theory of:
9.x: Meghnad Saha formulated the Saha, or ionisation, equation from his theory of thermal ionisation of elements.
9.tq: Link an equation to the theory from which it was derived.
xs: The Saha (ionisation) equation came from Saha's theory of **thermal ionisation of elements** — so option **(4)** is correct (UPPSC 2014).
**Plant response to stimuli** is **J.C. Bose**; **quantum statistics of bosons** is **S.N. Bose**.
xa: The Saha equation is a basic tool for reading **spectra of stars** (temperature, ionisation state).
Saha's instrument measures the **weight and pressure of solar rays**.
Saha: **FRS 1927**; elected to **Lok Sabha (1952)**.

9.s: The Saha equation is a basic tool for reading stellar spectra because it helps determine the:
o: Distance and magnetic field of oceans
Temperature and ionisation state of stars
Age and chemical composition of plants
Mass and rotation of planets only
9.x: The Saha equation helps interpret stellar spectra by indicating the temperature and ionisation state of stars.
9.tq: Apply the scientific equation to the observational problem it is used to solve.
xs: The Saha equation helps read stellar spectra by giving the **temperature and ionisation state of stars** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It came from Saha's theory of **thermal ionisation**.
xa: Saha's area: **astrophysics**.
⚠ **Saha** = thermal ionisation; **Bhabha** = cosmic rays.
Saha came from **Dacca district** (now Bangladesh).

9.s: Which statement best describes Meghnad Saha’s contribution to river planning in India?
o: He prepared the original plan for the Damodar Valley Project.
He designed the first irrigation project on the Krishna River.
He founded the first river-water tribunal in India.
He established the Central Water Commission.
9.x: Meghnad Saha was regarded as the chief architect of river planning in India and prepared the original plan for the Damodar Valley Project.
9.tq: Match a national development project with the scientist associated with its original plan.
xs: Meghnad Saha **prepared the original plan for the Damodar Valley Project** — so option **(1)** is correct.
He is called the **chief architect of river planning** in India.
xa: Saha was elected to the **Lok Sabha** in **1952**.
He founded **NASI** (**1930**) and the **Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics** (Kolkata).
⚠ **Saha** = thermal ionisation + Damodar Valley plan.

9.s:
Consider the following statements about Homi Bhabha:
1. He was the first chairman of the Atomic Energy Commission (1948).
2. He conceived India's three-stage nuclear power programme based on uranium.
3. He presided over the first UN Conference on the Peaceful Uses of Atomic Energy at Geneva in 1955.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: Statement 1 is correct: Bhabha was the AEC's first chairman (1948). Statement 2 is wrong: the three-stage programme is thorium-based. Statement 3 is correct: he presided over the 1955 Geneva conference. So only two are correct.
9.tq: Bhabha: AEC 1948, thorium three-stage plan, Geneva 1955.
xs: **Only two** statements (1 and 3) are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
1: Bhabha was the **first chairman** of the **Atomic Energy Commission (1948)** — correct.
2 is wrong: his **three-stage nuclear power programme** is **thorium-based**.
3: he presided over the **first UN Conference on Peaceful Uses of Atomic Energy**, **Geneva 1955** — correct.
xa: Bhabha founded **TIFR (1945)** and the **Atomic Energy Establishment, Trombay (1954)**, renamed **BARC** in **1967**.
He died in an Air India crash on **Mont Blanc**, **1966**.
**Bhabha scattering** (electron-positron) and cascade theory of **cosmic-ray** showers.

9.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: S.N. Bose — Quantum statistics and bosons
Birbal Sahni — Engineering and Diwan of Mysore
9.x: S.N. Bose is associated with quantum statistics and bosons. Prafulla Chandra Ray worked in chemistry, Birbal Sahni in palaeobotany, and Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar with CSIR.
9.tq: Match scientists with their areas while rejecting swapped specialised fields.
xs: **S.N. Bose — Quantum statistics and bosons** is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Prafulla Chandra Ray** = **chemistry**; **Birbal Sahni** = **palaeobotany**; **Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar** = **CSIR**.
xa: Engineering and Diwan of Mysore (**1912-1919**) = **M. Visvesvaraya**.
Number theory = **Ramanujan**.

9.s: Which of the following groups of scientists is associated with work at the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science?
o: V. Raman, Homi Bhabha, Tagore and Mahendra Lal Sircar only
Homi Bhabha, Albert Einstein, Paul Dirac and Ramanujan
J. C. Bose, Meghnad Saha, S. N. Bose and C. V. Raman
Ramanujan, Einstein, Saha and NASA scientists only
9.x: J. C. Bose, Meghnad Saha, S. N. Bose and C. V. Raman all worked at IACS.
9.tq: Identify the complete institutional association instead of selecting a partly overlapping group.
xs: **J.C. Bose, Meghnad Saha, S.N. Bose and C.V. Raman** all worked at IACS — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Einstein** and **Paul Dirac** are linked to S.N. Bose's statistics, not to IACS work; **Mahendra Lal Sircar** was its founder.
xa: Raman worked at IACS outside office hours while in the **Accountant General's Office** (from **1907**), invited by **Amrit Lal Sircar**.
IACS: founded **1876**; **150th anniversary in 2026**.

9.s: Who is known as the Father of India’s Atomic Energy Programme?
9.x: Homi J. Bhabha founded TIFR and BARC and is the father of India's atomic energy programme. C.V. Raman is known for the Raman effect.
9.tq: Recall the founders of Indian science institutions.
n: Homi J. Bhabha is called the father of India's atomic energy programme. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-10]
xs: **Homi J. Bhabha** is the **Father of India's atomic energy programme**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Niels Bohr** is the **Father of atomic physics**; **C.V. Raman** the **Father of Indian physics**.
**Ernest Rutherford** is the **Father of nuclear physics**.
xa: Bhabha was associated with **TIFR**.
**Enrico Fermi** is the **Architect of the Nuclear Age**.
**Oppenheimer** is often called the **father of the nuclear bomb**.

9.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Marie Curie was associated with Poland and France.
II. C.V. Raman was associated with India.
III. Homi J. Bhabha was associated with India.
IV. Henri Becquerel was associated with France.
V. Marie Curie was associated only with Poland.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
o: II, III, IV and V only
I, II, III and IV only
9.x: I–IV are correct: Curie was born in Poland and worked in France, Raman and Bhabha were Indian, and Becquerel was French. V is false because of the word "only".
9.tq: Check each statement for the word "only".
n: Marie Curie was associated with Poland. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 21-23]
Marie Curie was associated with France. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 21-23]
C.V. Raman was associated with India. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 21-23]
Homi J. Bhabha was associated with India. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 21-23]
Henri Becquerel was associated with France. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 21-23]
xs: Statements **I, II, III and IV** are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
I: **Marie Curie** → **Poland** and **France** — correct; so V ("**only Poland**") is wrong.
II and III: **C.V. Raman** and **Homi Bhabha** → **India** — correct.
IV: **Henri Becquerel** → **France** — correct.
xa: Curie worked at the **University of Paris** and the **Radium Institute**.
**Wilhelm Röntgen**, **Planck** and **Heisenberg** were from **Germany**.
Bhabha was associated with **TIFR**.

9.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Isaac Newton
(b) J.J. Thomson
(c) Enrico Fermi
(d) C.V. Raman

List-II
(i) Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science and IISc
(ii) Cambridge University and Royal Society
(iii) University of Chicago and Columbia
(iv) Cavendish Laboratory, Cambridge
9.x: Newton was at Cambridge and the Royal Society, J.J. Thomson at the Cavendish Lab, Fermi at Chicago and Columbia, and Raman at IACS and IISc, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
9.tq: Recall each scientist's institution.
n: Isaac Newton was associated with Cambridge University. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 21-23]
Isaac Newton was associated with the Royal Society. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 21-23]
J.J. Thomson was associated with the Cavendish Laboratory, Cambridge. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 21-23]
Enrico Fermi was associated with the University of Chicago. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 21-23]
Enrico Fermi was associated with Columbia. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 21-23]
C.V. Raman was associated with the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 21-23]
C.V. Raman was associated with IISc. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 21-23]
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Newton** → **Cambridge University** and the **Royal Society**; **J.J. Thomson** → **Cavendish Laboratory, Cambridge**.
**Fermi** → **University of Chicago** and **Columbia**; **C.V. Raman** → **IACS** and **IISc**.
xa: **Rutherford** → **Cavendish Laboratory** and **Manchester**.
**Einstein** → **Princeton Institute for Advanced Study**.
**Bohr** → **University of Copenhagen**.

9.s: Crescograph was invented by whom?
9.x: J.C. Bose invented the crescograph to measure tiny plant growth and responses. Köhler and Milstein made hybridomas and Funk named vitamins.
9.tq: Recall Bose's inventions.
n: The crescograph was invented by Jagadish Chandra Bose. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 20-21]
Hybridoma technology was invented by César Milstein. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 20-21]
Hybridoma technology was invented by Georges J. F. Köhler. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 20-21]
xs: The **Crescograph** was invented by **Jagadish Chandra Bose**, so option **(4)** is correct.
**César Milstein** and **Georges Köhler** developed **hybridoma technology**.
**Casimir Funk** gave the **concept of vitamins**.
xa: The Crescograph **measures plant growth**; Bose established that **plants have life**.
Bose founded the **Bose Institute, Kolkata** (**1917**).
⚠ **J.C. Bose** = plants + radio; **S.N. Bose** = bosons.

9.s:
Consider the following statements about C.V. Raman:
1. He founded the Indian Academy of Sciences in 1934.
2. He founded the Raman Research Institute in Bengaluru in 1948.
3. He was the first Indian director of the Indian Institute of Science.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: All three statements are correct. Raman founded the Indian Academy of Sciences in 1934 and the Raman Research Institute in 1948, and became the first Indian director of the Indian Institute of Science.
9.tq: Check a chronological institutional career through multiple statements.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is the answer.
Statement 1: Raman founded the **Indian Academy of Sciences** in **1934**.
Statement 2: he founded the **Raman Research Institute**, Bengaluru, in **1948**.
Statement 3: he was the **first Indian director of IISc**.
xa: Raman studied the harmonic nature of the **tabla and mridangam**.
Raman: **Nobel 1930**, **Bharat Ratna 1954**, knighted **1929**.

9.s:
Arrange the following events associated with Indian scientific institutions in chronological order:
A. Establishment of the Raman Research Institute
B. Establishment of the Indian Academy of Sciences
C. Establishment of the Bose Institute
D. Establishment of the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research
9.x: The Bose Institute was founded in 1917, the Indian Academy of Sciences in 1934, TIFR in 1945 and the Raman Research Institute in 1948.
9.tq: Arrange institutions by their foundation years, using the earliest and latest events first.
xs: The correct order is **C, B, D, A** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Bose Institute** (**1917**) → **Indian Academy of Sciences** (**1934**) → **TIFR** (**1945**) → **Raman Research Institute** (**1948**).
xa: **NASI** was founded by Meghnad Saha in **1930**.
**Atomic Energy Establishment, Trombay** (**1954**) was renamed **BARC** after Bhabha's death (**1967**).

9.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Atomic Energy Commission — First chairman, Homi Bhabha, 1948
Bhabha Atomic Research Centre — Founded by Homi Bhabha in 1945
9.x: The Atomic Energy Establishment at Trombay was founded in 1954 and was renamed BARC after Homi Bhabha's death in 1966. It was not founded as BARC in 1945.
9.tq: Find the institution-year statement that reverses the original name and later renaming.
xs: **BARC — founded by Homi Bhabha in 1945** is NOT correctly matched — so option **(4)** is correct.
Bhabha founded the **Atomic Energy Establishment, Trombay** in **1954**; it was **renamed BARC** after his death (**1967**).
The other pairs are correct: **AEC** first chairman Bhabha, **1948**; **TIFR** **1945**; **AEET** **1954**.
xa: ⚠ **1945** is the year of **TIFR**, not BARC.
Bhabha died in **1966** on **Mont Blanc**.

9.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the honours received by C. V. Raman?
o: Nobel Prize in 1930, Bharat Ratna in 1954 and knighthood in 1929
Nobel Prize in 1954, Bharat Ratna in 1929 and knighthood in 1930
Nobel Prize in 1929, Bharat Ratna in 1930 and knighthood in 1954
FRS in 1930, Padma Bhushan in 1954 and knighthood in 1929
9.x: C. V. Raman received the Nobel Prize in 1930, was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1954 and was knighted in 1929.
9.tq: Use the exact year-and-honour combination to avoid swapped-date traps.
xs: Raman got the **Nobel Prize in 1930**, **Bharat Ratna in 1954** and **knighthood in 1929** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Options 2 and 3 shuffle these years; **Padma Bhushan 1954** was **Bhabha**'s.
xa: Raman's Nobel was India's first science Nobel — **first Asian and first non-White** science Nobel.
⚠ **1954** = Raman's Bharat Ratna + Bhabha's Padma Bhushan + S.N. Bose's Padma Vibhushan.

9.s:
With reference to Homi Bhabha and S. N. Bose, consider the following statements:
1. Homi Bhabha became an FRS in 1941.
2. Homi Bhabha received the Padma Bhushan in 1954.
3. S. N. Bose received the Padma Vibhushan in 1954.
4. S. N. Bose became an FRS in 1958.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: All four statements are correct. Bhabha received the FRS in 1941 and Padma Bhushan in 1954, while S. N. Bose received Padma Vibhushan in 1954 and FRS in 1958.
9.tq: Treat a multi-person honour list as separate statements and verify every year.
xs: All four statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4** is the answer.
**Homi Bhabha**: **FRS 1941**, **Padma Bhushan 1954**.
**S.N. Bose**: **Padma Vibhushan 1954**, **FRS 1958**.
xa: Bhabha also won the **Adams Prize (1942)**.
S.N. Bose was made a **National Professor**.
⚠ **1954** also = Raman's **Bharat Ratna**.

9.s:
Consider the following statements about early Indian women scientists:
1. Anandibai Joshi was the first Indian woman to earn a degree in Western medicine (MD, 1886).
2. Kamala Sohonie was the first woman admitted to the Indian Institute of Science.
3. Kamala Sohonie was the first woman to obtain a D.Sc. from an Indian university.

Indian-origin Economics laureates: **Amartya Sen** (**1998**), **Abhijit Banerjee** (**2019**).

11.s: Which statement about Nobel laureate status is correct?
o: It can be revoked by the Nobel Committee after the award ceremony.
It automatically passes to the laureate's institution after death.

11.x: Nobel laureate status cannot be transferred, shared or revoked. Only the physical medal can change hands.
11.tq: Apply the distinction between an honour and the physical award object.
xs: Laureate status **cannot be transferred, shared or revoked; only the physical medal can change hands** — so option **(4)** is correct.
This was stated by the **Norwegian Nobel Institute** (Jan **2026**).
xa: The Nobel was first awarded in **1901**.
The Peace Prize is given by the **Norwegian Nobel Committee, Oslo**.

11.s:

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
11.x: Statement 1 is correct: Nobel invented dynamite in 1867 using nitroglycerine. Statement 2 is wrong: RDX was discovered by George Friedrich Henning of Germany (patented 1898), not Nobel. Statement 3 is correct. Hence '1 and 3 only'; options C and D include statement 2, option A leaves out statement 3.
11.tq: Nobel = dynamite; Henning = RDX.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
1: **Dynamite** was invented by **Alfred Nobel** in **1867** using **nitroglycerine** — correct.
2 is wrong: **RDX** was discovered by **George Friedrich Henning** (**Germany**), patented **1898** — not Nobel.
3: RDX was **used extensively** in **World War II** — correct.
xa: **HMX, CL-20 and LLM-105** are **high-performance explosives** of modern military research.
Nobel Prizes come from the **Will of Alfred Nobel**; first awarded **1901**.

11.s:
Consider the following statements about S. Chandrasekhar:
1. NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory (1999) is named after him.
2. The Chandrasekhar limit is the maximum mass of a stable white dwarf, about 1.4 solar masses.
3. A white dwarf that exceeds this limit settles into a stable main-sequence star.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
11.x: Statement 2 is correct: the limit is about 1.4 solar masses. Statement 3 is wrong: beyond the limit the star collapses into a neutron star or black hole. Statement 1 is correct. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
11.tq: Beyond 1.4 solar masses = collapse to neutron star / black hole.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
1: NASA's **Chandra X-ray Observatory** (**1999**) is named after him — correct.
2: the **Chandrasekhar limit** is the maximum mass of a stable **white dwarf**, about **1.4 solar masses** — correct.
3 is wrong: beyond the limit the star **collapses** into a **neutron star** or **black hole**.
xa: Chandrasekhar won the **1983 Physics** Nobel for **structure and evolution of stars**.
He was the **nephew of C.V. Raman** and a US citizen from **1953**.
His books include **The Mathematical Theory of Black Holes**.

11.s: Which one of the following statements about S. Chandrasekhar is correct?
o: He was the uncle of C.V. Raman and remained an Indian citizen throughout his career.
He was the nephew of C.V. Raman, became a US citizen in 1953 and guided more than 50 PhD students.
He discovered the genetic code and founded the Centre for Ecological Sciences.
He received the Turing Award as the first Asian recipient.
11.x: S. Chandrasekhar was C.V. Raman's nephew, became a US citizen in 1953 and guided more than 50 PhD students.
11.tq: Combine biographical facts while rejecting swapped achievements.
xs: Chandrasekhar was the **nephew of C.V. Raman**, a **US citizen from 1953**, and guided **50+ PhDs** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The genetic code is **Khorana**'s; the **CES** at IISc was founded by **Madhav Gadgil**; the first Asian Turing Award went to **Raj Reddy**.

He wrote **ten books**.

11.s:
Consider the following statements about the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize:
1. It is awarded by the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR).
2. It was first awarded in 1968.
3. It is named after the founder-director of CSIR.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
11.x: Statement 1 is correct: CSIR awards the prize. Statement 2 is wrong: CSIR has awarded it since 1958, not 1968. Statement 3 is correct: S.S. Bhatnagar was the founder-director of CSIR. So '1 and 3 only' is right; '1 only' misses statement 3, and options with statement 2 include the wrong year.
11.tq: CSIR + 1958 + founder-director; 1968 is the Khorana Nobel / Economics-prize year trap.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — so option **(3) 1 and 3 only** is the answer.
Statement 1 is **correct**: the prize is awarded by **CSIR**.
Statement 2 is **wrong**: it has been awarded since **1958**, not 1968.
Statement 3 is **correct**: **S.S. Bhatnagar** was the **founder-director of CSIR**.
xa: Age limit: **45 years**; **7 disciplines** (UPSC 2009).
It is now absorbed in the RVP as **Vigyan Yuva-Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar (VY-SSB)**.

11.s:
Consider the following statements about Nobel Prizes in Physics:
1. John Bardeen received the Nobel Prize in Physics twice, in 1956 and 1972.
2. Schrodinger and Dirac received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1933.
3. Niels Bohr received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1932.
4. Marie Curie received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903 and in Chemistry in 1911.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
11.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct as per the notes. Statement 3 is wrong: Bohr won in 1922; 1932 is Heisenberg's year. Options A, C and D include the false statement 3.
11.tq: Bohr 1922, Heisenberg 1932 - one decade apart.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 4** are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
1: **Bardeen** won physics **twice** — **1956** and **1972** — correct.
2: **Schrödinger** and **Dirac** — **Physics 1933** — correct.
3 is wrong: **Bohr** won in **1922**; **1932** was **Heisenberg**.
4: **Marie Curie** — **Physics 1903**, **Chemistry 1911** — correct.
xa: **Chadwick** won **Physics 1935**; **Fermi** **1938**.
**C.V. Raman** won **Physics 1930** — the **first Asian**.
**Röntgen** won the **first** physics Nobel in **1901** for **X-rays**.

11.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the disciplines covered by the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize?
11.x: The seven disciplines include biology, chemistry, earth/atmosphere/ocean/planetary sciences, engineering, mathematics, medicine and physics. Political science is not included.
11.tq: Find the outsider in a named disciplinary list.
xs: **Political science** is not a Bhatnagar Prize discipline — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **7 disciplines**: biology, chemistry, earth/atmosphere/ocean/planetary sciences, **engineering**, **mathematics**, **medicine**, physics.
xa: ⚠ Bhatnagar Prize = **7 disciplines**; RVP = **13 domains**; both age **45**.

11.s:

xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.

2: established in **2024**, RVP is India's **highest S&T recognition** — correct.
3: **Vigyan Team** is for a team of **3 or more** researchers — correct.
4 is wrong: RVP covers **13 domains**; the Bhatnagar Prize had **7 disciplines**.
xa: **Vigyan Ratna** = **lifetime achievement**; first awardee (2024) **G. Padmanabhan**.
**Vigyan Shri** = **distinguished contributions**.

xs: **G. Padmanabhan** was the first **Vigyan Ratna** (**2024**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Annapurni Subramaniam** won **Vigyan Shri**; **Narender K. Sehgal** and **Jayant V. Narlikar** won the **Kalinga Prize**.

11.s: Madhav Gadgil is associated with which of the following?
o: The genetic code and protein synthesis
The first Turing Award in computing
People's Biodiversity Register and the Gadgil Commission on the Western Ghats
The discovery of the Raman Effect and the Chandra Observatory

12.s:
Arrange the following computer generations in chronological order of their core technologies:
A. Integrated circuits
B. Vacuum tubes
C. Microprocessors
D. Transistors
12.x: The correct sequence is vacuum tubes, transistors, integrated circuits and microprocessors, corresponding broadly to the first through fourth generations.
12.tq: Fix the first and last technologies, then place the intermediate generations.
xs: The correct order is **B, D, A, C** — so option **(1)** is correct.
1st gen (**1940s-56**) **vacuum tubes** → 2nd (**1956-63**) **transistors** → 3rd (**1964-71**) **integrated circuits** → 4th (**1971**-) **microprocessors** (VLSI).
xa: 5th generation = **artificial intelligence**, **ULSI**, parallel processing.
First-generation examples: **ENIAC**, **UNIVAC**.

12.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the fifth generation of computers?
o: Artificial intelligence, ULSI and parallel processing
12.x: The fifth generation is associated with artificial intelligence, ultra-large-scale integration and parallel processing.
12.tq: Use the distinctive technology cluster to identify the generation.
xs: The 5th generation is linked to **artificial intelligence, ULSI and parallel processing** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Vacuum tubes** = 1st generation; **transistors** = 2nd generation.
xa: 4th generation = **microprocessors** (VLSI), from **1971**.
3rd generation (**1964-71**) = **integrated circuits**.

12.s: Which one of the following correctly describes a supercomputer?
o: A computer with the highest processing power, commonly expressed in FLOPS
A computer with the lowest processing speed, measured only in bytes
A computer that represents information only through qubits
A computer used exclusively as a word processor
12.x: Supercomputers provide the highest processing power and their speed is commonly expressed in FLOPS.
12.tq: Use the defining performance feature to distinguish supercomputers from other types.
xs: A supercomputer has the **highest processing power**, expressed in **FLOPS** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Qubits** describe **quantum computers**, not supercomputers.
xa: The **Linpack (HPL) benchmark** measures FLOPS → basis of world supercomputer rankings.
World's fastest (**ISC 2026**): China's **LineShine**, replacing US **El Capitan**.

12.s:
Consider the following pairs:
a. Charles Babbage — Analytical Engine
b. Ada Lovelace — First programmer
c. Douglas Engelbart — Computer mouse
d. Larry Tesler — Cut, copy and paste

xs: All four pairs are correct — so option **(4) a, b, c and d** is the answer.
**Charles Babbage** — **Analytical Engine** (father of the computer); **Ada Lovelace** — **first programmer**.
**Douglas Engelbart** — computer **mouse**; **Larry Tesler** — **cut/copy/paste**.
xa: **Tim Berners-Lee** — **WWW** (**1989**); **von Neumann** — stored-program architecture.

Consider the following pairs:
1. Richard Stallman — GPL licence
2. John von Neumann — Stored-program architecture
3. Tim Berners-Lee — World Wide Web (1989)
4. Linus Torvalds — GNU project (1983)
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?

12.s: In the context of computing history, “technology preservation” refers to a
o: method of storing data in RAM
12.x: “Technology preservation” is associated with a computer museum, where earlier technologies are retained and displayed.
12.tq: Recognise the exact term-to-meaning association instead of interpreting it literally.
xs: "Technology preservation" = a **computer museum** — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC 2019).
The term was asked in **APPSC 2019** as a direct match: technology preservation → **computer museum**.
xa: Firsts often asked: **ENIAC (1946)** — first general-purpose electronic computer (Eckert and Mauchly).
**TIFRAC** — India's first indigenous computer.

12.s: Which one of the following was India's first indigenous computer?
12.x: TIFRAC was the first indigenous computer built in India. ENIAC (1946, Eckert and Mauchly) was the world's first general-purpose electronic computer, and UNIVAC was another first-generation American computer. PARAM 8000 (1991) was India's first supercomputer, not its first computer.
12.tq: First Indian computer = TIFRAC; first Indian supercomputer = PARAM 8000.
xs: **TIFRAC** was India's **first indigenous computer** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**ENIAC (1946)** was the world's first general-purpose electronic computer; **UNIVAC** is another first-generation machine.
xa: **FORTRAN** was the first HLL (**1957**).
**Intel 4004 (1971)** — first commercial microprocessor.

12.s:
Consider the following statements about types of computers:
1. Analog computers work on continuous quantities, as in a speedometer or thermometer.
2. Hybrid computers, such as hospital ICU monitors, combine analog and digital features.
3. Digital computers process continuous quantities rather than discrete data.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
12.x: Statement 1 is correct: analog = continuous quantities (speedometer, thermometer). Statement 2 is correct: hybrid computers such as ICU monitors and ECG combine both. Statement 3 is wrong: digital computers process discrete (binary) data, as in PCs. Hence '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses statement 2, and the other options include the false statement 3.
12.tq: Analog = continuous, digital = discrete/binary, hybrid = both (ICU, ECG).
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — so option **(2) 1 and 2 only** is the answer.
Statement 1 is **correct**: **analog** = continuous quantities — **speedometer, thermometer**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: **hybrid** = both — **hospital ICU monitors, ECG**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: **digital** computers handle **discrete (binary)** data, as in PCs.
xa: **Mini / mainframe** = multi-user organisational machines.
**Supercomputer** = highest processing power, speed in **FLOPS**.

12.s: Which one of the following was the first commercial microprocessor?
12.x: The Intel 4004, introduced in 1971, was the first commercial microprocessor.
12.tq: Link the historical milestone with the specific processor model.
xs: The **Intel 4004** (**1971**) was the **first commercial microprocessor** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Microprocessors define the **4th generation** (VLSI).
xa: **ENIAC (1946)** — first general-purpose electronic computer.

12.s: Information and Communication Technology (ICT) is best understood as an umbrella term covering devices and applications used to
o: replace all forms of human communication
access, store, transmit and manipulate digital information

12.s:
Consider the following statements about CPU components:
1. Registers are the fastest storage inside the CPU.
2. The power supply unit fetches and decodes program instructions.
3. The Arithmetic and Logic Unit (ALU) performs arithmetic and logical operations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
12.x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the control unit fetches, decodes and directs; the PSU only supplies power. Statement 1 is correct. Hence '1 and 3 only'.
12.tq: CU = fetch-decode-direct; PSU = power only.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
1: **registers** are the **fastest storage inside the CPU** — correct.
2 is wrong: the **control unit (CU)** fetches, decodes and directs; the **PSU** only **supplies power**.
3: the **ALU** performs **arithmetic and logical operations** — correct.
xa: The **CPU** is the computer's **"brain"**.
The **motherboard** links components; **GPUs** handle **graphics/AI**.
Speed order: **registers > cache > RAM > SSD > HDD**.

12.s: Which one of the following devices can function as both an input and an output device?
12.x: A touch screen displays output and also receives input through touch.
12.tq: Apply the input-output classification to a dual-function device.
xs: A **touch screen** is both an input and an output device — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Keyboard** and **microphone** are input only; **plotter** is output only.
xa: Input devices also include **barcode reader**, **OCR**, **MICR** (cheques), **OMR** (answer sheets).
Output devices: monitor, printer, **plotter**, speaker, projector.

12.s:
Consider the following statements about printers:
1. A laser printer is an impact printer.
2. Dot-matrix and daisy-wheel printers are impact printers.
3. Printer quality is expressed in dpi and speed in ppm.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
12.x: Statement 1 is wrong: laser, inkjet and thermal printers are non-impact. Statements 2 and 3 are correct as per the notes. Hence '2 and 3 only'.
12.tq: Impact = dot-matrix, daisy-wheel, line; the rest are non-impact.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct, so option **(3)** is correct.
1 is wrong: **laser**, **inkjet** and **thermal** printers are **non-impact**.
2: **dot-matrix**, **daisy-wheel** (and **line**) printers are **impact** printers — correct.
3: print quality is in **dpi**; speed in **ppm/cps** — correct.
xa: A **plotter** is an output device.
A **touch screen** is both **input and output**.
**MICR** reads **cheques**; **OMR** reads **answer sheets**.

12.s: A nibble in computer terminology consists of
12.x: A nibble is a group of four bits.
12.tq: Recall the fixed-size relationship between binary storage units.
xs: A **nibble = 4 bits** — so option **(4)** is correct.
A **byte = 8 bits**; the **bit** is the smallest unit (APPSC 2025).
xa: Order: bit < nibble < byte < **KB (1,024 bytes)** < MB < GB < TB < PB < EB < ZB < YB.
**ASCII** is **7-bit** with **128** characters.

12.s:
Consider the following statements about RAM:
1. RAM is non-volatile memory that holds the BIOS.
2. DRAM is used as main memory.
3. SRAM is used as cache memory.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
12.x: Statement 1 is wrong: RAM is volatile temporary working memory; ROM is non-volatile and holds firmware/BIOS. Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Hence '2 and 3 only'.
12.tq: RAM volatile, ROM holds BIOS; SRAM = cache, DRAM = main.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
1 is wrong: **RAM** is **volatile** temporary working memory; **ROM** is **non-volatile** and holds **firmware/BIOS**.
2: **DRAM** is used as **main** memory — correct.
3: **SRAM** is used as **cache** — correct.
xa: **Cache** is small, very fast memory between **CPU and RAM**.
⚠ **EPROM** is erased by **UV**; **EEPROM** is erased **electrically**.
**Byte = 8 bits**; **nibble = 4 bits** (**APPSC 2025**).

12.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: EEPROM — erasable only by ultraviolet light
12.x: EPROM is erased using ultraviolet light. EEPROM is electrically erasable, while ROM is non-volatile.
12.tq: Use the exact technical distinction among closely related memory terms.
xs: **EPROM — erased by UV** is correctly matched — so option **(3)** is correct.
**EEPROM** is erased **electrically**; **ROM** is **non-volatile**, not volatile.
xa: ⚠ **EPROM** = UV; **EEPROM** = electrically.
**Flash drives** (pen drive, memory card) are **EEPROM-based** flash.

12.s:
Arrange the following in descending order of access speed:
A. RAM
B. Registers
C. Magnetic tape
D. Cache
12.x: The speed order is registers, cache, RAM and magnetic tape.
12.tq: Arrange items by performance hierarchy, beginning with the fastest.
xs: Descending speed: **Registers > Cache > RAM > Magnetic tape** — so option **(1) B, D, A, C** is correct.
Full order: **registers > cache > RAM > SSD > HDD > optical disc > magnetic tape**.
xa: **Registers** are inside the **CPU**.
**Magnetic tape** is **sequential access**, used for backup and archival.

12.s:
Consider the following statements about secondary storage:
1. Magnetic tape offers random access and is the fastest secondary storage.
2. A solid-state drive uses flash memory and has no moving parts.
3. Magnetic tape is used for backup and archival.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
12.x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: magnetic tape is sequential access and the slowest in the speed order. Statement 3 is correct. Hence '2 and 3 only'.
12.tq: Tape = sequential, slowest, archival.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
1 is wrong: **magnetic tape** is **sequential access** and the **slowest** in the speed order.
2: an **SSD** uses **flash memory**, has **no moving parts** and is faster — correct.
3: magnetic tape is used for **backup and archival** — correct.
xa: **HDD** uses magnetic **spinning disks**.
**DVD** holds **4.7 GB** single layer; **Blu-ray** **25 GB** (blue-violet laser).
Speed order: **registers > cache > RAM > SSD > HDD > optical disc > magnetic tape**.

12.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its file type?
12.x: MP4 stands for MPEG-4 Part 14 and is a video file format. MP3 is audio, PDF is a document format and MOV is a video format.
12.tq: Start from the sure file-type pair and eliminate the swapped categories.
xs: **MP4 — Video** is correctly matched — so option **(2)** is correct.
MP4 = **MPEG-4 Part 14**.
**MP3** is **audio**; **PDF** is a **document**; **MOV** is **video**, not image.
xa: **MP3** = MPEG-1 Audio Layer 3.
Other video formats: **MOV** (QuickTime, Apple), **AVI** (Audio Video Interleave, Microsoft).

12.s:
Consider the following statements about programming languages:
1. SQL is a fourth-generation language used for database queries.
2. FORTRAN, which appeared in 1957, was the first high-level language.
3. Assembly language (2GL) uses mnemonics and is converted into machine code by a compiler.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
12.x: Statement 3 is wrong: assembly language is converted by an assembler, not a compiler. Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
12.tq: Assembly -> assembler; HLL -> compiler/interpreter.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct, so option **(3)** is correct.
1: **SQL** is a **4GL** for **database queries** — correct.
2: **FORTRAN** (**1957**) was the **first high-level language** — correct.
3 is wrong: **assembly language** (2GL) uses **mnemonics** but is converted by an **assembler**, not a compiler.
xa: ⚠ **Compiler** translates the **whole program at once**; **interpreter** runs **line by line**.
**1GL** = machine language — binary **0s and 1s**.
**COBOL** is a business language.

12.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Operating system — system software
2. Disk cleanup — utility software
3. Word processor — application software
4. Device driver — application software
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
12.x: Operating systems, disk-cleanup tools and word processors are correctly classified. A device driver is system software, so pair 4 is false.
12.tq: Spot the wrongly classified software category.
xs: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct — so option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only** is the answer.
**Operating system** = system software; **disk cleanup** = utility; **word processor** = application.
Pair 4 is **wrong**: a **device driver** is **system software**.
xa: Utility software: **antivirus, disk cleanup, backup, compression**.
Language translators (**compiler, interpreter, assembler**) are also system software.

12.s:
Consider the following statements about types of operating systems:
1. In a batch operating system, jobs are grouped and run without user interaction.
2. In a time-sharing (multi-user) operating system such as UNIX, many users share CPU time.
3. Real-time operating systems have no fixed response deadlines, so they are unsuitable for missile guidance or air-traffic control.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
12.x: Statement 1 is correct: batch OS groups jobs and runs them without user interaction. Statement 2 is correct: time-sharing OS (e.g. UNIX) lets many users share CPU time. Statement 3 is wrong: real-time OS work to fixed response deadlines and are used precisely for missile guidance, air-traffic control and medical devices. Hence '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' and '1 and 3 only' drop statement 2 or add the false 3, and '1, 2 and 3' includes the false statement.
12.tq: Real-time = fixed deadlines (missiles, ATC, medical devices); time-sharing = UNIX.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — so option **(2) 1 and 2 only** is the answer.
Statement 1 is **correct**: **batch** OS groups jobs and runs them **without user interaction**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: **time-sharing** OS (e.g. **UNIX**) lets many users share CPU time.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: **real-time** OS have **fixed response deadlines** — used for missile guidance, air-traffic control, medical devices.
xa: Real-time OS are **hard** or **soft**.
**Distributed / network** OS link many machines.

12.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding mobile operating systems?
o: Android is Linux-based and associated with Google.
Android and iOS are command-line-only systems.
BharOS was developed by a private foreign corporation.
12.x: Android is Linux-based and associated with Google, while iOS is associated with Apple. BharOS was developed at IIT Madras.
12.tq: Use the developer-platform-location distinction to reject swapped associations.
xs: **Android** is **Linux-based** and from **Google** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**iOS** is **Apple**'s; **BharOS** was developed at **IIT Madras**.
Mobile OS have **GUI**s, not command-line only.
xa: CLI examples: **MS-DOS**, **UNIX shell**; GUI examples: **Windows**, **macOS**.
**Linux** kernel was written by **Linus Torvalds** (**1991**).

12.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: CLI — icons and windows controlled mainly by a mouse
12.x: MS-DOS is associated with a command-line interface. GUIs use icons, windows and mouse interaction, as in Windows and macOS.
12.tq: Distinguish CLI and GUI by their visible interaction method.
xs: **MS-DOS — command-line interface** is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
**GUI** uses **icons, windows, mouse** — as in **Windows** and **macOS**.
xa: The **UNIX shell** is another CLI.
The mouse was invented by **Douglas Engelbart**.

12.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes a compiler from an interpreter?
o: A compiler translates only comments, whereas an interpreter translates only variables.
An interpreter is used exclusively for assembly language.
A compiler translates the whole program at once, whereas an interpreter translates and runs it line by line.
Both always translate only one line at a time.
12.x: A compiler processes the complete program before execution, while an interpreter translates and executes line by line, making debugging easier.
12.tq: Compare paired translators by the unit and timing of translation.
xs: A **compiler** translates the **whole program at once**; an **interpreter** translates and runs **line by line** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Compiled code runs **faster**; interpreters make **debugging easier**.
xa: Assembly language is converted by an **assembler**.
All three are **language translators** (system software).

12.s:
Consider the following statements about logic gates:
1. NAND and NOR are universal gates.
2. An XOR gate gives output 1 when its inputs are the same.
3. AND, OR and NOT are the basic logic gates.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
12.x: Statement 1 is correct: NAND and NOR are the universal gates. Statement 2 is wrong: XOR gives 1 when the inputs differ, not when they are the same. Statement 3 is correct: AND, OR and NOT are the basic gates. Hence '1 and 3 only'; '1 only' misses statement 3, and the other two options include the false statement 2.
12.tq: XOR = 'exclusive' = 1 only when inputs differ; universal = NAND, NOR.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — so option **(3) 1 and 3 only** is the answer.
Statement 1 is **correct**: **NAND and NOR** are **universal gates**.
Statement 2 is **wrong**: **XOR** gives 1 when inputs **differ**.
Statement 3 is **correct**: **AND, OR, NOT** are the basic gates.
xa: Boolean algebra was given by **George Boole**.
**De Morgan**: (A+B)' = A'.B'.

12.s:
Consider the following Boolean identities:
1. A + A = A
2. A · A′ = 0
3. (A + B)′ = A′ · B′
Which of the statements given above are correct?
12.x: All three are valid Boolean identities; the third is De Morgan's law.
12.tq: Verify each algebraic identity independently before selecting the combined code.
xs: All three identities are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is the answer.
**(A+B)' = A'.B'** is **De Morgan**'s law.
xa: Boolean algebra: **George Boole**.
**NAND** and **NOR** are universal gates.

12.s:
Consider the following statements about computer performance terms:
1. Clock speed is measured in bits per second.
2. Bandwidth is the data-transfer rate, measured in bits per second.
3. Word length is the number of bits the CPU handles at once.
4. MIPS stands for million instructions per second.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
12.x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct as per the notes. Statement 1 is wrong: clock speed is measured in hertz (GHz); bits per second is the unit of bandwidth. Hence '2, 3 and 4 only'.
12.tq: Clock = GHz; bandwidth = bps.
xs: Statements **2, 3 and 4** are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
1 is wrong: **clock speed** is measured in **hertz (GHz)**; **bits per second** is the unit of **bandwidth**.
2: **bandwidth** = **data-transfer rate** in **bps** — correct; 3: **word length** = bits the CPU handles at once — correct.
4: **MIPS** = **million instructions per second** — correct.
xa: **FLOPS** = **floating-point operations per second** — supercomputer speed.
The **Linpack (HPL) benchmark** is the basis of world supercomputer rankings.
Word length examples: **32-bit**, **64-bit**.

12.s: Which benchmark measures floating-point performance while solving large dense linear systems and forms the basis of world supercomputer rankings?
12.x: The Linpack, or HPL, benchmark measures floating-point power in solving large dense linear systems and is used for world supercomputer rankings.
12.tq: Identify the benchmark from its distinctive workload and ranking application.
xs: The **Linpack (HPL) benchmark** measures floating-point power on **large dense linear systems** and underlies world supercomputer rankings — so option **(1)** is correct.
**ASCII** and **Unicode** are character codes, and **MIPS** counts instructions — none rank supercomputers.
xa: Results are in **FLOPS**.
**ISC 2026** list: China's **LineShine** replaced US **El Capitan** at the top.

12.s: According to the ISC 2026 ranking referred to here, the world’s fastest supercomputer is
o: El Capitan of the United States
12.x: China’s LineShine topped the ISC 2026 supercomputer list, replacing the United States’ El Capitan.
12.tq: Track the current ranking and the country-replacement relationship carefully.
xs: China's **LineShine** tops the **ISC 2026** list — so option **(1)** is correct.
It replaced the US's **El Capitan**, which held the top spot before.
**Param Shakti** is India's (**IIT Madras**), not Japan's; **PARAM 8000** is not on this list.
xa: Rankings use the **Linpack (HPL)** benchmark in **FLOPS**.
**Param Shakti**: **3.1 petaflops**, C-DAC **RUDRA** servers.

12.s:
Consider the following statements about Param Shakti:
1. It has a capacity of 3.1 petaflops and runs on C-DAC RUDRA servers with open-source AlmaLinux.
2. It was funded under the National Supercomputing Mission.
3. It was launched by ISRO at IISc Bengaluru.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
12.x: Statement 3 is wrong: Param Shakti was launched by MeitY at IIT Madras. Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
12.tq: Param Shakti = MeitY + IIT Madras + NSM.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct, so option **(3)** is correct.
1: **Param Shakti** has **3.1 petaflops**, runs on C-DAC **RUDRA** servers with open-source **AlmaLinux** — correct.
2: it was funded under the **National Supercomputing Mission** — correct.
3 is wrong: it was launched by **MeitY** at **IIT Madras**, not by ISRO at IISc.
xa: World's fastest (**ISC 2026**): China's **LineShine**, replacing US **El Capitan**.
**Q-Day:** when quantum computers can break **RSA-2048**.
Quantum computers use **qubits** — **superposition** and **entanglement**.

12.s: Q-Day refers to the point at which quantum computers may be capable of
o: breaking RSA-2048 public-key encryption using Shor’s algorithm
converting every file into PDF format
increasing the clock speed of classical processors
12.x: Q-Day denotes the anticipated point when quantum computers can break RSA-2048 public-key encryption through Shor’s algorithm, proposed in 1994.
12.tq: Link the specialised term to its specific security consequence and algorithm.
xs: **Q-Day** is when quantum computers can break **RSA-2048 public-key encryption** using **Shor's algorithm** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Shor's algorithm dates from **1994**.
xa: Quantum computers use **qubits** (superposition, entanglement).
Quantum applications include **cryptography** and **optimisation**.

12.s:
Consider the following statements regarding ASCII:
1. ASCII is a 7-bit character-encoding scheme.
2. ASCII represents 128 characters.
3. Unicode extends the character-representation capability of ASCII.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
12.x: ASCII is a 7-bit code representing 128 characters, while Unicode extends the range of character representation. All three statements are correct.
12.tq: Check each numerical and relationship statement before selecting the combined code.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is the answer.
**ASCII** is **7-bit** and represents **128** characters.
**Unicode** extends it.
xa: ASCII = **American Standard Code for Information Interchange**.
A **byte** = **8 bits**; a **nibble** = **4 bits**.

12.s:
ICT aims to facilitate communication among which of the following?
1. Human and human
2. Human and machine
3. Machine and machine
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
12.x: ICT aims at efficient human-human, human-machine and machine-to-machine communication. Therefore, all three forms are included.
12.tq: Read the communication relationships separately before selecting the combined option.
xs: ICT aims at **human-human, human-machine and machine-machine (M2M)** communication — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
All three channels are named in the notes: **M2M** stands for machine-to-machine.
xa: ICT covers **mobiles, networks, software, internet, satellites**.
⚠ Concerns include the **digital divide** and **privacy risks**.

12.s: A barcode is best described as
o: a printed image converted into editable text
