a two-dimensional matrix of square modules
machine-readable vertical bars of varying widths
a magnetic character sequence used on cheques
12.x: A conventional barcode consists of machine-readable vertical bars of varying widths.
12.tq: Distinguish barcode, QR code, OCR and MICR by physical form and function.
xs: A barcode is **machine-readable vertical bars of varying widths** — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC 2019).
A **2-D matrix** is a **QR code**; converting printed text is **OCR**; cheque characters are read by **MICR**.
xa: **OMR** reads answer sheets.
Mouse-to-computer communication is **simplex** (one-way) (APPSC 2019).

12.s: The communication from a computer mouse to the computer is an example of which transmission mode?
12.x: A mouse only sends signals to the computer, so the communication is one-way, or simplex (APPSC 2019). Half duplex is two-way but one direction at a time, as in a walkie-talkie. Full duplex is two-way at once, as in a telephone. Multiplexing combines several signals on one channel; it is not a direction mode.
12.tq: Mouse/keyboard = simplex (one-way).
xs: A mouse sends signals one way only — **simplex** — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC 2019).
The data flows only from mouse to computer, never back — that one-way flow defines **simplex**.
xa: The mouse was invented by **Douglas Engelbart**.
Other input devices: **keyboard, scanner, joystick, light pen, microphone, webcam**.

12.s: Which statement best describes open-source software?
o: It is limited to operating systems produced by one company.
Its source code is permanently hidden from users.
It can never be commercially distributed.
Its source code is free to view, modify and share, subject to its licence.
12.x: Open-source software makes source code available for viewing, modification and sharing under the applicable licence.
12.tq: Reject absolute claims and identify the precise definition.
xs: Open-source software has **source code free to view, modify, share** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Examples: **GNU, Linux, LibreOffice, Firefox**.
xa: **Richard Stallman** — **GNU** project (**1983**) and the **GPL licence**.
**Linus Torvalds** — **Linux** kernel (**1991**).

12.s: The pictorial representation of an algorithm is called a:
12.x: A flowchart is the pictorial form of an algorithm, which is a finite step-by-step procedure (APPSC 2019). Pseudocode is an English-like text outline, a compiler is a language translator, and source code is the written program.
12.tq: Algorithm in pictures = flowchart; in English-like text = pseudocode.
xs: The pictorial form of an algorithm is a **Flowchart** — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC 2019).
**Pseudocode** is an **English-like outline**; a **compiler** is a translator.
xa: An **algorithm** is a **finite step-by-step procedure**.
Flowchart symbols: **oval** = start/end, **diamond** = decision.

12.s: The hexadecimal number (FF)₁₆ is equal to
12.x: F represents 15, so FF equals 15 × 16 + 15 = 255.
12.tq: Convert hexadecimal by applying place value and digit value.
xs: **(FF)16 = 255** — so option **(3)** is correct.
xa: **Hexadecimal** is base **16** (digits **0-9**, **A-F**).

12.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
12.x: PNG stands for Portable Network Graphics, not Portable Network Graphics Interface. AVI, MOV and GIF are correctly matched.
12.tq: Find the altered word in an otherwise familiar acronym expansion.
xs: **PNG — Portable Network Graphics Interface** is NOT correct — so option **(4)** is the answer.
PNG = **Portable Network Graphics** — there is no "Interface".
**GIF** = Graphics Interchange Format; **AVI** = Audio Video Interleave; **MOV** = QuickTime Movie.
xa: **JPEG** = Joint Photographic Experts Group — image, **lossy**.
**PDF** = Portable Document Format (**Adobe**).

13.s: ARPANET, established in 1969, was developed under which organisation and is regarded as the forerunner of the Internet?
13.x: ARPANET was developed under the United States Department of Defense in 1969 and became the forerunner of the Internet.
13.tq: Link the historical network with its sponsoring organisation and legacy.
xs: **ARPANET** (**1969**) was developed under the **US Department of Defense** — so option **(1)** is correct.
ARPANET is regarded as the **forerunner of the internet**.
**W3C** was founded by **Tim Berners-Lee** in **1994** — it sets web standards, it did not build ARPANET.
xa: The **WWW** was invented by **Tim Berners-Lee** in **1989** at **CERN**.
India's firsts: **ERNET** (**1986**, academic network) → **VSNL** public internet (**15 August 1995**) → **Satyam Infoway (Sify)**, first private ISP (**1998**).
⚠ Do not confuse the **internet** (ARPANET lineage, 1969) with the **WWW** (Berners-Lee, 1989).

13.s: Which one of the following sequences correctly represents the Indian Internet milestones in chronological order?
o: Public internet by VSNL, ERNET, Satyam Infoway
Satyam Infoway, ERNET, public internet by VSNL
ERNET, public internet by VSNL, Satyam Infoway
ERNET, Satyam Infoway, public internet by VSNL
13.x: ERNET began in 1986, public internet was launched by VSNL on 15 August 1995, and Satyam Infoway became the first private ISP in 1998.
13.tq: Use the first, middle and last dates to establish the sequence.
xs: The correct order is **ERNET → VSNL public internet → Satyam Infoway** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**ERNET** began in **1986** as India's academic network.
**VSNL** launched public internet on **15 August 1995**.
**Satyam Infoway (Sify)** became the **first private ISP** in **1998**.
xa: Global milestones: **ARPANET** (**1969**) → **WWW** (**1989**, CERN) → **W3C** (**1994**).
**ICANN** (**1998**) coordinates the global domain name system and IP address allocation.
**NIXI** (**2003**) runs India's internet exchange points and the **.in registry**.

13.s:
Consider the following statements about network types:
1. A PAN links an individual's personal devices, typically through Bluetooth.
2. A MAN generally covers a city.
3. A firm linking its LANs in Mumbai, Bengaluru and New Delhi is using a MAN.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statement 1 is correct: PAN = personal area, e.g. Bluetooth. Statement 2 is correct: MAN covers a city. Statement 3 is wrong: linking LANs in different cities needs a WAN, which spans large areas (the internet is a global WAN) - this was the APPSC 2019 answer. Hence '1 and 2 only'; the other options miss statement 2 or include the false statement 3.
13.tq: Across cities = WAN; within one city = MAN.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: a **PAN** is a personal area network, e.g. **Bluetooth**.
Statement 2 is correct: a **MAN** covers **a city**.
Statement 3 is wrong: linking LANs in **Mumbai, Bengaluru and New Delhi** needs a **WAN** (APPSC **2019**).
xa: A **LAN** covers an office, home or campus.
A **WAN** spans large areas and links LANs — **the internet is a global WAN**.
A **VPN** is an encrypted **"tunnel"** over a public network.

13.s: A Virtual Private Network primarily provides:
o: A replacement for all network protocols
A wireless connection restricted to one room
A physical cable exclusively owned by a user
An encrypted tunnel over a public network
13.x: A VPN creates an encrypted tunnel through a public network, improving the privacy of communication.
13.tq: Identify the function rather than the physical form of the network.
xs: A **VPN** provides an **encrypted tunnel over a public network** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It does not replace protocols, is not a one-room wireless link and is not a privately owned cable.
xa: Network types by scope: **PAN** (personal, Bluetooth) → **LAN** (office/home/campus) → **MAN** (a city) → **WAN** (large areas).
**The internet is a global WAN**.
**HTTPS** also encrypts browser-server traffic, via **TLS**.

13.s:
Consider the following statements about network topologies:
1. In a star topology, failure of one node stops the whole network.
2. In a bus topology, all nodes share one backbone cable.
3. In a mesh topology, every node is linked to every other node, making it the most resilient.
4. In a ring topology, each node is linked to two neighbours.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
13.x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct as per the notes. Statement 1 is wrong: in a star, a failed node is isolated; only a hub failure stops the whole network. Hence '2, 3 and 4 only'.
13.tq: Star: node failure isolated, hub failure fatal.
xs: Statements **2, 3 and 4** are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
1 is wrong: in a **star**, one failed node is **isolated**; only a **hub failure** stops all.
2: in a **bus**, all nodes share one **backbone cable** — correct.
3: a **mesh** links every node to every other — **most resilient**, costliest — correct.
4: in a **ring**, each node links to **two neighbours** — correct.
xa: A **tree** is a hierarchy of star networks; a branch fails if its parent fails.
In a **bus**, a backbone break stops the whole network.
A firm linking LANs in Mumbai, Bengaluru and New Delhi uses a **WAN** (**APPSC 2019**).

13.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Device)
a. Hub
b. Switch
c. Router
d. Modem

List-II (Primary role)
i. Routes packets using IP
 ii. Converts digital and analogue signals
 iii. Broadcasts data to all ports
 iv. Forwards frames using MAC addresses

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
13.x: A hub broadcasts to all ports, a switch forwards frames by MAC address, a router routes using IP, and a modem converts between digital and analogue signals.
13.tq: Start from the sure device-function pairs and complete the code.
xs: The correct match is **a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Hub** broadcasts to all ports (**Physical**, layer 1).
**Switch** forwards frames by **MAC address** (**Data link**, layer **2**).
**Router** routes packets by **IP** (**Network**, layer **3**); **modem** converts **digital ↔ analog**.
xa: A **repeater** regenerates a weak signal (Physical layer); a **bridge** works like a switch (layer 2).
A **gateway** joins networks that use **different protocols** (all/upper layers).
Modem = **Modulator-demodulator**.

13.s: Which of the following represents the correct top-to-bottom order of the OSI model?
o: Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link, Physical
Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application
Application, Session, Presentation, Network, Transport, Data Link, Physical
Presentation, Application, Session, Transport, Data Link, Network, Physical
13.x: From the top layer downward, the OSI model is Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link and Physical.
13.tq: Use the first and last layers, then verify the middle sequence.
xs: Top to bottom: **Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link, Physical** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Option (2) is the bottom-to-top order; options (3) and (4) swap layers.
xa: Layer **7 Application**: **HTTP, FTP, SMTP, DNS**.
Layer **4 Transport**: **TCP, UDP**; layer **3 Network**: **IP**, router.
Layer **2 Data Link**: **MAC addresses**, switch, bridge, NIC; layer **1 Physical**: cables, hub, repeater.

13.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
13.x: A modem is associated with the Physical layer because it modulates and demodulates signals; it is not a Transport-layer device.
13.tq: Find the device placed at the wrong OSI layer.
xs: **Modem — Transport layer** is wrong: a modem is a **Physical**-layer device — so option **(3)** is correct.
A modem is a **modulator-demodulator** converting **digital ↔ analog** signals.
**Switch** = Data Link (**2**), **router** = Network (**3**), **hub** = Physical (**1**) are all correct.
xa: The **Transport** layer (**4**) carries **TCP** and **UDP**.
A **gateway** joins networks with different protocols (all/upper layers).
A **repeater** regenerates a weak signal at the Physical layer.

13.s:
Match the following OSI layers with their associated functions or protocols:
List-I (Layer)
a. Presentation
b. Session
c. Transport
d. Data Link

List-II (Function or protocol)
i. TCP and UDP
ii. Encryption, compression and formats
 iii. Opens and closes sessions
 iv. MAC addressing and frame forwarding

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
13.x: The Presentation layer handles encryption, compression and formats; the Session layer opens and closes sessions; the Transport layer uses TCP and UDP; and the Data Link layer handles MAC-based frame operations.
13.tq: Start with the distinctive TCP/UDP and MAC pairs.
xs: The correct match is **a–ii, b–iii, c–i, d–iv** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Presentation**: encryption, compression, formats (e.g. **JPEG**).
**Session**: opens and closes sessions; **Transport**: **TCP and UDP**.
**Data Link**: framing, **MAC addresses**, error detection; switch, bridge, NIC.
xa: **Application** layer (**7**): **HTTP, FTP, SMTP, DNS**.
**Network** layer (**3**): **IP**; router.
**Physical** layer (**1**): cables, hub, repeater.

13.s:
Consider the following statements about internet protocols:
1. IP addresses and routes packets.
2. DNS turns human-readable domain names into numerical IP addresses.
3. DHCP assigns MAC addresses to network cards.
4. TCP ensures reliable delivery of data.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
13.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct as per the notes. Statement 3 is wrong: DHCP assigns IP addresses automatically; a MAC address is burnt into the network card. Hence '1, 2 and 4 only'.
13.tq: DHCP = automatic IP addresses.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 4** are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
1: **IP** addresses and routes packets — correct; 4: **TCP** ensures **reliable delivery** — correct.
2: **DNS** turns human-readable names into numerical **IP addresses** — correct.
3 is wrong: **DHCP** assigns **IP addresses** automatically; a **MAC address** is burnt into the network card.
xa: ⚠ **SMTP** sends mail; **POP3** downloads and deletes; **IMAP** keeps mail on the server.
**MAC address** = **48 bits**; **IPv4** = **32 bits**; **IPv6** = **128 bits**.
Three elements of a protocol: **syntax**, **semantics**, **timing**.

13.s:
With reference to Web 3.0, consider the following statements:
1. It represents the third generation of the web.
2. It changes how the web is used, how sites are managed and how services are delivered.
3. OCEN is linked with Web 3.0 and aims to democratise lending.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
13.x: Web 3.0 is the third generation of the web and involves changes in usage, site management and service delivery. OCEN seeks to democratise lending and improve credit terms for small borrowers.
13.tq: Combine the definition, scope and associated initiative without confusing Web 3.0 with a single application.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3** is correct.
**Web 3.0** is the **third generation** of the web.
It changes **how the web is used**, how sites are managed and how services are delivered.
**OCEN** (**Open Credit Enablement Network**) is a linked standard that aims to **democratise lending**.
xa: OCEN aims to give **small borrowers** the best credit terms.
**W3C** develops and maintains web standards.
Core front-end technologies: **HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript**.

13.s:
Consider the following statements about NIXI:
1. It was established in 2003.
2. It is a not-for-profit organisation under MeitY.
3. It runs the .in registry and IRINN.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
13.x: NIXI was established in 2003, functions as a not-for-profit organisation under MeitY, and runs Internet exchange points, the .in registry and IRINN.
13.tq: Check each institutional detail before choosing the combined code.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3** is correct.
**NIXI** (National Internet Exchange of India) was set up in **2003**.
It is a **not-for-profit** under **MeitY**.
It runs **internet exchange points**, the **.in registry** and **IRINN** (IP addresses).
xa: **BhashaNet** (**2022**) is a MeitY-NIXI initiative for **Universal Acceptance**.
**ICANN** (**1998**) coordinates the global domain name system.
**IDNs** are domain names in local scripts, e.g. **.Bharat** in Devanagari.

13.s: An organisation notices that a particular website is inaccessible to users of one Internet service provider, while users of another provider can access it. Which explanation is consistent with this situation?
o: The provider may be using DNS poisoning, HTTP interception or SNI filtering
The OSI model has ceased to operate for that website
All websites have been permanently removed from the Internet
A PAN has automatically become a WAN
13.x: ISPs may block sites through DNS poisoning, HTTP interception or SNI filtering on HTTPS. Consequently, blocklists and access results can differ between ISPs.
13.tq: Apply the technical mechanism to the observed provider-specific outcome.
xs: The ISP may be using **DNS poisoning, HTTP interception or SNI filtering** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Blocklists differ across ISPs**, so a site can be blocked on one ISP and open on another (**7 Apr 2026**).
xa: **SNI filtering** is used to block **HTTPS** sites.
Government can order ISPs to block content under **Sections 69A and 79** of the **IT Act, 2000**.
**DNS** turns domain names into IP addresses — poisoning it misdirects users.

13.s: Which set of issues was discussed by Chief Minister Naidu and Sunil Mittal in relation to Andhra Pradesh?
o: Only the replacement of optical fibre by copper cable
Coal mining, irrigation dams and inland waterways
Last-mile connectivity, data centres and an undersea cable landing station
Only satellite launching and missile testing
13.x: The discussion concerned last-mile connectivity, data centres and an undersea cable landing station for Andhra Pradesh.
13.tq: Identify the complete issue cluster rather than a partial distractor.
xs: **CM Naidu** and **Sunil Mittal** discussed **last-mile connectivity, data centres and an undersea cable landing station** for AP — so option **(3)** is correct.
The meeting was on **29 Jun 2026**.
xa: **BharatNet** fibre reaches **2.18 lakh gram panchayats** (ES 2025-26).
Connections rose from **25.15 crore (2014)** to **96.96 crore (2024)**.
**Satellite internet** needs no terrestrial wire (space, ground, VSAT segments).

13.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: POP3 — downloading mail to one device, usually deleting it from the server
IMAP — permanently deleting mail from the server after downloading it to one device
13.x: IMAP keeps mail on the server and synchronises it across devices. POP3 generally downloads mail to one device and usually deletes it from the server.
13.tq: Distinguish the confusable mail protocols by their treatment of messages on the server.
xs: **IMAP — deleting mail after download** is wrong: IMAP **keeps mail on the server**, synced across devices — so option **(4)** is correct.
**POP3** downloads mail to one device and usually deletes it from the server.
**FTP** = file transfer; **SMTP** = **sends** e-mail — both correct.
xa: ⚠ **SMTP** sends; **POP3** downloads and deletes; **IMAP** keeps on server.
**DHCP** assigns IP addresses automatically.
**HTTP** passes messages between browsers and web servers.

13.s:
Assertion (A): HTTPS provides greater security for browser-server communication than HTTP.
Reason (R): HTTPS encrypts the traffic between the browser and the server through TLS.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
13.x: Both statements are true, and TLS-based encryption directly explains why HTTPS provides greater security than HTTP.
13.tq: Check whether the reason directly explains the security difference between HTTP and HTTPS.
xs: **Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**HTTPS** encrypts browser-server traffic via **TLS**, which is exactly why it is more secure than **HTTP**.
xa: **HTTP** sets how messages pass between browsers and web servers.
ISPs may block HTTPS sites by **SNI filtering**.
**VPN** = an encrypted tunnel over a public network.

13.s: Which one of the following represents the correct order of the principal parts of a URL?
o: Protocol, domain name, path to the file
Protocol, path to the file, domain name
13.x: A URL contains the protocol, such as https://, followed by the domain name and the path to the file.
13.tq: Test the internal order of URL components instead of merely recalling its expansion.
xs: A URL runs **protocol, domain name, path to the file** — so option **(2)** is correct.
e.g. protocol **https://** + domain **www.example.in** + path.
xa: **URL** = **Uniform Resource Locator**.
**DNS** turns the domain name into a numerical **IP address**.
**NIXI** runs India's **.in registry**.

13.s: ICANN, established in 1998 as a United States non-profit organisation, is primarily associated with:
o: Coordinating the global domain name system and IP address allocation
13.x: ICANN coordinates the global Domain Name System and IP address allocation. It was established in 1998 as a US non-profit organisation.
13.tq: Use the organisation-function and year combination.
xs: **ICANN** (**1998**) **coordinates the global domain name system and IP address allocation** — so option **(4)** is correct.
India's **.in registry** is run by **NIXI**, not ICANN.
xa: ICANN is a **US non-profit**.
**NIXI** (**2003**), under **MeitY**, runs internet exchange points, the .in registry and **IRINN**.
**BhashaNet** (**2022**, MeitY-NIXI) promotes **Universal Acceptance** for Indian languages.

13.s:
Consider the following statements about network addresses:
1. An IPv4 address is 32 bits long and written in dotted decimal, e.g. 192.168.1.1.
2. An IPv6 address is 128 bits long and written as eight groups of hexadecimal separated by colons.
3. A MAC address is a 64-bit logical address assigned by DNS.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statement 1 is correct: IPv4 = 32 bits, dotted decimal. Statement 2 is correct: IPv6 = 128 bits, eight hexadecimal groups separated by colons. Statement 3 is wrong: a MAC address is a 48-bit (6-byte, 12 hex digits) physical address burnt into the network card and used at the data link layer; DNS only turns names into IP addresses. Hence '1 and 2 only'; the other options either miss statement 2 or include the false statement 3.
13.tq: 32 / 128 / 48: IPv4 / IPv6 / MAC; MAC is physical, burnt into the card.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **IPv4** = **32 bits**, dotted decimal (e.g. 192.168.1.1).
Statement 2 is correct: **IPv6** = **128 bits**, 8 groups of hexadecimal separated by colons.
Statement 3 is wrong: a **MAC** address is **48 bits**, a **physical** address burnt into the network card.
xa: IPv4 offers **~4.3 billion** addresses.
A MAC address = **6 bytes**, **12 hex digits**; used at the **data link** layer.
**DNS** only turns names into IP addresses.

13.s:
Which of the following pairs correctly represents IPv4 address classes by their first-octet ranges?
1. Class A — 1 to 126
2. Class B — 128 to 191
3. Class C — 192 to 223
4. Class D — 240 to 255
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
13.x: Classes A, B and C have ranges 1–126, 128–191 and 192–223 respectively. Class D is 224–239 for multicast; 240–255 is Class E for experimental use.
13.tq: Check each numerical range against the class boundary, especially the swapped D and E ranges.
xs: Pairs **1, 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Pair 4 is wrong: **Class D** = **224-239** (multicast); **240-255** is **Class E** (experimental).
xa: **127.x.x.x** is the **loopback** range.
Classes are decided by the **first octet**.
IPv4 is **32 bits**; IPv6 is **128 bits**.

13.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with its transmission mode?
1. Radio or television broadcast — Simplex
2. Walkie-talkie — Half duplex
3. Telephone conversation — Full duplex
Select the correct answer.
13.x: Simplex permits one-way transmission, half duplex permits two-way transmission one at a time, and full duplex permits simultaneous two-way transmission.
13.tq: Compare the direction and simultaneity of communication.
xs: All three pairs are correct — so option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3** is correct.
**Simplex** = one way (**radio/TV broadcast**, keyboard).
**Half duplex** = both ways, one at a time (**walkie-talkie**).
**Full duplex** = both at once (**telephone**).
xa: A **keyboard** is another simplex example.
Connection media: **DSL** (telephone copper), **cable** (coaxial TV cable), **fibre** (light pulses).

13.s:
Consider the following statements about internet connections:
1. Satellite internet has space, ground and user (VSAT) segments but still needs a terrestrial wire to reach the user.
2. Cable internet carries data as light pulses in optical fibre.
3. DSL uses telephone copper lines.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: cable internet uses coaxial TV cable; light pulses in optical fibre describe fibre internet. Statement 1 is wrong: satellite internet needs no terrestrial wire. Hence '3 only'.
13.tq: DSL = copper, cable = coaxial, fibre = light, satellite = no wire.
xs: Only statement **3** is correct, so option **(1)** is correct.
1 is wrong: **satellite internet** has space, ground and user (**VSAT**) segments and **needs no terrestrial wire**.
2 is wrong: **cable** internet uses **coaxial TV cable**; **light pulses** in optical fibre describe **fibre** internet.
3: **DSL** uses **telephone copper lines** — correct.
xa: **Simplex** = one way; **half duplex** = both ways one at a time; **full duplex** = both at once.
**Li-Fi** carries data on **LED light**.
**Wi-Fi Direct** links devices with no LAN.

13.s:
Consider the following statements about wireless standards:
1. Bluetooth follows IEEE 802.15.1 and is a personal area network (PAN) technology.
2. Wi-Fi follows IEEE 802.11 and uses the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands, with 6 GHz in Wi-Fi 6E.
3. Wi-Fi Direct needs an existing LAN to link two devices.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statement 1 is correct: Bluetooth = IEEE 802.15.1, a PAN technology. Statement 2 is correct: Wi-Fi = IEEE 802.11 on 2.4 and 5 GHz (6 GHz in Wi-Fi 6E). Statement 3 is wrong: Wi-Fi Direct links devices with no LAN. Hence '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses statement 2, and the other options include the false statement 3.
13.tq: 802.15.1 = Bluetooth (PAN), 802.11 = Wi-Fi (WLAN); 'Direct' means no LAN needed.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Bluetooth** = **IEEE 802.15.1**, a **PAN** technology.
Statement 2 is correct: **Wi-Fi** = **IEEE 802.11**, **2.4 GHz and 5 GHz** (6 GHz in **Wi-Fi 6E**).
Statement 3 is wrong: **Wi-Fi Direct** links devices **with no LAN**.
xa: Bluetooth uses the **2.4 GHz ISM band**; microwave ovens and cordless phones share 2.4 GHz.
**Li-Fi** carries data on **LED light** — better bandwidth and security than Wi-Fi.
The **2019** APPSC key gave **Bluetooth 5.1** as the latest version.

13.s: HTTP primarily specifies which of the following?
o: How messages pass between web browsers and web servers
How domain names are converted into IP addresses
How wireless devices communicate within a PAN
How e-mails are downloaded to a device
13.x: HTTP specifies the communication of messages between web browsers and web servers. DNS, POP3 and Bluetooth serve different functions.
13.tq: Match the protocol with its immediate communication function rather than with a neighbouring networking function.
xs: **HTTP** sets **how messages pass between web browsers and web servers** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Turning domain names into IP addresses is **DNS**.
Downloading e-mail to a device is **POP3**; PAN devices use **Bluetooth**.
xa: **HTTPS** encrypts browser-server traffic via **TLS**.
HTTP is an **Application** layer (**7**) protocol.
Three elements of a protocol: **syntax** (format), **semantics** (meaning), **timing** (when and how fast).

13.s:
Consider the following statements regarding web technologies:
1. A web server stores webpages and sends them when requested.
2. A web browser requests webpages and displays them on the screen.
3. A search engine indexes webpages so that they can be found.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
13.x: All three statements are correct. The server stores and serves pages, the browser displays them, and the search engine indexes them for discovery.
13.tq: Separate the closely related functions of the server, browser and search engine.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3** is correct.
A **web server** stores webpages and **serves** them on request.
A **web browser** fetches and **displays** webpages (Chrome, Firefox); a **search engine** **indexes** them (Google, Bing).
xa: ⚠ Exam angle: "which one displays webpages" = **browser**; "which one stores them" = **server**.
**URL** parts: **protocol** + **domain name** + **path to the file**.
The **surface web** (~**4-5%**) is the part indexed by search engines.

13.s: The principal role of the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) is to:
o: Assign MAC addresses to network cards
Operate the global DNS root servers
13.x: W3C develops and maintains web standards so that webpages function consistently across different browsers.
13.tq: Identify the responsible body by its standard-setting function.
xs: **W3C** **develops and maintains web standards** so pages work the same across browsers — so option **(1)** is correct.
MAC addresses are **burnt into the network card**; the global domain name system is coordinated by **ICANN**.
xa: W3C was founded by **Tim Berners-Lee** in **1994**.
Berners-Lee invented the **WWW** in **1989** at **CERN**.
Core front-end technologies: **HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript**.

13.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its description?
o: Surface web — not indexed by search engines
Deep web — entirely associated with illegal markets
Dark web — hidden subset of the deep web requiring tools such as Tor or I2P
Surface web — accessible only through anonymous networks
13.x: The dark web is a small hidden subset of the deep web and is associated with anonymous access through tools such as Tor or I2P. The surface web is indexed, while the deep web is not necessarily malicious.
13.tq: Use the defining access and indexing features to separate surface, deep and dark web.
xs: **Dark web — hidden subset of the deep web needing Tor or I2P** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **surface web** **is indexed** by search engines, so options (1) and (4) are wrong.
The **deep web** is **not malicious** as such (e-mail inboxes, net banking, intranets), so option (2) is wrong.
xa: Shares: **surface web ~4-5%**, **deep web ~90-95%**, dark web a small subset.
The dark web is **anonymous** and linked with **illegal markets**.

13.s:
Consider the following statements about the multilingual internet:
1. Internationalised Domain Names (IDNs) are domain names in local scripts, such as .Bharat in Devanagari.
2. Universal Acceptance means every app and e-mail system accepts all such domain names and e-mail IDs.
3. BhashaNet was launched by ICANN in 2022 to promote Universal Acceptance for Indian languages.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statement 1 is correct: IDNs use local scripts, e.g. .Bharat in Devanagari. Statement 2 is correct: that is what Universal Acceptance means. Statement 3 is wrong: BhashaNet (2022) is a MeitY-NIXI initiative, not ICANN's. Hence '1 and 2 only'; the other options miss statement 2 or include the false statement 3.
13.tq: BhashaNet = MeitY + NIXI (Indian bodies); ICANN is the global DNS coordinator.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **IDNs** are domain names in **local scripts**, e.g. **.Bharat in Devanagari**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Universal Acceptance** = every app and e-mail system accepts all such names and IDs.
Statement 3 is wrong: **BhashaNet** (**2022**) is a **MeitY-NIXI** initiative, not ICANN's.
xa: **NIXI** (**2003**) runs the **.in registry** and IRINN.
**ICANN** (**1998**) is a US non-profit coordinating the global DNS.

13.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Sections 69A and 79 of the IT Act, 2000, the government can order ISPs and intermediaries to block content.
2. The Telecommunications Act, 2023 works alongside the Telegraph Act, 1885, which remains in force.
3. The power to suspend internet services is held under the Telecommunications Act, 2023.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Telecommunications Act, 2023 replaced the Telegraph Act. Statement 3 is correct. Hence '1 and 3 only'.
13.tq: Blocking = IT Act 69A/79; suspension = Telecom Act 2023.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
1: under **Sections 69A and 79** of the **IT Act, 2000**, government can order ISPs to **block content** — correct.
2 is wrong: the **Telecommunications Act, 2023** **replaced** the Telegraph Act.
3: the power to **suspend internet services** is held under the **Telecommunications Act, 2023** — correct.
xa: **NIXI** (**2003**) runs internet exchange points and the **.in registry** under **MeitY**.
**ICANN** (**1998**) coordinates the global domain name system.
Site blocking uses **DNS poisoning**, **HTTP interception** or **SNI filtering**.

13.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Protocol element)
A. Syntax
B. Semantics
C. Timing

List-II (Meaning)
1. Meaning of each field
2. Format of data
3. When and how fast to send

option_a
13.x: Syntax specifies the format of data, semantics specifies the meaning of each field, and timing specifies when and how fast data is sent.
13.tq: Start from the sure pair ‘syntax–format’ and complete the protocol-element mapping.
xs: **Syntax – format of data, Semantics – meaning of each field, Timing – when and how fast** — so option **(1)** **A-2, B-1, C-3** is correct.
**Syntax** is the format of data; **semantics** is the meaning of each field.
**Timing** is when and how fast to send.
xa: **TCP/IP** is the basic protocol suite of the internet.
⚠ E-mail protocols: **SMTP** sends, **POP3** downloads, **IMAP** keeps on server.
**DHCP** assigns IP addresses automatically.

14.s: What does the abbreviation SIM stand for in mobile telephony?
14.x: SIM stands for Subscriber Identity Module, the card that identifies the subscriber on a mobile network. The other expansions are invented.
14.tq: Test the exact expansion of a commonly confused telecommunications abbreviation.
xs: **SIM** stands for **Subscriber Identity Module** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The other expansions are made up; SIM has nothing to do with "Internet" or "Memory".
xa: The **first handheld call** was made by **Martin Cooper** (Motorola) on **3 April 1973**.
**Mobile Number Portability** began within a circle on **20 Jan 2011**, after a **Haryana** pilot on **25 Nov 2010**.
Generations: **1G (1980s) → 5G** now; **6G** expected in the early **2030s**.

14.s: Which of the following statements regarding mobile-generation technologies is correct?
o: 4G runs on LTE, using OFDM and MIMO.
WiMAX replaced LTE as the dominant 4G technology.
14.x: 4G runs on LTE and uses OFDM and MIMO. WiMAX lost out to LTE; 1G dates from the 1980s, while 6G is expected in the early 2030s.
14.tq: Use the technology-generation sequence and the LTE–WiMAX comparison to eliminate reversals.
xs: **4G runs on LTE**, using **OFDM and MIMO** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**WiMAX** lost out to **LTE**, so option (2) is reversed.
**1G** dates from the **1980s**; **6G** is expected only in the **early 2030s**.
xa: Mobile generations run **1G (1980s) → 5G now → 6G**.
**Martin Cooper** (Motorola) made the first handheld call on **3 April 1973**.
Android is Google's mobile OS built on the **Linux kernel**.

14.s: The first handheld mobile phone call was made on 3 April 1973 by:
14.x: Martin Cooper of Motorola made the first handheld mobile call on 3 April 1973. Bell is linked with the telephone, Marconi with radio, and Jack Dorsey co-founded Twitter.
14.tq: First handheld call = Martin Cooper (Motorola), 1973.
xs: **Martin Cooper** of **Motorola** made the first handheld call on **3 April 1973** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Jack Dorsey** co-founded **Twitter** (**2006**), not the mobile phone.
xa: **MNP** began within a circle on **20 Jan 2011**.
**SIM** = Subscriber Identity Module.
**6G** is expected in the early **2030s**.

14.s:
With reference to QR codes, consider the following statements:
1. QR stands for Quick Response.
2. QR codes were designed by Denso Wave in Japan.
3. Their original design in 1994 was for the car industry.
4. They are read quickly by a phone camera.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
14.x: All four statements are correct. QR means Quick Response; Denso Wave designed the codes in Japan in 1994 for the car industry, and phone cameras can read them quickly.
14.tq: Check the expansion, origin, year, purpose and practical use together.
xs: All four statements are correct — so option **(4)** **1, 2, 3 and 4** is correct.
**QR** = **Quick Response**; read **quickly by a phone camera**.
Designed in **1994** by **Denso Wave** (**Japan**) for the **car industry**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **"1996"** is wrong — the APPSC **2019** key was "only a".
**NFC** works at a few cm and **106-424 kbps**.
RBI allowed **offline UPI Lite payments over NFC**.

14.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
14.x: SWAYAM provides free online courses. Tele-MANAS concerns tele-mental health, Sugamya Bharat concerns accessibility reporting, and UMANG is a governance application.
14.tq: Use the sector-purpose association to detect swapped application functions.
xs: **SWAYAM — free online courses** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Tele-MANAS** is **tele mental health**, not market prices (that is **Agrimarket**).
**Sugamya Bharat** crowd-sources reports of **inaccessible places**; telemedicine is **eSanjeevani**.
**UMANG** is an **m-governance** app (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance).
xa: m-learning also covers **e-books** and **e-journals**.
Video editing software: **Adobe Premiere Pro**, **Apple Final Cut Pro**.
US telehealth apps: **Doctor on Demand**, **NowClinic**.

14.s: Which one of the following is an m-governance application that crowdsources reports of inaccessible places?
14.x: The Sugamya Bharat app crowdsources reports of inaccessible places and belongs to the m-governance sector.
14.tq: Identify the application from its distinctive real-world use.
xs: **Sugamya Bharat** app crowd-sources reports of **inaccessible places** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**SWAYAM** = free online courses (m-learning); **eHospital** and **NowClinic** are m-health.
xa: Another m-governance app: **UMANG** (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance).
**eSanjeevani** = telemedicine; **Tele-MANAS** = tele mental health.
**Agrimarket** = m-agriculture (prices **within 50 km**).

14.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with its digital-health function?
o: Doctor on Demand — United States health application
14.x: Agrimarket is an m-agriculture application. eSanjeevani provides telemedicine, Tele-MANAS concerns tele-mental health, and Doctor on Demand is a US health application.
14.tq: Find the application placed in the wrong sector.
xs: **Agrimarket — tele-mental health** is wrong: Agrimarket is an **m-agriculture** price app — so option **(4)** is correct.
**eSanjeevani** = telemedicine; **Tele-MANAS** = tele mental health.
**Doctor on Demand** is a **US** telehealth app (with **NowClinic**).
xa: Agrimarket uses **GPS** for markets **within 50 km**, data from **Agmarknet**.
Plan to widen **Tele-MANAS** to cover **digital addiction**.
**eHospital** is another m-health app.

14.s: Which one of the following statements about major social-media platforms is correct?
o: LinkedIn has been owned by Microsoft since 2016.
Twitter was renamed X in 2016 after Microsoft acquired it.
Facebook was founded by Elon Musk in 2006.
14.x: LinkedIn has been owned by Microsoft since 2016. Facebook is associated with Meta, while Twitter was renamed X in 2023 after Elon Musk's takeover.
14.tq: Trap the options by matching each platform with its correct parent and ownership event.
xs: **LinkedIn** has been owned by **Microsoft since 2016** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Facebook**'s parent is **Meta**, not Microsoft.
Twitter was renamed **X** in **2023** after **Elon Musk**'s takeover.
Facebook was founded by **Mark Zuckerberg** in **2004**.
xa: LinkedIn (**Reid Hoffman**, **2003**) = **professional networking**.
Twitter / X = **micro-blogging**.
The **hashtag** was popularised on **Twitter**.

14.s: Hashtag (#) was popularised on which social-media platform?
14.x: The hashtag (#) was popularised on Twitter (APPSC 2019), the micro-blogging platform founded by Jack Dorsey and others in 2006 and renamed X in 2023. Facebook and LinkedIn are networking sites and Amazon is an e-commerce company.
14.tq: Associate the content term with the platform that popularised it, not merely a platform where it is used.
xs: The **hashtag (#)** was popularised on **Twitter** (APPSC **2019**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Facebook** is social networking; **LinkedIn** is professional networking.
xa: Twitter was founded by **Jack Dorsey** and others (**2006**); renamed **X** (**2023**).
Twitter is a **micro-blogging** platform.
**Folksonomy** = user-created tagging (social tagging).

14.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Twitter is renamed X
B. LinkedIn comes under Microsoft ownership
C. LinkedIn is founded
D. Facebook is founded
14.x: LinkedIn was founded in 2003, Facebook in 2004, LinkedIn came under Microsoft ownership in 2016, and Twitter was renamed X in 2023.
14.tq: Place the dated platform events using the first and last events as anchors.
xs: Order: **Facebook founded → LinkedIn founded → LinkedIn under Microsoft → Twitter renamed X** — so option **(2)** **D, C, B, A** is correct.
⚠ This keyed order does not match the notes: **LinkedIn** was founded in **2003**, **Facebook** in **2004**.
**Microsoft** has owned LinkedIn since **2016**; Twitter became **X** in **2023**.
xa: ⚠ The notes give **LinkedIn (2003)** before **Facebook (2004)** — by the notes the order is C, D, B, A.
Twitter was founded in **2006** by **Jack Dorsey** and others.
Facebook's parent is **Meta**.

14.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (E-commerce model)
a. B2B
b. B2C
c. C2C
d. D2C

List-II (Nature of transaction)
i. Brand sells directly to the consumer without a middleman
ii. Business sells to another business
iii. Consumer sells to another consumer
aiv. Business sells to the consumer

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
14.x: B2B denotes business-to-business transactions, B2C business-to-consumer transactions, C2C consumer-to-consumer transactions, and D2C direct brand-to-consumer sales.
14.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes containing a reversed business-consumer relationship.
xs: The correct match is **a–ii, b–iv, c–iii, d–i** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**B2B** = business to business (wholesale, **IndiaMART**); **B2C** = business to consumer.
**C2C** = consumer to consumer (**OLX**-type resale); **D2C** = brand sells directly, **no middleman**.
xa: **ONDC** is an **open, network-based protocol**, not a platform.
ONDC connects any buyer app to any seller across **B2C and B2B**.
ONDC was beta-tested in **Bengaluru**.

14.s:
With reference to ONDC, consider the following statements:
1. It is an open, network-based protocol.
2. It functions as a single e-commerce platform owned by one seller.
3. It can connect a buyer application with a seller across B2C and B2B transactions.
4. It is intended to help MSMEs.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
14.x: ONDC is a network-based protocol rather than a single platform. It connects buyer and seller applications across B2C and B2B transactions and is intended to benefit MSMEs.
14.tq: Reject the statement that changes a network protocol into a single platform.
xs: Statements **1, 3 and 4** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **ONDC** is an **open, network-based protocol**.
Statement 2 is wrong: ONDC is **not a platform**.
Statements 3 and 4 are correct: it connects any buyer app to any seller across **B2C and B2B** and **helps MSMEs**.
xa: ONDC was **beta-tested in Bengaluru**.
**Digital India** (**11 years**, 2015-2026) is built on JAM, eSanjeevani, GeM, **ONDC** and AgriStack.
**D2C** = brand sells directly to the consumer.

14.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the textbook position regarding Foreign Direct Investment in e-commerce?
o: FDI is permitted only in the inventory model and prohibited in the marketplace model.
100% FDI is permitted under the automatic route in both marketplace and inventory models.
100% FDI is permitted under the automatic route in the marketplace model, while FDI is not permitted in the inventory model.
FDI is prohibited in both marketplace and inventory models.
14.x: The stated textbook position permits 100% FDI under the automatic route in the marketplace model but does not permit FDI in the inventory model.
14.tq: Split the options by comparing the treatment of marketplace and inventory models.
xs: Textbook position: **100% FDI** under the **automatic route** in the **marketplace model**, **no FDI** in the **inventory model** — so option **(3)** is correct.
This should be verified against the latest FDI policy.
xa: The **Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020** cover both **marketplace and inventory** entities.
They require a **grievance officer** and display of **country of origin**.
**ONDC** is an open protocol helping **MSMEs**.

14.s:
Consider the following statements about the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020:
1. They are framed under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
2. They cover marketplace entities only, not inventory entities.
3. They require a grievance officer and display of the country of origin.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
14.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Rules are under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. Statement 2 is wrong: they cover both marketplace and inventory entities. Statement 3 is correct: a grievance officer and display of country of origin are required. Hence '1 and 3 only'; '1 only' misses statement 3, and options with statement 2 include the false claim.
14.tq: Rules apply to both e-commerce models; watch for 'only' in a statement.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the Rules are under the **Consumer Protection Act, 2019**.
Statement 2 is wrong: they cover **marketplace and inventory** entities.
Statement 3 is correct: a **grievance officer** and display of **country of origin** are required.
xa: **IT Rules, 2021** regulate social media, **OTT** and digital news.
**Code on Social Security, 2020** defined **gig and platform workers** for the first time.

14.s:
Consider the following statements about the IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021:
1. They replaced the 2011 guidelines and regulate social media, OTT platforms and digital news.
2. They provide a Code of Ethics and a three-tier grievance redressal system.
3. They were framed under Section 79 of the IT Act.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
14.x: Statement 3 is wrong: the Rules were framed under Section 87; Section 79 is the safe-harbour provision. Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
14.tq: Rules under Sec 87; safe harbour = Sec 79.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct, so option **(3)** is correct.
1: the **2021 Rules** replaced the **2011 guidelines** and regulate **social media, OTT and digital news** — correct.
2: they provide a **Code of Ethics** and a **three-tier grievance redressal** system — correct.
3 is wrong: they were framed under **Section 87** of the IT Act; **Sec 79** is about **safe harbour**.
xa: **IT Amendment Rules, 2023:** platforms ignoring orders on false content lose **safe harbour**.
**Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020** require display of **country of origin**.
**50 OTT platforms** were blocked over two years for obscenity or IT Act violations.

14.s: Under the IT Amendment Rules, 2023, an intermediary may lose safe-harbour protection under which section if it ignores government orders concerning false content?
14.x: The 2023 amendment links failure to comply with government orders on false content with loss of safe-harbour protection under Section 79 of the IT Act.
14.tq: Distinguish the substantive safe-harbour section from the rule-making section.
xs: Platforms lose **safe harbour** under **Section 79** — so option **(2)** is correct.
This applies under the **IT Amendment Rules, 2023** when they ignore government orders on **false content**.
**Section 87** is the rule-making power used for the **IT Rules, 2021**.
xa: The rules were **amended again in Feb 2026**.
**Sections 69A and 79** let government order ISPs and intermediaries to block content.

14.s:
Consider the following statements about the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025:
1. It banned real-money gaming.
2. It created the Online Gaming Authority of India (OGAI) as a digital attached office of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.
3. Registration of e-sports is mandatory under it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
14.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Act banned real-money gaming. Statement 2 is wrong: OGAI is a digital attached office of MeitY (Ministry of Electronics and IT), not the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. Statement 3 is correct: e-sports registration is mandatory. Hence '1 and 3 only'; '1 only' misses statement 3, and options with statement 2 include the wrong ministry.
14.tq: Online gaming regulator sits with MeitY; MIB handles takedown notices in the 2026 IT Rules draft.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the Act banned **real-money gaming**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **OGAI** is a digital attached office of **MeitY**, not MIB.
Statement 3 is correct: **registration of e-sports is mandatory**.
xa: Rules notified **Apr 2026**; effective **1 May 2026**.
Also called the **"Online Gaming (Regulation) Act, 2025"** in some summaries.
WHO lists **Gaming Disorder** in **ICD-11**.

14.s:
Consider the following statements about gig and platform workers:
Statement I: They were defined for the first time in the Code on Social Security, 2020.
Statement II: Only the workers themselves contribute to their social-security fund; aggregators have no obligation.
Which one of the following is correct?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II
Neither Statement I nor Statement II
14.x: Statement I is correct as per the notes. Statement II is wrong: aggregators contribute to the social-security fund of gig and platform workers. Hence 'Statement I only'.
14.tq: Code on Social Security 2020: aggregators pay in.
xs: Only **Statement I** is correct, so option **(1)** is correct.
I: **gig and platform workers** were **defined for the first time** in the **Code on Social Security, 2020** — correct.
II is wrong: **aggregators contribute** to their **social-security fund**.
xa: The **Online Gaming Act, 2025** banned **real-money gaming**.
It created the **Online Gaming Authority of India (OGAI)** under MeitY.
The gaming rules took effect on **1 May 2026**; **e-sports** registration is mandatory.

14.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Term)
a. Nomophobia
b. FOMO
c. Doomscrolling
d. Cyberchondria
List-II (Meaning)
i. Endless scrolling through bad news
ii. Health anxiety fed by online symptom searches
iii. Fear of being without one's mobile phone
iv. Fear of missing out on what others are doing online
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
14.x: Nomophobia is fear of being without one's mobile phone (a-iii), FOMO is fear of missing out (b-iv), doomscrolling is endless scrolling through bad news (c-i) and cyberchondria is health anxiety fed by online symptom searches (d-ii), so A. B swaps both a/b and c/d, C swaps only doomscrolling and cyberchondria, and D gives nomophobia the meaning of doomscrolling.
14.tq: Break the words: no-mo(bile)-phobia; cyber + hypochondria.
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Nomophobia** = fear of being without one's mobile; **FOMO** = fear of missing out online.
**Doomscrolling** = endless bad news; **Cyberchondria** = health anxiety from symptom searches.
xa: **Digital detox** = a deliberate break from devices.
WHO lists **Gaming Disorder** in **ICD-11**.
Kerala Police run **D-DAD** (Digital De-Addiction) centres.

14.s: Which body includes Gaming Disorder in ICD-11?
14.x: The World Health Organization lists Gaming Disorder in ICD-11.
14.tq: Match the health classification with the responsible international body.
xs: The **World Health Organization (WHO)** lists **Gaming Disorder** in **ICD-11** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Other digital-age terms like **nomophobia**, **FOMO** and **doomscrolling** are not formal disorders in the notes.
xa: **NIMHANS, Bengaluru** runs the **SHUT Clinic** (Service for Healthy Use of Technology).
The **Online Gaming Act, 2025** banned **real-money gaming**.
Kerala Police run **D-DAD** centres.

14.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. 'Digital Detox Centre - Beyond Screens' is an initiative of Kerala.
2. Kerala Police run D-DAD (Digital De-Addiction) centres.
3. The SHUT Clinic (Service for Healthy Use of Technology) runs at NIMHANS, Bengaluru.
4. Andhra Pradesh announced a social-media ban for children under 13.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
14.x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct as per the notes. Statement 1 is wrong: 'Digital Detox Centre - Beyond Screens' is Karnataka's. Hence '2, 3 and 4 only'.
14.tq: Karnataka = Beyond Screens + under-16; AP = under-13; Kerala = D-DAD.
xs: Statements **2, 3 and 4** are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
1 is wrong: "**Digital Detox Centre - Beyond Screens**" is **Karnataka**'s initiative.
2: **Kerala** Police run **D-DAD** centres — correct; 3: **SHUT Clinic** runs at **NIMHANS, Bengaluru** — correct.
4: **Andhra Pradesh** announced a social-media ban for children **under 13** — correct.
xa: ⚠ **Karnataka** = **under 16**; **AP** = **under 13**.
**Australia** has the world's first nationwide **under-16** ban, effective **10 Dec 2025**.
**Gaming Disorder** is listed by WHO in **ICD-11**.

14.s: Which of the following is NOT a central measure concerning screen time and digital addiction?
o: PRAGYATA framework of the Ministry of Education
14.x: Agmarknet is related to agricultural market information. Central measures include the Ministry of Education's PRAGYATA framework, CBSE safe-internet guidelines, NCPCR screen-time guidelines and a plan to widen Tele-MANAS for digital addiction.
14.tq: Identify the unrelated programme among measures addressing screen use and digital addiction.
xs: **Agmarknet** is an agricultural market-price source, not a screen-time measure — so option **(4)** is correct.
Central measures: MoE's **PRAGYATA**, **CBSE** safe-internet guidelines, **NCPCR** screen-time guidelines.
xa: Plan to widen **Tele-MANAS** to cover **digital addiction**.
Agmarknet feeds the **Agrimarket** app (markets **within 50 km**).
**NIMHANS** runs the **SHUT Clinic**.

14.s: The proposed separate law on age-based access to social media is reported to favour:
o: A ban limited only to digital news platforms
A blanket ban for every person below 18 years
Graded limits based on age rather than a blanket ban
14.x: The proposed approach favours graded limits based on age instead of imposing a blanket ban on all persons below a specified age.
14.tq: Focus on the contrast between graded regulation and an absolute prohibition.
xs: The proposed law favours **graded limits based on age rather than a blanket ban** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is a separate law on **age-based social-media access**.
xa: **DPDP Act**: anyone **below 18** is a child; **verifiable parental consent** needed (**Sec 9**).
**Australia** = world's first nationwide **under-16** ban, effective **10 Dec 2025**.
⚠ AP's ban = **under 13**; Karnataka's = **under 16**.

14.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: SMTP — receiving e-mail from a mail server
POP3/IMAP — sending e-mail to a mail server
BCC — displaying all recipients to one another
14.x: SMTP is used for sending e-mail. POP3 and IMAP are used for receiving mail, while BCC hides recipients from one another.
14.tq: Discriminate between the sending protocol, receiving protocols and recipient-copy fields.
xs: **SMTP** is used for **sending e-mail** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**POP3/IMAP** **receive** mail, so options (2) and (3) swap the roles.
**BCC** **hides** recipients, so option (4) is wrong.
xa: An e-mail address = **username @ domain name** (e.g. name@gov.in).
**Attachments** are files sent with a mail.
**CC/BCC** send copies; only BCC hides recipients.

14.s: A sender wants to send copies of an e-mail to several recipients without revealing the recipients' addresses to one another. Which field should be used?
14.x: BCC, or blind carbon copy, sends copies while hiding the recipients' addresses from one another.
14.tq: Translate the privacy requirement in the scenario into the correct e-mail field.
xs: **BCC** sends copies while **hiding the recipients** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**CC** also sends copies but shows all recipients.
**SMTP** and **IMAP** are mail **protocols**, not address fields.
xa: **SMTP** sends mail; **POP3/IMAP** receive it.
An e-mail address = **username @ domain name**.

14.s: Which one of the following is NOT among the essentials of video conferencing?
14.x: Video conferencing needs a camera, microphone, speaker/display, a broadband link and conferencing software (codec). An RFID reader is used to read RFID tags and is not a video-conferencing component.
14.tq: VC kit: camera, mic, speaker/display, broadband, codec.
xs: An **RFID reader** is not a video-conferencing essential — so option **(4)** is correct.
Essentials: **camera, microphone, speaker/display, broadband link and conferencing software (codec)**.
xa: Multimedia components: **text, images/graphics, audio, video, animation**.
Telemedicine apps like **eSanjeevani** rely on such video links.
TV broadcasting methods: terrestrial, cable, satellite/**DTH**, IPTV/OTT.

14.s: ANI is associated with which distinction in Indian digital news media?
o: It was the first Indian company to design QR codes.
It created the Android operating system.
It was the first Indian news agency to offer syndicated video news.
It was the first agency to launch nationwide MNP.
14.x: ANI, established in 1971, was the first Indian news agency to offer syndicated video news.
14.tq: Match the organisation with its distinctive historical contribution.
xs: **ANI** was the **first Indian news agency to offer syndicated video news** — so option **(3)** is correct.
ANI dates from **1971**.
QR codes were designed by **Denso Wave** (Japan); Android is **Google**'s.
xa: **e-journals** are published on the **Internet** (APPSC **2019**).
TV broadcasting: terrestrial, cable, satellite/**DTH**, IPTV/OTT.

14.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, anyone below 18 years is a child.
2. Section 9 of the DPDP Act requires verifiable parental consent for a child's data.
3. India has the world's first nationwide under-16 social-media ban, effective 10 December 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
14.x: Statement 1 is correct: the DPDP Act treats anyone below 18 as a child. Statement 2 is correct: Section 9 requires verifiable parental consent. Statement 3 is wrong: Australia, not India, has the world's first nationwide under-16 ban, effective 10 December 2025; India's proposed law favours graded age-based limits. Hence '1 and 2 only'; the other options miss statement 2 or include the false statement 3.
14.tq: DPDP child = below 18; under-16 ban = Australia; AP = under-13, Karnataka = under-16.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: under the **DPDP Act**, anyone **below 18** is a **child**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Sec 9** requires **verifiable parental consent**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Australia**, not India, has the first nationwide **under-16** ban (**10 Dec 2025**).
xa: India's upcoming law favours **graded limits** over a blanket ban.
⚠ AP's ban = **under 13**; Karnataka's = **under 16**.
**Digital India** completed **11 years** (2015-2026).

14.s:
Consider the following statements about Near Field Communication (NFC):
1. It has a longer range and uses more power than Bluetooth.
2. It works over a few centimetres at 106-424 kbps.
3. RBI has allowed offline UPI Lite payments over NFC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
14.x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: NFC gives easier pairing and uses less power than Bluetooth, over only a few cm. Statement 3 is correct. Hence '2 and 3 only'.
14.tq: NFC = few cm, low power, UPI Lite offline.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
1 is wrong: **NFC** gives **easier pairing** and **lower power** than Bluetooth, over only **a few cm**.
2: NFC works at a few cm, **106-424 kbps** — correct.
3: **RBI** allowed **offline UPI Lite payments over NFC** — correct.
xa: **QR code** = **Quick Response**, designed in **1994** by **Denso Wave** (Japan).
First handheld call: **Martin Cooper** (Motorola), **3 April 1973**.
**Mobile Number Portability** began within a circle on **20 Jan 2011**.

14.s: e-journals are published on:
14.x: e-journals are electronic journals published on the Internet. Printed paper and microfilm are physical formats, and television broadcasting carries audio-visual programmes, not journals.
14.tq: e-journal = Internet (APPSC 2019).
xs: **e-journals** are published on **the Internet** (APPSC **2019**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
They are electronic, not print, microfilm or TV broadcast.
xa: m-learning includes **SWAYAM** courses, **e-books** and e-journals.
Multimedia components: text, images/graphics, audio, video, animation.
**ANI** (**1971**) first offered syndicated video news in India.

14.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Viral — Content spreading rapidly by sharing
Influencer — Content that spreads rapidly through sharing
Wall — Profile space where posts appear on Facebook
14.x: An influencer is a user whose following can sway opinions and buying decisions. Content spreading rapidly through sharing is described as viral.
14.tq: Find the swapped meanings among closely related social-media terms.
xs: **Influencer — content spreading rapidly** is wrong: an **influencer** is a **user whose following sways opinions and buying** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Content spreading rapidly by sharing is **viral**.
**Folksonomy** = user-created tagging; **Wall** = Facebook profile space where posts appear.
xa: **SMO** = **Social Media Optimisation**, raising reach through social platforms.
Folksonomy is also called **social tagging**.

15.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the sequence of defining technologies from Industry 1.0 to Industry 4.0?
o: Steam power — electricity — computers and electronics — cyber-physical systems
Electricity — steam power — cyber-physical systems — computers
Computers — electricity — steam power — artificial intelligence
Cyber-physical systems — steam power — electricity — computers
15.x: Industry 1.0 involved steam-powered mechanisation; Industry 2.0 electricity and mass production; Industry 3.0 computers and electronics; and Industry 4.0 cyber-physical systems.
15.tq: Arrange the stages by their defining technological progression.
xs: The sequence is **steam power → electricity → computers and electronics → cyber-physical systems** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Industry 1.0**: mechanisation, **steam power**, weaving loom; **2.0**: **electricity**, mass production, assembly line.
**Industry 3.0**: **automation, computers and electronics**; **4.0**: **cyber-physical systems**, IoT, AI, big data.
xa: **Industry 5.0** puts **human-machine collaboration** and people at the centre.
The term **Fourth Industrial Revolution** was coined by **Klaus Schwab** (WEF founder) in **2016**.
⚠ **3.0** = automation and computers; **4.0** = cyber-physical systems.

15.s:
Which of the following are characteristic features of Industry 4.0?
1. Cyber-physical systems
2. Internet of Things and networks
3. Artificial intelligence and big data
4. Steam-powered weaving looms
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
15.x: Industry 4.0 is characterised by cyber-physical systems, IoT, networks, AI and big data. Steam-powered weaving looms belong to Industry 1.0.
15.tq: Identify the stage-specific technologies and reject a feature from an earlier revolution.
xs: Items **1, 2 and 3** are Industry 4.0 features — so option **(2)** is correct.
Industry 4.0 = **cyber-physical systems**, **IoT**, **networks**, **AI** and **big data**.
**Steam-powered weaving looms** belong to **Industry 1.0**.
xa: Industry 4.0 brings **smart factories**, where digital, physical and biological technologies converge.
**SAMARTH Udyog Bharat 4.0** (Ministry of Heavy Industries) spreads Industry 4.0 via demonstration centres.
AP has an **Industry Policy 4.0** (**24 Apr 2026**).

15.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The term 'Fourth Industrial Revolution' was coined by Klaus Schwab, founder of the World Economic Forum, in 2016.
2. The Fourth Industrial Revolution involves the convergence of digital, physical and biological technologies.
3. Industry 5.0 seeks to remove people from the centre of industrial innovation in favour of full automation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
15.x: Statement 1 is correct: Klaus Schwab (WEF founder) coined the term in 2016. Statement 2 is correct: digital, physical and biological technologies converge, giving smart factories. Statement 3 is wrong: Industry 5.0 puts human-machine collaboration and people at the centre. Hence B; A omits statement 2, C and D accept the wrong statement 3.
15.tq: Industry 5.0 = humans back at the centre; 4.0 = cyber-physical convergence (Schwab, 2016).
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Klaus Schwab**, founder of **WEF**, coined the term in **2016**.
Statement 2 is correct: **digital + physical + biological** technologies converge, giving **smart factories**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Industry 5.0** puts **human-machine collaboration** and **people at the centre**.
xa: **WEF** is to set up a **Fourth Industrial Revolution Centre** in AP — India's **3rd** after Mumbai and Telangana.
Debate: automation and AI replace **intellectual as well as manual work** → job displacement.

15.s: Which one of the following correctly describes a cyber-physical system?
o: A rugged computer used only to control one machine
A robot designed exclusively for light shows
A virtual replica used only for simulation
Computing tightly integrated with physical processes
15.x: A cyber-physical system integrates computing closely with physical processes and is a core element of Industry 4.0 and the NM-ICPS mission.
15.tq: Distinguish system-level integration from the narrower meanings of PLC, digital twin and robot.
xs: A **cyber-physical system** is **computing tightly integrated with physical processes** — so option **(4)** is correct.
A rugged computer controlling machines is a **PLC**; a virtual replica is a **digital twin**.
xa: Cyber-physical systems are the **core of Industry 4.0**.
India's **NM-ICPS** mission targets them; it runs **25 Technology Innovation Hubs**.
⚠ **3.0** = automation; **4.0** = cyber-physical systems.

15.s:
Consider the following statements regarding IoT and AI:
1. IoT devices collect and exchange data through sensors.
2. AI analyses data, recognises patterns and makes decisions.
3. A smart thermostat is an example listed under AI rather than IoT.
4. Chatbots and image recognition are examples associated with AI.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
15.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. A smart thermostat is listed as an IoT example, whereas chatbots and image recognition are associated with AI.
15.tq: Separate data collection and exchange from analysis, pattern recognition and decision-making.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 4** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **IoT** collects and exchanges data through **sensors**.
Statement 2 is correct: **AI** analyses data, recognises patterns and decides.
Statement 3 is wrong: a **smart thermostat** is an **IoT** example; statement 4 is correct: **chatbot, image recognition** = AI.
xa: IoT is **rule-based, limited learning**; AI uses **machine and deep learning**.
A **fitness wearable** is another IoT example.

15.s:
Which of the following functions are commonly performed by wearable devices such as smartwatches and fitness bands?
1. Tracking heart rate, steps and sleep
2. Biometric authentication
3. Acting as typical IoT end-devices
4. Producing steam power for industrial machinery
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
15.x: Wearables track health and fitness indicators, support biometric authentication and function as typical IoT end-devices. They do not produce steam power for industrial machinery.
15.tq: Separate genuine wearable functions from an unrelated industrial-revolution feature.
xs: Items **1, 2 and 3** are wearable functions — so option **(2)** is correct.
Wearables (**smartwatches, fitness bands**) track **heart rate, steps, sleep**.
They support **biometric authentication** and are **typical IoT end-devices**.
Steam power belongs to **Industry 1.0**.
xa: IoT applications: smart farming, smart homes, smart grids, **healthcare**, logistics, smart cities.
A **fitness wearable** is an IoT (not AI) example.

15.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. HomoSEP — IIT Madras
2. Vyommitra — ISRO
3. Daksh — DRDO
4. Manav — Genrobotics
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
15.x: HomoSEP was developed by IIT Madras, Vyommitra by ISRO and Daksh by DRDO. Manav was developed by A-SET Training & Research Institutes, Delhi, not Genrobotics.
15.tq: Check each developer association and eliminate the swapped organisation.
xs: Pairs **1, 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
**HomoSEP** = **IIT Madras**; **Vyommitra** = **ISRO**; **Daksh** = **DRDO**.
Pair 4 is wrong: **Manav** was built by **A-SET Training & Research Institutes, Delhi**; **Genrobotics** made **Bandicoot**.
xa: Manav is India's **first 3D-printed humanoid** (**2017**).
**DRDO CAIR** builds unmanned and multi-agent robotic systems.
⚠ **Bandicoot** = sewers; **HomoSEP** = septic tanks.

15.s:
Consider the following statements regarding robotics standards and support:
1. ISO Technical Committee 299 deals with robotics.
2. ISO 10218 sets norms for the safety of surgical robots.
3. Robotics is one of the verticals of the 25 Technology Innovation Hubs under NM-ICPS.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
15.x: Statement 1 is correct: ISO TC 299 is the Robotics committee. Statement 2 is wrong: ISO 10218 covers industrial-robot safety, not surgical robots. Statement 3 is correct: robotics is a vertical of the 25 TIHs under NM-ICPS. So 1 and 3 only (B); A misses statement 3, C and D wrongly accept statement 2.
15.tq: ISO 10218 = industrial-robot safety; TC 299 = robotics.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **ISO Technical Committee 299** deals with **Robotics**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **ISO 10218** covers **industrial-robot safety**, not surgical robots.
Statement 3 is correct: robotics is a vertical of the **25 Technology Innovation Hubs** under **NM-ICPS**.
xa: MeitY's inter-ministerial committee (convener **Secretary MeitY**) is drafting a robotics ecosystem strategy.
Members: **DoT, DSIR, DST, DPIIT, NITI Aayog**.

15.s:
Consider the following statements about immersive technologies:
1. In Mixed Reality, real and virtual objects interact in real time.
2. Extended Reality (XR) is an umbrella term for VR, AR and MR.
3. Augmented Reality creates a fully computer-generated world that shuts out the real world.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
15.x: Statement 3 is wrong: AR places digital layers over the real world (e.g. Pokemon Go); a fully computer-generated world is VR. Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
15.tq: AR = overlay; VR = full immersion; XR = umbrella.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct, so option **(3)** is correct.
1: in **Mixed Reality**, real and virtual objects **interact in real time** — correct.
2: **XR** is the umbrella term for **VR + AR + MR** — correct.
3 is wrong: **AR** places **digital layers over the real world** (e.g. Pokemon Go); a fully computer-generated world is **VR**.
xa: In **VR** the user is still a **real person** (**APPSC 2024**).
**Metaverse** is a shared 3D virtual space using **XR** and **avatars**.
**VARCoE** is at **IIT Bhubaneswar**.

15.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Term)
 a. PLC
 b. SCADA
 c. Digital twin
 d. Cobot

List-II (Meaning)
 i. Virtual replica of a physical object or system
 ii. Collaborative robot working safely beside humans
 iii. Rugged industrial computer controlling machines
 iv. Remote monitoring of plants and grids

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
15.x: PLC controls machines as a rugged industrial computer; SCADA enables remote monitoring; a digital twin is a virtual replica; and a cobot works collaboratively with humans.
15.tq: Start from the distinctive acronym meanings and then verify the remaining pairs.
xs: The correct match is **a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**PLC** (Programmable Logic Controller) = rugged industrial computer controlling machines.
**SCADA** (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) = remote monitoring of plants and grids.
**Digital twin** = virtual replica; **cobot** = collaborative robot working safely beside humans.
xa: A **cyber-physical system** is computing tightly integrated with physical processes — core of Industry 4.0.
**Swarms** = many drones coordinated by software.
Cobots are **spreading in Indian factories**.

15.s: Internet of Things (IoT) refers to:
o: A network limited to industrial robots
Only computers connected through wired networks
A system in which data can be exchanged only after manual approval
Devices with sensors linked in a network and exchanging data without human intervention
15.x: IoT consists of sensor-equipped devices connected through networks that exchange data without human intervention.
15.tq: Select the precise definition and reject restrictive qualifiers such as ‘only’.
xs: **IoT** = **devices with sensors linked in a network, exchanging data without human intervention** — so option **(4)** is correct.
This definition was asked in APPSC **2023** and **2024**.
xa: IoT three-layer model: **perception** (sensors, RFID) → **network** → **application**.
The **mMTC** slice of **5G** serves dense IoT sensors.
IoT applications: smart farming, smart homes, **smart grids**, healthcare, logistics, smart cities.

15.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the role of the mMTC slice in 5G?
o: It serves dense deployments of IoT sensors.
It is used exclusively for high-definition video streaming.
It replaces all network security functions.
It is designed only for satellite communication.
15.x: mMTC means massive machine-type communication and is intended to support dense IoT sensor deployments in 5G networks.
15.tq: Apply the expansion and purpose of the communication category to the scenario.
xs: **mMTC** serves **dense IoT sensors** — so option **(1)** is correct.
mMTC = **massive machine-type communication**, a **5G** slice.
xa: **NDCP 2018** covers **5G, IoT and M2M**.
IoT devices exchange data **without human intervention**.
**DHRUV64** (C-DAC) is a **RISC-V** processor for **5G, IoT, automotive**.

15.s: Which policy covers 5G, the Internet of Things (IoT) and machine-to-machine (M2M) communication?
15.x: The National Digital Communications Policy (NDCP) 2018 covers 5G, IoT and M2M. The Drone Rules 2021 govern drones, the IT Rules 2021 regulate intermediaries and digital media, and the E-Commerce Rules 2020 protect online consumers.
15.tq: NDCP 2018 = 5G + IoT + M2M.
xs: **NDCP 2018** (National Digital Communications Policy) covers **5G, IoT and M2M** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Drone Rules, 2021** set drone weight classes; they do not cover 5G or IoT.
xa: The **mMTC** slice of 5G serves dense IoT sensors.
IoT is also part of **Digital India**.
MeitY-NASSCOM **IoT CoEs** include **Visakhapatnam**.

15.s: Which district was offered for aerospace, drone and semiconductor manufacturing under the stated Andhra Pradesh proposal?
15.x: Sri Sathya Sai district, near Bengaluru, was offered for aerospace, drone and semiconductor manufacturing.
15.tq: Use the precise district-location association; do not substitute a nearby technology centre.
xs: **Sri Sathya Sai district** (near **Bengaluru**) was offered — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was pitched for **aerospace, drone and semiconductor** manufacturing (**5 Jun 2026**).
xa: **WEF** Fourth Industrial Revolution Centre in AP = India's **3rd**, after **Mumbai** and **Telangana**.
AP has an **Industry Policy 4.0** (**24 Apr 2026**).
**JNTU Kakinada** + Efftronics launched an **M.Tech in IoT**.

15.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. 4D printing adds materials that change shape over time.
2. Additive manufacturing is a form of subtractive machining.
3. Additive manufacturing builds an object layer by layer from a digital (CAD) model.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
15.x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: additive manufacturing is the opposite of subtractive machining. Statement 1 is correct. Hence '1 and 3 only'.
15.tq: 3D = additive; 4D = shape changes over time.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
1: **4D printing** adds materials that **change shape over time** — correct.
2 is wrong: **additive manufacturing** is the **opposite** of **subtractive machining**.
3: additive manufacturing builds objects **layer by layer** from a **CAD** model — correct.
xa: India's first **3D-printed post office**: **Bengaluru**, **2023**.
3D printing is used for **prosthetics** and **implants**.
**Additive manufacturing** is a course area under **FutureSkills PRIME**.

15.s: A semi-passive RFID tag differs from an active RFID tag because the semi-passive tag:
o: Uses its battery to run the chip but uses the reader’s field to reply
Has no internal power and cannot contain identity data
Has an independent transmitter and broadcasts over a long range
