25.s:
The Digital Payments Index of RBI has which of the following characteristics?
1. Its base period is March 2018.
2. The base value is 100.
3. It is published half-yearly.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
25.x: The RBI Digital Payments Index uses March 2018 as its base period with a base value of 100 and is published half-yearly.
25.tq: Verify the base period, base value and publication frequency as separate facts.
xs: The RBI **Digital Payments Index** has base **March 2018 = 100** and is published **half-yearly** — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
It is an **RBI** index tracking the spread of digital payments.
xa: Digital payments grew from **2,071 crore** transactions (2017-18) to **22,831 crore** (2024-25) = **41% CAGR**.
UPI = **85%** of digital payments by volume in **FY 2025-26**.
Nodal body: **Department of Financial Services**, which gives the **Digital Payments Awards**.

25.s: Which of the following correctly describes the reported gender composition of PMJDY accounts?
o: Less than one-fourth were held by women
Exactly half were held by women
More than half were held by women
Women were not included as account holders
25.x: More than half of PMJDY accounts were reported to be held by women.
25.tq: Distinguish a qualitative majority from an exact numerical proportion.
xs: **More than half** of PMJDY accounts are **held by women** — so option **(3)** is correct.
PMJDY had **58.77 crore** accounts with deposits of **Rs 3,12,414 crore** (Aug 2026).
xa: Earlier figure: **56.04 crore** accounts (Jul 2025).
**JAM trinity** links Jan Dhan accounts, **Aadhaar** and **Mobile** for DBT.
DBT transfers reached **Rs 44 lakh crore** by **May 2025**.

25.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the recent relevance of UPI?
o: It accounted for 49% of the world’s real-time payments and recorded a FY 2025–26 high.
It was limited to offline transactions during FY 2025–26.
It accounted for 49% of India’s GDP and had no global share.
It was replaced by ONDC as the principal real-time payment system.
25.x: UPI recorded a FY 2025–26 record and accounted for 49 percent of the world’s real-time payments.
25.tq: Separate the global real-time-payment share from unrelated GDP and platform figures.
xs: UPI set a **FY 2025-26** record and **accounted for 49% of the world's real-time payments** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**ONDC** is an **e-commerce** network, not a payment system — option (4) is wrong.
The **49%** is a global real-time payment share, not a share of GDP; the digital economy is **12-14% of GDP**.
xa: UPI in **FY 2025-26**: **24,160 crore** transactions worth **Rs 314 lakh crore** = **85%** of digital payments by volume.
**France** = first in **Europe** to accept UPI; **PayNow-UPI** link with **Singapore (2023)**.

25.s: Which country was the first in Europe to accept UPI?
25.x: France was the first country in Europe to accept UPI.
25.tq: Use geographical discrimination among named international UPI markets.
xs: **France** was the first country in **Europe** to accept UPI — so option **(4)** is correct (asked in **APPSC 2025**).
**Singapore** is linked through **PayNow-UPI** (**2023**) but is not in Europe.
**Netherlands** is among other UPI markets, but not the first in Europe.
xa: Other UPI markets: **UAE, Netherlands**.
UPI = **49%** of the world's real-time payments.
UPI was launched in **April 2016** by **NPCI**.

25.s:
With reference to RBI's New Umbrella Entities (NUEs), consider the following statements:
1. They are meant to end NPCI's monopoly in retail payments.
2. The minimum capital required for an NUE is Rs 100 crore.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
25.x: Statement 1 is correct: NUEs are RBI's move to end NPCI's monopoly in retail payments. Statement 2 is wrong: the minimum capital is Rs 500 crore, not Rs 100 crore. So '2 only' and 'Both' are wrong, and 'Neither' ignores the correct statement 1.
25.tq: NUE: anti-NPCI-monopoly, Rs 500 crore capital.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **NUEs** are RBI's move to **end NPCI's monopoly in retail payments**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the minimum capital is **Rs 500 cr**, not Rs 100 crore — so option **(1) 1 only** is correct.
xa: NPCI runs **UPI, IMPS, AePS, NACH, RuPay** and BBPS.
RBI itself operates **NEFT and RTGS**.
Nodal body for digital payments now: **Department of Financial Services (Ministry of Finance)**.

25.s: Which of the following correctly states the inauguration details of DBT in Andhra Pradesh?
o: It was inaugurated at Amaravati on 6 January 2016 by UIDAI.
It was inaugurated at Tembhli, Maharashtra, on 29 September 2010.
It was inaugurated at Gollaprolu, East Godavari, on 6 January 2013.
It was inaugurated at Gollaprolu on 1 January 2014 by NPCI.
25.x: DBT was inaugurated at Gollaprolu in East Godavari on 6 January 2013 by Jairam Ramesh along with Chief Minister Kiran Kumar Reddy.
25.tq: Combine venue, district, date and associated persons without swapping the event with Aadhaar.
xs: DBT in AP was **inaugurated at Gollaprolu, East Godavari, on 6 January 2013** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was launched by **Jairam Ramesh** with CM **Kiran Kumar Reddy**.
**Tembhli, 29 Sept 2010** is the **first Aadhaar number**, not the DBT launch — option (2) is wrong.
xa: AP service chain: **e-Seva (2001)** = first integrated citizen service centres in India → **MeeSeva**.
First JAM application = **PAHAL** (LPG subsidy).
DBT Mission now in the **Cabinet Secretariat**.

26.s: The National Optical Fibre Network (NOFN), later associated with BharatNet, was approved on 25 October 2011 with an initial target of connecting:
26.x: NOFN was approved on 25 October 2011 with the objective of connecting 2.5 lakh gram panchayats.
26.tq: Recall the original programme name, date and numerical target together.
xs: **NOFN**, approved on **25 Oct 2011**, aimed to connect **2.5 lakh gram panchayats** — so option **(1)** is correct.
NOFN was the origin of **BharatNet** and was funded by **USOF**.
⚠ **6,44,131** is the number of villages in the **4G coverage** data, not the NOFN target.
xa: SPV **BBNL** was registered on **25 Feb 2012** and **merged with BSNL in Feb 2023**.
Status (**Mar 2025**): **2,18,347 GPs** connected; **6.92 lakh km** OFC.
Target bandwidth: **100 Mbps per GP, scalable to 1 Gbps**.

26.s: Which of the following correctly describes the institutional history of BharatNet's special purpose vehicle?
o: BBNL was registered on 25 February 2012 and merged with BSNL in February 2023.
BBNL was registered on 25 October 2011 and merged with RailTel in February 2023.
BBNL was registered in February 2023 and merged with BSNL in 2012.
BBNL was registered on 25 February 2012 and merged with PGCIL in February 2024.
26.x: Bharat Broadband Network Limited (BBNL) was registered on 25 February 2012 and merged with BSNL in February 2023.
26.tq: Use the sequence of registration and merger to reject swapped dates and organisations.
xs: **BBNL was registered on 25 February 2012 and merged with BSNL in February 2023** — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ **25 Oct 2011** is NOFN's approval date, not BBNL's registration.
**RailTel** and **PGCIL** are implementing CPSUs, not the partner BBNL merged into.
xa: Implementing CPSUs: **BSNL, RailTel, PGCIL**.
⚠ **USOF** → renamed **Digital Bharat Nidhi** (Telecommunications Act **2023**) — same year-cluster as the BBNL merger.
NOFN target: **2.5 lakh GPs**.

26.s: In February 2026, Andhra Pradesh signed a Memorandum of Cooperation under the Amended BharatNet Programme. Which of the following statements about it is correct?
o: It was signed with the Digital Bharat Nidhi Administrator and covers 13,426 village panchayats.
It was signed with BSNL and covers 2.5 lakh gram panchayats.
It was signed with RailTel and covers only 480 new gram panchayats.
It was signed with MeitY and is implemented by AP FiberNet as the Central SPV.
26.x: The MoC (22 Feb 2026, Amaravati) was signed between the Digital Bharat Nidhi Administrator and the AP government for 13,426 village panchayats, with the Centre committing Rs 2,432 crore and the state SPV being Andhra Pradesh BharatNet Infrastructure Ltd. 2.5 lakh GPs was the original NOFN target; 480 new GPs is only one part of the scope; the SPV is a state SPV, not a Central one.
26.tq: AP ABP MoC = DBN + 13,426 panchayats + Rs 2,432 cr.
xs: AP's MoC was **signed with the Digital Bharat Nidhi Administrator** and **covers 13,426 village panchayats** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was signed in **Amaravati** on **22 Feb 2026**; the Centre commits **Rs 2,432 crore**.
The SPV is a **state** SPV — **Andhra Pradesh BharatNet Infrastructure Ltd** — not a Central one; **2.5 lakh GPs** was the NOFN target.
xa: Scope: **1,692** Phase-I GPs upgraded + **11,254** Phase-II villages + **480** new GPs.
AP cabinet cleared the **rollout roadmap**.
**AP FiberNet** reached **4,000+ tribal hamlets** in the **Eastern Ghats**.

26.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. USOF was a lapsable fund meant for telecom in commercially viable urban areas.
2. 5% of Digital Bharat Nidhi collections (about Rs 500 crore a year) go to the Telecom Technology Development Fund.
3. USOF was renamed Digital Bharat Nidhi under the Telecommunications Act, 2023, and Digital Bharat Nidhi runs the Amended BharatNet MoCs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
26.x: Statement 1 is wrong: USOF is a non-lapsable fund for telecom in commercially unviable rural and remote areas (it funded NOFN). Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Hence '2 and 3 only'.
26.tq: USOF -> Digital Bharat Nidhi (2023), non-lapsable.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct, so option **(3)** is correct.
1 is wrong: **USOF** is a **non-lapsable** fund for **commercially unviable rural and remote areas**.
2: **5%** of DBN collections (**~Rs 500 cr/yr**) go to the **Telecom Technology Development Fund** — correct.
3: USOF was renamed **Digital Bharat Nidhi** under the **Telecommunications Act 2023**; DBN runs the **Amended BharatNet MoCs** — correct.
xa: USOF funded **NOFN**.
AP's MoC (**22 Feb 2026**) covers **13,426 village panchayats**; Centre commits **Rs 2,432 crore**.
Implementing CPSUs: **BSNL, RailTel, PGCIL**.

26.s: Which one of the following correctly describes India’s position and electronics trade status mentioned for 2025–26?
o: India is the world’s third-largest mobile maker and electronics is its second-largest export category.
India is the world’s second-largest mobile maker and electronics is its third-largest export category.
India is the world’s first-largest mobile maker and electronics is its third-largest export category.
India is the world’s second-largest mobile maker and electronics is its fifth-largest export category.
26.x: India was described as the world’s second-largest mobile maker, while electronics was identified as the third-largest export category.
26.tq: Check both sides of a paired ranking instead of accepting a partially correct option.
xs: **India is the world's second-largest mobile maker and electronics is its third-largest export category** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Options (1), (3), (4) swap or alter the **2nd** and **3rd** ranks.
xa: Some notes give **Rs 5.25 lakh crore** for 2024-25 for electronics.
**SPECS** = incentive for **electronic components and semiconductors**.
**EMC 2.0** = modified Electronics Manufacturing Clusters (**2020**).

26.s: BharatNet has been laid by which group of Central Public Sector Undertakings?
26.x: The BharatNet network has been laid by the CPSUs BSNL, RailTel and Power Grid Corporation of India Limited (PGCIL).
26.tq: Identify the correct implementing-agency combination rather than a related ministry or institution.
xs: BharatNet was laid by the CPSUs **BSNL, RailTel and PGCIL** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**MeitY, DARPG, NIC, NIELIT, NCERT** are ministries, departments or institutes, not BharatNet's implementing CPSUs.
xa: Phases **I and II** (from **2011**): fibre to GPs through **CPSUs and states**.
SPV **BBNL** merged with **BSNL** in **Feb 2023**.
**6.92 lakh km** of OFC laid by **Mar 2025**.

26.s: The target bandwidth under BharatNet is:
o: 10 Mbps per gram panchayat, scalable to 100 Mbps
100 Mbps per village, fixed without scalability
100 Mbps per gram panchayat, scalable to 1 Gbps
1 Gbps per gram panchayat, scalable to 10 Gbps
26.x: BharatNet targets 100 Mbps for each gram panchayat, with scalability up to 1 Gbps.
26.tq: Distinguish the base capacity from the scalable capacity in a two-number technical target.
xs: BharatNet targets **100 Mbps per gram panchayat, scalable to 1 Gbps** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The network is optical fibre: **6.92 lakh km** OFC by **Mar 2025**.
xa: Amended BharatNet (Phase III) costs **Rs 1.39 lakh crore** and links with **5G**.
**PM-WANI** public Wi-Fi: **3.15 lakh** hotspots; launched Dec **2020**.

26.s:
Consider the following statements about BharatNet:
1. Phases I and II took fibre to gram panchayats through CPSUs and States.
2. Phase III, the Amended BharatNet Programme, has an outlay of Rs 1.39 lakh crore.
3. The Amended BharatNet Programme is implemented only through CPSUs, with no private participation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
26.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Amended BharatNet Programme follows a PPP model with a bigger role for States, revenue sharing and last-mile links with 5G. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
26.tq: ABP = Rs 1.39 lakh crore, PPP.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
1: **Phases I and II** took fibre to GPs through **CPSUs and states** — correct.
2: **Phase III / Amended BharatNet** has **Rs 1.39 lakh crore** outlay — correct.
3 is wrong: Amended BharatNet follows a **PPP model**, bigger role for states, **revenue sharing**.
xa: Origin: **NOFN**, approved **25 Oct 2011** for **2.5 lakh GPs**.
Target: **100 Mbps per GP**, scalable to **1 Gbps**.
**BBNL** was merged with **BSNL** in **Feb 2023**.

26.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

List-I (Programme) — List-II (Description)
a. NDLM — i. Digital literacy scheme preceding PMGDISHA
b. DISHA — ii. Digital Saksharta Abhiyan
c. ICT@Schools — iii. Centrally sponsored scheme for computer labs and ICT learning

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
26.x: NDLM and DISHA refer to the digital literacy initiatives that preceded PMGDISHA, with DISHA expanded as Digital Saksharta Abhiyan. ICT@Schools was a centrally sponsored scheme for computer labs and ICT learning in government schools.
26.tq: Start from the sure acronym expansion and eliminate mismatched programme descriptions.
xs: **a-i, b-ii, c-iii** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**NDLM** = IT-training scheme that came **before PMGDISHA**; **DISHA** = **Digital Saksharta Abhiyan**.
**ICT@Schools** = centrally sponsored scheme for **computer labs + ICT learning** in government schools.
xa: **PMGDISHA**: **6 crore rural households**, **one person per household**, age **14-60**.
**Vidya Vahini** = school project focused on **computer education** (UPPSC **2013**).
**e-Pathshala** = **MHRD + NCERT**, **Nov 2015**.

26.s: MeghRaj refers to which of the following?
o: A public Wi-Fi programme initiated by DoT
A rural optical-fibre programme initiated by BSNL
The GI Cloud initiated by DeitY
A digital-literacy mission initiated by NCERT
26.x: MeghRaj is the GI Cloud initiative started by the Department of Electronics and Information Technology (DeitY).
26.tq: Expand and identify the exact identity and originating authority of an ICT initiative.
xs: **MeghRaj** is **the GI Cloud initiated by DeitY** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It is a common pool of **cloud infrastructure + apps available on demand**.
Public Wi-Fi is **PM-WANI**; rural fibre is **BharatNet**; digital literacy is **PMGDISHA** — not MeghRaj.
xa: ⚠ **5** characteristics - **3** service models - **4** deployment models.
**MeitY** empanels private **Cloud Service Providers** for government use.
ES 2025-26: MeghRaj gives **secure, scalable ICT** for departments.

26.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the five characteristics of cloud computing identified under MeghRaj?
o: Mandatory physical installation for every user
26.x: The five characteristics are on-demand self-service, ubiquitous network access, metered use, elasticity and resource pooling. Mandatory physical installation for every user is not one of them.
26.tq: Find the non-cloud characteristic among the standard feature list.
xs: **Mandatory physical installation for every user** is not a cloud characteristic — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **5** characteristics are **on-demand self-service, ubiquitous network access, metered use, elasticity, resource pooling**.
xa: **3** service models: **IaaS, PaaS, SaaS**.
**4** deployment models: **public, private, hybrid, community**.
Architecture: **national/state clouds** + an **e-Gov App Store**.

26.s: Which of the following is NOT a deployment model of MeghRaj GI Cloud?
26.x: The four deployment models are public, private, hybrid and community cloud. Satellite cloud is not one of the listed deployment models.
26.tq: Use the exact four-item classification and reject the invented category.
xs: **Satellite cloud** is not a MeghRaj deployment model — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **4** deployment models are **public, private, hybrid and community**.
xa: **3** service models: **IaaS, PaaS, SaaS**.
⚠ **5** characteristics - **3** service models - **4** deployment models.
**MeitY** empanels private **Cloud Service Providers**.

26.s: Which of the following correctly describes the architecture and empanelment arrangements under MeghRaj?
o: Only private clouds are permitted and no application store is included.
MeitY empanels private Cloud Service Providers; the architecture includes national and State clouds and an e-Gov App Store.
State governments empanel foreign providers without involvement of MeitY.
The architecture consists only of a single national cloud operated by BSNL.
26.x: MeitY empanels private Cloud Service Providers for government use. The architecture includes national and State clouds along with an e-Gov App Store.
26.tq: Check the responsible authority and the complete architecture rather than accepting a partial description.
xs: **MeitY empanels private Cloud Service Providers**, and the architecture has **national and State clouds and an e-Gov App Store** — so option **(2)** is correct.
So private providers are allowed, an **App Store** exists, and there is more than one cloud — options (1), (3), (4) are wrong.
xa: MeghRaj = **GI Cloud** started by **DeitY**.
**4** deployment models include **public** and **community** clouds, not only private.
ES 2025-26: **secure, scalable ICT** for departments.

26.s:
Consider the following statements about PMGDISHA:
1. It targeted 6 crore rural households, one person per household.
2. It was launched by PM Narendra Modi at Gandhinagar.
3. It covered people aged 18-60 years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
26.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the age group was 14-60 years. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
26.tq: PMGDISHA: 6 crore households, ages 14-60.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
1: **PMGDISHA** targeted **6 crore rural households**, **one person per household** — correct.
2: launched by **PM Modi** at **Gandhinagar** — correct.
3 is wrong: the age group was **14-60**, not 18-60.
xa: PMGDISHA closed on **31 March 2024**: **7.35 crore** registered, **6.39 crore** trained, **4.78 crore** certified.
**NDLM / DISHA** came before PMGDISHA.
**e-Pathshala** (MHRD + NCERT, **Nov 2015**) offers e-textbooks.

26.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the Samriddh Gram pilot location?
26.x: The Samriddh Gram pilots include Narakoduru in Andhra Pradesh, Ari and Umri in Madhya Pradesh, and Chaurawala in Uttar Pradesh.
26.tq: Use location-state matching to distinguish the four pilot sites.
xs: **Narakoduru** is the **Andhra Pradesh** Samriddh Gram pilot — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Ari and Umri** are in **MP**, and **Chaurawala** is in **UP** — so options (2), (3), (4) are mismatched.
xa: Samriddh Gram = **Telecom Centres of Excellence**; agreements **Oct 2025**.
AP **Samriddhi Kendra** at Narakoduru: passport + Aadhaar services, bill payments, soil testing, drone spraying, AI training.
⚠ **Digital Seva Setu** = **Gujarat**, not a Samriddh Gram pilot.

26.s: Digital Seva Setu, which delivers 321 services to over 14,078 gram panchayats through e-Gram centres, is an initiative of which State?
26.x: Digital Seva Setu is Gujarat's initiative delivering 321 services to 14,078+ GPs through e-Gram centres. Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh host Samriddh Gram pilot villages (Narakoduru; Ari and Umri; Chaurawala), not Digital Seva Setu.
26.tq: Digital Seva Setu = Gujarat, e-Gram centres.
xs: **Digital Seva Setu** is a **Gujarat** initiative — so option **(2)** is correct.
It delivers **321 services** to **14,078+ GPs** through **e-Gram centres**.
AP, MP and UP host **Samriddh Gram** pilots, not Digital Seva Setu.
xa: Samriddh Gram villages: **Narakoduru (AP)**, **Ari and Umri (MP)**, **Chaurawala (UP)**.
AP **Samriddhi Kendra** at Narakoduru gives **soil testing** and **drone spraying** among other services.

26.s: Which of the following correctly describes PM-WANI?
o: A digital-literacy programme launched in December 2020, covering 6 crore households.
A fibre-laying programme launched in October 2011, covering 2.5 lakh gram panchayats.
A cloud deployment model launched in March 2024, with 3.15 crore applications.
A public Wi-Fi programme launched in December 2020, with 3.15 lakh hotspots reported.
26.x: PM-WANI is a public Wi-Fi initiative launched in December 2020, with 3.15 lakh hotspots reported.
26.tq: Separate the programme's technology, launch date and scale from other digital initiatives.
xs: **PM-WANI** is **a public Wi-Fi programme launched in December 2020, with 3.15 lakh hotspots** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **6 crore households** target belongs to **PMGDISHA**; the **2011 / 2.5 lakh GPs** target to **NOFN**.
xa: **4G coverage (Dec 2024)**: **6,15,836 of 6,44,131** villages.
About **38%** of Indians are still offline.
BharatNet target: **100 Mbps per GP, scalable to 1 Gbps**.

26.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its focus?
o: e-Pathshala — optical-fibre connectivity to gram panchayats
Vidya Vahini — school project focused on computer education
26.x: Vidya Vahini was a school project focused on computer education. ICT@Schools concerned computer labs and ICT learning, NDLM concerned digital literacy, and e-Pathshala provided digital educational resources.
26.tq: Use nearby education and ICT schemes to detect the swapped programme descriptions.
xs: **Vidya Vahini** is a **school project focused on computer education** — so option **(4)** is correct (UPPSC **2013**).
**e-Pathshala** gives **e-textbooks**; **ICT@Schools** sets up **computer labs**; **NDLM** is a **digital literacy** scheme.
Fibre to GPs is **BharatNet**, and cloud for departments is **MeghRaj**.
xa: **E&ICT Academy Phase-II**: train **1,35,000** faculty through **14** agencies.
**PMGDISHA** closed **31 March 2024**.

26.s:
Consider the following statements about Digital India Bhashini:
1. It is MeitY's National Language Translation Mission, using AI for translation across Indian languages.
2. It is used in DARPG's SAMADHAN DIDI chatbot and NIC's CollabFiles.
3. It is the portal unveiled by NIXI and MeitY on Universal Acceptance Day, 21 March 2024.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
26.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the portal unveiled by NIXI and MeitY on UA Day (21 March 2024) is BhashaNet, not Bhashini. Hence options with 3 are wrong and '1 only' is incomplete.
26.tq: Bhashini = translation mission; BhashaNet = Universal Acceptance portal.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Bhashini** is MeitY's **National Language Translation Mission**, using AI translation.
Statement 2 is correct: it powers DARPG's **SAMADHAN DIDI** chatbot and NIC's **CollabFiles**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the portal unveiled on **21 March 2024** by **NIXI and MeitY** is **BhashaNet** — so option **(2) 1 and 2 only** is correct.
xa: SAMADHAN DIDI covers all **22** Eighth Schedule languages.
**GIGW** = accessibility norms for government websites.

26.s: SPECS, introduced as part of electronics manufacturing promotion, primarily provides incentives for which of the following?
26.x: SPECS is the scheme providing incentives for electronic components and semiconductors.
26.tq: Identify the precise sectoral scope of the scheme.
xs: **SPECS** gives incentives for **electronic components and semiconductors** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Village digital literacy is **PMGDISHA**; tribal hamlet connectivity is **AP FiberNet**; government cloud is **MeghRaj**.
xa: **EMC 2.0** = modified Electronics Manufacturing Clusters (**2020**).
India = **world's 2nd-largest** mobile maker.

26.s: The primary objective of the BhashaNet portal is to promote which of the following?
26.x: BhashaNet was launched to promote digital inclusion by advancing Universal Acceptance, including support for diverse languages and scripts.
26.tq: Match the named initiative with its principal objective rather than a neighbouring ICT programme.
xs: **BhashaNet** promotes **digital inclusion through Universal Acceptance** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was unveiled by **NIXI and MeitY** on **UA Day, 21 March 2024** (asked in **APPSC 2023**).
Cloud is **MeghRaj**; rural fibre is **BharatNet** — not BhashaNet.
xa: **Universal Acceptance** = domain names and e-mail addresses in **any language/script** should work in every application.
⚠ **BhashaNet** (NIXI + MeitY portal) ≠ **Bhashini** (National Language Translation Mission).

26.s: Universal Acceptance means that:
o: domain names and e-mail addresses in any language or script should function in every application
all internet services must be provided free of cost
all citizens must use one standard language on the internet
only government websites should accept Indian-language content
26.x: Universal Acceptance requires domain names and e-mail addresses in any language or script, including Indian-language domains, to work properly in every application.
26.tq: Test the precise definition of a confusable digital-access term.
xs: Universal Acceptance means **domain names and e-mail addresses in any language or script should function in every application** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Example: **Indian-language domains**.
xa: **BhashaNet** portal unveiled by **NIXI and MeitY** on **UA Day, 21 March 2024**.
**Digital India Bhashini** = AI translation across Indian languages (**MeitY**).

26.s: AP FiberNet reached more than 4,000 tribal hamlets in which geographical region?
26.x: AP FiberNet reached more than 4,000 tribal hamlets in the Eastern Ghats.
26.tq: Link the connectivity achievement with its correct geographical location.
xs: **AP FiberNet** reached **4,000+ tribal hamlets** in the **Eastern Ghats** — so option **(3)** is correct.
This is the AP angle of the topic, alongside AP's **Amended BharatNet MoC**.
xa: AP MoC: **13,426 village panchayats**, Centre commits **Rs 2,432 crore**; SPV = **Andhra Pradesh BharatNet Infrastructure Ltd**.
About **38%** of Indians still offline.

26.s: Which guidelines prescribe accessibility norms for Indian Government websites?
26.x: GIGW, or Guidelines for Indian Government Websites, prescribe accessibility norms for government websites.
26.tq: Identify the exact official acronym from closely related digital-governance terms.
xs: **GIGW** (Guidelines for Indian Government Websites) sets accessibility norms for government sites — so option **(1)** is correct.
**PMGDISHA** is digital literacy, **BharatNet** rural fibre, **ICT@Schools** school computer labs.
xa: **PwD access barriers** and the **digital gender gap** persist.
E-governance should offer **assisted access** for the elderly and disabled (UPSC).

27.s:
Consider the following statements about MeeSeva:
1. Category A services are over-the-counter services issued on the spot, such as certified copies.
2. Category B services are statutory services that need notices, hearings or field verification.
3. MeeSeva was launched in 2001 in the combined State of Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
27.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct descriptions of Category A and Category B services. Statement 3 is wrong: MeeSeva was launched in 2011 in the combined State; 2001 is the year of its predecessor e-Seva. So options with 3 are wrong and '1 only' is incomplete.
27.tq: B = statutory (notice, hearing, field verification); A = on the spot.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Category A** = over-the-counter services issued **on the spot**, e.g. certified copies.
Statement 2 is correct: **Category B** = **statutory** services needing **notices, hearings or field verification** (APPSC **2023** key).
Statement 3 is wrong: MeeSeva came in **2011**; **2001** was its predecessor e-Seva — so option **(2) 1 and 2 only** is correct.
xa: **EDS** department **prints MeeSeva certificates**.
Channels: **franchise centres + online portal**.

27.s: Which project succeeded e-Seva as a single-window mechanism for Government-to-Citizen service delivery in Andhra Pradesh?
27.x: MeeSeva succeeded e-Seva as a single-window G2C delivery mechanism.
27.tq: Use the succession relationship to distinguish neighbouring citizen-service platforms.
xs: **MeeSeva** succeeded **e-Seva** as AP's **single-window G2C** delivery mechanism — so option **(1)** is correct.
**AP Online** is a G2C web portal, **e-Office** is NIC's paperless office product, and **APSWAN** is the state-wide area network.
xa: MeeSeva was launched in **2011** in the combined state.
"**MeeSeva**" in Telugu = "**At your service**" (APPSC **2023**).
⚠ **Category A** = on the spot; **Category B** = statutory (notices, hearings, field verification).

27.s: Which of the following departmental functions under MeeSeva is correctly matched?
o: EDS Department — issuing migration certificates to passed candidates
27.x: The EDS Department prints MeeSeva certificates, while the Education Department issues migration certificates to passed candidates.
27.tq: Use the department-function pair and reject the swapped-authority trap.
xs: The **EDS Department prints MeeSeva certificates** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Education** department issues **migration certificates** to passed candidates — so options (1), (2), (4) are mismatched.
xa: In **APPSC 2023**, all three department pairs asked on MeeSeva were correct.
**CARD** is the **Registration Dept's** computer-aided registration of property documents.
**Category B** services are **statutory**.

27.s: The Telugu term 'MeeSeva', the name of Andhra Pradesh's single-window G2C service delivery project, means:
27.x: 'MeeSeva' in Telugu means 'At your service' (asked in APPSC 2023). It is a single-window G2C delivery project, launched in 2011, that succeeded e-Seva. The other renderings are not its meaning.
xs: "**MeeSeva**" in Telugu means "**At your service**" — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC **2023**).
It is AP's single-window **G2C** service project, launched in **2011**, succeeding **e-Seva**.
xa: **Category A** = on-the-spot services; **Category B** = statutory services.
**EDS** department prints MeeSeva certificates.
**Mana Mitra** (**30 Jan 2025**) added **WhatsApp governance**.

27.s: Mana Mitra, launched on 30 January 2025, is associated with which department or institution?
27.x: Mana Mitra is a WhatsApp-governance initiative launched on 30 January 2025 and run by RTGS.
27.tq: Combine the app's launch date with its implementing institution.
xs: **Mana Mitra**, launched **30 Jan 2025**, is run by **RTGS** — so option **(1)** is correct (APPSC **2025**).
**MAUD** runs **Pura Seva**; the **AP Police** runs **Disha SOS** and **AP Police Seva**.
xa: Mana Mitra = **WhatsApp governance**; **150 services (Jan 2025)** → **865** in 2025-26.
⚠ **Pura Seva** does **not** handle electricity bills; Mana Mitra does.

27.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated function of the Pura Seva application?
27.x: Pura Seva is a Municipal Administration and Urban Development application for grievances, building plan approval and vacant land tax; electricity bills are not its stated function.
27.tq: Find the one service belonging outside the municipal-app cluster.
xs: **Electricity bill payment** is not a Pura Seva function — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC **2023**).
Pura Seva (**MAUD**) handles **grievances, building plan approval and vacant land tax**.
xa: ⚠ Electricity bills are handled by **Mana Mitra**, run by **RTGS**.
Mana Mitra services also include **rice card eKYC, 1-B Adangal, APSRTC tickets**.

27.s: Which of the following is included among the pillars of Swarna Andhra @2047?
o: Paper registration of all citizen services
Effective Governance and AI-based Public Services
27.x: “Effective Governance and AI-based Public Services” is one of the pillars of Swarna Andhra @2047.
27.tq: Identify the exact policy phrase rather than a broad but unsupported development objective.
xs: "**Effective Governance and AI-based Public Services**" is a pillar of **Swarna Andhra @2047** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Its monitoring tracks **KPIs** and uses **OBD/IVRS calls + bulk WhatsApp** — the opposite of paper or cash-only systems.
xa: AP has **59 Chief Data Officers**.
**Kaushalam** = AI-powered skill-verification platform.

27.s: The significance of Andhra Pradesh’s e-governance legacy is associated with which combination?
o: The Singapore delegation and the introduction of GPON topology
The APSFL network and the construction of the Eastern Ghats
N. Chandrababu Naidu’s SMART governance model and the HITEC City IT push of 1995–2004
The e-Cabinet initiative of Himachal Pradesh and the IT push of 2019
27.x: Andhra Pradesh’s e-governance legacy is linked with N. Chandrababu Naidu’s SMART governance model and the HITEC City IT push during 1995–2004.
27.tq: Combine the associated person, governance model and time period precisely.
xs: AP's e-governance legacy = **N. Chandrababu Naidu's SMART governance model** and the **HITEC City IT push of 1995–2004** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**e-Cabinet** belongs to **Himachal Pradesh**; the **Singapore delegation** is a 2026 RTGS review.

RTGS reviewed by a **Singapore delegation** (Jul 2026).

27.s: MEDHAS, developed by the NIC-AP State Centre, is an all-in-one solution for which institution?
o: Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences
27.x: MEDHAS is the NIC-AP State Centre's all-in-one solution for Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences.
27.tq: Match the named NIC solution with its user institution.
xs: **MEDHAS** is the NIC-AP State Centre's all-in-one solution for **Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences** — so option **(4)** is correct (APPSC **2023**).
**e-Office** is the NIC product used in the **AP Secretariat**.
xa: **e-Granthalaya** = NIC library management software (**Web OPAC, Unicode**).
**Disha SOS** and **AP Police Seva** are AP Police apps.

27.s: Which of the following services is included among the Mana Mitra services?
27.x: Mana Mitra includes services such as rice card eKYC, electricity bills, 1-B Adangal, APSRTC tickets and temple darshan services.
27.tq: Recognise the listed citizen-facing service rather than an unrelated government function.
xs: **Rice card eKYC** is a Mana Mitra service — so option **(1)** is correct.
Others: **electricity bills, 1-B Adangal, APSRTC tickets, TTD and temple darshan**.

**Rs 22.26 crore** to **21** temples since launch; **Srikalahasti** earned the most.
~**30%** of darshan and seva bookings are made on WhatsApp.

27.s:
Consider the following statements about Mana Mitra, Andhra Pradesh's WhatsApp governance platform:
1. It grew from 150 services in January 2025 to 865 services in 2025-26.
2. Each service is capped at 5 user inputs and 2 documents.
3. Among temples offering darshan and seva bookings through it, Tirumala earned the most.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
27.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Mana Mitra grew from 150 services (Jan 2025) to 865 (2025-26), with a cap of 5 user inputs and 2 documents per service. Statement 3 is wrong: of the Rs 22.26 crore earned by 21 temples, Srikalahasti earned the most. So options with 3 are wrong and '1 only' is incomplete.
27.tq: Mana Mitra: 150 -> 865 services; 5 inputs, 2 docs; Srikalahasti top.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: Mana Mitra grew from **150 services (Jan 2025)** to **865** in 2025-26.
Statement 2 is correct: the cap is **5 user inputs and 2 documents** per service.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Srikalahasti** earned the most, not Tirumala — so option **(2) 1 and 2 only** is correct.
xa: **Rs 22.26 crore** to **21** temples since launch.
~**30%** of darshan and seva bookings come via WhatsApp.

27.s: Which one of the following correctly describes CARD in Andhra Pradesh?
o: State-wide networking of district headquarters and mandals
27.x: CARD is the computer-aided registration system of the Registration Department for property documents.
27.tq: Identify the department-service pair rather than the similar-sounding e-governance project.
xs: **CARD** = **computer-aided registration of property documents** in the Registration Dept — so option **(1)** is correct.
Paperless files = **e-Office**; online tendering = **e-Procurement**; state-wide network = **APSWAN**.
xa: **Registration Service Kendras** (2026): property registration on the **Passport Seva Kendra** model.
**AP Online** = web portal for G2C services.

27.s: Registration Service Kendras in Andhra Pradesh are modelled on which of the following, while statutory powers continue to remain with the Sub-Registrar Offices?
27.x: Registration Service Kendras provide property-registration services on the Passport Seva Kendra model, but statutory powers remain with the SROs.
27.tq: Separate the service-delivery model from the authority retaining statutory powers.
xs: **Registration Service Kendras** follow the **Passport Seva Kendra model**; statutory powers stay with **SROs** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**HIMSWAN** is Himachal's network, not a registration model.
xa: Debate: **document writers' livelihoods** under RSKs, and the State's assurance that **SROs are not being privatised**.
**CARD** = computer-aided registration of property documents.

27.s: The Andhra Pradesh Cyber Security Policy was formulated in which year, and what is its central objective?
o: 2015; to promote paperless cabinet meetings only
2017; to create a secure cyber ecosystem for citizens, businesses and government
2021; to provide online tendering across departments
2019; to establish municipal service centres only
27.x: The AP Cyber Security Policy was formulated in 2017 to establish a secure cyber ecosystem for citizens, businesses and government.
27.tq: Link the policy year with its stated broad coverage.
xs: The **AP Cyber Security Policy 2017** aims at **a secure cyber ecosystem for citizens, businesses and government** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Paperless cabinet is **e-Cabinet** (Himachal); online tendering is **e-Procurement**.
xa: **Kaushalam** = AI-powered employability and skill-verification platform.

xa: **Swarna Andhra @2047** has "**Effective Governance and AI-based Public Services**" as a pillar.
**AP Cyber Security Policy 2017**.

27.s: Which of the following represents a criticism or debate concerning Registration Service Kendras?
o: Their replacement of IPTV by satellite radio and voice services
Their possible effect on document writers’ livelihoods and the assurance that SROs are not being privatised
Their exclusive operation by the Singapore delegation
Their restriction to only 50 government services

xs: The RSK debate is about **document writers' livelihoods** and the assurance that **SROs are not being privatised** — so option **(2)** is correct.
RSKs do property registration on the **Passport Seva Kendra** model; statutory powers stay with **SROs**.
xa: **CARD** = computer-aided registration of property documents.
RSKs appear in current relevance for **Jul 2026**.

27.s: Which State was the first in India to introduce e-Cabinet as a paperless cabinet system?
27.x: Himachal Pradesh was the first State to introduce the paperless e-Cabinet system.
27.tq: Apply the state-project association without confusing it with other state digital platforms.
xs: **Himachal Pradesh** was the first state with a paperless **e-Cabinet** — so option **(1)** is correct (APPSC **2025**).
**Gujarat** is known for **Digital Seva Setu** and **GSWAN**; **Karnataka** for **Seva One**.
xa: Other HP projects: **HIMSWAN**, **Himachal Online Seva**, **Helpline 1100**.
⚠ First **e-Cabinet** = **Himachal Pradesh**.

27.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. HIMSWAN — Himachal Pradesh
2. Digital Seva Setu — Gujarat
3. Seva One — Karnataka
4. GSWAN — Gujarat

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
27.x: HIMSWAN belongs to Himachal Pradesh; Digital Seva Setu and GSWAN belong to Gujarat; and Seva One is Karnataka's digital citizen-services initiative.

xs: All four pairs match — so option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4** is correct.
**HIMSWAN** = Himachal Pradesh; **Digital Seva Setu** and **GSWAN** = Gujarat; **Seva One** = Karnataka (**Sept 2026**).
