xs: Agni is built by **DRDO**, is **fully indigenous** and is operated by the **Strategic Forces Command** — option **(1)**.
⚠ "**ISRO**" as developer is wrong (APPSC **2019**).
It uses its own **specialised navigation** for accuracy.
xa: In **Aug 2026**, conventional missiles (incl. **Nag**) went to private industry via ToT; **Agni** stays in **state production**.
Agni means **Fire**.
**Mission Divyastra (2024)**: Agni-V with **MIRV**.

48.s:
Consider the following statements about Trishul:
1. It is a short-range, quick-reaction surface-to-air missile.
2. It was inducted into the Army in 2008.
3. It flew above Mach 2 using solid propellant with thrust vector control.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
48.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Trishul was never inducted; the programme was shut on 27 Feb 2008 after failing operational requirements, delays and cost overruns. So '1 and 3 only'.
48.tq: Trishul = the IGMDP missile never inducted.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(4)**.
Statement 1 is correct: **Trishul** is a short-range **quick-reaction SAM**.
Statement 2 is wrong: Trishul was **never inducted**; the programme was shut on **27 Feb 2008**.
Statement 3 is correct: speed **above Mach 2**, **solid propellant + thrust vector control**.
xa: ⚠ Replacements: **Spyder** (IAF), **Barak-1** (Navy), **Akash** (Army).
Indigenous successor: **QRSAM**.
Trishul's range: ~**9 km** (some notes **12 km**).

48.s: What is meant by the term 'fire-and-forget' in missile technology?
o: The missile is incapable of changing its course after launch.
The missile can guide itself after launch, allowing the operator to take cover.
The missile is fired only after the target has been destroyed by another weapon.
The missile must remain continuously controlled by the operator until impact.
48.x: A fire-and-forget missile guides itself after launch, enabling the operator to seek cover or perform another task.
48.tq: Translate the technical term into its operational consequence.
xs: **Fire-and-forget**: the missile **guides itself after launch**, so the operator can **take cover** — option **(2)**.
Examples: **Nag**, **HELINA**, **MPATGM**.
xa: **Top attack**: missile climbs, then dives onto the tank's thin **top armour**.
**Nag** has both **top-attack** and **direct-attack** modes.
Nag is a **third-generation** fire-and-forget ATGM (APPSC-G1 **2018** key).

48.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
48.x: Nag uses an Imaging Infra-Red seeker, whereas Akash Prime uses an active RF seeker and SANT uses Lock-On After Launch. Therefore, Nag with an active RF seeker is not correctly matched.
48.tq: Find the one swapped seeker associated with a different missile.
xs: **Nag — active RF seeker** is wrongly matched — option **(4)**.
Nag uses an **Imaging Infra-Red (IIR)** seeker; the **active RF seeker** belongs to **Akash Prime**.
**SANT** uses **Lock-On After Launch** — correctly matched.
xa: **Akash Prime** = upgraded **Akash Mk-I**, first tested **27 Sep 2021**.
**Akash Mk-I** uses command guidance with the **Rajendra radar**.
Other guidance types: **laser**, **GPS**, **electro-optical**.

48.s: Which one of the following is NOT an identified spin-off of the IGMDP?
48.x: Long-range tracking systems, composites, ring laser gyros and radomes were identified as IGMDP spin-offs. A satellite-based navigation constellation is not included in this list.
48.tq: Find the item outside the stated group of technological spin-offs.
xs: A **satellite-based navigation constellation** is not listed among IGMDP spin-offs — option **(1)**.
The listed spin-offs are the **long-range tracking system**, **composites**, **ring laser gyros** and **radomes**.
xa: **Agni-IV** uses a **ring-laser-gyro INS** with **RINS + MINGS** navigation.
IGMDP was **launched in 1983** and **completed in 2008**.
Nodal lab: **DRDL Hyderabad**.

48.s:
With reference to Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, consider the following statements:
1. He was the project director of SLV-III, which launched Rohini.
2. He was the Chief Scientific Adviser at the Pokhran-I test of 1974.
3. He was the first Indian Head of State to fly a fighter aircraft.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
48.x: Statement 1 is correct: Kalam was project director of SLV-III (Rohini). Statement 2 is wrong: he was Chief Scientific Adviser at Pokhran in 1998 (Pokhran-II), not 1974. Statement 3 is correct: he was the first Indian Head of State to fly a fighter. So '1 and 3 only' is right; '1 and 2 only', '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' all wrongly include statement 2.
48.tq: Kalam's Pokhran role is 1998 (Pokhran-II); Pokhran-I (1974) was led by Raja Ramanna.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: Kalam was project director of **SLV-III** (**Rohini**).
Statement 2 is wrong: he was Chief Scientific Adviser at **Pokhran 1998**, not 1974.
Statement 3 is correct: he was the **first Indian Head of State to fly a fighter**.
xa: Kalam led **IGMDP** from **1983** and is called the "**Missile Man of India**".
⚠ **Dr Tessy Thomas** = "**Missile Woman of India**" / **Agniputri**.
**Pokhran Field Firing Range** is in **Rajasthan**.

48.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Prithvi missile:
1. Prithvi was the first missile developed under the IGMDP.
2. Prithvi-I is operated by the Army.
3. Prithvi-II is operated by the Air Force.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
48.x: All three statements are correct. Prithvi was the first IGMDP missile; Prithvi-I serves the Army and Prithvi-II serves the Air Force.
48.tq: Use service allocation and the first-development distinction together.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **Prithvi** was the **first IGMDP missile**.
Statement 2: **Prithvi-I** serves the **Army**.
Statement 3: **Prithvi-II** serves the **Air Force**.
xa: **Prithvi-III / Dhanush** serves the **Navy** (ship-launched).
Prithvi-II was **first tested in 1996** and **inducted in 2003**.
Prithvi-II and Agni-I were **test-fired together** (**Jul 2025**).

48.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Prithvi-I, Prithvi-II and Agni-I are nuclear-capable.
2. The Army fires these missiles from mobile transporter-erector-launcher trucks.
3. All three use liquid fuel.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
48.x: The first two statements are correct. Agni-I uses solid fuel, whereas Prithvi-I and Prithvi-II use liquid fuel; therefore statement 3 is false.
48.tq: Separate the common operational feature from the differing propulsion feature.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **Prithvi-I, Prithvi-II and Agni-I** are all **nuclear-capable**.
Statement 2: the **Army** fires them from **road-mobile TEL trucks**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Prithvi** is **liquid**-fuelled but **Agni** is **solid**-fuelled.
xa: Prithvi-II and Agni-I were test-fired together in **Jul 2025**.
**Agni-I**: single-stage solid, about **700-800 km**, about **15 m** long.
An **Agni-1** test was held at **ITR Balasore** on **22 May 2026**.

48.s: Agni-I is best described as a:
o: Two-stage liquid-fuel missile of about 2,000–3,000 km range
Single-stage solid-fuel missile of about 700–800 km range
Single-stage liquid-fuel missile of about 150 km range
Three-stage solid-fuel missile of about 5,000 km range
48.x: Agni-I is a single-stage solid-fuel missile with a range of about 700–800 km and is approximately 15 metres long.
48.tq: Identify the missile from its stage, fuel and range combination.
xs: **Agni-I** is a **single-stage solid-fuel** missile of about **700-800 km** range — option **(2)**.
It is about **15 m** long, with accurate navigation.
**2,000-3,000 km** is **Agni-II** (two-stage solid); **150 km** liquid is **Prithvi-I**; **5,000 km** three-stage is **Agni-V**.
xa: Agni-I is **nuclear-capable**, fired by the Army from **road-mobile TEL** trucks.
Agni-I test: **ITR Balasore**, **22 May 2026**.
⚠ Some notes give Agni-I as **~700-900 km** (SRBM/MRBM).

48.s:
Consider the following statements about the Agni series:
1. Agni-IV (about 4,000 km) is a three-stage solid-fuel missile.
2. Agni-II (2,000-3,000 km) is a two-stage solid-fuel missile.
3. Agni-III (about 3,500 km) is a two-stage solid-fuel missile.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
48.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Agni-IV is a two-stage, road-mobile solid-fuel missile; three-stage, canister-launched propulsion is Agni-V. So '2 and 3 only'.
48.tq: Agni-I single stage; II, III, IV two-stage; V three-stage.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — option **(4)**.
Statement 1 is wrong: **Agni-IV** (~**4,000 km**) is a **two-stage** solid, road-mobile missile; **three-stage** is **Agni-V**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Agni-II** (**2,000-3,000 km**) is two-stage solid.
Statement 3 is correct: **Agni-III** (**3,000-3,500 km**) is two-stage solid.
xa: **Agni-I**: single-stage solid, about **700-800 km**.
**Agni-V**: **5,000+ km**, canisterised, **MIRV** tested (Mission Divyastra, 2024).
⚠ The Agni series is developed by **DRDO**, not ISRO (APPSC 2019).

48.s:
Consider the following statements about Agni-V:
1. It is a three-stage solid-fuel missile.
2. It is canister-launched.
3. Its range is stated as 5,000 km or more.
4. MIRV technology has been tested with it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
48.x: Agni-V is a three-stage solid-fuel, canister-launched missile with a stated range of 5,000 km or more, and MIRV capability has been tested with it.
48.tq: Combine propulsion, launch mode, range and payload-technology clues.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
Agni-V is **three-stage solid**, **canister-launched**, with range **5,000+ km**.
**MIRV** was tested on it in **Mission Divyastra (2024)**.
xa: Agni-V is **fully indigenous** — ⚠ "not exclusively indigenous" is the wrong statement (UPPSC **2015**).
**Dr Tessy Thomas** played a key role in Agni-V.
⚠ Formally **IRBM** class: the ICBM threshold is **5,500 km**.

48.s:
Consider the following statements about Agni-Prime:
1. It is a new-generation canisterised missile with a range of 1,000-2,000 km.
2. On 24 September 2025 it was fired from a submarine.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
48.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: on 24 Sep 2025 Agni-Prime was fired from a rail-based mobile launcher. So '1 only'.
48.tq: Agni-P: canisterised, 1,000-2,000 km, rail launcher (2025).
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**: **Agni-P (Prime)** is a new-generation **canisterised** missile of **1,000-2,000 km**.
Statement 2 is wrong: on **24 Sep 2025** it was fired from a **rail-based mobile launcher**, not a submarine.
xa: Agni series operator: **Strategic Forces Command**.
**Agni-4** user trial: **ITR Chandipur, 6 Aug 2026**.
An advanced Agni with **MIRV** was tested on **8 May 2026**.

48.s: Mission Divyastra is associated with which one of the following developments?
o: Testing of MIRV capability on Agni-V in 2024
Development of the Akash missile’s liquid-fuel engine
48.x: Mission Divyastra, conducted in 2024, involved Agni-V with Multiple Independently targetable Re-entry Vehicles (MIRVs).
48.tq: Associate the named mission with its specific missile technology.
xs: **Mission Divyastra (2024)** tested **Agni-V** with **MIRV** (Multiple Independently targetable Re-entry Vehicles) — option **(1)**.
It put India in a **small club of MIRV states**.
**Trishul** was never inducted (closed **2008**); **Akash** is not liquid-fuelled; Prithvi-II's first test (**1996**) is unrelated.
xa: Advanced Agni with a **MIRV** was tested on **8 May 2026**.
Agni-V: **three-stage solid**, **canister-launched**, **5,000+ km**.
All 2026 Agni tests were under the **Strategic Forces Command**.

48.s:

3. The LRAShM is an example of a missile associated with such trials.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.

48.tq: Combine geographic location with the operational use of the coastal ranges.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **AP/Odisha coastal ranges** are used for **sea-skimming missile trials**.
Statement 2: **Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island** lies **off the Odisha coast**.
Statement 3: **LRAShM** (**Jan 2026**) is the example given.

**ITR Chandipur** is at **Balasore, Odisha**.

48.s:
Consider the following systems:
1. Pinaka
2. Tejas
3. Lakshya
4. Nishant
Which of the above are not missiles?
48.x: Pinaka is a multi-barrel rocket launcher, Tejas is an aircraft, Lakshya is a target drone, and Nishant is a UAV; none is a missile.
48.tq: Classify each named defence system by its platform or role.
xs: None of the four is a missile — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Pinaka** = multi-barrel **rocket launcher**; **Tejas** = **aircraft**.
**Lakshya** = **target drone**; **Nishant** = **UAV**.
xa: **Arjun** = tank; **Rustom** = UAV; **NAMICA** = Nag carrier vehicle.

48.s: The Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme is regarded as significant because it:
o: Ended all missile development in India after the completion of Prithvi.
Turned India from a missile importer into a missile-exporting power and formed a base for later Agni-V MIRV, BMD and BrahMos-era programmes.
Restricted India to importing surface-to-air missiles from foreign suppliers.
Was created exclusively for developing civilian launch vehicles.
48.x: The IGMDP transformed India from a missile importer into a missile-exporting power and provided the foundation for Agni-V MIRV, ballistic missile defence and BrahMos-era programmes.
48.tq: Select the option that captures both the strategic transformation and the later technological base.
xs: IGMDP turned India from a **missile importer** into a **missile-exporting power**, and laid the base for **Agni-V MIRV, BMD and BrahMos-era programmes** — option **(2)**.
Missile work did not end: after **2008**, later missiles came as **separate projects**.
xa: Launched in **1983** under **Dr APJ Abdul Kalam**, after the **1962, 1965, 1971** wars.
**Mission Divyastra (2024)**: Agni-V with **MIRV**.
Spin-offs: **long-range tracking system**, **composites**, **ring laser gyros**, **radomes**.

48.s:
With reference to Prithvi-II, consider the following statements:
1. It was first tested in 1996.
2. It was inducted in 2003.
3. It is a naval, ship-launched missile.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
48.x: Prithvi-II was first tested in 1996 and inducted in 2003. The naval, ship-launched version is Dhanush, not Prithvi-II.
48.tq: Spot the swapped variant in a three-statement question.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: Prithvi-II was **first tested in 1996**.
Statement 2 is correct: it was **inducted in 2003**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the naval ship-launched version is **Dhanush**, not Prithvi-II (an **Air Force** missile).
xa: Prithvi-II: **350 km**, payload **500-1,000 kg**, **nuclear-capable SRBM**.
Dhanush means **Bow**.
**PAD / Pradyumna** is the Prithvi-based exo-atmospheric interceptor.

48.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Dhanush is the naval, ship-launched version of the Prithvi missile.
2. Prithvi Air Defence (PAD/Pradyumna) is an exo-atmospheric interceptor operating at about 50–80 km altitude.
3. Prithvi-I is operated by the Navy and has a range of 350 km.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
48.x: Statement 1 is correct: Dhanush (Prithvi-III) is the Navy's ship-launched Prithvi (UPSC). Statement 2 is correct: PAD/Pradyumna intercepts exo-atmospherically at 50–80 km. Statement 3 is wrong: Prithvi-I is the Army's 150 km version; 350 km is Prithvi-II of the Air Force. So B; A leaves out statement 2, while C and D include the wrong statement 3.
48.tq: Prithvi-I Army 150 km; II Air Force 350 km; Dhanush Navy.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **Dhanush** (Prithvi-III) is the **naval, ship-launched** Prithvi.
Statement 2: **PAD / Pradyumna** is an **exo-atmospheric** interceptor at **50-80 km** altitude.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Prithvi-I** is the **Army**'s **150 km** missile; **350 km** is Prithvi-II (**Air Force**).
xa: Prithvi-I carries up to **1,000 kg**.
**Dr V.K. Saraswat** led the **ballistic missile defence** programme.
Prithvi-II: tested **1996**, inducted **2003**.

48.s:
Consider the following statements about Akash Prime:

2. It is an upgraded Akash Mk-I with an indigenous active RF seeker.
3. It is a canister-launched variant with a range of about 70 km.

48.x: Statement 3 is wrong: the canister-launched ~70 km variant is Akash-NG; Akash Prime has a range of 25-30 km. Statements 1 and 2 are correct (APPSC 2021 key). So '1 and 2 only'.
48.tq: Akash Prime = RF seeker (2021); Akash-NG = canister, ~70 km.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: **Akash Prime** was first tested on **27 Sep 2021** (APPSC 2021 key).
Statement 2 is correct: it is **Akash Mk-I** upgraded with an **indigenous active RF seeker**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **canister-launched ~70 km** variant is **Akash-NG**; Akash Prime reaches **25-30 km**.
xa: Akash Prime destroyed high-speed targets at high altitude in **Ladakh**.
Base Akash: **Mach 2.5**, altitude **18 km**.
⚠ **Akashteer** is an air-defence **control** system, not a missile.

48.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Akash-NG:
1. It is a canister-launched missile.
2. Its approximate range is 70 km.
3. It was cleared for induction in 2023 for both the Army and the Indian Air Force.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
48.x: Akash-NG is canister-launched, has an approximate range of 70 km, and was cleared for induction in 2023 by both the Army and the IAF.
48.tq: Verify each statement against the variant’s launch method, range and induction status.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Akash-NG** is **canister-launched** and quick-reaction.
Its range is about **70 km**, and it was cleared for induction in **2023** (**Army and IAF**).
xa: **Akash Mk-I** ~**25 km**; **Akash Prime** **25-30 km**; **Akash S1** **30-35 km**.

48.s: Which of the following statements regarding Nag variants is correct?
o: NAMIS is a tracked tank killer approved for Army procurement.
Dhruvastra is a ship-launched version of Prithvi.
SANT is a helicopter-launched Nag used by Army Aviation.
MPATGM is a canister-launched Akash variant.
48.x: Nag Mk-2 (NAMIS) is the tracked fire-and-forget 'tank killer' approved for Army procurement. Dhruvastra is the helicopter-launched Nag for the IAF (the ship-launched Prithvi is Dhanush); SANT is an air-launched stand-off ATGM with Lock-On After Launch (HELINA is the Army Aviation version); MPATGM is a man-portable Nag-family ATGM, not an Akash variant.
48.tq: Use the named-variant and platform distinction to avoid swapped identities.
xs: **Nag Mk-2 / NAMIS** is a tracked "**tank killer**", fire-and-forget, **approved for Army procurement** — option **(1)**.
**Dhruvastra** is the helicopter-launched Nag for the **IAF**; the ship-launched Prithvi is **Dhanush**.
**SANT** is an **air-launched stand-off ATGM** (Lock-On After Launch); **MPATGM** is a **man-portable** Nag variant.
xa: **NAMICA** = tracked amphibious **Nag Missile Carrier**, carries up to **six** missiles.
**HELINA** (about **7 km**) is for **Army Aviation**.
**SANT** range: **15-20 km**.

48.s: HELINA and Dhruvastra are respectively associated with:
o: The Indian Air Force and the Navy
Army Aviation and the Indian Air Force
48.x: HELINA is the helicopter-launched Nag variant for Army Aviation, whereas Dhruvastra is intended for the Indian Air Force.
48.tq: Discriminate between closely related helicopter-launched Nag variants by service.
xs: **HELINA** is for **Army Aviation**; **Dhruvastra** is for the **IAF** — option **(4)**.
Both are **helicopter-launched Nag** variants of about **7 km** range.
xa: ⚠ Remember: **HELINA** = Army Aviation; **Dhruvastra** = IAF.
HELINA is a **fire-and-forget** missile, like Nag and MPATGM.
**SANT** is the **air-launched stand-off** ATGM (**15-20 km**).

48.s:
Consider the following systems:
1. Nag
2. HELINA
3. MPATGM
4. Akash Prime
Which of the above are fire-and-forget systems?
48.x: Nag, HELINA (helicopter-launched Nag) and MPATGM are the listed fire-and-forget anti-tank missiles. Akash Prime is a surface-to-air missile (upgraded Akash Mk-I with an active RF seeker), not one of the fire-and-forget ATGMs. So C.
48.tq: Separate the fire-and-forget group from a seeker-based surface-to-air system.
xs: **Nag**, **HELINA** and **MPATGM** are fire-and-forget — option **(3) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
**Akash Prime** is a **SAM** (upgraded Akash Mk-I with an active RF seeker), not a fire-and-forget ATGM.
xa: Nag: **IIR** seeker and an **8 kg HEAT tandem warhead**.
**NAMIS** (Nag Mk-2) is also fire-and-forget — the tracked "**tank killer**".
⚠ "Which is a fire-and-forget anti-tank missile?" → **Nag** (not Prithvi, Akash or Trishul).

48.s:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding the Nag missile system?
1. It carries an 8 kg HEAT tandem warhead.
2. Each NAMICA can carry up to six missiles.
3. The Nag Missile Carrier is tracked and amphibious.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
48.x: Nag carries an 8 kg HEAT tandem warhead; NAMICA can carry up to six missiles; and the Nag Missile Carrier is a tracked amphibious vehicle.
48.tq: Combine warhead, carriage capacity and vehicle characteristics in one system-level question.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: Nag carries an **8 kg HEAT tandem warhead**.
Statement 2: each **NAMICA** carries **up to six missiles**.
Statement 3: NAMICA is the **tracked amphibious Nag Missile Carrier** of the Army.
xa: Nag is a **third-generation fire-and-forget ATGM** (APPSC-G1 **2018** key), range **4-7 km**.
Its **Imaging Infra-Red (IIR)** seeker gives **night-strike** capability.
**Nag Mk-2 / NAMIS** — tracked "**tank killer**", approved for Army procurement (**2026**).
⚠ NAMICA is a **carrier vehicle**, not a missile.

48.s: Dr Tessy Thomas is associated with which combination of descriptions?
o: Missile Woman of India, key role in Agni-V and “Agniputri”
Missile Man of India, leadership of IGMDP and SLV-III
Former DRDO chief, leadership of Prithvi and BMD
Chairman of DRDO, leadership of Akash Tarang and MPATGM
48.x: Dr Tessy Thomas is known as the “Missile Woman of India”, played a key role in Agni-V and is called “Agniputri”.
48.tq: Use the unique title-and-project combination to identify the correct person.
xs: **Dr Tessy Thomas** is the "**Missile Woman of India**", played a key role in **Agni-V** and is called "**Agniputri**" — option **(1)**.
"Missile Man", IGMDP and SLV-III describe **Dr APJ Abdul Kalam**; Prithvi and BMD describe **Dr V.K. Saraswat**.
The current **DRDO Chairman** is **Samir V. Kamat**.
xa: **Agni-V**: **three-stage solid**, **canister-launched**, range **5,000+ km**, **MIRV** tested.
**Mission Divyastra (2024)** tested Agni-V with **MIRVs**.
Agni is operated by the **Strategic Forces Command**.

48.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island — Rajasthan
Integrated Test Range, Chandipur — Andhra Pradesh
48.x: The Pokhran Field Firing Range is in Rajasthan. The Kurnool DRDO range is in Andhra Pradesh, while Chandipur and Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island are in Odisha.
48.tq: Use state-location matching and distinguish inland ranges from coastal ranges.
xs: **Pokhran Field Firing Range — Rajasthan** is correct — option **(1)**.
The **Kurnool** range is in **Andhra Pradesh**, not Odisha.
**Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island** and **ITR Chandipur** (Balasore) are both in **Odisha**.
xa: Kalam Island was formerly **Wheeler Island**.
Kurnool range hosted the **ULPGM-V3** trials (**2026**).
Kalam was Chief Scientific Adviser at **Pokhran 1998**.

48.s: Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island was formerly known as:
48.x: Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island was formerly known as Wheeler Island and lies off the Odisha coast.
48.tq: Recognise the renamed test location from its former name.
xs: **Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island** was formerly **Wheeler Island** — option **(4)**.
It lies **off the Odisha coast**.
**Chandipur** is the **Integrated Test Range** at Balasore; **Pokhran** is a field firing range in Rajasthan.
xa: **Agni-4** user trial: **ITR Chandipur**, **6 Aug 2026**.
**Agni-1** test: **ITR Balasore**, **22 May 2026**.
Kalam is the "**Missile Man of India**", who led IGMDP from **1983**.

48.s:
Consider the following statements about the Missile Technology Control Regime (MTCR):
1. India joined it in June 2018.
2. Membership has eased India's BrahMos exports and high-tech imports.
3. It covers missiles and UAVs able to carry a 500 kg payload over 300 km.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
48.x: Statement 1 is wrong: India joined the MTCR in June 2016 as its 35th member (China is not a member). Statements 2 and 3 are correct. So '2 and 3 only'.
48.tq: MTCR: India June 2016, 35th member; 500 kg / 300 km.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is wrong: India joined the **MTCR** in **June 2016** as its **35th member**.
Statement 2 is correct: membership eased **BrahMos exports** and high-tech imports.
Statement 3 is correct: MTCR covers missiles & UAVs carrying **500 kg over 300 km**.
xa: **China** is not an MTCR member.
**ITR Chandipur** (Balasore) and **Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island** are off/in **Odisha**.
The MTCR is an **informal export-control regime**.

48.s: Regarding the classification of Agni-V, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
o: It is classified as an SRBM because it is canister-launched.
It is a proposed missile and has not been associated with MIRV testing.
Its stated 5,000 km range is formally in the IRBM class, although some sources call it an ICBM.
Its 5,000 km range is formally above the 5,500 km ICBM threshold.
48.x: The stated range of Agni-V is 5,000 km or more, while the formal ICBM threshold cited is 5,500 km. Therefore it is formally in the IRBM class in that classification, although some sources call it an ICBM.
48.tq: Separate informal descriptions from the stated technical threshold.
xs: Agni-V's stated **5,000 km** range is formally **IRBM** class, though some sources call it an **ICBM** — option **(3)**.
The **ICBM threshold** is **5,500 km**, so 5,000 km is below it — option (4) is wrong.
It is not an **SRBM**, and **MIRV** was tested on it (**Mission Divyastra, 2024**).
xa: **Agni-VI** is the **proposed longer-range ICBM**.
Agni-V is **three-stage solid** and **canister-launched**.
Advanced Agni with a **MIRV** was tested on **8 May 2026**.

48.s: In the top-attack mode, a missile generally:
o: Climbs and dives onto the tank’s relatively thin top armour
Tracks the missile carrier rather than the target
Approaches only from the rear at ground level
Uses a ship-based launcher to strike aircraft
48.x: In top attack, the missile climbs and then dives onto the tank’s thinner top armour. Nag has both top-attack and direct-attack modes.
48.tq: Infer the tactical advantage from the direction of attack and armour vulnerability.
xs: In **top attack**, the missile **climbs and dives onto the tank's thin top armour** — option **(1)**.
**Nag** has both **top-attack and direct-attack modes**.
xa: Nag's **IIR** seeker gives **night-strike** capability.
**SANT** uses a **Lock-On After Launch** seeker.
Not missiles: **Arjun** (tank), **Pinaka** (rocket launcher), **NAMICA** (Nag carrier).

48.s: Which statement regarding BrahMos is correct?
o: It replaced Trishul in the Indian Army under the IGMDP.
It was the first missile project formally completed under the IGMDP in 2008.
It is a non-missile target drone associated with the IGMDP.
It was not part of the IGMDP, although it is sometimes listed alongside IGMDP missiles.
48.x: BrahMos, developed jointly by India and Russia, was not part of the IGMDP, though it may be listed next to IGMDP missiles.
48.tq: Separate an associated missile programme from the formal IGMDP group.
xs: **BrahMos** was **not part of IGMDP**, though some notes list it with IGMDP missiles — option **(4)**.
It is an **India-Russia** project.
Trishul's Army replacement was **Akash**, not BrahMos.
xa: **MTCR** membership (**June 2016**) eased **BrahMos exports**.
IGMDP's five missiles: **Prithvi, Agni, Akash, Trishul, Nag**.
IGMDP was **completed in 2008**.

49.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes a ballistic missile from a cruise missile?
o: A ballistic missile is powered throughout its flight, whereas a cruise missile is powered only during boost phase.
A ballistic missile follows a high parabolic trajectory after boost, whereas a cruise missile remains powered and generally flies at low altitude using aerodynamic lift.
A ballistic missile uses only aerodynamic lift, whereas a cruise missile follows a free-fall arc.
Both ballistic and cruise missiles follow the same powered, low-altitude trajectory.
49.x: A ballistic missile is powered mainly during the boost phase and subsequently follows a high parabolic or free-fall trajectory. A cruise missile is powered throughout its flight and uses aerodynamic lift while flying at relatively low altitude.
49.tq: Use the propulsion and flight-path contrast to separate the two missile classes.
xs: A **ballistic missile** is rocket-powered only in the **boost phase**, then follows a **high parabolic path**; a **cruise missile** stays **powered throughout** and flies low using **aerodynamic lift** — option **(2)**.
Option (1) reverses the two; option (3) wrongly gives lift to the ballistic missile.
Cruise missiles are **air-breathing** and fly at **constant speed** and **low altitude**.
xa: Ballistic examples: **Agni**, **Prithvi**, **Pralay**.
Cruise examples: **BrahMos**, **Nirbhay**.
⚠ **Pralay** is **quasi-ballistic** with **manoeuvrable re-entry**.

49.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: MPATGM — Third-generation fire-and-forget anti-tank guided missile
Prahaar — About 150 km tactical ballistic missile
VSHORADS — Man-portable air-defence system against low-altitude threats
49.x: LRGB Gaurav is a 1,000 kg glide bomb with a range of about 100 km, released from the Su-30MKI. The 120 km guided rocket is Pinaka LRGR-120.
49.tq: Find the swapped identity between two nearby weapon systems.
xs: **LRGB Gaurav — 120 km guided rocket** is wrong — option **(3)**.
**LRGB 'Gaurav'** is a **1,000 kg glide bomb**, ~**100 km**, released from the **Su-30MKI** (**Apr 2025**).
The **120 km** guided rocket is **Pinaka LRGR-120**, first flown **29 Dec 2025**.
xa: **Prahaar**: ~**150 km** tactical ballistic missile.
**MPATGM**: man-portable, third-generation **fire-and-forget**.
**VSHORADS**: man-portable defence against **low-altitude threats**.

49.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Hypersonic speed means speed faster than Mach 3.
2. The manoeuvrability of an HGV makes it hard to intercept.
3. A Hypersonic Glide Vehicle is rocket-boosted and then glides at Mach 5+ while manoeuvring in the upper atmosphere.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: Statement 1 is wrong: hypersonic means faster than Mach 5. Statements 2 and 3 are correct. So '2 and 3 only'.
49.tq: Hypersonic = Mach 5+.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is wrong: **hypersonic** means faster than **Mach 5**.
Statements 2 and 3 are correct: an **HGV** is rocket-boosted, **glides at Mach 5+** and manoeuvres, so it is **hard to intercept**.
xa: **HSTDV** = indigenous **scramjet** demonstrator, flew at **Mach 6+**.
**LR-AShM**: ~**1,500 km**, peak **Mach 10**, average **Mach 5**.
India's **first long-range hypersonic missile** flew on **16 Nov 2024**.

49.s: Which of the following is the correct description of a scramjet?
o: A solid-fuel motor designed only for submarine-launched missiles.
A jet engine in which combustion occurs at subsonic speed after the air is completely stopped.
A propulsion system using supersonic combustion and having no rotating parts.
A rocket engine that carries all oxygen required for combustion.
49.x: A scramjet uses supersonic combustion and does not have rotating compressor or turbine parts. It is distinct from a rocket, which carries its oxidiser.
49.tq: Break the propulsion term into its defining combustion characteristic.
xs: A **scramjet** uses **supersonic combustion** and has **no rotating parts** — option **(3)**.
India's **HSTDV** used an **indigenous scramjet**.
xa: HSTDV flew at **Mach 6+**, with thermal protection above **2,000°C**.
**Jan 2026**: a scramjet combustor ran **over 12 minutes**.
Compare **SFDR** (solid fuel ducted ramjet): also uses **atmospheric air** for combustion.

49.s: Solid Fuel Ducted Ramjet (SFDR) technology is intended mainly for
49.x: SFDR uses atmospheric air for combustion and was demonstrated from ITR Chandipur for application in long-range air-to-air missiles.
49.tq: Match the propulsion system with its stated operational application.
xs: **SFDR** (solid fuel ducted ramjet) is meant for **long-range air-to-air missiles** — option **(2)**.
It uses **atmospheric air for combustion** and was demonstrated from **ITR Chandipur**.
xa: **Astra Mk-3 'Gandiva'** is being built with an **SFDR** engine, range **350+ km**.
⚠ **BrahMos** uses a **liquid ramjet**; SFDR is a **solid fuel** ramjet.
**Astra Mk-2** uses a **dual-pulse solid motor** (about **200 km**).

49.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India's first MIRV flight test, Mission Divyastra (11 March 2024), used the K-4 missile.
2. In FOBS, a warhead is placed in a partial low orbit and can approach from an unexpected direction.
3. A MIRV lets one missile carry several warheads aimed at different targets.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Mission Divyastra used Agni-V; K-4 is a submarine-launched missile. So '2 and 3 only'.
49.tq: Divyastra = Agni-V MIRV (2024).
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1 is wrong: **Mission Divyastra** (**11 Mar 2024**) used **Agni-V**.
Statement 2 is correct: **FOBS** places a warhead in a **partial low orbit**, approaching from an unexpected direction.
Statement 3 is correct: a **MIRV** carries several warheads for **different targets**.
xa: **SFDR** = solid fuel ducted ramjet, using atmospheric air; for long-range air-to-air missiles.
**Ballistic** missiles are powered only in the **boost phase**; **cruise** missiles are powered throughout.
Examples: ballistic = **Agni, Prithvi, Pralay**; cruise = **BrahMos, Nirbhay**.

49.s:
Consider the following statements about BrahMos Aerospace:
1. The Inter-Governmental Agreement creating it was signed in Moscow in 1998.
2. The name joins the Brahmaputra and Moskva rivers.
3. NPOM of Russia holds 50.5% and DRDO 49.5%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 reverses the shares: DRDO holds 50.5% and NPOM (NPO Mashinostroyeniya) 49.5%. So '1 and 2 only'.
49.tq: BrahMos: India-Russia JV (1998), DRDO 50.5%.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1 is correct: the **Inter-Governmental Agreement** was signed in **Moscow in 1998**.
Statement 2 is correct: the name joins the **Brahmaputra + Moskva** rivers.
Statement 3 reverses the shares: **DRDO 50.5%**, **NPOM** (Russia) **49.5%**.
xa: BrahMos's first successful test: **12 June 2001**, **Chandipur**.
BrahMos is an **India-Russia** joint venture (APPSC-G2 2025 key).
**Philippines** = first BrahMos export customer, **$375 million** deal (**2022**).

49.s:
Consider the following statements about BrahMos:
1. Its first successful test was on 12 June 2001 at Chandipur, Odisha.
2. It is a supersonic cruise missile flying at about Mach 2.8-3.0.
3. It cruises at about 10 m and climbs to about 15 km in the terminal phase.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 reverses the profile: BrahMos cruises at about 15 km and dives to about 10 m in the terminal phase. So '1 and 2 only'.
49.tq: BrahMos: Mach ~3, cruise high, dive to 10 m.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 is correct: first successful test **12 June 2001**, **Chandipur, Odisha**.
Statement 2 is correct: **supersonic cruise missile**, **Mach 2.8-3.0**.
Statement 3 reverses the profile: BrahMos cruises at ~**15 km** and **dives to 10 m** in the terminal phase.
xa: Propulsion: **solid booster → liquid ramjet**.
Range: **290 km** originally, **290-400 km** in extended versions.
**BrahMos-NG** is lighter (**about 1.5 t**); **BrahMos-II** is planned **hypersonic**.
First reported combat use: **Operation Sindoor** (May 2025).

49.s:
Consider the following statements about BrahMos:
1. It uses a solid booster followed by a liquid ramjet.
2. Its navigation combines inertial navigation with satellite navigation.
3. It is launched from a Transport Launch Canister and follows a fire-and-forget principle.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: All three statements are correct. BrahMos uses a solid booster and liquid ramjet, combines inertial and satellite navigation, and can be fired from a Transport Launch Canister in fire-and-forget mode.
49.tq: Verify each statement independently by separating propulsion, navigation and launch-control features.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: propulsion is a **solid booster** then a **liquid ramjet**.
Statement 2: navigation is **inertial + satellite** (GPS/GLONASS).
Statement 3: it is **fire-and-forget** from a **Transport Launch Canister**.
xa: It cruises at ~**15 km** and dives to **10 m** in the terminal phase.
It has a **low radar cross-section**.
⚠ **Nirbhay** uses a **turbojet**, not a ramjet.

49.s:
With reference to BrahMos variants, consider the following statements:
1. The base BrahMos can be launched from land, ships, submarines and aircraft.
2. BrahMos-NG is lighter than the base BrahMos and is intended for platforms such as Tejas.
3. BrahMos-II is a planned hypersonic variant capable of speeds above Mach 5.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: All three statements are correct. The base system has land, ship, submarine and air-launched versions; BrahMos-NG is a lighter version for platforms including Tejas; and BrahMos-II is planned as a hypersonic missile.
49.tq: Use the platform and speed clues to distinguish the base, NG and BrahMos-II variants.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: base BrahMos can be launched from **land, ship, submarine and air** (**Su-30MKI**).
Statement 2: **BrahMos-NG** is lighter (**about 1.5 t** against **2.5 t**), for **Tejas**, smaller warships and submarines.
Statement 3: **BrahMos-II** is planned **hypersonic**, above **Mach 5** (up to **Mach 7**).
xa: **P-17A frigates** carry BrahMos.
BrahMos-NG flies at about **Mach 3.5**.
**Land-attack** BrahMos uses **mobile launchers** (Army).

49.s: BrahMos was reportedly used in combat for the first time during:
49.x: The first reported combat use of BrahMos was during Operation Sindoor in May 2025.
49.tq: Link the operation name with its reported year and avoid substituting another Indian military operation.
xs: BrahMos was first reportedly used in combat in **Operation Sindoor** (**May 2025**) — option **(4)**.
The notes do not link the other operations to BrahMos.
xa: **BrahMos Integration and Testing Facility, Lucknow** was inaugurated on **11 May 2025**.
First BrahMos export: **Philippines** (**$375 million**, **2022**).
**UAE**: early-stage talks on **BrahMos** and **Akashteer** (**23 Jun 2026**).

49.s: The BrahMos Integration and Testing Facility inaugurated on 11 May 2025 is located at
49.x: The BrahMos Integration and Testing Facility at Lucknow (in the UP defence corridor) was inaugurated on 11 May 2025, with the first batch flagged off within five months. Hyderabad and Nagpur are other defence-industry centres, and Chandipur is the test range where BrahMos was first tested in 2001.
49.tq: BrahMos unit = Lucknow, UP corridor.
xs: The **BrahMos Integration and Testing Facility** is at **Lucknow**, inaugurated **11 May 2025** — option **(2)**.
Its **first batch** was flagged off **within five months**.
**Chandipur** is the test range where BrahMos was **first tested** (**2001**).
xa: First combat use: **Operation Sindoor** (**May 2025**).
First export customer: **Philippines**.
BrahMos-NG is meant for **Tejas**, smaller warships and submarines.

49.s:
Consider the following statements about Nirbhay:
1. It is powered by a liquid ramjet.
2. It is India's subsonic long-range land-attack cruise missile with a range of about 1,000 km.
3. It hugs the terrain at low altitude to evade radar.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Nirbhay is turbojet-powered; the liquid ramjet belongs to the supersonic BrahMos. So '2 and 3 only'.
49.tq: Nirbhay = subsonic, turbojet; BrahMos = supersonic, ramjet.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1 is wrong: **Nirbhay** is **turbojet** powered; the **liquid ramjet** belongs to **BrahMos**.
Statement 2 is correct: Nirbhay is India's **subsonic LR-LACM**, range ~**1,000 km**.
Statement 3 is correct: it is **terrain-hugging** at low altitude to evade radar.
xa: Successor **ITCM** uses the indigenous **'Manik' small turbofan engine** (GTRE).
⚠ **Nirbhay** = **subsonic**; **BrahMos** = **supersonic**.
Nirbhay navigation: **inertial + GPS/NavIC**.

49.s: Astra is best classified as which one of the following?
o: A man-portable anti-tank guided missile with a laser seeker
A short-range surface-to-surface missile with an inertial seeker
A beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile family developed by DRDO with an active radar seeker
A ship-launched hypersonic cruise missile with an infrared seeker
49.x: Astra is a DRDO-developed family of beyond-visual-range air-to-air missiles using an active radar seeker.
49.tq: Identify the weapon by class, developer and seeker type.
xs: **Astra** is a **DRDO** family of **Beyond Visual Range Air-to-Air Missiles (BVRAAM)** with an **active radar seeker** — option **(3)**.
The man-portable ATGM is **MPATGM**; the ship-launched hypersonic cruise missile is Russia's **Zircon**.
xa: **BVR** = engaging beyond **20 nautical miles (37 km)**.
**Astra Mk-1** is on the **Su-30MKI**, planned for **Tejas Mk-1A** and **Rafale**.
**Indonesia** is the first Astra buyer (**Jul 2026**).

49.s:
Consider the following statements about the Astra family:
1. Astra Mk-2 uses a dual-pulse solid motor and has a range of about 200 km.
2. Astra Mk-1 has a range of 80-110 km and flies at Mach 4.5.
3. Astra Mk-3 'Gandiva' is powered by a scramjet.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Astra Mk-3 'Gandiva' uses a solid fuel ducted ramjet (SFDR), with range of 350+ km. So '1 and 2 only'.
49.tq: Astra Mk-3 Gandiva = SFDR.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(4)**.
Statement 1 is correct: **Astra Mk-2** has a **dual-pulse solid motor**, about **200 km**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Astra Mk-1** = **80-110 km**, **Mach 4.5**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Astra Mk-3 'Gandiva'** uses an **SFDR** engine, **350+ km** — not a scramjet.
xa: Astra is a **BVRAAM** with an **active radar seeker**; BVR = beyond **20 nautical miles (37 km)**.
**Indonesia** deal (Jul 2026) = **first-ever export** of the Astra family.
Astra was test-fired from an **LCA AF Mk1** prototype on **12 Mar 2025**.

49.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. VL-SRSAM : vertical-launch short-range SAM for Navy ships, derived from Astra
2. VSHORADS : man-portable system against low-altitude threats
3. QRSAM : man-portable very short-range air defence system
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
49.x: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. Pair 3 is wrong: QRSAM (Quick Reaction SAM) is the mid-range layer of IADWS for the Army; the man-portable system is VSHORADS. So '1 and 2 only'.
49.tq: QRSAM = mid layer; VSHORADS = man-portable.
xs: Pairs **1 and 2** are correctly matched — option **(3)**.
Pair 1 is correct: **VL-SRSAM** = vertical-launch short-range SAM for Navy ships, **derived from Astra**.
Pair 2 is correct: **VSHORADS** = **man-portable**, against low-altitude threats.
Pair 3 is wrong: **QRSAM** is the **mid-range layer of IADWS** for the Army, not man-portable.
xa: **Rudram-I** = India's **first indigenous anti-radiation missile**.
**Pralay** = quasi-ballistic, **150-500 km**; salvo of two on **31 Dec 2025**.
**NASM-SR** = first indigenous **helicopter-launched anti-ship** missile.

49.s: Which one of the following groups contains only missiles associated with Russia?
49.x: BrahMos is a joint venture with Russia, while R-73 Archer and S-400 are Russian systems. The other groups contain missiles associated with Israel, Iran, North Korea, Pakistan or the United States.
49.tq: Classify each item by partner or country before selecting the complete group.
xs: **BrahMos, R-73 Archer and S-400** are all linked to **Russia** — option **(3)**.
**Barak-1, Spyder, Barak-8** are **Israeli**; **Shahab, Fattah** are **Iranian** and **Hwasong** is **North Korean**.
**Abdali** is **Pakistani** and **Minuteman III** **American**.
xa: **Kinzhal** and **Zircon** are also Russian.
⚠ **Zircon** = ship-launched; **Kinzhal** = air-launched.
BrahMos is a **joint venture**: **DRDO 50.5%**, **NPOM 49.5%**.

49.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India's missile exports:
1. The Philippines is India's first BrahMos export customer under a 2022 deal, with deliveries from 2024.
2. The Astra Mk-1 deal with Indonesia, signed in July 2026, is the first export of the Astra family.
3. BrahMos and Akashteer have already been delivered to the UAE.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
49.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Philippines was the first BrahMos buyer (2022 deal, deliveries from 2024). Statement 2 is correct: the Indonesia Astra Mk-1 deal (Jul 2026) is the first Astra-family export. Statement 3 is wrong: with the UAE, BrahMos and Akashteer talks are only at an early stage. So '1 and 2 only' is right; '1 only' omits statement 2, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include statement 3.
49.tq: Delivered = Philippines (BrahMos); deal signed = Indonesia (Astra); only talks = UAE.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **Philippines** — first BrahMos buyer, **2022** deal, deliveries from **2024**.
Statement 2: the **Astra Mk-1** deal with **Indonesia** (**Jul 2026**) is the **first export** of the Astra family.
Statement 3 is wrong: with the **UAE**, BrahMos and Akashteer are only in **early-stage talks**.
xa: Philippines deal value: **$375 million**.
**Akashteer** is an air-defence **control** system.

49.s: The Minuteman III is associated with which one of the following descriptions?
o: An American ICBM forming the land leg of the US nuclear triad
49.x: Minuteman III is a United States intercontinental ballistic missile and forms the land leg of the US nuclear triad.
49.tq: Identify the system from its strategic role rather than its name alone.
xs: **Minuteman III** is an **American ICBM**, the **land leg of the US triad** — option **(2)**.
The **450 km** Pakistani SSM is **Abdali**; the Russian air-launched hypersonic missile is **Kinzhal**; the Iranian claimed hypersonic is **Fattah**.
xa: **Hwasong** is North Korea's ICBM/IRBM series.
**Abdali** (Pakistan) is a **450 km** SSM named after **Ahmed Shah Abdali**.
**Jun 2026**: India's multi-layered BMD showed it can engage threats **up to ICBM class**.

49.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India’s long-range missile capability:

2. India’s rocket force is still described as a concept rather than an established force.
3. The long-range missile systems are described as fully integrated into an operational rocket force.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the assessment states that the systems are not yet fully integrated and that the rocket force remains only a concept.
49.tq: Find the statement that reverses the reported assessment by changing an incomplete capability into a fully operational one.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **Agni, Nirbhay LR-LACM and BrahMos** are **not yet fully integrated** (**30 Jun 2026**).
Statement 2: the **rocket force** is **still only a concept**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it contradicts both points above.
xa: Another criticism: **hypersonics still maturing**.
**Nirbhay**: subsonic, ~**1,000 km**, **turbojet**.
**Mission Sudarshan Chakra** targets operational maturity by **2035**.

49.x: ITCM is the successor to Nirbhay and is powered by the indigenous Manik small turbofan engine developed by GTRE.

xs: **ITCM** (Indigenous Technology Cruise Missile), the Nirbhay successor, uses the **Manik small turbofan engine** — option **(3)**.
The Manik engine is from **GTRE**.
**SFDR** is for **Astra Mk-3**; the **scramjet** is in **HSTDV**.

Nirbhay itself is **turbojet** powered.

49.s: Which one of the following missiles is India's first indigenous anti-radiation missile designed to home passively on radar emissions?
49.x: Rudram-I is India's first indigenous anti-radiation missile. It passively homes on radar emissions to destroy enemy radars and communication sites.
49.tq: Identify the missile from its distinctive operational role.
xs: **Rudram-I** is India's **first indigenous anti-radiation missile** — option **(3)**.
It **homes passively on radar emissions** to **destroy enemy radars and communication sites** (APPSC-G1 **2018**).
**Pralay** is a quasi-ballistic SSM; **QRSAM** and **VSHORADS** are air-defence missiles.
xa: Rudram-I is **air-to-surface**, fired from the **Su-30MKI**, range **100-200 km**.
⚠ Rudram-I attacks **radars**; **Mission Shakti**'s interceptor attacked a **satellite**.

49.s:
Consider the following statements about Pralay:

2. It has a stated range of 150–500 km.
3. It uses a conventional warhead and has manoeuvrable re-entry capability.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: Pralay is a quasi-ballistic short-range tactical surface-to-surface missile with a 150–500 km range, conventional warhead and manoeuvrable re-entry capability.
49.tq: Check each technical characteristic before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Pralay** is a **quasi-ballistic short-range surface-to-surface** (tactical SSM) missile.
Range **150-500 km**, **conventional warhead**, **manoeuvrable re-entry**.

**Prahaar**: ~**150 km** tactical ballistic missile.
**Shaurya**: hypersonic, **700-1,900 km**, nuclear-capable.

49.s: Which one of the following missiles is a canister-launched, hypersonic, nuclear-capable surface-to-surface tactical missile with a range of about 700–1,900 km?
49.x: Shaurya is a canister-launched hypersonic surface-to-surface tactical missile with a range of about 700–1,900 km and nuclear capability.
49.tq: Use the range and launch-mode clues to identify the missile.
xs: **Shaurya** is a **canister-launched hypersonic surface-to-surface** tactical missile, about **700-1,900 km**, **nuclear-capable** — option **(2)**.
**Prahaar** is ~**150 km**; **Pralay** is **150-500 km** with a conventional warhead.
xa: **Pralay**: quasi-ballistic, **manoeuvrable re-entry**; salvo on **31 Dec 2025**.
**Rudram-I**: first indigenous **anti-radiation** missile.
Hypersonic = faster than **Mach 5**.

49.s:

**Philippines** = **first BrahMos buyer**; **Indonesia** = **first Astra buyer**.
xa: Philippines BrahMos deal: **$375 million** (**2022**), deliveries from **2024**.
Indonesia deal (**Jul 2026**) = **first-ever export** of the Astra family (**Astra Mk-1**).

49.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Hwasong is a North Korean ICBM/IRBM series.
2. Shahab and Fattah are Iranian missiles.
3. Kinzhal is a Russian ship-launched hypersonic cruise missile.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Kinzhal is Russia's air-launched hypersonic missile; Zircon is the ship-launched one. So '1 and 2 only'.
49.tq: Zircon = ship-launched; Kinzhal = air-launched.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(4)**.
Statement 1 is correct: **Hwasong** is a **North Korean** ICBM/IRBM series.
Statement 2 is correct: **Shahab** and **Fattah** are **Iranian** missiles.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Kinzhal** is Russia's **air-launched** hypersonic missile; **Zircon** is the ship-launched one.
xa: **Abdali** is a **Pakistan** **450 km** SSM.
**Minuteman III** is a **USA** ICBM, land leg of the US triad.
**Patriot** intercepted **six** Kinzhals in one night over **Kyiv** (May 2023).

49.s: Which one of the following statements about the HSTDV is correct?
o: It flew at above Mach 6 and validated scramjet combustion and thermal protection above 2,000°C.
It flew at speeds below Mach 2 and tested only navigation systems.
It is a submarine-launched missile with a range of 3,500 km.
It is an air-defence interceptor tested only in the endo-atmospheric layer.
49.x: India's HSTDV flew at above Mach 6 and validated scramjet combustion and thermal protection at temperatures exceeding 2,000°C.
49.tq: Use the distinctive speed and thermal-performance figures to identify the correct statement.
xs: **HSTDV** flew at **Mach 6+** and validated **scramjet combustion** and **thermal protection above 2,000°C** — option **(1)**.
It is a **Hypersonic Technology Demonstrator Vehicle**, not an interceptor or a submarine-launched missile.
xa: HSTDV uses an **indigenous scramjet** (supersonic combustion, **no rotating parts**).
A scramjet combustor ran for **over 12 minutes** (**Jan 2026**).
⚠ **HSTDV** = scramjet demonstrator (**Mach 6+**); **LR-AShM** = glide missile (peak **Mach 10**).

49.s: The first flight-trial of India's long-range hypersonic missile was reported on
49.x: India's first reported flight-trial of the long-range hypersonic missile took place on 16 November 2024.
49.tq: Separate closely spaced test dates by linking each date to its specific programme.
xs: India's **first long-range hypersonic missile** had its first flight-trial on **16 November 2024** — option **(4)**.
⚠ **11 Mar 2024** is **Mission Divyastra** (first **MIRV** test on **Agni-V**).
xa: **LR-AShM**: range ~**1,500 km**, peak **Mach 10**, **two-stage solid motor**.
LR-AShM was shown at the **77th Republic Day Parade**.
AP coast ranges were used for **LRAShM** validation rounds (**Jan 2026**).

49.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the reported flight characteristics of the long-range hypersonic anti-ship missile?
o: It uses skipping manoeuvres, with peak speed around Mach 10 and average speed around Mach 5.
It remains stationary in low orbit before descending vertically at Mach 3.
It flies only in a high parabolic arc, with average speed below Mach 2.
It uses underwater propulsion and approaches the target at subsonic speed.
49.x: The missile is reported to use skipping manoeuvres, with a peak speed of about Mach 10 and an average speed of about Mach 5.
49.tq: Use the peak-versus-average speed distinction to avoid reversing the figures.
xs: The missile uses **skipping manoeuvres**, with **peak Mach 10** and **average Mach 5** — option **(1)**.
This is the **LR-AShM**, a **hypersonic glide anti-ship missile** for **Navy coastal batteries**.
xa: Range: **1,500+ km**; **two-stage solid motor**.
First long-range hypersonic missile trial: **16 Nov 2024**.
⚠ **HSTDV** (**Mach 6+**) is a scramjet demonstrator, not LR-AShM.

49.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Mission Sudarshan Chakra is a proposed multi-layered air and missile defence network, to mature by 2035.
2. Project Kusha's M3 interceptor is expected to reach about 350-400 km.
3. Project Kusha is DRDO's short-range air-defence system.

49.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Project Kusha is DRDO's long-range air-defence system (M1/M2/M3 ~150/250/350-400 km). So '1 and 2 only'.
49.tq: Kusha = long-range (M1-M3).
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1 is correct: **Mission Sudarshan Chakra** is a multi-layered air and missile defence network, maturing by **2035**.
Statement 2 is correct: Kusha's **M3** interceptor reaches about **350-400 km**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Project Kusha** is DRDO's **long-range** air-defence system.
xa: Kusha interceptors **M1/M2/M3** = ~**150 / 250 / 350-400 km**.
⚠ **PAD = Pradyumna = exo** (**50-80 km**); **AAD = Ashwin = endo** (**15-30 km**).
Phase-II BMD: **AD-1** (exo) and **AD-2** (endo).

49.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (BMD layer)
 a. Phase-I exo-atmospheric
 b. Phase-I endo-atmospheric
 c. Phase-II exo-atmospheric

49.s:
Consider the following statements about Mission Shakti:
1. It was conducted on 27 March 2019.
2. It was a joint mission of DRDO and ISRO.
3. It was conducted in the upper atmosphere so that no debris would be created.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is the APPSC-G1 2022 trap: Microsat-R was hit in low LEO (~283 km) so that the debris would decay quickly - not in the upper atmosphere, and debris was created. So '1 and 2 only'.
49.tq: Mission Shakti: low LEO so debris decays; not 'no debris'.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 is correct: **Mission Shakti** was on **27 March 2019**.
Statement 2 is correct: a joint mission of **DRDO and ISRO** (APPSC-G1 2022).
Statement 3 is wrong: **Microsat-R** was hit in **low LEO** (~**283 km**) so the **debris would decay** quickly — not in the upper atmosphere.
xa: Interceptor: DRDO **PDV Mk-II**.
India = **4th nation** with ASAT capability, after **USA, Russia and China**.
Microsat-R was launched by **PSLV-C44** in Jan **2019**.

49.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the interceptor and its target in Mission Shakti?
49.x: A DRDO PDV Mk-II interceptor destroyed the live satellite Microsat-R during Mission Shakti.
49.tq: Match the specialised interceptor with the named satellite target instead of a neighbouring missile or satellite programme.
xs: The interceptor was DRDO's **PDV Mk-II** and the target the live satellite **Microsat-R** — option **(4)**.
PDV Mk-II came from the **ballistic missile defence** programme.
**Akash** is a SAM and **Agni-V** a ballistic missile — not the ASAT interceptor.
xa: Microsat-R orbited in **LEO** at about **283 km**.
Microsat-R was a **DRDO satellite** launched by **PSLV-C44** (**Jan 2019**).
⚠ Correct PYQ statement: "destroyed a **live satellite in LEO**".

49.s: India became the fourth country to demonstrate an anti-satellite capability. Which of the following shows the three countries that preceded India?
49.x: India became the fourth country with demonstrated ASAT capability after the USA, Russia and China.
49.tq: Use the rank clue to reconstruct the preceding three countries without adding other space powers.
xs: India was the **fourth** ASAT nation, after the **USA, Russia and China** — option **(4)**.
France, Japan, UK and Israel are not named in the notes as ASAT states.
xa: ASAT = **missile-based system to attack satellites**.
India's test: **Mission Shakti**, **27 March 2019**.
Interceptor **PDV Mk-II**; target **Microsat-R**.

49.s: Which one of the following speed classifications is correctly matched?
o: Nirbhay — subsonic; BrahMos — supersonic; BrahMos-II — hypersonic
Nirbhay — supersonic; BrahMos — subsonic; BrahMos-II — ballistic
Nirbhay — hypersonic; BrahMos — subsonic; BrahMos-II — supersonic
Nirbhay — ballistic; BrahMos — hypersonic; BrahMos-II — subsonic
49.x: Nirbhay is subsonic, BrahMos is supersonic, and BrahMos-II is associated with hypersonic technology.
49.tq: Arrange the missiles by speed class without confusing cruise and ballistic categories.
xs: **Nirbhay — subsonic**, **BrahMos — supersonic**, **BrahMos-II — hypersonic** — option **(1)**.
Nirbhay is a **turbojet**-powered subsonic cruise missile; BrahMos flies at **Mach 2.8-3.0** with a **liquid ramjet**.
**BrahMos-II** is planned at **Mach 5** or more (up to **Mach 7**).
xa: ⚠ **Nirbhay** = subsonic, turbojet; **BrahMos** = supersonic, ramjet.
**LR-AShM** is also in the **hypersonic** class.
**BrahMos-NG**: lighter (**about 1.5 t**), about **Mach 3.5**.

49.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
49.x: Spyder is an Israeli system used by the Indian Air Force and replaced Trishul. Iran is associated with Shahab and Fattah, not Spyder.
49.tq: Detect the substituted partner country in a bilateral defence list.
xs: **Spyder — Iran** is wrong — option **(4)**.
**Spyder** is **Israeli**; the **IAF** used it to replace **Trishul**.
Iran's missiles are **Shahab** and **Fattah**.
xa: **Barak-1** (Israel) replaced Trishul for the **Navy**.
**Barak-8 / MRSAM**: DRDO with **Israel Aerospace Industries**, on **P-17A** frigates.
**R-73 Archer** (Russia) is a short-range **air-to-air** missile.

49.s: The ranges along the Andhra Pradesh coast were used for which of the following purposes?
o: Testing of the Astra export configuration
Demonstration of the first indigenous anti-radiation missile
49.x: Ranges along the Andhra Pradesh coast were used for LRAShM validation rounds.
49.tq: Match the distinctive geographical clue with the specific validation activity rather than with a missile name alone.
xs: AP coast ranges were used for **LRAShM validation rounds** (**Jan 2026**) — option **(2)**.
**LR-AShM** is a **hypersonic glide anti-ship missile** for **Navy coastal batteries**.
xa: LR-AShM: ~**1,500 km**, peak **Mach 10**, average **Mach 5** via **skipping**.
It was shown at the **77th Republic Day Parade**.
The first indigenous anti-radiation missile is **Rudram-I**.

50.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes a fission weapon from a fusion (thermonuclear) weapon?
o: A fission weapon splits heavy nuclei such as U-235 or Pu-239 in a chain reaction, while a fusion weapon fuses light hydrogen isotopes using a fission primary as trigger.
A fission weapon fuses hydrogen isotopes, while a fusion weapon splits U-235 nuclei.
Both weapons work only by splitting heavy nuclei; they differ only in yield.
A fusion weapon needs no trigger, while a fission weapon needs a fusion primary to start.
50.x: Fission (atomic) weapons split heavy nuclei (U-235/Pu-239) in a neutron chain reaction, as in Pokhran-I. Fusion (hydrogen) weapons fuse light hydrogen isotopes, with a fission 'primary' supplying the heat to trigger fusion, as tested in Pokhran-II. The second option reverses the two, the third ignores fusion, and the fourth reverses the trigger relationship.
50.tq: Fission splits heavy; fusion joins light, lit by a fission primary.
xs: A **fission** weapon splits heavy nuclei (**U-235 / Pu-239**) in a **chain reaction**; a **fusion** weapon fuses **hydrogen isotopes** with a **fission primary** as trigger — option **(1)**.
Option (2) reverses the two; option (4) reverses the trigger relationship.
xa: Fission example: **Pokhran-I**; fusion was tested in **Pokhran-II**.
Pokhran-II used **five** devices, both **fission and fusion**.
Bomb detonators are fired by a **Krytron**.

50.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Pokhran-I is correct?
o: It comprised five fission and fusion devices led by A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.
It was conducted on 18 May 1974 under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and was described as a peaceful nuclear explosion.
It was conducted on 11 May 1998 under Prime Minister A.B. Vajpayee as a thermonuclear test.
It was conducted at Pokhran under Prime Minister Morarji Desai as Operation Shakti.
50.x: Pokhran-I took place on 18 May 1974 under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and was officially described as a peaceful nuclear explosion. The other options refer to features of Pokhran-II or contain incorrect details.
50.tq: Use the date, Prime Minister and official description together to eliminate mixed-up details.
xs: **Pokhran-I** was held on **18 May 1974** under PM **Indira Gandhi**, as a "**peaceful nuclear explosion**" — option **(2)**.
**Five** fission-and-fusion devices, **11 May 1998**, **Vajpayee** and **Operation Shakti** all belong to **Pokhran-II**.
xa: Pokhran-I code name: "**Smiling Buddha**"; team led by **Raja Ramanna**.
Site: **Pokhran Test Range**, **Jaisalmer district, Rajasthan**.
⚠ **Operation Shakti** (**1998**) ≠ **Mission Shakti** (**2019** ASAT).

50.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Pokhran-I (1974) - Smiling Buddha
2. Pokhran-II (1998) - Operation Shakti
3. Pokhran-II - a single fission device
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
50.x: Pokhran-I (18 May 1974) was code-named 'Smiling Buddha' and Pokhran-II (11 and 13 May 1998) 'Operation Shakti', so pairs 1 and 2 are correct. Pair 3 is wrong: Pokhran-II tested five devices, both fission and fusion. '1 only' misses pair 2, while the other two codes wrongly include pair 3.
50.tq: Buddha smiled in 1974; Shakti (5 devices) in 1998.
xs: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Pair 1: **Pokhran-I (1974)** = "**Smiling Buddha**".
Pair 2: **Pokhran-II (1998)** = "**Operation Shakti**".
Pair 3 is wrong: Pokhran-II tested **five** devices, both **fission and fusion**.
xa: Pokhran-I was a "**peaceful nuclear explosion**" under **Indira Gandhi**.
Pokhran-II: under **Vajpayee**, led by **Kalam** and **Chidambaram**.
**11 May** = **National Technology Day**.

50.s:
Consider the following statements about India's nuclear doctrine:
1. The draft doctrine with No First Use came in 1999 from the Vajpayee government, after Pokhran-II.
2. No First Use was first declared by the Indira Gandhi government after Pokhran-I.
3. It was formally adopted by the Cabinet Committee on Security on 4 January 2003.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
50.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: NFU dates from the Vajpayee government after Pokhran-II (1998), not from Pokhran-I (1974). So '1 and 3 only'.
50.tq: Doctrine: draft 1999, adopted 4 Jan 2003.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 is correct: the **NFU / draft doctrine** came in **1999** from the **Vajpayee** government after **Pokhran-II**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Pokhran-I** (**1974**) under **Indira Gandhi** was a "peaceful nuclear explosion"; NFU came after 1998.
Statement 3 is correct: the doctrine was **formally adopted** by the **CCS** on **4 January 2003**.
xa: Tenets: **credible minimum deterrence**, **massive** retaliation, **non-use against non-nuclear-weapon states**.
The **Political Council**, chaired by the **Prime Minister**, alone can authorise use; the **Executive Council** is chaired by the **NSA**.
**Strategic Forces Command** (tri-service, **2003**) manages the nuclear arsenal.

50.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India's nuclear doctrine:
1. India maintains credible minimum deterrence.
2. India has a No First Use policy.
3. The doctrine provides for massive retaliation causing unacceptable damage.
4. India has declared that it will use nuclear weapons against every non-nuclear-weapon state.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
50.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are tenets of the doctrine. Statement 4 is false because the doctrine provides for no use against non-nuclear-weapon states, subject to the stated doctrine concerning major biological or chemical attacks.
50.tq: Watch for an absolute statement that reverses the no-use commitment.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(1) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
Statements 1-3: **credible minimum deterrence**, **No First Use**, and **massive** retaliation causing **unacceptable damage**.
Statement 4 is wrong: the doctrine says **non-use against non-nuclear-weapon states**.
xa: Exception: nuclear option kept against a major **biological or chemical** attack.
Continued **moratorium on testing**; strict export controls.
Support for **disarmament** and the **FMCT**.

50.s: India's nuclear doctrine retains the nuclear option against a major attack involving
50.x: The doctrine retains the nuclear option against a major biological or chemical attack.
50.tq: Recall the specific exception rather than broadening it to every form of attack.
xs: The nuclear option is kept against a major **biological or chemical** attack — option **(4)**.
Otherwise the doctrine allows use **only in retaliation** against a **nuclear attack** on Indian territory or forces.
xa: **Non-use against non-nuclear-weapon states** is another tenet.
Retaliation will be **massive**, causing **unacceptable damage**.
Doctrine adopted by the **CCS**: **4 January 2003**.

50.s: Under India’s No First Use policy, nuclear weapons may be used in retaliation against
o: any conventional attack on Indian territory
a nuclear attack on Indian territory or Indian forces
a cyberattack on India’s strategic infrastructure
any military alliance formed against India
50.x: India’s No First Use policy permits nuclear weapons only in retaliation against a nuclear attack on Indian territory or Indian forces.
50.tq: Distinguish the exact condition attached to a strategic policy from broader military contingencies.
xs: Under **No First Use**, nuclear weapons are used only in **retaliation against a nuclear attack on Indian territory or forces** — option **(2)**.
A conventional or cyberattack alone does not qualify.
xa: Exception kept: a major **biological or chemical** attack.
**Non-use against non-nuclear-weapon states**.
Retaliation is **massive**, to cause **unacceptable damage**.

50.s: The next strategic step associated with India’s SSBN-based deterrence is
o: ending the No First Use policy
replacement of all missiles by free-fall bombs
50.x: Continuous at-sea deterrence is identified as the next step in strengthening India’s SSBN-based nuclear deterrence.
50.tq: Identify the policy objective that follows from the capability already described.
xs: The next step is **continuous at-sea deterrence** — option **(2)**.
SSBNs give **second-strike capability**, which supports **No First Use** — so ending NFU is not the step.
xa: **INS Aridhaman** (third boat) was commissioned on **3 Apr 2026** at **Visakhapatnam**.

**K-5 / K-6** longer-range SLBMs are **under development**.

50.s:

b. Executive Council of the Nuclear Command Authority

50.s: The Strategic Forces Command is best described as
o: a joint research body of DRDO and ISRO
a civilian body regulating nuclear exports
a tri-service command managing and operating India’s nuclear arsenal
a parliamentary committee supervising defence expenditure
50.x: The Strategic Forces Command is a tri-service command responsible for managing and operating India’s nuclear arsenal.
50.tq: Match the organisation with its precise institutional role.
xs: The **Strategic Forces Command** is a **tri-service** command that **manages and operates** the nuclear arsenal — option **(3)**.
It was set up in **2003**.

The **Political Council** (PM) alone authorises use.

50.s:
With reference to the legs of India's nuclear triad, consider the following statements:
1. The land leg comprises the Prithvi and Agni series, including canisterised road- and rail-mobile missiles.
2. The air leg comprises Su-30MKI and Rafale aircraft carrying free-fall nuclear bombs.
3. The sea leg comprises K-15 and K-4 SLBMs fired from Arihant-class SSBNs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
50.x: Statement 1 is correct: Prithvi and Agni (canisterised, road- and rail-mobile) form the land leg. Statement 2 is wrong: the air leg is Jaguar and Mirage 2000 with free-fall bombs. Statement 3 is correct: K-15/K-4 SLBMs from Arihant-class SSBNs form the sea leg. So '1 and 3 only' is right; '1 only' misses statement 3, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include statement 2.
50.tq: Air leg = Jaguar + Mirage 2000; watch for Su-30MKI/Rafale swapped in.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: the **land** leg is **Prithvi** and **Agni** (canisterised, **road- and rail-mobile**).
Statement 2 is wrong: the **air** leg is **Jaguar** and **Mirage 2000** with **free-fall** bombs.
Statement 3: the **sea** leg is **K-15 / K-4** SLBMs from **Arihant-class SSBNs**.
xa: **SSBNs** are the **most survivable** leg — they guarantee **second-strike capability**.
India has a **fully operational triad**, like **USA, Russia, China** (**Apr 2026**).
US triad: **Minuteman III**, strategic bombers, **Ohio/Columbia-class** SSBNs.

50.s: Why are SSBNs regarded as the most survivable leg of the nuclear triad?
o: They eliminate the need for land-based deterrence.
They remain permanently visible to adversaries.
Their concealment supports a guaranteed second-strike capability.
50.x: SSBNs are difficult to detect and destroy, thereby supporting a reliable second-strike capability that underpins India’s No First Use posture.
50.tq: Connect survivability with the strategic purpose of assured retaliation.
xs: **SSBNs** are the **most survivable** leg; they guarantee **second-strike capability** — option **(4)**.
That second-strike capability **underpins No First Use**.
xa: Next step: **continuous at-sea deterrence**.
**SIPRI** links **12** deployed warheads to **SSBN deterrence patrols**.
India's SSBNs are based at **Visakhapatnam**; **Rambilli** naval base is nearby.

50.s: The operational deployment of Indian warheads cited in the June 2026 assessment was linked particularly to
o: Dhanush missiles mounted exclusively on aircraft carriers
only free-fall bombs carried by Jaguar aircraft
SSBN deterrence patrols and canisterised Agni missiles
civilian nuclear reactors and space launch vehicles
50.x: The cited deployment was linked to SSBN deterrence patrols and canisterised Agni missiles.
50.tq: Match a current quantitative assessment with the two capabilities associated with it.
xs: **SIPRI** linked **12** "operationally deployed" Indian warheads to **SSBN deterrence patrols** and **canisterised Agni** — option **(3)**.
The assessment is dated **30 Jun 2026**.
xa: **SSBNs** are the **most survivable** leg, giving **second-strike capability**.
The air leg uses **Jaguar** and **Mirage 2000** with **free-fall** bombs.
**Agni-4** user trial, **6 Aug 2026**: **4,000 km**, **two-stage solid**, **road-mobile**.

50.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the United States nuclear triad?
o: Minuteman III ICBMs, strategic bombers and Ohio/Columbia-class SSBNs
Tomahawk missiles, aircraft carriers and attack submarines
Trident submarines, Agni missiles and Mirage 2000 aircraft
Prithvi missiles, Jaguar aircraft and Arihant-class SSBNs
50.x: The US triad consists of Minuteman III intercontinental ballistic missiles, strategic bombers and Ohio/Columbia-class SSBNs.
50.tq: Match a country-specific triad with all three of its stated components.
xs: The US triad = **Minuteman III ICBMs**, **strategic bombers** and **Ohio/Columbia-class SSBNs** — option **(1)**.
**Agni, Prithvi, Mirage 2000, Jaguar** and **Arihant-class** belong to **India**'s triad.
xa: India's land leg: **Prithvi** and **Agni**; air leg: **Jaguar** and **Mirage 2000**.
India's sea leg: **K-15 / K-4** from **Arihant-class SSBNs**.
India now has a **fully operational triad** (**Apr 2026**).

50.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its approximate U-235 enrichment level?
50.x: Natural uranium contains about 0.7% U-235. Reactor-grade LEU is about 3–5%, HEU is 20% or more, and weapons-grade uranium is about 90%.

xs: **Natural uranium** has about **0.7% U-235** — option **(4)**.
The others are mismatched: **HEU** is **20%+**, **weapons-grade** about **90%**, **reactor-grade LEU** **3-5%**.
xa: Fission weapons split **U-235 / Pu-239** in a neutron **chain reaction**.
India's **700 MW PHWRs** use **domestic uranium**, so no NSG clearance is needed.
⚠ The 20% line separates **LEU** from **HEU**.

50.s:
Consider the following statements about India's K-series SLBMs:

2. K-4 (about 3,500 km) is designed for Arihant-class submarines.

xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is wrong: **K-15 Sagarika** has a range of about **750 km**; **3,500 km** is **K-4**.

Statement 3 is correct: the "**K**" honours **Kalam**.
xa: **K-5 / K-6** are longer-range SLBMs under development.
The **SSBN** is the most survivable leg, guaranteeing **second-strike capability**.
Earlier, **Dhanush** was fired from ships (INS Subhadra, INS Rajput).

50.s:
Consider the following statements about the Arihant-class SSBNs:

50.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: INS Aridhaman (about 7,000 t) has 8 VLS for 24 K-15 or 8 K-4/K-5; the 4-VLS boats are the ~6,000 t Arihant and Arighaat. So '2 and 3 only'.

xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — option **(4)**.
Statement 1 is wrong: **INS Aridhaman** (about **7,000 t**) has **8 VLS** — **24 K-15 or 8 K-4/K-5**.
Statement 2 is correct: **INS Arighaat** (**2024**) had **K-4** tested from it.
Statement 3 is correct: **INS Arihant** (**2016**) is the **first indigenous SSBN**.
xa: Aridhaman was commissioned on **3 Apr 2026** at **Visakhapatnam**.
The **ATV** project built SSBNs with **Russian help**.

50.s: The ATV project was undertaken primarily to develop:
o: Indigenous SSBNs with DRDO and private-sector participation and Russian assistance
A network of anti-drone systems with Israel Aerospace Industries
A long-range air-defence radar with the United States
A conventional submarine fleet based entirely on German designs

xs: The **ATV (Advanced Technology Vessel)** project was started by **DRDO + private firms** with **Russian help** to build **SSBNs** — option **(1)**.

50.x: MRSAM/Barak-8 is an India-Israel programme involving DRDO and Israel Aerospace Industries (IAI).
50.tq: Use the development-agency trap to distinguish DRDO-IAI cooperation from other partnerships.
xs: **MRSAM / Barak-8** is an India-Israel system of **DRDO** and **Israel Aerospace Industries** — option **(1)**.
Its Army version was tested in **Apr 2025**.
xa: The **DAC** approved MRSAM procurement in **Jul 2026**.
MRSAM is a **building block** of **Mission Sudarshan Chakra**.
**Barak-1** (Israel) is the Navy's ship-based point-defence SAM.

50.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

xa: ⚠ Member: **MTCR 2016 – Wassenaar 2017 – Australia Group 2018**.

xs: India supports a **universal, verifiable FMCT** that **does not cap its existing stockpile** — option **(1)**.

xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.

**Pakistan** tested soon after in **1998**.

Pair 1 is correct: **INS Sindhuvir** = Russian **Kilo** (Sindhughosh class) diesel-electric.
