**Draft National Electricity Policy 2026** (Ministry of Power) replaces NEP 2005.

55.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the relationship between the new and earlier electricity policies?
o: The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 replaces the National Electricity Policy 2005.
The Draft National Electricity Policy 2017 replaced the Tariff Policy 2006.
The National Electricity Policy 2005 replaced the Draft National Electricity Policy 2026.
The Tariff Policy 2016 replaced the Electricity Act 2003.
55.x: The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026, issued by the Ministry of Power, is intended to replace the National Electricity Policy 2005.
55.tq: Discriminate between a policy, a tariff policy and an Act by testing the direction of replacement.
xs: The **Draft National Electricity Policy 2026** replaces the **National Electricity Policy 2005** — option **(1)**.
Both come from the **Ministry of Power**; the Electricity Act **2003** requires the NEP and the **Tariff Policy 2006** (revised **2016**).
The **Tariff Policy** did not replace the **Electricity Act 2003** — it is required by it.
xa: The 2026 draft covers **hybrid RE, BESS, smart grids, Time-of-Day tariffs**.
It also targets **100 GW PSH by 2047**.
It is paired with **EC Act 2001** targets for **208 industrial units** → domestic carbon market.

55.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Integrated Energy Policy:
1. The report was prepared in 2006.
2. It was approved by the Union Cabinet in December 2008.
3. Its core objective was to meet India's energy needs up to 2031-32.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
55.x: The report was prepared in 2006, approved in December 2008, and aimed to meet energy needs reliably, sustainably and at least cost up to 2031-32.
55.tq: Use the dates and the policy horizon together to identify the complete combination.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Statement 1: the report came in **2006** from **Kirit Parikh**'s Planning Commission committee.
Statement 2: the Union Cabinet approved it in **December 2008**.
Statement 3: aim — meet energy needs of all at least cost, reliably and sustainably, till **2031-32**.
xa: Pricing: **market-determined / trade-parity pricing** of tradable fuels.
Subsidies: **targeted** to the poor, not a general price subsidy.
Governance: **independent regulators + competition**.

55.s: The Integrated Energy Policy (2006) was prepared by an Expert Committee of the Planning Commission chaired by:
55.x: The Integrated Energy Policy was drafted by the Planning Commission's Expert Committee chaired by Kirit Parikh, reported in 2006 and was approved by the Cabinet in December 2008. The other economists did not chair this committee.
55.tq: IEP 2006 = Kirit Parikh committee.
xs: The expert committee was chaired by **Kirit Parikh** — option **(1)**.
The **Planning Commission** committee reported in **2006**; the Cabinet approved the policy in **December 2008**.
xa: Aim: meet energy needs at least cost, reliably and sustainably till **2031-32**.
Recommendations: **trade-parity pricing**, **targeted subsidies**, **efficiency**, **independent regulators**, **strategic oil reserves**.

55.s:
Consider the following statements about India Energy Security Scenarios 2047 (IESS 2047):
1. It is an open-access energy modelling and scenario tool of NITI Aayog.
2. It was launched in 2017.
3. It models energy supply and demand up to 2047 under Business-As-Usual and Ambitious scenarios.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
55.x: Statement 1 is correct: IESS 2047 is NITI Aayog's open-access modelling tool. Statement 2 is wrong: it was launched in 2014 (2017 is the Draft National Energy Policy). Statement 3 is correct: it models supply and demand to 2047 under BAU and Ambitious scenarios. So '1 and 3 only' is right; '1 only' leaves out the true statement 3, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 2.
55.tq: IESS 2047 launched 2014; Draft NEP 2017.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: **IESS 2047** is NITI Aayog's **open-access energy modelling / scenario tool**.
Statement 2 is wrong: it was launched in **2014**; **2017** is the **Draft National Energy Policy**.
Statement 3: it models supply and demand to **2047** under **Business-As-Usual** and **Ambitious** scenarios.
xa: Coal production: **582 Mtce (2012)** → **1190 (2040 BAU)** → **1385 (2040 Ambitious)**.
Primary energy import dependence: **31% (2012)** → **36-55% (2040)**.

55.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Electricity Act 2003 requires both a National Electricity Policy and a Tariff Policy.
2. The Tariff Policy of 2006 was revised in 2016.
3. The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026, which replaces the National Electricity Policy 2005, was issued by NITI Aayog.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
55.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Electricity Act 2003 requires the National Electricity Policy (2005) and the Tariff Policy (2006, revised 2016). Statement 3 is wrong: the Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 does replace NEP 2005, but it comes from the Ministry of Power, not NITI Aayog. So '1 and 2 only' is right; '1 only' leaves out the true statement 2, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 3.
55.tq: Electricity Act 2003 -> NEP 2005 + Tariff Policy 2006 (rev. 2016); Draft NEP 2026 = Ministry of Power.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: the **Electricity Act 2003** requires the **National Electricity Policy 2005** and the **Tariff Policy 2006**.
Statement 2: the Tariff Policy was revised in **2016**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **Draft National Electricity Policy 2026** comes from the **Ministry of Power**, not NITI Aayog.
xa: The Act lets **SERCs** fix the **RPO**.
The 2026 draft covers **hybrid RE, BESS, smart grids, Time-of-Day tariffs**.
⚠ NITI Aayog drafted the National **Energy** Policy (**2017**).

55.s: The energy-intensity targets for 208 industrial units under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001 are intended to feed into which mechanism?
o: The National Green Hydrogen Mission alone
The State Energy and Climate Index
55.x: Greenhouse-gas emission-intensity targets for 208 industrial units under the Energy Conservation Act 2001 feed into the domestic carbon market.
55.tq: Link the statutory target, the number of industrial units and the specific market mechanism.
xs: The **GHG emission-intensity targets for 208 industrial units** under the **EC Act 2001** feed the **domestic carbon market** — option **(1)**.
They are paired with the **Draft National Electricity Policy 2026** (Jun 2026).
The **State Energy and Climate Index** is a BEE index, not a market mechanism.
xa: **BEE** works under the **Energy Conservation Act 2001** and runs **NMEEE** under NAPCC.
Fiscal incentives (**13 May 2026**): States' incentives now linked to RE adoption → more **PPAs**.

55.s: India’s stated goal of achieving energy independence is associated with which year?
55.x: India has set the goal of achieving energy independence by 2047. Net zero emissions is the separate 2070 target.
55.tq: Distinguish the energy-independence year from the net-zero year.
xs: Energy independence is targeted by **2047** — option **(3)**.
**2070** is the separate **net zero** target.
xa: **INSA**'s framework: energy self-reliance by **2047**, net zero by **2070**.
**AP ICEP-2024** targets **Net Zero by 2047**, **160 GW+** clean energy.
**500 GW** non-fossil capacity by **2030** is the live Panchamrit target.

55.s: Which body is empowered under the Electricity Act, 2003 to fix Renewable Purchase Obligations?
o: The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy alone
55.x: The Electricity Act 2003 enables State Electricity Regulatory Commissions to fix Renewable Purchase Obligations.
55.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to distinguish the regulator from ministries and technical bodies.
xs: The **Electricity Act 2003** lets **State Electricity Regulatory Commissions (SERCs)** fix the **RPO** — option **(1)**.
RPO binds **DISCOMs** and **open-access/captive users** to buy a set share of RE power.
xa: The Act requires both the **National Electricity Policy 2005** and the **Tariff Policy 2006** (revised **2016**).
The **Central Electricity Authority** prepares the **National Generation Adequacy Plan 2026-27 to 2035-36**.
Electricity is a **concurrent subject** — **Entry 38, List III**.

55.s:
Under the Draft National Electricity Policy 2026, which combination of measures is associated with the stated current-policy direction?
1. 100 GW of pumped storage hydropower by 2047
2. Time-of-Day tariffs
3. A target of 100 GW of nuclear power by 2047
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
55.x: The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 includes 100 GW of pumped storage hydropower by 2047 and Time-of-Day tariffs. The 100 GW nuclear target by 2047 belongs to the newer NITI Aayog scenario study, not the stated policy combination here.
55.tq: Separate similarly dated policy proposals and avoid transferring a target from one document to another.
xs: Items **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
The **Draft National Electricity Policy 2026** includes **100 GW PSH by 2047** and **Time-of-Day (ToD) tariffs**.
Item 3 is wrong here: **~100 GW nuclear by 2047** is from NITI Aayog's "**Scenarios Towards Viksit Bharat and Net Zero**" study.
xa: The draft also covers **hybrid RE, BESS** and **smart grids**, and replaces **NEP 2005**.
It comes from the **Ministry of Power**.

55.s: The Entropy Effect, as discussed in energy-sector debates, refers to the risk that:
o: nuclear expansion automatically eliminates all import dependence
rapid decarbonisation without adequate buffers may increase grid volatility
slow electrification always reduces grid volatility
fuel subsidies cause a permanent fall in renewable generation
55.x: The Entropy Effect describes the possibility that rapid decarbonisation without sufficient buffers can raise grid volatility, as observed in the Netherlands and Spain.
55.tq: Apply the definition to the cause-effect relationship rather than selecting a general decarbonisation statement.
xs: The **"Entropy Effect"** is the risk that **rapid decarbonisation without buffers** raises **grid volatility** — option **(2)**.
The **Economic Survey 2025-26** cites the experience of the **Netherlands and Spain**.
xa: Other debates: import reliance **88% crude, 51% gas**; ~**25 GW** stranded gas capacity.
The **Draft National Electricity Policy 2026** answers with **BESS**, **100 GW PSH by 2047** and smart grids.

55.s: Which one of the following correctly reflects the Integrated Energy Policy's recommendation on tradable fuels?
o: Market-determined or trade-parity pricing with subsidies targeted to the poor
Free pricing only for imported petroleum products
Administrative pricing of all fuels without competition
Universal price subsidy irrespective of income
55.x: The policy recommended market-determined or trade-parity pricing for tradable fuels and targeted subsidies instead of a general price subsidy.
55.tq: Distinguish targeted subsidy from a general price subsidy.
xs: The policy recommended **market-determined / trade-parity pricing** of tradable fuels with **subsidies targeted to the poor** — option **(1)**.
It rejected a **general price subsidy**, so universal subsidy (4) is wrong; it backed **independent regulators + competition**, so administrative pricing without competition (3) is wrong.
xa: Pricing reforms followed: **petrol** deregulation **June 2010**, **diesel** **October 2014**.
**LPG subsidy** via DBT (**PAHAL**) — **2015**.
The government has cut **excise duty** on petrol and diesel during price spikes.

55.s:
Which of the following were recommended by the Integrated Energy Policy?
1. Diversifying energy supply across coal, nuclear, hydro, renewables and overseas assets
2. Building strategic oil reserves
3. A general price subsidy on fuels for all consumers
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
55.x: 1 and 2 are correct: for supply security the policy recommended diversifying supply (coal, nuclear, hydro, renewables, overseas assets) and building strategic oil reserves. 3 is wrong: it recommended subsidies targeted to the poor, not a general price subsidy, together with trade-parity pricing. So '1 and 2 only' is right; '1 only' leaves out the true item 2, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false item 3.
55.tq: IEP: market/trade-parity pricing + targeted (not general) subsidy.
xs: Items **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Item 1: for supply security it recommended **diversifying supply** across coal, nuclear, hydro, renewables and overseas assets.
Item 2: it recommended building **strategic oil reserves**.
Item 3 is wrong: subsidies were to be **targeted to the poor**, not a general price subsidy.
xa: Pricing logic: **trade-parity pricing + targeted subsidy**.
**PAHAL** (**2015**) delivered the LPG subsidy via **DBT**.
IEA's strategic oil stock standard: **90 days** of net imports.

55.s:
Consider the following statements about energy pricing reforms:
1. Diesel prices were deregulated along with petrol in June 2010.
2. LPG subsidy has been paid through Direct Benefit Transfer (PAHAL) since 2015.
3. Petrol prices were deregulated in June 2010.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
55.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: diesel was deregulated in October 2014. So '2 and 3 only'.
55.tq: Petrol 2010, diesel 2014, PAHAL 2015.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1 is wrong: **diesel** was deregulated in **October 2014**.
Statement 2 is correct: **LPG subsidy** via **DBT (PAHAL)** since **2015**.
Statement 3 is correct: **petrol** deregulated in **June 2010**.
xa: The **Integrated Energy Policy** recommended **trade-parity pricing** + **targeted** subsidies.
It was approved by the Cabinet in **December 2008**.
It also recommended building **strategic oil reserves**.

55.s:
The Draft National Energy Policy prepared by NITI Aayog has which of the following as its objectives?
1. Access to energy at affordable prices
2. Improved energy security and independence
3. Greater sustainability
4. Economic growth

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
55.x: The four objectives are affordable access, improved security and independence, greater sustainability and economic growth.
55.tq: Recognise a complete objectives list; the comprehensive option contains all four stated objectives.
xs: All four are objectives of the **Draft National Energy Policy** — option **(4)**.
They are **access at affordable prices**, **improved security and independence**, **greater sustainability** and **economic growth**.
xa: Fossil fuels supply nearly **90%** of commercial primary energy, increasingly imported → cutting fossil use serves both sustainability and security.
Prepared by **NITI Aayog** in **2017**.
Primary energy import dependence: **31% (2012)** → **36-55% (2040)**.

55.s: Fossil fuels account for approximately what share of India’s commercial primary energy supply, and what associated trend is highlighted?
o: Nearly 90%, with increasing dependence on imports
55.x: Fossil fuels constitute nearly 90% of commercial primary energy supply and are increasingly imported. Reducing fossil-fuel use therefore supports both sustainability and energy security.
55.tq: Combine the approximate share with the direction of import dependence; reject extreme percentage claims.
xs: Fossil fuels are **nearly 90%** of commercial primary energy supply and **increasingly imported** — option **(1)**.
So cutting fossil use serves both **sustainability** and **energy security**.
xa: Import reliance (**2 Jul 2026**): **88% crude, 51% gas**.
MoPNG target: cut oil imports **10%** from the **2014-15** level by **2022**.
Primary energy import dependence: **31% (2012)** → **36-55% (2040)**.

55.s:
Consider the following statements about the Ministry of Power:
1. It became an independent ministry from 2 July 1992.
2. It was earlier known as the Ministry of Energy Sources.
3. Its mandate includes exploration, refining and marketing of oil and gas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
55.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Ministry of Power became independent on 2 July 1992, having earlier been the Ministry of Energy Sources. Statement 3 is wrong: exploration, refining and marketing of oil and gas belong to MoPNG; the Ministry of Power handles electricity development, perspective planning, policy and project monitoring. So '1 and 2 only' is right; '1 only' leaves out the true statement 2, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 3.
55.tq: Power = electricity; oil and gas = MoPNG.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: the **Ministry of Power** became independent from **2 July 1992**.
Statement 2: it was earlier the **Ministry of Energy Sources**.

Statement 3 is wrong: **exploration, production, refining and marketing of oil and gas** is the mandate of **MoPNG**; the Ministry of Power handles **electricity development, perspective planning, policy and project monitoring**.
xa: Electricity is a **concurrent subject** — **Entry 38, List III**.
**MoPNG**'s regulator is **PNGRB** (Act **2006**); **OIL India** is a Navratna under it.
The **Draft National Electricity Policy 2026** comes from the **Ministry of Power** and replaces **NEP 2005**.

55.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the stated missions of the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy?
55.x: MNRE's missions include energy security, a larger share of clean power, energy availability and access, affordability and equity. Exclusive dependence on imported energy is not a mission.
55.tq: Find the option that reverses the objective of an energy ministry.
xs: **Exclusive dependence on imported energy** is not an MNRE mission — option **(1)**.
MNRE's five missions: **energy security**, **bigger share of clean power**, **energy availability + access**, **affordability** and **equity** — so options (2), (3) and (4) are all missions.
xa: This list of all five missions was the **APPSC-G2 2025** key.
MNRE evolved from **DNES 1982** → **MNES 1992** → **MNRE 2006**.
India's import reliance: **88% crude, 51% gas** — why energy security tops the agenda.

55.s:
Consider the following statements about NITI Aayog's 'Scenarios Towards Viksit Bharat and Net Zero' (Feb 2026):
1. It recommends small modular reactors and private participation.
2. It recommends about 50 GW of nuclear capacity by 2047.
3. It recommends 200-300 GW of nuclear capacity by 2070.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
55.x: Statement 2 is wrong: the study recommends about 100 GW of nuclear by 2047. Statements 1 and 3 are correct. So '1 and 3 only'.
55.tq: Nuclear: ~100 GW by 2047, 200-300 GW by 2070.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: it recommends **SMRs** + **private participation**.
Statement 2 is wrong: it recommends **~100 GW** of nuclear by **2047**.
Statement 3 is correct: **200-300 GW** by **2070**.
xa: IESS 2047 models scenarios to **2047** under **BAU** and **Ambitious**; launched **2014**.
Draft NEP 2017's four objectives: **access**, **security**, **sustainability**, **economic growth**.
Fossil fuels give nearly **90%** of commercial primary energy.

55.s:
Consider the following statements about India's NDCs:
1. The updated NDC (Aug 2022) targets a 45% cut in emissions intensity of GDP by 2030 from 2005 levels.
2. The new NDC (2031-35) targets 50% non-fossil capacity and a 45% cut in emissions intensity by 2035.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
55.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the new NDC targets 60% non-fossil capacity and a 47% cut in emissions intensity by 2035 (the 50% / 45% figures are the 2030 targets). So '1 only'.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(4)**: the **2022** NDC targets a **45%** cut in emissions intensity by **2030** over **2005**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the new NDC (**2031-35**) targets **60%** non-fossil and **47%** intensity cut by **2035**.
xa: The earlier NDC targeted **33-35%**.
**Long-Term Low Emission Development Strategy** went to **UNFCCC** at **COP27 (2022)**.

55.s: Before the expansion of electricity and clean cooking access, approximately how many people in India were without electricity and how many relied on solid biomass for cooking?
55.x: The earlier baseline was approximately 304 million people without electricity and 500 million relying on solid biomass for cooking.
55.tq: Avoid reversing the two baseline figures by matching each number with its sector.
xs: Earlier baseline: **~304 million** without electricity and **~500 million** on solid biomass for cooking — option **(1)**.
Option (3) simply reverses the two figures.
xa: Now: **near-universal household electrification** + expanded clean cooking access.
Supply hours (Jul 2026): **22.6 h rural / 23.4 h urban**; peak shortage **0.03%**.
Schemes behind it: **DDUGJY**, **Saubhagya**, **PMUY**.

55.s: Which one of the following combinations is correctly associated with the energy-sector challenges highlighted in recent debates?
o: 25 GW of stranded gas capacity and net-zero investment needs exceeding $20 trillion
88 GW of stranded gas capacity and no major investment requirement
51 GW of stranded gas capacity and investment needs of $5 trillion
25 GW of stranded nuclear capacity and investment needs below $2 trillion
55.x: The highlighted challenges include approximately 25 GW of stranded gas capacity and net-zero investment requirements exceeding $20 trillion.
55.tq: Match the two challenge figures and reject exaggerated or reversed values.
xs: ~**25 GW stranded gas capacity** and net-zero needs of **over $20 trillion** — option **(1)**.
**88%** and **51%** are import-reliance figures for crude and gas, not stranded capacity.
xa: The ES 2025-26 "**Entropy Effect**": fast decarbonisation without buffers raises grid volatility.
Net zero target: **2070** (Panchamrit).

55.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India's Panchamrit targets:
I. India targets 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030.
II. India targets meeting 50% of its energy requirements from renewable energy by 2030.
III. India targets reducing projected cumulative carbon emissions by 1 billion tonnes by 2030.
IV. India targets reducing carbon intensity by 45% by 2030.
V. India targets achieving Net Zero by 2070.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
o: I, II, III and IV only
II, III, IV and V only
I, II, III, IV and V
55.x: All five are correct: 500 GW non-fossil capacity, 50% of energy from renewables, 1 billion tonnes less emissions, and 45% lower carbon intensity by 2030, plus net zero by 2070.
55.tq: Recall the five Panchamrit targets.
n: India targets 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 13-16]
India targets meeting 50% of its energy requirements from renewable energy by 2030. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 13-16]
India targets reducing projected cumulative carbon emissions by 1 billion tonnes by 2030. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 13-16]
India targets reducing carbon intensity by 45% by 2030. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 13-16]
India targets achieving Net Zero by 2070. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 13-16]
xs: **All five — I, II, III, IV and V** — are correct — option **(4)**.
**Panchamrit** (**COP26, Glasgow, 2021**): **500 GW** non-fossil, **50%** energy from RE, **1 billion tonnes** less emissions by **2030**.
Also: **45%** lower carbon intensity by **2030** and **Net Zero by 2070**.
xa: Updated NDC (**2022**): **50%** installed capacity non-fossil by **2030**.
New NDC: **60%** non-fossil + **47%** intensity cut by **2035**.
Non-fossil share: **51.55%** on **30 Nov 2025**.

55.s: Which of the following is the correct constitutional position regarding electricity in India?
o: It is in Entry 38 of the Concurrent List in List III.
It is in Entry 97 of the Union List in List I.
It is in Entry 38 of the Union List in List I.
It is in Entry 28 of the State List in List II.
55.x: Electricity is a concurrent subject, placed under Entry 38 of List III.
55.tq: Check both the entry number and the list before choosing the constitutional classification.
xs: Electricity is a **concurrent subject** placed at **Entry 38 of List III** — option **(1)**.
It is therefore not in the **Union List (List I)** or the **State List (List II)**; both the Centre and the States can legislate on it.
xa: The **Electricity Act 2003** requires a **National Electricity Policy 2005** and a **Tariff Policy 2006** (revised **2016**).
Under the Electricity Act 2003, **SERCs** fix the **RPO** (Renewable Purchase Obligation).
The **Ministry of Power** became an independent ministry on **2 July 1992**.

55.s:
Consider the following statements about MNRE:
1. It began as the Department of Non-Conventional Energy Sources (DNES) in 1982.
2. It notified the National Policy on Geothermal Energy on 15 September 2025.
3. It was renamed MNRE in 1992.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
55.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: 1992 is when it became the Ministry of Non-Conventional Energy Sources (MNES); it was renamed MNRE in 2006. So '1 and 2 only'.
55.tq: DNES 1982 -> MNES 1992 -> MNRE 2006.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1 is correct: it began as **DNES** in **1982**.
Statement 2 is correct: MNRE notified the **National Policy on Geothermal Energy** on **15 Sep 2025**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **1992** = **MNES**; renamed **MNRE** in **2006**.
xa: Ministry of Power became independent on **2 July 1992**.
Electricity is a **concurrent subject**: **Entry 38, List III**.
**PNGRB** (Act **2006**) is the regulator under **MoPNG**.

55.s: The first in-depth review of India's energy policies was published by which institution?
55.x: The first in-depth review of India's energy policies was published by the International Energy Agency in 2020, in association with NITI Aayog.
55.tq: Identify the publishing institution rather than the associated Indian body.
xs: The first in-depth review of India's energy policies was by the **International Energy Agency (IEA)** — option **(3)**.
It was the **India 2020 Energy Policy Review**, released with **NITI Aayog** in **January 2020** (APPSC 2018 key).
**WEF** publishes the **Energy Transition Index**; **BEE** the **State Energy and Climate Index**.
xa: IEA is an **OECD-affiliated** body headquartered in **Paris**.
IEA reports: **World Energy Outlook**, **India Energy Outlook**, **Global Methane Tracker**, **Electricity Market Report**.
Exam distractors: **World Energy Council**, **OPEC**, **IRENA**.

55.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Energy Transition Index — World Economic Forum
State Energy and Climate Index — International Energy Agency
National Generation Adequacy Plan — NITI Aayog
India Energy Outlook — Bureau of Energy Efficiency
55.x: The Energy Transition Index is published by the World Economic Forum. The State Energy and Climate Index is associated with BEE, the National Generation Adequacy Plan with CEA, and India Energy Outlook with IEA.
55.tq: Start from the sure publisher-report pair and eliminate swapped institutions.
xs: **Energy Transition Index — World Economic Forum** is correctly matched — option **(1)**.
The **State Energy and Climate Index** is by **BEE**, not IEA.
The **National Generation Adequacy Plan 2026-27 to 2035-36** is by the **Central Electricity Authority**; **India Energy Outlook** is by the **IEA**.
xa: ⚠ Energy Transition Index = **WEF**; State Energy and Climate Index = **BEE** — a classic swap.
**Renewables Integration in India 2021** = **NITI Aayog + IEA**.

55.s: The report 'Renewables Integration in India 2021' was brought out by:
o: NITI Aayog and the International Energy Agency
MNRE and the International Renewable Energy Agency
Central Electricity Authority and the World Bank
Bureau of Energy Efficiency and the World Economic Forum
55.x: Renewables Integration in India 2021 was prepared by NITI Aayog with the IEA (APPSC-G1 2022 key). IRENA, the World Bank and WEF are common distractors; WEF publishes the Energy Transition Index and BEE the State Energy and Climate Index.
55.tq: RE Integration in India 2021 = NITI + IEA.
xs: **Renewables Integration in India 2021** was by **NITI Aayog and the International Energy Agency** — option **(1)** (APPSC-G1 2022 key).
**IRENA**, the **World Bank** and **WEF** are distractors; **WEF** publishes the **Energy Transition Index**, and **BEE** the **State Energy and Climate Index**.
xa: IEA and NITI Aayog also released the **India 2020 Energy Policy Review** in **January 2020**.
The **Central Electricity Authority** prepares the **National Generation Adequacy Plan 2026-27 to 2035-36**.

55.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Programme)
a. DDUGJY
b. PM Ujjwala Yojana
c. Saubhagya

List-II (Primary aim)
i. Last-mile household electrification
ii. LPG connections to BPL women
iii. Rural feeder separation and village electrification

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
55.x: DDUGJY is associated with feeder separation and village electrification, PMUY with LPG connections to BPL women, and Saubhagya with household electrification.
55.tq: Start from the sure pair PMUY–LPG and complete the programme-purpose mapping.
xs: Correct matching: **a–iii, b–ii, c–i** — option **(1)**.
**DDUGJY** (**2014**) → rural feeder separation, village electrification.
**PMUY** (**May 2016**, Ballia) → LPG connections to BPL women.
**Saubhagya** (**2017**) → last-mile household electrification.
xa: **PAHAL** (**2015**) → LPG subsidy via DBT.
**National Bioenergy Programme (2021-26)**: Phase I outlay **₹858 crore**; waste-to-energy, biomass, biogas.

55.s: The three components of Phase I of the National Bioenergy Programme are:
o: Solar pumps, wind farms and fuel cells
Coal gasification, oil refining and hydrogen storage
55.x: The three parts are waste-to-energy, biomass and biogas.
55.tq: Test the exact composition of the programme rather than its broader renewable-energy context.
xs: Phase I of the **National Bioenergy Programme** has three parts: **waste-to-energy, biomass and biogas** — option **(4)**.
**Solar pumps** belong to **PM-KUSUM**; **fuel cells** and **rooftop solar** are examples of distributed energy resources, not bioenergy components.
xa: The programme runs **2021-26**, with a Phase I outlay of **₹858 crore**.
**PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana**: rooftop solar for **1 crore households**.
**PM-KUSUM**: solar pumps + decentralised plants.

55.s: Which of the following set consists entirely of distributed energy resources?
o: Battery storage, biomass generators, fuel cells and rooftop solar PV
Large hydropower dams, coal plants, fuel cells and refineries
Battery storage, oil terminals, nuclear reactors and rooftop solar PV
Coal mines, biomass generators, gas pipelines and fuel cells
55.x: Battery storage, biomass generators, fuel cells and rooftop solar PV all qualify as distributed energy resources.
55.tq: Check every item against the small, consumer-near generation or storage concept.
xs: **Battery storage, biomass generators, fuel cells and rooftop solar PV** are all distributed energy resources — option **(1)** (UPSC 2024 key: all four).
DERs are **small generation/storage units near the consumer**; large dams, coal plants, refineries, oil terminals, nuclear reactors and pipelines are centralised assets, not DERs.
xa: DERs turn users into "**prosumers**" and **ease grid load**.
DER policy vehicles: **PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana** (rooftop solar for **1 crore households**) and **PM-KUSUM** (solar pumps + decentralised plants).
AP: **virtual net metering** with a focus on **SC/ST** households.

55.s: A household installs rooftop solar panels and battery storage, produces part of its own electricity and supplies surplus power to the grid. In the context of distributed energy resources, the household is functioning as a:
55.x: A consumer who also produces or stores electricity is a prosumer. DERs can make consumers prosumers and help ease the load on the grid.
55.tq: Apply the concept to a consumer who both produces and consumes electricity.
xs: A household that both produces and consumes power is a **prosumer** — option **(2)**.
**Distributed energy resources** — small generation/storage units near the consumer — let users become prosumers and **ease grid load**.
xa: Qualifying DERs: **battery storage, biomass generators, fuel cells, rooftop solar PV** (UPSC 2024 key).
**PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana**: rooftop solar for **1 crore households**.
AP uses **virtual net metering**, focused on **SC/ST** households.

55.s: Which of the following correctly matches the policy vehicle with its principal focus?
o: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana — rooftop solar for one crore households
PM-KUSUM — strategic oil stocks for 90 days of imports
PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana — coal-mine allocation
PM-KUSUM — nuclear research under the Prime Minister
55.x: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana focuses on rooftop solar for one crore households. PM-KUSUM concerns solar pumps and decentralised plants.
55.tq: Match each scheme with its target beneficiary and technology.
xs: **PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana — rooftop solar for 1 crore households** is correctly matched — option **(1)**.
**PM-KUSUM** is about **solar pumps + decentralised plants**, not oil stocks or nuclear research.
**90 days** of net imports is the **IEA** strategic oil-stock standard; nuclear research is under the **Department of Atomic Energy**.
xa: Both schemes are **DER policy vehicles** (Nov 2025; Mar 2026).
AP: **virtual net metering** for **SC/ST** households.

55.s: In Andhra Pradesh, virtual net metering associated with distributed energy policy has a particular focus on:
o: Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe households
55.x: Andhra Pradesh has introduced virtual net metering with a focus on SC/ST households.
55.tq: Identify the targeted beneficiary group rather than the technology alone.
xs: AP's **virtual net metering** focuses on **SC/ST households** — option **(3)**.
It is one of the **DER policy vehicles**, alongside **PM Surya Ghar** and **PM-KUSUM**.
xa: **NEDCAP** is AP's state nodal agency for renewable energy.
AP's **ICEP-2024**: **160 GW+** clean energy, **₹10 lakh crore** investment, **7.5 lakh jobs**, **Net Zero by 2047**.
First ICEP project: SAEL's **600 MW** solar in **Kadapa** (Rayalaseema).

55.s: Under the Renewable Purchase Obligation mechanism, which entities are required to purchase a prescribed share of electricity from renewable energy sources?
o: DISCOMs and open-access or captive users
Only generating companies owned by the Union Government
Only households consuming less than 100 kW
55.x: RPO requires DISCOMs and open-access or captive users to purchase a prescribed share of power from renewable energy sources. State Electricity Regulatory Commissions fix the obligation.
55.tq: Identify the obligated entities separately from the authority that sets the obligation.
xs: Under the **RPO**, **DISCOMs and open-access/captive users** must buy a set share of power from RE — option **(1)**.
The obligation is fixed by **SERCs** under the **Electricity Act 2003**, so the commissions are the setters, not the buyers.
xa: The Electricity Act 2003 also requires the **National Electricity Policy 2005** and **Tariff Policy 2006** (revised **2016**).
Fiscal incentives (**13 May 2026**) linked to RE adoption → more **PPAs**.
RE (incl. large hydro) stood at **253.96 GW** on **30 Nov 2025**.

55.s:
Consider the following statements about IREDA:
1. It is a specialised public-sector financial institution that promotes, develops and finances renewable-energy projects.
2. It was set up in 1987 under the Ministry of Power.
3. It was listed on the stock exchanges in November 2023 and received Navratna status in April 2024.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
55.x: Statement 1 is correct: IREDA promotes, develops and finances RE projects and also gives technical help. Statement 2 is wrong: it was set up in 1987 under MNRE, not the Ministry of Power. Statement 3 is correct: listed in November 2023, Navratna in April 2024. So '1 and 3 only' is right; '1 only' leaves out the true statement 3, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 2.
55.tq: IREDA: 1987, under MNRE; listed 2023, Navratna 2024.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: **IREDA** is a specialised public-sector FI that **promotes, develops and finances RE projects** and gives technical help.
Statement 2 is wrong: it was set up in **1987** under **MNRE**, not the Ministry of Power.
Statement 3: listed **Nov 2023**; **Navratna** status **Apr 2024**.
xa: MNRE lineage: **DNES 1982** → **MNES 1992** → **MNRE 2006**.
Sovereign green bonds were first issued by the **RBI** for the Government in **Jan 2023**.
Net-zero financing need: **over $20 trillion** by **2070**.

55.s:
Consider the following statements about green bonds:
1. The RBI first issued sovereign green bonds for the Government in January 2022.
2. Their proceeds are ring-fenced for projects with climate or environmental benefits.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
55.x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the first sovereign green bonds were issued in January 2023. So '2 only'.
55.tq: Sovereign green bonds: Jan 2023.
xs: Only statement **2** is correct — option **(1)**: green bond proceeds are **ring-fenced** for climate/environmental projects.
Statement 1 is wrong: **RBI** first issued **sovereign green bonds** in **Jan 2023**.
xa: **IREDA** was set up in **1987** under **MNRE**; **Navratna** in **Apr 2024**.
**RPO**: DISCOMs must buy a set share of power from RE.
DERs (UPSC 2024): **battery storage, biomass generators, fuel cells, rooftop solar PV** — all four.

55.s:
Consider the following statements about AP's Integrated Clean Energy Policy 2024 (ICEP-2024):
1. Its first project, SAEL's 600 MW solar plant in Kadapa (Rayalaseema), was commissioned on 22 May 2026.
2. It targets 160 GW+ of clean energy, Rs 10 lakh crore of investment and 7.5 lakh jobs.
3. It targets net zero for the State by 2070.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
55.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: ICEP-2024 targets net zero by 2047 (2070 is India's national target). So '1 and 2 only'.
55.tq: AP ICEP-2024: 160 GW+, net zero 2047; NEDCAP = nodal agency.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1 is correct: **SAEL's 600 MW** solar in **Kadapa** was commissioned **22 May 2026**.
Statement 2 is correct: **160 GW+**, **₹10 lakh crore**, **7.5 lakh jobs**.
Statement 3 is wrong: ICEP-2024 targets **Net Zero by 2047**; **2070** is India's national target.
xa: **NEDCAP** is AP's state nodal agency.
**ASSET** aims to cut power purchase cost to **₹4.20/unit by 2030**.
AP's DER push includes **virtual net metering** for **SC/ST** households.

55.s: Which body is Andhra Pradesh's state nodal agency for new and renewable energy?
55.x: NEDCAP (New and Renewable Energy Development Corporation of AP) is the state nodal agency. APGENCO is the state generation company, APERC the electricity regulator and APTRANSCO the transmission utility.
55.tq: AP RE nodal agency = NEDCAP.
xs: **NEDCAP** is Andhra Pradesh's **state nodal agency** for renewable energy — option **(1)**.
It is AP's counterpart to **MNRE**, the Centre's nodal ministry for all new and renewable energy.
xa: AP's **ICEP-2024**: **160 GW+** clean energy, **Net Zero by 2047**.
AP: **virtual net metering** with focus on **SC/ST** households.
First ICEP project: SAEL's **600 MW** solar in **Kadapa** (Rayalaseema).

55.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the International Energy Agency (IEA)?
o: An OECD-affiliated energy policy body headquartered in Paris
A UN specialised agency headquartered in Abu Dhabi
An oil producers' cartel headquartered in Vienna
A treaty body of solar-rich nations headquartered in Gurugram
55.x: The IEA is an OECD-affiliated energy policy body with headquarters in Paris; it publishes the World Energy Outlook. Abu Dhabi hosts IRENA, Vienna hosts OPEC and Gurugram hosts the International Solar Alliance.
55.tq: IEA = OECD-linked, Paris.
xs: The **IEA** is an **OECD-affiliated energy policy body headquartered in Paris** — option **(1)**.
It publishes the **World Energy Outlook**; its strategic oil stock standard is **90 days** of net imports.
xa: IEA reports: **Global Methane Tracker** (annual), **Electricity Market Report**, **Energy Efficiency Report**, **Net Zero Roadmap**.
With **NITI Aayog**: **India 2020 Energy Policy Review** and **Renewables Integration in India 2021**.
Exam distractors: **World Energy Council**, **OPEC**, **IRENA**.

55.s: The Long-Term Low Emission Development Strategy of India was submitted to which body at which event?
55.x: India submitted its Long-Term Low Emission Development Strategy to the UNFCCC at COP27 in 2022.
55.tq: Discriminate between the international body, conference number and year.
xs: India submitted its **Long-Term Low Emission Development Strategy** to the **UNFCCC at COP27 (2022)** — option **(3)**.
**COP26 (2021, Glasgow)** was where **Panchamrit** was announced, not the LT-LEDS submission.
xa: **Updated NDC (2022)**: **45%** emission intensity cut by **2030** over **2005**; **50%** non-fossil capacity.
**Net zero by 2070** is a Panchamrit pledge.

56.s:
Consider the following statements about the evolution of MNRE:
1. The Commission for Additional Sources of Energy (CASE) was set up in 1981.
2. The Department of Non-Conventional Energy Sources was created in 1982 in the Ministry of Science and Technology.
3. It was upgraded to a separate Ministry of Non-Conventional Energy Sources in 1992.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
56.x: Statement 1 is correct: CASE was set up in 1981. Statement 2 is wrong: DNES (1982) was created in the Ministry of Energy. Statement 3 is correct: it became the separate Ministry of Non-Conventional Energy Sources in 1992 (renamed MNRE in 2006). So '1 and 3 only' is right; '1 only' leaves out the true statement 3, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 2.
56.tq: CASE 1981 -> DNES 1982 (Ministry of Energy) -> MNES 1992 -> MNRE 2006.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: **CASE** (Commission for Additional Sources of Energy) was set up in **1981**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **DNES** (**1982**) was created in the **Ministry of Energy**, not the Ministry of Science and Technology.
Statement 3: it became the separate **Ministry of Non-Conventional Energy Sources (MNES)** in **1992**.
xa: MNES was renamed **MNRE** in **2006**.
⚠ Sequence: **CASE 1981 → DNES 1982 → MNES 1992 → MNRE 2006**.
India was the **first country in the world** to set up a ministry for non-conventional energy sources (APPSC 2023).

56.s:
Consider the following statements about institutions under MNRE:
1. NIBE, Kapurthala (Punjab), works on bio-energy.
2. SECI is the PSU implementing arm for the National Solar Mission and wind projects.
3. NIWE is located in Gurugram and is the technical focal point for solar R&D.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
56.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: NIBE (Kapurthala) is for bio-energy and SECI is the implementing arm for the National Solar Mission and wind projects. Statement 3 is wrong: NIWE is in Chennai (wind R&D, wind roadmap); the Gurugram solar R&D body is NISE. So '1 and 2 only' is right; '1 only' leaves out the true statement 2, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 3.
56.tq: NISE-Gurugram solar, NIWE-Chennai wind, NIBE-Kapurthala bio.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: **NIBE**, **Kapurthala** (Punjab), works on **bio-energy**.
Statement 2: **SECI** is the PSU implementing arm for the **National Solar Mission** and wind projects.
Statement 3 is wrong: **NIWE** is in **Chennai** (wind R&D); the **Gurugram** solar R&D focal point is **NISE**.
xa: ⚠ **NISE** = solar, Gurugram; **NIWE** = wind, Chennai; **NIBE** = bio-energy, Kapurthala.
NIWE is the **nodal agency for the wind roadmap**.
**DHRE, IIT Roorkee** gives technical support for small hydro but is **not** under MNRE's control.

56.s:
Consider the following statements about IREDA:
1. It is a PSU and NBFC under MNRE, set up in 1992.
2. It raises funds from the Government, multilaterals and capital markets, including green bonds.
3. It gives term, bridge and working-capital loans for renewable-energy and energy-efficiency projects.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
56.x: Statement 1 is wrong on the year: IREDA was set up in 1987 (1992 is when MNES was formed). Statements 2 and 3 are correct. So '2 and 3 only'.
56.tq: IREDA 1987; MNES 1992; MNRE 2006.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is wrong: **IREDA** was set up in **1987**; **1992** is when **MNES** was formed.
Statement 2 is correct: funds from Govt, multilaterals, capital market incl. **green bonds**.
Statement 3 is correct: **term, bridge and working-capital** loans for RE and EE.
xa: IREDA signed an MoU with **IIT Bhubaneswar** (APPSC 2024).
⚠ **NISE** = solar, **Gurugram**; **NIWE** = wind, **Chennai**; **NIBE** = bio-energy, **Kapurthala**.
**SECI** implements the **National Solar Mission**.

56.s: IREDA signed a Memorandum of Understanding for innovation and research in renewable energy with which institution?
56.x: IREDA's MoU for innovation and research in renewable energy was with IIT Bhubaneswar (APPSC 2024). IIT Tirupati is linked to an AP solar Centre of Excellence with UNSW, and IIT Roorkee's DHRE supports small hydro; IIT Madras is not mentioned.
56.tq: IREDA MoU = IIT Bhubaneswar.
xs: IREDA's MoU for RE innovation and research was with **IIT Bhubaneswar** — option **(1)** (APPSC 2024).
**IIT Tirupati** is linked to AP's **Solar CoE with UNSW** (31 Jul 2026); **IIT Roorkee** hosts **DHRE** (small hydro support).
xa: IREDA: **PSU + NBFC** under MNRE, est. **1987**.
It funds itself partly through **green bonds**.
⚠ **DHRE, IIT Roorkee** is **not** under MNRE's control.

56.s:
Consider the following statements regarding renewable-energy initiatives in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Tata Renewable has a planned 800 MW hybrid project involving an investment of ₹5,750 crore.
2. A solar Centre of Excellence is associated with IIT Tirupati and the University of New South Wales.
3. The reported hybrid project is a 5,000 MW floating solar project implemented by SECI.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
56.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Tata Renewable's 800 MW hybrid project (₹5,750 crore) and the solar Centre of Excellence with IIT Tirupati and UNSW. Statement 3 is false: the Tata project is an 800 MW hybrid project, not a 5,000 MW SECI floating solar project. So '1 and 2 only'.
56.tq: Separate the State-specific project from a similarly worded national scheme.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: **Tata Renewable**'s **800 MW hybrid** project costs **₹5,750 crore**.
Statement 2: AP's **Solar CoE** is with **IIT Tirupati + UNSW** (31 Jul 2026).
Statement 3 is wrong: the reported hybrid project is Tata's **800 MW**, not a SECI floating solar project.
xa: **SECI** is the implementing arm for the **National Solar Mission** and wind projects.
⚠ IREDA's research MoU was with **IIT Bhubaneswar**, not IIT Tirupati.

56.s: The National Clean Energy Fund was primarily established to fund:
o: Oil and gas exploration by private companies
Research and innovative projects in clean energy technologies
56.x: The NCEF was intended to fund research and innovative projects in clean energy technologies, promote renewable energy technologies and reduce carbon emissions.
56.tq: Match the fund with its stated purpose rather than its revenue source.
xs: The **NCEF** was set up to fund **research and innovative projects in clean energy technologies** — option **(4)**.
In exam wording: **promote renewable energy technologies and reduce carbon emissions** (APPSC-G2 2025 key).
xa: Created in **2010-11**, financed by a **clean energy cess on coal** (lignite and peat too).
Cess rose from **₹50/tonne** to **₹400/tonne**; later renamed **Clean Environment Cess**.
Coal cess subsumed into **GST Compensation Cess** (**July 2017**) → NCEF lost its dedicated inflow.

56.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Clean Energy Fund (NCEF):
1. It was financed by a clean energy cess on coal (including lignite and peat) from 2010-11.
2. With GST in July 2017, the cess was doubled, raising NCEF's dedicated inflow.
3. The cess rose from Rs 50 to Rs 400 per tonne.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
56.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the coal cess was subsumed into the GST Compensation Cess (July 2017), which ended NCEF's dedicated inflow. So '1 and 3 only'.
56.tq: NCEF: coal cess 2010-11, Rs 50 -> 400; ended by GST 2017.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(4)**.
Statement 1 is correct: **NCEF** (**2010-11**) was financed by a **clean energy cess on coal**.
Statement 2 is wrong: in **July 2017** the cess was **subsumed into GST Compensation Cess**, ending NCEF's dedicated inflow.
Statement 3 is correct: the cess rose from **₹50** to **₹400** per tonne.
xa: NCEF purpose: fund **research and innovative projects** in clean energy (APPSC-G2 2025).
The cess was later renamed **Clean Environment Cess**.

56.s: One Sun One World One Grid (OSOWOG) refers to:
o: A national coal transmission grid under the Ministry of Coal
A transnational solar grid under the International Solar Alliance
A biofuel blending programme under the Global Biofuels Alliance
A global wind-purchasing platform operated by IREDA
56.x: OSOWOG is a transnational solar grid under the International Solar Alliance; its roadmap was operationalised at the 8th ISA Assembly in New Delhi. It is not a coal grid, a biofuel programme or an IREDA platform.
56.tq: Distinguish the grid concept from other renewable-energy programmes by its transnational scope.
xs: **OSOWOG** is a **transnational solar grid under the International Solar Alliance** — option **(2)**.
Its roadmap was operationalised at the **8th ISA Assembly** in **New Delhi**.
xa: **Green Grids Initiative-OSOWOG** was launched by **India and UK** at **COP26 Glasgow (2021)**.
The **Global Biofuels Alliance** (G20 New Delhi, **Sept 2023**) promotes sustainable biofuels — a separate initiative.

56.s:
Match the initiative with the partners that launched it:
A. International Solar Alliance
B. Green Grids Initiative-OSOWOG
C. Global Biofuels Alliance
D. LeadIT
1. India and Sweden
2. India, USA and Brazil
3. India and the United Kingdom
4. India and France
56.x: ISA was launched by India and France (COP21, 2015); GGI-OSOWOG by India and the UK (COP26, 2021); the Global Biofuels Alliance by India, USA and Brazil (G20 New Delhi, 2023); and LeadIT by India and Sweden (UN Climate Action Summit, 2019). The other codes swap at least two pairs.
56.tq: ISA-France, GGI-UK, GBA-USA+Brazil, LeadIT-Sweden.
xs: Correct matching: **A-4, B-3, C-2, D-1** — option **(1)**.
**ISA** → **India + France** (COP21 Paris, **2015**); **GGI-OSOWOG** → **India + UK** (COP26 Glasgow, **2021**).
**Global Biofuels Alliance** → **India, USA, Brazil** (G20 New Delhi, **Sept 2023**); **LeadIT** → **India + Sweden** (UN Climate Action Summit **2019**).
xa: **LeadIT** focuses on **low-carbon heavy industry**.
ISA HQ: **Gurugram**.

56.s: The headquarters of the International Solar Alliance is located at:
56.x: The ISA, launched by India and France at COP21 in Paris in 2015, is headquartered in Gurugram (Haryana). Paris was only the launch venue, New Delhi hosted the 8th ISA Assembly, and Abu Dhabi hosts IRENA.
56.tq: ISA HQ = Gurugram.
xs: The **ISA** is headquartered at **Gurugram** — option **(1)**.
**Paris** was the launch venue (**COP21, 2015**); **New Delhi** hosted the **8th ISA Assembly**.
xa: ⚠ Gurugram also hosts **NISE**, MNRE's solar R&D focal point.
ISA is an **India + France** initiative and a **solar deployment** platform.

56.s: The 8th Mission Innovation ministerial meeting held with the 14th Clean Energy Ministerial in July 2023 was hosted at:
56.x: The combined MI-8 and 14th Clean Energy Ministerial event was held in Goa in July 2023.
56.tq: Match the energy event with its host city.
xs: **MI-8** with the **14th Clean Energy Ministerial** (**July 2023**) was hosted at **Goa** — option **(3)** (APPSC 2024).
**Gandhinagar** hosted **RE-INVEST** (4th edition, Sept 2024); **New Delhi** hosted the **8th ISA Assembly**.
xa: **India Energy Week**: **2023** Bengaluru, **2024** Goa, **2025** New Delhi.
8th ISA Assembly: **137 nations**, **36 organisations**.

56.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: First 24x7 solar-powered village — Cochin International Airport
56.x: Diu was the first 100% solar-powered Union Territory during daytime. Modhera was the first 24x7 solar-powered village, Cochin International Airport the first fully solar-powered airport, and Aditya the first solar ferry.
56.tq: Start with the distinctive Union Territory-location pair and eliminate crossed firsts.
xs: **Diu** was the **first 100% solar-powered UT** (daytime) — option **(1)**.
The solar ferry **Aditya** (**2017**) runs on the **Vaikom–Thavanakkadavu** route in Kerala, not at Ayodhya.
xa: **Ayodhya** hosts the **2-year biodiesel project** by Belgian firm **VITO** (Apr 2023; APPSC 2023).
India was the **first country** to set up a ministry for non-conventional energy sources.

56.s: The two-year biodiesel project of the Belgian firm VITO, launched in April 2023, is located at:
56.x: VITO's two-year biodiesel project (April 2023) is at Ayodhya, UP (APPSC 2023). Diu is the first 100% solar-powered UT in daytime, Vaikom is on the route of the solar ferry Aditya, and Gandhinagar hosted RE-INVEST 2024.
56.tq: VITO biodiesel = Ayodhya.
xs: **VITO**'s **2-year biodiesel project** (Apr 2023) is at **Ayodhya**, UP — option **(1)** (APPSC 2023).
**Diu** = first **100% solar UT** (daytime); **Vaikom** = solar ferry **Aditya**; **Gandhinagar** = **RE-INVEST** 4th edition.
xa: VITO is a **Belgian** firm.
First solar ferry **Aditya** dates to **2017**.

56.s:
Consider the following statements about India's global renewable-energy position:
1. India ranks 3rd in the world in total renewable-energy capacity.
2. India ranks 4th in the world in wind capacity.
3. India overtook China to become the 3rd-largest solar power producer.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
56.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: India is 3rd in total RE capacity and 4th in wind. Statement 3 is wrong: India overtook Japan, not China, to become the 3rd-largest solar power producer. So '1 and 2 only' is right; '1 only' leaves out the true statement 2, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 3.
56.tq: 3rd RE, 4th wind, passed Japan in solar generation.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: India is **3rd** in total RE capacity (ES 2025-26).
Statement 2: India is **4th** in wind.
Statement 3 is wrong: India overtook **Japan**, not China, to become the **3rd-largest solar power producer** (Aug 2026).
xa: ⚠ Older notes put India **4th** in total RE capacity (IYB 2026).
India was the **2nd-largest solar growth market** in 2025.

56.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India’s target is to achieve 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030.
2. The COP26 Panchamrit goal of 50% non-fossil capacity by 2030 was reported as having been achieved five years early.
3. The non-fossil share was reported as 51.93% by December 2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
56.x: India has a 500 GW non-fossil capacity target for 2030; the 50% Panchamrit capacity goal was reported as achieved five years early, and the share was 51.93% by December 2025.
56.tq: Separate a long-term capacity target from an already-reported milestone and percentage.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Statement 1: target **500 GW** non-fossil capacity by **2030**.
Statement 2: the Panchamrit goal of **50%** non-fossil capacity by **2030** was met **five years early** (Nov 2025).
Statement 3: the share was **51.93%** by **Dec 2025**.
xa: Installed capacity (15 Aug 2026): ~**552 GW**; non-fossil **>54%**.
⚠ Coal is still ~**55%** of primary energy and **>70%** of generation (Aug 2026).

56.s: Which one of the following correctly states the reported wind-energy targets?
56.x: The reported wind-energy targets are 100 GW by 2030 and 155 GW by 2035.
56.tq: Check the order of milestones before selecting the numerical pair.
xs: Wind targets: **100 GW by 2030** and **155 GW by 2035** — option **(4)** (Jun 2026).
**58.14 GW** is current wind capacity and **172 GW** is solar **module** manufacturing capacity — not targets.
xa: India ranks **4th** in the world in wind.
**NIWE** (Chennai) is the nodal agency for the **wind roadmap**.
Solar capacity: **164.59 GW** (15 Aug 2026).

56.s: India became the first country in the world to establish a Ministry specifically for:
56.x: India was the first country in the world to set up a ministry for non-conventional energy sources.
56.tq: Direct recall of a distinctive international first.
xs: India was the **first country in the world** to set up a ministry for **non-conventional energy sources** — option **(2)** (APPSC 2023).
That ministry was the **MNES**, created in **1992** by upgrading **DNES** (**1982**).
xa: MNES was renamed **MNRE** in **2006**.
The earliest body was **CASE** (**1981**).
Institutions under MNRE: **NISE** (Gurugram, solar), **NIWE** (Chennai, wind), **NIBE** (Kapurthala, bio-energy).

56.s: PM Surya Sarovar projects are required to add battery energy storage systems (BESS) having a minimum duration of:
56.x: PM Surya Sarovar projects must add BESS with a minimum storage duration of two hours.
56.tq: Identify the minimum technical specification from close duration options.
xs: **PM Surya Sarovar** projects must add **BESS** of at least **2 hours** — option **(2)** (1 Aug 2026).
Globally, **25%** of new utility-scale solar is paired with batteries (**IRENA 2025**) — battery storage is a key distributed energy resource.
xa: Rooftop Solar Phase-II (target **40,000 MW**) was **subsumed in PM Surya Ghar**.
Bio-power stands at ~**11.75 GW** (Aug 2026).
Green-hydrogen **fuel cells** are more efficient than combustion engines.

56.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The National Biogas and Manure Management Programme supports family biogas plants.
2. The Biomass Power and Bagasse Co-generation Programme supports biomass-based power and bagasse co-generation.
3. Phase-II of the Grid-Connected Rooftop Solar Programme continues as a scheme separate from PM Surya Ghar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
56.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: family biogas plants come under the National Biogas and Manure Management Programme, and biomass power and bagasse co-generation under its own programme. Statement 3 is wrong: Phase-II of the Grid-Connected Rooftop Solar Programme (target 40,000 MW) was subsumed in PM Surya Ghar. So '1 and 2 only' is right; '1 only' leaves out the true statement 2, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 3.
56.tq: Rooftop Phase-II is now inside PM Surya Ghar.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: the **National Biogas and Manure Management Programme** supports **family biogas plants**.
Statement 2: the **Biomass Power and Bagasse Co-generation Programme** covers biomass power and bagasse co-generation.
Statement 3 is wrong: Rooftop Solar Phase-II (target **40,000 MW**) was **subsumed in PM Surya Ghar**.
xa: Bio-power capacity: ~**11.75 GW** (Aug 2026).
Off-grid tribal: New Solar Power Scheme under **PM JANMAN + DA JGUA** electrified **4,919 households** in 2025.

56.s:
Match List-I (Report) with List-II (Publisher):
List-I
a. Renewable Energy Country Attractiveness Index (RECAI)
b. Renewable Capacity Statistics
c. World Energy Outlook
d. Renewables Integration in India (2021)
List-II
i. IEA
ii. EY (Ernst & Young)
iii. IRENA
iv. IEA with NITI Aayog
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
56.x: RECAI is EY's (ii); Renewable Capacity Statistics is IRENA's (iii); the World Energy Outlook is the IEA's (i); Renewables Integration in India 2021 was by the IEA with NITI Aayog (iv; APPSC-G1 2022).
56.tq: RECAI = EY; capacity statistics and cost reports = IRENA; WEO = IEA.
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv** — option **(4)**.
**RECAI** = **EY**; **Renewable Capacity Statistics** = **IRENA**.
**World Energy Outlook** = **IEA**; **Renewables Integration in India (2021)** = **IEA with NITI Aayog**.
xa: IRENA's **Renewable Power Generation Costs in 2025**: >**90%** of new RE cheaper than fossil.
India: **3rd** in total RE capacity, **4th** in wind (Aug 2026).
India overtook Japan as **3rd-largest solar power producer**.

56.s: Which statement correctly compares green-hydrogen fuel cells and combustion engines?
o: Fuel cells convert electricity exclusively into biomass.
Fuel cells can operate only with coal-derived hydrogen.
Green-hydrogen fuel cells are generally more efficient than combustion engines.
Combustion engines are always more efficient than fuel cells.
56.x: Green-hydrogen fuel cells are more efficient than combustion engines in the comparison stated.
56.tq: Use the direct efficiency comparison and reject absolute reversals.
xs: **Green-hydrogen fuel cells** are **more efficient than combustion engines** — option **(3)**.
Fuel cells are listed as a **distributed energy** resource alongside rooftop PV, batteries and biomass.
xa: Battery storage: **25%** of new utility-scale solar paired with batteries (IRENA 2025).
**PM Surya Sarovar** projects need **≥2-hour BESS**.

57.s:
Arrange the following coal types in descending order of carbon content:
A. Lignite
B. Anthracite
C. Peat
D. Bituminous
E. Sub-bituminous
57.x: The descending order is anthracite, bituminous, sub-bituminous, lignite and peat.
57.tq: Arrange the grades by the carbon-content hierarchy, not by age or colour.
xs: Descending carbon order: **anthracite > bituminous > sub-bituminous > lignite > peat** — **B, D, E, A, C** — option **(1)**.
Bituminous has **60-80%** carbon, lignite **40-55%**, peat **<40%**.
xa: **Peat** is the **first stage of wood to coal**.
**Sub-bituminous** lies between bituminous and lignite and is used in **power plants**.
**Bituminous** is the most widely used type and the **coking grade**.

57.s: Which type of coal is most widely used and is also the coking grade?
57.x: Bituminous coal is the most widely used type and includes the coking grade.
57.tq: Identify the coal type by its use and industrial grade.
xs: **Bituminous** coal is the most widely used type and the **coking grade** — option **(1)**.
It has **60-80%** carbon (some notes say 40-80%) and occurs in **Jharkhand, Odisha, WB, Chhattisgarh, MP**.
**Lignite** is "brown coal" with **40-55%** carbon; **sub-bituminous** is used in power plants.
xa: **Jharia** is the largest **coking-coal** field.
Coking coal is imported mainly from **Australia**.

57.s:
Consider the following statements about types of coal:
1. Lignite, also called brown coal, contains about 60-80% carbon.
2. Peat contains less than 40% carbon and is the first stage in the change of wood into coal.
3. Sub-bituminous coal lies between bituminous coal and lignite in rank and is used in power plants.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
57.x: Statement 3 is correct: sub-bituminous coal is between bituminous and lignite and is used in power plants. Statement 1 is wrong: lignite (brown coal) has about 40-55% carbon; 60-80% is bituminous. Statement 2 is correct: peat has under 40% carbon and is the first stage from wood to coal. So '2 and 3 only'; '3 only' misses statement 2, and the options with 2 include a false statement.
57.tq: Carbon ladder: anthracite > bituminous (60-80) > sub-bituminous > lignite (40-55) > peat (<40).
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is wrong: **lignite** (brown coal) has **40-55%** carbon; **60-80%** is **bituminous**.
Statement 2 is correct: **peat** has **<40%** carbon — first stage from wood to coal.
Statement 3 is correct: **sub-bituminous** lies between bituminous and lignite; used in **power plants**.
xa: Carbon order: **anthracite > bituminous > sub-bituminous > lignite > peat**.
⚠ **Gondwana** coal = **98%** of reserves, coking coal; **Tertiary** = NE India, ~**2%**.
Lignite leaders: **Tamil Nadu (Neyveli)** → Rajasthan → Gujarat.

57.s: Which of the following set of places is associated with lignite occurrences mentioned in the classification?
57.x: Neyveli, Palana and Lakhimpur are identified with lignite occurrences. The other groups are associated with major coalfields of higher-rank coal regions.
57.tq: Recognise the lignite-location group instead of a group of Gondwana coalfields.
xs: **Neyveli, Palana and Lakhimpur** are lignite sites — option **(1)**.
**Korba, Raigarh** (Chhattisgarh), **Singrauli** (MP), **Talcher, Deogarh** (Odisha), **Raniganj** (WB), **Jharia, Bokaro, Giridih** (Jharkhand) are coalfields.
xa: Neyveli is in **Tamil Nadu**, Palana in **Rajasthan**, Lakhimpur in **Assam**.
Lignite: **40-55%** carbon, "**brown coal**"; reserves **47.295 BT**.

57.s: Jharia coalfield is particularly noted for which of the following?
o: Lignite deposits in the Satpura Basin
The first commercial coal mine in India
57.x: Jharia in Jharkhand is the largest coking-coal field and is situated in the Damodar Valley.
57.tq: Directly distinguish the coalfield by its special characteristic.
xs: **Jharia** (Jharkhand) is India's **largest coking-coal field** — option **(2)**.
The **first coal mine** was at **Raniganj** (**1774**); **Tertiary coal** is at **Mawlong** (Meghalaya) and Makum (Assam); **Satpura** is an MP basin.
xa: **Jharkhand** has India's **largest coal reserves**; other Jharkhand fields: **Bokaro, Giridih, Karanpura**.
The **Damodar valley** holds about **one-fourth** of India's coal.
Coking coal is a **Gondwana** coal; the MMDR amendment made it a **Critical and Strategic Mineral**.

57.s: Which of the following pairs of coalfields is correctly associated with Odisha?
57.x: Talcher and Deogarh, including the IB Valley, are coalfields of Odisha. Jharia and Bokaro are in Jharkhand, Korba and Raigarh in Chhattisgarh, and Singareni and Makum in Telangana and Assam respectively.
57.tq: Group coalfields by State and reject cross-State substitutions.
xs: **Talcher and Deogarh (IB Valley)** are Odisha coalfields — option **(4)**.
**Korba, Raigarh** = **Chhattisgarh**; **Jharia, Bokaro** = **Jharkhand**; **Singareni** = **Telangana** and **Makum** = **Assam**.
xa: **Talcher** lies on the **Brahmani**; it will host the first **gasification-based fertiliser plant** (due Dec **2027**).
APGENCO buys washed coal from **MCL's IB Valley Washery**.

57.s: To improve coal quality for its RTPP and Dr NTTPS units, APGENCO buys washed coal from:
57.x: APGENCO buys washed coal from MCL's IB Valley Washery, posts engineers at mines to stop grade slippage and seeks better coal from SCCL. The other sources are not the ones stated.
57.tq: APGENCO washed coal = MCL IB Valley Washery.
xs: APGENCO buys **washed coal from MCL's IB Valley Washery** — option **(1)**.
It feeds **RTPP 600 MW** and **Dr NTTPS 500/800 MW** units.
xa: APGENCO also **posts engineers at mines** to stop grade slippage.
It seeks **better coal from SCCL**.
IB Valley (**Deogarh**) is in **Odisha**.

57.s: Which one of the following coalfields is correctly matched with its State and distinctive feature?
57.x: Mawlong is located in Meghalaya and is associated with Tertiary coal. Satpura and Umaria are in Madhya Pradesh, while Talcher is in Odisha.
57.tq: Use the distinctive geological term as the anchor pair.
xs: **Mawlong — Meghalaya — Tertiary coal** is correctly matched — option **(1)**.
**Satpura** (Pench-Kanhan, Pathakhera) is in **Madhya Pradesh**, not Odisha.
**Talcher** is in **Odisha** on the **Brahmani**; the **Hasdeo** valley belongs to **Korba** (Chhattisgarh).
xa: **Tertiary coal**: NE India and J&K, about **2%** of reserves.
⚠ **Gondwana** = **98%**, coking coal; **Tertiary** = NE India, about 2%.
**Makum** (Assam) is another NE coalfield.

57.s: Which of the following correctly represents the reserve and leading-State position of lignite?
o: 15.000 billion tonnes; Rajasthan led by Singrauli
47.295 billion tonnes; Odisha led by Talcher
47.295 billion tonnes; Tamil Nadu led by Neyveli
389.421 billion tonnes; Jharkhand led by Jharia
57.x: Lignite resources are estimated at 47.295 billion tonnes, with Tamil Nadu leading through the Neyveli region, followed by Rajasthan and Gujarat.
57.tq: Match the resource figure with the correct leading State and field.
xs: Lignite reserves are **47.295 BT**, led by **Tamil Nadu (Neyveli)** — option **(3)**.
Order of lignite states: **Tamil Nadu → Rajasthan → Gujarat**.
**389.421 BT** is total **coal** resources (GSI, **1 Apr 2024**); **Talcher** and **Jharia** are coal, not lignite, fields.
xa: Lignite ("**brown coal**") has **40-55%** carbon.
Other lignite sites: **Palana** (Rajasthan), **Lakhimpur** (Assam); **Barmer** (Rajasthan).

57.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Bokaro — Jharkhand
2. Giridih — Jharkhand
3. Raigarh — Chhattisgarh
4. Neyveli — Tamil Nadu
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
57.x: Bokaro and Giridih are in Jharkhand, Raigarh is in Chhattisgarh and Neyveli lignite field is in Tamil Nadu.
57.tq: Verify each location pair before selecting the complete combination.
xs: All four pairs are correct — option **(4)**.
**Bokaro** and **Giridih** are in **Jharkhand**; **Raigarh** is in **Chhattisgarh**; **Neyveli** is in **Tamil Nadu**.
xa: Other Jharkhand fields: **Jharia** (largest coking coal), **Karanpura**.
**Korba** (Chhattisgarh) lies on the **Hasdeo** (Mahanadi basin).
**Singareni** is in **Telangana**.

57.s:
Consider the following statements about Gondwana coal:
1. It is approximately 250–300 million years old.
2. It accounts for about 98% of India’s coal reserves.
3. It occurs in the Damodar, Mahanadi, Son and Godavari valleys.
4. It consists predominantly of Tertiary lignite deposits.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
57.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Gondwana coal is not predominantly Tertiary lignite; Tertiary deposits are younger and include lignite.
57.tq: Reject the statement that swaps Gondwana characteristics with Tertiary characteristics.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Gondwana coal is **250-300 million years** old, forms **98%** of reserves and occurs in the **Damodar, Mahanadi, Son, Godavari** valleys.
Statement 4 is wrong: **Tertiary** coal is separate — found in **NE India and J&K**, about **2%** of reserves.
xa: Gondwana coal holds the **coking coal**.
⚠ **Gondwana** = 98%, coking; **Tertiary** = NE India, about 2% (e.g. **Mawlong**, Meghalaya).

57.s:
Consider the following statements about India's coal reserves:
1. The GSI estimated India's coal resources at 389.421 billion tonnes as of 1 April 2024.
2. Jharkhand has the largest coal reserves among the States.
3. The Damodar valley holds about half of India's coal reserves.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
57.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: GSI put resources at 389.421 BT (1 April 2024) and Jharkhand leads. Statement 3 is wrong: the Damodar valley holds about one-fourth, not half, of India's coal. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses true statement 2, and the other two include false statement 3.
57.tq: 389.421 BT; Jharkhand first; Damodar = one-fourth.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: **GSI** put coal resources at **389.421 BT** (**1 Apr 2024**).
Statement 2: **Jharkhand** has the largest reserves.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **Damodar** valley holds about **one-fourth**, not half.
xa: Reserves are mainly in **Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh**, WB, MP, Telangana, Maharashtra.
⚠ Older notes: about **344 BT** and "**4th largest in the world**".

57.s: India recorded coal production of how much in 2024–25, marking the first year in which production exceeded one billion tonnes?
57.x: India recorded 1,047.50 MT of coal production in 2024–25, the first time production crossed one billion tonnes.
57.tq: Use the exact production figure and distinguish it from the target and import figures.
xs: Coal output was **1,047.50 MT in 2024-25**, the first year above **1 billion tonnes** — option **(2)**.
xa: Imports fell **7.9%** to **243.62 MT**, saving about **$7.13 billion**.
By Aug 2025 output reached **381.749 MT**.
Coal meets about **55%** of commercial energy needs.

57.s: Coal accounts for approximately what share of India’s commercial energy needs?
57.x: Coal meets about 55% of India’s commercial energy needs.
57.tq: Distinguish the share in commercial energy needs from the higher share in power generation.
xs: Coal meets about **55%** of India's **commercial energy needs** — option **(3)**.
**About 70%** (some notes **71.4%**) is coal's share of **power generation**, not energy needs.

57.s:
Consider the following statements about Coal India Limited (CIL):
1. CIL is described as the world's largest coal producer.
2. CMPDI functions as the planning arm of CIL.
3. Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) is one of CIL's seven producing subsidiaries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
57.x: Statement 1 is correct: CIL is the world's largest coal producer. Statement 3 is wrong: the seven producing subsidiaries are ECL, BCCL, CCL, NCL, WCL, SECL and MCL; SCCL is a Telangana-GoI company, not a CIL subsidiary. Statement 2 is correct: CMPDI is CIL's planning arm. So '1 and 2 only'.
57.tq: CIL subsidiaries are all '...CL' coalfields companies; SCCL belongs to Telangana (51%) and GoI (49%).
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1 is correct: **Coal India Ltd** is the **world's largest coal producer**.
Statement 2 is correct: **CMPDI** is CIL's **planning arm**.
Statement 3 is wrong: CIL's seven subsidiaries are **ECL, BCCL, CCL, NCL, WCL, SECL, MCL**; **SCCL** is **51% Telangana, 49% GoI**.
xa: **SHAKTI policy** (**2017**) replaced the NCDP-2007 linkage regime.
Commercial coal auctions began in **2020**; **134 mines** sold after **12 rounds**.
**Coking coal** is now a **Critical and Strategic Mineral**.

57.s:
Consider the following statements about the SHAKTI coal linkage policy:
1. It was introduced in 2017.
2. It replaced the NCDP-2007 linkage regime.
3. Under it, coal linkages are given only through administrative nomination.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
57.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: SHAKTI (2017) replaced the NCDP-2007 linkage regime. Statement 3 is wrong: under SHAKTI, linkages are given through auction or tariff-based bidding, not administrative nomination. So '1 and 2 only' is right; '1 only' leaves out the true statement 2, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 3.
57.tq: SHAKTI 2017 = auction/tariff-based bidding for linkages.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
**SHAKTI** came in **2017** and replaced the **NCDP-2007** linkage regime.
Statement 3 is wrong: linkages are given through **auction or tariff-based bidding**.
xa: **199 mines** were allocated under the **CMSP Act 2015** and **MMDR Act 1957**.
Revenue-sharing **commercial auctions** began in **2020**.

57.s:
Consider the following statements about coal gasification:
1. The syngas produced consists mainly of ammonia and nitrogen.
2. Syngas can be used to run Integrated Gasification Combined Cycle (IGCC) power plants.
3. Coal is partly oxidised with oxygen and steam at high temperature and pressure.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
57.x: Statement 3 is correct: coal gasification partly oxidises coal with oxygen and steam at high temperature and pressure. Statement 1 is wrong: syngas is CO + H2 + CH4 + CO2; ammonia is a downstream product, not a syngas constituent. Statement 2 is correct: syngas can run IGCC plants. So '2 and 3 only'.
57.tq: Syngas = CO, H2, CH4, CO2; ammonia/urea, methanol, SNG are products made from it.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 is wrong: **syngas** = **CO + H2 + CH4 + CO2**; **ammonia** is a downstream product.
Statement 2 is correct: syngas can run **IGCC** power plants.
Statement 3 is correct: coal is **partly oxidised** with **oxygen + steam** at high temperature and pressure.
xa: ⚠ UPSC 2025: of ethanol, nitroglycerine and urea, **only two** (ethanol + urea) come from gasification.
**National Coal Gasification Mission**: **100 MT of coal by 2030**.
**JSPL Angul** is the only commercial-scale gasification plant.

57.s:
Consider the following substances:
1. Ethanol
2. Nitroglycerine
3. Urea
Which of the substances listed above can be produced through coal gasification?
57.x: Ethanol and urea can be produced through coal gasification. Nitroglycerine is not included among the stated products.
57.tq: Discriminate between direct gasification products and an unrelated chemical.
xs: Only **ethanol and urea** can be made by coal gasification — option **(4)** (UPSC 2025 key: **only two**).
**Nitroglycerine** is not among the gasification products.
xa: Urea comes via **ammonia for fertilisers**.
Other products: **SNG, methanol, hydrogen, DME, ammonium nitrate**.
**Talcher** will host the first gasification-based fertiliser plant (by Dec **2027**).

57.s:
With reference to the Scheme for Promotion of Surface Coal/Lignite Gasification, consider the following statements:
1. It was approved by the Cabinet on 13 May 2026.
2. Its outlay is ₹37,500 crore.
3. The incentive may be up to 20% of plant and machinery cost.
4. The incentive is capped at ₹5,000 crore per project.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
57.x: All four statements correctly describe the scheme approved on 13 May 2026, including its outlay, incentive rate and project-wise ceiling.
57.tq: Check the date, outlay, percentage and cap as separate components of one scheme.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Approved by the Cabinet on **13 May 2026**, outlay **₹37,500 crore**.
Incentive up to **20% of plant and machinery cost**, capped at **₹5,000 crore per project**.
xa: It targets about **75 MT** toward the **100 MT** goal; coal linkage tenure extended to **30 years**.
Earlier scheme (**2024**): **₹8,500 crore** for public and private projects.
Status (5 Sep 2026): **no bidders** so far.

57.s: To promote coal gasification, commercial coal blocks get what rebate on revenue share, and on what condition?
o: 50% rebate if at least 10% of output goes to gasification
10% rebate if at least 50% of output goes to gasification
20% rebate if at least 5% of output goes to gasification
100% rebate if at least 25% of output goes to gasification
57.x: Commercial blocks get a 50% rebate on revenue share if at least 10% of their output is used for gasification. The other options swap or invent the figures.
57.tq: Gasify >=10% -> 50% revenue-share rebate.
xs: Commercial blocks get a **50% rebate on revenue share** if **≥10%** of output goes to gasification — option **(1)**.
Option (2) simply swaps the two figures.
