Ammonification = **decomposer bacteria and fungi**.
Fixation agents include **Azotobacter** and the **Haber process**.

74.s:
Consider the following processes:
1. Biological fixation
2. Ammonification
3. Nitrification
4. Denitrification
Which of the above add usable nitrogen to soil?
74.x: Biological fixation, ammonification and nitrification add usable nitrogen to soil. Denitrification removes nitrogen from soil by returning it as N2 gas to the atmosphere.
74.tq: Classify each process by its net effect on soil nitrogen.
xs: **Biological fixation, ammonification and nitrification** (1, 2 and 3 only) add usable N — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Denitrification removes** N by turning nitrate into N2 returned to air.
xa: Other N inputs: **lightning** (atmospheric fixation) and **industrial fixation** (fertilisers).
Biological fixation uses the enzyme **nitrogenase**.
Fertiliser runoff (**N and P**) → **algal blooms / eutrophication**.

74.s:
Consider the following pairs:
a. Azotobacter — Free-living nitrogen fixer
b. Azospirillum — Associated with cereals, millets and vegetables
c. Frankia — Symbiotic actinomycete in non-legumes
d. Azolla — Denitrifying organism
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
74.x: Azotobacter and Azospirillum are free-living nitrogen fixers used with crops. Frankia forms symbiotic associations with non-legumes such as Alnus and Casuarina, whereas Azolla fixes nitrogen in association with rice fields and is not a denitrifying organism.
74.tq: Find the wrong organism–function pairing before selecting the coded combination.
xs: Pairs **a, b and c** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Azotobacter** and **Azospirillum** are **free-living** fixers for cereals, millets, vegetables.
**Frankia** is a **symbiotic actinomycete** in non-legumes (Alnus, Casuarina).
Pair d is wrong: **Azolla** is an aquatic fern with **Anabaena** that fixes N in rice fields, not a denitrifier.
xa: Denitrifiers: **Pseudomonas, Thiobacillus**.
**Rhizobium** = symbiotic, in **root nodules of legumes**.
Phosphate solubilisers: **Bacillus megaterium**, **Pseudomonas striata**.

74.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Azolla — aquatic fern associated with Anabaena and useful for nitrogen supply in paddy
Mycorrhiza — free-living aerobic bacterium for non-legumes
Blue-green algae — fungus-root association for phosphorus uptake
PSB — aquatic fern used only in flooded rice fields
74.x: Azolla is an aquatic fern associated with Anabaena and supplies nitrogen in paddy systems. The other pairs confuse the functions or types of biofertilisers.
74.tq: Start from the distinctive aquatic-fern pair and eliminate swapped organism-function combinations.
xs: **Azolla — aquatic fern with Anabaena**, N for paddy, is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Mycorrhiza** (VAM) is a **fungus-root association** for phosphorus and water uptake, not a bacterium.
**Blue-green algae** fix N in rice fields; **PSB** are bacteria that **solubilise phosphate**.
xa: Azolla and cyanobacteria **fix N and add organic matter** in rice fields.
**Frankia** = symbiotic actinomycete in non-legumes (Alnus, Casuarina).
PSB examples: **Bacillus megaterium**, **Pseudomonas striata**.

74.s: Mycorrhiza, particularly VAM, primarily helps plants in the uptake of:
74.x: VAM is a fungus-root association that improves phosphorus and water uptake by plants.
74.tq: Distinguish nutrient- and water-uptake functions from nitrogen fixation.
xs: **VAM** helps plants take up **phosphorus and water** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Mycorrhiza** is a **fungus-root association**.
xa: **PSB** (Bacillus, Pseudomonas) **solubilise phosphate**.
**Azolla** with **Anabaena** supplies N for paddy.
Phosphorus has **no atmospheric phase**; it is released by weathering of rocks.

74.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Azotobacter is associated with free-living nitrogen fixation.
Anabaena is a symbiont of Azotobacter.
Lactobacillus is associated with curd formation.
Cyanobacteria perform photosynthesis and nitrogen fixation.
74.x: Option B is incorrect: Anabaena lives in the leaves of the water fern Azolla, not with Azotobacter, which is free-living. The other statements are right.
74.tq: Discriminate Azolla (fern host) from Azotobacter (free-living).
n: Azotobacter performs free-living nitrogen fixation. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 122-124]
Cyanobacteria perform photosynthesis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 122-124]
Cyanobacteria perform nitrogen fixation. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 122-124]
Anabaena is a symbiont of Azolla. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 122-124]
Lactobacillus is used for curd formation. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 122-124]
xs: The **incorrect** statement is "**Anabaena** is a symbiont of **Azotobacter**" — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Anabaena** is a **symbiont** of **Azolla**, an **aquatic fern**, not of Azotobacter.
**Azotobacter** is a **free-living** nitrogen fixer; **cyanobacteria** perform **photosynthesis** and **nitrogen fixation**.
xa: The **Azolla–Anabaena** association **fixes nitrogen** in **rice fields** — a **biofertilizer** and **green-manure**.
**Rhizobium** does **symbiotic N₂ fixation** in **legume root nodules**.
**Rhizobium japonicum** is linked with **soybean**.
⚠ **Frankia** = non-legumes (Alnus, Casuarina); **Rhizobium** = legumes.

74.s:
Consider the following statements:

II. Anabaena is associated with Azolla.
III. Azolla plus Anabaena is associated with rice fields.
IV. Rhizobium is free-living.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
74.x: I, II and III are correct: blue-green algae fertilise paddy, and Anabaena lives in Azolla in rice fields. IV is false because Rhizobium lives in legume nodules; Azotobacter is free-living.
74.tq: Discriminate symbiotic from free-living nitrogen fixers.
n: Rhizobium is associated with legume root nodules for nitrogen fixation. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 128-131]
Cyanobacteria, also called blue-green algae, are associated with paddy for nitrogen fixation. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 128-131]
Anabaena is associated with Azolla for nitrogen fixation. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 128-131]
The Azolla–Anabaena association fixes nitrogen in rice fields. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 128-131]
xs: Statements **I, II and III** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
I: **cyanobacteria (blue-green algae)** are biofertilizers for **paddy** / rice fields.
II and III: **Anabaena** is a symbiont of **Azolla**; the **Azolla–Anabaena** association fixes nitrogen in **rice fields**.
IV is wrong: **Rhizobium** is a **symbiotic** bacterium of **legume root nodules**; **Azotobacter** is the **free-living** fixer.
xa: **Azotobacter** and **Azospirillum** serve cereals, millets and vegetables.
**Leg-haemoglobin** (red or pink) in **legume root nodules** is linked with **Rhizobium symbiosis**.
**Frankia** is a symbiotic actinomycete in **non-legumes**.

**Rhizobium** — **legume root nodules**; **Rhizobium japonicum** — **soybean**.
**Azotobacter** — **free-living**; **Anabaena** — **Azolla**.
xa: The **Azolla–Anabaena** association enriches nitrogen in **paddy fields**.
**Cyanobacteria (BGA)** fix nitrogen and add organic matter in **rice** fields.
**Frankia** — **Alnus**, **Casuarina** (non-legumes).

74.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

 b. Azotobacter

 i. Group of photosynthetic prokaryotes (blue-green algae) that fix nitrogen

74.x: Rhizobium fixes N₂ in legume nodules, Azotobacter is free-living, cyanobacteria are the blue-green algae as a group, and Anabaena lives inside Azolla leaves, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv.
74.tq: Separate the whole group from the one genus known for its host fern.
n: Rhizobium performs symbiotic N₂ fixation in legume root nodules. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #56 · pp 100-102]
Azotobacter is a free-living nitrogen fixer. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #56 · pp 100-102]

Anabaena performs nitrogen fixation. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #56 · pp 100-102]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Rhizobium** — **symbiotic N₂ fixation** in **legume root nodules**; **Azotobacter** — **free-living** nitrogen fixer.
**Cyanobacteria** — **blue-green algae** that do **photosynthesis** and **nitrogen fixation**; **Anabaena** — symbiont of the fern **Azolla**.
xa: Rhizobium **converts atmospheric N₂** into **usable nitrogen compounds**; its hosts are **pea**, pulses and legumes.

n: Rhizobium performs nitrogen fixation. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 102-105]
Azotobacter performs free-living nitrogen fixation. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 102-105]

Mycorrhiza improves water acquisition. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 102-105]
Phosphate-solubilizing microbes solubilize phosphorus. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 102-105]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Rhizobium** — **symbiotic nitrogen fixation** in **legume root nodules**; **Azotobacter** — **free-living** nitrogen fixation.
**Mycorrhiza** — **improves nutrient and water acquisition**; **phosphate-solubilizing microbes** — **solubilize phosphorus**.
xa: Mycorrhiza especially improves **phosphorus uptake** and gives **better plant growth**.
**PSB** include **Bacillus** and **Pseudomonas**.

74.x: Rhizobium is a symbiotic bacterium, Azolla an aquatic fern, mycorrhiza a fungus–root link and leghaemoglobin the pink pigment in nodules, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.

n: Rhizobium is a symbiotic bacterium. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 102-105]

Mycorrhiza is a fungus–plant-root association. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 102-105]

74.s: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of the phases proposed by Frederic Clements?
o: Invasion → Nudation → Reaction → Competition and co-action → Stabilisation
Nudation → Competition and co-action → Invasion → Reaction → Stabilisation
Nudation → Invasion → Competition and co-action → Reaction → Stabilisation
Nudation → Reaction → Invasion → Stabilisation → Competition and co-action
74.x: Clements’ sequence begins with formation of a bare area, followed by invasion, competition and co-action, reaction, and stabilisation.
74.tq: Identify the fixed first and final stages before arranging the intermediate stages.
xs: Clements' order is **Nudation → Invasion → Competition and co-action → Reaction → Stabilisation** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Nudation** (bare area) must come first and **stabilisation** (climax) last.
xa: **Reaction** — organisms modify soil, water, light, temperature — is the **most important** stage.
Invasion includes **ecesis** (successful establishment) and **aggregation**.
Nudation causes: erosion, landslide, volcanic activity, fire.

74.s: The term ‘ecesis’ in ecological succession refers to
o: the final stabilisation of a climax community
the successful establishment of invading organisms
the seasonal disappearance of a community
the elimination of unfit species through competition
74.x: Ecesis is the successful establishment of organisms that have migrated into an area during the invasion phase.
74.tq: Discriminate between closely related terms belonging to the invasion and stabilisation phases.
xs: **Ecesis** is the **successful establishment** of invading organisms — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is part of the **invasion** phase: migration of seeds/spores, ecesis, **aggregation**.
Elimination of unfit species is **competition and co-action**; the climax is **stabilisation**.
xa: **Reaction** is the **most important** stage.
**Pioneer species** = first hardy colonisers, e.g. **lichens** on bare rock.
**Climax community** = final stable community, in equilibrium with climate.

74.s: In Clements' phases of ecological succession, which phase is regarded as the most important, in which organisms modify soil, water, light and temperature?
74.x: Reaction is the most important phase: organisms modify soil, water, light and temperature, making the site suitable for later species. Nudation forms the bare area, invasion brings migration, ecesis and aggregation, and stabilisation produces the climax community.
74.tq: Reaction = organisms change the site; the key phase.
xs: **Reaction** is the most important phase — so option **(3)** is correct.
In reaction, organisms **modify soil, water, light, temperature**.
**Nudation** forms the bare area; **invasion** brings migration, ecesis and aggregation; **stabilisation** gives the climax.
xa: Clements' order: **Nudation → Invasion → Competition and co-action → Reaction → Stabilisation**.
Phases proposed by **Frederic Clements (1916)**.
**Competition and co-action**: intra- and inter-specific competition; unfit eliminated.

74.s: Seasonal succession differs from succession caused by a disturbance because seasonal succession is
o: caused exclusively by the removal of soil
a permanent replacement ending only in a forest climax
a cyclic change driven by environmental rhythms
74.x: Seasonal succession is cyclical and is driven by environmental rhythms; it is not caused by a disaster or disturbance.
74.tq: Separate cyclic seasonal change from directional succession caused by disturbance.
xs: Seasonal succession is **a cyclic change driven by environmental rhythms** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is **not** caused by a disturbance (disaster), unlike primary or secondary succession.
xa: **Succession** = orderly, sequential replacement of one community by another, with change in species composition.
**Odum (1971)**: succession = an orderly process of community change within a unit area.
**Nudation** (bare area) results from erosion, landslide, volcanic activity, fire.

74.s:
Consider the following statements regarding primary and secondary succession:

1. Primary succession begins on an area where no soil is present.
2. Secondary succession follows the destruction of an existing community.
3. Secondary succession is generally slower than primary succession.
4. Seeds and roots may already be present in secondary succession.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
74.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Secondary succession is generally faster, not slower, because soil, seeds or roots may remain.
74.tq: Use the presence of soil and propagules to distinguish primary from secondary succession.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 4** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1: primary succession has **no soil**; statement 2: secondary follows removal of an existing community (**fire, flood, logging**).
Statement 3 is wrong: secondary succession is **faster**, more common, with higher biomass.
Statement 4: in secondary succession **seeds and roots are already present**.
xa: Primary begins on areas that never had life: **lava, bare rock, volcanic island**.
Primary: **lichens and mosses** first; slower, low biomass.
**Grasslands** do not turn into forest because of **water limits and fire**.

74.s: Which one of the following pairs of climax theories and proponents is correctly matched?
74.x: Frederic Clements proposed the monoclimax theory, Tansley proposed the polyclimax theory, and Whittaker proposed the climax-pattern theory.
74.tq: Use the person-theory association and watch for swapped proponents.
xs: **Monoclimax — Frederic Clements** is correctly matched — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Polyclimax** = **Tansley**; **climax-pattern** = **Whittaker**.
xa: Monoclimax = **one climax per climatic region**.
Climax community = final stable community **set by climate** (forest, grassland, coral reef).
**Grasslands** do not turn into forest because of **water limits and fire**.

74.s:
In the sequence of ecological succession on bare rock, which one of the following represents the correct order after the appearance of lichens?

1. Crustose lichens
2. Foliose lichens
3. Mosses
4. Herbs
5. Shrubs
6. Forest

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
74.x: The xerosere sequence on bare rock proceeds from crustose lichens to foliose lichens, mosses, herbs, shrubs and finally forest.
74.tq: Use the first-to-last sequence to eliminate options that reverse adjacent seral stages.
xs: The xerosere order is **1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Sequence: **crustose lichens → foliose lichens → mosses → herbs and grasses → shrubs → forest climax**.
xa: **Lichens** = symbiotic association of **algae and fungi** — the bare-rock pioneers.
Scrub attracts **birds** whose droppings and seeds speed colonisation.
Pioneer trees (**birch, oak**) need high light; **shade-tolerant** species form the climax.

74.s: In a hydrosere, which one of the following represents the correct broad sequence of community development?
o: Phytoplankton → submerged rooted plants → floating plants → reed-swamp → sedge-meadow → woodland → forest
Floating plants → phytoplankton → forest → submerged rooted plants
Submerged rooted plants → forest → floating plants → sedge-meadow
74.x: Hydrosere proceeds from phytoplankton through submerged and floating plants, reed-swamp, sedge-meadow, woodland and finally forest.
74.tq: Arrange the aquatic succession from the simplest early community to the terrestrial climax.
xs: The hydrosere sequence is **phytoplankton → submerged rooted plants → floating plants → reed-swamp → sedge-meadow → woodland → forest** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It starts in **water** (pond, lake) with **phytoplankton** and ends in forest; the other options jumble this order.
xa: Floating stage: duckweed **Lemna**, **Pistia** and the alga **Chara**.
Sedge peat above water is invaded by **alders and willows**; ends in wet woodland = **fen carr**.
Lake sediments keep a **permanent record** → hydroseres better studied than xeroseres.

74.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Lithosere is a succession beginning on bare rock.
2. Psammosere is a succession beginning on sand.
3. Lithosere and psammosere are sub-types of xerosere.
4. Halosere begins on saline soil or water.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
74.x: All four statements are correct. Xerosere begins on dry land and includes lithosere and psammosere; halosere begins on saline soil or water.
74.tq: Test the hierarchy of the succession types along with their starting environments.
xs: All four statements — **1, 2, 3 and 4** — are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Lithosere** = bare rock; **psammosere** = sand.
Both are **sub-types of xerosere** (dry land); **halosere** = saline soil/water.
xa: **Hydrosere** begins in water (pond, lake).
Xerosere: **crustose lichens → foliose lichens → mosses → herbs and grasses → shrubs → forest**.
Whole sequence of stages = **sere**; each step = **seral stage**.

74.s: Biodegradation contributes to the functioning of an ecosystem primarily by
o: removing biodiversity from the food chain
converting organic waste into nutrients through microorganisms
74.x: Biodegradation recycles waste when microorganisms break down organic material and release nutrients. This makes nutrients available for reuse in the ecosystem.
74.tq: Apply the process to its practical ecological outcome: microbial breakdown and nutrient release.
xs: Biodegradation works by **converting organic waste into nutrients through microorganisms** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **biodegradation function** = recycling waste: microorganisms break organic material into nutrients by **biological action** (**APPSC 2023**).
It does not prevent decomposition or remove biodiversity; it is itself decomposition that returns nutrients for reuse.
xa: **Waste decomposition** is classed as a **regulating** service under the **MEA 2005**.
Removing **decomposers** would **block mineral movement** — nutrients locked in dead matter never return to the soil (**APPSC 2025**).
Other environment functions: **supplies resources**, **sustains life**, **aesthetic services**.

74.s:
Match List-I (Function of the environment) with List-II (Description):
a. Waste decomposition
b. Cultural heritage
c. Recreation and aesthetics
d. Medicinal resources
i. Scenic and leisure value
ii. Supply of drugs and herbal remedies
iii. Breakdown of organic waste into simpler compounds
iv. Source of traditional practices and identity
74.x: Waste decomposition is the breakdown of organic waste into simpler compounds (iii); cultural heritage is a source of traditional practices and identity (iv); recreation and aesthetics give scenic and leisure value (i); medicinal resources supply drugs and herbal remedies (ii). This is the APPSC 2023 matching.
74.tq: Decomposition = breakdown; heritage = tradition.
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Waste decomposition** = breakdown of organic waste into simpler compounds; **cultural heritage** = source of traditional practices and identity.
**Recreation and aesthetics** = scenic and leisure value; **medicinal resources** = supply of drugs and herbal remedies.
xa: This matching was asked in **APPSC 2023**.
Under the **MEA**: medicinal resources = **provisioning**; waste decomposition = **regulating**; recreation and cultural heritage = **cultural**.
The **biodegradation function** recycles waste via microorganisms.

74.s:
Which of the following are recognised ecosystem functions?
1. Ecological succession
2. Nutrient cycling
3. Energy flow through food chains
4. Homeostasis

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
74.x: All four are ecosystem functions. They describe change in communities, movement of nutrients, transfer of energy and maintenance of ecological balance.
74.tq: Test the complete set by checking whether each item describes an ecological process or system property.
xs: All four — **1, 2, 3 and 4** — are ecosystem functions, so option **(4)** is correct.
The notes list ecosystem functions as **ecological succession**, **nutrient cycling**, **energy flow via food chain** and **homeostasis**.
xa: Forest **economic** functions: timber, bamboo, fuelwood, fodder, **NTFPs**.
Forest **ecological** functions: **carbon sequestration**, soil and water conservation, groundwater recharge, flood moderation, air purification.
The **MEA 2005** grouped ecosystem services into **provisioning, regulating, cultural, supporting**.

74.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (MEA category)
 a. Provisioning
 b. Regulating
 c. Cultural
 d. Supporting

List-II (Example)
 i. Soil formation
 ii. Recreation
 iii. Food and water
 iv. Climate regulation
74.x: Provisioning services supply food and water; regulating services include climate regulation; cultural services include recreation; supporting services include soil formation.
74.tq: Start from the sure pairs, especially food–provisioning and soil formation–supporting.
xs: The correct match is **a–iii, b–iv, c–ii, d–i** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Provisioning** = food and fresh water; **regulating** = climate regulation.
**Cultural** = recreation; **supporting** = soil formation.
xa: The four categories come from the **Millennium Ecosystem Assessment (2005, UN)**.
⚠ **Pollination** and **waste decomposition** = **regulating**; **nutrient cycling** and **soil formation** = **supporting**.
Supporting services also include **primary production**.

74.s: Which one of the following is NOT a provisioning ecosystem service under the Millennium Ecosystem Assessment classification?
74.x: Pollination is a regulating service. Timber, medicinal resources and fresh water are provisioning services.
74.tq: Use category discrimination: identify the service that performs regulation rather than material supply.
xs: **Pollination** is NOT a provisioning service — so option **(2)** is correct.
Under the **MEA**, pollination is a **regulating** service, along with climate, flood and disease regulation and water purification.
**Fresh water**, **timber** and **medicinal resources** are all **provisioning** services.
xa: Provisioning also covers **food** and **fibre**.
⚠ Waste decomposition = **regulating**; nutrient cycling = **supporting**.
**Cultural** services: recreation, aesthetics, cultural heritage, spiritual value.

74.s:
Which of the following forest benefits is primarily an ecological service rather than an economic product?
1. Timber
2. Bamboo
3. Groundwater recharge
4. Flood moderation

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
74.x: Groundwater recharge and flood moderation are ecological services. Timber and bamboo are economic products obtained from forests.
74.tq: Separate marketable forest products from regulating and conservation functions.
xs: **Groundwater recharge** and **flood moderation** (3 and 4 only) are ecological services — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Timber** and **bamboo** are **economic** products of forests, along with fuelwood, fodder and NTFPs.
Forest **ecological** functions: carbon sequestration, soil and water conservation, **groundwater recharge**, **flood moderation**, air purification.
xa: Forests are vital **carbon sinks**.
**Wetlands** act as sponges — store floodwater, recharge aquifers, sustain lean-season flow.
AP's forests regulate water flow and conserve soil and moisture → **intangible ecosystem services**.

74.s: Why are estimates of the economic value of ecosystem services considered lower than their true value?
o: Regulating services have no measurable ecological effects
Provisioning services are excluded from all assessments
Supporting services are always traded in markets
Cultural services are difficult to express in monetary terms
74.x: Cultural services such as spiritual value, heritage and aesthetics are difficult to price accurately. Therefore, monetary estimates may understate the true value of ecosystem services.
74.tq: Link the valuation limitation to the service category that is difficult to monetise.
xs: Estimates are lower than true values because **cultural services are difficult to express in monetary terms** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The notes state: true values are higher since **cultural services are hard to price**.
Cultural services are **recreation, aesthetics, cultural heritage, spiritual value**.
xa: Criticism: pricing nature (**Costanza**, **TEEB**) aids decisions but **undervalues cultural and spiritual services**.
**Costanza et al. (1997)**: about **US$33 trillion a year**.
Coral reefs valued at **$375 billion-$9.9 trillion** a year.

74.s: Nutrients in an ecosystem differ from energy in that nutrients
o: flow only through the atmosphere and never through organisms
are consumed permanently and cannot return to the ecosystem
are recycled indefinitely, whereas energy is not
74.x: Nutrients are recycled through ecosystems, while energy flows through the system and is not recycled indefinitely.
74.tq: Discriminate between the cycling of matter and the one-way flow of energy.
xs: Nutrients **are recycled indefinitely, whereas energy is not** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Nutrients cycle between **living organisms, air and the Earth's crust**; energy flows through and is lost.
They are not consumed permanently, nor generated by decomposers; decomposers only release them from dead matter.
xa: **Energy flow** drives the cycles; all cycles are linked to the **water cycle**.
**C, H, O, N and P** make up about **97%** of body mass.
Common components of all cycles: **inputs, internal cycling, outputs**.

74.s:
Which of the following statements correctly describes the relationship among pioneer community, seral community and climax community?

1. Pioneer communities are hardy early colonisers.
2. Seral communities are intermediate communities.
3. The climax community is generally stable and in equilibrium with climate.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
74.x: Pioneer communities colonise first, seral communities occupy intermediate stages, and the climax community is the stable terminal community related to the prevailing climate.
74.tq: Test the roles of the three community categories in the succession sequence.
xs: All three statements — **1, 2 and 3** — are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
Statement 1: **pioneer species / community** = first hardy colonisers.
Statement 2: **seral communities** = intermediate stages; the whole sequence = **sere**.
Statement 3: the **climax community** is the final stable community, in equilibrium with **climate**.
xa: Climax examples: **forest, grassland, coral reef**.
FIRST/LAST: **lichens** first on bare rock; **climax community** = last stage.
**Succession** = gradual, orderly, sequential replacement of one community by another over time.

74.s:
Which of the following are ecosystem services associated with forests in Andhra Pradesh?
1. Acting as carbon sinks
2. Regulating water flow
3. Conserving soil and moisture
4. Providing only market-priced goods and no intangible benefits
74.x: Andhra Pradesh forests act as carbon sinks, regulate water flow and conserve soil and moisture, thereby providing important intangible ecosystem services. Statement 4 is false because their benefits are not limited to market-priced goods.
74.tq: Reject the restrictive word ‘only’ and identify the full range of ecosystem services.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
AP's forests act as **carbon sinks**, **regulate water flow** and **conserve soil and moisture**.
Statement 4 is wrong: these are **intangible ecosystem services**, not only market-priced goods.
xa: Forest **economic** products: timber, bamboo, fuelwood, fodder, **NTFPs**.
Pricing nature (**Costanza, TEEB**) undervalues cultural and spiritual services.
AP has the **second-largest mangrove** ecosystem in India (**Godavari and Krishna** estuaries).

74.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Biofertilizers contribute to nutrient addition and growth promotion.
Statement B: Phosphate-solubilizing microbes solubilize phosphorus.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
74.x: Both are true: biofertilisers add nutrients and promote growth, and phosphate-solubilising microbes release bound phosphorus.
74.tq: Recall the roles of biofertilisers.
n: Phosphate-solubilizing microbes solubilize phosphorus. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 102-105]
Biofertilizers add nutrients. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 102-105]
Biofertilizers promote growth. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 102-105]
xs: **Both statements are true** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement A: **biofertilizers** **add nutrients** and **promote growth**.
Statement B: **phosphate-solubilizing microbes** **solubilize phosphorus**.
xa: Phosphate solubilisers: **Bacillus megaterium**, **Pseudomonas striata**.
**Mycorrhiza (VAM)**: a fungus–root association improving **phosphorus uptake**.
**Azolla–Anabaena** is a **biofertilizer** and **green-manure** association for **rice**.

74.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the functions of wetlands:
I. Wetlands control erosion.
II. Wetlands retain sediment.
III. Wetlands support nutrient cycling.
IV. Wetlands support biodiversity.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
74.x: All four are correct: wetlands control erosion, trap sediment, cycle nutrients and support biodiversity.
74.tq: Recall the functions of wetlands.
n: Wetlands control erosion. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 38-39]
Wetlands retain sediment. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 38-39]
Wetlands support nutrient cycling. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 38-39]
Wetlands support biodiversity. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 38-39]
xs: **All four** statements — **I, II, III and IV** — are correct, so option **(3)** is correct.
Wetlands give **erosion control** and **sediment retention**.
Wetlands support **nutrient cycling** and **biodiversity**.
xa: They also act as **flood buffers**, store water and **purify water**.
They **recharge aquifers** and regulate the **microclimate**.
**Fertiliser runoff** of **N and P** causes **algal blooms / eutrophication**.

74.s:
Consider the following statements about the functions of the environment:
1. The environment provides renewable resources only.
2. Sustaining life includes protection from UV radiation by ozone.
3. Scenery and recreation are aesthetic services of the environment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
74.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the environment supplies both renewable and non-renewable resources ('renewable only' was the incorrect statement in APPSC 2022). Statement 2 is correct: sustaining life includes genetic diversity, biodiversity and ozone's UV protection. Statement 3 is correct: scenery and recreation are aesthetic services. Hence '2 and 3 only'.
74.tq: Resources = renewable AND non-renewable.
xs: Only statements **2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is wrong: the environment supplies **both renewable AND non-renewable** resources (the "renewable only" trap, **APPSC 2022**).
Statement 2 is correct: **sustaining life** includes genetic diversity, biodiversity and **UV protection by ozone**.
Statement 3 is correct: **scenery and recreation** are **aesthetic services**.
xa: Supplying resources is the **first function** of the environment.
**Assimilating waste** = the **biodegradation function**.
Recreation, aesthetics, cultural heritage and spiritual value are **cultural** services under the **MEA 2005**.

74.s: Costanza and his associates first valued global ecosystem services in 1997 at approximately
74.x: Costanza et al. estimated the annual value of global ecosystem services at approximately US$33 trillion in 1997.
74.tq: Handle the figure by checking the order of magnitude and the decimal placement.
xs: **Costanza et al. (1997)** valued global ecosystem services at about **US$33 trillion a year** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was the **first** attempt to value global ecosystem services.
xa: Later values: coral reefs **$375 billion-$9.9 trillion** a year; Amazon **$2.2-3.4 trillion** a year.
True values are higher — **cultural services** are hard to price.
**TEEB** (launched **2007**, G8+5, Potsdam; hosted by **UNEP**) makes nature's values visible in decisions.

74.s:
Which one of the following statements about TEEB is correct?
1. It was hosted by UNEP.
2. It seeks to make nature’s values visible in decision-making.
3. It was launched in 2007 in the G8+5 context.
74.x: TEEB was launched in 2007 in the G8+5 context at Potsdam, hosted by UNEP, and aims to make the economic and other values of nature visible in decisions.
74.tq: Check the institutional host, date and objective together.
xs: All three statements — **1, 2 and 3** — are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
Statement 1: TEEB is hosted by **UNEP**.
Statement 2: it **makes nature's values visible in decisions**.
Statement 3: it was launched in **2007** (**G8+5**, Potsdam).
xa: TEEB = **The Economics of Ecosystems and Biodiversity**.
The **MEA (2005, UN)** gave the four service categories.
Pricing nature aids decisions but **undervalues cultural and spiritual services**.

74.s: What is the principal function of leg-haemoglobin in legume root nodules?
o: Maintaining suitable oxygen conditions for nitrogen fixation
74.x: Leghaemoglobin binds oxygen to keep its level low in nodules, because nitrogenase is destroyed by oxygen.
74.tq: Recall why nodules contain leghaemoglobin.
n: Leg-haemoglobin is located in legume root nodules. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 102-105]
Leg-haemoglobin helps maintain suitable oxygen conditions for nitrogen fixation. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 102-105]
xs: **Leg-haemoglobin** helps **maintain suitable oxygen conditions** for **nitrogen fixation** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is **located** in **legume root nodules**, is **red or pink**, and is linked with **Rhizobium symbiosis**.
It supports an **efficient nitrogen-fixing environment**; it does not solubilise **phosphorus** (that is phosphate-solubilising microbes).
xa: A **legume root nodule** has a **symbiotic relationship** with **Rhizobium**.
**Free-living** nitrogen fixation is done by **Azotobacter**.
Biological fixation needs the enzyme **nitrogenase**.

74.s: EnviStats India, compiled annually by MoSPI, is associated with:
o: Only the enumeration of endangered species
Assessment of atmospheric nitrogen fixation by legumes
Natural capital accounting under the UN SEEA framework
74.x: EnviStats India is an annual MoSPI compilation of environmental-economic accounts under the UN System of Environmental-Economic Accounting framework.
74.tq: Identify the responsible ministry and the accounting framework from the institutional description.
xs: EnviStats India is linked to **natural capital accounting under the UN SEEA framework** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is compiled **annually by MoSPI** and compiles **environmental-economic accounts** under SEEA.
xa: **TEEB** (2007, hosted by **UNEP**) also aims to make nature's values visible in decisions.
**Costanza et al. (1997)**: about **US$33 trillion a year** for global ecosystem services.
The **MEA (2005, UN)** gave the four service categories.

74.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
74.x: Bacillus megaterium is a phosphate solubiliser (PSB), so A is right. Pseudomonas striata is also a phosphate solubiliser, not linked to nitrogenase (used in nitrogen fixation); VAM aids phosphorus and water uptake, not denitrification; Nitrobacter converts nitrite to nitrate in nitrification, not phosphate uptake.
74.tq: Start with the sure organism–function pair and eliminate swapped microbial roles.
xs: **Bacillus megaterium — phosphate solubiliser** is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Pseudomonas striata** is also a **phosphate solubiliser**, not linked to nitrogenase.
**VAM** aids **phosphorus and water uptake**, not denitrification; **Nitrobacter** turns nitrite into nitrate in nitrification.
xa: **PSB** (Bacillus, Pseudomonas) **solubilise phosphate**.
**Mycorrhiza** (VAM) = fungus-root association.
Denitrification = **Pseudomonas, Thiobacillus**.

74.s: Hydroseres are generally better studied than xeroseres because:
o: Their climax communities are exclusively aquatic.
Lake sediments preserve a permanent record of their development.
They always contain more species than xeroseres.
They are unaffected by climatic changes.
74.x: Lake sediments preserve a permanent record of ecological changes, making hydroseres better studied than xeroseres.
74.tq: Identify the evidence-based reason rather than an ecological generalisation.
xs: Hydroseres are better studied because **lake sediments preserve a permanent record** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The notes give this as the reason hydroseres are better studied than **xeroseres**.
xa: Hydrosere ends in wet woodland = **fen carr**.
Xerosere pioneers are **lichens** (algae + fungi) on bare rock.
⚠ Lithosere and psammosere are sub-types of **xerosere**, not hydrosere.

75.s: Deforestation contributes to the greenhouse effect primarily because it
o: raises soil fertility in all regions
reduces the carbon sink capacity of forests
75.x: Deforestation removes vegetation that acts as a carbon sink. The resulting loss of carbon absorption adds to the greenhouse effect.
75.tq: Link the environmental impact directly to the underlying ecological function.
xs: Deforestation adds to the greenhouse effect because it **reduces the carbon sink capacity of forests** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Notes: **loss of CO2 sink** adds to the greenhouse effect.
It does not raise fertility or prevent erosion — it causes **faster erosion** and **falling fertility**.
xa: Drivers: agriculture, urbanisation, industry, **mining**.
**Forest Declaration Assessment 2025**: forest loss **8.1 Mha in 2024**.
About **94%** of loss is in **tropical** forests.

75.s: Desertification is best understood as
o: the conversion of all forests into agricultural land
the spread of existing deserts alone into neighbouring regions
the natural formation of sand dunes only
the spread of desert-like conditions into non-arid areas through climatic and human factors
75.x: Desertification involves land degradation in arid, semi-arid and dry sub-humid areas due to climatic variation and human activity; it is not merely the spread of existing deserts.
75.tq: Discriminate between the broad process of desertification and the narrower idea of desert expansion.
xs: Desertification is **the spread of desert-like conditions into non-arid areas through climatic and human factors** — so option **(4)** is correct.
In the **UNCCD** sense it is land degradation in **arid, semi-arid and dry sub-humid** areas from climatic variation and human activity.
⚠ It is **not** the spread of existing deserts alone — so option (2) is wrong.
xa: Main cause in semi-arid regions: **overgrazing and deforestation** (**APPSC 2025**).
**LDN** = no net loss of land health; target year **2030** (SDG 15.3).
**Rajasthan** has over **23%** of India's desertified land.

75.s: In semi-arid regions, the principal causes of desertification are
o: low population pressure and regular rainfall
75.x: Overgrazing and deforestation are identified as the main causes of desertification in semi-arid regions.
75.tq: Select the primary cause rather than a secondary contributing factor.
xs: **Overgrazing and deforestation** are the main causes in semi-arid regions — so option **(3)** is correct (**APPSC 2025**).
Afforestation, water harvesting and improved drainage are remedies, not causes.
xa: Other causes: **improper irrigation**, excess chemicals, **erratic rainfall**, droughts, **population pressure**.
**Overgrazing** strips vegetation cover; **deforestation** exposes soil to wind and water erosion.
**Tragedy of the Commons** (Garrett Hardin, **1968**): overgrazing of shared pasture lowers land quality.

75.s: The concept used to describe degradation caused by over-use of a shared pasture is
75.x: Over-use of a commonly shared pasture is described as the Tragedy of the Commons, a concept associated with Garrett Hardin in 1968.
75.tq: Match the exact conceptual term with the common-resource situation.
xs: Over-use of a shared pasture is the **Tragedy of the Commons** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The concept is of **Garrett Hardin, 1968**; overgrazing lowers land quality (**APPSC 2018**).
xa: **Overgrazing** strips vegetation cover — a main cause of desertification in semi-arid regions.
**LDN** = no net loss of land health by **2030**.
Over-use of shared land drives the degradation that the UNCCD targets.

75.s: Which of the following is the most conspicuous set of effects associated with modern agriculture?
o: Reduced irrigation, increased soil carbon and forest expansion
Declining crop production without any environmental effect
Soil formation, afforestation and ecological stability
Soil degradation, pollution and ecological imbalance
75.x: The most conspicuous effects of modern agriculture are soil degradation, pollution and ecological imbalance.
75.tq: Recognise the complete three-part consequence set rather than selecting one component.
xs: Modern agriculture's main effects are **soil degradation, pollution and ecological imbalance** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The answer "**all of these**" was keyed in **APPSC 2018**.
xa: Excess **urea** skewed the **NPK ratio** in Punjab and Haryana.
Over-irrigation + poor drainage → **waterlogging and salinity**.
**Soil organic carbon** reportedly fell from **1% to 0.3%** over 70 years.

75.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India and the UNCCD:
1. UNCCD COP14 was held in New Delhi in 2019.
2. At COP14, India raised its land-restoration target to 26 million hectares by 2030.
3. The target year for Land Degradation Neutrality under SDG 15.3 is 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
75.x: Statement 1 is correct: COP14 was held in New Delhi in 2019. Statement 2 is correct: India raised its target to 26 Mha by 2030 (from the 21 Mha pledged at Paris 2015). Statement 3 is wrong: the LDN target year is 2030. Hence 1 and 2 only.
75.tq: COP14 Delhi 2019 -> 26 Mha by 2030; LDN also 2030 - one year for both.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1: **COP14** was held in **New Delhi, 2019**.
Statement 2: India raised its target to **26 Mha by 2030** (earlier **21 Mha** at Paris **2015**).
Statement 3 is wrong: the **LDN** target year is **2030**, not 2025.
xa: LDN = **no net loss of land health** (SDG **15.3**).
**COP17**: **Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia (2026)**.
MoEFCC-IUCN report: India restored **~21.76 Mha** during 2011-2020.

75.s: Under the Watershed Development Component of PMKSY, watershed development in India follows which approach?
75.x: Watershed development under the PMKSY Watershed Development Component follows the 'ridge to valley' approach, treating the upper catchment first and moving downstream. The other options are not the stated approach.
75.tq: Watershed = ridge to valley.
xs: PMKSY watershed development follows **'ridge to valley'** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is the approach of the **PMKSY Watershed Development Component**.
xa: Other soil-conservation support: **MGNREGA**, state watershed projects, **participatory forest management**.
**Soil Health Cards** + village-wise soil nutrient mapping.
Water erosion causes **loss of topsoil** and sedimentation of rivers and reservoirs.

75.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Process)
A. Overgrazing
B. Deforestation
C. Water erosion
D. Wind erosion

List-II (Effect)
I. Topsoil is blown away in dry areas
II. Soil is exposed to wind and water erosion
III. Vegetation cover is stripped
IV. Topsoil is lost and rivers and reservoirs receive sediment

Select the correct answer using the code below.
75.x: Overgrazing strips vegetation, deforestation exposes soil, water erosion removes topsoil and causes sedimentation, and wind erosion blows topsoil away in dry areas.
75.tq: Start with the sure pair—wind erosion and blown topsoil—then eliminate inconsistent combinations.
xs: The correct match is **A–III, B–II, C–IV, D–I** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Overgrazing** strips vegetation cover; **deforestation** exposes soil to wind and water erosion.
**Water erosion** = loss of topsoil + sedimentation of rivers and reservoirs; **wind erosion** = topsoil blown away in dry areas.
xa: Wind erosion example: **Anantapur**.
**Salinisation/waterlogging** from poor drainage and over-irrigation (**AP delta regions**).
The 2021 Atlas names **water erosion + chemical degradation** as major contributors in India.

75.s: Salinisation and waterlogging are particularly associated with
75.x: Poor drainage and over-irrigation cause salinisation and waterlogging, including in delta regions.
75.tq: Link the land-management practice to its characteristic degradation outcome.
xs: Salinisation and waterlogging come from **poor drainage and over-irrigation** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Brick production** depletes **topsoil**; **wind erosion** blows topsoil away in dry areas — different processes.
xa: In AP, **delta areas** suffer salinity + waterlogging.
By **2050, 50%** of world arable land could be affected by waterlogging and salinity.
**Mitti Bachao Abhiyan** (MP, **1977**) opposed waterlogging and salinity.

75.s: In the context of intensive agriculture, excess urea is reported to have skewed the NPK ratio particularly in
75.x: Excess use of urea has skewed the nitrogen-phosphorus-potassium balance in the soils of Punjab and Haryana.
75.tq: Use the location-specific agriculture trap and distinguish it from other state pairs.
xs: Excess **urea** has skewed the **NPK ratio** in **Punjab and Haryana** (CSE) — so option **(2)** is correct.
Synthetic fertilisers and pesticides **contaminate soil and water**.
xa: Effects of intensive agriculture: soil degradation, pollution, ecological imbalance — **all of these** (**APPSC 2018**).
Indian **soil organic carbon** reportedly fell from **1% to 0.3%** over 70 years.
⚠ **Punjab** has the best (lowest) degraded-land share, **3.15%**.

75.s:
Consider the following statements about the extent of land degradation:
1. The Desertification and Land Degradation Atlas of India 2021 reports about 97.85 Mha, i.e. 29.77% of India's area, as degraded.
2. Water erosion and chemical degradation are the major contributors to land degradation in India.
3. According to FAO, about one-half of the world's soils are degraded.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
75.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 2021 Atlas (ISRO-SAC) gives 97.85 Mha = 29.77%. Statement 2 is correct: water erosion and chemical degradation are the major contributors. Statement 3 is wrong: FAO says one-third, not one-half, of world soils are degraded. Hence 1 and 2 only.
75.tq: Remember the trio: 97.85 Mha / 29.77% (India), one-third (world soils, FAO), over 10% of global GDP (UNCCD GLO).
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1: the **2021 Atlas** reports **97.85 Mha = 29.77%** of India degraded.
Statement 2: major contributors are **water erosion + chemical degradation**.
Statement 3 is wrong: FAO says **one-third**, not one-half, of world soils are degraded.
xa: The Atlas is by **ISRO's Space Applications Centre (SAC), Ahmedabad**.
India is adding **2.2 lakh ha** of degraded land a year.
UNCCD: degradation costs over **10% of global GDP**.

75.s: The Desertification and Land Degradation Atlas was published by which organisation and centre?
o: Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education, Dehradun
National Atlas and Thematic Mapping Organisation, Kolkata
75.x: The Desertification and Land Degradation Atlas was published by ISRO's Space Applications Centre located at Ahmedabad.
75.tq: Identify the correct institution-location pair.
xs: The Atlas was published by **ISRO's Space Applications Centre, Ahmedabad** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is the **Desertification and Land Degradation Atlas of India 2021** (ISRO-SAC).
xa: It reports **97.85 Mha = 29.77%** of India degraded.
Major contributors: **water erosion + chemical degradation**.

75.s: According to the AP SDG 15-related figures, the percentage of degraded land in Andhra Pradesh is:
75.x: Under SDG 15 (SDG India Index 2023-24), degraded land is 33.81% of AP, about ten times Punjab's 3.15%. 18.28% is AP's forest cover and 21.26% its fallow-land share.
75.tq: Distinguish the degradation percentage from forest cover and fallow-land figures.
xs: Degraded land is **33.81%** of AP (SDG 15, **SDG India Index 2023-24**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**18.28%** is AP's **forest cover** and **21.26%** its **fallow-land** share.
xa: The best state is **Punjab** at **3.15%** — AP's share is about ten times Punjab's.
AP's desertification area went up **3.45%** (Rajasthan **-1.34%**).
AP fallow land: **34.65 lakh ha** — more than its forest area.
AP tree cover: **2.87%**.

75.s: Approximately what proportion of the Earth's land is covered by forests?
75.x: FAO FRA 2025 puts forests at about 32% of Earth's land. 54% is the share of forests held by five countries (Russia, Brazil, Canada, USA, China), and 21.76 (Mha) is the land India restored in 2011-2020.
75.tq: Use the numerical-value option set and distinguish a global figure from India-specific figures.
xs: Forests cover about **32%** of Earth's land (**FAO FRA 2025**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**54%** is the share of forests held by five countries; **21.76** Mha is what India restored during 2011-2020.
xa: Five countries with over **54%** of forests: **Russia, Brazil, Canada, USA, China**.
Net forest loss fell from **10.7 Mha/yr (1990s)** to **4.12 Mha/yr (2015-2025)**.
India rose to **9th** in total forest area (**10th in 2020**).

75.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the five countries that together contain more than half of the world's forests?
o: Russia, Brazil, Canada, the United States and China
India, Brazil, Canada, Australia and China
Brazil, Canada, Australia, India and the United States
Russia, India, the United States, Indonesia and China
75.x: More than 54% of the world's forests are found in Russia, Brazil, Canada, the United States and China.
75.tq: Test a named-list fact; distinguish the exact membership of the group.
xs: **Russia, Brazil, Canada, the USA and China** hold over **54%** of forests — so option **(1)** is correct.
**India**, **Australia** and **Indonesia** are not in the FRA 2025 list of five.
xa: Forests cover about **32%** of Earth's land (**FAO FRA 2025**, Oct 2025).
**Asia** = only region with net gain 1990-2025, led by **China and India**.
India stays **3rd** in annual forest gain.

75.s: The older FAO Forest Resources Assessment figures cited for the annual net forest loss show a decline from 8.3 million hectares in the 1990s to
75.x: The older FRA figures record a decline from 8.3 million hectares per year in the 1990s to 5.2 million hectares per year during 2000–2010.
75.tq: Check the edition and time period before selecting a familiar-looking forest-loss figure.
xs: The older FRA figures fell from **8.3 million ha/yr (1990s)** to **5.2 million ha/yr (2000-2010)** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**4.12** and **10.7** belong to the newer **FRA 2025** series.
xa: This FRA 2010-basis figure was asked in **APPSC 2018**.
Forests cover about **32%** of Earth's land.

75.s: The zones identified as having the highest forest loss are mainly the
o: coniferous forests of Russia and Canada alone
tropical forests of the Amazon, Congo Basin and Southeast Asia
temperate forests of Europe and North America
mangrove forests of the Indian coastline alone
75.x: The highest forest loss is concentrated in tropical forests, especially in the Amazon, Congo Basin and Southeast Asia.
75.tq: Use the geographic-cluster clue to identify the correct region rather than a single country.
xs: Highest forest loss is in **tropical forests of the Amazon, Congo Basin and Southeast Asia** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The Forest Declaration Assessment 2025 puts about **94%** of loss in **tropical** forests.
xa: Drivers: clearing for **agriculture**, urbanisation, industry, mining.
Impact: loss of the **CO2 sink** adds to the greenhouse effect.
⚠ **Asia** was the only region with net forest gain 1990-2025.

75.s:
Consider the following statements regarding desertified land in India:
1. About one-fourth of degraded land faces desertification.
2. Rajasthan accounts for more than 23% of India's desertified land.
3. All degraded land in India is classified as desertified land.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
75.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because only about one-fourth of degraded land faces desertification.
75.tq: Reject the extreme word 'all' while retaining the stated proportion and regional share.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1: about **a quarter** of degraded land faces desertification.
Statement 2: **Rajasthan** has over **23%** of India's desertified land.
Statement 3 is wrong: only about a quarter, not all, degraded land is desertified.
xa: ⚠ Desertification is land degradation in **drylands**, not the spread of existing deserts alone.
**Aravalli Green Wall** aims to check the **Thar's eastward spread**.
AP's desertification area went up **3.45%** (Rajasthan **-1.34%**).

75.s:
Which combination of factors most directly contributes to the formation of urban heat islands?
1. Low-albedo concrete and asphalt surfaces
2. Loss of urban vegetation
3. Waste heat from air-conditioners and vehicles
4. Dense built-up canyons
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
75.x: All four factors contribute to urban heat islands. Concrete and asphalt absorb and store heat, while reduced vegetation, artificial heat and dense construction intensify warming.
75.tq: Use the all-inclusive option after checking whether each listed factor contributes to the phenomenon.
xs: All four — **1, 2, 3 and 4** — cause urban heat islands, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Concrete/asphalt** have low albedo and store heat; **loss of vegetation** adds to it.
**Waste heat** from ACs and vehicles (ACs worsen UHI) and **dense built canyons** complete the list.
xa: **UHI** = cities markedly hotter than surroundings.
**Cool roofs** (high-reflectance coatings) cut heat absorption and indoor cooling load.
**Namo Van - Nagar Van Scheme**: urban forests to reduce the UHI effect.

75.s: The Namo Van–Nagar Van Scheme primarily seeks to achieve which of the following?
o: Replacement of all rural forests with plantations
Expansion of mining areas around cities
Reduction of the urban heat island effect through urban forests
75.x: The Namo Van–Nagar Van Scheme promotes urban forests with the aim of reducing the urban heat island effect.
75.tq: Match the scheme with its specific environmental purpose.
xs: The **Namo Van - Nagar Van Scheme** aims at **reduction of the urban heat island effect through urban forests** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was noted in **Jul 2026**.
xa: **Loss of vegetation** is one cause of UHI.
**AP Cool Surface Policy 2023**: affordable solutions against urban heat.
**NDMA** heat-wave action plan guidelines: **2016** (revised later).

75.s:
With reference to the UNCCD, consider the following statements:
1. It was adopted in 1994 in Paris.
2. Its secretariat is located in Bonn.
3. India is a party to the Convention.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
75.x: All three statements are correct: the UNCCD was adopted in Paris in 1994, its secretariat is in Bonn, and India is a party.
75.tq: Check each statement against the treaty’s date, headquarters and membership.
xs: All three statements — **1, 2 and 3** — are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
UNCCD was adopted in **1994** in **Paris**; its secretariat is in **Bonn**.
**India** is a party; it ratified in **1996**.
xa: UNCCD came **in force in 1996**.
It is one of three **Rio conventions** (with **UNFCCC and CBD**).
It is the **only legally binding** framework on desertification and drought.

75.s:
Consider the following statements regarding UNCCD-related initiatives:
1. COP17 was held at Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, in 2026.
2. India launched its first guide to Grasslands and Open Natural Ecosystems at COP17.
3. Grasslands and Open Natural Ecosystems constitute over 10% of India’s area and less than 5% is protected.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
75.x: All three statements are correct. The guide was launched by India’s MoEFCC at COP17 in 2026.
75.tq: Test a cluster of linked facts through a coded combination.
xs: All three statements — **1, 2 and 3** — are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
**COP17** was at **Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia (2026)**, where **MoEFCC** launched the first guide to **Grasslands and Open Natural Ecosystems**.
These ecosystems are **over 10%** of India's area, **under 5%** protected; key to **LDN** targets.
xa: COP14 (**New Delhi, 2019**): target raised to **26 Mha by 2030**.
**2026** Desertification Day theme: "**Rangelands: Recognise. Respect. Restore.**"
**Grasslands** do not turn into forest because of water limits and fire.

75.s: The World Day to Combat Desertification and Drought is observed on:
75.x: The World Day to Combat Desertification and Drought is observed on 17 June, following a 1994 UNGA decision.
75.tq: Distinguish the environmental observance from other internationally known dates.
xs: The World Day to Combat Desertification and Drought is on **17 June** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was set by the **UNGA** in **1994**.
xa: **2026** host: **Kenya**; theme "**Rangelands: Recognise. Respect. Restore.**"
⚠ Sand and dust storms day = **12 July**.
UNCCD adopted **1994**, in force **1996**.

75.s: The Bonn Challenge was launched in 2011 by which of the following?
75.x: The Bonn Challenge was launched in 2011 by Germany and the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN).
75.tq: Test the launch-year and institutional partnership as a single factual pair.
xs: The Bonn Challenge was launched in **2011** by **Germany and IUCN** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **African Union** leads the **Great Green Wall** in Africa, not the Bonn Challenge.
xa: Targets: **150 Mha by 2020**, **350 Mha by 2030** (extended **2014**, New York Declaration on Forests).
India joined at **Paris 2015** (21 Mha pledge) → raised to **26 Mha** (COP14, 2019).
Telangana led restoration 2011-2020 (**4.18 Mha**).

75.s:
Consider the following statements about India and the Bonn Challenge:
1. India joined the Bonn Challenge at Paris in 2015 with a pledge of 21 million hectares.
2. Andhra Pradesh led all States in land restored during 2011-2020 as per the MoEFCC-IUCN report.
3. As per the MoEFCC-IUCN report, India restored about 21.76 million hectares during 2011-2020, beating its original pledge.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
75.x: Statement 1 is correct: India joined at Paris 2015 with a 21 Mha pledge. Statement 2 is wrong: Telangana led (4.18 Mha), followed by MP, Odisha, Gujarat and then Andhra Pradesh. Statement 3 is correct: about 21.76 Mha was restored in 2011-2020. Hence 1 and 3 only.
75.tq: Telangana first, AP fifth - the AP-angle trap; 21 Mha pledge vs ~21.76 Mha achieved.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
Statement 1: India joined at **Paris 2015** with a **21 Mha** pledge.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Telangana** led (**4.18 Mha**), then MP, Odisha, Gujarat, **Andhra Pradesh**.
Statement 3: India restored **~21.76 Mha during 2011-2020** (MoEFCC-IUCN report).
xa: India raised its target to **26 Mha by 2030** at **COP14 (2019)**.
⚠ Bonn Challenge = **Germany + IUCN, 2011**.
AP's degraded land is **33.81%**, about ten times Punjab's.

75.s: Which two regions are identified as the worst-hit continents or zones in terms of desertification?
o: Africa, particularly the Sahel, and Asia
75.x: Africa, especially the Sahel region, and Asia are identified as the worst-hit regions in relation to desertification.
75.tq: Use geographical pairing to distinguish the most affected regions from unrelated continents.
xs: The worst-hit regions are **Africa (Sahel) and Asia** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The notes name these two as the **worst-hit continents**; Europe, North America and Australia are not listed.
xa: The **Great Green Wall** (Africa) is an **African Union** belt across the Sahel, Senegal to Djibouti, to restore **100 Mha by 2030**.
Dust storms hit drylands of **NW India (Rajasthan)** and **West Asia/Sahel**.
UNCCD = treaty on **desertification, land degradation and drought**.

75.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Initiative)
 a. Aravalli Green Wall
 b. Great Green Wall of Africa
 c. Bonn Challenge
List-II (Description)
 i. African Union-led belt across the Sahel
 ii. Restoration targets of 150 Mha by 2020 and 350 Mha by 2030
 iii. Restoration of the Aravallis across four Indian regions to check the eastward spread of the Thar
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
75.x: The Aravalli Green Wall concerns the Aravallis; the Great Green Wall is the Sahelian belt; and the Bonn Challenge has the specified restoration targets.
75.tq: Start from the sure geographical pair and eliminate codes that misplace the initiatives.
xs: The correct match is **a–iii, b–i, c–ii** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Aravalli Green Wall**: restore the Aravallis across **Gujarat, Rajasthan, Haryana, Delhi** against the Thar's eastward spread.
**Great Green Wall (Africa)**: **African Union** belt across the Sahel; **Bonn Challenge**: **150 Mha by 2020**, **350 Mha by 2030**.
xa: Aravalli Green Wall: **41,410 ha** planted in 2024-25.
⚠ Bonn Challenge = **Germany + IUCN, 2011**.
**Great Green Wall of AP**: **SPSR Nellore** targets **50% green cover by 2047**.

75.s: On 24 December 2025, which measure was announced in relation to the Aravallis?
o: Transfer of the Aravalli region to the African Union
A ban by MoEFCC on granting any new mining leases in the Aravallis
A target to plant 100 million trees in the Aravallis
A ban on all existing mining operations in India
75.x: The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change banned the grant of any new mining leases in the Aravallis on 24 December 2025.
75.tq: Identify the precise administrative action, avoiding the broader and unsupported claim of banning all mining.
xs: On **24 Dec 2025**, **MoEFCC banned grant of any new mining leases in the Aravallis** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The ban covers **new leases**, not all existing mining in India.
xa: The **Aravalli Green Wall** restores Aravallis across **Gujarat, Rajasthan, Haryana, Delhi**.
It acts as a barrier to the **Thar's eastward spread**; **41,410 ha** planted in 2024-25.
MoEFCC gets only **0.07%** of the Union budget (TH, 5 Jun 2026).

75.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the Appiko Movement?
75.x: The Appiko Movement occurred in Karnataka in 1983 and was associated with Panduranga Hegde.
75.tq: Use a movement–state–leader–year combination to distinguish Appiko from Chipko.
xs: **Appiko — Karnataka — Panduranga Hegde — 1983** is correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Madhya Pradesh — 1977 — waterlogging and salinity** is the **Mitti Bachao Abhiyan**.
**Garrett Hardin (1968)** gave the **Tragedy of the Commons**, not a movement.
xa: Mitti Bachao Abhiyan: **Tawa dam, Hoshangabad**.
Both are forest and soil conservation movements.

75.s: SPSR Nellore has set a target of achieving what level of green cover by 2047?
75.x: SPSR Nellore targets 50% green cover by 2047 (Jul 2026) under the Great Green Wall of Andhra Pradesh, which aims to raise green cover and combat desertification.
75.tq: Match the district target with its deadline and percentage.
xs: **SPSR Nellore** targets **50% green cover by 2047** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The target is pursued via the **Great Green Wall of AP** and allied schemes (Jul 2026).
xa: The Great Green Wall of AP aims to **raise green cover + combat desertification**.
AP forest cover is **18.28%**; tree cover **2.87%**.
India's restoration target: **26 Mha by 2030** (COP14, 2019).

75.s: In Andhra Pradesh, drought-induced land degradation, desertification, wind erosion of topsoil and groundwater depletion are especially associated with:
o: Anantapur and Sri Sathya Sai districts
Uppada and the Krishna delta only
75.x: Anantapur and Sri Sathya Sai are associated with drought-induced degradation, desertification, wind erosion of topsoil and groundwater depletion.
75.tq: Link the cluster of degradation processes to the correct area.
xs: These problems are linked to **Anantapur and Sri Sathya Sai** (Rayalaseema) — so option **(1)** is correct.
They face **drought-induced degradation**, desertification, **topsoil loss by wind erosion**, **groundwater depletion**.
**Uppada** faces **coastal erosion**; **delta areas** face salinity + waterlogging.
xa: AP's degraded land = **33.81%** (SDG India Index 2023-24).
AP fallow land: **34.65 lakh ha = 21.26%** — more than forest area.
**SPSR Nellore**: **50% green cover by 2047** target.

75.s: Which of the following regional pairs is correctly matched?
75.x: Uppada in Kakinada is associated with coastal erosion. Delta areas are associated with salinity and waterlogging.
75.tq: Distinguish location-specific forms of land degradation.
xs: **Uppada — coastal erosion** is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Uppada** is in **Kakinada** on the AP coast.
**Delta areas** face **salinity + waterlogging**, not wind erosion; **Anantapur** faces drought and **wind erosion**, not tidal flooding.
xa: **Rayalaseema** (Anantapur, Sri Sathya Sai): desertification and **groundwater depletion**.
AP desertification area up **3.45%** (SDG India Index 2023-24).
AP forest cover **18.28%**; tree cover **2.87%**.

75.s: The United Nations General Assembly declared 2025–2034 as the UN Decade on Combating Sand and Dust Storms. The related international day is observed on:
75.x: The related day is observed on 12 July, while 2025–2034 has been declared the UN Decade on Combating Sand and Dust Storms.
75.tq: Separate the decade period from the associated calendar date.
xs: The sand and dust storms day is **12 July** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was declared by the **UNGA** along with the **2025-2034** Decade.
**24 December** (2025) is the date of the Aravalli mining-lease ban, not a UN day.
xa: ⚠ **World Day to Combat Desertification and Drought** = **17 June** (UNGA, **1994**).
**2026 host Kenya**; theme "**Rangelands: Recognise. Respect. Restore.**"
Dust storms hit **Rajasthan** and West Asia/Sahel.

75.s: Which of the following best describes a cool roof?
o: A roof designed to store solar heat for night-time use
A roof made only of metallic sheets
A roof treated with a high-reflectance coating to reduce heat absorption
A roof covered entirely with vegetation
75.x: Cool roofs use white or reflective, high-reflectance coatings that reduce heat absorption and lower the indoor cooling load.
75.tq: Identify the precise functional definition instead of selecting a merely related roofing technology.
xs: A cool roof is **treated with a high-reflectance coating to reduce heat absorption** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Cool roofs use **white/reflective** coatings and cut the **indoor cooling load**.
xa: The **AP Cool Surface Policy 2023** promotes **reflective materials**.
UHI causes: **concrete/asphalt** (low albedo), loss of vegetation, waste heat, dense built canyons.
**NDMA** issued national heat-wave action plan guidelines in **2016**.

75.s: Which one of the following is NOT an objective of the Andhra Pradesh Cool Surface Policy, 2023?
o: Promoting the use of reflective materials
Promoting rural heat as a separate policy objective
Providing affordable solutions against urban heat
75.x: The policy objectives include affordable urban heat solutions, reduction of heat and energy demand, and promotion of reflective materials. Rural heat is not identified as an objective.
75.tq: Find the option that falls outside the stated policy objectives.
xs: **Rural heat** is NOT an objective of the AP Cool Surface Policy 2023 — so option **(2)** is correct.
Its objectives: affordable solutions against **urban** heat, tackle **heat and energy demand**, promote **reflective materials**.
xa: ⚠ The **"rural heat"** trap was asked in **APPSC 2023**.
**Cool roofs** = high-reflectance roof coatings.
**71%** of Indians surveyed had faced heat waves (Yale survey, TH 5 Jun 2026).

76.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the principal significance of the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980?
o: It required Central approval for diversion of forest land.
It transferred all forests to local bodies.
It established the National Green Tribunal.
76.x: The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 made Central approval necessary for diversion of forest land.
76.tq: Match the statute with its distinctive regulatory function rather than its subject in general terms.
xs: The **Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980** requires **Central approval for diverting forest land** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Coastal stretches are regulated by the **CRZ (1991)** notification under EPA.
The specialised environmental tribunal came with the **NGT Act 2010**.
xa: Chronology: **Water 1974 → Water Cess 1977 → Forest 1980 → Air 1981 → EPA 1986 → NGT 2010**.
**Green Credit** afforestation can be swapped for compensatory afforestation under **Van (S&S) Rules 2023**.
The **Wildlife (Protection) Act** dates from **1972**.

76.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 — legal basis for EIA and CRZ notifications
Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 — creation of the pollution control boards
76.x: The pollution control boards were created under the Water Act, 1974. The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is an umbrella law whose Section 3 supports EIA and CRZ notifications.
76.tq: Reject the option that assigns a body’s origin to the wrong statute.
xs: **EPA 1986 — creation of the pollution control boards** is NOT correctly matched — so option **(3)** is correct.
The boards (CPCB and SPCBs) were created by the **Water Act 1974**; the Air Act gave the same boards air functions.

xa: APPCB implements **Water, Air and EP Acts** + waste rules.
