**Draft 2020** proposed cutting the notice from **30 to 20 days**.
Hearings are conducted by the **SPCB**, with the **District Collector** presiding.

77.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes Categories B1 and B2 under the EIA Notification, 2006?
o: B1 projects are cleared by EAC, whereas B2 projects are cleared by MoEFCC.
B1 projects do not require EIA, whereas B2 projects require full EIA.
B1 projects require EIA, whereas B2 projects do not require EIA.
Both B1 and B2 projects always require full EIA by MoEFCC.
77.x: Category B1 projects require an EIA, while Category B2 projects do not; both are associated with state-level appraisal and clearance arrangements.
77.tq: Discriminate between the closely named B1 and B2 categories.
xs: **B1 projects require EIA, whereas B2 projects do not** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Both are appraised by **SEAC** and cleared by **SEIAA**, not by EAC or MoEFCC.
xa: ⚠ **A** → EAC → MoEFCC; **B1/B2** → SEAC → SEIAA; only **B2** has no EIA.
**B2** projects are also **exempt from public hearing**.
**Draft 2020** proposed moving more projects to **B2/exempt**.

77.s: PARIVESH is best described as:
o: A single-window portal for online environment, forest, wildlife and CRZ clearances
A programme for preparing baseline biodiversity data
A committee for appraisal of Category A projects
77.x: PARIVESH is an online single-window platform for environment, forest, wildlife and Coastal Regulation Zone clearances.
77.tq: Distinguish a digital clearance platform from statutory bodies.
xs: PARIVESH is a **single-window portal for online environment, forest, wildlife and CRZ clearances** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is not a tribunal (the **NGT**) or an appraisal committee (the **EAC**).
xa: Launched **2018**; now **PARIVESH 3.0** using **AI** (Economic Survey 2025-26).
Platform for the **120-day** escalation to **SCEIA**.
Expansion: **Pro-Active and Responsive facilitation by Interactive, Virtuous and Environmental Single-window Hub**.

77.s: Which statement regarding the Draft EIA Notification, 2020 is correct?
o: It was not finalised and was criticised for provisions including post-facto clearance.
It proposed longer public consultation periods than the 2006 notification.
It was finally enacted without modification.
It abolished penalties and remediation plans for violations.
77.x: The 2020 draft was not finalised and was contested, particularly for proposing post-facto clearance and shorter consultation periods.
77.tq: Reject absolute claims about a draft becoming final law.
xs: The Draft 2020 **was not finalised** and was criticised for **post-facto clearance** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It proposed **shorter** consultation (**30 to 20 days**), not longer.
It relied on **penalties, compensation, remediation plans** for violations — it did not abolish them.
xa: Other contested items: more **B2/exempt** projects; **yearly** compliance reports.
**Vanashakti** final verdict (**29 July 2026**) quashed the **2021 Office Memorandum** on retrospective EC.
Prior EC is **mandatory** under EIA 2006.

77.s: Which one of the following has been suggested as a measure to address the criticism that EIA consultants may lack independence?
o: Transfer of EIA preparation entirely to project proponents
Permitting post-facto clearances as a routine measure
Creation of an independent EIA authority
77.x: An independent EIA authority has been suggested to improve the credibility and independence of environmental assessments.
77.tq: Match the identified institutional defect with the appropriate reform.
xs: The suggested fix is an **independent EIA authority** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It answers the criticism that EIAs are prepared by **proponent-paid consultants**.
Routine post-facto clearance and abolishing hearings would worsen, not fix, the problem.
xa: Other criticisms: **no central baseline data bank**; **weak emergency plans**.
UPSC way-forward: **sector-wide EIAs** (strategic/cumulative).
Jul 2026 concern: **bureaucrats replace scientists**.

77.s:
Arrange the following developments relating to EIA in chronological order:
A. Enactment of NEPA in the United States
B. First use of EIA in India
C. First formal EIA notification in India
D. EIA amendment creating SCEIA and prescribing a 120-day timeline
77.x: The sequence is NEPA in 1969, first use of EIA in India in 1978, the first formal notification in 1994, and the later amendment creating SCEIA with a 120-day timeline.
77.tq: Anchor the sequence using the earliest and latest dates first.
xs: The order is **A, B, C, D** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**NEPA 1969** (US) → EIA first used in India **1978** → first formal notification **1994** → **SCEIA** + **120-day** amendment (**23 Jul 2026**).
xa: ⚠ Sources differ on India's start: **1976-77** (DST, river-valley) vs **1978**.
EIA Notification **2006** replaced the 1994 notification.
Public hearing added by the **1997 amendment**.

77.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: River-valley projects — first sector appraised in India
LG Polymers gas leak — Visakhapatnam, 2020 — National Green Tribunal
Great Nicobar EIA — absence of any baseline data collection
NEPA — first EIA law — United States, 1969
77.x: The Great Nicobar EIA was criticised for thin baseline data, not for the complete absence of baseline data collection. The other pairs are correctly matched.
77.tq: Find the overstatement by distinguishing thin or inadequate data from total absence of data.
xs: **Great Nicobar EIA — absence of any baseline data** is wrongly matched — so option **(3)** is correct.
The criticism was **thin baseline data** in the Great Nicobar EIA (11 May 2026), not its total absence.
**River-valley projects** = first sector appraised; **LG Polymers** (Visakhapatnam, 2020) handled by **NGT**; **NEPA 1969** = first EIA law.
xa: A **High-Powered Committee** on the Great Nicobar project was set up on NGT directions.
Wider criticism: **no central baseline data bank**.
EIA first used in India in **1978**; first notification **1994**.

77.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Tool)
a. Environmental Impact Assessment
b. Life-Cycle Assessment
c. Cumulative Impact Assessment
d. Environmental audit

List-II (Scope)
i. Compliance check of an operating unit after the fact
ii. A product or process across its whole life cycle
iii. A project evaluated before it starts
iv. Combined effect of several projects in one area or basin

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
77.x: EIA concerns a project before it starts; LCA covers a product or process through its life cycle; cumulative impact assessment examines combined effects; and an environmental audit checks an operating unit after the fact.
77.tq: Start from the sure EIA pair and complete the one-to-one matching without repeating a scope.
xs: The correct match is **a–iii, b–ii, c–iv, d–i** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**EIA** = a specific **project before it starts**; **LCA** = a **product/process across its life**.
**Cumulative Impact Assessment** = combined effect of several projects in one area/basin; **environmental audit** = compliance check of an **operating** unit after the fact.
xa: **SEA** = impacts of **policies, plans and programmes**, upstream of projects.
⚠ EIA = **project**; LCA = **product**; SEA = **policies/plans**; audit = **after** the fact.
The EIA/LCA definitions were asked in **APPSC 2025**.

77.s: A government is assessing the environmental implications of a new transport policy before individual road projects are selected. Which tool is most appropriate?
77.x: Strategic Environmental Assessment examines policies, plans and programmes upstream of individual projects. A project-level EIA is conducted for a specific project, whereas an environmental audit is generally an after-the-fact compliance check.
77.tq: Identify the level of decision-making before choosing between project and strategic assessment.
xs: A new transport policy calls for **Strategic Environmental Assessment** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**SEA** covers **policies, plans and programmes**, upstream of projects.
**Project-level EIA** studies one project before it starts; **LCA** a product's life cycle; an **audit** checks an operating unit after the fact.
xa: UPSC way-forward: **sector-wide EIAs** (strategic/cumulative) needed.
**Cumulative Impact Assessment**: combined effect of several projects in one basin.
EIA requires **assessment of alternatives** in location and process technology.

77.s: The 12 principles of green chemistry were formulated by:
77.x: The 12 principles of green chemistry (prevent waste, atom economy, safer solvents, renewable feedstocks, design for degradation) were set out by Anastas and Warner in 1998. The Brundtland Commission (1987) defined sustainable development; Rachel Carson wrote Silent Spring (1962); the Club of Rome issued Limits to Growth (1972).
77.tq: Green chemistry = 12 principles, Anastas and Warner, 1998.
xs: The **12 principles** of green chemistry are by **Anastas and Warner, 1998** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Examples: **prevent waste**, **atom economy**, **safer solvents**, **renewable feedstocks**, **design for degradation**.
xa: Green chemistry: reduce or eliminate **hazardous substances**.
**Cleaner production**: cut waste **at source** (process change, input substitution).
EIA requires assessment of alternatives in **process technology**.

77.s:
Consider the following statements about the early stages of EIA:
1. Screening decides whether a project needs EIA and which category it falls in.
2. Scoping identifies the key issues and sets the Terms of Reference.
3. Scoping is the stage at which an expert committee evaluates the final EIA report.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
77.x: Statement 1 is correct: screening decides need for EIA and category. Statement 2 is correct: scoping fixes key issues and Terms of Reference. Statement 3 is wrong: evaluation of the EIA report by the expert committee is appraisal, not scoping. So 1 only is incomplete and options with 3 are wrong.
77.tq: Screening = whether/which category; Scoping = ToR; Appraisal = expert committee.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1: **screening** decides whether a project needs EIA and its **category**.
Statement 2: **scoping** fixes the key issues and **Terms of Reference**.
Statement 3 is wrong: expert evaluation of the EIA report is **appraisal**.
xa: EIA 2006 stages: **Screening → Scoping → Public consultation → Appraisal → Decision**.
⚠ **Category A** has **no screening** — always full EIA.
**Baseline data** = survey of the existing environment.

77.s:
Match the stage of EIA with what happens at it:
List-I (Stage)
a. Appraisal
b. Decision
c. Monitoring
List-II (What happens)
i. Environmental clearance granted with conditions or rejected
ii. Expert committee evaluates the EIA report
iii. Implementation of the Environmental Management Plan is checked
Select the correct answer:
77.x: Appraisal is evaluation of the EIA report by the expert committee (a-ii); Decision is EC granted with conditions or rejected (b-i); Monitoring checks EMP implementation (c-iii). Option B swaps appraisal and decision; C and D wrongly link the EMP to appraisal or decision.
77.tq: Appraisal = committee reads report; Decision = grant/reject; Monitoring = EMP.
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-i, c-iii** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Appraisal**: expert committee evaluates the EIA report; **decision**: EC granted with conditions or rejected.
**Monitoring**: **EMP** implementation checked.
xa: Category **A** appraised by **EAC**; **B1/B2** by **SEAC**.
Clearance: **MoEFCC** for A; **SEIAA** for B.
Earlier stages: **screening**, **scoping**, baseline data, **public consultation**.

77.s:
Arrange the following stages of EIA in the correct chronological order:
A. Appraisal
B. Screening
C. Decision
D. Scoping
77.x: The sequence is Screening, Scoping, Appraisal and Decision; public consultation occurs before appraisal.
77.tq: Use the first and last stages, then place the intervening steps.
xs: The order is **B, D, A, C** — **Screening → Scoping → Appraisal → Decision** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Under EIA 2006, **public consultation** comes between scoping and appraisal.
xa: **Scoping** sets the **Terms of Reference**.
**Monitoring** of EMP follows the decision.
**Category A** skips screening; always full EIA.

77.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Category)
a. Category A
b. Category B
c. Category A clearance
 d. Category B clearance

List-II (Authority)
i. State Environment Impact Assessment Authority
 ii. State Expert Appraisal Committee
 iii. Expert Appraisal Committee at the Centre
 iv. Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
77.x: Category A projects are appraised by the central EAC and cleared by MoEFCC. Category B projects are appraised by the State EAC and cleared by SEIAA.
77.tq: Separate the appraisal authority from the clearance authority before matching the categories.
xs: The correct match is **a–iii, b–ii, c–iv, d–i** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Category A**: appraised by central **EAC**, cleared by **MoEFCC**.
**Category B**: appraised by **SEAC**, cleared by **SEIAA**.
xa: ⚠ Only **B2** has no EIA; **B1** needs EIA.
**Category A**: no screening; always full EIA.
Backup bodies (2026): **SAEIA** for SEIAA; **SCEIA** for SEAC.

77.s: Under the July 2026 amendment, if a State Expert Appraisal Committee fails to decide a proposal within 120 days, the proposal may escalate to:
o: The new Standing Committee on Environmental Impact Assessment on PARIVESH
77.x: The July 2026 amendment provides for escalation after 120 days to the new SCEIA through PARIVESH.
77.tq: Link the time limit with the newly designated authority.
xs: After **120 days**, a SEAC proposal escalates to the new **SCEIA** via **PARIVESH** — so option **(4)** is correct.
This is the **Jul 2026** amendment (23 Jul 2026), with auto-transfer via PARIVESH.
xa: ⚠ **SAEIA** ↔ SEIAA; **SCEIA** ↔ SEAC.
Category B no longer defaults to the central **EAC** when a state committee lapses.
Backup bodies' tenure: **6 + 6 months** (max 1 year).

77.s: The proposal for sector-wide EIAs is intended primarily to strengthen which approach?
77.x: Sector-wide EIAs are intended to incorporate strategic and cumulative perspectives, allowing impacts across a sector or region to be assessed rather than examining projects in isolation.
77.tq: Infer the broader assessment level from the phrase sector-wide.
xs: **Sector-wide EIAs** aim to strengthen **strategic and cumulative assessment** — so option **(3)** is correct.
This is the **UPSC way-forward**: sector-wide EIAs (i.e., strategic/cumulative) needed.
xa: **SEA** = policies, plans, programmes; **Cumulative Impact Assessment** = several projects in one area/basin.
Criticism: EIAs by **proponent-paid consultants**; no central baseline data bank.
Suggested fix: an **independent EIA authority**.

77.s: Under the EIA Notification, 2006, environmental clearance is compulsory for how many project categories?
77.x: The 2006 notification made environmental clearance compulsory for 39 project categories.
77.tq: Direct quantitative recall with nearby numerical distractors.
xs: EC is compulsory for **39 project categories** under EIA 2006 — so option **(2)** is correct.
The 2006 notification also covers safeguards for **air, water, land, biodiversity, wildlife habitat**.
xa: Focus shifted from **investment to impact potential**.
Categories: **A** (EAC → MoEFCC), **B1** and **B2** (SEAC → SEIAA).
Notified **14 Sep 2006**, replacing the **1994** notification.

77.s: Who presides over the public hearing conducted by the State Pollution Control Board?
77.x: The State Pollution Control Board conducts the hearing, while the District Collector presides over it.
77.tq: Use the authority-role distinction to avoid swapping institutions.
xs: The **District Collector** presides over the public hearing — so option **(1)** is correct.
The hearing is **conducted by the SPCB** (22 May 2026).
xa: Notice at least **30 days**; hearing within **45 days** (EIA 2006).
APPCB hearing on the **Water Aerodrome at Prakasam Barrage** — HRF called the draft EIA error-ridden.
**SEIAA** and **EAC** clear projects; they do not preside over hearings.

77.s: Under the EIA Notification, 2006, the public-hearing notice must be given at least how many days in advance, and the hearing must be completed within what period?
77.x: The notice period is at least 30 days, and the hearing is to be completed within 45 days.
77.tq: Pair two procedural time limits without reversing their order.
xs: EIA 2006: notice at least **30 days**; hearing completed within **45 days** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**20 days** is the **Draft 2020** proposal, not EIA 2006.
xa: ⚠ Notice **30 days** (EIA 2006) vs **20 days** (Draft 2020); hearing within **45 days**.
Hearings are conducted by the **SPCB**.
Public consultation = hearing + **written responses**.

77.s: Which of the following was a provision of the July 2026 amendment to the EIA framework?
o: The Centre may remove EAC, SEAC or SEIAA members mid-term for persistent delays.
Scientists alone must replace all administrative members.
All Category B projects must automatically be transferred to the central EAC.
State committees may retain proposals indefinitely without escalation.
77.x: The amendment permits the Centre to remove members of EAC, SEAC or SEIAA mid-term for persistent delays. It also introduced an escalation mechanism rather than automatic transfer of all Category B projects to the central EAC.
77.tq: Identify the precise institutional power among reversed alternatives.
xs: The Centre **may remove EAC, SEAC or SEIAA members mid-term for persistent delays** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Category B **no longer defaults to the central EAC** — escalation goes to **SCEIA** after **120 days**, so options (3) and (4) are wrong.
xa: Member tenure: **3 to 4 years**; max **two terms**; age limit **70**.
Concern: **bureaucrats replace scientists**; speed over science.
MoEFCC had proposed **SCEIA and SAEIA** earlier (Mar 2026).

77.s: Which of the following correctly represents the backup arrangement referred to for environmental appraisal bodies in 2026?
o: NGT for SEIAA and NEAA for SEAC
SCEIA for SEIAA and SAEIA for SEAC
EAC for SEIAA and CPCB for SEAC
SAEIA for SEIAA and SCEIA for SEAC
77.x: The stated backup bodies are SAEIA in place of SEIAA and SCEIA in place of SEAC.
77.tq: Discriminate between the similar abbreviations by matching each backup body to its parent body.
xs: **SAEIA** stands in for **SEIAA** and **SCEIA** for **SEAC** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Option (2) swaps the pair.
xa: Tenure of backup bodies: **6 + 6 months** (max 1 year).
They step in when a State's **SEIAA or SEAC lapses**.
MoEFCC had proposed **SCEIA and SAEIA** earlier (**Mar 2026**).

77.s:
Consider the following provisions associated with the Draft EIA Notification, 2020:
1. The public-hearing notice period was proposed to be reduced from 30 days to 20 days.
2. More projects were proposed to be moved to Category B2 or exempted.
3. Compliance reports were proposed to be submitted yearly instead of half-yearly.
4. Violations could be reported by any member of the public without restriction.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: The draft proposed a 20-day notice period, more B2 or exempt projects and yearly compliance reports. It restricted reporting of violations to the violator or government, so statement 4 is false.
77.tq: Locate the false statement by testing the reporting restriction.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Draft 2020: notice cut **30 to 20 days**; more projects moved to **B2/exempt**; compliance reports **yearly instead of half-yearly**.
Statement 4 is wrong: violations were reportable **only by the violator or government**.
xa: It also proposed **post-facto clearance** on payment of penalties.
The draft has **not been finalised**.
EIA 2006: notice at least **30 days**; hearing within **45 days**.

77.s: The time limit prescribed in the August 2023 direction for the Border Roads Organisation to plant the trees was:
77.x: The NGT directed the plantation of the trees within one month.
77.tq: Separate the quantity of the direction from its compliance period.
xs: The NGT gave the **Border Roads Organisation** **one month** to plant trees — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Aug 2023** order (Uttarakhand) required at least **10,000 trees** within **one month** (PYQ).
xa: **Rat-hole mining** in **Meghalaya (2014)** was declared illegal/banned by NGT.
NGT fined **Maharashtra and West Bengal (2022)** for waste mismanagement.
**LG Polymers** (May 2020): **Rs 50 crore** interim deposit.

77.s:
Consider the following statements regarding criticisms of the Environmental Impact Assessment process:
1. EIA reports are often prepared by consultants paid by the project proponents.
2. There is no central baseline data bank for EIA purposes.
3. Emergency plans associated with projects may be weak.
4. Certain projects or situations may be exempted from public hearings.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: All four statements describe identified criticisms of the EIA process: proponent-paid consultants, absence of a central baseline data bank, weak emergency plans and exemptions from hearings.
77.tq: Test the complete set of criticisms by checking each statement independently.
xs: All four — **1, 2, 3 and 4** — are criticisms of EIA, so option **(4)** is correct.
EIA is prepared by **proponent-paid consultants**; there is **no central baseline data bank**.
**Weak emergency plans** and **hearings exempted** complete the list.
xa: Fix: **independent EIA authority**.
Exempted from hearings: **defence and strategic** projects, **B2** projects.
Post-facto clearances risk becoming "**the design**".

77.s:
Consider the following statements about the evolution of EIA in India:
1. The EIA Notification, 1994 was issued on 27 January 1994 under the Environment (Protection) Act.
2. Before the 1994 notification, environmental clearance was only an administrative decision.
3. The EIA Notification, 2006 replaced the 1994 notification.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: The 1994 notification was issued on 27 January under the EPA, clearance had earlier been only administrative, and the 2006 notification replaced it.
77.tq: Arrange the legal transition in sequence and verify both the date and the status of clearance before 1994.
xs: All three statements — **1, 2 and 3** — are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
Statement 1: EIA Notification **1994** was notified on **27 Jan 1994** under **EPA**.
Statement 2: **till 1994**, EC was only an **administrative decision**.
Statement 3: the **EIA Notification 2006** (**14 Sep 2006**) replaced the 1994 notification.
xa: Public hearing was made mandatory by the **1997 amendment**.
Later amendments: **2009** (expanded list), **2013** (thermal power), **2015** (expansion and modernisation).
**Draft 2020** (post-facto, shorter consultation) has **not been finalised**.

77.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Renewable feedstocks are associated with green chemistry.
2. Designing products for degradation is an example of a green chemistry principle.
3. Cleaner production relies exclusively on end-of-pipe treatment.
4. Both cleaner production and green chemistry seek to reduce impacts at the design stage.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is false because cleaner production is preventive and seeks process or input changes at the source rather than relying exclusively on end-of-pipe treatment.
77.tq: Reject the extreme word exclusively and combine the related design-stage principles.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 4** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statements 1 and 2: **renewable feedstocks** and **design for degradation** are green chemistry principles.
Statement 3 is wrong: cleaner production is **preventive**, cutting waste **at source**, versus end-of-pipe treatment.
Statement 4: both **shrink impacts at design stage**, so EIA/LCA find fewer residual impacts.
xa: Other principles: **prevent waste**, **atom economy**, **safer solvents**.
**12 principles**: Anastas and Warner, **1998**.
APPCB encourages **cleaner production technologies**.

77.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the EIA process:
1. Baseline data represents a survey of the existing environment.
2. Impact prediction includes comparison of alternatives.
3. The Environmental Management Plan forms part of the mitigation planning process.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: Baseline environmental conditions are surveyed, alternatives are compared during impact prediction, and mitigation planning includes an Environmental Management Plan.
77.tq: Combine three linked components of the impact-assessment stage.
xs: All three statements — **1, 2 and 3** — are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Baseline data**: existing environment surveyed.
**Impact prediction**: alternatives compared; mitigation plan + **Environmental Management Plan**; risk assessment.
xa: **Monitoring**: EMP implementation is checked.
EIA requires **assessment of alternatives** in location and **process technology**.
Criticism: **no central baseline data bank**; thin baseline in the **Great Nicobar** EIA.

77.s:
Consider the following statements about exemption from public hearing in the EIA process:
1. Defence, national-security and strategic projects are exempt, as their details are kept confidential.
2. B2 projects and units inside notified industrial estates are exempt.
3. Whether a project is 'strategic' is decided by the State Pollution Control Board.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
77.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct exemptions. Statement 3 is wrong: 'strategic' is determined by the Central Government, which is criticised as arbitrary; the SPCB only conducts the hearing. So 1 only is incomplete and options with 3 are wrong.
77.tq: Exempt: defence/strategic, B2, industrial estates; 'strategic' is the Centre's call.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
Statement 1: **defence, national-security and strategic** projects are exempt (details kept confidential).
Statement 2: **B2** projects + units inside **notified industrial estates** are exempt.
Statement 3 is wrong: "strategic" is **determined by the Central Government** — criticised as arbitrary.
xa: The SPCB only **conducts** the hearing, with the **District Collector** presiding.
The executive-exemption criticism dates to **2 Jan 2026**.
Criticism also: **hearings exempted**; EIAs by proponent-paid consultants.

77.s: The principal criticism of the July 2026 amendment to the EIA framework is that it may:
o: Replace scientists with bureaucrats and prioritise speed over science
Give excessive control to local communities over scientific appraisal
Make every project subject to a full EIA
77.x: The amendment has been criticised on the ground that bureaucratic control may replace scientific expertise and that speed may be prioritised over scientific appraisal.
77.tq: Identify the stated criticism rather than the procedural detail.
xs: The main criticism: **bureaucrats replace scientists** and **speed over science** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The amendment speeds appraisal (**120-day** escalation, removal of members for delays), it does not abolish clearances.
xa: Wider criticism: EIAs by **proponent-paid consultants**; **no central baseline data bank**; weak emergency plans.
Fix suggested: **independent EIA authority**.
Post-facto clearances risk becoming "**the design**" (31 Jul 2026).

77.s:
Consider the following statements about Supreme Court cases on environmental clearance:
1. Common Cause v. Union of India (2017) concerned mining in Odisha without or beyond environmental clearance and directed compensation equal to 100% of the value of illegally extracted minerals.
2. Noble M. Paikada v. Union of India (2024) examined the 2020 exemption from environmental clearance for extraction of ordinary earth for linear projects.
3. In Noble M. Paikada, the Supreme Court upheld the blanket exemption as valid.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
77.x: Statement 1 is correct: Common Cause (2017) dealt with Odisha mining without or beyond EC and ordered compensation of 100% of the value of illegally extracted minerals. Statement 2 is correct: Noble M. Paikada (2024) examined the 2020 exemption from EC for extraction of ordinary earth for linear projects. Statement 3 is wrong: the Court held the blanket exemption arbitrary, not valid. Hence 1 and 2 only.
77.tq: Common Cause = Odisha mining, 100% value; Paikada = ordinary earth exemption, held arbitrary.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1: **Common Cause v UoI (2017)** — Odisha mining without or beyond EC; compensation of **100%** of the mineral's value.
Statement 2: **Noble M. Paikada v UoI (2024)** — the **2020 exemption from EC** for ordinary earth for linear projects (**APPSC 2024**).
Statement 3 is wrong: the SC held the **blanket exemption arbitrary**.
xa: **Alembic Pharmaceuticals (2020)**: ex post facto EC contrary to EIA; **2002** MoEF circular quashed.
⚠ Vanashakti: **May 2025** struck down → **Nov 2025** recalled (**2:1**) → **29 July 2026** final, prospective.
**S.P. Muthuraman (2025)** also held retrospective ECs illegal.

77.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Alembic Pharmaceuticals v. Rohit Prajapati:
1. It was decided in 2020.
2. The Supreme Court held that ex post facto environmental clearance was contrary to the EIA regime.
3. The 2002 Ministry of Environment and Forests circular permitting such clearance was quashed.
4. The Court necessarily directed closure of every project concerned.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because compensation was imposed instead of ordering closure in every case.
77.tq: Find the wrong consequence in an otherwise case-specific statement set.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Alembic Pharmaceuticals v Rohit Prajapati (2020)** held ex post facto EC **contrary to the EIA regime**.
It **quashed the 2002 MoEF circular** allowing such clearance.
Statement 4 is wrong: **compensation was imposed instead of closure**.
xa: **Common Cause v UoI (2017)**: Odisha mining; compensation of **100%** of the mineral's value.
**S.P. Muthuraman (2025)** also held retrospective ECs illegal.
Exam angle: prior EC is **mandatory** under EIA 2006; post-facto only as a narrow exception.

77.s:
With reference to the Vanashakti litigation, consider the following statements:
1. The May 2025 ruling struck down the 2017 Notification and the 2021 Office Memorandum.
2. In November 2025, the ruling was recalled by a 2:1 majority.
3. The recall relied, among other decisions, on D. Swamy (2021) and Pahwa Plastics (2022).
4. Approximately ₹20,000 crore worth of projects was reported to be at stake.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: All four statements are correct. The May 2025 ruling struck down the specified instruments, was recalled in November 2025 by a 2:1 majority, relied on the cited earlier cases, and affected projects valued at approximately ₹20,000 crore.
77.tq: Track multiple stages of a case without confusing the original ruling with its recall.
xs: All four statements — **1, 2, 3 and 4** — are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
**May 2025** ruling struck down the **2017 Notification / 2021 OM**; **Nov 2025** recall by **2:1** majority.
The recall relied on **D Swamy (2021)** and **Pahwa Plastics (2022)**, which allowed post-facto EC in exceptional cases.
About **₹20,000 crore** of projects faced demolition (LENS, Nov 2025).
xa: Final verdict: **29 July 2026**, led by **CJI Surya Kant**; ruling **prospective**.
May 2025 language: "**gross illegality**" and "anathema".
**S.P. Muthuraman (2025)** also held retrospective ECs illegal.

77.s: Which one of the following correctly states the effect of the final Vanashakti verdict of 29 July 2026?
o: It retrospectively validated all clearances obtained under the 2021 Office Memorandum.
It prospectively nullified the 2021 Office Memorandum, while earlier clearances under the 2017 Notification and 2021 Office Memorandum survived.
It made the 2017 Notification available to all fresh violators seeking regularisation.
It permanently prohibited the Centre from issuing any time-limited notification under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
77.x: The final verdict prospectively nullified the 2021 Office Memorandum, but earlier environmental clearances under the 2017 Notification and 2021 Office Memorandum survived. It did not open those instruments to fresh violators or permanently bar time-limited notifications under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
77.tq: Distinguish prospective effect, retrospective validation and future eligibility.
xs: The verdict **prospectively nullified the 2021 Office Memorandum**, while **earlier ECs under the 2017 Notification and 2021 OM survive** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Fresh violators** cannot seek regularisation under the 2017 Notification or 2021 SOP, so option (3) is wrong.
The Centre **may issue time-limited notifications under EPA 1986**, so option (4) is wrong.
xa: Bench led by **CJI Surya Kant** (**29 July 2026**).
Ex post facto EC must pass **Arts 14 and 21** (proportionality).
SC keeps its power under **Article 142**.

77.s: In the context of environmental clearance, which of the following is the correct general rule?
o: Prior clearance is required only for products assessed through LCA.
Environmental clearance is needed only after an environmental audit identifies non-compliance.
Prior environmental clearance is mandatory under the EIA framework, while post-facto approval is only a narrow exception.
Post-facto approval is the normal rule and prior clearance is optional.
77.x: The general rule under the EIA framework is that prior environmental clearance is mandatory. Post-facto approval, where recognised at all, is treated only as a narrow exception.
77.tq: Distinguish the governing rule from exceptional regularisation mechanisms.
xs: **Prior EC is mandatory under EIA; post-facto approval is only a narrow exception** — so option **(3)** is correct.
This is the exam angle in the notes: prior EC mandatory under **EIA 2006**.
An **environmental audit** is an after-the-fact compliance check, and **LCA** is a product tool — neither is the clearance trigger.
xa: **Vanashakti (29 July 2026)**: ex post facto EC only via **Arts 14 and 21** test and **Article 142**.
**Alembic (2020)**: ex post facto EC contrary to the EIA regime.
**Draft 2020** proposed post-facto clearance but was **not finalised**.

77.s: According to the final Vanashakti verdict of 29 July 2026, any ex post facto environmental clearance must satisfy the test of:
o: Article 252 read with the Water Act, 1974
Article 323B read with the NGT Act, 2010
77.x: The Court held that ex post facto EC must meet Articles 14 and 21 (a proportionality test), while the Supreme Court keeps its power under Article 142. Articles 48A and 51A(g) are a Directive Principle and a Fundamental Duty, not the test laid down. Article 252 is the Water Act's basis; Article 323B concerns tribunals generally.
77.tq: Vanashakti 2026: Arts 14 + 21 test; Art 142 reserved for the SC.
xs: Ex post facto EC must satisfy **Articles 14 and 21 (proportionality)** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The SC also **keeps its power under Article 142**.
⚠ **Article 252** is the **Water Act's** basis — not this test.
xa: The ruling was **prospective** — earlier ECs under the **2017 Notification and 2021 OM** survive.
The Centre may issue **time-limited notifications under EPA 1986**.
Verdict date **29 July 2026**; Bench led by **CJI Surya Kant**.

77.s: Which of the following correctly describes the NGT action concerning the LG Polymers incident at Visakhapatnam?
o: It transferred the matter to the National Environment Appellate Authority without any financial direction.
It took suo motu cognisance and ordered an interim deposit of Rs 50 crore.
It ordered a permanent ban on all chemical industries in Andhra Pradesh.
It directed the Border Roads Organisation to undertake plantation in Uttarakhand.
77.x: Following the Visakhapatnam styrene leak in May 2020, the NGT took suo motu cognisance and ordered an interim deposit of Rs 50 crore.
77.tq: Match the authority’s action to the correct incident instead of confusing separate NGT orders.
xs: The NGT **took suo motu cognisance and ordered an interim deposit of Rs 50 crore** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The incident was the **Visakhapatnam styrene leak, May 2020** (LG Polymers).
BRO plantation in **Uttarakhand** is a separate NGT order (**Aug 2023**).
xa: The **LG Polymers** leak is part of the AP angle, handled by NGT.
NGT **Jan 2026** suo motu: Rajasthan, MP, UP over sewage in drinking water.
Rat-hole mining: **Meghalaya (2014)**.

77.s: The inter-state dispute concerning the Polavaram project primarily relates to submergence in:
77.x: The Polavaram inter-state dispute concerns submergence in neighbouring Odisha and Chhattisgarh and was raised before the Supreme Court.
77.tq: Identify the neighbouring states directly affected by the project’s submergence issue.
xs: The Polavaram dispute is over **submergence in Odisha and Chhattisgarh** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was raised before the **Supreme Court**.
xa: **Telangana** moved the SC seeking an EIA review of **Indira Sagar Polavaram** (**APPSC 2018**).
EIA in India began with **river-valley projects**.
AP angle also: APPCB hearing on the **Water Aerodrome at Prakasam Barrage**.

77.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Environmental Impact Assessment identifies, predicts and evaluates the environmental impacts of development projects.
R2 Code of Practices is a framework for environmentally responsible electronics recycling.
R2 Code of Practices is another name for Environmental Impact Assessment.
EIA assesses the likely environmental consequences of a proposed project or activity before implementation.
77.x: Option C is incorrect: R2 is a code for responsible electronics recycling. EIA is the process of assessing a project's likely environmental impact before it starts.
77.tq: Discriminate R2 from EIA.
n: EIA assesses the likely environmental consequences of a proposed project or activity before implementation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 66-68]
EIA identifies environmental impacts of development projects. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 66-68]
EIA predicts environmental impacts of development projects. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 66-68]
EIA evaluates environmental impacts of development projects. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 66-68]
R2 Code of Practices is not EIA. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 66-68]
R2 Code of Practices is for environmentally responsible electronics recycling. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 66-68]
EIA stands for Environmental Impact Assessment. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 66-68]
EIA is linked with project and development impacts. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 66-68]
xs: The **incorrect** statement is that the **R2 Code of Practices** is another name for **EIA** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **R2 Code of Practices** is **not EIA** — it is for **environmentally responsible electronics recycling**.
**EIA** **identifies**, **predicts** and **evaluates** the environmental impacts of **development projects**, **before implementation**.
xa: EIA stages under **EIA 2006**: **Screening → Scoping → Public consultation → Appraisal → Decision**.
⚠ EIA = **project**; **LCA** = product life cycle; **SEA** = policies/plans; **audit** = after the fact.
Global origin: **NEPA, USA, 1969**; India codified EIA in **1994**.

77.s: Cleaner production is best described as a strategy that:
o: Treats pollution only after it has been generated at the end of a pipe
Cuts waste and pollution at the source through process change or input substitution
Replaces environmental assessment with an operating-unit audit
Focuses exclusively on disposal of hazardous waste
77.x: Cleaner production is preventive: it reduces waste and pollution at source through measures such as process change and input substitution, rather than relying mainly on end-of-pipe treatment.
77.tq: Distinguish prevention at source from treatment after pollution is generated.
xs: Cleaner production **cuts waste and pollution at source** through **process change or input substitution** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is a **preventive** strategy, the opposite of **end-of-pipe treatment**.
xa: **APPCB's** mandate includes encouraging **cleaner production technologies**.
**Green chemistry** designs products/processes that reduce or eliminate hazardous substances.
Both shrink impacts **at design stage**.

77.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Great Nicobar project—High-Powered Committee on NGT directions
Sewage in drinking water—suo motu notice to Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh
Styrene leak—Maharashtra and West Bengal waste-management fines
77.x: The styrene leak concerned LG Polymers at Visakhapatnam and led to an interim deposit of Rs 50 crore. Maharashtra and West Bengal were associated with fines for waste mismanagement.
77.tq: Find the swapped incident-and-state pairing.
xs: **Styrene leak — Maharashtra and West Bengal fines** is wrongly matched — so option **(4)** is correct.
The styrene leak was **LG Polymers, Visakhapatnam** (May 2020) → **Rs 50 crore** interim deposit.
**Maharashtra and West Bengal (2022)** were fined for **waste mismanagement**.
xa: **Rat-hole mining — Meghalaya (2014)**; **Great Nicobar — High-Powered Committee** on NGT directions.
Sewage in drinking water: suo motu notice to **Rajasthan, MP, UP** (15 Jan 2026).
BRO: **10,000 trees** within one month (Aug 2023).

78.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Ministry of Environment and Forests formed
B. Department of Environment created
C. Ministry renamed MoEFCC
D. Air-pollution functions added to CPCB by the Air Act
Select the correct sequence.
78.x: The correct sequence is Department of Environment in 1980, Air Act in 1981, Ministry of Environment and Forests in 1985, and MoEFCC renaming in 2014.
78.tq: Place the dated institutional milestones from earliest to latest.
xs: The correct order is **B, D, A, C** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**B:** **Department of Environment** created in **1980**; **D:** air functions added to CPCB by the **Air Act 1981**.
**A:** **Ministry of Environment and Forests** formed in **1985**; **C:** renamed **MoEFCC** in **2014** when Climate Change was added.
xa: CPCB itself is older: constituted in **1974** under the **Water Act**, renamed **CPCB** by the **1988** amendment.
⚠ Trap order: **1974** CPCB → **1985** MoEF → **1988** CPCB renamed → **2014** MoEFCC.
**EPA 1986** widened CPCB's scope — it did not add the air functions.
The **1985** formation of the Ministry was an **APPSC 2024** statement marked correct.

78.s:
Consider the following statements about the Central Pollution Control Board:
1. It was constituted in 1974 under the Water Act as the Central Board for the Prevention and Control of Water Pollution.
2. It was renamed CPCB by a 1988 amendment.
3. Its air-pollution functions were added by the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
4. It is a statutory body under MoEFCC.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: air functions were added by the Air Act, 1981; EPA 1986 only widened its scope. So options including 3, and 1 and 2 only (missing 4), are wrong.
78.tq: CPCB: Water Act 1974 -> Air Act 1981 adds air -> renamed 1988 -> EPA 1986 widens scope.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 4** are correct — option **(2)**.
**Statement 1:** correct — constituted in **1974** under the **Water Act** as the Central Board for the Prevention and Control of Water Pollution.
**Statement 2:** correct — renamed **CPCB** by the **1988** amendment.
**Statement 3:** wrong — air functions came from the **Air Act 1981**; **EPA 1986** only widened its scope.
**Statement 4:** correct — CPCB is a **statutory body under MoEFCC**.
xa: CPCB has a **full-time chairman nominated by the Central Government**.
CPCB (**1974**) is the **oldest national pollution body**.
CPCB runs **NAMP** and the **National AQI** (launched **2015**, daily bulletins).
Air network: **516 cities**, **1,400+** stations with real-time CAAQMS.

78.s: Which body is primarily responsible for enforcing environmental standards under the Environment (Protection) Act framework?
78.x: The CPCB is the body responsible for enforcing environmental standards under the Environment (Protection) Act framework.
78.tq: Assign the enforcement function to the regulatory rather than adjudicatory body.
xs: The **Central Pollution Control Board** enforces environmental standards under the EPA framework — option **(3)**.
This was the **APPSC-G2 2025** answer.
The **NGT** only **adjudicates** disputes and awards compensation; the **NBA** deals with **biodiversity** access and biopiracy.
xa: CPCB is a **regulator**: sets standards, monitors pollution, advises the Centre.
Its scope was widened by **EPA 1986**; air functions came by the **Air Act 1981**.
CPCB coordinates the **NCAP** with SPCBs, tracked on the **PRANA** portal.
**Environmental (Protection) Fund Rules 2026** finance CPCB and SPCBs.

78.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board:
1. It enforces the Water Act, Air Act and Environment Protection Act.
2. It enforces rules relating to hazardous, biomedical, plastic and solid waste.
3. It issues siting guidelines and develops SOPs for marine outfalls and hazardous waste.
4. It promotes cleaner production.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: All four statements describe stated APPCB responsibilities, including enforcement, waste-management rules, siting guidance, SOPs and cleaner production.
78.tq: Test the full range of State Board responsibilities rather than only its core Acts.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Statements 1 and 2:** correct — APPCB enforces the **Water, Air, EP Acts** plus **Hazardous, Bio-medical, Plastic, Solid waste** rules.
**Statement 3:** correct — it issues **siting guidelines** and SOPs on **marine outfalls** and hazardous waste.
**Statement 4:** correct — it **promotes cleaner production**.
xa: APPCB was set up in **1976** by the **AP Government** under the **Water Act 1974**.
It is the body **entrusted to implement environmental laws and rules in AP** (**APPSC 2025** answer).
It runs **computerised inspection under EoDB**.
Like other SPCBs it grants **Consent to Establish** and **Consent to Operate**.

78.s: The Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board was established in 1976 under the authority of the:
o: Government of India under the Air Act, 1981
Government of Andhra Pradesh under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
National Green Tribunal under the Water Act, 1974
Government of Andhra Pradesh under the Water Act, 1974
78.x: The APPCB was established in 1976 by the Government of Andhra Pradesh under the Water Act, 1974.
78.tq: Combine the correct State authority, year and parent legislation.
xs: APPCB was set up in **1976** by the **Government of Andhra Pradesh** under the **Water Act, 1974** — option **(4)**.
It is a State body, so not set up by the **Government of India** or the **NGT** (which came only in **2010**).
The **Air Act 1981** and **EPA 1986** came after **1976**, so they could not be its basis.
xa: APPCB is **entrusted to implement environmental laws and rules in AP** (**APPSC 2025** answer).
It enforces **Water, Air, EP Acts** and the **Hazardous, Bio-medical, Plastic, Solid waste** rules.
It issues **siting guidelines** and SOPs on **marine outfalls** and hazardous waste.
CPCB too began under the **Water Act** in **1974**.

78.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the National Green Tribunal from the Central Pollution Control Board?
o: The NGT sets emission standards, whereas the CPCB awards compensation.
The CPCB hears appeals against NGT orders in environmental disputes.
The NGT adjudicates disputes and awards compensation, whereas the CPCB regulates, sets standards and monitors pollution.
Both bodies perform exactly the same adjudicatory and regulatory functions.
78.x: The NGT is an adjudicatory body that decides environmental disputes and awards compensation. The CPCB is a regulatory body that sets standards, monitors pollution and advises the Centre.
78.tq: Separate adjudication from regulation by asking who performs the job.
xs: The **NGT adjudicates disputes and awards compensation**, while the **CPCB regulates, sets standards and monitors** — option **(3)**.
Option (1) swaps the two roles; option (4) wrongly makes them identical.
Appeals from NGT go to the **Supreme Court** within **90 days**, not to the CPCB.
xa: CPCB also **advises the Centre**.
CPCB is a **statutory body under MoEFCC** (**1974**); NGT is a **statutory** tribunal (**2010**).
CPCB runs **NAMP**, **National AQI** and **RTWQMS**.
NGT is guided by **natural justice**, not bound by **CPC 1908**.

78.s: Which one of the following bodies replaced the Environment Pollution (Prevention and Control) Authority (EPCA) in the National Capital Region and adjoining areas?
78.x: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM), established under the CAQM Act, 2021, replaced EPCA in the NCR and adjoining areas.
78.tq: Use the replacement relationship and distinguish air-quality authority from water and biodiversity bodies.
xs: The **Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM)** replaced **EPCA** — option **(2)**.
CAQM is based on the **CAQM Act 2021** and covers **NCR and adjoining areas**.
**NMCG** implements Namami Gange; **CGWA** regulates groundwater; **NBA** handles biodiversity.
xa: **CGWA**: constituted **1997** under **S.3(3) EPA**.
NGT fined **12 stadiums ₹5,000 each** for not giving CGWA water-use data.
**NMCG** is the successor to **NGRBA** (**2009**).

78.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the oldest national pollution body and the institution that replaced the NEAA?
o: NGT, established in 1974; CPCB, established in 2010
CPCB, established in 1981; CAQM, established in 2010
CGWA, established in 1974; NMCG, established in 2010
CPCB, established in 1974; NGT, established in 2010
78.x: CPCB, established in 1974, is the oldest national pollution body. The NGT, established in 2010, replaced the National Environment Appellate Authority (NEAA).
78.tq: Pair the correct institution with its year and distinguish the pollution regulator from the appellate tribunal.
xs: **CPCB** (**1974**) is the oldest national pollution body and the **NGT** (**2010**) replaced the **NEAA** — option **(4)**.
CPCB was constituted in **1974** under the **Water Act**; **1981** is when the **Air Act** added its air functions.
**CGWA** dates from **1997** and **CAQM** from the CAQM Act **2021**; **NMCG** succeeded the **NGRBA**, not the NEAA.
xa: The NEAA (Act of **1997**) heard appeals against **environmental clearances**; its Act was **repealed in 2010**.
NGT = **original jurisdiction** + the NEAA's **appellate role**.
CPCB was **renamed** in **1988**; it started as the Central Board for the Prevention and Control of Water Pollution.
NGT dates: Act **2 June 2010** → set up **18 Oct 2010** → functioning **July 2011**.

78.s:
Consider the following pairs relating to CPCB monitoring:
1. NAMP — National Air Monitoring Programme
2. RTWQMS — Real-time water-quality monitoring on the Ganga and Yamuna
3. PRANA — Daily National AQI bulletins
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
78.x: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. Pair 3 is wrong: PRANA is the portal tracking NCAP; daily bulletins come from the National AQI launched in 2015. So 1 only is incomplete and options with 3 are wrong.
78.tq: NAMP = air, RTWQMS = Ganga/Yamuna water, PRANA = NCAP tracker.
xs: Pairs **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
**Pair 1:** correct — **NAMP** is the **National Air Monitoring Programme**.
**Pair 2:** correct — **RTWQMS** is real-time water-quality monitoring on the **Ganga and Yamuna**.
**Pair 3:** wrong — **PRANA** is the portal tracking **NCAP**; daily bulletins come from the **National AQI** (launched **2015**).
xa: CPCB air network: **516 cities**, **1,400+** stations; **CAAQMS** gives real-time data.
CPCB also runs **National Water Quality Monitoring**.
NGT told southern States and Puducherry to execute **NCAP** plans — **86%** of spend went on **road dust**.
CPCB coordinates **SPCBs** with technical help, research and training.

78.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional status and powers of the National Green Tribunal?
o: It is a statutory body with powers similar to those of a civil court.
It is a constitutional body with powers exclusively of an administrative authority.
It is an executive body exercising only advisory jurisdiction.
It is a constitutional body established under Article 323B without civil-court powers.
78.x: The NGT is a statutory, not constitutional, body and possesses civil-court powers in matters within its jurisdiction.
78.tq: Discriminate between constitutional, statutory and executive bodies before considering their powers.
xs: The NGT is a **statutory** body with **powers of a civil court** — option **(1)**.
It was set up under the **NGT Act, 2010**, so it is **not a constitutional body** — options (2) and (4) are wrong.
It **adjudicates** disputes and awards compensation, so it is not merely advisory.
xa: It is **not bound by CPC 1908**; it is guided by the **principles of natural justice**.
Cases are to be disposed of within **6 months**.
Appeal lies to the **Supreme Court** within **90 days**.
It gives effect to the right to a healthy environment under **Art. 21**.

78.s: The establishment of the National Green Tribunal gives effect, in the environmental context, to which Fundamental Right?
o: Right to constitutional remedies under Article 32
78.x: The NGT gives effect to the right to a healthy environment, which is treated as part of the right to life under Article 21.
78.tq: Match the environmental entitlement with the relevant Fundamental Right.
xs: The NGT gives effect to the right to a healthy environment under **Article 21** (**right to life**) — option **(1)**.
The notes link the NGT only to **Art. 21**, not to Articles 14, 23 or 32.
xa: NGT purpose: **effective and expeditious disposal** of cases on environmental protection and conservation of forests.
It also enforces **environmental legal rights** and gives **relief and compensation** for damage.
It was set up on **18 October 2010** — asked in **APPSC 2018**.
**APPSC-G2 2025**: purpose = to handle **environmental protection and pollution-control cases**.

78.s: An appeal against an order of the National Green Tribunal lies to the Supreme Court within:
78.x: An appeal against an NGT order may be filed before the Supreme Court within 90 days.
78.tq: Use the exact statutory time limit and compare the middle numerical options carefully.
xs: An appeal against an NGT order lies to the **Supreme Court** within **90 days** — option **(3)**.
The other periods (30, 60, 120 days) are not the NGT Act limit.
xa: The NGT must dispose of cases within **6 months**.
⚠ Sequence: Act **2 June 2010** → set up **18 Oct 2010** → functioning **July 2011**.
It is not bound by **CPC 1908**; follows **natural justice**.
It has **powers of a civil court**.

78.s:
With reference to the National Green Tribunal, consider the following statements:
1. Its Chairperson is a retired judge of the Supreme Court.
2. It is bound by all the procedures of the Code of Civil Procedure.
3. It follows the principles of natural justice.
4. It is required to decide cases within six months.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is false because the Tribunal is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure, though it follows natural justice.
78.tq: Split the options by checking the procedural exception concerning the CPC.
xs: Statements **1, 3 and 4** are correct — option **(3)**.
**Statement 1:** correct — the Chairperson is a **retired SC judge**.
**Statement 2:** wrong — the NGT is **not bound by CPC 1908**.
**Statement 3:** correct — it is guided by **principles of natural justice**; **Statement 4:** correct — disposal within **6 months**.
xa: The Act also allows a judge of the SC or **Chief Justice of a High Court** as Chairperson.
It has **powers of a civil court**.
Appeal: to the **Supreme Court** within **90 days**.
Members: **Judicial and Expert Members**, **10 to 20** each.

78.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Green Tribunal:
1. The NGT Act was passed on 2 June 2010.
2. The Tribunal was set up on 18 October 2010.
3. The Tribunal started functioning in July 2010.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
78.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Act was passed on 2 June 2010. Statement 2 is correct: the Tribunal was set up on 18 October 2010 (asked in APPSC 2018). Statement 3 is wrong: it started functioning in July 2011. So 1 only is incomplete and options with 3 are wrong.
78.tq: Act 2 June 2010 -> set up 18 Oct 2010 -> working July 2011.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
**Statement 1:** correct — the NGT Act was passed on **2 June 2010**.
**Statement 2:** correct — the Tribunal was set up on **18 October 2010**.
**Statement 3:** wrong — it started functioning in **July 2011**, not July 2010.
xa: **APPSC 2018** asked the date it was set up: **18 October 2010**.
It is a **statutory** body under the **NGT Act, 2010**, not constitutional.
Disposal within **6 months**; appeal to the SC within **90 days**.

78.s: The National Mission for Clean Ganga is the successor set-up to which body?
78.x: NMCG is the successor set-up to the National Ganga River Basin Authority (NGRBA), which was established in 2009 under the Environment (Protection) Act.
78.tq: Use the predecessor–successor relationship and distinguish river-basin institutions from pollution authorities.
xs: **NMCG** is the successor set-up to the **NGRBA** — option **(1)**.
NGRBA was set up in **2009** under the **EPA**; NMCG implements **Namami Gange**.
**CGWA** is a groundwater authority (**1997**), **EPCA** was replaced by **CAQM**, and **NBA** handles biodiversity.
xa: **NRCP** covers **38 rivers** in **16 states** outside the Ganga basin.
CPCB runs **RTWQMS** on the **Ganga and Yamuna**.
**Ganga pollution** was among NGT cases in **2026**.

78.s: The National Green Tribunal directed southern States and Puducherry to execute action plans under which programme?
78.x: The NGT directed southern States and Puducherry to execute action plans under the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP).
78.tq: Distinguish the air-quality programme from river-conservation and biodiversity programmes.
xs: The NGT told southern States and Puducherry to execute **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP)** action plans — option **(4)**.
**86%** of NCAP spend went on **road dust**.
**Namami Gange** and **NRCP** are river programmes; the **City Biodiversity Index** is an APSBB initiative.
xa: CPCB coordinates NCAP with SPCBs; progress tracked on the **PRANA** portal.
**Environmental (Protection) Fund Rules 2026** finance CPCB/SPCBs.
**Guntur** was **2nd** in the towns category of **Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan 2026**.

78.s:
How many of the following are associated with the National Green Tribunal?
I. Environmental matters
II. Forests
III. Natural resources
IV. A constitutional connection with Article 21
V. The concept of the right to a healthy environment
78.x: All five are linked with the NGT: environmental matters, forests and natural resources, a basis in Article 21, and the right to a healthy environment.
78.tq: Recall the NGT's scope.
n: The National Green Tribunal covers environmental matters. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 10-12]
The National Green Tribunal covers forests. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 10-12]
The National Green Tribunal covers natural resources. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 10-12]
The National Green Tribunal has a constitutional connection with Article 21. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 10-12]
