CPCB **coordinates the SPCBs** with technical help, research and training.

79.s: The Ramsar Convention was adopted in 1971 at
79.x: The Ramsar Convention was adopted in 1971 at Ramsar in Iran.
79.tq: Identify the treaty by its adoption place and year.
xs: The Ramsar Convention was adopted in **1971** at **Ramsar, Iran** — option **(3)**.
**Gland, Switzerland** is its **Secretariat**, not the place of adoption; **Montreal** hosts the **CBD** Secretariat and **Bonn** the **UNCCD**.
xa: India has been a Party since **1982**; first Indian site **Chilika (1981)**.
Three pillars: designate **wetlands of international importance**, **wise use** of all wetlands, **international cooperation**.
**World Wetlands Day** = **2 February**, the Ramsar adoption day.
Ramsar (**1971**) is **older than the Stockholm Conference** (**1972**).

79.s: The Secretariat of the Ramsar Convention is located at
79.x: The Ramsar Convention Secretariat is located at Gland, Switzerland.
79.tq: Distinguish the treaty Secretariat’s location from other environment bodies’ headquarters.
xs: The Ramsar Secretariat is at **Gland, Switzerland** — option **(4)**.
**Geneva** hosts the **CITES** Secretariat; **Bonn** the **UNCCD**; **Paris** the **World Heritage Convention**.
xa: Adopted **1971** at **Ramsar, Iran**.
**Montreux Record** (threatened sites): **Keoladeo NP** and **Loktak Lake**.
India has **101** Ramsar sites, the most in Asia; latest **Glaw Lake (Arunachal Pradesh)**, **3 Aug 2026**.

79.s: The United Nations Conference on the Human Environment, 1972, was held at:
79.x: The UN Conference on the Human Environment was held in Stockholm, Sweden, from 5 to 16 June 1972.
79.tq: Use the official conference name to distinguish Stockholm 1972 from UNCED 1992.
xs: The **UN Conference on the Human Environment** was held at **Stockholm, Sweden** (**5-16 June 1972**) — option **(2)**.
**Nairobi** is UNEP's HQ; **Rio de Janeiro** hosted the **1992 Earth Summit**; **Montreal** is the CBD Secretariat.
xa: It was the **APPSC 2025** answer.
Outcome: **Stockholm Declaration** (**26** principles) + Action Plan.
**UNEP** set up in **1972**; **5 June** became World Environment Day.
PM **Indira Gandhi** was the **only visiting head of government**.

79.s: The headquarters of the United Nations Environment Programme, established in 1972, is located at:
79.x: UNEP was established in 1972 and its headquarters is in Nairobi, Kenya.
79.tq: Distinguish UNEP’s headquarters from the venue of the Stockholm Conference and the CBD Secretariat.
xs: UNEP's headquarters is **Nairobi** — option **(1)**.
**Stockholm** hosted the **1972** conference that created it; **Rio** hosted the **1992** Earth Summit; **Montreal** is the CBD Secretariat.
xa: ⚠ **UNEP** (Stockholm **1972**) and **UNEA** (Rio+20, **2012**) are both in **Nairobi**.
UNEA has universal membership (**193**) and meets **biennially**.
The **Ozone Secretariat** (Montreal Protocol) is also in **Nairobi**.
The **CITES** Secretariat at **Geneva** is administered by **UNEP**.

79.s: Which one of the following comparisons between the Stockholm Conference and the Rio Earth Summit is correct?
o: Stockholm established the CBD, whereas Rio established the UNEP in 1972.
Stockholm 1972 concerned the human environment, whereas Rio 1992 concerned environment and development.
Stockholm 1992 concerned biodiversity, whereas Rio 1972 concerned human rights.
Both were held in Rio de Janeiro and produced the same declaration.
79.x: The 1972 Stockholm Conference was the UN Conference on the Human Environment, while the 1992 Rio Summit was UNCED, focused on environment and development.
79.tq: Compare the official names and years before comparing their institutional outcomes.
xs: **Stockholm 1972** was on the **Human Environment**; **Rio 1992** (**UNCED**) was on **Environment and Development** — option **(2)**.
Stockholm created **UNEP**; the **CBD** opened for signature at **Rio** — option (1) swaps them.
The two were held in different cities with different outputs (**Stockholm Declaration** vs **Agenda 21**).
xa: Rio **1992** was the **first international Earth Summit**.
Rio outputs: **Agenda 21**, **Forest Principles**, **UNFCCC** and **CBD** opened for signature.
**UNCCD** (**1994**) completes the three **Rio Conventions**.

79.s:
Consider the following statements regarding CITES:
1. It was adopted on 3 March 1973 at Washington, D.C.
2. It entered into force on 1 July 1975.
3. Its Secretariat is located in Geneva and is administered by UNEP.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
79.x: CITES was adopted on 3 March 1973, entered into force on 1 July 1975, and has a UNEP-administered Secretariat in Geneva.
79.tq: Combine date, commencement and institutional-location facts in a coded statement question.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Statement 1:** adopted **3 March 1973**, **Washington D.C.**
**Statement 2:** in force **1 July 1975**.
**Statement 3:** Secretariat in **Geneva**, administered by **UNEP**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes say "**1963**" — wrong; **1973** is correct.
Other name: **Washington Convention**.
**184 Parties**; about **35,000 species** covered.
**World Wildlife Day = 3 March**, the day CITES was signed.

79.s: Which one of the following international agreements is also known as the 'Washington Convention', and whose signing date is observed as World Wildlife Day (3 March)?
79.x: CITES was signed at Washington D.C. on 3 March 1973, hence 'Washington Convention', and 3 March is World Wildlife Day. CMS is the Bonn Convention, Ramsar is tied to World Wetlands Day (2 February), and CBD to the International Day for Biological Diversity (22 May).
79.tq: Washington = CITES, 3 March 1973 (not 1963); Bonn = CMS.
xs: **CITES** is the **Washington Convention**, signed **3 March 1973** — now **World Wildlife Day** — option **(3)**.
**CMS** is the **Bonn Convention**; **Ramsar** marks **2 February**; **CBD** marks **22 May**.
xa: World Wildlife Day was proclaimed by UNGA in **2013**.
**APPSC G2 2025** key: Washington Convention = CITES.
⚠ **Bonn** = CMS (migratory species); **Washington** = CITES (trade).
**5 June** (World Environment Day) marks the Stockholm opening.

79.s: Which one of the following species is correctly matched with CITES Appendix I?
79.x: The Indian star tortoise is listed in Appendix I; it was uplisted on India’s proposal at CoP18 in 2019. Red sanders, golden gecko and rosewood are listed in Appendix II.
79.tq: Use species-level discrimination among Indian taxa listed in different appendices.
xs: The **Indian star tortoise** is in **Appendix I** — option **(4)**; uplisted on India's proposal at **CoP18, 2019**.
**Golden gecko**, **red sanders** and **rosewood** are all **Appendix II**.
xa: Other Appendix I species: **tiger**, **clouded leopard**, **Indian and Chinese pangolins**.
**Striped hyena** — Appendix II.
The golden gecko is an **AP endemic**.

79.s: Which of the following groups of species was added to CMS Appendix I at CMS COP-13 hosted by India?
o: Blue whale, dugong and olive ridley turtle
Ganges dolphin, snow leopard and blackbuck
Great Indian Bustard, Asian elephant and Bengal florican
Tiger, Asiatic lion and one-horned rhinoceros
79.x: The Great Indian Bustard, Asian elephant and Bengal florican were added to CMS Appendix I at COP-13.
79.tq: Recall the exact species group attached to a conference decision.
xs: **Great Indian Bustard, Asian elephant and Bengal florican** were added to CMS **Appendix I** at **COP-13** — option **(3)**.
The notes list no other species for COP-13.
xa: COP-13: **Gandhinagar, Feb 2020**.
CMS Appendix I = **endangered** migratory species under **strict protection**.
CMS = **Bonn Convention**, **1979**.

79.s: Which one of the following pairs of instruments was opened for signature at the Rio Earth Summit, 1992?
79.x: The United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change and the Convention on Biological Diversity were opened for signature at Rio in 1992.
79.tq: Start with the sure pair of agreements associated with the Rio Summit itself.
xs: The **UNFCCC** and **CBD** were opened for signature at **Rio 1992** — option **(1)**.
**UNCCD** came in **1994**; **Ramsar** is of **1971**; **CITES** is of **1973**; **Cartagena** (**2000**) and **Nagoya** (**2010**) are later CBD protocols.
xa: With the **UNCCD**, they form the three **Rio Conventions**.
Rio = **UNCED**, the **first international Earth Summit**.
Other Rio outputs: **Agenda 21**, **Forest Principles**.

79.s: Rio+5, held in 1997, primarily involved which of the following?
o: A special session of the UN General Assembly reviewing Agenda 21
Establishment of the UNEA at Nairobi
79.x: Rio+5 was a special session of the United Nations General Assembly held in New York in 1997 to review the implementation of Agenda 21.
79.tq: Match the review conference with its specific institutional setting and subject.
xs: **Rio+5** (**1997**) was a **UN General Assembly special session** in New York that **reviewed Agenda 21** — option **(1)**.
**KMGBF** came in **2022**; **UNEA** came from **Rio+20** (**2012**).
xa: **Rio+10** = **Johannesburg WSSD 2002**.
**Rio+20 (UNCSD)** produced "**The Future We Want**" and launched the SDG process.
**Agenda 21** = action plan for sustainable development at all levels.

79.s: Which of the following was an output of the Rio+20 Conference held in 2012?
o: The Montreal Protocol and Kyoto Protocol
Stockholm Declaration and creation of UNEP
The Future We Want and initiation of the SDG process
79.x: Rio+20, held in Rio de Janeiro in 2012, produced “The Future We Want”, launched the Sustainable Development Goal process and was associated with the High-Level Political Forum.
79.tq: Use the conference title and year to identify its characteristic outcome document.
xs: **Rio+20** (**2012**) produced "**The Future We Want**" and launched the **SDG process** — option **(4)**.
**Agenda 21** and **Forest Principles** were from **Rio 1992**; **Stockholm Declaration** and **UNEP** from **1972**; Montreal Protocol is **1987**.
xa: Rio+20 is also called **UNCSD**.
It set up **UNEA** (universal membership, **193**).
⚠ UNEA and UNEP are both in **Nairobi**.

79.s: Agenda 21, an action plan for sustainable development at all levels, was an outcome of:
o: The UN Conference on Environment and Development, 1992
The World Summit on Sustainable Development, 2002
The UN Conference on Sustainable Development, 2012
79.x: Agenda 21 came from UNCED, the 1992 Rio Earth Summit, the first international Earth Summit. Stockholm 1972 produced the Stockholm Declaration and UNEP, WSSD 2002 the Johannesburg Plan of Implementation, and Rio+20 'The Future We Want'.
79.tq: Agenda 21 / Rio Declaration = Earth Summit 1992.
xs: **Agenda 21** came from **UNCED** — the **UN Conference on Environment and Development** (**1992**), the Rio Earth Summit — option **(2)**.
**Stockholm 1972** gave the **Stockholm Declaration** and **UNEP**; **Rio+20** (**2012**) gave "**The Future We Want**".
xa: Rio **1992** = the **first international Earth Summit** (**APPSC 2025**).
Agenda 21 was an **APPSC-G2 2025** answer.
**Rio+5** (**1997**) reviewed Agenda 21.

79.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Forest Principles adopted at Rio in 1992 are a legally binding convention on forests.
2. The UNCCD, adopted in 1994 as a follow-up to Rio, forms the three 'Rio Conventions' along with the UNFCCC and CBD.
3. Rio+10 was the World Summit on Sustainable Development held at Johannesburg in 2002.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
79.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the Forest Principles were a non-binding statement. Statement 2 is correct: UNCCD (1994) joins UNFCCC and CBD as the Rio Conventions. Statement 3 is correct: Rio+10 was the Johannesburg WSSD, 2002. Hence '2 and 3 only'.
79.tq: Forest Principles = non-binding; Rio Conventions = UNFCCC, CBD, UNCCD.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
**Statement 1:** wrong — the **Forest Principles** were a **non-binding** statement.
**Statement 2:** correct — **UNCCD** (**1994**) + **UNFCCC** + **CBD** = the **Rio Conventions**.
**Statement 3:** correct — **Rio+10** was the **Johannesburg WSSD 2002**.
xa: The Rio Conventions are meant to work together on **climate, biodiversity and land**.
**UNCCD** Secretariat: **Bonn**; India hosted COP-14 (**2019**).
**UNCCD COP-17**: **Mongolia**, theme "**Restoring Land. Restoring Hope**".

79.s:
Consider the following statements about the Convention on Biological Diversity:
1. It was opened for signature at the Rio Earth Summit in 1992.
2. It entered into force in 1993.
3. Its Secretariat is located in Montreal, Canada.
4. India ratified it in 1994.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
79.x: All four statements are correct. The CBD was opened at Rio in 1992, entered into force in 1993, has its Secretariat in Montreal and was ratified by India in 1994.
79.tq: Check treaty facts in the order of adoption, entry into force, headquarters and national ratification.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Opened at **Rio 1992** (legally binding); in force **1993**.
Secretariat at **Montreal, Canada**; India ratified in **1994**.
xa: First COP: **Nassau, Bahamas, 1994**; COPs every **two years**.
India hosted **COP11** at **Hyderabad, 2012**.
**22 May** (International Day for Biological Diversity) marks CBD text adoption on **22 May 1992**.

79.s: The Global Biodiversity Framework Fund is set up under the:
o: International Union for Conservation of Nature
Convention on Biological Diversity Secretariat alone
79.x: The Global Biodiversity Framework Fund is set up under the Global Environment Facility.
79.tq: Apply the institutional-authority test to identify the responsible financial mechanism.
xs: The **GBF Fund** is set up under the **Global Environment Facility (GEF)** — option **(3)**.
The GEF is also the **financial mechanism** of the **CBD** and **UNFCCC**.
xa: ⚠ **US$200 billion a year** (Target 19) is the overall target, **not** the Fund's size.
**COP16** created the **Cali Fund** on DSI.
IUCN is a union of governments and NGOs, **not a UN organ**.

79.s: Which one of the following statements regarding WDPA is correct?
o: It is updated every four years by the CBD Secretariat and tracks Target 19.
It records only terrestrial protected areas and excludes oceans.
It is updated monthly by UNEP-WCMC with IUCN and tracks Target 3.
It is maintained by the GBF Fund and tracks Target 2 only.
79.x: WDPA is updated monthly by UNEP-WCMC with IUCN and is used to track Target 3. It covers protected areas relevant to both terrestrial and marine conservation.
79.tq: Combine the database, updating frequency, institutional association and target.
xs: **WDPA** is run by **UNEP-WCMC with IUCN**, **updated monthly**, and tracks **Target 3** — option **(3)**.
It covers oceans too: ~**10%** of oceans protected, only **1.66%** of high seas.
xa: **UNEP-WCMC** also keeps the **CITES Trade Database**.
The **BBNJ** (High Seas Treaty) entered into force on **17 January 2026**.

79.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
79.x: The UNCCD was adopted in 1994 and its Secretariat is at Bonn. The World Heritage Secretariat is in Paris, the IWC headquarters is in Cambridge, and the Basel Secretariat is in Geneva.
79.tq: Start with the complete treaty-year-secretariat combination and reject location swaps.
xs: **UNCCD — 1994 — Bonn** is correct — option **(1)**.
**World Heritage** Secretariat is **Paris** (not Geneva); **IWC** is at **Cambridge, UK** (not Paris); **Basel** is at **Geneva** (not Rome).
xa: India hosted UNCCD **COP-14** (**2019**).
**UNCCD COP-17**: **Mongolia**, **197** parties.
**Rotterdam** Secretariat: **Geneva/Rome**.

79.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Convention on Migratory Species is also known as the Bonn Convention.
2. It deals with the conservation of migratory species.
3. It is a binding treaty under UNEP.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
79.x: All three statements are correct. CMS is also called the Bonn Convention, focuses on migratory species and is a binding treaty under UNEP.
79.tq: Use the coded combination to verify the name, mandate and legal status together.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**1:** CMS = **Bonn Convention**; **2:** conserves **migratory species** (PYQ **2019**).
**3:** it is a **binding treaty under UNEP**.
xa: CMS dates from **1979**; India a Party since **1983**.
**CMS COP-13**: **Gandhinagar, Feb 2020**.
⚠ **Bonn** = CMS; **Washington** = CITES.

79.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: TRAFFIC — Wildlife trade should not threaten conservation
IUCN — Enforcement of CITES through customs inspections
CITES — Regulation of international wildlife trade
79.x: IUCN is associated with the Red List and field projects. Customs inspections for CITES consignments are assisted by the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau, while TRAFFIC is an NGO network concerned with wildlife trade.
79.tq: Find the mismatched mandate rather than selecting the most familiar organisation.
xs: **IUCN — CITES enforcement via customs** is wrongly matched — option **(3)**; customs help is the **WCCB**'s job.
The others are right: **CMS** — migratory species; **TRAFFIC** — trade not a threat to conservation; **CITES** — wildlife trade.
xa: IUCN keeps the **Red List** and runs field projects.
WCCB: set up **2007**, HQ **New Delhi**.
IUCN is **not a UN organ**.

79.s: Which one of the following correctly expresses the chronological relationship among the Ramsar Convention, the Stockholm Conference and the Rio Earth Summit?
o: Ramsar Convention precedes the Stockholm Conference, which precedes the Rio Earth Summit
Stockholm Conference precedes the Ramsar Convention, which precedes the Rio Earth Summit
Rio Earth Summit precedes the Ramsar Convention, which precedes the Stockholm Conference
Ramsar Convention and Rio Earth Summit both precede the Stockholm Conference
79.x: The Ramsar Convention dates from 1971, the Stockholm Conference from 1972 and the Rio Earth Summit from 1992.
79.tq: Use first-and-last dates to establish the sequence before checking the middle event.
xs: Ramsar is **older than the Stockholm Conference**.
xa: Rio **1992** = **first Earth Summit**.
Stockholm created **UNEP**; Rio gave **Agenda 21**.
**CITES** came in **1973**, just after Stockholm.

79.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Global Environment Facility (GEF) is incorrect?
o: The pilot GEF was agreed in 1990.
The GEF was established around the Rio Earth Summit.
Its initial implementing partners were UNDP, UNEP and the CBD.
Its initial implementing partners were UNDP, UNEP and the World Bank.
79.x: Option C is incorrect: the GEF's first implementing partners were UNDP, UNEP and the World Bank. The CBD is a convention it funds.
79.tq: Discriminate GEF partners from GEF-funded conventions.
n: The pilot Global Environment Facility (GEF) was agreed in 1990. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-10]
The Global Environment Facility was established around the Rio Earth Summit. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-10]
The initial implementing partners of the Global Environment Facility included the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-10]
The initial implementing partners of the Global Environment Facility included the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP). [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-10]
The initial implementing partners of the Global Environment Facility included the World Bank. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-10]
xs: The **incorrect** statement is that the GEF's partners included the **CBD** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The GEF's **initial implementing partners** were **UNDP**, **UNEP** and the **World Bank**.
The **pilot** GEF was **agreed** in **1990** and **established** around the **Rio Earth Summit**.
xa: The GEF is the **financial mechanism** for the **CBD**, **UNFCCC**, **UNCCD**, **Minamata** and **Stockholm** Conventions.
**India** is both a **donor** and a **recipient**.
The **UNFCCC** was adopted at Rio (**1992**) and came into **force** on **21 March 1994**.

79.s:
With reference to CITES, consider the following statements:
1. Appendix II includes species that are not yet threatened with extinction but whose trade is controlled through permits.
2. Appendix III includes species listed by one Party seeking the assistance of other Parties to control trade.
3. Appendix I consists of species for which commercial trade is permitted without restrictions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
79.x: Appendix II covers species whose trade requires control and permits, while Appendix III covers species listed by one Party for international assistance. Appendix I generally prohibits commercial trade.
79.tq: Find the false statement by checking the reversed trade rule.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
**Statement 1:** correct — **Appendix II** = not yet threatened, trade **controlled by permits** (export permit).
**Statement 2:** correct — **Appendix III** = listed by **one Party** seeking others' help to control trade.
**Statement 3:** wrong — **Appendix I** commercial trade is **prohibited**.
xa: Appendix I examples: **tiger, snow leopard, rhino**.
Appendix II examples: **corals, many sharks and rays**.
Appendix III example: **walrus** (**Canada**).
Species move between Appendices only by **COP vote**.

79.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Appendix I — Corals and many sharks and rays
Appendix III — Walrus protected by Canada
Appendix I — Trade allowed merely with a certificate of origin
79.x: The walrus is an example associated with Appendix III, where Canada’s protection and request for cooperation are relevant. Tigers and rhinoceroses are Appendix I species, while corals and many sharks and rays are generally in Appendix II.
79.tq: Start from the sure species-example pair and reject the reversed appendix descriptions.
xs: **Appendix III — Walrus (Canada)** is correctly matched — option **(3)**.
**Corals and many sharks and rays** are **Appendix II**, not I.
**Tiger and rhino** are **Appendix I**, not II.
A **certificate of origin** belongs to **Appendix III** trade, not Appendix I.
xa: Appendix III = protected in **at least one country** that asks others for help.
Appendix I = **threatened with extinction**; commercial trade prohibited.
**54 shark and ray species** were moved to App II at **CoP19** (Panama, **2022**).

79.s: Which one of the following statements regarding sharks and rays under CITES is correct?
o: Most are in Appendix II; 54 were added at CoP19, while whale shark, oceanic whitetip and manta rays moved to Appendix I at CoP20.
They were all placed in Appendix III at CoP3.
Most are excluded from CITES regulation because they are marine species.
All sharks and rays are listed in Appendix I.
79.x: Most sharks and rays are listed in Appendix II. Fifty-four were added at CoP19, while the whale shark, oceanic whitetip and manta rays were listed in Appendix I at CoP20.
79.tq: Track the change across conferences and distinguish the majority category from specific exceptions.
xs: Sharks and rays: **mostly Appendix II**; **54** added at **CoP19**; **whale shark, oceanic whitetip, manta rays → I** at **CoP20** — option **(1)**.
They are clearly regulated, not all in Appendix I or III.
xa: CoP19: **Panama, 2022**; rosewood and **sea cucumbers** also protected.
CoP20: **Samarkand, Uzbekistan**, **2025** — **77 species** added.
**Wedgefish** is among India's CITES proposals.

79.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its CITES Appendix?
79.x: Indian and Chinese pangolins are in Appendix I. The striped hyena is in Appendix II, rosewood (Dalbergia) is in Appendix II, and the AP-endemic golden gecko is in Appendix II, not III.
79.tq: App I Indian species: tiger, clouded leopard, pangolins, star tortoise.
xs: **Indian pangolin — Appendix I** is correct — option **(2)**.
**Striped hyena** and **rosewood (Dalbergia)** are **Appendix II**, not I.
The **golden gecko** is **Appendix II**, not III.
xa: Over **500,000** pangolins were seized globally **2016-2024**.
**Chinese pangolin** is also in Appendix I.
**Clouded leopard** and **tiger** — Appendix I.

79.s: Red sanders, scientifically known as Pterocarpus santalinus, is
o: endemic to the Seshachalam and southern Eastern Ghats and listed as Endangered by IUCN
native only to the Western Ghats and listed as Vulnerable by IUCN
an invasive alien species of the Eastern Himalaya
a Himalayan species listed as Critically Endangered by CITES
79.x: Pterocarpus santalinus is endemic to the Seshachalam and southern Eastern Ghats and is classified as Endangered by IUCN.
79.tq: Combine scientific name, geographic range and conservation status in one precise identification.
xs: **Red sanders** (Pterocarpus santalinus) is **endemic to the Seshachalam and southern Eastern Ghats** and **IUCN Endangered** — option **(1)**.
It is not Western Ghats, Himalayan or invasive; CITES lists it in **Appendix II**, not as "Critically Endangered".
xa: Smuggled for demand in **China and Japan**.
AP's **Red Sanders Protection Area** = **5,300.97 sq km** across **7 districts**.
It gives **45% (Rs 120 crore)** of India's ABS income — the single largest ABS earner.

79.s:
With reference to the Convention on Migratory Species (Bonn Convention), consider the following statements:
1. Appendix II lists migratory species whose international trade is allowed only with an export permit.
2. Appendix I lists endangered migratory species that receive strict protection.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
79.x: Statement 2 is correct: CMS Appendix I lists endangered migratory species under strict protection. Statement 1 is wrong: CMS Appendix II lists species that need international cooperation agreements; trade with an export permit describes CITES Appendix II. Hence 2 only.
79.tq: CMS = migratory species (Bonn); CITES = trade (Washington). Do not mix their appendices.
xs: Only statement **2** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 2 is correct: **CMS Appendix I** lists **endangered migratory species** under **strict protection**.
Statement 1 is wrong: **CMS Appendix II** lists species **needing international cooperation agreements**; trade with an **export permit** is **CITES Appendix II**.
xa: India has been a **CMS** Party since **1983**.
**CMS COP-13**, **Gandhinagar, Feb 2020**: **Great Indian Bustard**, Asian elephant, Bengal florican added to Appendix I.
⚠ **Bonn Convention** = CMS (migratory species); **Washington Convention** = CITES (trade).

79.s:
Match List-I (KMGBF 2050 goal) with List-II (aim):
List-I
A. Goal A
B. Goal B
C. Goal C
D. Goal D
List-II
i. Sustainable use of biodiversity
ii. Adequate finance and technology, closing the US$700 billion a year finance gap
iii. Cut the extinction rate and risk of all species tenfold and halt human-induced extinction
iv. Fair sharing of benefits from genetic resources
Select the correct answer:
79.x: Goal A is the tenfold cut in extinction (iii), Goal B sustainable use (i), Goal C fair benefit-sharing from genetic resources (iv), Goal D finance and technology closing the US$700 bn gap (ii). Option B swaps B and C; option C swaps A and D; option D mismatches all four.
79.tq: A = extinction, B = use, C = benefit-sharing, D = finance (US$700 bn gap).
xs: Correct match: **A-iii, B-i, C-iv, D-ii** — option **(1)**.
**Goal A**: cut extinction rate and risk **tenfold**; halt human-induced extinction.
**Goal B**: **sustainable use**; **Goal C**: **fair sharing of benefits** from genetic resources.
**Goal D**: adequate **finance and technology**; close the **US$700 billion a year** gap.
xa: KMGBF: **4 goals** for **2050**, **23 targets** for **2030**.
⚠ **US$200 billion** = mobilise (Target 19); **US$500 billion** = cut subsidies (Target 18); **US$700 billion** = gap (Goal D).
Adopted at **COP15, Montreal, December 2022**.

79.s: With reference to the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), which one of the following is correct?
o: It is a specialised organ of the United Nations.
It is a treaty exclusively regulating wildlife trade.
It is a bureau of UNEP responsible for wildlife crime enforcement.
It is a union of governments and NGOs that maintains the Red List and runs field projects.
79.x: IUCN is a union of governments and non-governmental organisations. It maintains the Red List or Red Data Book and runs thousands of field projects; it is not a UN organ.
79.tq: Apply the organisation-versus-UN-body distinction to eliminate the wrong institutional descriptions.
xs: **IUCN** is a **union of governments and NGOs** that keeps the **Red List/Red Data Book** and runs field projects — option **(4)**.
It is **not a UN organ** (UPSC **2015** key), not a trade treaty (**CITES**), and not an enforcement bureau.
xa: IUCN dates from **1948**.
**TRAFFIC** is a joint programme of **WWF and IUCN**.
**WDPA** is kept by **UNEP-WCMC with IUCN**.

79.s: Which of the following was among the first Indian sites designated under the Ramsar Convention?
79.x: Chilika Lake, along with Keoladeo National Park, was among the first Indian Ramsar sites, designated on 1 October 1981.
79.tq: Use first-in-sequence recall for national treaty-site facts.
xs: **Chilika (1981)** is India's **first Ramsar site** — option **(1)**.
**Loktak Lake** is on the **Montreux Record**; **Kolleru** (AP) was designated in **2002**.
xa: ⚠ Chilika was later **removed from the Montreux Record** after restoration.
India became a Party in **1982**.
India had only **26** sites till **2013**; **68** added after **2014**; now **101**.
Domestic law: **Wetlands Rules 2017**.

79.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the Ramsar Convention?
o: Udaipur and Indore — India's first accredited Wetland Cities
Chilika and Kolleru — Wetland Cities accredited in 2025
Keoladeo and Loktak — first accredited Wetland Cities
Gland and Ramsar — Indian Wetland Cities
79.x: Udaipur and Indore became India's first accredited Wetland Cities in January 2025.
79.tq: Match the designation with the correct sites rather than the better-known Ramsar locations.
xs: **Udaipur and Indore** are India's **first accredited Wetland Cities** (**Jan 2025**) — option **(1)**.
**Chilika** and **Kolleru** are Ramsar sites, **Keoladeo and Loktak** are on the **Montreux Record**, and **Gland/Ramsar** are the Secretariat and adoption places — none is a Wetland City.
xa: At **CoP-15** (**30 Jul 2025**) India's resolution on **sustainable lifestyles for wise use of wetlands** was adopted.
**Amrit Dharohar** strategy: **Jun 2023**.
India's count: **101** Ramsar sites.

79.s: Which of the following Indian wetlands are currently on the Montreux Record of the Ramsar Convention?
o: Keoladeo National Park and Loktak Lake
Keoladeo National Park and Wular Lake
79.x: The Montreux Record lists Ramsar sites under threat; India's sites on it are Keoladeo NP and Loktak Lake. Chilika was on it but was removed after restoration, so options with Chilika are wrong; Kolleru and Wular are not on the Record.
79.tq: Montreux = threatened list: Keoladeo + Loktak; Chilika removed.
xs: India's Montreux Record sites are **Keoladeo NP** and **Loktak Lake** — option **(2)**.
**Chilika** was removed after restoration, so options with Chilika are wrong.
The notes do not place **Kolleru** or **Wular** on the Record.
xa: ⚠ **Chilika** = first Indian site (**1981**) and removed from the Record.
The Montreux Record lists **threatened** Ramsar sites.
India: Party since **1982**; **101** sites.

79.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India and the Ramsar Convention:
1. India has been a Party to the Convention since 1982.
2. India has 101 Ramsar sites, the most in Asia.
3. The obligation of 'wise use' applies only to wetlands designated as Ramsar sites.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
79.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: India joined in 1982 and now has 101 sites, the most in Asia. Statement 3 is wrong: the wise-use pillar covers all wetlands, not only designated sites. So the options containing 3 are wrong.
79.tq: Three pillars: designate sites, wise use of ALL wetlands, international cooperation.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
**Statement 1:** correct — India is a Party since **1982**.
**Statement 2:** correct — **101** Ramsar sites, the **most in Asia**.
**Statement 3:** wrong — the **wise use** pillar covers **all wetlands**, not just designated sites.
xa: Three pillars: designate sites, **wise use**, **international cooperation**.
Earlier counts: **96** (IYB 2026), **98** (Apr 2026).
Only **26** sites till **2013**; **68** added after **2014**.

79.s: The decisions of the Stockholm Conference in India were implemented through the:
79.x: The Stockholm decisions were implemented in India through the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
79.tq: Match the international conference outcome with the specific Indian legal instrument.
xs: Stockholm decisions were implemented in India through the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986** — option **(3)**.
The notes link Stockholm to the **EPA 1986** only; the **Wildlife Act 1972** implements **CITES**, and the **BD Act 2002** implements the **CBD/Nagoya**.
xa: Stockholm: **UN Conference on the Human Environment**, **5-16 June 1972**.
It produced the **Stockholm Declaration** (**26** principles) and **UNEP**.
PM **Indira Gandhi** linked **poverty and environment** there.

79.s: Which one of the following statements about the movement of species between CITES Appendices is correct?
o: It is automatically made every five years by UNEP.
It occurs only through a vote of the Conference of the Parties.
It is decided exclusively by IUCN’s Red List Committee.
It may be done by any national wildlife authority without international approval.
79.x: Species move between CITES Appendices only through a vote of the Conference of the Parties.
79.tq: Identify the competent authority rather than the advisory or domestic body.
xs: Species move between CITES Appendices **only by COP vote** — option **(2)**.
The notes give this power to the **COP** alone — not UNEP, IUCN or national authorities.
xa: The COP meets **every 2-3 years**.
Example: **whale shark, oceanic whitetip, manta rays → I** at **CoP20** (2025).
**Indian star tortoise** uplisted to I on India's proposal at **CoP18, 2019**.

79.s: The principal Indian legislation implementing CITES is the
79.x: CITES is implemented in India through the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
79.tq: Identify the domestic implementing law instead of the related environmental statutes.
xs: CITES is implemented in India through the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972** — option **(1)**.
The **BD Act 2002** implements the **CBD/Nagoya**; **EPA 1986** implemented **Stockholm**.
xa: The **2022 amendment** added a **CITES chapter** and **Schedule IV** for CITES-listed specimens.
India became a Party to CITES in **1976**.
**WCCB** was set up in **2007** under the WPA (**2006** amendment).

79.s: In which year did India become a Party to CITES?
79.x: India became a Party to CITES in 1976. 1973 is the year CITES was adopted, 1975 the year it entered into force, and 1982 the year India joined the Ramsar Convention.
79.tq: CITES: adopted 1973, in force 1975, India 1976.
xs: India became a Party to CITES in **1976** — option **(3)** (PYQ **2018**).
**1973** = adoption; **1975** = entry into force; **1982** = India joined **Ramsar**.
xa: Implementing law: **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**.
India hosted **CoP3** (New Delhi, **1981**) — its only CITES COP.
India joined **CMS** in **1983**.

79.s: The Conference of the Parties to CITES ordinarily meets
79.x: The CITES COP meets every two to three years.
79.tq: Discriminate between the recurring conference interval and the fixed schedules of other environmental bodies.
xs: The CITES COP meets **every 2-3 years** — option **(3)**.
The notes give no yearly, five-yearly or UNEP-called schedule.
xa: Species move between Appendices only by **COP vote**.
⚠ **CBD** COPs meet **every two years**.

79.s: Which one of the following statements regarding CITES CoP3 is correct?
o: It was held in Panama in 2022 and added 54 sharks and rays to Appendix II.
It was held in Samarkand in 2025 and marked 50 years of CITES.
It was held in New Delhi in 1981 and remains the only CITES COP hosted by India.
It was held in New Delhi in 2019 and uplisted the Indian star tortoise.
79.x: CoP3 was held in New Delhi in 1981 and is the only CITES COP hosted by India.
79.tq: Distinguish the unique Indian-hosted COP from the more recent COP milestones.
xs: **CoP3** was held in **New Delhi, 1981** — the **only CITES COP hosted by India** — option **(3)**.
xa: CoP19 added **54 shark and ray species** to App II.
CoP20 marked **50 years** of CITES and added **77 species**.
India hosted **CBD COP11** (**Hyderabad, 2012**) and **CMS COP-13** (**Gandhinagar, Feb 2020**).

79.s: At CoP20, India defeated a European Union proposal seeking a stricter listing of
79.x: At CoP20, India defeated the European Union proposal for a stricter listing of Guggul, scientifically known as Commiphora wightii.
79.tq: Use the species-scientific-name pair to avoid confusing India’s different CITES proposals.
xs: India defeated the EU proposal on **Guggul (Commiphora wightii)** at **CoP20** — option **(4)**.
**Red sanders** is already **App II**; the **star tortoise** was uplisted at **CoP18**; the **golden gecko** is App II.
xa: CoP20: **Samarkand, Uzbekistan**, **2025**; **77 species** added.
India's proposals: **rosewood, otters, tortoises, Tokay gecko, wedgefish**.
CoP20 uplisted **whale shark, oceanic whitetip, manta rays** to App I.

79.s: Under the Kigali Amendment, India is associated with an HFC freeze by
79.x: Under the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol, India's HFC freeze year is 2028.
79.tq: Recall the treaty-specific target year rather than the protocol-adoption year.
xs: Under **Kigali**, India's **HFC freeze** is by **2028** — option **(3)**.
Kigali is an amendment to the **Montreal Protocol** (**1987**).
xa: Ozone Secretariat: **Nairobi**.
**Ozone Day**: **16 September**.
⚠ Some APP tables wrongly place the Montreal Protocol at **Helsinki**.

79.s: Kolleru Lake is associated with which of the following international conservation designations?
79.x: Kolleru is a Ramsar wetland of international importance.
79.tq: Use the location-to-treaty association without confusing wetlands with species-trade instruments.
xs: **Kolleru Lake** is a **Ramsar site** — option **(1)**.
It is AP's Ramsar wetland (designated **2002**).
xa: **Visakhapatnam wetlands** come under **Operation Lungs 2.0**.
India has **101** Ramsar sites.
Montreux Record (India): **Keoladeo** and **Loktak**.

79.s: CITES CoP20 was historically significant because it was the:
o: First CITES COP held in Central Asia
First CITES COP held in Europe
First CITES COP held in Africa
First CITES COP held in South Asia
79.x: CITES CoP20 was the first CITES Conference of the Parties held in Central Asia.
79.tq: Test the precise regional description rather than the host-city name alone.
xs: **CITES CoP20** was the **first CITES COP in Central Asia** — option **(1)**.
It was held at **Samarkand, Uzbekistan**, **2025**.
xa: It marked **50 years** of CITES; **77 species** added.
It uplisted **whale shark, oceanic whitetip, manta rays** to App I.
India **defeated an EU proposal** on **Guggul**.

79.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Chilika Lake
(b) Keoladeo
(c) Wular Lake
(d) Loktak Lake

List-II
(i) Manipur
(ii) Odisha
(iii) Rajasthan
