79.x: Chilika is in Odisha, Keoladeo in Rajasthan, Wular in J&K, and Loktak in Manipur. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
79.tq: Match each wetland to its State.
n: Chilika Lake is located in Odisha. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 38-39]
Keoladeo is located in Rajasthan. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 38-39]
Wular Lake is located in J&K. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 38-39]
Loktak Lake is located in Manipur. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 38-39]
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Chilika Lake** — **Odisha**; **Keoladeo** — **Rajasthan**.
**Wular Lake** — **J&K**; **Loktak Lake** — **Manipur**.
xa: ⚠ Montreux Record = **Keoladeo + Loktak**; **Chilika** was removed after restoration.
**Sambhar Lake** is also in **Rajasthan**.
India joined Ramsar in **1982**; Secretariat at **Gland, Switzerland**.

79.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
79.x: The Nagoya Protocol is a protocol under the Convention on Biological Diversity. The Cartagena Protocol is also under the CBD, while the Nagoya-Kuala Lumpur Supplementary Protocol is linked to the Cartagena Protocol.
79.tq: Start with the sure parent convention and eliminate unrelated climate and wetland treaties.
xs: **Nagoya Protocol — CBD** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Cartagena** is also under the **CBD**, not Ramsar or Paris.
The **Nagoya-Kuala Lumpur Supplementary Protocol** is under **Cartagena**, hence **CBD**, not UNFCCC.
xa: **PYQ 2025**: Nagoya is part of the **CBD** (not UNFCCC, Ramsar or Paris).
Nagoya = **ABS**; Cartagena = **biosafety**.
The Supplementary Protocol on **Liability and Redress** dates from **2010**.

79.s: The Cartagena Protocol primarily regulates the safe transfer, handling and use of:
o: Carbon credits generated by forest plantations
Endangered species traded across international borders
Living Modified Organisms resulting from modern biotechnology
79.x: The Cartagena Protocol deals with the safe transfer, handling and use of Living Modified Organisms resulting from modern biotechnology.
79.tq: Distinguish the subject matter of closely related environmental agreements.
xs: Cartagena regulates safe transfer, handling and use of **Living Modified Organisms (LMOs)** from modern biotechnology — option **(4)**.
Endangered-species trade is **CITES**; hazardous chemicals fall under **Rotterdam/Basel**.
xa: It was a **PYQ 2018** key.
**Advance Informed Agreement**: importing country consents before the first transboundary movement.
In India: nodal ministry **MoEF&CC**; GM approvals by **GEAC**.

79.s:
With reference to the Cali Fund, consider the following statements:
1. It emerged from CBD COP16 held at Cali.
2. It is connected with benefit-sharing from the use of Digital Sequence Information on genetic resources.
3. Large users are expected to pay 1% of profits or 0.1% of revenue.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
79.x: All three statements are correct. The Cali Fund was associated with COP16 at Cali in October 2024 and addresses benefit-sharing from DSI use, with the stated contribution expectations for large users.
79.tq: Use the all-correct option when the venue, subject and numerical contribution align.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**1:** the **Cali Fund** came from **COP16, Cali** (Oct-Nov **2024**).
**2:** it shares benefits from use of **Digital Sequence Information (DSI)**.
**3:** large users pay **1% of profits or 0.1% of revenue**.
xa: COP16 resumed at **Rome, Feb 2025**.
COP16 also pushed **KMGBF** implementation incl. **30x30**.
NBA's **April 2025** regulations include rules on **DSI**.

79.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Montreal Protocol — India is a Party
79.x: The Montreal Protocol was adopted at Montreal in 1987, its Ozone Secretariat is at Nairobi, and India is a Party. Helsinki is not the Secretariat location.
79.tq: Catch the deliberately swapped headquarters in a not-correctly-matched question.
xs: **Montreal Protocol — Secretariat at Helsinki** is wrong — option **(3)**; the **Ozone Secretariat** is at **Nairobi**.
The other pairs are right: adopted **1987** at **Montreal**; India is a **Party**.
xa: ⚠ An APP table wrongly says **Helsinki**.
**Kigali** amendment: India's **HFC freeze** by **2028**.
**Ozone Day** = **16 September**.

79.s: Which of the following is a criticism directed at the Biological Diversity Amendment Act, 2023?
o: It transferred all biodiversity powers to the UNCCD
It completely abolished access and benefit-sharing mechanisms
It was criticised for diluting access and benefit-sharing and reducing the role of local communities
It prohibited the use of genetic resources for research
79.x: The amendment has been criticised for diluting access and benefit-sharing, increasing biopiracy risks and reducing the role of local communities.
79.tq: Find the option that accurately captures a criticism without converting it into an absolute legal prohibition.
xs: The **BD Amendment 2023** was criticised for **diluting ABS**, raising **biopiracy risk** and **cutting local communities' role** — option **(3)**.
It did not abolish ABS or hand powers to the **UNCCD**; India still runs ABS through the **NBA** and **BMCs**.
xa: India implements Nagoya via the **BD Act 2002** (amended **2023**) + **BD Rules 2024**.
NBA's **ABS/BD Regulations** (**April 2025**) include rules on **Digital Sequence Information**.
**BMCs** can **levy collection fees** on access to bio-resources.
ABS income: over **Rs 266 crore since 2008**; red sanders **45%**.

79.s:
Assertion (A): In-situ conservation means conservation outside the natural habitat.
Reason (R): Ex-situ conservation means conservation outside the natural habitat.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
79.x: A is false and R is true: in-situ conservation protects species in their natural habitat. Conservation outside the habitat is ex-situ.
79.tq: Discriminate in-situ from ex-situ.
n: In-situ conservation occurs in the natural habitat. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 53-55]
Ex-situ conservation occurs outside the natural habitat. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 53-55]
xs: **A is false**, but **R is true** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**In-situ** conservation is conservation **in the natural habitat** — so A is false.
**Ex-situ** conservation is conservation **outside** the natural habitat — R is true.
xa: The **CBD** was **adopted** at **Rio** in **1992**; in force **29 December 1993**.
CBD objectives: **conservation**, **sustainable use**, **fair and equitable benefit-sharing**.
CBD Secretariat: **Montreal, Canada**; India ratified in **1994**.

79.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
 a. CBD COP 10
 b. CBD COP 11
 c. CBD COP 12
 d. CBD COP 13

List-II
 i. 2010 — Nagoya, Japan
 ii. 2012 — Hyderabad, India
 iii. 2014 — Pyeongchang, Korea
 iv. 2016 — Cancun, Mexico
79.x: CBD COP10 was held at Nagoya (2010), COP11 Hyderabad (2012), COP12 Pyeongchang (2014), and COP13 Cancún (2016). The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
79.tq: Arrange the CBD COPs in time order.
n: The venue of CBD COP 10 was Nagoya, Japan. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
CBD COP 11 was held in 2012. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The venue of CBD COP 11 was Hyderabad, India. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
CBD COP 12 was held in 2014. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The venue of CBD COP 12 was Pyeongchang, Korea. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
CBD COP 13 was held in 2016. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The venue of CBD COP 13 was Cancun, Mexico. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
xs: The correct match is **a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**COP 10** — **2010**, **Nagoya, Japan**; **COP 11** — **2012**, **Hyderabad, India**.
**COP 12** — **2014**, **Pyeongchang, Korea**; **COP 13** — **2016**, **Cancun, Mexico**.
xa: COP 10 gave the **Nagoya Protocol** and **Aichi Targets**.
**COP 11** is the COP **hosted by India**.
First CBD COP: **Nassau, Bahamas, 1994**.

79.s:
Consider the following statements:

I. CBD COP 14 was held in 2018 at Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt.
II. CBD COP 15 was held during 2021–22 in Kunming and Montreal.
III. CBD COP 16 was held in 2024 at Cali, Colombia.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
79.x: All three are correct: CBD COP14 was held at Sharm el-Sheikh (2018), COP15 at Kunming and Montreal (2021–22), and COP16 at Cali (2024).
79.tq: Arrange the CBD COPs in time order.
n: CBD COP 14 was held in 2018. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The venue of CBD COP 14 was Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
CBD COP 15 was held during 2021–22. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
CBD COP 15 was held in Kunming and Montreal. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
CBD COP 16 was held in 2024. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The venue of CBD COP 16 was Cali, Colombia. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
xs: **All three** statements — **I, II and III** — are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
I: **COP 14** — **2018**, **Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt**; II: **COP 15** — **2021–22**, **Kunming** and **Montreal**.
III: **COP 16** — **2024**, **Cali, Colombia**.
xa: COP 15 adopted the **KMGBF**: **4 goals**, **23 targets**.
COP 16 created the **Cali Fund** on **Digital Sequence Information (DSI)**.
COP 14 began the post-2020 framework — "**New Deal for Nature**".

79.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) UNCCD
(b) Convention on Biological Diversity
(c) Cartagena Protocol
(d) Nagoya Protocol

List-II
(i) Access and Benefit Sharing
(ii) Biosafety / LMOs-GMOs
(iii) Biodiversity conservation
(iv) Desertification and land degradation
79.x: The UNCCD covers desertification, the CBD biodiversity conservation, Cartagena biosafety and GMOs, and Nagoya access and benefit sharing. The answer is a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i.
79.tq: Match each treaty to its subject.
n: The UNCCD focuses on desertification. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
The UNCCD focuses on land degradation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
The CBD focuses on biodiversity conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
The Cartagena Protocol concerns biosafety. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
The Cartagena Protocol concerns living modified organisms (LMOs) and genetically modified organisms (GMOs). [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
The Nagoya Protocol concerns access and benefit sharing. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
xs: The correct match is **a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**UNCCD** — **desertification** and **land degradation**; **CBD** — **biodiversity conservation**.
**Cartagena Protocol** — **biosafety**, **LMOs/GMOs**; **Nagoya Protocol** — **access and benefit sharing**.
xa: Cartagena: adopted **2000**, in force **2003**, **173 parties**.
Nagoya: adopted **2010**, in force **2014**, **137 parties**; India ratified **2012**.
UNCCD was **established 1994**; linked with **SDG 15** and **Land Degradation Neutrality**.

79.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three objectives of the Convention on Biological Diversity?
o: Sustainable use of the components of biodiversity
Compulsory transfer of all genetic technologies to developing countries
Fair and equitable sharing of benefits from genetic resources
79.x: The CBD objectives are conservation, sustainable use and fair and equitable benefit-sharing. Compulsory transfer of all genetic technologies is not one of its objectives.
79.tq: Identify the option that extends the treaty beyond its stated three-objective structure.
xs: **Compulsory transfer of all genetic technologies** is not a CBD objective — option **(2)**.
The three objectives: **conservation**, **sustainable use**, and **fair and equitable benefit-sharing** from genetic resources.
xa: CBD opened at **Rio 1992**; in force **1993**; Secretariat **Montreal**.
Financial mechanism: **GEF** (also for UNFCCC).
APSBB's objectives **mirror the CBD**.

79.s: The Nagoya-Kuala Lumpur Supplementary Protocol on Liability and Redress, adopted in 2010, is a supplementary protocol to the:
o: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
79.x: The Nagoya-Kuala Lumpur Supplementary Protocol on Liability and Redress is supplementary to the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety and is therefore connected to the CBD framework.
79.tq: Distinguish a supplementary protocol from the principal protocol and its parent convention.
xs: The **Nagoya-Kuala Lumpur Supplementary Protocol** on **Liability and Redress** (**2010**) supplements the **Cartagena Protocol** — option **(2)**.
Despite the "Nagoya" in its name, it is not under the **Nagoya Protocol on ABS**.
xa: Its parent chain: **Cartagena → CBD**.
Cartagena: adopted **2000**, in force **2003**, **173 parties**.
Cartagena regulates **LMOs** from modern biotechnology.

79.s:
With reference to the Cartagena Protocol, consider the following statements:
1. Under the Advance Informed Agreement, the importing country is informed and consents before the first transboundary movement of an LMO.
2. Shipments of LMOs carry documentation identifying the LMO.
3. The Biosafety Clearing-House is a laboratory that tests all genetically modified crops before export.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
79.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: AIA needs the importing country's informed consent, and LMO shipments carry identifying documentation. Statement 3 is wrong: the Biosafety Clearing-House is an online platform for sharing LMO information and decisions, not a testing laboratory. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
79.tq: AIA = importer consents; BCH = online information platform.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
**Statement 1:** correct — under **AIA** the importing country is informed and **consents** before the first transboundary movement.
**Statement 2:** correct — shipments carry **documentation identifying the LMO**.
**Statement 3:** wrong — the **Biosafety Clearing-House** is an **online platform** for sharing LMO information, not a lab.
xa: Cartagena: adopted **2000**, in force **2003**.
**173 parties** incl. India.
India's GM approvals: **GEAC**.

79.s: In India, the nodal ministry for the Cartagena Protocol is the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, while approvals for genetically engineered organisms are given by the:
79.x: MoEF&CC is India's nodal ministry, and the Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee handles approvals for genetically engineered organisms.
79.tq: Separate the nodal ministry from the specialised approval committee.
xs: GM approvals in India are given by the **Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee (GEAC)** — option **(1)**.
The **BCH** is only an online information platform; the **NBA** handles **ABS** approvals; SBBs are the state tier.
xa: Nodal ministry for Cartagena: **MoEF&CC**.
Cartagena is named after **Cartagena, Colombia**.
⚠ Cartagena = **biosafety/LMOs**; Nagoya = **ABS**.

79.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety:
1. It was adopted in 2000 and entered into force in 2003.
2. It is named after Cartagena in Colombia.
3. It is a protocol under the UNFCCC.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
79.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Protocol was adopted in 2000, entered into force in 2003 and is named after Cartagena, Colombia. Statement 3 is wrong: it is a protocol under the CBD, not the UNFCCC. So '1 only' misses a true statement and the options with 3 are wrong.
79.tq: Cartagena 2000/2003 (biosafety); Nagoya 2010/2014 (ABS) — both CBD.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
**Statement 1:** correct — adopted **2000**, in force **2003**.
**Statement 2:** correct — named after **Cartagena, Colombia**.
**Statement 3:** wrong — it is a protocol under the **CBD**, not UNFCCC.
xa: **173 parties** incl. India.
Supplementary Protocol on **Liability and Redress** (**2010**) is under Cartagena.
**COP-15** also served as **10th MOP** Cartagena and **4th MOP** Nagoya.

79.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Kunming-Montreal GBF — adopted in 2000 and entered into force in 2003
Cartagena Protocol — adopted in 2010 and entered into force in 2014
Nagoya Protocol — adopted in 2010 and entered into force in 2014
Aichi Targets — adopted in 2022 for the period 2030–2050
79.x: The Nagoya Protocol was adopted at COP10, Nagoya, in 2010 and entered into force in 2014. The other pairs are wrong: the Cartagena Protocol was adopted in 2000 and in force in 2003 (not 2010/2014), the KMGBF was adopted in 2022 (not 2000), and the Aichi Targets were adopted in 2010 for 2011-2020 (not 2022 for 2030-2050).
79.tq: Check each instrument against its adoption and entry-into-force dates rather than relying on the protocol names alone.
xs: **Nagoya Protocol — adopted 2010, in force 2014** is correct — option **(3)**.
**KMGBF** was adopted in **2022**, not 2000; **Aichi** Targets were adopted in **2010** for **2011-2020**.
xa: Nagoya: **137 parties**; India ratified in **2012**.
Cartagena: **173 parties**.
KMGBF: **4 goals** for **2050**, **23 targets** for **2030**.

79.s: The Nagoya Protocol covers genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge relating to:
o: Only animal and human genetic material
Plants, animals and microorganisms, but not human genetic material
All genetic material, including human genetic material
79.x: The Protocol covers plant, animal and microbial genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge, while excluding human genetic material.
79.tq: Identify the inclusion and exclusion in the scope of an international instrument.
xs: Nagoya covers **plant, animal and microbial** genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge, **excluding human genetic material** — option **(2)**.
So options limited to plants/animals or including human material are wrong.
xa: **Utilisation** = R&D on genetic and/or **biochemical** composition (**APPSC 2025** key).
Pillars: **prior informed consent**, **Mutually Agreed Terms**, **compliance**.
NBA's **April 2025** regulations include rules on **Digital Sequence Information**.

79.s: Which of the following is NOT a pillar of the Nagoya Protocol?
o: Compliance against illegal acquisition of genetic resources
Compulsory transfer of all genetic resources to the National Biodiversity Authority
Mutually Agreed Terms for monetary and non-monetary benefits
79.x: The pillars are prior informed consent, Mutually Agreed Terms for benefit-sharing, and compliance against illegal acquisition. Compulsory transfer of all genetic resources is not a pillar.
79.tq: Find the option that introduces an authority or obligation not included among the stated pillars.
xs: **Compulsory transfer of all genetic resources to the NBA** is not a Nagoya pillar — option **(3)**.
The pillars: **prior informed consent**, **Mutually Agreed Terms** for monetary/non-monetary benefits, and **compliance** against illegal acquisition.
xa: India's implementing law: **BD Act 2002** (amended **2023**) + **BD Rules 2024**.
**BMCs** can **levy collection fees** on access to bio-resources in their area.
The NBA gives **ABS approvals** for foreign users.

79.s: Under the Nagoya Protocol, 'utilisation of genetic resources' means:
o: Commercial sale of whole organisms across borders
Research and development on the genetic and/or biochemical composition of genetic resources
Cultivation of genetically modified crops for food
Conservation of genetic resources in gene banks only
79.x: The Protocol defines utilisation as research and development on the genetic and/or biochemical composition of genetic resources. Cross-border sale of organisms is a trade matter (CITES), GM crop cultivation is a biosafety matter (Cartagena), and gene-bank storage alone is conservation, not utilisation.
79.tq: Utilisation = R&D on genetic AND/OR biochemical composition.
xs: **Utilisation** = **R&D on the genetic and/or biochemical composition** of genetic resources — option **(2)** (**APPSC 2025** key).
Cross-border trade is a **CITES** matter; GM crops come under **Cartagena** (biosafety).
xa: Nagoya excludes **human genetic material**.
It is **legally binding**, under the **CBD**.
India ratified in **2012**; in force **2014**.

79.s: India submitted its first National Report on the Nagoya Protocol with which of the following figures?
o: 3,556 IRCCs, constituting less than 30% of the global total
1,556 IRCCs, constituting over 60% of the global total
3,556 IRCCs, constituting over 60% of the global total
2,556 IRCCs, constituting over 50% of the global total
79.x: India's first National Report recorded 3,556 IRCCs, more than 60% of the global total.
79.tq: Split the option into two independently verifiable numerical parts.
xs: India's **1st National Report** on Nagoya recorded **3,556 IRCCs**, over **60%** of the global total — option **(3)**.
The other options change the count or the share.
xa: India ratified Nagoya in **2012**; in force **2014**.
NBA's **April 2025** regulations cover **Digital Sequence Information**.
India's ABS income: over **Rs 266 crore since 2008**.

79.s: The Andhra Pradesh State Biodiversity Board aims at achieving zero loss of biodiversity and ecosystem services by:
79.x: The AP State Biodiversity Board aims at zero loss of biodiversity and ecosystem services by 2050.
79.tq: Use the stated target year rather than inferring it from the decade-based observances.
xs: APSBB aims at **zero loss of biodiversity and ecosystem services by 2050** — option **(3)**.
**2030** is the KMGBF target year, not APSBB's aim.
xa: APSBB objectives **mirror the CBD**.
APSBB Chairman: **Neelayapalem Vijay Kumar**; plans **OECMs** outside PAs to help meet **30x30**.
KMGBF goals also run to **2050**.

79.s: The Aichi Biodiversity Targets were adopted at which Conference of the Parties and in which year?
79.x: The 20 Aichi Biodiversity Targets were adopted at CBD COP10, held at Nagoya in 2010. COP12 at Pyeongchang reviewed their progress but did not adopt them.
79.tq: Use the adoption venue and year, while distinguishing adoption from later review.
xs: The **Aichi Targets** were adopted at **COP10, Nagoya, 2010** — option **(3)**.
⚠ **COP12, Pyeongchang** (**2014**) only **reviewed** them; **COP15** adopted the **KMGBF**; **COP16** was Cali.
xa: Structure: **20 targets** under **5 strategic goals**; plan **2011-2020**.
**None of the 20** were fully met by **2020** (**Global Biodiversity Outlook 5**).
The **Nagoya Protocol** was adopted at the same **COP10**.

79.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Aichi Biodiversity Targets:
1. They comprised 20 targets under five strategic goals in the Strategic Plan 2011-2020.
2. All 20 targets were fully met by 2020.
3. Weak buy-in beyond environment ministries was one reason for their shortfall.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
79.x: Statement 1 is correct: 20 targets under 5 strategic goals for 2011-2020. Statement 2 is wrong: Global Biodiversity Outlook 5 found none of the 20 fully met. Statement 3 is correct: weak buy-in beyond environment ministries is cited. Hence '1 and 3 only'.
79.tq: Aichi: 20 targets, 5 goals, none fully met (GBO-5).
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(3)**.
**Statement 1:** correct — **20 targets** under **5 strategic goals**, **2011-2020**.
**Statement 2:** wrong — **none of the 20** were fully met (**GBO-5**).
**Statement 3:** correct — **weak buy-in beyond environment ministries**.
xa: Adopted at **COP10, Nagoya (2010)**.
Successor: **KMGBF** — **23** targets, **4** goals.
KMGBF adds numeric targets, a **monitoring framework** and finance.

79.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

List-I (Instrument)
a. Cartagena Protocol
b. Nagoya Protocol
c. Aichi Targets
d. Kunming-Montreal GBF

List-II (Subject or feature)
i. Access and benefit-sharing
 ii. Biosafety and living modified organisms
 iii. Twenty targets for 2011–2020
 iv. Four goals for 2050 and 23 targets for 2030
79.x: Cartagena concerns biosafety, Nagoya concerns access and benefit-sharing, the Aichi Targets numbered 20 for 2011–2020, and the Kunming-Montreal GBF contains four 2050 goals and 23 targets for 2030.
79.tq: Begin with the distinctive subject of Cartagena and eliminate codes that swap the protocols.
xs: Correct match: **a–ii, b–i, c–iii, d–iv** — option **(1)**.
**Cartagena** → **biosafety/LMOs**; **Nagoya** → **access and benefit-sharing**.
xa: Aichi and Nagoya were both adopted at **COP10, Nagoya, 2010**.
KMGBF: **COP15, Montreal, December 2022**.

79.s:
With reference to the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, consider the following statements:
1. It contains four goals for 2050 and 23 targets for 2030.
2. It was adopted at COP-15 in December 2022.
3. It includes the 30x30 objective.
4. It seeks to halve food waste.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
79.x: All four statements are correct. The framework has four 2050 goals, 23 targets for 2030, the 30x30 objective and a target to halve food waste.
79.tq: Test the numerical framework together with its major action targets.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**1:** **4 goals** for **2050**, **23 targets** for **2030**; **2:** adopted at **COP15**, **December 2022**.
**3:** **30x30** is **Target 3**; **4:** **Target 16** halves global **food waste**.
xa: **Target 18**: cut **harmful subsidies** by at least **US$500 billion a year**.
**Target 6**: cut invasive alien species by **at least 50%**.
**Target 7**: halve excess **nutrients** and **pesticide** risk.
⚠ **30x30** = protection (Target 3); restoring **30% of degraded** ecosystems = **Target 2**.

79.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. First segment of CBD COP15 at Kunming
B. Adoption of the KMGBF at Montreal
C. Adoption of the Aichi Biodiversity Targets at Nagoya
D. COP16 at Cali
79.x: The correct sequence is Nagoya in 2010, Kunming in 2021, Montreal in December 2022, and Cali in October 2024.
79.tq: Fix the first and last events, then arrange the two KMGBF stages.
xs: Order: **C, A, B, D** — option **(1)**.
**Aichi** adopted at **Nagoya 2010** → **Kunming** first segment **Oct 2021** → **KMGBF** adopted at **Montreal, December 2022** → **COP16 Cali**, **Oct-Nov 2024**.
xa: ⚠ KMGBF was **adopted at Montreal**, not Kunming.
COP16 resumed at **Rome, Feb 2025**.
Aichi: **20** targets, **2011-2020**; KMGBF: **23** targets for **2030**.
COP15: **China presidency, Canada host**.

79.s: Target 2 of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework relates to which of the following?
o: Restoration of 30% of degraded land and water ecosystems
Conservation of 30% of land and oceans
Reducing harmful subsidies by US$500 billion annually
79.x: Target 2 calls for effective restoration of 30% of degraded land and water ecosystems by 2030. Conservation of 30% of land and oceans is Target 3.
79.tq: Discriminate between the closely related restoration and protection targets.
xs: **Target 2** = effective **restoration of 30% of degraded** land and water ecosystems — option **(2)**.
**Conservation of 30% of land and oceans** is **Target 3** (**30x30**); food waste is **Target 16**; subsidies are **Target 18**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes (Block06) wrongly call restoration "the 30x30 target".
**Target 1**: bring loss of high-biodiversity areas **close to zero**.
**Target 6**: cut invasive alien species by **at least 50%**.

79.s:
Match List-I (KMGBF target) with List-II (content by 2030):
List-I
a. Target 3
b. Target 6
c. Target 7
d. Target 16
List-II
i. Halve global food waste
ii. Cut introduction and establishment of invasive alien species by at least 50%
iii. Halve excess nutrients lost to the environment and overall pesticide risk
iv. Conserve 30% of land and 30% of oceans/waters
Select the correct answer:
79.x: Target 3 is 30x30 conservation (iv), Target 6 cuts invasive alien species by at least 50% (ii), Target 7 halves excess nutrients and pesticide risk (iii), Target 16 halves food waste (i). Option B swaps Targets 6 and 7; option C swaps Targets 3 and 16; option D mismatches all four.
79.tq: 3 = 30x30, 6 = invasives 50%, 7 = nutrients/pesticides, 16 = food waste.
xs: Correct match: **a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i** — option **(1)**.
**Target 3** → **30x30**; **Target 6** → invasive alien species cut by **at least 50%**.
**Target 7** → halve excess **nutrients** and **pesticide** risk; **Target 16** → halve **food waste**.
xa: **Target 18**: cut **harmful subsidies** by **US$500 billion a year**.
**Target 2**: restore **30% of degraded** ecosystems.
**Target 19**: mobilise **US$200 billion a year** by **2030**.

79.s: Target 18 calls for reducing harmful subsidies by at least:
79.x: Target 18 calls for a reduction of harmful subsidies by at least US$500 billion a year.
79.tq: Distinguish the annual harmful-subsidy figure from the wider biodiversity-finance figures.
xs: **Target 18**: reduce harmful subsidies by at least **US$500 billion a year** — option **(1)**.
**US$700 billion** is the **Goal D** finance gap; **US$200 billion** is the **Target 19** mobilisation goal.
xa: ⚠ Remember the trio: **200** mobilise, **500** subsidies, **700** gap.
KMGBF new features: numeric targets (**30x30**, **US$500 bn** subsidies), monitoring framework, finance.
**GBF Fund** is set up under the **GEF**.

79.s: Target 19 of the KMGBF seeks mobilisation of at least how much annually by 2030 from all sources?
79.x: Target 19 seeks at least US$200 billion per year by 2030 from all sources. This is the overall resource-mobilisation target, not the size of the GBF Fund itself.
79.tq: Distinguish the overall annual mobilisation target from related finance figures.
xs: **Target 19**: mobilise at least **US$200 billion a year by 2030** from all sources — option **(4)**.
**US$500 billion** = subsidy cut (**Target 18**); **US$700 billion** = **Goal D** finance gap.
xa: ⚠ Some notes tie **US$200 billion** to the **GBFF** — it is the overall target.
The **GBF Fund** sits under the **GEF**.
**Cali Fund**: large DSI users pay **1% of profits or 0.1% of revenue**.

79.s: India’s updated National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan for 2024–2030 contains:
79.x: India’s updated NBSAP contains 23 national targets matching the 23 targets of the KMGBF.
79.tq: Match the national target count with the corresponding global framework.
xs: India's updated NBSAP (**2024-2030**) has **23 national targets**, matching the **KMGBF** — option **(1)**.
**20** was the Aichi count; **21** was an older KMGBF draft.
xa: Released at **COP16, Cali (Oct 2024)**; aligned with **30x30**.
Some notes call it **NBSAP-II, 2023-2030**.
**Target 13** = access and benefit-sharing.

79.s: India's seventh National Report to the Convention on Biological Diversity was notable because it represented:
o: The first review of the Sendai Framework targets
The first national report under CITES
The first report on Ramsar implementation in India
The first full review against the 23 targets of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework
79.x: India's seventh CBD National Report was the first full review against all 23 KMGBF targets.
79.tq: Separate the reporting mechanism of CBD from those of CITES, Ramsar and disaster-risk frameworks.
xs: India's **7th National Report (NR7)** was the **first full review against the 23 KMGBF targets** — option **(4)**.
It is a **CBD** report, not a CITES, Ramsar or Sendai one.
xa: National reports come under **Article 26** of the CBD, about every **four years**.
Progress is tracked through **headline indicators** of the KMGBF monitoring framework.
NBA SOP under **Sec. 38, BD Act**: **159 plant** and **173 animal** species notified.

79.s:
Which of the following were outcomes of the Stockholm Conference, 1972?
1. Stockholm Declaration containing 26 principles
2. An Action Plan
3. Establishment of UNEP
4. Recognition of 5 June as World Environment Day
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
79.x: The Stockholm Conference produced the 26-principle Stockholm Declaration and an Action Plan, led to the establishment of UNEP and resulted in 5 June being observed as World Environment Day.
79.tq: Group the declaration, institutional outcome, action plan and commemorative date as conference results.
xs: All four are Stockholm outcomes — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**1 and 2:** the **Stockholm Declaration** (**26** principles) and an **Action Plan**.
**3:** **UNEP** set up in **1972**, HQ **Nairobi**; **4:** **5 June** became **World Environment Day**.
xa: Venue/dates: **Stockholm, Sweden**, **5-16 June 1972**.
In India Stockholm decisions were implemented through the **EPA 1986**.
⚠ **UNEA** (from **Rio+20**, **2012**) is also in **Nairobi**.

79.s:
Consider the following statements about the implementation of CITES:
1. The Management Authority of a Party deals with permits.
2. The Scientific Authority of a Party provides scientific advice.
3. The CITES Trade Database is maintained by the CITES Secretariat at Geneva.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
79.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Management Authority handles permits and the Scientific Authority gives scientific advice. Statement 3 is wrong: the CITES Trade Database is kept by UNEP-WCMC, not the Secretariat. So '1 only' misses statement 2, and the options containing 3 are wrong.
79.tq: Management = permits, Scientific = advice; database = UNEP-WCMC.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
**Statement 1:** correct — **Management Authority** handles **permits**.
**Statement 2:** correct — **Scientific Authority** gives **advice**.
**Statement 3:** wrong — the **CITES Trade Database** is kept by **UNEP-WCMC**.
xa: **TRAFFIC**: trade-monitoring network, joint programme of **WWF and IUCN** (**1976**).
**ICCWC** links CITES with **INTERPOL, UNODC, WCO**.
**MIKE** tracks elephant poaching.

79.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB)?
o: An international treaty secretariat headquartered in Geneva
A voluntary NGO network of WWF and IUCN
A scientific authority that alone decides CITES Appendix listings
A statutory body under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change that enforces CITES and prevents wildlife trafficking
79.x: WCCB is a statutory body under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. It enforces CITES and works to prevent wildlife trafficking.
79.tq: Distinguish the Indian statutory enforcement body from international treaties and NGO networks.
xs: **WCCB** is a **statutory body under MoEF&CC** that **enforces CITES** and prevents **wildlife trafficking** — option **(4)**.
The NGO network of **WWF and IUCN** is **TRAFFIC**; the Geneva secretariat is **CITES**'s.
xa: Set up in **2007** under the **WPA** (**2006** amendment); HQ **New Delhi**.
Helps **Customs** inspect wildlife consignments under **CITES and EXIM policy**.
Builds the **wildlife-crime database**.

79.s:
Which of the following are functions of the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau?
1. Assisting Customs in inspecting wildlife consignments under CITES and EXIM policy
2. Building a wildlife-crime database
3. Monitoring elephant poaching through MIKE
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
79.x: WCCB assists Customs and builds the wildlife-crime database. MIKE, rather than WCCB, tracks elephant poaching.
79.tq: Identify the one function belonging to a linked but separate international monitoring programme.
xs: WCCB functions are **1 and 2** — option **(2)**.
**1:** it helps **Customs** inspect wildlife consignments under **CITES and EXIM policy**; **2:** builds the **wildlife-crime database**.
**3** is wrong: **MIKE** tracks **elephant poaching** — it is a global monitoring tool, not WCCB.
xa: WCCB: set up **2007**, HQ **New Delhi**.
**ICCWC** links CITES with **INTERPOL, UNODC, WCO**.
**TRAFFIC** = **WWF and IUCN** joint programme.

79.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022:
1. It added a chapter on CITES to the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
2. It created a new Schedule IV for specimens listed in the CITES Appendices.
3. The new Schedule IV lists invasive alien species.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
79.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the 2022 amendment added a CITES chapter and a Schedule IV for CITES-listed specimens. Statement 3 is a trap: invasive alien species are regulated under a separate new section, not Schedule IV. So '1 only' misses a true statement and options with 3 are wrong.
79.tq: Schedule IV (2022) = CITES specimens, NOT invasive species.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
**Statement 1:** correct — the **2022 amendment** added a **chapter on CITES**.
**Statement 2:** correct — new **Schedule IV** for specimens in the **CITES Appendices**.
**Statement 3:** wrong — **invasive alien species** are regulated under a **separate new section**.
xa: It also provides **Management and Scientific Authorities**.
Parent Act: **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**.
**WCCB** was created by the WPA's **2006** amendment (set up **2007**).

79.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Tiger — Appendix I
2. Clouded leopard — Appendix I
3. Red sanders — Appendix II
4. Golden gecko — Appendix I
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
79.x: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The golden gecko, which is endemic to Andhra Pradesh, is listed in Appendix II, not Appendix I.
79.tq: Find the single reversed species-appendix pair among otherwise familiar matches.
xs: Pairs **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(1)**.
**Tiger** — **I**; **Clouded leopard** — **I**; **Red sanders** — **II**.
**Pair 4:** wrong — the **golden gecko** (AP endemic) is in **Appendix II**.
xa: **Indian and Chinese pangolins** — **I**; over **500,000** pangolins seized globally **2016-2024**.
**Rosewood (Dalbergia)** and **striped hyena** — **II**.
Red sanders is IUCN **Endangered**.

79.s:
At CITES CoP19 held in Panama in 2022, which of the following occurred?
1. Fifty-four sharks and rays were added to Appendix II.
2. Rosewood and sea cucumbers received protection.
3. CITES completed its first meeting in Central Asia.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
79.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct for CoP19 in Panama in 2022. The first CITES COP in Central Asia was CoP20 at Samarkand in 2025.
79.tq: Separate the achievements of consecutive COPs and identify the statement transferred from CoP20.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
**1:** correct — **54 shark and ray species** moved to **App II** at CoP19 (**Panama, 2022**).
**2:** correct — **rosewood** and **sea cucumbers** were protected.
**3:** wrong — the first COP in **Central Asia** was **CoP20, Samarkand, 2025**.
xa: CoP20 uplisted **whale shark, oceanic whitetip, manta rays** to App I.
**Rosewood (Dalbergia)** is in Appendix **II**.
COP meets **every 2-3 years**.

79.s: The financial mechanism associated with the Convention on Biological Diversity, and also with the UNFCCC, is the:
o: International Union for Conservation of Nature
79.x: The Global Environment Facility serves as a financial mechanism for both the CBD and the UNFCCC.
79.tq: Identify the common financial institution rather than a treaty body or conservation network.
xs: The **Global Environment Facility (GEF)** is the financial mechanism of the **CBD** and **UNFCCC** — option **(2)**.
**IUCN** is a union of governments and NGOs; **UNEA** is the Rio+20 assembly.
xa: The **GBF Fund** was set up under the **GEF**.
⚠ Target 19's **US$200 billion a year** is the overall goal, not the GBF Fund's size.
**COP16** added the **Cali Fund** on DSI.

79.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India and the Nagoya Protocol:
1. India implements it through the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 (amended 2023) and the Biological Diversity Rules, 2024.
2. The National Biodiversity Authority notified ABS/BD Regulations in April 2025, including rules on Digital Sequence Information.
3. India ratified the Nagoya Protocol in 2014.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
79.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: India ratified in 2012; 2014 is the year the Protocol entered into force. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' omits a true statement and the options with 3 are wrong.
79.tq: Trap: 2012 = India ratified, 2014 = entry into force.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
**Statement 1:** correct — implemented via **BD Act 2002** (amended **2023**) and **BD Rules 2024**.
**Statement 2:** correct — NBA's **ABS/BD Regulations** (**April 2025**) include **Digital Sequence Information**.
**Statement 3:** wrong — India ratified in **2012**; **2014** is entry into force.
xa: India's **1st National Report**: **3,556** Certificates of Compliance, **>60%** of global total.
**Target 13** of India's NBSAP = access and benefit-sharing.
Criticism: **BD Amendment 2023** said to dilute ABS and raise biopiracy risk.

79.s:
With reference to the Biological Diversity framework in India, consider the following statements:
1. The National Biodiversity Authority is located at Chennai and gives ABS approvals for foreign users.
2. Biodiversity Management Committees can levy collection fees for access to biological resources in their area.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
79.x: Both are correct: the NBA at Chennai handles regulation, advice and ABS approvals for foreign users and IPR, and BMCs can levy collection fees on access to bio-resources in their area (UPSC 2023 key). Hence '1 only', '2 only' and 'neither' are wrong.
79.tq: UPSC 2023 trap: both statements on BMCs/NBA are correct.
xs: Both statements are correct — option **(3)**.
**Statement 1:** correct — the **NBA** (**Chennai**) gives **ABS approvals** for foreign users and IPR.
**Statement 2:** correct — **BMCs** can **levy collection fees** on access to bio-resources in their area (UPSC **2023** key).
xa: The **NBA Fund** is a statutory fund under the Act.
BMCs maintain **People's Biodiversity Registers**.
**Red Sanders** gives **45%** of India's ABS income.

79.s:
Consider the following statements about indigenous peoples and local communities under the biodiversity framework:
1. COP15 recognised their essential role in conservation and management.
2. KMGBF Target 22 seeks their full participation and rights over lands and resources.
3. The 30x30 objective is intended to disregard indigenous territories in protected-area planning.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
79.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because implementation of 30x30 is to respect indigenous territories.
79.tq: Reject the rights-reversal trap in a statement about indigenous territories.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
**Statement 1:** correct — **COP15** recognised the essential role of **IPLCs**.
**Statement 2:** correct — **Target 22** secures their **full participation** and rights over lands and resources.
**Statement 3:** wrong — **30x30** is to **respect indigenous territories**.
xa: India's route: **BMCs, PBRs and ABS** carry benefits to local and tribal communities.
**COP16** set up a permanent subsidiary body on Indigenous peoples (**Art. 8(j)**).
Criticism: **BD Amendment 2023** said to cut local communities' role.

79.s: The Agreement on Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ), commonly called the High Seas Treaty, entered into force on
79.x: The BBNJ Agreement entered into force on 17 January 2026.
79.tq: Distinguish the entry-into-force date from the date of India’s signature.
xs: The **BBNJ** entered into force on **17 January 2026** — option **(4)**.
India **signed** it in **Sept 2024**.
xa: Full name: **Agreement on Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction**.
Only **1.66%** of high seas are protected (WDPA).
It is listed among current developments with **UNCCD COP-17** in **Mongolia**.

79.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Basel Convention deals with hazardous waste; it was adopted in 1989 and entered into force in 1992.
2. India ratified the Basel Convention in June 1992.
3. The Rotterdam (PIC) Convention entered into force in 2004 and India acceded to it in 2010.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
79.x: Statement 1 is correct: Basel covers hazardous waste, adopted 1989, in force 1992. Statement 2 is correct: India ratified Basel in June 1992. Statement 3 is wrong: Rotterdam entered into force in 2004 but India acceded in 2005, not 2010. Hence '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' leaves out a true statement and the options with 3 are wrong.
79.tq: Basel 1989/1992, India June 1992; Rotterdam in force 2004, India 2005.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
**Statement 1:** correct — **Basel** = hazardous waste, **1989**, in force **1992**.
**Statement 2:** correct — India ratified Basel in **June 1992**.
**Statement 3:** wrong — **Rotterdam** came into force in **2004**, but India **acceded in 2005**, not 2010.
xa: Basel has **190 Parties**; Secretariat **Geneva**.
Rotterdam = **PIC** convention; Secretariat **Geneva/Rome**.
Montreal Protocol: **1987**; Ozone Secretariat **Nairobi**.

79.s: International Day for Biological Diversity is observed on
79.x: International Day for Biological Diversity is observed annually on 22 May.
79.tq: Recall the exact date of a named international observance.
xs: **International Day for Biological Diversity** = **22 May** — option **(4)**; CBD text adopted **22 May 1992**.
**5 June** = World Environment Day; **17 June** = Desertification and Drought Day; **16 September** = Ozone Day.
xa: ⚠ **2 Feb** Ramsar, **3 Mar** CITES, **22 May** CBD, **5 June** Stockholm.
International Year of Biodiversity: **2010**.
UN Decade on Biodiversity: **2011-2020**.

79.s: Which one of the following pairs of environmental observance and date is correctly matched?
79.x: World Wetlands Day is 2 February, the day the Ramsar Convention was adopted. World Wildlife Day is 3 March (CITES signed), so the first two options swap the dates, and 22 May is the International Day for Biological Diversity.
79.tq: 2 Feb Ramsar/wetlands; 3 March CITES/wildlife; 22 May CBD.
xs: **World Wetlands Day — 2 February** is correct — option **(3)**; it is the **Ramsar** adoption day.
**World Wildlife Day** is **3 March** (CITES signed) — options (1) and (2) swap the dates.
**22 May** is the **International Day for Biological Diversity**.
xa: **5 June** = World Environment Day (Stockholm).
World Wildlife Day was proclaimed by UNGA in **2013**.
**17 June** = Desertification and Drought Day.

79.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the legal character of the Nagoya Protocol?
o: It is a legally binding supplementary agreement to the CBD.
It is a voluntary declaration under the CBD.
It is a non-binding protocol under the UNFCCC.
It is a regional agreement applicable only to Asian countries.
79.x: The Nagoya Protocol is a legally binding supplementary agreement to the Convention on Biological Diversity; it is not merely voluntary.
79.tq: Distinguish a legally binding supplementary agreement from a voluntary declaration.
xs: The Nagoya Protocol is a **legally binding supplementary agreement to the CBD** — option **(1)**.
⚠ It is **NOT voluntary** (PYQ trap), and it is under the CBD, not UNFCCC; it is not regional.
xa: **137 parties** incl. India.
India implements it via the **BD Act 2002** (amended **2023**) and **BD Rules 2024**.
**PYQ 2025**: Nagoya is part of the **CBD**.

79.s:
With reference to the 30x30 target, consider the following statements:
1. It is a biodiversity conservation target.
2. It seeks conservation of 30% of land and 30% of oceans or waters by 2030.
3. It is primarily a renewable-energy deployment target.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
79.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because 30x30 is a biodiversity target concerning conservation of land and oceans or waters.
79.tq: Reject the subject-switch trap between biodiversity and renewable energy.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
**Statement 1:** correct — **30x30** is a **biodiversity** target (**APPSC G1 2024** PYQ).
**Statement 2:** correct — conserve **30% of land and 30% of oceans/waters** by **2030** (**Target 3**).
**Statement 3:** wrong — it is **NOT a renewable-energy** target.
xa: ⚠ 30x30 = **protection** (Target 3); restoration = **Target 2**.
**WDPA** tracks Target 3 → ~**10%** of oceans protected, only **1.66%** of high seas.
30x30 is to **respect indigenous territories** (Target 22).

79.s: The BBNJ Agreement, referred to in the context of marine conservation, deals primarily with:
o: Protection of biodiversity inside national parks
Biodiversity beyond national jurisdiction in the high seas
Biosafety regulation of genetically modified crops
79.x: The BBNJ Agreement (High Seas Treaty) concerns marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction, i.e. the high seas. It entered into force on 17 January 2026; India signed it in September 2024. Wetlands (Ramsar), national parks and GM-crop biosafety (Cartagena) are covered by other instruments.
79.tq: Expand the acronym conceptually and distinguish high-seas governance from domestic conservation.
xs: BBNJ deals with **biodiversity beyond national jurisdiction** in the **high seas** — option **(3)**.
Wetlands are **Ramsar**; GM-crop biosafety is **Cartagena**.
xa: Entered into force **17 January 2026**; India signed **Sept 2024**.
Only **1.66%** of the high seas are protected.
~**10%** of oceans are protected (WDPA).

79.s: The United Nations observed the International Year of Biodiversity in:
79.x: 2010 was the International Year of Biodiversity (PYQ 2018). It was followed by the UN Decade on Biodiversity, 2011-2020, which is why 2011 and 2020 are its start and end years, not the Year; 2002 is the Johannesburg WSSD year.
79.tq: Year of Biodiversity 2010; Decade 2011-2020.
xs: **2010** was the **International Year of Biodiversity** — option **(2)** (PYQ **2018**).
**2011-2020** was the **UN Decade on Biodiversity**; **2002** was the **Johannesburg WSSD**.
xa: **2010** also saw **COP10, Nagoya** adopt the **Aichi Targets** and **Nagoya Protocol**.
Aichi plan period: **2011-2020**.
**22 May** = International Day for Biological Diversity.

79.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Harike Wetland is located in Punjab.
East Kolkata Wetlands are located in West Bengal.
Sundarban Wetland is located in Odisha.
Kabartal/Kanwar Lake is located in Begusarai, Bihar.
79.x: Option C is incorrect: the Sundarban wetland is in West Bengal, not Odisha. Harike is in Punjab and Kabartal in Begusarai, Bihar.
79.tq: Match each wetland to its State.
n: Harike Wetland is located in Punjab. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 38-39]
Kabartal Lake is also called Kanwar Lake. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 38-39]
Kabartal/Kanwar Lake is located in Begusarai, Bihar. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 38-39]
East Kolkata Wetlands is located in West Bengal. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 38-39]
Sundarban Wetland is located in West Bengal. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 38-39]
xs: The **incorrect** statement is that the **Sundarban Wetland** is in **Odisha** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Sundarban Wetland** is in **West Bengal**.
**Harike** is in **Punjab**, **East Kolkata Wetlands** in **West Bengal**, **Kabartal (Kanwar Lake)** in **Begusarai, Bihar**.
xa: **Chilika Lake** is in **Odisha** — India's **first** Ramsar site (**1981**).
**Kolleru Lake** — **Andhra Pradesh**; **Loktak** — **Manipur**.
India has **101** Ramsar sites; latest: **Glaw Lake (Arunachal Pradesh)**.

80.s: Which of the following is consistent with the scope of sustainable development?
o: Running down natural capital to maximise current output
Excluding disadvantaged groups from development planning
Treating environmental protection and development as mutually exclusive
Meeting present needs while promoting equity within and across generations
80.x: Sustainable development includes meeting present needs, equity within and across generations, and inclusion. It rejects depletion of natural capital and the opposition of environment to development.
80.tq: Select the option that combines present needs, equity and inclusion.
xs: Sustainable development includes **meeting present needs** with **equity within and across generations** — option **(4)**.
It **excludes** growth that **runs down natural capital** and treating **environment and development as opposites**.
It also stresses **inclusion** ("**leave no one behind**"), so excluding disadvantaged groups is wrong.
xa: **NEP 2006**: conservation and livelihood security are **linked, not opposed**.
Present generation **may use** resources but must not **compromise** future generations.
First definition: **Brundtland 1987**.

80.s: The National Environment Policy, 2006 treats conservation and livelihood security as:
o: Objectives that cannot be pursued together
Objectives applicable only to urban areas
80.x: The National Environment Policy, 2006 holds that conservation and livelihood security are linked rather than opposed.
80.tq: Watch for the reversed comparison between conservation and livelihoods.
xs: **NEP 2006** treats conservation and livelihood security as **linked, not opposed** — option **(1)**.
This matches the scope of sustainable development, which excludes treating **environment and development as opposites**.
xa: Sustainable development includes meeting **present needs** — development is not rejected.
It excludes growth that **runs down natural capital**.
Pillars: **economic development, social equity, environmental protection**.

80.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three classic pillars of sustainable development?
80.x: The three classic pillars are economic development, social equity and environmental protection. Military security is not one of them.
80.tq: Identify the outsider from the standard three-pillar framework.
xs: **Military security** is not a classic pillar — option **(1)**.
The three pillars: **economic development**, **social equity**, **environmental protection**.
xa: ⚠ Odd-one-out trap: **political, military or cultural** dimensions are not pillars.
**Triple bottom line**: **People, Planet, Profit** — the business version.
The idea is to **balance all three**, not maximise any one.

80.s: In the business-oriented expression of sustainable development, the triple bottom line is represented by:
80.x: The triple bottom line is commonly expressed as People, Planet and Profit, corresponding broadly to social, environmental and economic concerns.
80.tq: Recall the exact three-part phrase used for the business version of sustainability.
xs: The **triple bottom line** = **People, Planet, Profit** — option **(1)**.
It is the **business version** of the three pillars: social, environmental, economic.
xa: Classic pillars: **economic development**, **social equity**, **environmental protection**.
The aim is **balance**, not maximising one.
⚠ Political, military or cultural dimensions are **not** pillars.

80.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Green Tribunal:
1. Its headquarters is at New Delhi.
2. It aims to dispose of cases within six months.
3. It has a bench at Hyderabad.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
80.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the NGT is headquartered at New Delhi and aims to dispose of cases within six months. Statement 3 is wrong: its benches are at Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata and Chennai, not Hyderabad. So the options containing 3 are wrong.
80.tq: NGT: HQ Delhi + Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata, Chennai; 6-month disposal.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
**Statement 1:** correct — HQ **New Delhi**; **Statement 2:** correct — disposal within **6 months**.
**Statement 3:** wrong — benches are at **Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata and Chennai**, not Hyderabad.
xa: It must apply **sustainable development**, **precautionary** and **polluter-pays** principles.
**M.C. Mehta v. UoI (1996)** applied polluter pays.
**Vellore (1996)** applied all three.

80.s: Which of the following correctly represents the first occurrence and the first definition associated with sustainable development in the stated international chronology?
80.x: The first Earth Summit was held at Rio in 1992, while the first definition is associated with the Brundtland Commission in 1987.
80.tq: Separate the event from the definition and pair each with its correct year.
xs: **First Earth Summit = Rio 1992**; **first definition = Brundtland 1987** — option **(1)**.
Options (2)-(4) swap the events and years.
xa: Rio **1992** (**UNCED**, **3-14 June**) gave **Agenda 21** and the **Rio Declaration** (**27 principles**).
PYQs here mostly ask **Stockholm, Rio, Brundtland and the SDGs**.
Rio+20 (**2012**) decided to frame the **SDGs**.

80.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The National Environment Policy was formulated in 2006 to provide a policy framework for environmental conservation and sustainable development.
Statement B: The Wetlands (Conservation & Management) Rules, 2010 were framed on the recommendation of an Expert Panel constituted under the provisions of the National Environment Policy, 2006.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
80.x: Both are true: the National Environment Policy (2006) frames conservation policy, and an expert panel under it led to the Wetlands Rules, 2010.
80.tq: Recall the NEP 2006 links.
n: The National Environment Policy was formulated in 2006. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
The National Environment Policy, 2006, provides the policy framework for environmental conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
The National Environment Policy, 2006, provides the policy framework for sustainable development. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
The Wetlands (Conservation & Management) Rules, 2010, were framed on the recommendation of an Expert Panel. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
The Expert Panel was constituted under the provisions of the National Environment Policy, 2006. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
xs: **Both statements are true** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement A: the **National Environment Policy, 2006** is the **policy framework** for **environmental conservation** and **sustainable development**.
Statement B: the **Wetlands (Conservation & Management) Rules, 2010** were framed on an **Expert Panel**'s recommendation under the **NEP 2006**.
xa: NEP 2006: **conservation** and **livelihood security** are **linked, not opposed**.
Sustainable development excludes **growth that runs down natural capital**.
The present generation **may use** resources, but not so as to **compromise** future generations.

80.s:
Arrange the following reports/declarations in chronological order:

A. Johannesburg Declaration
B. Stockholm Declaration
C. Rio Declaration on Environment & Development
D. Our Common Future (Brundtland Report)
80.x: The order is the Stockholm Declaration (1972), Our Common Future (1987), the Rio Declaration (1992) and the Johannesburg Declaration (2002). The answer is B, D, C, A.
80.tq: Arrange the declarations in time order.
n: The Stockholm Declaration was issued in 1972. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 70-71]
Our Common Future was published in 1987. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 70-71]
The Rio Declaration on Environment and Development was issued in 1992. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 70-71]
The Johannesburg Declaration was issued in 2002. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 70-71]
xs: The chronological order is **B, D, C, A** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Stockholm Declaration** (**1972**) → **Our Common Future / Brundtland Report** (**1987**).
→ **Rio Declaration** (**1992**) → **Johannesburg Declaration** (**2002**).
xa: **Millennium Declaration** (**2000**): the **MDGs framework**.
**The Future We Want** (**2012**): the **Rio+20 outcome document**.
First definition of sustainable development = **Brundtland 1987**.

80.s:
Consider the following statements about principles of sustainable development:
1. Intergenerational equity requires the present generation to avoid depleting resources at the cost of future generations.
2. The precautionary principle permits postponement of preventive action until complete scientific certainty is available.
3. The polluter pays principle places the cost of preventing and controlling pollution on the polluter.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
80.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The precautionary principle states that lack of full scientific certainty is no reason to postpone cost-effective preventive measures, making statement 2 false.
80.tq: Spot the statement that reverses the precautionary principle.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
**Statement 1:** correct — **intergenerational equity**: the present must not deplete resources at the cost of future generations.
**Statement 2:** wrong — the **precautionary principle** says lack of **full scientific certainty** is **no reason to postpone** preventive measures.
**Statement 3:** correct — **polluter pays**: the polluter bears the cost of preventing and controlling pollution.
xa: These principles were endorsed at **Rio 1992**.
**Vellore Citizens' Welfare Forum (1996)** made precaution and polluter pays part of Indian law.
**CBDR**: shared but differentiated duties; developed nations carry more.

80.s: The principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR) implies that:
o: Responsibilities are shared, but developed nations carry greater duties
Only developing countries bear responsibility for environmental protection
All countries have identical environmental duties and identical capacities
Environmental duties are restricted to countries that caused no historical pollution
80.x: CBDR recognises shared responsibility while assigning greater duties to developed nations in view of their capacities and historical contribution.
80.tq: Discriminate between shared responsibility and identical responsibility.
xs: **CBDR**: duties are **shared but differentiated**; **developed nations carry more** — option **(1)**.
So duties are neither identical for all nor placed only on developing countries.
xa: Other principles: **intergenerational equity**, **precautionary**, **polluter pays**, **carrying capacity**.
All were endorsed at **Rio 1992** and underpin international environmental law.
The **Rio Declaration** has **27 principles**.

80.s: The National Green Tribunal is required to apply which combination of principles while adjudicating environmental cases?
o: Sustainable development, precautionary principle and polluter-pays principle
Public trust doctrine, absolute liability and eminent domain
Common but differentiated responsibilities, prior appropriation and res judicata
Inter-generational equity, federal supremacy and parliamentary privilege
80.x: The NGT must apply the principles of sustainable development, precautionary action and polluter pays.
80.tq: Select the complete statutory-principle combination rather than a partly related doctrine.
xs: The NGT must apply **sustainable development**, **precautionary** and **polluter-pays** principles — option **(1)**.
The other combinations are not in its mandate.
xa: HQ **New Delhi**; benches **Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata, Chennai**.
Disposal within **6 months**.
**Vellore (1996)** brought these principles into Indian environmental law.

80.s: Which of the following was NOT an outcome associated with the 1992 United Nations Conference on Environment and Development?
80.x: The Future We Want was adopted at the 2012 Rio+20 Conference. Agenda 21, the Rio Declaration, the UNFCCC and the CBD were associated with the 1992 Earth Summit.
80.tq: Use the summit-outcome association to eliminate the later document.
xs: "**The Future We Want**" came from **Rio+20** (**2012**), not **UNCED 1992** — option **(3)**.
Rio **1992** gave **Agenda 21**, the **Rio Declaration** (**27 principles**), **UNFCCC**, **CBD** and **Forest Principles**.
xa: UNCED: **3-14 June 1992**, **Rio de Janeiro** — the **first Earth Summit**.
Rio+20 (**UNCSD**) also decided to frame the **SDGs** and stressed the **green economy**.
**WSSD 2002** (Johannesburg) gave the **Johannesburg Plan of Implementation**.

80.s: The Rio Declaration adopted at the 1992 Earth Summit contained how many principles?
80.x: The Rio Declaration contains 27 principles relating to environment and development.
80.tq: Separate the numerical details of the Rio Declaration from SDG figures.
xs: The **Rio Declaration** has **27 principles** — option **(3)**.
**17** is the number of **SDGs**; **169** the number of SDG **targets**.
xa: It was adopted at **UNCED**, **3-14 June 1992**, Rio de Janeiro.
Other Rio outputs: **Agenda 21**, **UNFCCC**, **CBD**, **Forest Principles**.
⚠ **17 - 169 - 232** = SDGs - targets - indicators.

80.s:
With reference to the 2012 United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development, consider the following statements:
1. It is popularly known as Rio+20.
2. It produced the document titled 'The Future We Want'.
3. It initiated the decision to frame the Sustainable Development Goals.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
80.x: All three statements are correct. The 2012 UNCSD at Rio de Janeiro was known as Rio+20, adopted The Future We Want and decided to frame the SDGs.
80.tq: Use the all-correct combination when the summit, document and institutional decision align.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**1:** **UNCSD 2012** is **Rio+20**; **2:** it produced "**The Future We Want**".
**3:** it decided to frame the **SDGs**.
xa: It was held in **June 2012** at **Rio de Janeiro**.
It also stressed the **green economy**.
The SDGs were adopted in **2015** at **New York**.

80.s: The document titled 'Transforming our World: the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development' contains:
80.x: The 2030 Agenda contains 17 Sustainable Development Goals and 169 targets. It is also associated with 232 indicators.
80.tq: Separate goals, targets and indicators rather than interchanging their figures.
xs: The **2030 Agenda** has **17 goals** and **169 targets** — option **(1)**.
**232** is the number of **indicators**, not targets; **27** is the Rio Declaration's principle count.
xa: ⚠ **17 - 169 - 232** = SDGs - targets - indicators.
Adopted **25 Sept 2015**, New York; in force **2016**.
**MDGs** (**2000-2015**) came before.

80.s:
Arrange the following milestones in chronological order:
A. Millennium Development Goals
B. Rio+20 Conference
C. World Summit on Sustainable Development at Johannesburg
D. Agenda 2030 and Sustainable Development Goals
80.x: The MDGs began in 2000, WSSD was held in 2002, Rio+20 in 2012 and Agenda 2030 was adopted in 2015.
80.tq: Use the first and last milestones, then place the 2002 and 2012 events between them.
xs: Order: **A, C, B, D** — option **(1)**.
xa: The MDGs ran **2000-2015**.
SDGs in force from **2016**.
Rio+20 made the **decision to frame the SDGs**.

80.s: The first World Conference on Environment was held at which place and in which year?
80.x: The first world conference on the environment was held at Stockholm in 1972 (UNCHE). Rio (1992) was the Earth Summit and Johannesburg (2002) Rio+10.
80.tq: Arrange the environment summits in time order.
n: The Stockholm Conference was the first World Conference on Environment. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
The Stockholm Conference was held in 1972. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
xs: The first **World Conference on Environment** was at **Stockholm** in **1972** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was the **UN Conference on Human Environment (UNCHE)** — the **origin** of **UNEP**.
**Rio de Janeiro, 1992** was the **Earth Summit**; **New York, 1997** was **Rio+5**; **Johannesburg, 2002** was **Rio+10 (WSSD)**.
xa: **Rio 1992** adopted **Agenda 21**, the **UNFCCC** and **CBD**, and the **Rio Declaration** (**27 principles**).
**Rio+20 (2012)** produced "**The Future We Want**".
**2015** UN summit: "**Transforming our World: the 2030 Agenda**" — **17 SDGs, 169 targets**.

80.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: UNEP originated from the Rio Earth Summit, 1992.
UNEP focuses on global environmental coordination.
The headquarters of UNEP is in Nairobi, Kenya.
80.x: Option B is incorrect: UNEP came out of the 1972 Stockholm Conference, not the 1992 Rio summit. It is headquartered in Nairobi.
80.tq: Match UNEP to the conference it came from.
n: The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) was established in 1972. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
The headquarters of UNEP is in Nairobi, Kenya. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
The origin of UNEP was the Stockholm Conference. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
UNEP is responsible for global environmental coordination. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
xs: The **incorrect** statement is that **UNEP** originated at the **Rio Earth Summit, 1992** — so option **(2)** is correct.
UNEP originated from the **Stockholm Conference (UNCHE), 1972**.
The other options are correct: UNEP was **established in 1972**, works on **global environmental coordination**, and is headquartered in **Nairobi, Kenya**.
xa: Stockholm **1972** was the **first major global environmental conference**, on the **Human Environment**.
Rio **1992** (UNCED) adopted **Agenda 21**, the **UNFCCC** and **CBD**.
The **Stockholm Declaration** (**1972**) concerns the **human environment**.

80.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Stockholm Conference as UNCHE
(b) Rio+5
(c) Rio+10
(d) Rio+20

List-II
(i) Rio de Janeiro, 2012
(ii) New York, 1997
(iii) Stockholm Conference, also called the UN Conference on Human Environment
(iv) Johannesburg, 2002
80.x: Stockholm was the UN Conference on the Human Environment, Rio+5 was held in New York (1997), Rio+10 in Johannesburg (2002), and Rio+20 in Rio (2012). The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
80.tq: Arrange the Rio follow-ups in time order.
n: The Stockholm Conference is also called the UN Conference on Human Environment (UNCHE). [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
Rio+5 was held in New York in 1997. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
Rio+10 was held in Johannesburg in 2002. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
Rio+20 was held in Rio de Janeiro in 2012. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Stockholm** — the **UN Conference on Human Environment (UNCHE)**; **Rio+5** — **New York, 1997**.
**Rio+10** — **Johannesburg, 2002** (**WSSD**); **Rio+20** — **Rio de Janeiro, 2012** (**UNCSD**).
xa: **Rio+5** **reviewed the progress** of the Rio Summit.
Rio+20 produced "**The Future We Want**" and decided to frame the **SDGs**.
Johannesburg gave the **Johannesburg Plan of Implementation**.

80.s:
Match the conferences in List-I with their year and key concern or designation in List-II:

List-I
 a. Stockholm conference
 b. Rio conference
 c. Kyoto conference
 d. Johannesburg conference

List-II
 i. 1972 — Human Environment
 ii. 1992 — UNCED or Earth Summit
 iii. 1997 — Climate change
 iv. 2002 — Sustainable development
80.x: Stockholm (1972) dealt with the human environment, Rio (1992) was the Earth Summit, Kyoto (1997) dealt with climate change, and Johannesburg (2002) with sustainable development. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
80.tq: Arrange the conferences in time order.
n: The Stockholm conference concerned the Human Environment. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The Rio conference was called UNCED or the Earth Summit. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The Kyoto conference was held in 1997. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The Kyoto conference concerned climate change. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The Johannesburg conference concerned sustainable development. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
xs: The correct match is **a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Stockholm** — **1972**, **Human Environment**; **Rio** — **1992**, **UNCED / Earth Summit**.
**Kyoto** — **1997**, **climate change**; **Johannesburg** — **2002**, **sustainable development** (WSSD).
xa: Rio **1992** was the **first Earth Summit**; it gave **Agenda 21**.
**Rio+5** was also in **1997**, in **New York**.
⚠ **17 - 169 - 232** = SDGs - targets - indicators.

80.s:
Consider the following statements:

I. Agenda 21 is a global action plan for sustainable development.
II. The Forest Principles concern the sustainable management of forests.
III. The Future We Want was the 2000 outcome document of Rio+20.
IV. The Millennium Declaration provided the framework for the MDGs.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
80.x: I, II and IV are correct: Agenda 21 is the action plan, the Forest Principles cover forests, and the Millennium Declaration set up the MDGs. III is false because 'The Future We Want' came out of Rio+20 in 2012.
80.tq: Match each document to its year.
n: Agenda 21 is a global action plan for sustainable development. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 70-71]
The Forest Principles concern the sustainable management of forests. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 70-71]
The Future We Want was issued in 2012. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 70-71]
The Future We Want is the Rio+20 outcome document. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 70-71]
The Millennium Declaration provides the MDGs framework. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 70-71]
xs: Statements **I, II and IV** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
I: **Agenda 21** is a **global action plan** for **sustainable development**; II: the **Forest Principles** concern **sustainable management of forests**.
IV: the **Millennium Declaration** (**2000**) provided the **MDGs framework**.
III is wrong: **The Future We Want** was the **Rio+20 outcome document** of **2012**, not 2000.
xa: **Agenda 21** was adopted in **1992**, for local, national and global levels.
The **MDGs (2000-2015)** preceded the SDGs.
**Johannesburg Declaration** (**2002**): **WSSD** — implementation commitments.

80.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Our Common Future
(b) Rio Declaration on Environment and Development
(c) Agenda 21
(d) Forest Principles

List-II
(i) Defined sustainable development as meeting present needs without compromising future generations
(ii) 27 principles on environment and development

SDG 14 is Life Below Water. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 20-21]
SDG 15 is Life on Land. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 20-21]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**SDG 11** — **Sustainable Cities & Communities**; **SDG 12** — **Responsible Consumption & Production**.
**SDG 14** — **Life Below Water**; **SDG 15** — **Life on Land**.
xa: **SDG 13** — **Climate Action**; **SDG 16** — **Peace, Justice & Strong Institutions**.
SDG **11** schemes: **Smart Cities Mission**, **AMRUT**.
SDG **13** scheme: **NAPCC** and its eight missions.

81.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (SDG)

**SDG 3** → **Ayushman Bharat**; **SDG 4** → **Samagra Shiksha**.

81.s: Which of the following is associated with SDG 13, Climate Action, in India?
o: National Action Plan on Climate Change and its eight missions
National Food Security Act and POSHAN Abhiyaan
81.x: India’s National Action Plan on Climate Change, comprising eight missions, is associated with SDG 13.
81.tq: Match the goal with the policy package designed for its subject area.
xs: **SDG 13 (Climate Action)** maps to the **NAPCC** and its **eight missions** — option **(3)**.
**Samagra Shiksha/PM POSHAN** → SDG 4; **Smart Cities/AMRUT** → SDG 11; **NFSA/POSHAN Abhiyaan** → SDG 2.
