87.tq: Start from the sure species–centre pair and match the remaining pairs.
xs: Correct code: **a–iii, b–ii, c–i** — option **(1)**.
**Vultures** — **Jatayu** Conservation Breeding Centre, **Pinjore**, Haryana (BNHS).
**Great Indian Bustard** — **Sam and Ramdevra**, **Jaisalmer** (with WII); **red panda** — **Padmaja Naidu** Himalayan ZP, **Darjeeling**.
xa: **GIB** is **Critically Endangered**, population **<150**.
Breeding programmes (2026): **Snow Leopard**, **Asiatic Lion**, **GIB**.
The **CZA** coordinates planned conservation breeding.

87.s: The 2024 Supreme Court order relating to the habitat of the Great Indian Bustard mandated which measure?
o: Conversion of the habitat into a marine reserve
87.x: The 2024 Supreme Court order mandated underground power lines in the Great Indian Bustard’s habitat to reduce threats to the species.
87.tq: Match the judicial order with its precise conservation measure.
xs: The **2024 SC order** mandated **underground power lines** in the GIB's habitat — option **(3)**.
The order did not relocate villages, ban research or create a marine reserve.
xa: The **GIB (Godawan)** is **Critically Endangered**, population **<150**.
Conservation breeding: **Sam and Ramdevra**, **Jaisalmer**.
It is one of the 2026 breeding programmes, with **Snow Leopard** and **Asiatic Lion**.

87.s: Which one of the following correctly compares in-situ and ex-situ conservation?
o: In-situ conserves only genes, whereas ex-situ conserves complete ecosystems in nature.
In-situ protects the whole ecosystem, whereas ex-situ primarily conserves the species or its genes outside the natural habitat.
Ex-situ is used only for landscapes, whereas in-situ is used only for laboratories.
Both methods necessarily conserve the whole ecosystem in its original location.
87.x: In-situ conservation protects species along with their ecological setting, while ex-situ conservation focuses mainly on species or genetic material outside the natural habitat.
87.tq: Use the level of conservation—ecosystem versus species or genes—to distinguish the two methods.
xs: **In-situ protects the whole ecosystem**; **ex-situ saves the species or its genes only** — option **(2)**.
Options (1) and (3) reverse the roles; option (4) is wrong because ex-situ cannot save the ecosystem.
xa: In-situ is the **most effective** method — it keeps species interactions intact.
Ex-situ = **off-site**: zoos, botanical gardens, seed and gene banks, cryopreservation.
PYQ: "not an in-situ site" = **Botanical Garden**.

87.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. National Parks are examples of in-situ conservation.
II. Seed Banks are examples of ex-situ conservation.
III. Sacred Groves are examples of ex-situ conservation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
87.x: I and II are correct: national parks are in-situ conservation and seed banks ex-situ. III is false because sacred groves protect species where they live, so they are in-situ.
87.tq: Ask whether the species stays in its own habitat.
n: A national park is an example of in-situ conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
A sacred grove is an example of in-situ conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
A seed bank is an example of ex-situ conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
xs: Statements **I and II** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
I: **national parks** are **in-situ** — conservation **within the natural habitat**.
II: **seed banks** are **ex-situ** — conservation **outside** the natural habitat.
III is wrong: **sacred groves** are **in-situ**.
xa: **In-situ** is the **most effective** method — keeps species interacting with their environment.
Ex-situ also includes **pollen banks**, **tissue culture banks** and **cryopreservation**.
Sacred groves are a **traditional method of conserving tree cover** (e.g. **Devrai** — Maharashtra; **Kavu** — Kerala).

87.s:
How many of the following are examples of in-situ conservation?
I. Wildlife sanctuary
II. Biosphere reserve
III. Reserved forest
IV. Protected forest
V. Nature reserve
VI. Botanical garden
87.x: Five are in-situ: wildlife sanctuary, biosphere reserve, reserved forest, protected forest and nature reserve. A botanical garden is ex-situ.
87.tq: Ask whether the species stays in its own habitat.
n: In-situ conservation occurs within the natural habitat. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
A wildlife sanctuary is an example of in-situ conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
A biosphere reserve is an example of in-situ conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
A reserved forest is an example of in-situ conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
A protected forest is an example of in-situ conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
A nature reserve is an example of in-situ conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
xs: **Only five** are in-situ — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Wildlife sanctuary**, **biosphere reserve**, **reserved forest**, **protected forest** and **nature reserve** are **in-situ**.
A **botanical garden** is **ex-situ** — "not an in-situ site" (PYQ).
xa: Other in-situ sites: **tiger reserve**, **sacred grove**, **community reserve**, **gene sanctuary**, **OECM**.
Ex-situ: **zoological park**, **seed bank**, **gene bank**, **cryobank**.
Ex-situ limits: needs space and money; **cannot save the ecosystem**.

87.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. A botanical garden is an example of ex-situ conservation.
II. A zoological park is an example of ex-situ conservation.
III. A gene bank is an example of ex-situ conservation.
IV. A zoological park is an example of in-situ conservation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
87.x: I, II and III are correct: botanical gardens, zoos and gene banks are ex-situ. IV is false because a zoo removes animals from their habitat.
87.tq: Ask whether the species stays in its own habitat.
n: A botanical garden is an example of ex-situ conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
A zoological park is an example of ex-situ conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
A gene bank is an example of ex-situ conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
xs: Statements **I, II and III** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Botanical gardens**, **zoological parks** and **gene banks** are **ex-situ** — outside the natural habitat, in a **controlled environment**.
IV is wrong: a **zoological park** is **ex-situ**, not in-situ.
xa: Ex-situ value: **education**, **research**, **reintroduction**.
**Captive breeding**: for species whose habitat is permanently lost — e.g. **Gangetic gharial** reintroduced.
The **National Gene Bank** of **ICAR-NBPGR**, **New Delhi**, was set up in **1996**.

87.s: Which of the following is an example of ex-situ conservation?
87.x: A cryobank stores seeds, sperm or tissue frozen outside the habitat, so it is ex-situ. Sanctuaries, biosphere reserves and national parks are in-situ.
87.tq: Ask whether the species stays in its own habitat.
n: A cryobank is an example of ex-situ conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
xs: A **cryobank** is **ex-situ** conservation — so option **(2)** is correct.
It stores material **outside** the natural habitat, in a **controlled environment**.
**Wildlife sanctuary**, **biosphere reserve** and **national park** are **in-situ**.
xa: **Cryopreservation** stores gametes and embryos in **liquid nitrogen at -196°C** (APPSC **2021** key).
**LaCONES** at **CSIR-CCMB, Hyderabad** is India's **frozen zoo**.
**Svalbard Global Seed Vault** (**Norway**) is the world's **largest seed bank**.

87.s: Meristem culture is particularly useful in ex-situ conservation because it enables:
o: Conversion of a Community Reserve into a National Park
Protection of animals in a wildlife sanctuary
Natural pollination in a protected forest
87.x: Meristem culture is a tissue-culture technique used for virus-free propagation of plants.
87.tq: Associate the specialised biotechnology term with its direct application rather than with a protected-area category.
xs: **Meristem culture** allows **virus-free propagation** of plants — option **(2)**.
It is part of **tissue culture banks**, an **ex-situ** method.
Converting reserves, protecting animals in sanctuaries and natural pollination are **in-situ** matters, not meristem culture.
xa: Disease-free **meristems** can also be stored by **cryopreservation** in **liquid nitrogen at -196°C**.
Other ex-situ tools: **pollen banks**, **captive breeding**, **animal translocation**, **in-vitro fertilisation**.
A **gene bank** stores germplasm under controlled temperature and humidity; each sample = an **accession**.

87.s: Which one of the following is NOT a protected area category under the Wildlife (Protection) Act framework?
87.x: The four protected area categories are National Park, Wildlife Sanctuary, Conservation Reserve and Community Reserve. Biosphere Reserve is not included in this four-category classification.
87.tq: Find the one item outside the legally specified group.
xs: **Biosphere Reserve** is not one of the four PA types under the Act — option **(3)**.
The four PA types: **sanctuary, national park, conservation reserve, community reserve**.
BRs rest on **UNESCO MAB recognition** and do not change the land's legal status.
xa: **Conservation reserve** and **community reserve** were added in **2002**.
**Tiger reserves** are notified under the **NTCA chapter**.
India has **18 BRs**, about **91,425.11 sq km**.

87.s:
Arrange the following protected-area categories in the order in which they were introduced into the statutory classification, beginning with the categories existing earlier:
A. Community Reserve
B. Wildlife Sanctuary
C. Conservation Reserve
D. National Park
87.x: Wildlife Sanctuary and National Park were the earlier categories. Conservation Reserve and Community Reserve were added in 2002, giving the sequence B, D, C, A.
87.tq: Separate the two earlier categories from the two categories added in 2002.
xs: Correct order: **B, D, C, A** — option **(2)**.
**Wildlife Sanctuary** and **National Park** came earlier, under the **WPA 1972**.
**Conservation reserve** and **community reserve** were added later, by the **2002** amendment.
xa: ⚠ Conservation reserve = **government land**; community reserve = **private/community land**.
⚠ **Amchang** and **Bhagwan Mahavir** are cited as community reserves but are notified as **wildlife sanctuaries**.
West Bengal is planning the **first community reserve for the Gangetic dolphin**.

87.s: An Other Effective Area-based Conservation Measure (OECM) is best described as:
o: A temporary area protected only during a breeding season
An ex-situ facility for storing genetic material
An area outside the formal protected-area network that delivers long-term in-situ conservation outcomes
A formally notified National Park with the highest legal protection
87.x: An OECM is outside the formal protected-area network but delivers long-term in-situ conservation outcomes and is recognised on the basis of its results.
87.tq: Use the outside-the-network distinction to separate OECMs from formal protected areas.
xs: An **OECM** is a CBD-defined area **outside the formal PA network** that delivers **long-term in-situ conservation** — option **(3)**.
It is recognised for its **outcomes**, not as a notified National Park.
xa: It **confers no legal, financial or management authority** — land ownership does not change.
**4 criteria**: outside the PA network, demarcated, inclusive governance, lasting benefits.
**India's first OECM**: **Aravalli Biodiversity Park, Gurugram (2022)**.
**APSBB** plans OECMs in sacred groves, greenbelts and wetlands to help meet **30x30**.

87.s: An Eco-sensitive Zone (ESZ) around a National Park or Wildlife Sanctuary is best understood as a
o: shock absorber and transition zone between high protection and areas where some development may be allowed
strictly urbanised buffer for industrial development
zone where all forms of human activity are permanently prohibited
separate category of biosphere reserve administered by UNESCO
87.x: An ESZ functions as a shock absorber around a protected area, providing a transition from high protection to areas where regulated development may be permitted.
87.tq: Distinguish the transition-zone concept from absolute protection and unrestricted development.
xs: An **ESZ** is a **"shock absorber"** / transition zone from high protection to areas where development may be permitted — option **(1)**.
ESZs have **prohibited, regulated and permitted** activities — not a total ban and not an industrial buffer.
ESZs are notified by **MoEF&CC**, not UNESCO.
xa: Legal basis: **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986** — ⚠ not the WPA 1972.
**MoEF's 2011 guidelines** allow an ESZ **up to 10 km**.
Prohibited in ESZs: **commercial mining**, **quarrying**, **polluting industries**, **major hydro projects**.

87.s: Projects affecting wildlife in or around protected areas require clearance from the
o: Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife
87.x: Projects affecting wildlife require clearance from the Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife (NBWL).
87.tq: Identify the authority by matching the function—wildlife project clearance—with the competent statutory body.
xs: Projects affecting wildlife are vetted by the **Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife (NBWL)** — option **(1)**.
The notes name no role here for a State Biodiversity Board, NDMA or CPCB.
xa: **National Park** boundaries can be altered only on **NBWL** recommendation.
Mining **within 10 km of wetland conservation reserves** also needs wildlife clearance.
SC: mining impermissible **within 1 km** of every NP/WLS.

87.s: Which one of the following sets contains only activities classified as REGULATED in an Eco-sensitive Zone?
o: Tree felling, hotels and resorts, road widening
Ongoing agriculture, organic farming, rainwater harvesting
Major hydro projects, commercial mining, ongoing agriculture
87.x: Tree felling, hotels and resorts, and road widening are regulated activities. Commercial mining and major hydro projects are prohibited, while ongoing agriculture, organic farming and rainwater harvesting are permitted.
87.tq: Use category elimination by checking whether each activity belongs to the same regulatory class.
xs: **Tree felling, hotels and resorts, road widening** are **regulated** in an ESZ — option **(1)**.
**Commercial mining, quarrying, polluting industries** and **major hydro projects** are **prohibited**.
**Ongoing agriculture, organic farming, rainwater harvesting** are **permitted**.
xa: ESZ = **"shock absorber"** around an NP or sanctuary.
Notified by **MoEF&CC** under the **EP Act, 1986**.
ESZ width: **up to 10 km** (2011 guidelines).

87.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Biosphere Reserve)
a. Nilgiri
b. Nanda Devi
c. Sundarbans
 d. Manas

xs: Correct code: **a–ii, b–iv, c–iii, d–i** — option **(1)**.

**Sundarbans** — **Sundarbans NP**; **Manas** — **Manas WLS**.

87.s: Which one of the following pairs of National Park and State is correctly matched?
o: Silent Valley National Park - Tamil Nadu
Valley of Flowers National Park - Himachal Pradesh
87.x: Silent Valley National Park (tropical evergreen forest) is in Palakkad, Kerala. Valley of Flowers is in Chamoli, Uttarakhand, not Himachal; Keibul Lamjao is in Manipur, not Meghalaya; Silent Valley is not in Tamil Nadu.

xs: **Silent Valley NP** is in **Kerala** (Palakkad) — option **(3)**.
**Valley of Flowers** is in **Uttarakhand** (Chamoli), not Himachal.
**Keibul Lamjao** is in **Manipur**, not Meghalaya; Silent Valley is not in Tamil Nadu.
xa: Silent Valley = **tropical evergreen forest**.
Valley of Flowers forms a **UNESCO WHS** with **Nanda Devi**.
**Yasuni NP** (Ecuador): voters rejected oil drilling in a referendum (RPSC **2023**).

87.s: Sacred groves are best described as forest tracts that are primarily preserved by communities on the basis of
o: religious beliefs, with trees and wildlife being venerated
87.x: Sacred groves are forest patches preserved by communities on religious grounds, where trees and wildlife are traditionally venerated.
87.tq: Identify the defining purpose rather than a merely associated land-use activity.
xs: Sacred groves are forest tracts preserved by communities on **religious grounds**, with **all trees and wildlife venerated** — option **(4)**.
They are community-kept, not timber or shifting-cultivation land, and not exclusively government-owned.
xa: PYQ: sacred groves = a **traditional method of conserving tree cover**.
They are an **in-situ** method, like **sacred lakes**.
Local names: **Devrai** (Maharashtra), **Kavu** (Kerala), **Orans** (Rajasthan), **Sarna** (Jharkhand).

87.s: Papikonda National Park primarily protects the:
o: mangrove forests of the Krishna delta
87.x: Papikonda National Park protects the Papikondalu ranges situated along the Godavari River.
87.tq: Associate the protected area with its defining landscape and river.
xs: **Papikonda NP** protects the **Papikondalu ranges on the Godavari** (Godavari gorge) — option **(4)**.
Nallamala tiger habitat is **NSTR**; the Tirupati hills belong to **Seshachalam**.
xa: Papikonda was the release site of a tiger that walked **650+ km** from **Tadoba** (Jul 2026).
⚠ A "Papikondalu Tiger Reserve" in some notes is wrong — **NSTR** is AP's only TR.
AP has **3 NPs** and **13 WLS**.

87.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

a. National Botanical Garden of CSIR-NBRI
b. Lloyd Botanical Garden
c. Government Botanical Garden
d. Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

List-II (Location)

87.x: The National Botanical Garden of CSIR-NBRI is at Lucknow, Lloyd Botanical Garden at Darjeeling, Government Botanical Garden at Ooty and Kew at London.
87.tq: Begin with the international Kew–London pair and then complete the three Indian location matches.
xs: Correct code: **a–ii, b–iv, c–i, d–iii** — option **(1)**.
**CSIR-NBRI** — **Lucknow**; **Lloyd** — **Darjeeling**; **Government Botanical Garden** — **Ooty**; **Kew** — **London**.
xa: NBRI's **Banthara** station holds a **field gene bank**.
**Indian Botanic Garden** (Great Banyan) is at **Shibpur, Howrah**.

87.s: The National Medicinal Plants Board (NMPB), established in 2000, functions under which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
87.x: The NMPB was established in 2000 under the Ministry of AYUSH and promotes the cultivation and conservation of medicinal plants.
87.tq: Use the establishment year and ministry pairing to distinguish the board from environmental bodies.
xs: The **National Medicinal Plants Board (2000)** is under the **Ministry of AYUSH** — option **(2)**.
It promotes **cultivation and conservation** of medicinal plants.
⚠ The **CZA** is under **MoEF&CC** — do not confuse.
xa: **Phyto-Pharma Plant Mission** is a **CSIR** mission.
**BD Rules 2024** encourage **cultivated** medicinal plants.
NBA/SBB approvals now take **90 days** (**180** for IPR).

87.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the position of human rights and grazing in the three categories of protected areas?
o: Settlements are prohibited in every zone of a Biosphere Reserve; National Parks permit grazing; Wildlife Sanctuaries permit unrestricted grazing.
National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries provide identical rights, while Biosphere Reserves permit no settlements.
Settlements are allowed in the transition zone of a Biosphere Reserve; National Parks permit no rights or grazing; grazing in a Wildlife Sanctuary is regulated by the Chief Wildlife Warden.
Settlements are allowed throughout National Parks; Biosphere Reserves prohibit all human use; grazing in Wildlife Sanctuaries is regulated by UNESCO.
87.x: Settlements may exist in the transition zone of a Biosphere Reserve. National Parks provide no rights and no grazing, while some rights exist in sanctuaries and grazing is regulated by the Chief Wildlife Warden.
87.tq: Compare the authorities and the degree of human-use restriction rather than treating all protected areas alike.
xs: BRs allow **settlements in the transition zone**; NPs allow **no rights, no grazing**; sanctuary grazing is **regulated by the Chief Wildlife Warden** — option **(3)**.
NPs and sanctuaries do not give identical rights — sanctuaries allow **some rights**.
xa: NP boundaries change only on **NBWL** recommendation.
A BR does not change **land ownership**.
Sanctuaries regulate human activity but **permit it to an extent**.

87.s: Anamalai Tiger Reserve is associated with which of the following conservation firsts?
87.x: Anamalai is associated with India's first Hornbill Conservation Centre.
87.tq: Use the named-site and named-facility association to avoid swapping the conservation firsts.
xs: **Anamalai** is India's **first Hornbill Conservation Centre** (2026) — option **(2)**.
First OECM = **Aravalli Biodiversity Park**; first dugong reserve = **Palk Bay**; first marine BR = **Gulf of Mannar**.
xa: Palk Bay's dugong reserve covers **448 sq km**.
Aravalli Biodiversity Park (**2022**) is a restored mining site.
First community reserve: **Keshopur-Chhamb (Punjab)**.

87.s:
Consider the following statements regarding National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries:
I. Hunting is completely prohibited in National Parks.
II. Hunting in Wildlife Sanctuaries is prohibited without permission.
III. Cattle grazing is completely prohibited in National Parks.
IV. Grazing of livestock may be permitted in National Parks by the Chief Wildlife Warden.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
87.x: I, II and III are correct: hunting and grazing are fully banned in national parks, and hunting in sanctuaries needs permission. IV is false because livestock grazing cannot be permitted in a national park; it may be regulated only in sanctuaries.
87.tq: Contrast what may be regulated in sanctuaries with what is barred in national parks.
n: Hunting in a Wildlife Sanctuary is prohibited without permission. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
Hunting in a National Park is completely prohibited. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
Cattle grazing is completely prohibited in a National Park. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
No human activity is permitted in a National Park except activity permitted by the Chief Wildlife Warden. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
A protected animal may not be hunted normally. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
xs: Statements **I, II and III** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
I: **hunting** is **completely prohibited** in **National Parks**; II: in **Wildlife Sanctuaries** it is **prohibited without permission**.
III: **cattle grazing** is **completely prohibited** in National Parks.
IV is wrong: grazing is **not** permitted in a National Park; in a sanctuary grazing is **regulated by the Chief Wildlife Warden**.
xa: Both are under the **Wildlife Protection Act, 1972**.
NP boundaries can be altered only on **NBWL** recommendation.
A **Biosphere reserve** allows **settlements** in the transition zone.

87.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the formation of a Community Reserve:
I. Land already designated as a National Park cannot form a Community Reserve.
II. Land already designated as a Wildlife Sanctuary cannot form a Community Reserve.
III. Land already designated as a Conservation Reserve cannot form a Community Reserve.
IV. A Community Reserve is declared by the State Government.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
87.x: All four are correct: land already under a national park, sanctuary or conservation reserve cannot become a community reserve, and the State Government declares it.
87.tq: Recall the community reserve rules.
n: Land already designated as a National Park cannot form a Community Reserve. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
Land already designated as a Wildlife Sanctuary cannot form a Community Reserve. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
Land already designated as a Conservation Reserve cannot form a Community Reserve. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
A Community Reserve is declared by the State Government. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
xs: **All four** statements — **I, II, III and IV** — are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
I, II, III: a **Community Reserve** cannot be formed on land already a **National Park**, **Wildlife Sanctuary** or **Conservation Reserve**.
IV: it is **declared** by the **State Government**, on **private** or **community land**.
xa: Community Reserve = **Section 36C**; added by the **2002** amendment.
⚠ Conservation reserve = **government land**; community reserve = **private/community land**.
First community reserve: **Keshopur-Chhamb (Punjab)**.

87.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The purpose of a Community Reserve is the conservation of fauna and flora.
Statement B: A Community Reserve conserves traditional and cultural values.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
87.x: Both are true: a community reserve conserves plants and animals as well as traditional and cultural values.
87.tq: Recall the aims of community reserves.
n: The purpose of a Community Reserve is the conservation of fauna and flora. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
A Community Reserve conserves traditional and cultural values. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
xs: **Both statements are true** — so option **(1)** is correct.
A Community Reserve is declared for the **conservation** of **fauna and flora**.
It also conserves **traditional and cultural values**.
xa: The State declares it when a **community volunteers**.
It is run by a **CRMC** (Community Reserve Management Committee).
Four PA types: **sanctuary, national park, conservation reserve, community reserve**.

87.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Cattle grazing is regular or allowed in a Wildlife Sanctuary.
Statement B: Some human activities are permitted in a Wildlife Sanctuary as restricted activities.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
87.x: Both are true: in a wildlife sanctuary, grazing and some other human activities are allowed under rules, unlike in a national park.
87.tq: Discriminate national parks from sanctuaries.
n: Cattle grazing is regular or allowed in a Wildlife Sanctuary. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
Some human activities are permitted in a Wildlife Sanctuary as restricted activities. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
xs: **Both statements are true** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement A: in a **Wildlife Sanctuary**, **cattle grazing** is **regular / allowed**.
Statement B: **some** human activities are permitted as **restricted activities**.
xa: In a **National Park**, grazing and hunting are **completely prohibited**; no human activity except as permitted by the **Chief Wildlife Warden**.
⚠ Other notes say sanctuary grazing is **regulated** by the Chief Wildlife Warden.
India has **109 NPs** and **573 WLS** (**2026**).

87.s: Which one of the following is NOT a limitation of ex-situ conservation?
o: Maintaining captive populations can be resource-intensive.
It may support education, research and reintroduction.
It cannot by itself save the entire ecosystem.
It requires considerable space and money.
87.x: Education, research and reintroduction are values of ex-situ conservation, not limitations. Space and financial requirements, as well as inability to save the whole ecosystem, are limitations.
87.tq: Separate benefits from limitations before selecting the exception.
xs: **Education, research and reintroduction** are the **values** of ex-situ conservation, not its limits — option **(2)**.
The notes list the limits: ex-situ **needs space and money** and **cannot save the ecosystem**.
Keeping captive populations is resource-intensive — the same point as space and money.
xa: Ex-situ = **off-site** conservation away from the natural habitat.
In-situ protects the **whole ecosystem**; ex-situ saves only the species or its genes.
**Cryopreservation** keeps gametes and embryos viable for **decades or centuries**.

87.s: Which organisation maintains the World Database on Protected Areas (WDPA) in collaboration with IUCN?
87.x: The WDPA is run by UNEP-WCMC, based in Cambridge, in collaboration with IUCN, and tracks progress towards the 30x30 target.
87.tq: Use the institutional-identity trap by distinguishing UNEP-WCMC from neighbouring UN bodies.
xs: The **WDPA** is run by **UNEP-WCMC**, Cambridge, with **IUCN** — option **(1)**.
It **tracks 30x30 progress**.
xa: WDPA data (Apr 2026): nearly **10% of the ocean** protected; only **1.66% of the high seas**.
In **2014**, PAs covered **15.2% of land** and **8.4%** of coastal and marine areas.
Marine protection must **triple by 2030**.

87.s:
Consider the following statements about the zonation of a biosphere reserve:
1. The core zone is legally protected, usually as a National Park or sanctuary, and allows only conservation and monitoring.
2. The transition zone permits settlements, agriculture, forestry and tourism.
3. The buffer zone is the outer interface where settlements, farming and tourism are concentrated.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
87.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the buffer zone surrounds the core and allows regulated activities such as research, education, training, eco-restoration and limited recreation; settlements, farming and tourism belong to the transition zone, the outer interface. So '1 and 2 only'.
87.tq: Core = no human use; buffer = research and eco-restoration; transition = people.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the **core** is **legally protected** (usually an NP or sanctuary), with **conservation and monitoring only**.
Statement 2 is correct: the **transition** zone permits **settlements, farming, forestry and tourism**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **buffer** **surrounds the core** with **regulated activities** — research, education, training, eco-restoration, limited recreation.
xa: **Seville Strategy (1995)** added social, cultural and economic needs and **community participation**.
Funding: **CSS "Biodiversity Conservation"** — **60:40**, and **90:10** for NE and Himalayan States.
UNESCO criteria include a **management authority** involving local communities.

87.s: With reference to the boundaries of protected areas, which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: National Park — boundaries are not clearly demarcated
Biosphere Reserve — zoned into core, buffer and transition areas
Biosphere Reserve — only a single undivided core zone
Wildlife Sanctuary — boundaries are always strictly specified
87.x: A Biosphere Reserve is organised into core, buffer and transition zones. National Parks are clearly demarcated, whereas sanctuary boundaries are not strictly specified.
87.tq: Match each category with its distinctive boundary characteristic and reject reversed comparisons.
xs: A **BR** is zoned into **core, buffer and transition** areas — option **(2)**.
**NPs** are **clearly demarcated**, so option (1) is wrong.
**Sanctuary** boundaries are **not strictly specified**, so option (4) is wrong.
xa: The **core** is usually an NP or sanctuary under the **WPA 1972**.
The **buffer** allows research, education, eco-restoration.
The **transition zone** holds settlements, farming, tourism.

87.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a major criticism or pressure affecting protected areas?
o: Complete absence of human pressure in protected landscapes
Evictions and conflicts in certain Biosphere Reserves
87.x: Protected areas face human pressure rather than its absence. The stated concerns include inadequate funding and staffing, land grabbers, poachers, miners and eviction-related conflicts.
87.tq: Look for the absolute reversal of the documented criticism.
xs: PAs face **human pressure**, so "**complete absence of human pressure**" is not a criticism — option **(1)**.
Real criticisms: PAs are **small, underfunded, short-staffed**; they face **land-grabbers, poachers, miners**.
**Evictions in Agasthyamalai** and ESZ width versus mining are listed debates.
xa: A **growing share of tigers** now lives **outside reserves**.
Only **5.32%** of India's area is under PAs.
The **SC ordered eviction of encroachers** from Agasthyamalai BR (Jun 2026).

87.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of an OECM?
o: Recognition automatically changes land ownership and confers new legal authority.
It is demarcated and has inclusive governance.
It is outside the formal protected-area network.
87.x: Recognition of an OECM is outcome-based and does not change land ownership or confer new legal, financial or management authority. The other three are among its criteria.
87.tq: Look for the statement that reverses the no-new-authority feature of an OECM.
xs: OECM recognition does **not** change land ownership or confer legal authority — so option **(1)** is not a feature.
An OECM **confers no legal, financial or management authority**; it is recognised for its **outcomes**.
Options (2), (3) and (4) are among its **4 criteria**: outside PA network, demarcated, inclusive governance, lasting benefits.
xa: OECM = **Other Effective Area-based Conservation Measure**, defined by the **CBD**.
**India's first OECM**: **Aravalli Biodiversity Park, Gurugram (2022)**, a restored mining site.
India's PA share of **5.32%** means **30x30** needs OECMs.

87.s: Which of the following correctly describes the funding pattern for biosphere reserves?
o: 100 per cent central funding for all biosphere reserves
60:40 for the North-Eastern States, and 90:10 for all other States
90:10 for the North-Eastern and three Himalayan States, and 60:40 for other States
87.x: The funding pattern is 90:10 for the North-Eastern States and three Himalayan States, and 60:40 for other States.
87.tq: Compare the two funding ratios with the regional categories.
xs: BR funding: **90:10** for **North-Eastern and three Himalayan States**, **60:40** for others — option **(3)**.
Option (2) reverses the ratios.
Funding comes through the **CSS "Biodiversity Conservation"**, implemented by the **State Forest Department**.
xa: Umbrella scheme: **Conservation of Natural Resources and Ecosystems**.
**Integrated Management Plans**: five years, in four BRs, since **FY 2022-23**.
States prepare **Management Action Plans**; the **IN-MAB Committee** recommends sites.

87.s: Which of the following is NOT a criterion associated with UNESCO's Biosphere Reserve framework?
o: A management authority involving local or tribal communities
Viable populations representing all trophic levels in the core
An effectively protected and minimally disturbed core
Compulsory transfer of land ownership to UNESCO
87.x: UNESCO's criteria include a protected core, viable populations across trophic levels and participatory management. Transfer of land ownership to UNESCO is not a criterion.
87.tq: Find the option that confuses international designation with ownership or administration.
xs: **Compulsory transfer of land ownership to UNESCO** is not a BR criterion — option **(4)**.
A BR **does not change legal status or ownership** of land.
Real criteria: a **minimally disturbed core** with **all trophic levels**, and a **management authority** involving local communities.
xa: The **Seville Strategy (1995)** added social, cultural, economic needs and **community participation**.
BRs are designated under UNESCO's **MAB Programme** (**1971**).
BRs are **nominated by national governments**.

87.s: Biosphere Reserves are designated under the Man and the Biosphere (MAB) Programme, an intergovernmental programme launched in 1971 by:
87.x: The MAB Programme, launched in 1971, is a UNESCO programme, and Biosphere Reserves were started by UNESCO, not IUCN. IUCN deals with the Red List and PA categories, UNEP with the environment programme and WDPA (via UNEP-WCMC), and WWF is an NGO.
87.tq: MAB = UNESCO, 1971.
xs: The **MAB Programme** (launched **1971**) is a **UNESCO** programme — option **(3)**.
BRs were started by **UNESCO, not IUCN**.
**UNEP** runs the **WDPA** through **UNEP-WCMC**; **WWF** publishes the Living Planet Report.
xa: ⚠ Some keys give **1972** (RPSC 2013) or **1973-74**.
India's first BR: **Nilgiri (1986)**; first Indian entry in the WNBR (**2000**).
**13** of India's **18** BRs are in UNESCO's **WNBR**.

87.s: Which one of the following is correctly associated with the Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve?
o: It is India’s first marine Biosphere Reserve in Tamil Nadu
It is India’s first high-altitude cold desert site in the WNBR and includes Lahaul-Spiti
It is located in the Nilgiri Hills and was included in 1986
It is located in the Sundarbans and is known primarily for mangroves
87.x: Cold Desert is in Lahaul-Spiti and includes areas such as Pin Valley National Park, Kibber Wildlife Sanctuary and Chandratal. It is India’s first high-altitude cold desert site in the WNBR.
87.tq: Distinguish the landscape type and location from marine, mangrove and Western Ghats reserves.
xs: Cold Desert is **India's first high-altitude cold desert site in the WNBR** and includes **Lahaul-Spiti** — option **(2)**.
India's first **marine BR** is the **Gulf of Mannar**; the **Nilgiri** BR dates from **1986**; **Sundarbans** is the mangrove BR.
xa: It also covers **Pin Valley NP**, **Kibber WLS** and **Chandratal**; flagship animal **snow leopard**.
It joined the WNBR in **September 2025** at Hangzhou.
⚠ PYQ G1 **2024** marked Cold Desert as not in MAB — true then.

87.s: India has how many Biosphere Reserves and how many of them are included in UNESCO’s World Network of Biosphere Reserves?
87.x: India has 18 Biosphere Reserves, of which 13 are included in UNESCO’s World Network of Biosphere Reserves.
87.tq: Distinguish the total number from the UNESCO-listed subset.
xs: India has **18 BRs**, of which **13** are in UNESCO's **WNBR** — option **(3)**.
Option (1) reverses the numbers; **5** is the count still outside the WNBR.
xa: The **18 BRs** cover about **91,425.11 sq km**.
Outside the WNBR: **Manas**, **Dibru-Saikhowa**, **Dehang-Dibang**, **Great Rann of Kutch**, **Seshachalam**.
⚠ "All Indian BRs are in the UNESCO network" — false (**13 of 18**).

87.s: Which of the following is NOT among the five Indian biosphere reserves that are not yet included in UNESCO’s World Network?
87.x: Agasthyamalai is included in UNESCO’s World Network, since it received recognition in 2016. The five not yet included are Manas, Dibru-Saikhowa, Dehang-Dibang, Great Rann of Kutch and Seshachalam.
87.tq: Find the exception by recalling the complete list of non-WNBR reserves.
xs: **Agasthyamalai** is in the WNBR (joined **2016**), so it is not one of the five — option **(4)**.
The five outside: **Manas**, **Dibru-Saikhowa**, **Dehang-Dibang**, **Great Rann of Kutch**, **Seshachalam**.
xa: **Agasthyamalai** (Kerala-TN) was established in **2001**; home of the **Kani tribe**.
**Seshachalam** (AP, **2010**) is "under process" for the WNBR.
**13** of India's **18** BRs are in the WNBR.

87.s: Which was the first Biosphere Reserve established in India?
87.x: Nilgiri was India’s first Biosphere Reserve, designated in 1986.
87.tq: Use the first-in-sequence fact with its establishment year.
xs: India's first BR is **Nilgiri** (**1986**) — option **(4)**.
It was also the first Indian entry in the **WNBR** (**2000**).
**Agasthyamalai** came in **2001**, **Great Rann of Kutch** in **2008**, **Seshachalam** in **2010**.
xa: Nilgiri spans **TN, Kerala, Karnataka** — India's only **three-state BR**.
It lies within the **Western Ghats WHS**.
**Madhav Gadgil**'s work shaped landscape-level conservation in the Nilgiri BR.

87.s: The largest Biosphere Reserve in India by area is:
87.x: The Great Rann of Kutch in Gujarat is the largest Indian Biosphere Reserve by area.

xa: **Sundarbans** has the most animal species of any Indian BR — **2,626**.
**Nilgiri** is the only three-state BR; **Seshachalam** is AP's only BR.
India's **18 BRs** cover about **91,425.11 sq km**.

87.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: TRAFFIC is an alliance of WWF and IUCN.
Statement B: BirdLife International identifies Important Bird and Biodiversity Areas.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true

n: TRAFFIC is an alliance of WWF and IUCN. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-42]
BirdLife International identifies Important Bird and Biodiversity Areas. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-42]
xs: **Both statements are true** — so option **(1)** is correct.

Statement B: **BirdLife International** identifies **Important Bird and Biodiversity Areas (IBAs)**.

87.s:

n: IUCN is associated with conservation and the Red List. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-42]
GEF is associated with environmental financing. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-42]
IPCC is associated with climate-change assessment. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-42]
FAO is associated with food, agriculture, and forestry. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-42]
xs: Statements **I, II and III** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
I: **GEF** — **environmental financing**; II: **FAO** — **food, agriculture and forestry**.
III: **IUCN** — **conservation** and the **Red List**.
IV is wrong: **climate-change assessment** is the **IPCC**; **WWF** is about **wildlife and biodiversity conservation**.
xa: **UNEP** — the **global environment**; **WMO** — **meteorology and climate**.
**WHO** — **health and environmental health**.
**TRAFFIC** — wildlife-trade monitoring; **BirdLife International** — **IBAs**.

87.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with respect to marine protected areas in India?
