89.s:
Arrange the following projects in chronological order of their launch:
A. Project Snow Leopard
B. Project Tiger
C. Indian Rhino Vision 2020
D. Crocodile Breeding and Management Project
89.x: The correct order is Project Tiger (1973), Crocodile Project (1975), Indian Rhino Vision 2020 (2005), and Project Snow Leopard (2009).
89.tq: Fix the earliest and latest projects first, then arrange the middle years.
xs: Correct order: **B, D, C, A** — option **(1)**.
**Project Tiger 1973** → **Crocodile Project 1975** → **Indian Rhino Vision 2020** (launched **2005**) → **Project Snow Leopard 2009**.
xa: ⚠ Indian Rhino Vision **2020** was launched in **2005** — the "2020" is its target, not its launch.
**Project Elephant** came in **Feb 1992**; **Project Lion** and **Project Dolphin** in **2020**.
The Crocodile Project covered **gharial, mugger, saltwater crocodile**, with **FAO and UNDP** support.

89.s: Which of the following was NOT among the five new national projects added by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change?
89.x: The five additions were dolphin, Asian elephant, gharial, Great Indian Bustard and Olive Ridley turtle. Project Snow Leopard was not among these five new additions.
89.tq: Find the excluded project from a closely related list of species-specific initiatives.
xs: **Project Snow Leopard** (**2009**) is not one of the five new projects — option **(3)**.
MoEFCC's **five national projects** (2026): **Dolphin**, **Asian elephant**, **gharial**, **GIB**, **Olive Ridley turtle**.
xa: India has **718 snow leopards** (first assessment, Apr 2026).
The **GIB** is also on the **Species Recovery Programme**.
Olive Ridley mass nesting (**arribada**) occurs at **Rushikulya** and on **Srikakulam and Vizianagaram** beaches.

89.s: Which one of the following was the first tiger reserve under Project Tiger?
89.x: Corbett was the first tiger reserve under Project Tiger, formally included on 1 April 1973.
89.tq: Distinguish the first reserve from other reserves associated with the programme.
xs: **Corbett** was the first tiger reserve (**1 April 1973**) — option **(4)**.
**Palamau** (Jharkhand) was among the **first nine**, but not first.
**NSTR** is the **largest**, not the first.
xa: Project Tiger began with **9 reserves**, **18,278 sq km**.
Today: **58 reserves** in **18 States**.
**NSTR** core area is about **5,443 sq km**.

89.s: Projects located in tiger corridors require clearance from the:
o: Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife
89.x: Projects in tiger corridors require clearance from the Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife.
89.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to identify the competent wildlife authority.
xs: Projects in tiger corridors need **NBWL Standing Committee** clearance — option **(3)**.
The **NTCA** implements Project Tiger but does not alone clear corridor projects.
xa: A **3rd railway line** threatens the **Satpura-Melghat corridor** (4 Aug 2026).
A **growing share of tigers** disperses **outside reserves**, raising conflict.
The **Global Tiger Forum** is an international body, not a clearance authority.

89.s: Project Elephant was launched as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme in which month and year?
89.x: Project Elephant was launched in February 1992 as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (some sources say 1991-92). '1990' is the trap: APPSC 2022 treated a 1990 launch as the incorrect statement.
89.tq: Use the precise month-year rather than confusing the financial year with the launch year.
xs: **Project Elephant** was launched in **February 1992** as a **Centrally Sponsored Scheme** — option **(3)**.
⚠ "Launched in **1990**" is wrong (APPSC **2022**); some notes say **1991-92**.
xa: It covers **33 Elephant Reserves** in **14 States**.
It also covers the welfare of **captive** elephants.
The elephant became the **National Heritage Animal** in **2010**.

89.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the seven big cats covered by the International Big Cat Alliance?
89.x: The seven big cats are tiger, lion, leopard, snow leopard, cheetah, jaguar and puma. Gharial is not a big cat covered by the IBCA.
89.tq: Find the non-member by checking the exact species composition.
xs: The **gharial** is a crocodilian, not a big cat — option **(4)**.
IBCA's **7 big cats**: **tiger, lion, leopard, snow leopard, cheetah, jaguar, puma**.
xa: IBCA is open to **96 range countries** plus non-range countries.
**37 countries** have consented to join; **Saudi Arabia** was the **26th** member and **Bangladesh** the **27th**.
The gharial was covered by the **Crocodile Project** (**1975**).

89.s:
Consider the following pairs:
a. Rushikulya — Ganjam district, Odisha
b. Srikakulam — Andhra Pradesh
c. Vizianagaram — Andhra Pradesh

The above places are particularly associated with:
89.x: Rushikulya in Ganjam, Odisha, and beaches in Srikakulam and Vizianagaram in Andhra Pradesh are associated with Olive Ridley mass nesting, known as arribada.
89.tq: Start from the sure geographical pair and identify the common species focus.
xs: **Rushikulya**, **Srikakulam** and **Vizianagaram** are **Olive Ridley mass nesting** sites — option **(2)**.
Mass nesting is called **arribada**.
xa: **Operation Olivia** (Coast Guard) has protected Olive Ridleys annually since the early **1980s**.
**Olive Ridley turtle** is one of MoEFCC's **five new national projects**.
**National Marine Turtle Action Plan**: **2021**.

89.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Protected area)    List-II (Principal focus)
a. Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park/Biosphere Reserve    i. Saltwater crocodile and mangroves
b. Malvan Marine Sanctuary    ii. Mangroves and Godavari estuary
c. Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary    iii. Coral reefs, islands and dugong
 d. Bhitarkanika    iv. Corals and marine life

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
89.x: Gulf of Mannar is associated with coral reefs, islands and dugong; Malvan with corals and marine life; Coringa with mangroves and the Godavari estuary; and Bhitarkanika with saltwater crocodiles and mangroves.
89.tq: Start from the sure pair and match each protected area with its species or habitat focus.
xs: Correct code: **a–iii, b–iv, c–ii, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**Gulf of Mannar** — **coral reefs, islands, dugong**; **Malvan** — **corals, marine life**.
**Coringa** — **mangroves, Godavari estuary**; **Bhitarkanika** — **saltwater crocodile, mangroves**.
xa: About **64 bird species** are found on **Hope Island** near Coringa.
The **Baula** (saltwater crocodile) project is at **Dangamal**, Bhitarkanika.
**Palk Bay** = first **Dugong Conservation Reserve**.

89.s:
Consider the following statements about CAMPA:
1. The Supreme Court set up an ad hoc CAMPA in 2006.
2. It received statutory backing through the Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016.
3. Under the Act, 90% of the money goes to the National Fund and 10% to the State Funds.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
89.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the SC created ad hoc CAMPA in 2006 and the CAF Act, 2016 gave it statutory backing. Statement 3 reverses the split: 90% goes to the State Funds and 10% to the National Fund. So only '1 and 2 only' fits.
89.tq: CAMPA split: 90 to States, 10 to Centre.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: the SC set up an **ad hoc CAMPA** in **2006**.
Statement 2: statutory backing came from the **Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016**.
Statement 3 reverses the split: **90%** goes to **State funds**, **10%** to the **National Fund**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes date the Act to **2021**.
CAMPA funds go to **wildlife management** and **human-wildlife conflict**.
The **National CAMPA Advisory Council** funds the Recovery Programme for **5 years**.

89.s:
Consider the following statements about Project Tiger:
1. It began in 1973 with 9 reserves covering 18,278 sq km.
2. Today there are 58 tiger reserves in 18 States, covering about 2.6% of India's area.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
89.x: Both are correct: Project Tiger started in 1973 with 9 reserves (18,278 sq km), and it now has 58 reserves in 18 States covering about 84,488 sq km, roughly 2.6% of India's area. So 'Both 1 and 2'.
89.tq: 9 reserves (1973) to 58 reserves now; about 2.6% of India's area.
xs: **Both statements** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
Statement 1: **Project Tiger** began in **1973** with **9 reserves** covering **18,278 sq km**.
Statement 2: there are now **58 reserves** in **18 States**, about **84,488 sq km** — about **2.6%** of India's area.
xa: First tiger reserve: **Corbett** (**1 April 1973**).
**NTCA**: statutory body via the **2006 amendment** to the WPA; chaired by the **Union Environment Minister**.
**Section 38V(3)**: each State must prepare a **Tiger Conservation Plan**.
India's largest TR: **NSTR**, about **5,443 sq km** core.

89.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Project Tiger is/are correct?
1. It was launched on the advice of a task force set up by Indira Gandhi.
2. WWF support was associated with its launch.
3. Palamau was among the first nine tiger reserves.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
89.x: All three statements are correct. Project Tiger was launched on the advice of Indira Gandhi’s task force, had WWF support, and included Palamau among its first nine reserves.
89.tq: Check each historical association separately before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Project Tiger (**1973**) followed a task force set up by **Indira Gandhi**, with **WWF** support.
**Palamau (Jharkhand)** was among the **first nine** reserves.
xa: First reserve: **Corbett**.
It is implemented by the **NTCA** under **MoEFCC**.
IBCA was launched in **April 2023** to mark **50 years of Project Tiger**.

89.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA):
1. It is a statutory body created through the 2006 amendment to the Wildlife (Protection) Act.
2. It is chaired by the Prime Minister.
3. Under Section 38V(3), each State must prepare a Tiger Conservation Plan for every tiger reserve.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
89.x: Statement 1 is correct: NTCA became statutory through the 2006 WPA amendment. Statement 2 is wrong: NTCA is chaired by the Union Environment Minister (the Prime Minister chairs the NBWL). Statement 3 is correct: Section 38V(3) requires a Tiger Conservation Plan for every reserve. Hence 1 and 3 only.
89.tq: PM chairs NBWL; Environment Minister chairs NTCA and the NBWL Standing Committee.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: the **NTCA** became statutory via the **2006 amendment** to the **WPA 1972**.
Statement 2 is wrong: it is **chaired by the Union Environment Minister**.
Statement 3: **Section 38V(3)** requires a **Tiger Conservation Plan** for every reserve.
xa: The **Tiger Task Force** led to the NTCA and the **WCCB**.
The NTCA runs the **All India Tiger Estimation** with **WII** every **4 years**.
**MEE 2022**: **51** TRs assessed, **12** "Excellent", average **78%**.

89.s:
Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the Global Tiger Summit of 2010?
1. It was held in St Petersburg in November 2010.
2. It set the TX2 goal.
3. International Tiger Day on 29 July traces its origin to this effort.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
89.x: The summit was held in St Petersburg in November 2010, adopted TX2, and is associated with International Tiger Day on 29 July.
89.tq: Combine event location, date, objective and legacy in a coded statement question.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
The summit met in **St Petersburg** in **November 2010**, set **TX2**, and began **International Tiger Day, 29 July**.
xa: TX2 = double wild tigers by **2022**; India met it early.
The **Global Tiger Forum** dates from **1993** (HQ **New Delhi**).
Other efforts: **IBCA**, **ITHCP** (led by **IUCN**), **CA|TS**.

89.s: The All India Tiger Estimation is conducted at what interval and jointly by which organisations?
o: Every five years by MoEFCC and BNHS
Every three years by WII and Forest Survey of India
Every four years by NTCA and WII
Every two years by NTCA and Zoological Survey of India
89.x: All India Tiger Estimation is conducted every four years by NTCA and the Wildlife Institute of India.
89.tq: Match frequency with the correct institutional partnership.
xs: The **All India Tiger Estimation** is held every **four years** by **NTCA with WII** — option **(3)**.
It uses **camera traps** and the **M-STrIPES** monitoring system.
xa: The camera-trap survey holds a **Guinness World Record**.
The old **pugmark** method gave way to **camera trapping + ExtractCompare**.

89.s: Which of the following correctly describes the fifth cycle of All India Tiger Estimation conducted in 2022?
o: 3,925 tigers, with an upper estimate of 3,682
3,682 tigers, with an upper estimate of 3,925
2,967 tigers, with an upper estimate of 3,682
3,682 tigers, with an upper estimate of 4,925
89.x: The 2022 estimation recorded 3,682 tigers, with an upper estimate of 3,925.
89.tq: Distinguish the principal estimate from the upper estimate in paired figures.
xs: **2022 (5th cycle)**: **3,682 tigers**, upper estimate **3,925** — option **(2)**.
Option (1) reverses the two figures.
xa: Annual growth: **6.1%**.
India holds about **70-75%** of the world's wild tigers.

89.s: India holds approximately what share of the world’s wild tiger population?
89.x: India holds approximately 70–75% of the world’s wild tigers.
89.tq: Use the range rather than confusing it with an exact census figure.
xs: India holds about **70-75% of the world's wild tigers** — option **(3)**.
⚠ Some notes say **70%**, others **75%**.
xa: India also has **60%** of the world's **Asian elephants**.
**58 tiger reserves** cover about **2.56%** of India's area.

89.s: Which technique replaced the old pugmark method in all-India tiger estimation?
o: Camera trapping supported by ExtractCompare software
Counting tiger kills reported by villages
Only satellite imagery without field verification
89.x: The old pugmark technique was replaced by camera trapping and ExtractCompare software, which identifies tigers through stripe patterns.
89.tq: Identify the modern method by contrasting it with the obsolete field technique.
xs: The **pugmark** method gave way to **camera trapping** with **ExtractCompare** software — option **(1)**.
ExtractCompare identifies tigers by their **stripe pattern**.
xa: The survey uses the **M-STrIPES** monitoring system.
It is held every **4 years** by **NTCA with WII**.
It holds a **Guinness World Record** as a camera-trap survey.

89.s:
The Action Plan for Vulture Conservation 2020–25 called for: 
1. A State-level vulture committee in every State.
2. Establishment of more vulture breeding centres.
3. Extension of the plan up to 2030.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
89.x: The 2020–25 Action Plan called for State-level committees and more breeding centres. Its extension up to 2030 is a subsequent development, not part of the original call described here.
89.tq: Find the statement that belongs to a later development rather than the original action plan.
xs: The plan called for a **State-level vulture committee** in each State and **more breeding centres** — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
The **extension to 2030** came later; it is not one of the plan's original calls.
xa: ⚠ **Vulture Recovery Plan** = **2006**; **Action Plan** = **2020-25**, now to **2030**.
**SAVE** (Saving Asia's Vultures from Extinction) is the partner consortium.
First vulture portal: **"The Vulture Network"**.

89.s: Project HANUMAN was launched by Andhra Pradesh on World Wildlife Day primarily to:
o: Restore coral reefs along the coast
Increase tiger numbers through captive breeding
89.x: Andhra Pradesh launched Project HANUMAN on 3 March 2026, World Wildlife Day, to reduce human-wildlife conflict.
89.tq: Link the project name, launch occasion and stated objective.
xs: AP's **Project HANUMAN** aims to **reduce human-wildlife conflict** — option **(3)**.
It was launched on **World Wildlife Day**, **3 March 2026**.
xa: **Human-elephant conflict** in AP: crop raids in **Chittoor** and **Anantapur**.
Nationally, human-elephant conflict causes **over 500 human deaths a year**.
**CAMPA** funds are also used for **wildlife management** and **human-wildlife conflict**.

89.s:
Which of the following is a reported concern associated with tiger conservation in and around reserves?
1. Tigers dispersing outside reserves
2. Rising human-wildlife conflict
3. A railway line through the Satpura-Melghat corridor

Select the correct answer using the code below:
89.x: All three are reported concerns: tiger dispersal outside reserves, increasing conflict, and a railway line through the Satpura-Melghat corridor.
89.tq: Recognise that the question combines ecological, social and infrastructure pressures.
xs: All three are reported concerns — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Tigers are **dispersing outside reserves** with **rising conflict** (29 Jul 2026).
A **3rd railway line** threatens the **Satpura-Melghat corridor** (4 Aug 2026).
xa: Projects in tiger corridors need **NBWL Standing Committee** clearance.
**58 reserves** in **18 States** cover **84,488 sq km** (about **2.56%** of India).
Tigers, **2022**: **3,682**, about **70-75%** of the world's wild tigers.

89.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Project Lion was launched in 2020 for the Asiatic lion.
2. Project Dolphin was launched in 2020 for riverine and marine dolphins.
3. Indian Rhino Vision 2020 was launched in 2005 for the one-horned rhinoceros in Assam.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
89.x: All three statements are correct. Project Lion and Project Dolphin began in 2020, while Indian Rhino Vision 2020 began in 2005 for Assam's one-horned rhinoceros.
89.tq: Check each project against both its year and target species or region.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Project Lion** (**2020**) — **Asiatic lion, Gir**; **Project Dolphin** (**2020**) — **riverine and marine** dolphins.
**Indian Rhino Vision 2020** began in **2005** for the **one-horned rhino, Assam**.
xa: ⚠ **Project Snow Leopard** = **2009**, not 2020.
India has **891 Asiatic lions** and **over 4,000 rhinos** (Apr 2026).
India's riverine dolphins number **6,327**.

89.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with the population figure mentioned for 2026?
89.x: The reported figures were 891 Asiatic lions and 718 snow leopards. Assam had 2,650 rhinos in 2018, while the overall rhino population was over 4,000.
89.tq: Keep species-specific population figures separate while rejecting reversed pairs.
xs: **Asiatic lions — 891** is correct — option **(2)**.
**718** is the **snow leopard** count; **891** is not.
Assam had **2,650** rhinos in **2018**; **over 4,000** is India's total.
xa: ⚠ Compare: **3,682** tigers (**2022**), **22,446** elephants, **891** lions, **718** snow leopards.
The **718** snow leopards came from the **first assessment** (Apr 2026).
**Project Lion** (**2020**) protects the **Gir** lions.

89.s: Under the Wildlife Protection Act, the Ganges River Dolphin is included in:
89.x: The Ganges River Dolphin is listed in Schedule I of the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972.
89.tq: Test the exact statutory schedule, a common legal-classification trap.
xs: The Ganges River Dolphin is in **Schedule I** of the **WPA 1972** — option **(3)**.
Its scientific name is **Platanista gangetica**; it is India's **National Aquatic Animal**.
xa: It is the **National Aquatic Animal** (**5 October 2009**).
Threats: **dams**, barrages, **pollution**, **bycatch**, poaching for oil, boat traffic.
**Project Dolphin** (**2020**) covers riverine and marine dolphins.

89.s: The first national assessment of riverine dolphins recorded a total of:
89.x: The first national assessment recorded 6,327 riverine dolphins. The survey covered 8,500 km across 28 rivers in eight States; 8,500 is therefore a distance, not the dolphin count.
89.tq: Separate the population figure from the survey-distance figure.
xs: The first national survey counted **6,327** riverine dolphins — option **(4)**.
**8,500 km** is the distance surveyed, not the count.
⚠ "Fewer than **2,000**" is an older note.
xa: The survey covered **28 rivers** in **8 States**.
Compare: **3,682** tigers, **22,446** elephants, **891** lions.
The Gangetic dolphin is in **Schedule I**.

89.s: Which is the largest tiger reserve in India by area?
89.x: Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve (NSTR) in the Nallamala hills of Andhra Pradesh is India's largest tiger reserve, with a core area of about 5,443 sq km. Bandipur, Corbett and Kanha are smaller.
89.tq: Test the largest-reserve comparison using the area-based distinction.
xs: **Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam (NSTR)** is **India's largest tiger reserve** — option **(1)**.
Its core area is about **5,443 sq km**, in the **Nallamala** hills of AP.
**Corbett** is the **first** reserve, not the largest.
xa: NSTR anti-poaching camps are rising from **89 to 150** (30 Jul 2026).
AP will receive **4 female tigers** from **Maharashtra** and **MP**.
**Gaur** are being reintroduced in NSTR (Jul 2026).

89.s: Which one of the following is NOT an objective of Project Elephant?
o: Protection of elephant habitats and corridors
Protection of only captive elephants and not wild elephants
89.x: Project Elephant covers wild elephants, their habitats and corridors, mitigation of conflict, and the welfare of captive elephants. It is not restricted to captive elephants.
89.tq: Find the option narrowed by the extreme word ‘only’.
xs: "**Only captive elephants, not wild ones**" is not an objective — option **(3)**.
Objectives: protect elephants, their **habitats and corridors**; mitigate **man-elephant conflict**; welfare of **captive** elephants.
⚠ The reverse trap — "only wild elephants" — is also wrong (UPPSC **2017**).
xa: Human-elephant conflict causes **over 500 human deaths a year**.
**MIKE** (Monitoring the Illegal Killing of Elephants) is a **CITES** programme.
Launched **February 1992**.

89.s: MIKE, associated with elephant conservation, stands for:
o: Monitoring the Illegal Killing of Elephants
89.x: MIKE stands for Monitoring the Illegal Killing of Elephants and is a CITES programme.
89.tq: Expand the exact acronym and identify the associated international programme.
xs: **MIKE** = **Monitoring the Illegal Killing of Elephants** — option **(1)**.
It is a **CITES** programme.
xa: ⚠ **MIKE** = elephants; **M-STrIPES** = tigers.
**Project Elephant** began in **February 1992**.
India has **60%** of the world's Asian elephants.

89.s:
Consider the following statements about Asian elephants:
1. Only male Asian elephants carry tusks; tuskless males are called makhnas.
2. An elephant herd is usually led by the strongest adult male.
3. The gestation period is about 22 months, the longest of any mammal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
89.x: Statement 1 is correct: only males have tusks and tuskless males are makhnas. Statement 2 is wrong: the herd is led by a female (matriarch). Statement 3 is correct: gestation is about 22 months, the longest among mammals. Hence 1 and 3 only.
89.tq: Matriarch leads the herd (UPSC 2020 trap).
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: only male Asian elephants have **tusks**; tuskless males are **"makhnas"**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the herd is led by a **female (matriarch)** (UPSC 2020).
Statement 3: gestation is about **22 months**, the **longest of any mammal**.
xa: Elephant = **National Heritage Animal** (**2010**).
⚠ Gangetic dolphin = **National Aquatic Animal** (**2009**).
India has **22,446 elephants** (Apr 2026).

89.s: In which year was the elephant declared India's National Heritage Animal?
89.x: The elephant was declared the National Heritage Animal in 2010. 1992 is the launch of Project Elephant, 2009 is when the Ganges river dolphin became the National Aquatic Animal, and 2020 is the launch of Project Lion and Project Dolphin.
89.tq: Heritage Animal 2010; Aquatic Animal (dolphin) 2009.
xs: The elephant was declared the **National Heritage Animal** in **2010** — option **(3)**.
**1992** = Project Elephant; **2009** = Gangetic dolphin as **National Aquatic Animal**; **2020** = Project Lion and Project Dolphin.
xa: The dolphin was declared on **5 October 2009** — now **National Dolphin Day**.
**Project Elephant** was a **Centrally Sponsored Scheme**.
Only male Asian elephants carry **tusks**.

89.s: Which of the following is the correct scope of Project Dolphin?
o: It covers only marine turtles and Olive Ridley nesting sites.
It covers riverine and marine dolphins and other cetaceans.
It covers only terrestrial mammals in the Thar region.
It covers only the Ganges River Dolphin in Bihar.
89.x: Project Dolphin covers both riverine and marine dolphins as well as other cetaceans; it is not restricted to one riverine species or one State.
89.tq: Reject the ‘only’ restriction and identify the broader programme scope.
xs: **Project Dolphin (2020)** covers **riverine and marine** dolphins plus other **cetaceans** — option **(2)**.
It is not limited to one species or to **Bihar**.
xa: **Dolphin** is also among MoEFCC's **five new national projects** (2026).
The **Gangetic dolphin** is the **National Aquatic Animal** (**2009**).
⚠ **Project Lion** was launched in the same year, **2020**.

89.s: India's Vulture Conservation and Breeding Centre (Jatayu centre), the first vulture breeding centre, is located at:
89.x: The Vulture Conservation and Breeding Centre is at Pinjore, Haryana. Keoladeo is where the decline was first noticed (1998), Jaisalmer hosts the GIB breeding centres, and Darjeeling breeds red pandas.
89.tq: Vultures - Pinjore; GIB - Jaisalmer; red panda - Darjeeling.
xs: The **Jatayu** Vulture Conservation and Breeding Centre is at **Pinjore, Haryana** — option **(1)**.
**Keoladeo** is where the decline was noticed (**1998**); **Jaisalmer** breeds the **GIB**.
xa: It is India's **first vulture breeding centre**.
Vulture plans: **Recovery Plan 2006**; **Action Plan 2020-25**, extended to **2030**.
The plan calls for **more breeding centres**.

89.s: India's first Dugong Conservation Reserve was established in:
89.x: India's first Dugong Conservation Reserve was established in Palk Bay, Tamil Nadu, in 2022.
89.tq: Distinguish the dugong reserve location from other marine protected areas.
xs: India's **first Dugong Conservation Reserve** is in **Palk Bay, Tamil Nadu** (**2022**) — option **(4)**.
**Gulf of Mannar** is linked with dugongs too, but is a marine NP/BR; **Malvan** and **Coringa** are sanctuaries.
xa: **Dugong** is on the **Species Recovery Programme**.
**Malvan Marine Sanctuary** (Maharashtra) protects **corals**.
**Coringa** (Kakinada) protects **mangroves**.

89.s: The headquarters of the Wildlife Institute of India is located at:
89.x: The Wildlife Institute of India (WII) is headquartered at Dehradun.
89.tq: Test the location of the institution directly against nearby headquarters.
xs: The **Wildlife Institute of India (WII)**, set up in **1982**, is headquartered at **Dehradun** — option **(3)**.
**Gland** is the HQ of **IUCN** and **WWF**; **Mumbai** of **BNHS**; **Noida** of **WTI**.
xa: WII runs the **All India Tiger Estimation** with the **NTCA**, every **four years**.
The **Aqua Life Conservation Monitoring Centre** (Jan 2026) is at **WII Dehradun**, under **Namami Gange**.

89.s: Which of the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh's protected-area profile is correct?
o: Andhra Pradesh has India's largest tiger reserve and its only elephant reserve, Rayala.
Rollapadu is Andhra Pradesh's only elephant reserve.
Rayala is Andhra Pradesh's only marine biosphere reserve.
Andhra Pradesh has India's only elephant reserve and India's largest tiger reserve.
89.x: Andhra Pradesh contains India's largest tiger reserve and its only elephant reserve, Rayala.
89.tq: Watch for reversed or shifted State-level superlatives.
xs: AP has **India's largest tiger reserve (NSTR)** and its **only elephant reserve, Rayala** — option **(1)**.
**Rollapadu** is a **GIB** sanctuary, not an elephant reserve.
**Rayala** is an **elephant reserve** (Anantapuramu Circle), not a marine biosphere reserve.
Option 4 is wrong: Rayala is AP's only elephant reserve; India has **33 Elephant Reserves** in **14 States**.
xa: NSTR: about **5,443 sq km** core; anti-poaching camps going up from **89 to 150**.
⚠ **Koundinya** = sanctuary (Chittoor), AP's **only elephant habitat**; **Rayala** = elephant reserve.

89.s:
Consider the following statements about the Species Recovery Programme under CSS-Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats:
1. Hangul, dugong, the Great Indian Bustard and marine turtles are among the species it covers.
2. It covers 22 critically endangered species.
3. Gharial and sloth bear have been covered by it from the start.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
89.x: Statement 2 is correct: the programme covers 22 critically endangered species. Statement 3 is wrong: gharial and sloth bear were only recommended for inclusion (Jun 2026). Statement 1 is correct: Hangul, dugong, GIB, Gangetic dolphin, snow leopard, Asiatic lion, vultures and marine turtles are covered. So '1 and 2 only'.
89.tq: Gharial + sloth bear = 'recommended for inclusion', not yet covered.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the programme covers **Hangul**, **dugong**, **GIB**, **marine turtles**, snow leopard, Asiatic lion, Gangetic dolphin, vultures.
Statement 2 is correct: it covers **22 critically endangered species**, under **CSS-IDWH**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **gharial** and **sloth bear** were only **recommended for inclusion** (**Jun 2026**).
xa: The Recovery Programme is funded via the **National CAMPA Advisory Council**, for an initial **5 years**.
**CAMPA**: statutory backing by the **Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016**; split **90%** State / **10%** National.
**Vulture Action Plan 2020-25** extended to **2030**.

89.s:
Consider the following statements about the Great Indian Bustard:
1. It is known as Godawan and is the state bird of Rajasthan.
2. It is classified as Endangered on the IUCN Red List.
3. Fewer than 150 birds are left in the wild.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
89.x: Statement 1 is correct: the GIB (Ardeotis nigriceps) is called Godawan and is Rajasthan's state bird. Statement 2 is wrong: it is Critically Endangered, not Endangered. Statement 3 is correct: fewer than 150 birds remain. Hence 1 and 3 only; options with 2 are wrong.
89.tq: Status trap: GIB is Critically Endangered (CR), not just Endangered.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: the **GIB (Ardeotis nigriceps)** is the **Godawan**, **Rajasthan's state bird**.
Statement 2 is wrong: it is **Critically Endangered (CR)**, not Endangered.
Statement 3: **fewer than 150** birds are left.
xa: Main threat: collisions with **overhead power lines** in solar and wind zones.
Conservation breeding at **Jaisalmer, Rajasthan**.
AP site: **Rollapadu WLS** (**Kurnool**; now **Nandyal**).

89.s: The principal natural range of the Great Indian Bustard is associated with which of the following regions?
89.x: The Great Indian Bustard is found mainly in the Thar region of Rajasthan, although its range also extends into parts of Gujarat, Maharashtra and Karnataka.
89.tq: Use the core range as the distinguishing geographical fact.
xs: The GIB lives mainly in the **Thar (Rajasthan)** — option **(3)**.
It also occurs in **Gujarat**, **Maharashtra** and **Karnataka**.
xa: In AP: **Rollapadu WLS** (**Kurnool**; now **Nandyal**).
The GIB is **Critically Endangered**, with **fewer than 150** birds.
It is one of MoEFCC's **five new national species projects**.

89.s: The major conservation threat to the Great Indian Bustard in solar and wind-energy zones is:
89.x: Collisions with overhead power lines are a major threat to the Great Indian Bustard, particularly in solar and wind-energy zones.
89.tq: Match the conservation problem with the habitat-specific human infrastructure causing it.
xs: The GIB's main threat is **collision with overhead power lines** in solar and wind zones — option **(1)**.
Net entanglement and pollution are **dolphin** threats; mangrove loss is a coastal issue.
xa: The SC ordered GIB-area power lines laid **underground** in **2021**.
**M.K. Ranjitsinh (March 2024)** modified the blanket order and set up an **expert committee**.
⚠ CMS **COP13** mascot **"Gibi"** was a GIB.

89.s:
Consider the following statements about Gangetic dolphin conservation:
1. Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary is located at Bhagalpur, Bihar.
2. The National Dolphin Research Centre is located at Patna.
3. Project Dolphin was launched in 2018.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
89.x: Statement 1 is correct: Vikramshila sanctuary is at Bhagalpur. Statement 2 is correct: the National Dolphin Research Centre is at Patna. Statement 3 is wrong: Project Dolphin was launched in 2020. So 1 and 2 only; '1 only' misses statement 2, and the options with 3 are wrong.
89.tq: Bhagalpur = sanctuary, Patna = research centre; Project Dolphin = 2020 (same year as Project Lion).
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **Vikramshila** sanctuary is at **Bhagalpur, Bihar**.
Statement 2: the **National Dolphin Research Centre** is at **Patna**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Project Dolphin** began in **2020**.
xa: ⚠ **Vikramshila** = **Bhagalpur** (sanctuary); **Patna** = research centre.
New (Jan 2026): a **Dolphin Rescue Ambulance** and an **Aqua Life Conservation Monitoring Centre** (**WII Dehradun**, **Namami Gange**).
Riverine dolphins: **6,327**.

89.s: Which one of the following is NOT a recognised threat to the Ganges River Dolphin?
89.x: Pollution, entanglement or bycatch in fishing nets, dams and barrages, poaching, killing for oil and boat traffic are recognised threats. Expansion of desert grasslands is not identified as a threat to the river dolphin.
89.tq: Find the geographically unrelated option among the listed threats.
xs: **Expansion of desert grasslands** is not a threat to the river dolphin — option **(3)**.
Listed threats: **dams**, barrages, water diversion, **pollution**, **bycatch** in nets, poaching for oil, boat traffic.
xa: Range: **Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna** and **Karnaphuli-Sangu** systems.
A **Dolphin Rescue Ambulance** started in **Jan 2026**.
Sanctuary: **Vikramshila**, **Bhagalpur**.

89.s: Which one of the following was declared India's National Aquatic Animal in 2009?
89.x: The Ganges River Dolphin (Platanista gangetica) was declared the National Aquatic Animal on 5 October 2009. The Olive Ridley turtle, gharial and humpback dolphin are the distractors used in the APPSC 2019 question.
89.tq: National Aquatic Animal = Ganges river dolphin (5 Oct 2009).
xs: The **Ganges River Dolphin** became the **National Aquatic Animal** in **2009** — option **(3)**.
⚠ It is **not** the Olive Ridley, humpback dolphin or gharial (APPSC **2019**).
xa: The date, **5 October**, is **National Dolphin Day**.
Elephant = **National Heritage Animal** (**2010**).
Scientific name: **Platanista gangetica**.

89.s:
Consider the following statements about the decline of vultures in India:
1. Vultures died after eating cattle carcasses containing the veterinary painkiller diclofenac.
2. Meloxicam is a safe alternative to diclofenac.
3. Diclofenac kills vultures mainly by causing liver cancer.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
89.x: Statement 1 is correct: vultures declined after feeding on carcasses with diclofenac (decline noticed at Keoladeo, 1998). Statement 3 is wrong: diclofenac causes kidney failure (visceral gout), not liver cancer. Statement 2 is correct: meloxicam is the safe alternative. So '1 and 2 only'.
89.tq: Diclofenac = kidney failure / visceral gout; meloxicam = safe.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: vultures died after eating cattle carcasses containing **diclofenac**.
Statement 2 is correct: **meloxicam** is the **safe alternative**.
Statement 3 is wrong: diclofenac causes **kidney failure (visceral gout)**, not liver cancer.
xa: The decline was noticed at **Keoladeo** in **1998**.
Veterinary diclofenac was **banned in 2006**; **aceclofenac and ketoprofen** banned in **2023**.
First vulture breeding centre: **Jatayu (Pinjore)**, Haryana.
India has **9 vulture species**, **4 CR**.

89.s:
Which of the following veterinary drugs were banned for animal use in 2023?
1. Aceclofenac
2. Ketoprofen
3. Diclofenac

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
89.x: Aceclofenac and ketoprofen were banned for animal use in 2023. Diclofenac had already been banned in 2006.
89.tq: Use the date distinction to separate the 2023 bans from the earlier diclofenac ban.
xs: **Aceclofenac** and **ketoprofen** were banned for animal use in **2023** — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
**Diclofenac** had been banned earlier, in **2006**.
xa: **Meloxicam** is the safe alternative.
**Action Plan for Vulture Conservation 2020-25** is extended to **2030**.
Breeding centre: **Pinjore (Haryana)**; also **Vulture Safe Zones**.

89.s:
Consider the following statements about vultures in India:
1. India has nine vulture species, of which four are Critically Endangered.
2. The red-headed vulture is one of the Critically Endangered species.
3. The vulture decline was first noticed at Keoladeo in 2006.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
89.x: Statement 1 is correct: 9 species, 4 CR (white-rumped, slender-billed, long-billed, red-headed). Statement 2 is correct: the red-headed vulture is among the four. Statement 3 is wrong: the decline was noticed at Keoladeo in 1998; 2006 is the year veterinary diclofenac was banned. Hence 1 and 2 only.
89.tq: 1998 = decline noticed; 2006 = diclofenac ban; 2023 = aceclofenac and ketoprofen ban.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: India has **9 vulture species**, **4 CR** — **white-rumped, slender-billed, long-billed, red-headed**.
Statement 2: the **red-headed vulture** is one of the four.
Statement 3 is wrong: the decline was noticed at **Keoladeo** in **1998**; **2006** is the diclofenac ban.
xa: **Vultures** were added to the **Species Recovery Programme** (2026).
First vulture portal: **"The Vulture Network"**.
**5 slender-billed vultures** were released in **Assam** — a world first.

89.s:
Consider the following statements about the Amur falcon:
1. It stops over in huge numbers at the Doyang reservoir in Nagaland.
2. Pangti is called the 'Falcon Capital of the World'.
3. Its migration includes a non-stop crossing of the Bay of Bengal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
89.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the falcon gathers at Doyang reservoir and Pangti is the 'Falcon Capital of the World'. Statement 3 is wrong: the non-stop crossing is of the Arabian Sea, not the Bay of Bengal. Hence 1 and 2 only.
89.tq: Amur falcon: Nagaland (Doyang, Pangti) stopover, non-stop over the Arabian Sea to southern Africa.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: huge numbers stop at **Doyang reservoir**, **Nagaland**.
Statement 2: **Pangti** is the **"Falcon Capital of the World"**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the non-stop crossing is of the **Arabian Sea**, not the Bay of Bengal.
xa: Route: **SE Russia** and **northern China** → **southern Africa**.
It is one of the **longest raptor migrations**.
Migratory species fall under **CMS** (Bonn Convention, **1979**).

89.s: The Great hornbill is associated as the logo of the:
o: International Union for Conservation of Nature
89.x: The Great hornbill is the logo of the Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS).
89.tq: Discriminate between similar conservation organisations using their emblem.
xs: The **Great hornbill** is the logo of the **Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS)** — option **(2)**.
BNHS was founded in **1883** and is based in **Mumbai**.
**WWF**'s logo is the **Giant panda**.
xa: **IUCN (1948)** and **WWF (1961)** are both headquartered at **Gland, Switzerland**.
**WTI (1998)** is at **Noida, UP**; **WII (1982)** is at **Dehradun**.
BNHS released the world's first captive-bred **slender-billed vultures** in **Assam** (**Aug 2026**).

89.s: The cheetahs introduced under Project Cheetah are correctly identified as
o: African lions surviving only in Namibia
Asiatic cheetahs sourced from Botswana and Iran
African cheetahs, while the Asiatic cheetah survives only in Iran
89.x: The introduced animals are African cheetahs. The critically endangered Asiatic cheetah survives only in Iran.
89.tq: Separate the African cheetah from the geographically restricted Asiatic cheetah.
xs: Project Cheetah uses **African cheetahs**; the **Asiatic cheetah** (CR) survives only in **Iran** — option **(4)**.
Sources were **Namibia**, **South Africa** and **Botswana** — not Iran.
The cheetah was declared **extinct in India in 1952**, so none survive in India.
xa: ⚠ One report names "**Nigeria**" — the correct country is **Namibia**.
Release site: **Kuno NP**, **Sheopur, MP**.
**2** **Botswana** females were released into the wild in **May 2026**.

89.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Batch)
A. Eight cheetahs
B. Twelve cheetahs
C. Two female cheetahs

List-II (Source and date)
1. Namibia — 17 September 2022
2. South Africa — February 2023
3. Botswana — May 2026

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
89.x: Eight cheetahs came from Namibia in September 2022, twelve from South Africa in February 2023, and two females were released from Botswana in May 2026.
89.tq: Start from the sure batch-date pair and eliminate mismatched codes.
xs: Correct code: **A-1, B-2, C-3** — option **(1)**.
**8 cheetahs** — **Namibia**, **17 Sep 2022**; **12 cheetahs** — **South Africa**, **Feb 2023**.
**2 females** — **Botswana**, released **May 2026**.
xa: All went to **Kuno NP** (**Sheopur, MP**).
Population: about **30** with India-born cubs.
⚠ "**Nigeria**" in one report is wrong — it is **Namibia**.

89.s: The cheetah, the only large mammal to have gone extinct in India in recent history, was declared extinct in India in:
89.x: The cheetah was declared extinct in India in 1952. 1947 is Independence, 1972 is the Wildlife (Protection) Act, and 2012 is when the Supreme Court first ruled on its reintroduction.
89.tq: Cheetah extinct 1952; back at Kuno 2022.
xs: The cheetah was declared **extinct in India in 1952** — option **(2)**.
It is the **only large mammal** lost in India in recent history.
**2012** is the SC's first ruling on its reintroduction.
xa: The **Asiatic cheetah** survives only in **Iran**.
**Project Cheetah** aims to restore **open forest and grassland**.
First batch to **Kuno**: **17 Sep 2022**.

89.s: The International Big Cat Alliance was launched in April 2023 primarily to mark
o: the declaration of the cheetah as extinct in India
the first census of Asiatic lions
89.x: The International Big Cat Alliance was launched in April 2023 to mark 50 years of Project Tiger.
89.tq: Link an organisation's launch with the milestone it commemorated.
xs: **IBCA** was launched in **April 2023** at **Mysuru** to mark **50 years of Project Tiger** — option **(4)**.
Project Tiger began in **1973**.
xa: IBCA is a **treaty-based inter-governmental organisation**.
Secretariat: **New Delhi** — ⚠ **not Geneva**.
First IBCA summit: **New Delhi**, **1-3 June 2026**.

89.s:
Consider the following statements about the International Big Cat Alliance:
1. It is a treaty-based inter-governmental organisation.
2. Its Secretariat is in New Delhi.
3. Its headquarters is in Geneva.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
89.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The IBCA Secretariat is in New Delhi; Geneva is not its headquarters.
89.tq: Use a location trap involving a well-known international-city distractor.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: IBCA is a **treaty-based inter-governmental organisation**.
Statement 2: its **Secretariat is in New Delhi**.
Statement 3 is wrong: ⚠ "**HQ in Geneva**" is false.
xa: The India-IBCA agreement was signed **17 April 2025**.
⚠ **Global Tiger Forum** and **IBCA** are both in **New Delhi**; **IUCN** and **WWF** are both in **Gland**.
**China is unlikely to join** (12 May 2026).

89.s: Kuno was initially selected as a second home for which animal before being used for Project Cheetah?
o: Gharials from the National Chambal Sanctuary
89.x: Kuno was initially chosen as a second home for Gir's Asiatic lions. The Supreme Court ordered lion translocation in 2013, but Gujarat did not implement it.
89.tq: Use the earlier conservation purpose of the same site as the discriminator.
xs: **Kuno** was first chosen as a second home for **Gir's Asiatic lions** — option **(1)**.
The SC ordered the translocation in **2013**, but **Gujarat did not carry it out**, so **Kuno went to cheetahs**.
xa: The new proposed lion second home is **Barda WLS** (Gujarat).
⚠ **Kuno** = first chosen for lions; **Barda** = proposed lion second home.
Kuno NP lies in **Sheopur, MP**, on the Kuno river.

89.s: Barda Wildlife Sanctuary has been proposed as a second home for Asiatic lions. The principal criticism of this proposal is that Barda:
o: Is too close to Gir to provide a genuine metapopulation safeguard
Has no forest cover at all
Is exclusively a marine protected area
89.x: Critics argue that Barda Wildlife Sanctuary is too close to Gir to function as an effective separate metapopulation safeguard.
89.tq: Identify the ecological rationale behind the second-home debate.
xs: Critics say **Barda WLS** is **too close to Gir** for a real **metapopulation** safeguard — option **(2)**.
Barda is in **Gujarat**, so option (1) is wrong.
xa: **Kuno** was first chosen for the lions but went to **cheetahs** after Gujarat ignored the **2013** SC order.
**Project Lion** (**2020**) covers surveillance, research and disease management.
The **Gir** lion translocation was **never carried out**.

89.s: MISHTI, launched in 2023, is primarily associated with:
89.x: MISHTI is a mangrove restoration initiative launched in 2023, covering approximately 22,561 hectares in 13 States and Union Territories.
89.tq: Match the programme with its environmental objective rather than its geographical setting.
xs: **MISHTI (2023)** is about **mangrove restoration** — option **(3)**.
It covers about **22,561 ha** in **13** States/UTs.
xa: **National Marine Turtle Action Plan** dates from **2021**.
**Coringa** and **Bhitarkanika** are major mangrove sanctuaries.
**BBNJ Agreement (2024)** covers the high seas.

89.s:
With reference to M.K. Ranjitsinh v. Union of India, consider the following statements:
1. The case concerned protection of the Great Indian Bustard from power-line impacts.
2. In 2021, the Supreme Court directed that power lines in Great Indian Bustard habitat be laid underground.
3. In March 2024, the blanket direction was modified and an expert committee was constituted.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
89.x: All three statements correctly describe the proceedings concerning power lines in Great Indian Bustard habitat and the changes made in 2024.
89.tq: Track the legal sequence by separating the original order from its later modification.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **M.K. Ranjitsinh** concerned **protecting the GIB** from power lines (APPSC 2024).
Statement 2: in **2021** the SC ordered power lines laid **underground**.
Statement 3: in **March 2024** it **modified the blanket order** and set up an **expert committee**.
xa: The case recognised a **right against the adverse effects of climate change** under **Articles 14 and 21**.
⚠ Some notes describe the **2024** order as mandating underground lines.
The GIB has **fewer than 150** birds left.

89.s: In the context of the Supreme Court’s March 2024 proceedings concerning the Great Indian Bustard, which constitutional rights were recognised in relation to adverse effects of climate change?
89.x: The Supreme Court recognised a right against the adverse effects of climate change under Articles 14 and 21.
89.tq: Use the exact constitutional-article pair rather than a broad description of environmental rights.
xs: The SC recognised a **right against the adverse effects of climate change** under **Articles 14 and 21** — option **(3)**.
This came in **M.K. Ranjitsinh v. Union of India** (**March 2024**).
xa: The case was about **protecting the GIB** from power lines.
It modified the **2021** blanket underground-lines order and set up an **expert committee**.
Main GIB threat: **overhead power lines** in solar and wind zones.

89.s: The National Chambal Sanctuary, India's only tri-state riverine protected area, is shared by:
o: Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh
Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Madhya Pradesh
89.x: The National Chambal Sanctuary (1979) spans Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh along the Chambal river. Gujarat, Bihar and Haryana are not part of it.
89.tq: Chambal = MP + Rajasthan + UP; gharial stronghold.
xs: The **National Chambal Sanctuary** spans **MP, Rajasthan and UP** — option **(1)**.
It was set up in **1979** and is India's **only tri-state riverine PA**.
xa: The SC took **suo motu** cognisance to protect **gharials** there.
**Gharials** were reintroduced in **several states** through captive breeding.
The **Crocodile Project** began in **1975**.

89.s:
Consider the following statements about the Convention on Migratory Species (CMS) meetings:
1. CMS COP13 was held at Gandhinagar, Gujarat, in February 2020.
2. The mascot of CMS COP13, 'Gibi', represented the Amur falcon.
3. CMS COP14 was held at Samarkand, Uzbekistan, in February 2024.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
89.x: Statement 1 is correct: COP13 was at Gandhinagar in February 2020. Statement 2 is wrong: 'Gibi' represented the Great Indian Bustard, not the Amur falcon. Statement 3 is correct: COP14 was at Samarkand in February 2024. Hence 1 and 3 only.
89.tq: Gibi = GIB. Gandhinagar (2020) then Samarkand (2024).
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: **COP13** met at **Gandhinagar** in **February 2020**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **"Gibi"** was a **GIB**, not an Amur falcon.
Statement 3: **COP14** met at **Samarkand** in **February 2024**.
xa: CMS was signed in **1979** under **UNEP**.
The **Amur falcon** crosses the **Arabian Sea** non-stop.
The GIB is **Rajasthan's state bird**.

89.s: The Recovery Programme for Critically Endangered Species funded through the National CAMPA Advisory Council was sanctioned initially for:
89.x: The programme was sanctioned for an initial period of five years.
89.tq: Use the programme-duration figure directly and reject nearby durations.
xs: The **Recovery Programme for Critically Endangered Species** was sanctioned for an initial **5 years** — option **(3)** (APPSC 2019 key).
It is funded via the **National CAMPA Advisory Council**.
xa: The SC set up an **ad hoc CAMPA** in **2006**.
Statutory backing: **Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016**.
CAMPA money: **90%** to State funds, **10%** to the National Fund.

89.s:
Which of the following locations in India have been identified as IUCN and Mission Blue Hope Spots?
1. Lakshadweep
2. Andaman and Nicobar Islands
3. Gulf of Mannar
4. Palk Bay
89.x: Lakshadweep and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands are the Indian locations identified as IUCN and Mission Blue Hope Spots.
89.tq: Eliminate locations belonging to nearby but different marine conservation initiatives.
xs: India's **Hope Spots** are **Lakshadweep** and the **Andaman and Nicobar Islands** — option **(1) 1 and 2 only** (APPSC-G1 2024).
**Gulf of Mannar** is a marine NP/BR and **Palk Bay** a dugong reserve — not Hope Spots.
xa: Hope Spots are named by **IUCN** and **Mission Blue**.
**Palk Bay** = India's **first Dugong Conservation Reserve** (**2022**).
**Gulf of Mannar** is known for **coral reefs, islands, dugong**.

89.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The whale shark is India's largest fish.
The Gujarat coast is an important seasonal location for whale sharks.
The protection programme for whale sharks visiting the Gujarat coast started in 2006.
The whale shark can reach about 50 feet.
89.x: Option C is incorrect: Gujarat's whale shark protection programme began in 2004, not 2006. The whale shark is India's largest fish, up to about 50 feet long.
89.tq: Recall the programme year, 2004.
n: The Whale Shark is India's largest fish. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 31-33]
The Whale Shark can reach about 50 feet. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 31-33]
The Gujarat coast is an important seasonal location for Whale Sharks. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 31-33]
A protection programme for Whale Sharks visiting the Gujarat coast started in 2004. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 31-33]
The Whale Shark is associated with the Gujarat coast. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 31-33]
xs: The **incorrect** statement is that the whale-shark programme started in **2006** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **protection programme** for whale sharks on the **Gujarat coast** **started** in **2004**.
The whale shark is **India's largest fish**, about **50 feet**; the Gujarat coast is an **important seasonal location** — options (1), (2), (4) are correct.
xa: **Kharai Camel** **swims** in seawater up to **3 km** and **grazes on mangroves**.
India's first **Dugong Conservation Reserve**: **Palk Bay, Tamil Nadu** (**2022**).
Olive Ridley mass nesting (**arribada**): **Rushikulya** (Odisha) and **Srikakulam / Vizianagaram** beaches (AP).

89.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I (Organisation)
a. IUCN
b. WWF
c. BNHS
d. WTI
List-II (Headquarters)
i. Mumbai

89.x: IUCN and WWF are headquartered at Gland, Switzerland; BNHS at Mumbai; and WTI at Noida, Uttar Pradesh.
89.tq: Start from the repeated sure pair of IUCN and WWF, then complete the remaining matches.
xs: Correct code: **a–ii, b–ii, c–i, d–iii** — option **(1)**.
**IUCN** and **WWF** — **Gland, Switzerland**; **BNHS** — **Mumbai**; **WTI** — **Noida, UP**.
**Dehradun** is the HQ of **WII**, not in the code.
xa: WWF's logo is the **giant panda**; BNHS's is the **great hornbill**.

89.s: The Kharai Camel can survive in which of the following ecosystems?
89.x: The Kharai camel of Kutch survives in both coastal and dry ecosystems, swimming to mangrove islands to feed. It is not found in alpine, glacial or forest habitats.
89.tq: Recall where in Gujarat the Kharai camel lives.
n: The Kharai Camel can survive in coastal and dry ecosystems. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 31-33]
xs: The **Kharai Camel** survives in **coastal and dry ecosystems** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It **swims** in **seawater** up to **3 km** and **grazes** on **mangroves**.
It is **recognised** as a **separate camel breed**; alpine, glacial and forest habitats do not fit it.
xa: The **whale shark** is **India's largest fish**, about **50 feet**.
Whale-shark protection on the **Gujarat coast** started in **2004**.
**Coringa WLS** (Kakinada) protects **mangroves** of the **Godavari estuary**.

90.s:
Arrange the following laws and policies in chronological order of their enactment or adoption:
A. National Forest Policy, 1952
B. Indian Forest Act, 1927
C. Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972
D. Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980
90.x: The correct sequence is the Indian Forest Act, 1927, National Forest Policy, 1952, Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, and Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980.
90.tq: Use the first and last dates to eliminate sequences before checking the middle entries.
xs: The correct order is **B, A, C, D** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Indian Forest Act** came in **1927**, the first post-Independence **National Forest Policy** in **1952**.
The **Wildlife (Protection) Act** followed in **1972** and the **Forest (Conservation) Act** in **1980**.
xa: The **first Indian Forest Act** was drafted in **1865**; the **1878** Act introduced reserved, protected and village forests.
The **42nd Amendment (1976)** came between WPA and FCA: it inserted **Art. 48A** and **Art. 51A(g)**.
The **National Forest Policy 1988** set a **33%** forest/tree cover target.
⚠ **1865** = first Forest Act; **1878** = three forest categories; **1927** = Act still in force.

90.s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Forest Acts:
1. The first Indian Forest Act was drafted in 1865.
2. The Indian Forest Act, 1878 introduced reserved, protected and village forests.
3. The Indian Forest Act, 1927 was repealed after Independence by the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
90.x: Statement 1 is correct: the first Forest Act was drafted in 1865. Statement 2 is correct: the 1878 Act introduced reserved, protected and village forests. Statement 3 is wrong: the 1927 Act is a colonial consolidating law that is still in force. Hence 1 and 2 only.
90.tq: 1865 first, 1878 three categories, 1927 consolidating and still in force.
xs: Only statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the **first Indian Forest Act** was drafted in **1865** (APPSC 2024 key).
Statement 2 is correct: the **1878** Act introduced **reserved, protected and village forests**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **1927** Act is a colonial consolidating law that is **still in force**.
xa: The **Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980** came into force on **25 October 1980**; it did not repeal the 1927 Act.
Under the **1927** Act, **Sec. 26** lists acts prohibited in a reserved forest and makes **trespass** punishable.
The **2017 amendment** removed **bamboo grown outside forest areas** from the definition of "tree" in **Sec. 2(7)**.

90.s: The Forest (Conservation) Amendment Act, 2023 renamed the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 as the
90.x: The 2023 amendment renamed it the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980.
90.tq: Distinguish the exact official title from plausible but unofficial alternatives.
xs: The 2023 amendment renamed the FCA as the **Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980** — option **(2)**.
The Act was **renamed, not repealed**, so both names appear in questions; the renaming took effect from **29 Dec 2023**.
xa: **Exemptions** from Central approval: strategic linear projects within **100 km** of the **IB, LoC or LAC**, eco-tourism, zoos and safaris.
**Compensatory afforestation**: **non-forest land of equal area**, else **twice the area of degraded forest land**, plus **NPV**.
Critics say it takes **"deemed forests"** out of scope, diluting the **Godavarman** ruling.
AP had diverted **27,641.252 ha** of forest under the Adhiniyam up to **31.12.2024**.

90.s:
The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 transferred which of the following subjects from the State List to the Concurrent List?
1. Forests
2. Protection of wild animals and birds
3. Public health
Which of the statements given above are correct?
90.x: The 42nd Amendment transferred forests through Entry 17A and protection of wild animals and birds through Entry 17B to the Concurrent List. Public health was not transferred by this amendment.
90.tq: Identify the two related entries and reject the unrelated subject.
xs: **Forests** and **protection of wild animals and birds** were moved — **1 and 2 only**, option **(3)**.
Forests became **Entry 17A** and protection of wild animals and birds **Entry 17B** of the **Concurrent List**.
**Public health** was not part of this transfer.
xa: The same **42nd Amendment (1976)** inserted **Art. 48A** (DPSP) and **Art. 51A(g)** (Fundamental Duty).
The **T.N. Godavarman** case (**1995**) read "forest" as every area recorded as forest in government records.
⚠ **17A** = forests; **17B** = wild animals and birds.

90.s:
Consider the following statements about the 42nd Constitutional Amendment, 1976:
1. It inserted Article 48A, a Directive Principle on protecting the environment, forests and wildlife.
2. It inserted Article 51A(g), which is a Directive Principle of State Policy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
90.x: Statement 1 is correct: Article 48A is a DPSP inserted by the 42nd Amendment. Statement 2 is wrong: Article 51A(g), also added in 1976, is a Fundamental Duty of citizens, not a Directive Principle. So '1 only'.
90.tq: 48A = DPSP (State); 51A(g) = Fundamental Duty (citizen).
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the **42nd Amendment** inserted **Article 48A**, a **DPSP** on protecting the environment, forests and wildlife.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Article 51A(g)** is a **Fundamental Duty** of citizens, not a Directive Principle.
xa: The 42nd Amendment (**1976**) moved forests and wildlife to the **Concurrent List**.
⚠ **Entry 17A** = forests; **Entry 17B** = wild animals and birds.
**T.N. Godavarman (1995)**: "forest" = every area recorded as forest, **whatever the ownership**.

90.s: The 2002 amendment to the Wildlife (Protection) Act replaced the Indian Board for Wildlife with the
90.x: The 2002 amendment replaced the Indian Board for Wildlife with the National Board for Wildlife.
90.tq: Track the institutional replacement rather than confusing it with bodies created in 2006.
xs: The **2002** amendment replaced the Indian Board for Wildlife with the **National Board for Wildlife** — option **(2)**.
**NTCA** and **WCCB** came with the **2006** amendment; the **Animal Welfare Board** is under the **PCA Act 1960**.
xa: **NBWL** is chaired by the **Prime Minister**; its **Standing Committee** by the **Union Environment Minister**.
The **State Board for Wildlife** is chaired by the **Chief Minister**.
The full NBWL met in **2025** after a **13-year** gap; the Standing Committee cleared **over 97%** of diversion proposals.

90.s: Which international convention’s provisions were specifically brought into the Wildlife (Protection) Act through the 2022 amendment?
90.x: The 2022 amendment incorporated CITES-related provisions, including provisions concerning management and scientific authorities.
90.tq: Distinguish the wildlife-trade convention from other environmental treaties.
xs: The 2022 amendment brought **CITES** provisions into the WPA — option **(3)**.
It provides for CITES **management and scientific authorities**.
xa: After 2022, **Schedule IV** lists specimens in the **CITES Appendices** (**APPSC-GS 2024**).
⚠ The **CBD** is implemented by the **BD Act 2002**, not the WPA.
The amendment came into force in **April 2023**.

90.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the exemptions associated with the Forest Conservation Amendment Act, 2023?
o: Strategic projects within 100 km of international borders
Mandatory Gram Sabha consent for every new exemption
90.x: The amendment is criticised because it is silent on the Forest Rights Act and does not mandate Gram Sabha consent for the new exemptions. Strategic projects, eco-tourism and zoos are among the mentioned exemptions.
90.tq: Find the option that reverses the criticism about the absence of Gram Sabha consent.
xs: **Mandatory Gram Sabha consent** is not in the amendment — option **(4)**.
The amendment is **silent on FRA** and mandates no Gram Sabha consent for the new exemptions.
**Eco-tourism**, strategic projects within **100 km** of borders and **zoos** are listed exemptions.
xa: **FCR 2022** dropped the consent clause, sparking an **NCST-MoEFCC** dispute.
**Van (S.E.S.) Amendment Rules 2025**: assisted natural regeneration counts as **"forestry activities"**; CA and NPV do not apply.
Coverage excludes land converted to non-forest use before **12 Dec 1996**.

90.s: Which one of the following correctly describes a change introduced by the Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act, 2023?
o: All biodiversity offences were made criminal offences with imprisonment only
Benefit-sharing was abolished for all users
Offences were decriminalised and civil penalties were introduced
Foreign entities were exempted from NBA approval
90.x: The amendment decriminalised offences and introduced civil penalties. It did not abolish benefit-sharing or exempt foreign entities from prior NBA approval.
90.tq: Identify the precise legal-consequence change and reject extreme alternatives.
xs: The BD (Amendment) Act 2023 **decriminalised offences** and introduced **civil penalties** — option **(3)**.
It did not abolish benefit-sharing; it only exempted **AYUSH practitioners** and **cultivated medicinal plants**.
**Foreign nationals and foreign-incorporated entities** still need prior **NBA** approval.
xa: It came into force on **1 April 2024** with the **BD Rules 2024**.
NBA approval time cut from **180 to 90 days**; IPR applications stay at **180**.
The **NBA** is headquartered in **Chennai**.

90.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the National Green Tribunal's jurisdiction as described in the legal framework?
o: It hears cases under the Forest Rights Act but not under the Forest (Conservation) Act.
It has jurisdiction only over the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act.
It hears cases under the Wildlife (Protection) Act but not under the Environment (Protection) Act.
It hears cases under seven laws, including the Forest (Conservation) Act, Environment (Protection) Act and Biological Diversity Act.
90.x: The NGT hears cases under seven specified laws, including the FCA 1980, EPA 1986 and BD Act 2002. The framework states that it cannot hear cases under the WPA 1972 or FRA 2006.
90.tq: Use the inclusion and exclusion of statutes to separate NGT jurisdiction from ordinary wildlife law.
xs: The NGT hears cases under **seven laws**, incl. the **Forest (Conservation) Act**, **Environment (Protection) Act** and **Biological Diversity Act** — option **(4)**.
It **cannot** hear cases under the **WPA 1972** or **FRA 2006**, so options (1) and (3) are wrong.
xa: The **FCA 1980** regulates diversion of forest land.
The **BD Act 2002** implements the **CBD**.
The **PCA Act 1960** is the parent Act of the **Animal Welfare Board**.

90.s: Which one of the following Acts was enacted to protect wild animals, birds and plants and to manage their habitats?
o: Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960
90.x: The WPA 1972 protects wild animals, birds and plants and manages their habitats (APPSC 2025 key). The EPA 1986 is an umbrella law for environmental protection and pollution control; the FCA 1980 checks deforestation and regulates diversion of forest land; the PCA Act 1960 prevents cruelty to animals and is the parent Act of the AWBI.
90.tq: Wild animals, birds AND plants = WPA 1972, not EPA or FCA.
xs: The **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972** protects **wild animals, birds and plants** and manages their habitats — option **(2)**.
**EPA 1986** is the pollution umbrella law; **FCA 1980** checks deforestation; **PCA Act 1960** prevents cruelty to animals.
xa: This was the **APPSC 2025** key.
The WPA has **66 sections** in **7 chapters**.

90.s: Why would a Maharashtra Bill amending Section 12 of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 require the assent of the President of India?
o: Because relocation of leopards is exclusively a constitutional power of the President
Because the Bill concerns only private forests
Because it seeks to amend a central law
Because every wildlife sanctuary is administered by the President
90.x: The Bill requires Presidential assent because it amends a central law, the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. The other statements assign incorrect constitutional or administrative reasons.
90.tq: Ask who has authority when a State Bill affects a central law.
xs: The Bill needs **President's assent** because it **amends a central law** — option **(3)**.
It is the **WPA (Maharashtra Amendment) Bill 2026** on **Sec. 12** to relocate leopards.
xa: **Section 12** gives permits for education, research, scientific management, incl. **translocation**.
It also proposed moving the leopard from **Schedule I to II**.
Environmentalists called the down-listing **"regressive"**.

90.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
 a. Indian Forest Act, 1927
 b. Wildlife Protection Act, 1972
 c. Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980
 d. Environment Protection Act, 1986

List-II
 i. Forest administration/legal framework
 ii. Wildlife protection
 iii. Regulation of forest-land diversion
 iv. Environmental protection
90.x: The Indian Forest Act, 1927, sets the forest legal framework, the WPA, 1972, protects wildlife, the FCA, 1980, controls diversion of forest land, and the EPA, 1986, protects the environment. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
90.tq: Match each Act to its subject.
n: The Indian Forest Act was enacted in 1927. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The Indian Forest Act provides a forest administration and legal framework. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The Wildlife Protection Act was enacted in 1972. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The Wildlife Protection Act concerns wildlife protection. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The Forest (Conservation) Act was enacted in 1980. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The Forest (Conservation) Act regulates forest-land diversion. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The Environment Protection Act was enacted in 1986. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The Environment Protection Act concerns environmental protection. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
xs: The correct match is **a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Indian Forest Act, 1927** — **forest administration and legal framework**; **WPA, 1972** — **wildlife protection**.
**Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980** — **regulates forest-land diversion**; **EPA, 1986** — **environmental protection**.
xa: First Indian Forest Act: **1865**; the **1878** Act introduced reserved, protected and village forests.
FCA 1980 came into force on **25 October 1980**.
**Forest Rights Act, 2006**: rights of forest-dwelling communities.

90.s: The Supreme Court’s restriction relating to mining provides that mining is barred within what distance of every national park and sanctuary, unless a larger eco-sensitive zone is notified?
90.x: Mining is barred within 1 kilometre of every national park and sanctuary boundary unless a larger eco-sensitive zone is notified.
90.tq: Recall the statutory-distance figure and distinguish it from larger possible buffer zones.
xs: The SC bars mining within **1 kilometre** of every national park and sanctuary boundary — option **(2)**.
The bar applies **unless a larger eco-sensitive zone (ESZ)** is notified.
xa: Under the **WPA**, mining is **prohibited inside NPs and sanctuaries** themselves.
India has **1,000+ protected areas** covering **1,75,169.42 sq km**, i.e. **5.32%** of land area.
The **NBWL Standing Committee** clears projects in or near PAs and tiger corridors.

90.s:
Consider the following statements about forest categories under the Indian Forest Act, 1927:
1. Reserved forests have the strictest protection; felling, grazing and hunting are barred unless expressly permitted.
2. A village forest is a protected forest assigned to a village community.
3. In a protected forest, activities are allowed unless specifically prohibited.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
90.x: Statement 1 is correct: reserved forests are the most strictly protected. Statement 2 is wrong: a village forest is a reserved forest (not a protected forest) assigned to a village community. Statement 3 is correct: in protected forests everything is allowed unless specifically prohibited. Hence 1 and 3 only.
90.tq: Reserved = barred unless permitted; protected = allowed unless prohibited; village = reserved forest given to a village.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: **reserved forests** are the strictest — felling, grazing and hunting barred unless expressly permitted.
Statement 2 is wrong: a **village forest** is a **reserved** forest (not a protected forest) assigned to a village community.
Statement 3: in a **protected forest**, activities are allowed unless specifically prohibited.
xa: Reserved forest = **Ch. II, Sec. 3-27**; village forest = **Ch. III, Sec. 28**; protected forest = **Ch. IV, Sec. 29-34**.
⚠ **Reserved** = barred unless permitted; **Protected** = allowed unless prohibited.
The three categories were first introduced by the **1878** Indian Forest Act.

90.s: Section 26 of the Indian Forest Act, 1927 primarily deals with
o: regulation of forests that are not government property
assignment of reserved forests to village communities
acts prohibited in a reserved forest, including punishable trespass
removal of bamboo from non-forest land without a permit
90.x: Section 26 lists prohibited acts in a reserved forest and makes trespass punishable.
90.tq: Match the offence section with its specific prohibited conduct.
xs: **Sec. 26** lists **acts prohibited in a reserved forest** and makes **trespass** punishable — option **(3)**.
Regulating non-government forests is **Sec. 35**; village forests come under **Sec. 28**.
Bamboo removal without permit came from the **2017 amendment** to **Sec. 2(7)**.
xa: Sec. 26 was the **APPSC 2024** key.
Reserved forests (**Ch. II, Sec. 3-27**) are the most strictly protected category.
The 2017 change came as an Ordinance in **2017** and an Act in **2018**.

90.s:
Consider the following statements about the 2017 amendment to the Indian Forest Act, 1927:
1. It was first issued as an Ordinance in 2017 and enacted as an Act in 2018.
2. It removed bamboo grown outside forest areas from the definition of 'tree' in Section 2(7).
3. Bamboo grown on private or non-forest land still needs a transit permit to be felled and transported.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
90.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Ordinance 2017, Act 2018, removing bamboo grown outside forests from 'tree' in Section 2(7). Statement 3 is wrong: such bamboo can now be felled and transported without a permit. Hence 1 and 2 only.
90.tq: Bamboo outside forests is no longer a 'tree', so no permit is needed.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: Ordinance in **2017**, Act in **2018**.
Statement 2: **bamboo grown outside forest areas** was removed from "tree" in **Sec. 2(7)**.
Statement 3 is wrong: such bamboo can now be felled and transported **without a permit**.
xa: The 1927 Act was criticised for hurting **forest-dwellers' livelihoods**, pushing reform towards **community rights**.
**Sec. 35** lets the State regulate forests that are not government property.
The **1927** Act is a colonial consolidating law **still in force**.

90.s: Unclassed forests are best described as forests:
o: outside the reserved and protected categories
with the highest restriction on activities
regulated more strictly than protected forests
90.x: Unclassed forests are those outside the reserved and protected classes, and they are the least regulated.
90.tq: Rank reserved, protected and unclassed forests.
n: Unclassed forests are forests outside the reserved and protected categories. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
xs: **Unclassed forests** lie **outside the reserved and protected categories** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Reserved forests** have the **highest restrictions** — activities **prohibited unless permitted**.
**Protected forests** are **more regulated** than unclassed forests.
xa: ⚠ **Reserved** = barred unless permitted; **Protected** = allowed unless prohibited.
**Sec. 26** of the IFA lists acts prohibited in a reserved forest and makes **trespass** punishable.
**Village forest**: a reserved forest assigned to a village community (**Sec. 28**).

90.s: Under the National Forest Policy, 1952, which one of the following combinations correctly represents the prescribed forest-cover targets?
o: Two-thirds of the land under forest, including 60% in hills and 25% in plains
One-fourth of the land under forest, including 50% in hills and 33% in plains
One-third of the land under forest, including 25% in hills and 60% in plains
One-third of the land under forest, including 60% in hills and 25% in plains
90.x: The 1952 policy aimed at one-third of the total land under forest, with 60% forest cover in hills and 25% in plains.
90.tq: Split the overall target from the separate hill and plain targets.
xs: **NFP 1952**: **one-third** of land under forest, **60% in hills** and **25% in plains** — option **(4)**.
Option (3) swaps the hill and plain figures; **two-thirds** is the 1988 target for hills only.
xa: **NFP 1988**: **33%** of geographical area under forest/tree cover; **two-thirds (66%)** in hilly and mountainous regions.
⚠ **1952** hills = **60%**; **1988** hills = **two-thirds (66%)**; national target both ≈ one-third.
NFP **1952** was the first post-Independence forest policy.

90.s: Under the National Forest Policy, 1952, which of the following was included in the forest classification?
o: National, Protected and Village forests, along with Tree-lands
Protected, Village and Urban forests, along with Wetlands
National, Private and Social forests, along with Wastelands
National, Reserved and Community forests, along with Grasslands
90.x: The 1952 Forest Policy classified forests as national, protected and village forests, plus tree-lands.
90.tq: Recall the 1952 forest classes.
n: The National Forest Policy, 1952, classified forests as national forests. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
The National Forest Policy, 1952, classified forests as protected forests. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
The National Forest Policy, 1952, classified forests as village forests. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
The National Forest Policy, 1952, classified tree-lands as a forest category. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
The National Forest Policy was formulated in 1952. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
xs: The **National Forest Policy, 1952** classified forests as **national**, **protected** and **village forests**, plus **tree-lands** — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ **National parks** were **not** among its classes.
No urban, private, social, reserved or community forest classes appear in the 1952 scheme.
xa: 1952 target: one-third under forest — **60% in hills**, **25% in plains**.
The **1988** Policy set **33%** nationally and **two-thirds** in hills.
A **Draft** National Forest Policy came in **2018**.

90.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) National Forest Policy, 1952
(b) National Forest Policy, 1988
(c) National Action Plan on Climate Change
(d) Draft National Forest Policy

List-II
(i) Launched in 2008
(ii) Issued in 2018
(iii) Classified forests as national, protected and village forests and tree-lands
(iv) Target of one-third of the geographical area under forest
90.x: The 1952 Policy classified forests as national, protected and village forests plus tree-lands, the 1988 Policy set a one-third forest-cover target, the NAPCC was launched in 2008, and the Draft Forest Policy came in 2018, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
90.tq: Link each policy to its year or defining feature.
n: Ecological afforestation is a major objective of the National Forest Policy, 1988. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
