xa: Water vapour's GWP is **variable**; lifetime **~9 days**.
**India's irrigated paddy** emits **3.9 million t methane/yr**.
The **Global Methane Pledge** targets **30%** cut from **2020** levels by **2030**.

92.s: Which one of the following statements about the classification of atmospheric gases is correct?
o: Carbon monoxide is the largest natural contributor to the greenhouse effect
Nitrogen and oxygen are indirect greenhouse gases, while argon is the principal greenhouse gas
Nitrogen, oxygen and argon are major greenhouse gases, whereas carbon monoxide is a primary greenhouse gas
Nitrogen, oxygen and argon are not greenhouse gases, while carbon monoxide acts only as an indirect greenhouse gas
92.x: N2, O2 and Ar are not greenhouse gases. Carbon monoxide is considered only an indirect greenhouse gas rather than a primary one.
92.tq: Distinguish primary greenhouse gases from gases that influence warming indirectly.
xs: **N2, O2 and Ar are not GHGs**; **carbon monoxide** is only an **indirect GHG** — option **(4)**.
The largest natural contributor is **water vapour**, not CO.
xa: Nitrogen **78.08%**, oxygen **20.95%**, argon **0.93%** — the bulk of air does not absorb IR.
Asked in **APPSC 2025**.
**CO2** is only ~**0.04%** of air yet the main anthropogenic driver.

92.s: The United Nations Secretary-General’s Call to Action on Methane was launched during which event and covered which sectors?
o: Montreal Protocol Conference; refrigeration, aerosols and solvents
London Climate Action Week; waste, agriculture and fossil fuels
World Water Week; irrigation, fisheries and tourism
92.x: The Call to Action on Methane was launched at London Climate Action Week on 24 June 2026 and addresses waste, agriculture and fossil-fuel operations.
92.tq: Match the initiative with its event date and sectoral scope.
xs: The **UN Secretary-General** launched it at **London Climate Action Week**, covering **waste, agriculture and fossil fuels** — option **(2)**.
It was launched on **24 Jun 2026**.
**COP26** is where the separate **Global Methane Pledge** was launched.
xa: The **Global Methane Pledge** targets a **30%** cut from **2020** levels by **2030**.
**India has not signed** the Pledge.
Methane supplies about **16%** of long-lived GHG forcing.

92.s: Which one of the following is the largest contributor to greenhouse-gas emissions among the sources listed below?
o: Fossil-fuel combustion for energy, transport and industry
92.x: Fossil-fuel combustion involving coal, oil and gas for energy, transport and industry is the largest contributor. Other important sources include deforestation, industrial processes, agriculture and waste.
92.tq: Identify the dominant sector and distinguish it from other recognised sources.
xs: **Fossil-fuel combustion** (coal, oil, gas for energy, transport and industry) is the largest contributor — option **(3)**.
Others: deforestation/land use, **cement**, agriculture, waste.
xa: Top CO2 emitters (**2024**): **China 12**, **USA 4.9**, **India 3.2** billion tonnes.
**425 "carbon bombs"** found by **LINGO** would use up the 1.5°C budget **twice over**.
India's carbon bombs: **Gevra** (Chhattisgarh) and **Rajmahal** (Jharkhand) coal mines.

92.s: Which one of the following statements about the European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) is correct?
o: It was fully enforced from 1 January 2025.
It was fully enforced from 1 January 2024.
It is scheduled to be fully enforced from 1 January 2027.
It was fully enforced from 1 January 2026.
92.x: The European Union's CBAM was fully enforced from 1 January 2026.
92.tq: Distinguish the implementation year from nearby transition or proposed dates.
xs: The EU **CBAM** was fully enforced from **1 January 2026** — option **(4)**.
**2024**, **2025** and **2027** are distractor years.
xa: The USA **repealed** the **2009 "endangerment finding"** on six GHGs.
India's **social cost of carbon** is **$86 per tonne** — highest globally.

92.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Water vapour is the most abundant natural greenhouse gas.
II. Carbon dioxide contributes about two-thirds of the warming effect of long-lived greenhouse gases.
III. CFCs are not greenhouse gases.
IV. Sulphur dioxide is an acid-rain gas, but not a greenhouse gas.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: I, II and IV are correct: water vapour is the most abundant natural greenhouse gas, CO₂ causes about 66% of the warming from long-lived greenhouse gases (WMO), and SO₂ causes acid rain but is not a greenhouse gas. III is false because CFCs are greenhouse gases as well as ozone-depleting.
92.tq: Separate greenhouse gases from acid-rain gases; CFCs are both ozone-depleting and greenhouse.
n: Water vapour is the most abundant natural greenhouse gas. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 57-59]
Carbon dioxide has a 66% share according to the WMO source. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 57-59]
CFCs are ozone-depleting substances and greenhouse gases. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 57-59]
Sulfur dioxide (SO₂) is an acid-rain gas and not a greenhouse gas. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 57-59]
xs: Statements **I, II and IV** are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
I: **water vapour** is the **most abundant natural** GHG.
II: **CO₂** is the **main contributor** — a **66% share** per the **WMO**.
III is wrong: **CFCs** are **greenhouse gases** as well as **ozone-depleting**; IV: **SO₂** is an **acid-rain** gas, not a GHG.
xa: Anthropogenic / synthetic GHGs: **CFCs**, **HFCs**, **PFCs**, **SF₆**.
Textbook share of enhanced effect: **CO2 60% > CH4 20% > CFCs 15% > N2O 5%**.

92.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Nitrous oxide
(b) Ozone in the troposphere
(c) Ozone in the stratosphere
(d) Methane

List-II
(i) Marsh gas
(ii) Associated with nitrogen fertilizers
(iii) Pollutant formed from NOx and hydrocarbons in sunlight
(iv) Provides ultraviolet protection
92.x: Nitrous oxide comes from nitrogen fertilisers, tropospheric ozone is a smog pollutant formed from NOx and hydrocarbons in sunlight, stratospheric ozone blocks UV, and methane is marsh gas, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
92.tq: Distinguish ground-level ozone from the protective stratospheric layer.
n: Nitrous oxide is associated with nitrogen fertilizers. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 57-59]
Ozone is a greenhouse gas. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 57-59]
Ozone provides ultraviolet protection in the stratosphere. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 57-59]
Methane is known as marsh gas. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 57-59]
xs: The correct match is **(a)-(ii), (b)-(iii), (c)-(iv), (d)-(i)** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Nitrous oxide** — **nitrogen fertilizers**; **tropospheric ozone** — formed from **NOx** and hydrocarbons in sunlight.
**Stratospheric ozone** — **ultraviolet protection**; **methane** — **marsh gas**.
xa: Paddy fields release **methane** under **anaerobic conditions**.
N2O GWP **265-298**, lifetime **~114 years**.
Methane GWP **28-36**, lifetime **~12 years**.

92.s: Among the following, which is the correct order of the major natural contributors to the greenhouse effect, from highest to lowest contribution?
o: Water vapour > Methane > Carbon dioxide > Ozone > CFCs
Carbon dioxide > Water vapour > Methane > CFCs > Ozone
Carbon dioxide > Methane > Water vapour > Ozone > CFCs
Water vapour > Carbon dioxide > Methane > Ozone > CFCs
92.x: Water vapour is the largest natural contributor, followed by carbon dioxide, methane, ozone and CFCs.
92.tq: Use the complete contribution order rather than identifying only the largest gas.
xs: **Water vapour > CO2 > CH4 > O3 > CFCs** — option **(4)**.
**Water vapour** is the biggest natural contributor; CO2 leads only the **enhanced** effect.
xa: Enhanced-effect shares: **CO2 60% > CH4 20% > CFCs 15% > N2O 5%**.
⚠ Natural effect: **water vapour** biggest; enhanced effect: **CO2** biggest.

92.s:
Consider the following gases in relation to the enhanced greenhouse effect:
1. Carbon dioxide
2. Methane
3. CFCs
4. Nitrous oxide
Which of the following represents their approximate shares in descending order?
92.x: The textbook distribution given is approximately CO2 60%, methane 20%, CFCs 15% and nitrous oxide 5%.
92.tq: Compare the numerical shares and check both the order and the percentages.
xs: Option (4) swaps **CH4** and **CFCs**.
xa: **CO2** contributes most to the **enhanced** effect (**APPSC 2025** key).
**WMO Bulletin**: CO2 accounted for about **81%** of the **54%** rise in warming effect, **1990-2024**.
**CH4** supplies about **16%** of radiative forcing from long-lived GHGs.

92.s: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct regarding the relationship between deforestation and carbon dioxide?
o: Deforestation is an anthropogenic activity associated with enhanced greenhouse effect
Deforestation generally raises the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere
Deforestation can reduce the capacity of vegetation to absorb carbon dioxide
Deforestation decreases atmospheric carbon dioxide by removing carbon-storing trees
92.x: Deforestation does not decrease atmospheric CO2; it reduces carbon uptake and may release stored carbon, thereby raising atmospheric CO2.
92.tq: Find the reversed cause-and-effect statement in the environmental process.
xs: "Deforestation **decreases** atmospheric CO2" is **not correct** — option **(4)**.
Deforestation **raises** CO2 by destroying sinks; burning or rotting trees release stored carbon.
xa: The same trap appeared in **APPSC 2025** and **APPSC-G2 2025**.
**CO2** sources: fossil fuels, **deforestation**, cement.
**Carbon sequestration** stores carbon in sinks: soil carbon, biochar, agroforestry, forests.

92.s: Which of the following greenhouse gases does not occur naturally and is entirely man-made?
92.x: CFCs are synthetic chemicals made for refrigerants and aerosols, so they are entirely man-made greenhouse gases. Water vapour, methane and nitrous oxide all occur naturally, though human activity adds to them.
92.tq: Pick the gas that exists only because industry makes it.
n: Nitrogen oxide is not a naturally occurring greenhouse gas in the cited PYQ. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 57-59]
xs: **CFCs** are **entirely man-made** (**synthetic**) greenhouse gases — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Water vapour**, **methane** and **nitrous oxide** are **natural** GHGs.
⚠ Other notes say nitrous oxide is **both natural and man-made**.
xa: Other synthetic GHGs: **HFCs**, **PFCs**, **SF₆**.
CFCs come from **coolants/refrigeration**, foams and **aerosol sprays**.
**Perfluoromethane** comes from **aluminium production**.

92.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Global Warming Potential (GWP)?
o: The amount of solar radiation reflected by a gas in comparison with water vapour
The atmospheric concentration of a gas compared with that of oxygen over one year
The heat absorbed by a gas over a specified period, usually 100 years, relative to the same mass of carbon dioxide
The time required by a gas to disappear completely from the atmosphere
92.x: GWP compares the heat absorbed over a specified period, generally 100 years, by a given mass of a greenhouse gas with that absorbed by the same mass of CO2.
92.tq: Discriminate between GWP, atmospheric lifetime and concentration.
xs: **GWP** = heat a gas absorbs over a period, usually **100 years**, **relative to the same mass of CO2** — option **(3)**.
It is not reflection, concentration or lifetime — lifetime is a separate column (e.g. **CH4 ~12 years**).
xa: Older values CH4 **21** and N2O **310** are superseded.

92.s: Tipping points in the climate system are best understood as:
o: Thresholds beyond which small changes may trigger self-perpetuating shifts that cannot be reversed on human timescales
Fixed temperature values that apply equally to every ecosystem
Linear changes that can always be reversed immediately
Short-term daily variations in weather with no long-term effects
92.x: Tipping points are thresholds at which small changes can initiate self-perpetuating, non-linear shifts that are not reversible on human timescales.
92.tq: Distinguish threshold-driven non-linear change from ordinary gradual variation.
xs: **Tipping points** are thresholds where small changes trigger **self-perpetuating shifts that cannot be reversed on human timescales** — option **(1)**.
They are **non-linear**, so options (2)-(4) are wrong.
xa: Example: beyond about **2°C**, parts of the **Amazon** could turn into savanna → a carbon source.
Source: **UNSG Scientific Advisory Board Brief #12**.
India sought clarity at the **Bonn talks** on using tipping points for policy.

92.s: The Keeling curve refers to the continuous record of atmospheric carbon dioxide measured at:
o: Mauna Loa, Hawaii, maintained since 1958 by Charles David Keeling
Barrow, Alaska, maintained by the IPCC
Vostok, Antarctica, maintained since 1979 by the WMO
92.x: The Keeling curve is the continuous atmospheric CO2 record from Mauna Loa, Hawaii, begun in 1958 by Charles David Keeling.
92.tq: Combine the place, starting year and scientist to avoid location and agency swaps.
xs: The **Keeling curve** is the CO2 record at **Mauna Loa, Hawaii**, since **1958**, by **Charles David Keeling** — option **(1)**.
Greenland, Barrow and Vostok are not the Keeling site.
xa: **Ice cores** give past CO2 and temperature from trapped air bubbles.
CO2 reached **423.9 ppm** in **2024**.
⚠ **Keeling curve** = **Mauna Loa** (**1958**); **climate sensitivity** = doubling of CO2.

92.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the natural and enhanced greenhouse effects:
1. The natural greenhouse effect occurs without human intervention and helps keep Earth habitable.
2. The enhanced greenhouse effect results when human activities raise atmospheric greenhouse-gas concentrations.
3. Greenhouse-gas levels in the natural greenhouse effect have remained stable for thousands of years, whereas fossil fuels, deforestation, industry, agriculture and waste contribute to the enhanced effect.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: All three statements correctly distinguish the natural greenhouse effect from its anthropogenically enhanced form.
92.tq: Compare the two columns by checking human role, stability of gas levels and consequences.
xs: All three statements are correct — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
Statement 1: the **natural** effect needs **no human role** and keeps Earth habitable.
Statement 2: the **enhanced** effect comes from human activities raising **GHG concentrations**.
Statement 3: natural GHG levels were **stable for millennia**; fossil fuels, deforestation, industry, agriculture and waste drive the enhanced effect.
xa: Without the greenhouse effect, Earth would average about **-18°C** instead of **+15°C**.
**APPSC 2025** key: the primary cause of global warming is an **increase in GHGs**.

92.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Water vapour is the most important greenhouse gas.
2. Human beings increase atmospheric water vapour mainly indirectly by warming the air.
3. Water vapour is primarily a synthetic greenhouse gas released by refrigeration equipment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: Water vapour is the most important greenhouse gas, and human influence on it is mainly indirect through warming. It is natural, not primarily synthetic or refrigeration-derived.
92.tq: Use the natural-versus-synthetic distinction to reject the false statement.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: **water vapour is the most important GHG** (**APPSC GS 2023**).
Statement 2: humans raise it only **indirectly**, by warming the air.
Statement 3 is wrong: water vapour is **natural**; refrigeration gives **CFCs / HFCs**.
xa: **Water vapour feedback**: warmer air holds more water vapour and traps more heat.
Its atmospheric lifetime is about **9 days**.
⚠ Natural effect: **water vapour** biggest; enhanced effect: **CO2** biggest.

92.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Radiative forcing is the change in Earth's energy balance caused by a factor such as a greenhouse gas, expressed in W/m2.
2. Climate sensitivity is the warming that follows a 50% rise in atmospheric CO2 over the pre-industrial level.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
92.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: climate sensitivity is the warming after a doubling of CO2 over pre-industrial levels, not a 50% rise. So '1 only'.
92.tq: Climate sensitivity = doubling of CO2.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **radiative forcing** is the change in Earth's **energy balance** (**W/m²**) caused by a factor such as a GHG.
Statement 2 is wrong: **climate sensitivity** is the warming after a **doubling of CO2**, not a 50% rise.
xa: **Albedo feedback**: melting ice lowers albedo → more heat absorbed.
**Keeling curve**: CO2 record at **Mauna Loa, Hawaii**, since **1958**.
**Tipping points**: thresholds triggering **self-perpetuating shifts** that cannot be reversed.

92.s:
Consider the following statements based on the WMO Greenhouse Gas Bulletin (October 2025):
1. Methane supplies about 16% of the radiative forcing from long-lived greenhouse gases.
2. Carbon dioxide accounted for about 81% of the 54% rise in the warming effect of long-lived greenhouse gases during 1990-2024.
3. Methane accounted for most of the rise in the warming effect of long-lived greenhouse gases during 1990-2024.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: Statement 1 is correct: CH4 gives about 16% of long-lived GHG forcing. Statement 2 is correct: CO2 accounted for about 81% of the 54% rise. Statement 3 is wrong: it was CO2, not methane, that drove most of the rise. So '1 and 2 only'; options with 3 are wrong.
92.tq: CH4 = 16% of forcing; CO2 = 81% of the rise.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: **CH4** supplies about **16%** of long-lived GHG forcing.
Statement 2: **CO2** accounted for about **81%** of the **54%** rise (**1990-2024**).
Statement 3 is wrong: **CO2**, not methane, drove most of the rise.
xa: CH4 is at **266%** of pre-industrial; CO2 **152%**; N2O **125%**.

92.s:
Consider the following statements about climate feedbacks:
1. Melting ice lowers albedo, so more heat is absorbed.
2. Warming can release methane from methane hydrates in permafrost and seabed sediments, a positive feedback.
3. Warmer air holds less water vapour, so the water vapour feedback cools the climate.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct positive feedbacks. Statement 3 is wrong: warmer air holds more water vapour, which traps more heat, so the water vapour feedback amplifies warming. So '1 and 2 only'.
92.tq: Albedo, methane hydrate and water vapour feedbacks are all positive.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **albedo feedback** — melting ice **lowers albedo**, so more heat is absorbed.
Statement 2 is correct: warming releases methane from **methane hydrates** in permafrost and seabed — a **positive feedback**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **warmer air holds more water vapour**, which **traps more heat**.
xa: **Ice cores**: trapped air bubbles give past CO2 and temperature.
Tipping example: beyond about **2°C**, parts of the **Amazon** could turn into savanna.
Climate sensitivity = warming after a **doubling of CO2**.

92.s:
Consider the following statements about tropospheric ozone:
1. It is a primary pollutant emitted directly from vehicle exhausts.
2. It is a short-lived greenhouse gas that cuts crop yields.
3. Its effects are generally worst in summer.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: tropospheric ozone is a secondary pollutant formed from NOx and VOCs in sunlight, not emitted directly. So '2 and 3 only'.
92.tq: Surface ozone = secondary (NOx + VOCs + sunlight).
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is wrong: tropospheric ozone is a **secondary** pollutant formed from **NOx + VOCs in sunlight**.
Statements 2 and 3 are correct: it is a **short-lived GHG** that **cuts crop yields**, and is **worst in summer**.
xa: SLCPs: **black carbon**, **methane**, **HFCs**, **tropospheric ozone** — tackled by the **Climate and Clean Air Coalition**.
**Black carbon** comes from **incomplete combustion** and **darkens snow and ice**.
Methane lifetime is **~12 years**.

92.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Black carbon can darken snow and ice surfaces.
2. Darkening of snow and ice by black carbon can accelerate glacier melt.
3. Black carbon is produced exclusively by fossil-fuel combustion.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: Black carbon darkens snow and ice and accelerates melting. It is produced by incomplete combustion of both biomass and diesel, so statement 3 is false.
92.tq: Find the false statement containing the extreme word ‘exclusively’.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statements 1 and 2: black carbon **darkens snow and ice**, reduces albedo and **speeds glacier melt**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it comes from **incomplete combustion** of **biomass** as well as **diesel**.
xa: Lifetime: **days to weeks**.
It is one of the **SLCPs**, with methane, HFCs and tropospheric ozone.

92.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Deforestation and land-use change can remove carbon sinks.
2. Agricultural fertilisers contribute to nitrous oxide emissions.
3. Livestock contribute to methane emissions.
4. Deforestation increases carbon sinks in all circumstances.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Deforestation and land-use change generally remove or reduce carbon sinks rather than increase them in all circumstances.
92.tq: Find the absolute and reversed statement before selecting the coded option.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: deforestation **destroys carbon sinks**.
Statements 2 and 3: **synthetic fertilisers** release **N2O**; **livestock** (enteric fermentation) release **CH4**.
Statement 4 is wrong: deforestation removes sinks, it never increases them.
xa: **Fossil-fuel combustion** is the largest contributor.
**Rice paddies** also release CH4.

92.s:
Consider the following pairs relating to global carbon dioxide emissions in 2024:
1. China — 12 billion tonnes a year
2. United States of America — 4.9 billion tonnes a year
3. India — 3.2 billion tonnes a year
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
92.x: The reported 2024 figures are China 12 billion tonnes, the United States 4.9 billion tonnes and India 3.2 billion tonnes. India ranked third among these top emitters.
92.tq: Check both the ranking and the associated numerical values.
xs: All three pairs are correct — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(1)**.
**China 12**, **USA 4.9**, **India 3.2** billion tonnes a year (**Global Carbon Budget 2025**).
India is the **3rd** largest emitter.
xa: India's **social cost of carbon** is the **highest globally**, **$86 per tonne** of CO2.
The **GHG Emission Intensity Target (Amendment) Rules 2025** cover **208 units**.

92.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the 2024 atmospheric carbon dioxide concentration is correct?
o: It was about 423.9 ppm, the highest level in approximately two million years.
It was close to the pre-industrial level and represented a two-century low.
It was below 280 ppm because of increased ocean absorption.
It was about 1,000 ppm, the highest level since the formation of Earth.
92.x: CO₂ reached about 423.9 ppm in 2024, described as the highest concentration in approximately two million years; the pre-industrial level was around 280 ppm.
92.tq: Combine a precise numerical value with its historical comparison.
xs: CO2 was about **423.9 ppm** in **2024**, the **highest in about two million years** — option **(1)**.
Pre-industrial was only about **278-280 ppm**, so options (2) and (3) are wrong.
xa: The **3.5 ppm** rise was the **largest annual rise since 1957**.
CO2 is **152%** of pre-industrial.
Earlier notes give **419 ppm**.

92.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the WMO Greenhouse Gas Bulletin 2025 (data for 2024):
1. Atmospheric CO2 rose by 3.5 ppm in 2024, the largest annual rise since 1957.
2. Methane stood at about 266% of its pre-industrial level.
3. Nitrous oxide stood at about 152% of its pre-industrial level.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: Statement 1 is correct: CO2 rose 3.5 ppm to 423.9 ppm, the biggest rise since 1957. Statement 2 is correct: CH4 is at 266% of pre-industrial. Statement 3 is wrong: 152% is the figure for CO2; N2O is at 125%. So '1 and 2 only'.
92.tq: CO2 152%, CH4 266%, N2O 125% - don't swap them.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: CO2 rose **3.5 ppm** in **2024**, the **largest since 1957**.
Statement 2: CH4 is at **266%** of pre-industrial.
Statement 3 is wrong: **152%** is CO2; **N2O** is at **125%**.
xa: CO2 stood at **423.9 ppm**.
CH4 supplies about **16%** of long-lived GHG forcing.

92.s: During 1971–2010, the oceans absorbed approximately what proportion of the extra energy associated with warming?
92.x: The oceans took up more than 90% of the extra energy during 1971–2010.
92.tq: Identify the approximate range rather than choosing an absolute claim.
xs: The oceans took up **more than 90%** of the extra energy (**1971-2010**) — option **(4)**.
**Ocean heat** uptake is one of the main observed impacts of warming, alongside ice loss.
xa: Oceans absorb CO2 → **carbonic acid** (ocean acidification).
**Coral bleaching** is driven by warming; recovery takes **15+ years**.
**Arctic sea ice** shrank **3.5-4.1% per decade** (**1979-2012**).

92.s:
Consider the following statements about observed cryospheric changes:
1. Both the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets are losing mass.
2. Arctic sea ice shrank by approximately 3.5–4.1% per decade during 1979–2012.
3. Antarctic sea ice has shown uninterrupted expansion since 2015.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: Both major ice sheets are losing mass, and Arctic sea ice declined by about 3.5–4.1% per decade during 1979–2012. The statement about uninterrupted Antarctic expansion is incorrect.
92.tq: Find the false trend statement among otherwise precise cryosphere observations.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: **Greenland and Antarctic** ice sheets are both **losing mass**.
Statement 2: **Arctic sea ice** shrank **3.5-4.1% per decade** (**1979-2012**).
Statement 3 is wrong: Antarctic sea ice has **collapsed since 2015**, not expanded.
xa: The collapse: **GHGs + ozone hole** strengthened the westerlies, lifting warm **Circumpolar Deep Water**.
Oceans took up **over 90%** of extra energy (**1971-2010**).
**Albedo feedback**: melting ice lowers albedo → more heat absorbed.

92.s: Ocean acidification is primarily caused by which of the following processes?
o: Evaporation of seawater and formation of sulphuric acid
Absorption of atmospheric CO2 by oceans and formation of carbonic acid
Freezing of seawater and release of hydrochloric acid
Absorption of atmospheric oxygen and formation of nitric acid
92.x: When oceans absorb carbon dioxide, carbonic acid forms, lowering ocean pH and causing acidification.
92.tq: Link the environmental effect with the specific chemical process responsible.
xs: Ocean acidification = oceans **absorb CO2** and form **carbonic acid** — option **(2)**.
It is not sulphuric, hydrochloric or nitric acid.
xa: **Coral bleaching** is driven by warming; recovery takes **15+ years**.
CO2 reached **423.9 ppm** in **2024**.
Oceans took up **over 90%** of the extra energy (**1971-2010**).

92.s: Which year marked the first occasion on which the global mean temperature exceeded 1.5°C above the pre-industrial level?
92.x: The year 2024 was reported as the first year in which the global mean temperature exceeded 1.5°C above the pre-industrial level.
92.tq: Distinguish the specific record year from nearby climate-policy years.
xs: **2024** was the **first calendar year above 1.5°C** (WMO) — option **(3)**.
Average warming is about **1.3°C** above pre-industrial (UNSG brief, **24 Jun 2026**).
xa: The world is now described as a **1.5°C world**; a strong **El Niño** is expected in **2027**.
Each of the last three decades was warmer than any since **1850**.
CO2 rose **3.5 ppm** in **2024**, the **largest since 1957**.

92.s:
Consider the following statements regarding carbon bombs:
1. A carbon bomb is a fossil-fuel project capable of emitting over 1 gigatonne of CO2.
2. LINGO has identified 425 such carbon bombs.
3. The identified projects would use the 1.5°C carbon budget twice over.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: Each carbon bomb can emit over 1 Gt CO2; LINGO identified 425, and their combined emissions would consume the 1.5°C carbon budget twice over.
92.tq: Combine the definition, count and consequence without confusing gigatonne with megatonne.
xs: All three are correct — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
A **carbon bomb** can emit over **1 gigatonne CO2**.
**LINGO** found **425** of them; together they would use up the **1.5°C** budget **twice over**.
xa: India's: **Gevra** (Chhattisgarh) and **Rajmahal** (Jharkhand) coal mines.
⚠ **CCUS** = point sources; **direct air capture** = ambient air.

92.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Carbon footprint is the total greenhouse gases emitted by the activities of a person, organisation or product, expressed in tonnes of CO2 per year.
2. Carbon sequestration means storing carbon in sinks such as soil carbon, biochar, agroforestry and forests.
3. CCUS refers to machines that pull CO2 straight from ambient air.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: Statement 1 is correct: this is the definition of carbon footprint. Statement 2 is correct: sequestration stores carbon in sinks like soil, biochar, agroforestry and forests. Statement 3 is wrong: pulling CO2 from ambient air is direct air capture; CCUS captures CO2 from factory flue gases (point sources). So '1 and 2 only'.
92.tq: CCUS = point source (flue gas); DAC = ambient air.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: **carbon footprint** = total GHGs emitted by a person, organisation or product, in **tonnes CO2 per year** (**APPSC-GS 2025**).
Statement 2: **carbon sequestration** = storing carbon in sinks — soil carbon, biochar, agroforestry, forests.
Statement 3 is wrong: pulling CO2 from ambient air is **direct air capture**; **CCUS** captures it from **factory flue gases**.
xa: ⚠ **CCUS** = point sources; **direct air capture** = ambient air.
India's **CCUS road map** covers **industry only**.

92.s:
Consider the following statements about the Global Methane Pledge:
1. It aims to cut global methane emissions by 30% from 2020 levels by 2030.
2. It was launched at COP26 in Glasgow in 2021.
3. India is a signatory to the Pledge.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
92.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Pledge targets a 30% cut in methane from 2020 levels by 2030 and was launched at COP26 (Glasgow, 2021). Statement 3 is wrong: India has not signed it (Global Methane Status Report 2025 by UNEP and CCAC). Hence 1 and 2 only.
92.tq: Methane Pledge = 30% by 2030 from 2020, COP26; India has NOT signed.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: cut methane **30% from 2020 levels by 2030**.
Statement 2: launched at **COP26 (Glasgow, 2021)**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **India has not signed** (Global Methane Status Report **2025**, UNEP and CCAC).
xa: India's irrigated paddy emits **3.9 million t methane/yr** — a little more than Germany's total.
The UNSG's **Call to Action on Methane** came at **London Climate Action Week** (**2026**).

92.s: The UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2025 assessed that updated nationally determined contributions would lead approximately to warming of:
92.x: The UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2025 projected approximately 2.3–2.5°C of warming even with updated NDCs.
92.tq: Test the projected range and distinguish it from the Paris temperature goals.
xs: Even updated NDCs lead to **2.3-2.5°C** — option **(4)**.
The report is the **UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2025 ("Off Target")**.
xa: **UNEP Limiting Overshoot (Sep 2026)**: **1.8°C** if every pledge delivered vs **2.6°C** on current policies.
Path: **"overshoot, peak and decline"** back below **1.5°C** by **2100**.
**2024** was already the first year above **1.5°C**.

92.s: According to the UNEP Limiting Overshoot assessment, which pair correctly represents the projected warming outcomes?
o: 2.6°C if every pledge is delivered; 1.8°C under current policies
1.5°C if every pledge is delivered; 2.0°C under current policies
1.8°C under current policies; 1.5°C if every pledge is delivered
1.8°C if every pledge is delivered; 2.6°C under current policies
92.x: The assessment indicates 1.8°C if every pledge is delivered and 2.6°C under current policies. It outlines an overshoot, peak and decline pathway back below 1.5°C by 2100.
92.tq: Use the reversed-comparison trap by matching each outcome to the policy condition.
xs: **1.8°C if every pledge is delivered**; **2.6°C under current policies** — option **(4)**.
Option (1) swaps the two figures.
xa: It sets an **"overshoot, peak and decline"** path back below **1.5°C** by **2100**.
The **Emissions Gap Report 2025** projects **2.3-2.5°C** even with updated NDCs.

92.s: India’s CCUS road map, as described in the context of sectoral application, covers primarily:
o: Industry, while agricultural removal is associated with soil carbon, biochar and agroforestry
Only household cooking, while agriculture and industry are excluded
Only direct air capture facilities in urban areas
92.x: India’s CCUS road map covers industry. Agricultural carbon removal is associated with measures such as soil carbon management, biochar and agroforestry.
92.tq: Identify the correct sectoral allocation and reject the reversed scope.
xs: India's CCUS road map covers **industry**; agricultural removal fits **soil carbon, biochar and agroforestry** — option **(2)**.
Agriculture is left out because farm emissions are **diffuse**.
xa: Farm removals fall under **Carbon Dioxide Removal**.
**CCUS** captures CO2 from **factory flue gases** (point sources only).
**Direct air capture** machines pull CO2 from ambient air.

92.s: India's country-level social cost of carbon is reported to be:
92.x: India's country-level social cost of carbon is reported as $86 per tonne of CO2, the highest globally.
92.tq: For numerical options, distinguish the exact reported figure from nearby values.
xs: India's **social cost of carbon** is **$86 per tonne of CO2** — option **(2)**.
It is the **highest globally** at country level.
xa: India is the **3rd** largest emitter at **3.2** billion tonnes (**2024**).
India's carbon bombs: **Gevra** and **Rajmahal** coal mines.

92.s: Which one of the following is the primary cause of the present global warming?
o: Increase in the concentration of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere
Depletion of the stratospheric ozone layer
Increase in the amount of incoming solar radiation
Rise in the proportion of nitrogen and oxygen in the air
92.x: The primary cause of global warming is the increase in greenhouse gases (APPSC 2025 key): heat from sunlight re-radiated by the Earth is absorbed by CO2 and other gases. Ozone depletion is a separate problem; the warming is not explained by more incoming sunlight; and nitrogen and oxygen are not greenhouse gases.
92.tq: Global warming = more GHGs trapping re-radiated infrared.
xs: The primary cause is an **increase in the concentration of greenhouse gases** — option **(1)** (**APPSC 2025** key).
**N2, O2 and Ar are not GHGs**, so a rise in nitrogen and oxygen cannot warm the planet.
Heat re-radiated by the earth is absorbed by **CO2** and other gases (**APPSC GS 2021**).
xa: In the enhanced effect, **CO2** contributes most (**APPSC 2025** key).
**2024** was the **first calendar year above 1.5°C** (WMO).
CO2 reached **423.9 ppm** in **2024**, highest in about **2 million years**.

92.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the short-lived climate pollutants listed?
92.x: The listed short-lived climate pollutants are black carbon, methane, HFCs and tropospheric ozone. Water vapour is not included in that list.
92.tq: Find the odd item outside the specified pollutant group.
xs: **Water vapour** is not an SLCP — option **(4)**.
SLCPs: **black carbon, methane, HFCs, tropospheric ozone** — short lifetime but strong warming.
xa: They are tackled by the **Climate and Clean Air Coalition**.
Black carbon lasts **days to weeks**; methane **~12 years**; tropospheric ozone **weeks to months**.

92.s: The Climate and Clean Air Coalition is associated with action against:
92.x: The Climate and Clean Air Coalition works to address short-lived climate pollutants such as black carbon, methane, HFCs and tropospheric ozone.
92.tq: Match the coalition with the precise environmental problem it addresses.
xs: The **Climate and Clean Air Coalition** tackles **short-lived climate pollutants** — option **(3)**.
SLCPs: **black carbon, methane, HFCs, tropospheric ozone**.
xa: **Black carbon** comes from **incomplete combustion** (biomass, diesel).
The **Global Methane Status Report 2025** was by **UNEP and CCAC**.
Tropospheric ozone is a **secondary** pollutant.

92.s: Which of the following correctly describes the contrasting climate effects of the aerosol types listed below?
o: All aerosols invariably cool the air
Black and brown carbon cool the air, while sulphate droplets warm it
All aerosols invariably warm the air
Black and brown carbon warm the air, while sulphate droplets cool it
92.x: Black and brown carbon have a warming effect on the air, whereas sulphate droplets exert a cooling effect.
92.tq: Test the reversed comparison between warming and cooling aerosol types.
xs: **Black and brown carbon warm** the air; **sulphate droplets cool** it — option **(4)**.
Option (2) reverses the effects; aerosols are not uniformly warming or cooling.
xa: Black carbon comes from **incomplete combustion**.
It darkens **snow and ice**, speeding glacier melt.

92.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Issue — Principal effect
o: Habitat loss — Oxygen depletion caused by oil spillage
92.x: Global warming is associated with rising sea levels. Air pollution is associated with respiratory illness, whereas patches of cooling are linked with sub-regional temperature variation.
92.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate reversed cause-effect relationships.
xs: **Global warming — Rising sea levels** — option **(1)** (**APPSC-GS 2025** match).
**Air pollution** pairs with **respiratory illness**; **sub-regional temperature** shows **patches of cooling**.
**Oxygen depletion** is the effect of **oil spillage**, not habitat loss.
xa: **Burning plastic** reduces **seed germination** (**APPSC-G2 2025**).
Each of the last three decades was warmer than any since **1850**.

92.s: With reference to environmental effects, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Burning plastic has no effect on plant growth.
Oil spillage can cause oxygen depletion in water bodies.
Oil spillage commonly increases dissolved oxygen in affected water bodies.
Burning plastic enhances seed germination by releasing nutrients.
92.x: Oil spillage can cause oxygen depletion in water bodies. Burning plastic can reduce seed germination, not enhance it.
92.tq: Identify the direct ecological consequence rather than choosing an absolute or reversed effect.
xs: **Oil spillage** can cause **oxygen depletion** in water bodies — option **(2)** (**APPSC-G2 2025**).
**Burning plastic** reduces **seed germination** — so options (1) and (4) are wrong.
Option (3) is the reverse of the oil-spill effect.
xa: Global warming → **rising sea levels**; air pollution → **respiratory illness**.
Sub-regional temperature shows **patches of cooling**.

92.s: The 2009 United States endangerment finding was legally connected with which case?
92.x: The 2009 US 'endangerment finding' on six greenhouse gases, which let the EPA regulate vehicle GHG emissions, flowed from the Supreme Court's ruling in Massachusetts v. EPA (2007). The US has since repealed that finding.
92.tq: Use the exact authority and case-name pairing rather than a thematically similar title.
xs: The 2009 **endangerment finding** dated from **Massachusetts vs EPA (2007)** — option **(2)**.
It covered **six GHGs** and let the **EPA** regulate vehicle GHGs.
xa: The USA has since **repealed** the **2009** finding.
The EU **CBAM** was fully enforced from **1 Jan 2026**.

93.s:
Consider the following sequence in ocean carbonate chemistry:
1. Carbonic acid releases hydrogen ions and bicarbonate.
2. Atmospheric carbon dioxide dissolves in seawater.
3. Extra hydrogen ions bind carbonate ions.
4. Less carbonate remains available for shell formation.
Which is the correct sequence?
93.x: Dissolved carbon dioxide forms carbonic acid, which releases hydrogen ions and bicarbonate. The hydrogen ions bind carbonate ions, reducing carbonate availability for shells.
93.tq: Follow the cause-to-effect chemical chain from dissolution to reduced shell-building material.
xs: The sequence is **2, 1, 3, 4** — option **(1)**.
CO2 **dissolves** → **carbonic acid** releases **H+ and bicarbonate**.
Extra H+ **binds carbonate ions** → **less carbonate** for shells.
xa: Shellfish get **weaker shells**; **pteropods** suffer **shell dissolution**.
Corals show **slower skeleton growth**, more bleaching and erosion.

93.s:
Consider the following statements about ocean acidification:
1. It is called the 'evil twin of global warming' because it is another consequence of anthropogenic CO2.
2. The oceans absorb only about one-tenth of anthropogenic CO2.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
93.x: Statement 1 is correct: ocean acidification, 'the other CO2 problem', comes from dissolution of atmospheric CO2. Statement 2 is wrong: the oceans absorb about one-third (30-40%) of anthropogenic CO2. So '1 only'.
93.tq: Oceans take up about one-third of human CO2.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: ocean acidification — the "**evil twin of global warming**" — comes from **dissolution of atmospheric CO2**.
Statement 2 is wrong: oceans absorb about **one-third** of anthropogenic CO2 (also cited **30-40%**).
xa: CO2 + H2O → **carbonic acid** → less carbonate for shells.
Surface pH **8.2 → ~8.1** = roughly **30%** rise in acidity; ocean still **alkaline**.
Worst in **cold/temperate and Arctic waters**.

93.s:
Consider the following statements regarding surface-ocean pH:
1. It has fallen from about 8.2 in the pre-industrial period to about 8.1 today.
2. This fall represents roughly a 30% rise in acidity.
3. As a result, ocean water has now become acidic (pH below 7).
Which of the statements given above are correct?
93.x: Statement 1 is correct: pH fell from 8.2 to about 8.1. Statement 2 is correct: this is about a 30% rise in acidity. Statement 3 is wrong: at pH ~8.1 the ocean is still alkaline; it has only become less alkaline. So '1 and 2 only'.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: surface pH fell from **8.2** (pre-industrial) to **~8.1**.
Statement 2: that is roughly a **30% rise in acidity**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the ocean is **still alkaline**.
xa: Oceans absorb about **one-third** of anthropogenic CO2.
**SDG 14.3** indicator = **average marine pH** at representative stations.

93.s: Ocean acidification is expected to be more severe in cold, temperate and Arctic waters primarily because:
o: Arctic waters contain no marine organisms capable of calcification.
Carbonate ions are completely absent from tropical waters.
Cold waters do not exchange gases with the atmosphere.
Carbon dioxide is more soluble in colder water, and melting sea ice exposes additional water.
93.x: Cold water dissolves more carbon dioxide, while melting sea ice exposes previously covered water to atmospheric carbon dioxide.
93.tq: Connect the regional pattern with gas solubility and sea-ice exposure.
xs: **CO2 is more soluble in colder water**, and **melting sea ice exposes** more water — option **(4)**.
So **cold/temperate and Arctic waters** are the worst areas.
xa: **Eutrophic bloom collapse** also raises CO2 and worsens acidification.
⚠ pH **8.2 → ~8.1** yet acidity up ~**30%**; the ocean is still **alkaline**.

93.s: Which organism is popularly known as the ‘sea butterfly’ and is vulnerable to shell dissolution under ocean acidification?
93.x: Pteropods are commonly called sea butterflies. Ocean acidification can dissolve their shells, and they are also an important food source for fish.
93.tq: Discriminate the common name from other calcifying organisms in the same ecological group.
xs: The **Pteropod** is the "**sea butterfly**", hit by **shell dissolution** under acidification — option **(4)**.
**Oysters** and **clams** are shellfish (weaker shells); **calcareous phytoplankton** show reduced growth.
xa: Pteropods are a **key food for fish**.
Calcareous phytoplankton effect was asked in **UPSC 2012**.

93.s:
Consider the following statements about marine heatwaves (MHWs):
1. The number of marine heatwaves has halved since 1982.
2. A marine heatwave is a sea-surface temperature 3-4°C above average for at least 5 days.
3. Cyclones passing over marine heatwaves can have up to 20% stronger winds.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
93.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct; such cyclones also get up to 12% more rain. Statement 1 is wrong: the number of marine heatwaves has doubled since 1982, not halved. So '2 and 3 only'.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is wrong: the number of marine heatwaves has **doubled since 1982**, not halved.
Statement 2 is correct: an **MHW** is SST **3-4°C** above average for **at least 5 days**.
Statement 3 is correct: cyclones over MHWs can have up to **20%** stronger winds and **12%** more rain.
xa: Heatwaves are now the **strongest global driver of coral-cover decline** (GCRMN **2026**).
**Deoxygenation**: algal blooms decay → hypoxic **dead zones**.
**Pteropods** ("**sea butterflies**") suffer shell dissolution.

93.s: According to recent assessments, the strongest global driver of coral-cover decline is:
93.x: Marine heatwaves are identified as the strongest global driver of coral-cover decline.
93.tq: Select the dominant driver rather than a possible but secondary environmental factor.
xs: **Marine heatwaves** are the strongest global driver of coral-cover decline — option **(2)** (**GCRMN 2026**).
An MHW is SST **3-4°C** above average for at least **5 days**.
xa: **INCOIS** (SAMUDRA app) issues **coral bleaching alerts**.
**NCCR, Chennai** monitors reef health via **D-COIN**.

93.s: Which sequence correctly explains the formation of hypoxic dead zones from nutrient runoff?
o: Nutrient runoff → algal bloom → decay consumes oxygen → hypoxic dead zone
Nutrient runoff → oxygen production only → reef expansion → hypoxic dead zone
Nutrient runoff → carbonate formation → oxygen release → dead zone
Nutrient runoff → sea-ice formation → oxygen enrichment → dead zone
93.x: Nutrient runoff promotes algal blooms; when the biomass decays, decomposition consumes oxygen and can create hypoxic dead zones.
93.tq: Arrange the causal chain from nutrient input to oxygen depletion.
xs: **Nutrient runoff → algal bloom → decay consumes oxygen → hypoxic dead zone** — option **(1)**.
This is **deoxygenation**; decay also adds CO2 and worsens acidification.
xa: **Eutrophic bloom collapse** raises CO2.
Cold and **Arctic waters** are worst for acidification.

93.s: In relation to the Great Nicobar project, the National Green Tribunal in February 2026 asked the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change to ensure:
o: Suspension of all marine research until 2030
Coral protection and regeneration through a proved scientific method
Complete removal of all coral colonies from the islands
Exclusive use of Biorock technology in every Indian reef
93.x: The NGT asked MoEFCC to ensure coral protection and coral regeneration through a proved scientific method for the Great Nicobar project.
93.tq: Match the authority with the specific direction, avoiding broader claims not stated.
xs: NGT asked for **coral protection** and **regeneration through a proved scientific method** — option **(2)**.
The project uses **coral translocation**, moving colonies away from project sites.
xa: **Biorock** is used in the **Gulf of Kutch** by **ZSI**.
**3D-printed reef modules** are off **Ramanathapuram (TN)** under **PMMSY**.

93.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 3D-printed artificial reef modules off Ramanathapuram (Tamil Nadu):
1. They were deployed under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY).
2. The nearby Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve is India's first terrestrial biosphere reserve.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
93.x: Statement 1 is correct: the modules were deployed under PMMSY. Statement 2 is wrong: the Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve is India's first marine biosphere reserve, not terrestrial. So '1 only'.
93.tq: Ramanathapuram reefs = PMMSY; Gulf of Mannar = first MARINE BR.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: the modules were deployed under **PMMSY**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Gulf of Mannar** is India's first **marine** biosphere reserve.
xa: ⚠ **Biorock** = **Gulf of Kutch**; 3D-printed reefs = **Ramanathapuram**.
**Lakshadweep** is entirely **atoll reef**.

93.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. SDG target 14.3 seeks to minimise and address ocean acidification.
2. The indicator for SDG 14.3 is average marine pH measured at representative stations.
3. NCCR, Chennai issues coral bleaching alerts and marine heatwave advisories through the SAMUDRA app.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
93.x: Statement 1 is correct: SDG 14.3 is about minimising and addressing ocean acidification. Statement 2 is correct: its indicator is average marine pH at representative stations. Statement 3 is wrong: the SAMUDRA app alerts come from INCOIS; NCCR, Chennai monitors reef health through D-COIN. So '1 and 2 only'.
93.tq: SDG 14.3 = acidification, measured by pH; SAMUDRA = INCOIS.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: **SDG 14.3** aims to minimise and address ocean acidification.
Statement 2: its indicator is **average marine pH** at representative stations.
Statement 3 is wrong: **SAMUDRA** alerts come from **INCOIS**; **NCCR, Chennai** uses **D-COIN**.
xa: **SDG 14** is not ranked by **NITI Aayog** for AP.
Surface pH has fallen from **8.2 → ~8.1**.

93.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with respect to deep-sea exploration?
o: Varaha — deep-sea mining system trialled at 5,270 m
Matsya 6000 — artificial reef module off Ramanathapuram
SAMUDRA — coral transplantation frame in Gulf of Kutch
93.x: Varaha is the deep-sea mining system trialled at 5,270 metres. Matsya 6000 is the submersible used under Samudrayaan, while SAMUDRA and D-COIN are associated with monitoring and advisories.
93.tq: Use the equipment-function-depth association and reject cross-domain substitutions.
xs: **Varaha — deep-sea mining system trialled at 5,270 m** — option **(1)**.
**Matsya 6000** is the **submersible**; **SAMUDRA** is INCOIS's app; **D-COIN** is NCCR's monitoring platform.
xa: Indian scientists dived to **5,002 m** in the Atlantic.
⚠ **Matsya 6000** = submersible; **Varaha** = deep-sea mining system.

93.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Biorock technology:
1. It passes a low-voltage current through steel frames so that limestone is deposited and coral fragments grow faster.
2. It has been used in the Gulf of Kutch by the Zoological Survey of India.
3. It involves moving coral colonies away from project sites.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
93.x: Statement 1 is correct: Biorock (mineral accretion) uses low-voltage current on steel frames to deposit limestone. Statement 2 is correct: ZSI has used it in the Gulf of Kutch. Statement 3 is wrong: moving colonies away from project sites is coral translocation/transplantation, a different method. So '1 and 2 only'.
93.tq: Biorock = current + steel + limestone (ZSI, Gulf of Kutch).
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: **Biorock** (mineral accretion) runs **low-voltage current** on steel frames to deposit **limestone**.
Statement 2: **ZSI** used it in the **Gulf of Kutch**.
Statement 3 is wrong: moving colonies is **coral translocation/transplantation**.
xa: **UPSC 2022**: Biorock = "restoration of damaged coral reefs".
⚠ **Biorock** = **Gulf of Kutch**; 3D-printed reefs = **Ramanathapuram**.

93.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the reef character of Lakshadweep?
o: It is entirely composed of atoll reefs.
It is entirely composed of barrier reefs.
It contains only deep-sea cold-water reefs.
It is entirely composed of fringing reefs.
93.x: Lakshadweep is made up entirely of atoll reefs. The giant Pavona clavus (potato patch coral) colony was found there at Kadmat. Fringing, barrier and deep-sea cold-water reefs do not describe it.
93.tq: Discriminate among the closely related reef-formation terms: fringing, barrier and atoll.
xs: **Lakshadweep** is **entirely atoll reef** — option **(1)**.
A giant **Pavona clavus** (**potato patch coral**) colony was found at **Kadmat**.
xa: **Gulf of Mannar** is India's first **marine** biosphere reserve.
**Biorock** restoration is used in the **Gulf of Kutch**.

94.s:
With reference to the climate of India, consider the following statements:
1. The year 2019 was the seventh warmest year in India since 1901.
2. Bihar suffered the most among the States during the conditions associated with the 2019 climate record.
3. The official temperature series records a rise of more than 2°C in India between 1901 and 2018.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
94.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect; the MoES assessment places the rise at about 0.7°C.
94.tq: Find the exaggerated numerical statement among otherwise precise facts.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: **2019** was India's **7th warmest year** since **1901** (**APPSC 2018** key).
Statement 2: **Bihar** suffered the most in 2019.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **MoES** assessment gives about **0.7°C over 1901-2018**; "crossed 2°C" does not match the official series.
xa: IMD: India's **2020** average yearly temperature was **25.78°C** (**APPSC 2021** key).
⚠ **MoES 2020** = India's first national climate assessment.

94.s: Which organisation published India's first national climate assessment, *Assessment of Climate Change over the Indian Region*, in 2020?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
94.x: India's first national climate assessment was published in 2020 by the Ministry of Earth Sciences.
94.tq: Apply the institution-publication association and distinguish neighbouring ministries.
xs: The **Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES)** published it in **2020** — option **(3)**.
The **IMD** issues the separate annual **Statement on Climate of India**.
xa: It records about **0.7°C** warming over **1901-2018**.
IMD: **2019** was the **7th warmest year**; **2020** averaged **25.78°C**.
⚠ **MoES 2020** = first national assessment; **2019** = 7th warmest (Bihar); **2020** = **25.78°C**.

94.s: According to the IMD Statement on Climate of India, the average yearly temperature of India in 2020 was about
94.x: The IMD statement put India's 2020 average yearly temperature at 25.78°C (APPSC 2021 key). The other values are distractors not given in the statement; for context, the MoES assessment puts India's long-term rise at about 0.7°C over 1901-2018.
94.tq: IMD 2020 average = 25.78°C (APPSC 2021).
xs: India's **2020** average yearly temperature was **25.78°C** — option **(1)** (**APPSC 2021** key).
The figure comes from the **IMD Statement on Climate of India**.
xa: **2019** was the **7th warmest year** since **1901**; **Bihar** suffered the most.
MoES puts India's long-term rise at about **0.7°C** over **1901-2018**.

94.s:
Assertion (A): Climate change can intensify extreme rainfall and flash-flood risks in India.
Reason (R): Each 1°C rise in temperature enables the atmosphere to hold approximately 7 percent more moisture.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
94.x: Both statements are true, and the greater moisture-holding capacity of warmer air helps explain the intensification of extreme rainfall and associated flash floods.
94.tq: Test whether the quantitative reason directly explains the climate-impact assertion.
xs: **Both A and R are true**, and R is the **correct explanation** of A — option **(1)**.
Each **1°C** of warming lets air hold about **7%** more moisture → heavier rain.
xa: Extreme pre-monsoon rainfall events **doubled** (**1981-2020**).
Flash floods surged in **Brahmaputra, Ganga and Krishna** basins.

94.s: Which of the following statements regarding climate change and Indian agriculture is correct?
o: Climate change is already reducing wheat productivity in India, requiring climate-resilient varieties and digital soil-health tools.
Climate change is already increasing wheat productivity throughout India.
Digital soil-health tools are used exclusively for livestock management.
Climate change affects only rice and has no reported effect on wheat.
94.x: Climate change is already cutting wheat productivity in India. Climate-resilient varieties and digital soil-health tools are identified as responses.
94.tq: Identify the precise cause-and-response relationship rather than an absolute claim.
xs: Climate change is **already cutting wheat productivity**, so **climate-resilient varieties** and **digital soil-health tools** are needed — option **(1)**.
Productivity is falling, not rising, and wheat is clearly affected.
xa: Wheat/maize lose **4-10%** yield per **1 C**.
**2,996** climate-resilient varieties released **2014-2025**; heat-tolerant wheat **HD 3385**.

94.s: Which organisation monitors glacier mass balance and retreat, maps areas vulnerable to Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs) and updates the Himalayan glacier inventory in India?
o: Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services
National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research
94.x: The Geological Survey of India performs these monitoring, mapping and inventory-related functions for Himalayan glaciers.
94.tq: Identify the organisation by matching it with its specific scientific responsibility.
xs: The **Geological Survey of India** does this — option **(1)**.
It monitors **mass balance and retreat**, maps **GLOF**-vulnerable areas and updates the **Himalayan glacier inventory**.
**NCPOR** runs the **Himansh** station, a separate role.
xa: **Himansh**: above **4,000 m**, **Lahaul-Spiti**, **2016**.
**CWC** issues flood forecasts at **350** stations.

94.s:
Consider the following statements about the Climate Risk Index (CRI) 2025:
1. It ranked India the 9th most climate-affected country over 1995-2024.
2. It is published by Germanwatch, a German NGO based in Bonn, and is usually released at the COP.
3. India's annual rank worsened from 15th to 10th.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
94.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; India saw 430 extreme events and about $170 billion losses over 1995-2024. Statement 3 is wrong: India's annual rank improved from 10th to 15th, not the reverse. So '1 and 2 only'.
94.tq: CRI 2025: 9th over 30 years, 15th annual.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **CRI 2025** ranked India the **9th most climate-affected** country over **1995-2024**.
Statement 2 is correct: published by **Germanwatch**, a German NGO in **Bonn**, usually released at the **COP**.
Statement 3 is wrong: India's annual rank **improved** from **10th to 15th**.
xa: India had **430** extreme events and **$170 billion** losses over 1995-2024.
**68%** of India's area is **drought-prone** (NDMA).
NICRA: **651** districts assessed → **310** highly vulnerable.

94.s: Which of the following statements regarding the World Meteorological Organization is correct?
o: It is a financial institution established in 1950 with headquarters at London.
It is a UN specialised agency established in 1950 with headquarters at Geneva.
It is a UN environmental programme established in 1988 with headquarters at Bonn.
It is a scientific panel established in 2007 with headquarters at Paris.
94.x: WMO was set up in 1950, became a UN specialised agency in 1951 and is headquartered in Geneva.
94.tq: Use the organisation–status–date–headquarters combination to reject swapped institutional identities.
xs: **WMO** is a **UN specialised agency** set up in **1950**, HQ **Geneva** — option **(2)**.
It became a UN specialised agency in **1951**; it is not a financial institution or based in London.
**1988** is the **IPCC**'s founding year (by WMO + UNEP), and **2007** is its Nobel Peace Prize year.
xa: WMO publishes the **State of the Global Climate** (2026 edition: indicators "**flashing red**").
The **UK Met Office** is lead centre for WMO's **Global Annual to Decadal Climate Update 2026-2035**.
The **IPCC** assesses literature and does **no research of its own**.

94.s: The ODI has estimated that climate change could have which of the following effects on India by 2100 and 2040, respectively?
o: Loss of 1–2% of GDP a year by 2100 and a 3.5% fall in poverty by 2040
Loss of 3–10% of GDP a year by 2100 and a 3.5% rise in poverty by 2040
Loss of 3–10% of GDP a year by 2040 and a 1.5% rise in poverty by 2100
Loss of 10–15% of GDP a year by 2040 and a 5% fall in poverty by 2100
94.x: The ODI estimates that India could lose 3–10% of GDP annually by 2100, while poverty could rise by 3.5% by 2040.
94.tq: Match each figure with its correct time horizon before eliminating reversed-year options.
xs: **ODI**: India could lose **3-10% of GDP** a year by **2100**; poverty could **rise 3.5%** by **2040** — option **(2)**.
Option (3) swaps the years; options (1) and (4) show a poverty fall.
xa: World Bank: **45 million Indians** into extreme poverty within **15 years**.
India's **CRI 2025** losses: **$170 billion** over **1995-2024**.

94.s: The Andhra Pradesh Heat Wave Action Plan is cited as an example of which adaptation measure?
94.x: The Andhra Pradesh Heat Wave Action Plan is cited as a model of early-warning and preparedness action.
94.tq: Recognise the function of a named action plan from its hazard context.
xs: It is cited as a model of **early warning and preparedness** — option **(2)**.
In the same row, **CWC** flood forecasts at **350** stations.
xa: **APSDMA Heatwave Action Plan 2026**: heatwaves kill more in AP than any other natural disaster.
**Ahmedabad** drew up South Asia's first Heat Action Plan (**2013**).

94.s: The 2026 edition of the WMO's State of the Global Climate report characterised climate indicators as
94.x: The 2026 edition described the indicators as 'flashing red' and highlighted accelerating change.
94.tq: Identify the exact headline phrase rather than a general description of climate change.
xs: The **2026** edition said indicators are **"flashing red"**, with **accelerating change** — option **(1)**.
The report is the **WMO State of the Global Climate**.
xa: WMO's decadal update gives a **91%** chance of one year above **1.5 C** (**2026-2035**).
WMO HQ is in **Geneva**.

94.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with respect to climate-related risks in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Kurnool — sea-level rise caused by polar ice sheets
94.x: Heat stress is specifically noted in Rayalaseema. Coastal erosion is associated with Uppada, while the other two pairs assign unrelated risks or locations.
94.tq: Use location-risk matching and reject geographically misplaced hazards.
xs: **Rayalaseema — heat stress** is correctly matched — option **(2)**.
AP's climate risks include **heat in Palnadu + Rayalaseema**; Rayalaseema also faces **chronic drought**.
**Palnadu** is a heat hotspot, not an erosion site; coastal erosion is at **Uppada (Kakinada district)**.
**Uppada** has nothing to do with Himalayan glaciers, and **Kurnool** is linked to **Pre-Monsoon Dry Sowing (PMDS)**, not sea-level rise.
xa: Hottest place in AP: **Rentachintala** (Palnadu); heat waves more frequent in **Palnadu, Kurnool and Anantapur**.
IMD heat wave: actual maximum **≥45°C**, whatever the normal maximum.
AP cyclones hit hardest in **North Coastal AP** + **Nellore/Bapatla**, peaking **October-December**.
AP coastline: **1,053 km** (older **974 km**), Srikakulam to Nellore.

94.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
 a. Green alert
 b. Yellow alert
 c. Orange alert
 d. Red alert

List-II
 i. Take action
 ii. Be updated / Monitor
 iii. No action
 iv. Be prepared
94.x: Green means no action, yellow means stay updated, orange means be prepared, and red means take action. The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
94.tq: Order the colour alerts by severity.
n: The green colour alert level indicates normal conditions. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 70-72]
The green colour alert level requires no action. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 70-72]
The yellow colour alert level indicates a heat alert. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 70-72]
The yellow colour alert level requires people to be updated and monitor conditions. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 70-72]
The orange colour alert level indicates a severe heat alert. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 70-72]
The orange colour alert level requires preparedness. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 70-72]
The red colour alert level indicates an extreme heat alert. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 70-72]
The red colour alert level requires action. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 70-72]
The IMD provides early warning through colour-coded alerts. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 70-72]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Green** — **normal**, **no action**; **Yellow** — **heat alert**, **be updated / monitor**.
**Orange** — **severe heat alert**, **preparedness**; **Red** — **extreme heat alert**, **action**.
xa: IMD heat wave: maximum **≥45°C**, whatever the normal.
**Loo** is a heat-wave cause over the **Gangetic plains**.
AP heat hotspots: **Palnadu, Kurnool, Anantapur**; hottest place **Rentachintala**.

94.s: The India Meteorological Department declares a heat wave when the actual maximum temperature reaches
o: 42°C, only when the normal maximum is exceeded
94.x: IMD declares a heat wave when the actual maximum temperature is at least 45°C, regardless of the normal maximum temperature.
94.tq: Separate the absolute threshold from conditions based on normal temperature.
xs: IMD declares a heat wave when the actual maximum is **≥45°C**, **irrespective of the normal maximum** — option **(2)**.
**40°C** or **42°C** are not the IMD threshold given in the notes.
xa: Causes include **meandering Rossby waves → heat domes** and the **loo** over the Gangetic plains.
Indians faced **19.8 heatwave days** in **2024**; **6.6** due to climate change (Lancet Countdown 2025).
⚠ Heat wave = **≥45°C**; survivability = wet-bulb **~35°C**; first Heat Action Plan = **Ahmedabad** (**2013**).

94.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Rentachintala — hottest place in Andhra Pradesh
Palnadu — location of the first Heat Action Plan in South Asia
94.x: Rentachintala in Palnadu is the hottest place in Andhra Pradesh. The other pairs are wrong: South Asia's first Heat Action Plan was Ahmedabad's (2013), CRIDA is in Hyderabad and ICRISAT is at Patancheru, Hyderabad.
94.tq: Use location-based matching and eliminate places linked to other climate institutions or initiatives.
xs: **Rentachintala** (Palnadu) is the **hottest place in Andhra Pradesh** — option **(1)**.
South Asia's first Heat Action Plan was **Ahmedabad's** (**2013**); **CRIDA** is in **Hyderabad**; **ICRISAT** is at **Patancheru, Hyderabad**.
xa: Heat waves are more frequent and intense in **Palnadu, Kurnool and Anantapur**.
**APSDMA Heatwave Action Plan 2026**: heatwaves kill more in AP than any other natural disaster.

94.s: The increasing frequency and intensity of heat waves in Andhra Pradesh have been specifically reported in
94.x: Palnadu, Kurnool and Anantapur are the Andhra Pradesh districts identified as experiencing increasingly frequent and intense heat waves.
94.tq: Test a direct geographic list without substituting nearby districts.
xs: **Palnadu, Kurnool and Anantapur** — option **(3)**.
AP's hottest place, **Rentachintala**, is in **Palnadu**.
xa: **Rayalaseema** faces chronic drought.
**Kurnool** has Pre-Monsoon Dry Sowing in the **2026 El Niño** plan.
AP's **Heat Wave Action Plan** is cited as a model for early warning.

94.s: A wet-bulb temperature of about 35°C is considered a critical limit for human survivability because
o: blood circulation stops immediately at that temperature
humidity becomes zero at that temperature
sweat can no longer cool the body effectively above that temperature
the body stops producing sweat below that temperature
94.x: At a wet-bulb temperature above about 35°C, sweat can no longer cool the body sufficiently, making human survival highly difficult.
94.tq: Link the physical threshold to its physiological mechanism.
xs: Above a **wet-bulb temperature of about 35°C**, **sweat can no longer cool the body** — option **(3)**.
The **World Bank** says India could be among the first to cross it routinely (**UPSC 2025**).
xa: **Kerala and Tamil Nadu** already see wet-bulb about **31°C**.
**Around 40 coastal districts** could warm by more than **1°C by 2040** (CMIP6 study).
Wet-bulb equals dry-bulb at **100%** humidity.

94.s: The first Heat Action Plan in South Asia was prepared for which city in 2013?
94.x: Ahmedabad prepared the first Heat Action Plan in South Asia in 2013.
94.tq: Directly test the paired city and year.
xs: **Ahmedabad** drew up South Asia's first Heat Action Plan in **2013** — option **(3)**.
Plans like this are key because heat → **heatstroke** and **cardiovascular strain**.
xa: **APSDMA Heatwave Action Plan 2026** is AP's equivalent.
IMD heat wave: actual maximum **≥45°C**.
Lancet Countdown: **heat deaths up 23%** since the 1990s.

94.s: Why are adaptation measures considered necessary for Andhra Pradesh’s energy sector under the State Action Plan on Climate Change?
o: Because cyclones have completely stopped electricity generation in coastal districts
Because only solar power is affected by changes in rainfall
Because increased snowfall threatens coal-based power plants
Because heat and erratic rainfall threaten thermal and hydropower generation
94.x: Heat affects thermal power generation, while erratic rainfall threatens hydropower generation. These risks necessitate adaptation measures in the energy sector.
94.tq: Identify the cause-effect relationship between a climate stress and the vulnerable sector.
xs: **Heat and erratic rain** threaten **thermal and hydro generation** — option **(4)**.
The **AP State Climate Change Cell** prescribed **8 adaptation measures for the energy sector**.
xa: Plan: **AP State Action Plan on Climate Change 2025-30**.
**APSDMA Heatwave Action Plan 2026**: heatwaves kill more in AP than any other natural disaster.

94.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Approximately 68% of India's geographical area is drought-prone.
II. Large parts of India are vulnerable because they depend on rain-fed agriculture.
III. In Peninsular India, surface-water availability can become scarce in years of insufficient rainfall.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
94.x: All three are correct: about 68% of India is drought-prone, rain-fed farming makes it vulnerable, and peninsular surface water runs short in poor-rain years.
94.tq: Recall India's drought exposure.
n: Approximately 68% of India’s geographical area is drought-prone. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-24]
Large parts of India depend on rain-fed agriculture and are vulnerable to drought. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-24]
Surface-water availability itself becomes scarce in Peninsular India during years of insufficient rainfall. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-24]
xs: **All three** statements — **I, II and III** — are correct, so option **(3)** is correct.
I: about **68%** of India's area is **drought-prone** (NDMA).
II: large parts of India **depend** on **rain-fed agriculture**, making them **vulnerable** to drought.
III: in **Peninsular India**, **surface-water availability** becomes **scarce** in years of **insufficient rainfall**.
xa: Drought types: **meteorological**, **agricultural**, **hydrological**.
**Over 75%** of districts are extreme-event hotspots (CEEW).
Excess **groundwater withdrawal** aggravates drought in the long run.

94.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. In India, drought is mainly caused by the inadequacy and uneven distribution of rainfall.
II. More than 80% of India’s rainfall is received in less than 100 days during the southwest monsoon.
III. Excess withdrawal of groundwater over replenishment aggravates drought in the long run.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
94.x: All three are correct: uneven and inadequate rain is the main cause, over 80% of rain falls in under 100 monsoon days, and overusing groundwater worsens drought over time.
94.tq: Recall the causes of drought.
n: In India, drought is mainly caused by the inadequacy and uneven distribution of rainfall. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-24]
More than 80% of India’s rainfall is received in less than 100 days during the southwest monsoon. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-24]
Excess withdrawal of groundwater over replenishment aggravates drought in the long run. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-24]
xs: **All three** statements — **I, II and III** — are correct, so option **(3)** is correct.
I: drought is mainly caused by the **inadequacy** and **uneven distribution** of **rainfall**.
II: **more than 80%** of rainfall comes in **less than 100 days** of the **southwest monsoon**.
III: **excess withdrawal of groundwater** over replenishment **aggravates** drought in the long run.
xa: ⚠ Other notes say the SW monsoon gives about **75%** of annual rain.
The **NE monsoon** (Oct-Dec) gives about **11%** of annual rain.
Each **1°C** of warming → about **7%** more atmospheric moisture.

94.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: South Lhonak lake — Sikkim GLOF, October 2023
South Lhonak lake — Nepal flash flood, August 2026
94.x: The South Lhonak lake GLOF occurred in Sikkim in October 2023. The Chamoli disaster occurred in Uttarakhand in February 2021, while Thame floods occurred in 2024.
94.tq: Use the place-event-date combination and reject swapped locations or dates.
xs: **South Lhonak lake — Sikkim GLOF, October 2023** — option **(1)**.
**Chamoli** is in **Uttarakhand** (**Feb 2021**); **Thame** floods were in **2024**.
The **Nepal** flash floods were on **26 Aug 2026** (**>1,000** dead).
xa: ⚠ **Chamoli** = Uttarakhand; **South Lhonak** = Sikkim.
**Gangabal and Nundkol** lakes are highly GLOF-prone.

94.s: Which of the following disease-environment relationships is correctly matched?
o: Warmer and wetter conditions — expansion of dengue and malaria
Floods — reduction of cholera and hepatitis
Heat — prevention of heatstroke and cardiovascular strain
94.x: Warmer and wetter conditions expand dengue and malaria. Floods and heat tend to increase, rather than reduce, the other listed health risks.
94.tq: Match each environmental condition with its actual health consequence.
xs: **Warmer and wetter** conditions → **expansion of dengue and malaria** — option **(1)**.
Floods **raise** cholera and hepatitis; heat **causes** heatstroke and cardiovascular strain; waterlogging **spreads** leptospirosis.
xa: **Dasra** report "**Under the Weather**": **nearly 40% of districts** at high risk.
**Lancet Countdown 2025**: dengue potential **+85%** in India.

94.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India's rainfall:
1. The south-west monsoon gives about 75% of India's annual rainfall.
2. The north-east monsoon (October-December) gives about 11% of the annual rainfall.
3. The north-east monsoon gives more than half of India's annual rainfall.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
94.x: Statement 1 is correct: the SW monsoon gives about 75% of annual rain. Statement 2 is correct: the NE monsoon (Oct-Dec) gives about 11%. Statement 3 is wrong: the NE monsoon's share is about 11%, far below half; it also contradicts statement 1. So '1 and 2 only'.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: the **SW monsoon** gives about **75%** of annual rain.
Statement 2: the **NE monsoon (Oct-Dec)** gives about **11%**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the NE share is far below half.
xa: Some notes give **70-90%** for the SW monsoon.
AP cyclones peak **October-December**.

94.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the approximate yield loss associated with a 1°C rise for wheat and maize?
94.x: Wheat and maize are reported to lose approximately 4–10 percent of yield per 1°C rise.
94.tq: Separate crop-yield loss percentages from livestock heat-stress figures.
xs: Wheat and maize lose **4-10 percent** yield per **1°C** — option **(4)**.
**15-25%** is the milk-yield loss under extreme heat.
xa: Climate change is already **cutting wheat productivity**.
Heat-tolerant wheat: **HD 3385**.

94.s:
With reference to the Himansh station, consider the following statements:
1. It is operated by the National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research.
2. It is located above 4,000 metres in Lahaul-Spiti.
3. It was established in 2016 to study glaciers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
94.x: Himansh is an NCPOR station situated above 4,000 metres in Lahaul-Spiti and established in 2016 for glacier studies.
94.tq: Combine three related factual statements and verify the institution, location and year.
xs: All three are correct — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
**Himansh** is an **NCPOR** station above **4,000 m** in **Lahaul-Spiti**, set up in **2016**.
xa: **GSI** monitors glacier mass balance and maps GLOF areas.
⚠ **Chamoli** = Uttarakhand (**2021**); **South Lhonak** = Sikkim (**2023**); **Himansh** = Lahaul-Spiti.

94.s: Sea-level rise is caused principally by:
o: Decline in atmospheric water vapour alone
Cooling of seawater and expansion of sea ice
Thermal expansion of seawater and melting of glaciers and ice sheets
94.x: Sea-level rise results mainly from thermal expansion of seawater and the addition of water from melting glaciers and ice sheets.
94.tq: Select the option containing both major physical mechanisms.
xs: Sea-level rise comes from **thermal expansion** and **melting glaciers and ice sheets** — option **(4)**.
Cooling and sea-ice growth would not raise sea level.
xa: **IPCC SROCC (Sept 2019)**: oceans absorbed **over 90%** of excess heat.
Sea level is up **~11 cm since 1993** (WMO).
