3. The summits were established as a mechanism of the European Union's CBAM.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: The summits were hosted by India from January 2023 and addressed developing-country finance and technology needs. They were not established as a CBAM mechanism.
95.tq: Reject the unrelated institutional claim and retain the two linked policy statements.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
India has hosted the **Voice of Global South Summits** from **January 2023**.
They voice **developing-country finance and technology needs**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **CBAM** is an **EU carbon levy on imports**, which India opposes.
xa: The **G20 New Delhi Summit (9-10 Sept 2023)** adopted the **Green Development Pact**.
India **leads Global South positions** in climate talks.

95.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Paris Agreement aims to keep warming well below 2°C above the pre-industrial level.
II. The Paris Agreement aims to pursue efforts toward limiting warming to 1.5°C above the pre-industrial level.
III. INDC stands for Intended Nationally Determined Contributions.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
95.x: All three are correct: Paris aims to keep warming well below 2°C and to try for 1.5°C, and INDCs are Intended Nationally Determined Contributions.
95.tq: Recall the Paris temperature goals.

95.s: The UNFCCC seeks primarily to:

xs: India **did not sign the Global Methane Pledge** and stayed out of the **Glasgow Leaders' Declaration on Forests and Land Use** — option **(4)**.
India also did **not** sign the **COP28 Global Renewables and Energy Efficiency Pledge**, so option (1) is wrong.
India ratified the **Paris Agreement** on **2 Oct 2016**.
xa: Global Methane Pledge: launched at **COP26** by **USA and EU**; **30%** cut by **2030**.
India joined the **TFFF** only as an **observer** at COP30.
At COP26 India announced **Panchamrit**.

95.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the change concerning India's proposed hosting of COP33?
o: India announced the bid at COP26 and confirmed it at COP30.
India announced the bid at COP28 and withdrew it in April 2026 after reviewing its commitments for 2028.
India announced and withdrew the bid at COP29.
India withdrew the bid before COP28 was held.
95.x: The Prime Minister announced India's bid for COP33 at COP28 on 1 December 2023; it was withdrawn in April 2026 after a review of commitments for 2028.
95.tq: Track the announcement and withdrawal as a two-event sequence.
xs: India announced its **COP33** bid at **COP28** and **withdrew it in April 2026** after reviewing its **commitments for 2028** — option **(2)**.
PM Modi made the offer at **COP28 Dubai** on **1 Dec 2023**.
xa: The withdrawal letter was dated **2 Apr 2026** and reported **9 Apr 2026**.
**BRICS** had welcomed the bid in **July 2025**.
**South Korea** is now the only Asia-Pacific contender.

95.s: The European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) applies to imports including
o: iron and steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen and electricity
only crude oil and natural gas
95.x: CBAM covers imports of iron and steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen and electricity.
95.tq: Recall the complete sector list rather than selecting a partial or unrelated list.
xs: CBAM covers **iron and steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen and electricity** — option **(2)**.
It is an **EU carbon levy on imports** in these carbon-intensive sectors.
xa: Transitional phase from **2023**; **definitive phase from 1 January 2026**.
India says it **raises export costs for steel and aluminium**.
CBAM aims to prevent **carbon leakage**.

95.s: India has criticised the EU CBAM mainly on the ground that it
o: eliminates all export costs for Indian producers
supports CBDR-RC and strengthens climate equity
violates CBDR-RC and represents green protectionism
applies only to domestic European production
95.x: India argues that CBAM violates the principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC) and amounts to green protectionism.
95.tq: Distinguish India's criticism from the stated purpose of the EU measure.
xs: India says CBAM **violates CBDR-RC** and is **green protectionism** — option **(3)**.
It **raises export costs** for Indian **steel and aluminium**, rather than eliminating them, and applies to **imports**.
xa: India fears **others may copy it**.
The **12th BRICS Environment Ministers' Meeting** (New Delhi) called CBAM "**unilateral, punitive, discriminatory and protectionist**".
CBDR-RC = **Principle 7** (Rio) = **Article 3.1** (UNFCCC) = **Article 2.2** (Paris).

95.s: Which one of the following correctly describes India's position on its net-zero target for 2070?
o: India rejects CBDR and treats the target as an immediate obligation by 2030.
India bases the target exclusively on the 1951 Refugee Convention.
India has abandoned the target because of the CBAM.
India defends the target on the grounds of CBDR and development, although it is criticised as late.
95.x: India's 2070 net-zero target is criticised as late, while India defends it using the principles of common but differentiated responsibilities and development needs.
95.tq: Contrast criticism of the timeline with India's stated justification.
xs: India **defends** its **net zero 2070** on **CBDR** and **development** grounds, though it is **criticised as late** — option **(4)**.
Most developed countries target **2050**.
xa: A large population in poverty needs **growth** and room to industrialise.
India depends on **coal**; it uses clean-coal technology and **CCS/CCUS**.
India's NDC targets **47% by 2035**.

95.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Ocean and Cryosphere — oceans absorbed more than 90% of excess heat
Climate Change and Land — food security
Climate Change and Land — desertification and land degradation
Ocean and Cryosphere — reduction in the frequency of marine heatwaves
95.x: The Ocean and Cryosphere report highlighted that marine heatwaves became more frequent, along with coral bleaching and fisheries impacts. The other pairs are correctly matched.
95.tq: Find the one statement that reverses the reported trend.
xs: **Ocean and Cryosphere — reduction in marine heatwaves** is wrong — option **(4)**.
SROCC says **marine heatwaves became more frequent** (coral bleaching, fisheries).
The other pairs hold: SROCC — oceans absorbed **>90%** of excess heat; SRCCL — **food security**, **desertification** and **land degradation**.
xa: SROCC (**September 2019**): sea level rising from **thermal expansion and ice melt**.
AR6: marine heatwave frequency **doubled (1982-2016)**.
Indicators of Global Climate Change 2025: **marine heatwaves up 61%**.

95.s: Black carbon deposited on snow accelerates glacier melting primarily by
o: preventing solar radiation from reaching the snow
95.x: Black carbon lowers the albedo of snow, causing it to absorb more solar energy and thereby accelerating melting.
95.tq: Apply the albedo relationship to identify the correct cause-and-effect link.
xs: Black carbon on snow **lowers its albedo**, causing faster melting — option **(1)**.
Increasing albedo would slow melting — the opposite effect.
xa: High mountains are warming at **twice the global average**.
**Gangotri Glacier** retreated **1,700 m since 1935**.
Up to **25% of mountain species** may face extinction by **2100**.

95.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
95.x: SSP3 represents Regional Rivalry. SSP1 represents Sustainability, SSP2 the Middle of the Road, SSP4 Inequality and SSP5 Fossil-fuelled Development.
95.tq: Use elimination across the closely related SSP narrative names.
xs: **SSP3 — Regional rivalry** is correctly matched — option **(3)**.
**SSP1** = Sustainability; **SSP2** = Middle of the road; **SSP4** = Inequality; **SSP5** = Fossil-fuelled development.
xa: SSPs are used in **AR6** scenarios.
AR6 illustrative scenario for SSP3: **SSP3-7.0**.
SSPs replaced the **RCPs** of AR5.

96.s: What was the base year adopted for India's Nationally Determined Contributions relating to the reduction of emissions intensity?
96.x: India's NDC commitments on emissions intensity use 2005 as the base year.
96.tq: Direct recall of the base year.
xs: India's NDC emissions-intensity targets use **2005** as the base year — option **(2)**.
The target year is **2030** (APPSC 2019 asked the base year).
xa: India achieved a **36%** cut by **2020**.

96.s:
With reference to India's 2015 INDC, consider the following statements:
1. It targeted about 40% of cumulative electric power installed capacity from non-fossil fuel sources by 2030.
2. It targeted 40% of total electricity generation from non-fossil fuel sources by 2030.
3. It proposed an additional carbon sink of 2.5–3 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent through extra forest and tree cover by 2030.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The target concerned installed electric capacity, not 40% of actual power generation; hence statement 2 is false.
96.tq: Separate installed capacity from electricity generation, a frequent comparison trap.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: about **40%** of cumulative electric power **installed capacity** from non-fossil sources by **2030**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the target is **installed capacity**, not **generation** — a common trap in UPSC notes.
Statement 3 is correct: an additional carbon sink of **2.5-3 billion tonnes CO2e** by 2030.
xa: ⚠ Some notes write "30-35%" and "40% of power generation"; correct = **33-35%** and **installed capacity**.
NDC 3.0 raises the sink to **3.5-4.0 bn t CO2e**; **2.29 bn t** added so far.

96.s:
Consider the following statements about India's updated NDC:
1. It was communicated in August 2022.
2. It raised the emissions-intensity reduction target for 2030 to 47% below 2005 levels.
3. It added Mission LiFE (sustainable lifestyles) as a qualitative element.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Statement 1 is correct: the updated NDC was communicated in August 2022, formalising the Panchamrit. Statement 2 is wrong: the 2022 target is 45%; 47% is the NDC 3.0 target for 2035. Statement 3 is correct: Mission LiFE was added as a qualitative element. Hence 1 and 3 only; options with 2 are wrong.
96.tq: Updated NDC = Aug 2022, 45%, LiFE; 47% belongs to NDC 3.0.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: the **updated NDC** was communicated in **August 2022**, formalising the **Panchamrit**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the 2022 target is **45%**; **47%** is the **NDC 3.0** target for **2035**.
Statement 3 is correct: it added **Mission LiFE** (sustainable lifestyles) as a qualitative element.
xa: The Aug 2022 intensity target of **45%** was asked in **APPSC 2022**.
The 2022 non-fossil capacity target is **50%**.

96.s: India's emissions intensity of GDP had fallen by what percentage below the 2005 level by 2020?
96.x: India achieved a 36% reduction in emissions intensity of GDP below the 2005 level by 2020.
96.tq: Direct recall of a progress figure, separated from the 2030 target figures.
xs: India's emissions intensity fell **36%** below **2005** levels by **2020** — option **(3)**.
**33%** is the lower end of the **2015** target; **45%** is the **2022** target for 2030.
xa: Panchamrit pledge 4: cut emissions intensity **45%** from 2005 by **2030**.
BTR1: **over 20%** of 2022 emissions came from industry.

96.s:
Consider the following statements about India's non-fossil electricity position:
1. More than 50% of installed electric capacity was non-fossil by 2025.
2. About 25% of electricity generated was non-fossil because storage remains limited.
3. The share of non-fossil electricity generation was necessarily equal to its share of installed capacity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Installed capacity and actual generation are different measures; therefore statement 3 is false.
96.tq: Contrast capacity with generation instead of treating the two percentages as identical.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: non-fossil capacity **crossed 50% in June 2025**.
Statement 2 is correct: only ~**25% of power generated** is non-fossil, due to **storage shortage**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **capacity** and **generation** are different measures — the classic trap.
xa: The **National Generation Adequacy Plan** expects **70%** of **1,121 GW** non-fossil by **2035-36**.
BESS under implementation: **43 GWh** by **2028**.

96.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Commitment)
a. INDC 2015 emissions-intensity reduction
b. Updated NDC 2022 emissions-intensity reduction
c. NDC 3.0 emissions-intensity reduction
d. NDC 3.0 non-fossil installed-capacity share

List-II (Target)
i. 47%
ii. 33–35%
iii. 60%
iv. 45%

Codes:
96.x: The 2015 INDC target was 33–35%, the 2022 target was 45%, and NDC 3.0 sets 47% emissions-intensity reduction and 60% non-fossil installed capacity.
96.tq: Start from the sure percentage pairs and eliminate codes with swapped targets.
xs: The match is **a–ii, b–iv, c–i, d–iii** — option **(1)**.
NDC 3.0 → **47%** intensity cut and **60%** non-fossil installed capacity.
xa: All targets use the **2005** base year.
NDC 3.0 carbon sink: **3.5-4.0 bn t CO2e**.
Non-fossil capacity targets rose from about **40%** (2015) to **50%** (2022) to **60%**.

96.s:
With reference to the Panchamrit renewable-energy commitment, consider the following statements:
1. It concerns 50 percent of energy requirements from renewables.
2. In the NDC formulation, it is expressed as 50 percent of installed capacity.
3. Its target year is 2070.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The target year for this commitment is 2030, not 2070; 2070 applies to the net-zero commitment.
96.tq: Apply the capacity-versus-energy distinction and identify the wrong target year.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
The pledge is **50%** of energy needs from **renewables**, expressed in the NDC as **50% of installed capacity**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the target year is **2030**; **2070** is the **net zero** pledge.
xa: It was achieved in **June 2025**; ~**51%** by **Sept 2025**.
Only ~**25%** of power generated is non-fossil.

96.s: Which two Panchamrit commitments entered India's August 2022 Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC)?
o: 500 GW non-fossil capacity and net zero by 2070
45 percent emissions-intensity reduction and 50 percent renewable-energy commitment
One billion tonnes reduction and 500 GW capacity
Net zero by 2070 and one billion tonnes reduction
96.x: The 45 percent emissions-intensity reduction commitment and the 50 percent renewable-energy commitment entered the August 2022 NDC.
96.tq: Identify the two medium-term percentage pledges rather than the capacity, reduction-volume or long-term pledge.
xs: The **45%** intensity cut and **50%** renewable-energy pledges entered the **Aug 2022 NDC** — option **(2)**.
**500 GW**, **1 billion tonnes** and **net zero 2070** stayed outside the NDC.
xa: The 2022 NDC also added **Mission LiFE** as a qualitative element.
Panchamrit was announced at **COP26** on **1 Nov 2021**.
India's **LT-LEDS** was submitted at **COP27 (Nov 2022)**.

96.s:
With reference to net-zero emissions, consider the following statements:
1. It means that greenhouse gases emitted by a country are balanced by removals.
2. Forests and carbon capture can contribute to such removals.
3. It necessarily means that all gross greenhouse-gas emissions have become zero.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Net zero does not require gross emissions to become zero; residual emissions are balanced by removals.
96.tq: Reject the absolute interpretation that confuses net-zero emissions with zero gross emissions.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(3)**.
**Net zero**: remaining GHG emissions are **balanced by removals**.
Removals come from **forests** and **carbon capture**.
Statement 3 is wrong: residual emissions remain — they are offset, so **net additions are zero**.
xa: **CCS/CCUS** captures CO2 from industrial processes.
India's target year: **2070**.

96.s:
Consider the following statements about the Green India Mission:
1. It covers forest cover on 5 Mha and quality improvement on another 5 Mha.
2. Its original 2020 sequestration goal of 50-60 Mt a year was abandoned after 2020.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
96.x: Statement 1 is correct: GIM covers forest cover on 5 Mha plus quality improvement on another 5 Mha. Statement 2 is wrong: the original 50-60 Mt/yr goal was not abandoned but folded into the 2030 carbon-sink target. Hence 1 only.
96.tq: 5 + 5 Mha; old goal folded into the 2030 sink target.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 is correct: GIM covers forest cover on **5 Mha** + quality improvement on another **5 Mha**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the **50-60 Mt/yr** goal was **folded into the 2030 sink target**, not abandoned.
xa: Supporting drives: **Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam (2024)** and **MISHTI**.
A **CAG audit** flagged inadequate funding for GIM.

96.s:
Consider the following statements about Mission LiFE:
1. It shifts the focus from individual behaviour to state action.
2. LiFE is written into India's NDC 3.0.
3. LiFE stands for Lifestyle for Environment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 reverses the idea: Mission LiFE shifts the focus from state action to individual behaviour and mindful consumption. So '2 and 3 only'.
96.tq: LiFE = from state action to individual behaviour.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
Statement 1 is wrong: Mission LiFE shifts the focus **from state action to individual behaviour** (mindful consumption).
Statement 2 is correct: LiFE is written into **NDC 3.0**.
Statement 3 is correct: **LiFE** = **Lifestyle for Environment** (APPSC **2024** key).
xa: Idea **introduced at COP26, Glasgow (2021)**; **Mission LiFE** launched **October 2022** at **Kevadia**.
**LiFE Global Movement**: **5 June 2022**.
Aligned schemes: **UJALA** (LED bulbs), **PAT** (industrial efficiency).

96.s: The Carbon Credit Trading Scheme was designed to contribute to which intensity-reduction target?
96.x: The scheme was designed to meet the 45 percent intensity target.
96.tq: Use the nearby percentage figures as a numerical discrimination test.
xs: The CCTS was designed to meet the **45 percent** intensity target — option **(3)**.
The **45%** target (from **2005**) is in the **Aug 2022** NDC and Panchamrit.
xa: NDC 3.0 raises it to **47%** by **2035**.
India achieved **36%** by **2020**.
CCTS is **intensity-based**, not cap-based.

96.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India’s negotiating stance on climate change:
1. India invokes equity and climate justice.
2. India supports the principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities.
3. NDC 3.0 is framed around continuity and incremental advance within India’s equitable share.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: All three statements describe India’s stated negotiating position: equity, climate justice, CBDR-RC, and continuity with incremental advance within its equitable share.
96.tq: Combine the three linked principles and policy formulations in a coded statement question.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
India's principles: **equity, CBDR-RC and climate justice**.
**NDC 3.0** is framed as "**continuity and incremental advance**" within India's **equitable share**.
xa: India relies mainly on **domestic resources (about 83%)** for climate finance.
At **Bonn SB64** India sought an agenda item on developed-country finance obligations.

96.s: The Power Ministry's National Generation Adequacy Plan expects what share of 1,121 GW to be non-fossil by 2035–36?
96.x: The plan expects 70% of the projected 1,121 GW capacity to be non-fossil by 2035–36.
96.tq: Pair the percentage with the total capacity and target year.
xs: The **National Generation Adequacy Plan** expects **70%** of **1,121 GW** to be non-fossil by **2035-36** — option **(3)**.
**60%** is the **NDC 3.0** capacity target; **50%** was crossed in **June 2025**.
xa: ⚠ **Capacity** crossed **50%**, but **generation** is only ~**25%**.
Peak demand: **270.8 GW (May 2026)**.

96.s: The principal criticism concerning the capacity-versus-generation gap is that:
o: Installed capacity alone does not indicate the actual electricity generated
Renewable capacity cannot be measured in gigawatts
Generation is always greater than installed capacity
96.x: The criticism is that capacity figures may overstate the transition unless actual electricity generation is also considered.
96.tq: Translate a policy debate into its practical implication.
xs: **Installed capacity** does not show the **electricity actually generated** — option **(1)**.
Non-fossil **capacity** crossed **50%**, but only ~**25%** of power **generated** is non-fossil, due to **storage shortage**.
xa: NDC 3.0 is called easily achievable, but **generation, not capacity**, is what counts.
The NDC target is non-fossil **installed capacity**, not generation.

96.s: The Intended Nationally Determined Contribution (INDC) of India was submitted to the UNFCCC in:
96.x: India submitted its INDC to the UNFCCC in October 2015, before the Paris Climate Change Conference, COP21.
96.tq: Distinguish the submission date and its position relative to COP21.
xs: India submitted its **INDC** to the UNFCCC in **October 2015**, **before COP21** — option **(4)**.
**August 2022** is when the **updated NDC** was communicated.
xa: In the INDC, **four of the eight NAPCC missions** focus on adaptation.
INDC targets: **33-35%** intensity cut and about **40%** non-fossil **installed capacity** by 2030.
**MoEFCC** prepares NDCs; the **Union Cabinet** approves them.

96.s: Who prepares India's NDCs and who gives their final approval?
o: NITI Aayog prepares them and Parliament approves them
The UNFCCC prepares them and MoEFCC approves them
MoEFCC prepares them and the Union Cabinet gives final approval
The Ministry of Power prepares them and the President approves them
96.x: The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change prepares India's NDCs, while the Union Cabinet gives final approval.
96.tq: Use the authority-role test to distinguish preparation from approval.
xs: **MoEFCC** prepares India's NDCs and the **Union Cabinet** gives final approval — option **(3)**.
Parliament, the UNFCCC and the President play no such role in the notes.
xa: The Union Cabinet approved **NDC 3.0** in **March 2026**.
The updated NDC was communicated in **August 2022**.
The INDC went to the UNFCCC in **October 2015**.

96.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the adaptation dimension of India's climate commitments:
1. The 2015 INDC stressed adaptation.
2. Four of the eight missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change focus on adaptation.
3. The updated NDC removed adaptation from India's climate commitments.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Adaptation was not removed; it continued to be an important part of India's climate commitments, making statement 3 false.
96.tq: Find the statement that reverses the continuity of a policy objective.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
The **2015 INDC** stressed adaptation: **four of the eight NAPCC missions** focus on adaptation.
Statement 3 is wrong: adaptation was never removed — **NDC 3.0** in fact **scales up adaptation** (coasts, agriculture, Himalayan states).
xa: NDC 3.0 also embeds **LiFE** and seeks **new, low-cost climate finance**.
The **NAPCC Dashboard** tracks the national missions (launched **Sept 2026**).

96.s: NDC 3.0 for the period 2031–2035 was approved by the Union Cabinet in:
96.x: The Union Cabinet approved NDC 3.0 for 2031–2035 in March 2026.
96.tq: Direct recall of the approval authority and date.
xs: NDC 3.0 (**2031-35**) was approved by the **Union Cabinet** in **March 2026** — option **(4)**.
**August 2022** was the updated NDC; **June 2025** is when non-fossil capacity crossed 50%.
xa: It embeds **LiFE** and scales up adaptation.
It was described as "continuity and incremental advance" within India's **equitable share**.

96.s: The five commitments collectively known as 'Panchamrit' were announced by the Prime Minister at Glasgow on:
96.x: The Panchamrit commitments were announced at Glasgow on 1 November 2021 during COP26.
96.tq: Pair the named initiative with its exact announcement date and venue.
xs: **Panchamrit** was announced at **Glasgow (COP26)** on **1 November 2021** — option **(3)**.
**12 December 2015** is the date the **Paris Agreement** was adopted.
xa: Two pledges (**45%** and **50%**) entered the **Aug 2022** NDC.
The net-zero **2070** target was announced at the same COP.

96.s: India announced its target of achieving net-zero emissions by 2070 at which international climate conference?
96.x: India announced its 2070 net-zero target at COP26 held in Glasgow in 2021.
96.tq: Use the event-year association to distinguish the announcement from the later strategy submission.
xs: India announced **net zero by 2070** at **COP26, Glasgow, 2021** — option **(3)**.
It is the fifth **Panchamrit** pledge.
xa: Asked in **APPSC 2024** (key left blank).
The **LT-LEDS** went to the UNFCCC at **COP27 (Nov 2022)**.
Supporting missions: **National Green Hydrogen Mission** and **Nuclear Mission**.

96.s:
Consider the following statements about India's Net Zero Portal (Sept 2026):
1. It provides for mandatory disclosure of corporate net-zero targets.
2. Scope 1 and Scope 2 reporting is encouraged, while Scope 3 reporting is voluntary.
3. It was launched along with a NAPCC Dashboard that tracks the national missions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the portal is for voluntary disclosure of corporate net-zero targets. Statement 2 is correct: Scope 1 and 2 are encouraged, Scope 3 is voluntary. Statement 3 is correct: it was launched with a NAPCC Dashboard tracking the national missions. Hence 2 and 3 only.
96.tq: Portal = voluntary disclosure; Dashboard = tracks missions.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is wrong: the **Net Zero Portal** is for **voluntary disclosure** of corporate net-zero targets.
Statement 2 is correct: **Scope 1 and 2** reporting encouraged; **Scope 3 voluntary**.
Statement 3 is correct: launched with a **NAPCC Dashboard** tracking national missions.
xa: Both were launched in **Sept 2026**.
India's net-zero target year is **2070**.

96.s: Forest and tree cover constituted approximately what proportion of India’s geographical area in 2021?
96.x: Forest and tree cover accounted for approximately 24.6 percent of India’s geographical area in 2021.
96.tq: Discriminate the exact percentage using the decimal figure.
xs: Forest and tree cover was ~**24.6 percent** of India's geographical area in **2021** — option **(3)**.
This cover underpins the **additional carbon sink** target of the NDCs.
xa: Official sink estimate **2005-2019**: **1.97 bn t**.
**Green India Mission**: **5 Mha** forest cover + **5 Mha** quality improvement.
**MISHTI** covers mangroves over **540 sq km**.

96.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the International Solar Alliance (ISA) is correct?
1. It is the first international intergovernmental organisation headquartered in India.
2. Its headquarters is at New Delhi.
3. Its headquarters is at Gurugram in Haryana.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
96.x: The ISA is the first international intergovernmental organisation headquartered in India, and its Secretariat is at Gurugram, Haryana. New Delhi is associated with its founding conference, not its headquarters.
96.tq: Separate two nearby locations by matching the institution with its actual headquarters.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(3)**.
The **ISA** is the **first treaty-based international intergovernmental organisation headquartered in India**.
Its HQ is **Gurugram, Haryana**, not New Delhi.
xa: **New Delhi** hosted its **Founding Conference** on **11 March 2018**.
**New Delhi** is the **CDRI** secretariat.
Framework agreement in force **Dec 2017**.

96.s:
Consider the following statements about climate finance:
1. Global climate finance was about USD 1.9 trillion in 2023.
2. Developing countries other than China received about half of it.
3. India relies mainly on domestic resources, about 83%, for its climate finance.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Statement 1 is correct: global climate finance was USD 1.9 trillion in 2023. Statement 2 is wrong: developing countries other than China got only about 15%. Statement 3 is correct: India relies mainly on domestic resources (about 83%). Hence 1 and 3 only.
96.tq: 1.9 trillion; only ~15% to developing countries other than China; India ~83% domestic.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: global climate finance was **USD 1.9 trillion in 2023**.
Statement 2 is wrong: developing countries other than China got only ~**15%**, not half.
Statement 3 is correct: India relies mainly on **domestic resources (about 83%)**.
xa: India sought a dedicated agenda item on developed-country finance at **Bonn SB64**.
NDC 3.0 also demands **new, low-cost climate finance**.

96.s: Which of the following correctly represents the quantitative memory sequence of the five Panchamrit commitments?
96.x: The Panchamrit sequence is 500 GW, 50 percent, 1 billion tonnes, 45 percent and net zero by 2070.
96.tq: Retain the five-number memory hook in its stated order.
xs: The Panchamrit memory hook is **500, 50, 1, 45, 2070** — option **(4)**.
**500 GW** non-fossil; **50%** from renewables; **1 billion tonnes** cut; **45%** intensity cut; **net zero 2070**.
Options with **2050** or a reordered sequence are wrong.
xa: The first four pledges are for **2030**.
Exam trap: **capacity** versus **generation**.
Announced at **COP26, Glasgow, 1 Nov 2021**.

96.s:
Which of the following pairs of Panchamrit commitments and target years is correctly matched?
1. 500 GW non-fossil capacity — 2030
2. 45 percent reduction in emissions intensity — 2030
3. Net zero — 2070
4. One billion tonnes reduction in projected emissions — 2050
96.x: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The one-billion-tonne reduction in projected emissions is targeted for 2030, not 2050.
96.tq: Find the single wrong year among otherwise correctly paired commitments.
xs: Pairs **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Pair 4 is wrong: the **1 billion tonnes** cut in projected emissions is for **2030**, not 2050.
xa: The **50%** renewables pledge is also for **2030**.

96.s: India defends its comparatively later net-zero target primarily on the grounds of:
o: Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and development needs
The absence of forest and tree cover
96.x: India invokes the principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR) and its development requirements to justify the 2070 target, later than the 2050 targets of most developed countries.
96.tq: Identify the principle and policy rationale rather than merely recalling the target year.
xs: India defends its later target on **CBDR** and **development** grounds — option **(3)**.
Most developed countries target **2050**.
Carbon-removal technology exists in its pathway: **CCUS technology pathways** were announced on **27 Mar 2026**.
xa: The pathway also relies on **forest and tree cover**.
India's principles: **equity, CBDR-RC and climate justice**.

96.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the seven transitions identified in India's LT-LEDS?
96.x: The seven transitions include low-carbon electricity systems, low-carbon transport, urban adaptation and efficient buildings, decoupling growth from industrial emissions, CO2 removal, forest and vegetation cover, and low-carbon finance. Expansion of fossil-fuel electricity systems is not one of them.
96.tq: Find the option that reverses the low-carbon direction common to the listed transitions.
xs: **Expansion of fossil-fuel electricity systems** is not an LT-LEDS transition — option **(1)**.

The seven transitions: **low-carbon electricity**, **low-carbon transport**, **urban adaptation and efficient buildings**, **decoupling growth from industry emissions**, **CO2 removal**, **forest and vegetation cover**, **low-carbon finance**.
xa: LT-LEDS was submitted at **COP27 (Nov 2022)**.
The **Green India Mission** is key for the carbon-sink transition.

96.s: The Nuclear Energy Mission aims to establish how many indigenous small modular reactors by 2033?
96.x: The mission targets five indigenous small modular reactors by 2033.
96.tq: Match a mission with its reactor target and deadline.
xs: The **Nuclear Energy Mission** targets **5 indigenous SMRs by 2033** — option **(2)**.
It is a supporting mission for **net zero 2070**.
xa: Nuclear capacity today: **8.78 GW**.
**National Green Hydrogen Mission**: **₹19,744 crore**, **5 MMT/year** by **2030**.

96.s: Which of the following statements regarding identified pumped storage potential and planning is correct?
o: India has 258 GW of identified potential, of which 7 GW is operational and more than 17 GW is expected by 2030.
India has 25.8 GW of identified potential, of which 17 GW is operational and 7 GW is planned by 2030.
India has 7 GW of identified potential and 258 GW planned to be commissioned by 2030.
India has 258 GW operational capacity and no additional capacity planned by 2030.
96.x: The identified pumped storage potential is 258 GW, with 7 GW operational and more than 17 GW additional capacity planned by 2030.
96.tq: Keep potential, operational capacity and planned addition as separate quantities.
xs: Pumped storage: **258 GW** identified potential, **7 GW** operational, **>17 GW** due by **2030** — option **(1)**.
The other options swap or misstate these figures.
xa: **LDES** = storage over **8 hours**.
First standalone BESS: **180 MW**.
**AP angle**: **Pinnapuram 1,680 MW IREP**.

96.s: The National Green Hydrogen Mission is associated with which outlay and production target?
o: ₹1.97 lakh crore; 5 MMT a year by 2070
96.x: The mission has an outlay of ₹19,744 crore and targets 5 MMT/year capacity by 2030, supporting energy independence by 2047 and net zero by 2070. The other options either change the target (50 or 10 MMT) or the outlay, or confuse the 2047/2070 goals with the target year.
96.tq: Green H2: 19,744 crore, 5 MMT, 2030.
xs: National Green Hydrogen Mission: **₹19,744 crore**; **5 MMT a year by 2030** — option **(1)**.
**2047** (energy independence) and **2070** (net zero) are the wider goals, not the target year.
xa: The mission supports India's **net-zero pathway**.
**Nuclear Mission**: **5 SMRs by 2033**.
India joined the **Global Biofuels Alliance** launched in its **G20 Presidency (2023)**.

96.s: Which one of the following is identified as a key programme for achieving the carbon-sink target in India's LT-LEDS?
96.x: The Green India Mission is identified as a key programme for the carbon-sink target in the LT-LEDS.
96.tq: Match the programme with the specific function assigned to it.
xs: The **Green India Mission (GIM)** is the key programme for the **carbon-sink target** — option **(4)**.
Solar, water and nuclear missions serve other goals.
xa: GIM: forest cover on **5 Mha** + quality improvement on another **5 Mha**.
Its **50-60 Mt/yr** goal was folded into the **2030** sink target.
A **CAG audit** found weak convergence with **CAMPA** and **MGNREGS**.

96.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the timeline of LiFE:
1. The idea of LiFE was introduced at COP26, Glasgow, in 2021.
2. The LiFE Global Movement was launched on 5 June 2022.
3. Mission LiFE was launched in October 2022 at New Delhi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Statement 1 is correct: the idea was introduced at COP26, Glasgow (2021), not COP25. Statement 2 is correct: the LiFE Global Movement began on 5 June 2022. Statement 3 is wrong: Mission LiFE was launched in October 2022 at Kevadia, with the UN Secretary-General, not at New Delhi. Hence 1 and 2 only.
96.tq: COP26 idea -> 5 June 2022 movement -> Oct 2022 Kevadia launch.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 is correct: the LiFE idea came at **COP26, Glasgow (2021)**, not COP25.
Statement 2 is correct: the **LiFE Global Movement** began on **5 June 2022**.
Statement 3 is wrong: Mission LiFE was launched in **October 2022** at **Kevadia**, with the **UN Secretary-General**.
xa: **75 LiFE actions** under **7 themes**.
⚠ LiFE idea = **COP26 (2021)**; Mission launch = **October 2022**.

96.s:
Consider the following statements about Mission LiFE:
1. It lists 75 LiFE actions under 10 themes.
2. Behaviour change is planned in three phases: demand, then supply, then policy.
3. 'P3' stands for the Pro-Planet People community.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Mission LiFE lists 75 actions under 7 themes (save energy, save water, say no to single-use plastic, sustainable food systems, reduce waste, reduce e-waste, healthy lifestyles). So '2 and 3 only'.
96.tq: 75 actions, 7 themes; demand -> supply -> policy.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is wrong: Mission LiFE lists **75 LiFE actions** under **7 themes**, not 10.
Statement 2 is correct: behaviour change in three phases — **demand → supply → policy**.
Statement 3 is correct: **P3** = **Pro-Planet People** community.
xa: The 7 themes: save energy, save water, **no single-use plastic**, sustainable food, reduce waste, **reduce e-waste**, healthy lifestyles.
⚠ LiFE idea = **COP26 (2021)**; Mission launch = **October 2022**.
The **Updated NDC** (**August 2022**) added LiFE as a qualitative element.

96.s: UJALA and PAT are associated respectively with:
o: Single-use plastic bans and e-waste recycling
Water conservation and sustainable food systems
96.x: UJALA is associated with LED bulbs, while PAT is an industrial-efficiency initiative aligned with LiFE.
96.tq: Separate two similarly placed schemes by their specific application areas.
xs: **UJALA** = **LED bulbs**; **PAT** = **industrial efficiency** — option **(1)**.
Both are aligned with **Mission LiFE**.
xa: LiFE focuses on **individual behaviour** and mindful consumption.
**Save energy** is one of LiFE's **7 themes**.
The **CCTS** is administered by the **Bureau of Energy Efficiency**.

96.s: IRIS, the Infrastructure for Resilient Island States initiative, was launched at:
o: The UN Climate Action Summit in 2019
96.x: IRIS was launched at COP26 in 2021 and focuses on Small Island Developing States.
96.tq: Distinguish the launch year and forum of a related climate initiative.
xs: **IRIS** was launched at **COP26 (2021)** — option **(1)**.
It focuses on **SIDS** under the **CDRI**.
**COP21 (2015)** saw the **ISA**; the **2019 UN Climate Action Summit** saw **CDRI** itself.
xa: CDRI is led by India with **UNDRR** support.
**Jordan** recently joined **ISA, CDRI and GBA**.

96.s:
Consider the following statements about the Green Credit Programme (GCP):
1. It is administered by the Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education (ICFRE), Dehradun.
2. It was launched in October 2023 under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
96.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the GCP was launched in October 2023 under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986; the Energy Conservation Act (Section 14AA) is the basis of the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme run by BEE. So '1 only'.
96.tq: GCP = EPA 1986 / ICFRE; CCTS = Energy Conservation Act / BEE.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the **Green Credit Programme** is administered by **ICFRE, Dehradun**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the GCP was launched in **Oct 2023** under the **EPA 1986**, not the Energy Conservation Act.
The **Energy Conservation Act, 2001** (**Section 14AA**) is the basis of the **CCTS**, run by **BEE**.
xa: **CCTS** notified **June 2023**; India's **first mandatory compliance carbon market**.
GCP afforestation is exchangeable for CA; guidelines **16 Sep 2025**.
The GCP is a **market-based incentive for voluntary environmental actions**.

96.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Green Credit Programme:
1. It is a market-based incentive mechanism.
2. It is intended only for compulsory environmental actions.
3. Afforestation credits under it can be exchanged for compensatory-afforestation obligations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: The programme is a market-based incentive for voluntary environmental actions, so statement 2 is false. Afforestation under the programme can be exchanged for compensatory-afforestation obligations.
96.tq: Identify the false extreme word ‘only’ and retain the two supported statements.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1 is correct: the GCP is a **market-based incentive**.
Statement 2 is wrong: it rewards **voluntary** environmental actions, not compulsory ones.
Statement 3 is correct: GCP afforestation is **exchangeable for compensatory afforestation (CA) obligations**.
xa: CA exchange guidelines came on **16 Sep 2025**.
⚠ The **CCTS** is India's **mandatory compliance** market; the GCP is voluntary.

96.s: The Carbon Credit Trading Scheme of India combines which of the following mechanisms?
o: A compliance mechanism and an offset mechanism
A voluntary mechanism and an import mechanism
A taxation mechanism and a subsidy mechanism
A conservation mechanism and a litigation mechanism
96.x: The Indian Carbon Market combines a compliance mechanism for energy-intensive sectors with an offset mechanism for voluntary projects in ten sectors.
96.tq: Distinguish the two complementary designs of the carbon market.
xs: The **CCTS** combines a **compliance mechanism** and an **offset mechanism** — option **(1)**.
**Compliance**: energy-intensive obligated entities get **GEI targets**.
**Offset**: voluntary projects in **10 sectors** (e.g. agriculture, waste).
xa: CCTS is India's **first mandatory compliance carbon market** (Indian Carbon Market).
**Nine** offset methodologies have been published.
It is designed to meet the **45%** intensity target.

96.s: Under the compliance mechanism of the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, an obligated entity that performs better than its notified GHG Emission Intensity target:
o: Must purchase additional Carbon Credit Certificates
Receives a Carbon Credit Certificate that can be traded
Receives a direct compensation from the Union Budget
Is exempted from all environmental regulations
96.x: Entities that beat their notified GHG Emission Intensity targets earn tradeable Carbon Credit Certificates. Entities that miss their targets must buy certificates.
96.tq: Apply the compliance rule to the entity’s performance against its target.
xs: An entity that beats its **GEI target** earns tradeable **Carbon Credit Certificates** — option **(2)**.
Entities that **miss** their targets **must buy** certificates.
xa: GEI targets notified **Oct 2025** for **aluminium, cement, chlor-alkali, and pulp and paper** → **282 obligated entities**.
CCTS now covers **7 sectors**, ~**490 industries**, ~**477 Mt CO2e**.
Only **China, EU and South Korea** cover more.

96.s:
Consider the following statements about India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS):
1. It was notified in June 2023 under Section 14AA of the Energy Conservation Act, 2001 (amended 2022).
2. It is administered by the Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education (ICFRE), Dehradun.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
96.x: Statement 1 is correct: the CCTS was notified in June 2023 under Section 14AA of the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, as amended in 2022. Statement 2 is wrong: the CCTS is administered by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency under the Ministry of Power; ICFRE, Dehradun administers the Green Credit Programme. Hence 1 only.
96.tq: CCTS = EC Act + BEE; GCP = EPA 1986 + ICFRE.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 is correct: CCTS was notified in **June 2023** under **Section 14AA** of the **Energy Conservation Act, 2001** (amended **2022**).
Statement 2 is wrong: CCTS is administered by the **Bureau of Energy Efficiency** (Ministry of Power); **ICFRE, Dehradun** runs the **GCP**.
xa: ⚠ CCTS = **Energy Conservation Act** / **BEE**; GCP = **EPA 1986** / **ICFRE**.
CCTS is India's **first mandatory compliance carbon market**.

96.s: The United Kingdom's recognition of India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) means that:
o: CCTS counts as a qualifying carbon price under the UK CBAM from 1 January 2027, avoiding double charging of Indian exports
Indian exporters are fully exempt from all UK import duties from 2026
CCTS credits can be used to meet EU CBAM obligations
The UK will administer the CCTS jointly with the Bureau of Energy Efficiency
96.x: CCTS is a qualifying carbon price under the UK CBAM (from 1 Jan 2027), so Indian exports are not charged twice. It does not remove all import duties, concerns the UK (not EU) CBAM, and CCTS remains administered by BEE alone.
96.tq: UK CBAM 2027 recognises CCTS → no double charge.
xs: The UK treats **CCTS** as a **qualifying carbon price** under the **UK CBAM** from **1 Jan 2027**, **avoiding double charging** of Indian exports — option **(1)**.
It concerns the **UK** CBAM, not the EU, and gives no blanket exemption from import duties.
CCTS stays administered by the **Bureau of Energy Efficiency**.
xa: The recognition came in **Sep 2026**.
The **EU CBAM** definitive phase began **1 January 2026**.

96.s: Which statement best describes the nature of India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme as discussed in the context of industrial decarbonisation?
o: It is exclusively a voluntary market for households
It is a market only for methane emissions
It is an intensity-based market rather than a cap-based market
It is a cap-based market rather than an intensity-based market
96.x: CCTS is described as an intensity-based, rather than cap-based, carbon market.
96.tq: Discriminate between the closely related terms intensity-based and cap-based.
xs: The CCTS is **intensity-based** rather than **cap-based** — option **(3)**.
Obligated entities get **GHG Emission Intensity (GEI) targets**, not absolute caps.
xa: It covers **7 sectors**, ~**490 industries**, ~**477 Mt CO2e**.
It is designed to meet the **45%** intensity target.

96.s:
Consider the following statements about the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI):
1. Its secretariat is in New Delhi.
2. It is a treaty-based intergovernmental organisation.
3. It was launched in 2019 at the UN Climate Action Summit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Statement 1 is correct: CDRI's secretariat is in New Delhi, led by India with UNDRR support. Statement 2 is wrong: CDRI is a partnership of countries and agencies, not a treaty body (the ISA is the treaty-based body). Statement 3 is correct: it was launched in 2019 at the UN Climate Action Summit. Hence 1 and 3 only.
96.tq: ISA = treaty body, Gurugram; CDRI = partnership, New Delhi.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: the **CDRI** secretariat is in **New Delhi**.
Statement 2 is wrong: CDRI is a **partnership of countries and agencies**, not a treaty body — the **ISA** is the treaty-based one.
Statement 3 is correct: launched in **2019** at the **UN Climate Action Summit**.
xa: CDRI is led by India with **UNDRR** support; **30+** national governments.
Its **IRIS** initiative (COP26, **2021**) focuses on **SIDS**.

96.s: The present membership principle of the International Solar Alliance is best represented by which one of the following?
o: Membership is restricted to countries between the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn.
Membership is open to all United Nations member states.
Membership is restricted to countries that generate more than half of their electricity from solar power.
Membership is restricted to countries belonging to the European Union and SAARC.
96.x: Although the ISA initially began with the idea of bringing together sunshine countries between the tropics, its membership is now open to all UN member states.
96.tq: Track the change from an initial geographical conception to the present membership rule.
xs: ISA membership is **open to all UN member states** — option **(2)**.
It **began** with "**sunshine countries**" between the tropics but no longer restricts membership.
xa: Strength: **125 member and signatory countries** (Mar 2026).
**Malta** became the **119th** member in **Feb 2024**.
The apex body is the **ISA Assembly**.

96.s: The International Solar Alliance was launched on 30 November 2015:
o: at COP21, Paris, by India and France
at the UN Climate Action Summit, New York, by India alone
at COP26, Glasgow, by India and the UK
at New Delhi, as its Founding Conference
96.x: ISA was launched at COP21, Paris, on 30 Nov 2015 by India and France. The 2019 UN Climate Action Summit is where CDRI was launched; COP26 is linked to IRIS and Panchamrit; New Delhi hosted the Founding Conference on 11 March 2018, not the launch.
96.tq: ISA: Paris 2015 with France; CDRI: New York 2019.
xs: The ISA was launched on **30 Nov 2015** at **COP21, Paris**, by **India and France** — option **(1)**.
**New Delhi** hosted the **Founding Conference** on **11 March 2018**, not the launch.
The **2019 UN Climate Action Summit** launched **CDRI**; **COP26** is linked to **IRIS** and Panchamrit.
xa: ISA HQ: **Gurugram, Haryana**.
Framework agreement in force **Dec 2017**.

96.s: The Surat Emissions Trading Scheme demonstrated the effectiveness of market-based regulation by reducing emissions of:
96.x: The Surat Emissions Trading Scheme reduced particulate-matter emissions by 20–30 percent.
96.tq: Link the scheme with the pollutant and the reduction range.
xs: The **Surat ETS** cut **particulate matter** emissions by **20-30%** — option **(4)**.
It was a precursor showing that **markets work**.
xa: The **CCTS** is India's **first mandatory compliance carbon market**.
**Khasi Hills Community REDD+ (Meghalaya)** is the first **Plan Vivo**-certified REDD+ project.

96.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Coalition)
A. Global Biofuels Alliance
B. LeadIT
C. Mission Innovation
D. International Big Cat Alliance

List-II (Origin or launch)
1. COP21, Paris, 2015
2. India’s G20 Presidency, 2023
3. Mysuru, April 2023

96.x: The Global Biofuels Alliance was launched during India’s G20 Presidency; LeadIT was set up by India and Sweden in 2019; Mission Innovation began at COP21 in 2015; and the Big Cat Alliance was launched at Mysuru in April 2023.

**Mission Innovation** → **COP21 Paris (2015)**; **International Big Cat Alliance** → **Mysuru, April 2023**.
xa: The Big Cat Alliance marked **50 years of Project Tiger** and covers **7 big cats**.

96.s: LeadIT primarily works towards the low-carbon transition of which sectors?
96.x: LeadIT focuses particularly on low-carbon transitions in the steel and cement sectors and aligns heavy industry with the Paris goals.
96.tq: Match the coalition with its specialised industrial focus.
xs: **LeadIT** aligns heavy industry, especially **steel and cement**, with Paris goals — option **(3)**.
Its aim is **low-carbon transitions** in these hard-to-abate sectors.
xa: LeadIT was launched at the **UN Climate Action Summit, 2019**, by **India and Sweden**.
At **COP29 (Baku, Nov 2024)** India co-chaired its summit.
BTR1: **over 20%** of 2022 emissions came from industry.

96.s: The Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI) is published by which group of organisations?
o: Germanwatch, NewClimate Institute and Climate Action Network International
96.x: The CCPI is published by Germanwatch, the NewClimate Institute and Climate Action Network (CAN) International.
96.tq: Use the publisher-organisation combination to distinguish the CCPI from UN and financial institutions.
xs: The CCPI is published by **Germanwatch, NewClimate Institute and Climate Action Network (CAN International)** — option **(2)**.
It is not a UN (UNEP/IPCC/UNFCCC) publication, though it is released at the **COP**.
xa: It is released **annually since 2005**.
India was **11th** in CCPI 2019 and **9th** in CCPI 2020.

96.s: In the Climate Change Performance Index 2019 considered in the APPSC 2018 examination, India's rank was:
96.x: India was ranked 11th in CCPI 2019 (released at COP24, December 2018); 9th was its rank in CCPI 2020. ⚠ APPSC key said 9th.
96.tq: Distinguish the specified index edition from unspecified later editions.
xs: India ranked **11th** in **CCPI 2019** (released **Dec 2018**) — option **(4)**.
**9th** was India's rank in **CCPI 2020**.
xa: ⚠ The **APPSC 2018** key said **9th**, mixing up the two editions.
The CCPI is published by **Germanwatch, NewClimate Institute** and **CAN International**.

96.s: The Khasi Hills Community REDD+ project in Meghalaya is significant because it is India’s first:
o: Compensatory-afforestation project under the Green Credit Programme
96.x: The Khasi Hills Community REDD+ project is India’s first Plan Vivo-certified REDD+ project.
96.tq: Use the certification body as the decisive identifier.
xs: The **Khasi Hills Community REDD+ project (Meghalaya)** is India's **first Plan Vivo-certified REDD+ project** — option **(3)**.
This was the **UPSC 2026** key.
xa: The **Surat ETS** cut particulate emissions by **20-30%**.
GCP afforestation is exchangeable for **compensatory afforestation** obligations.

96.s: Which country became the 119th member of the International Solar Alliance in February 2024?
96.x: Malta became the 119th ISA member in February 2024 (APPSC 2024 key). Romania is noted for ratifying the Framework Agreement and Jordan for joining ISA, CDRI and GBA; Cyprus is not mentioned.
96.tq: Malta = 119th ISA member (Feb 2024).
xs: **Malta** became the **119th ISA member** in **Feb 2024** — option **(1)**.
**Romania** ratified the Framework Agreement; **Jordan** joined **ISA, CDRI and GBA**.
xa: This was the **APPSC 2024** key.
ISA now has **125** member and signatory countries (Mar 2026).
The **USA** joined in **2021** and announced withdrawal in **January 2026**.

97.s: Which of the following correctly describes the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)?
o: It is a framework concerned exclusively with greenhouse-gas mitigation.
It deals only with air-pollution control in urban areas.
It is limited to biodiversity conservation and wildlife protection.
It is an overarching domestic framework addressing both mitigation and adaptation.
97.x: The NAPCC is India’s overarching domestic climate framework and covers both mitigation and adaptation. It is not confined exclusively to greenhouse gases, biodiversity or air pollution.
97.tq: Reject exclusive descriptions and identify the broader framework.
xs: The NAPCC is India's **overarching domestic** climate framework covering **both mitigation and adaptation** — option **(4)**.
⚠ It is not limited to GHGs, biodiversity or air pollution (APPSC 2023 answer).
xa: It was India's **first** overarching domestic climate policy framework, implemented through **nodal ministries**.
**Four of the eight missions** focus on adaptation.
Released **30 June 2008** by PM **Dr Manmohan Singh**.

97.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC):
1. It was released on 30 June 2008 by Prime Minister Dr Manmohan Singh.
2. It was prepared under the Prime Minister's Council on Climate Change, constituted in 2010.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
97.x: Statement 1 is correct: NAPCC was released on 30 June 2008 by PM Dr Manmohan Singh. Statement 2 is wrong: it was prepared under the PM's Council on Climate Change, but that Council was constituted in 2007, before the plan, not in 2010. Hence 1 only.
97.tq: Council 2007 -> NAPCC 30 June 2008.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 is correct: NAPCC was released on **30 June 2008** by PM **Dr Manmohan Singh**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the **PM's Council on Climate Change** was constituted in **2007**, not 2010.
xa: The Council sets **policy**; the **Executive Committee on Climate Change** coordinates.
The **National Water Mission** was also set up on **30 June 2008**.

97.s: How many of the eight core missions under the NAPCC focus on adaptation?
97.x: Four of the eight core missions focus on adaptation, while the NAPCC as a whole addresses both adaptation and mitigation.
97.tq: Work from the stated subset count rather than the total number of missions.
xs: **Four** of the **eight** core missions focus on **adaptation** — option **(4)**.
The NAPCC as a whole covers **both mitigation and adaptation**.
xa: The 2015 INDC also stressed that four NAPCC missions are adaptation-focused.
APPSC **2025** asked the count of core missions: **8**.
Economic Survey 2025-26 counts **nine missions**, adding **health**.

97.s: Which institution launched the India Climate Change Knowledge Portal in 2020 as a supporting tool for tracking climate-related actions?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
97.x: The India Climate Change Knowledge Portal was launched in 2020 and tracks ministry-wise climate actions; it is associated with the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
97.tq: Identify the administrative owner of the supporting climate portal.
xs: The keyed answer is the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change** — option **(3)**.
The **India Climate Change Knowledge Portal (2020)** tracks **ministry-wise actions**; MoEFCC's **Climate Change Division** is the nodal unit for **NAPCC coordination**.
xa: The **NAPCC Dashboard** (MoEFCC) tracks mission progress on set indicators.
**India's Net Zero Portal** (MoEFCC) takes **voluntary** net-zero disclosures.
Both the Dashboard and Net Zero Portal were launched in **Sept 2026**.

97.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the original eight National Missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change?
o: National Mission for a Green India
97.x: The National Mission on Clean Air is not one of the original eight NAPCC missions. The other three are among the eight core missions.
97.tq: Eliminate the plausible-looking scheme that is outside the original eight.
xs: A **National Mission on Clean Air** is not among the original eight — option **(1)**.
Clean air (**NCAP**) is listed among things **not** in the original eight.
**National Water Mission**, **Sustainable Habitat** and **Green India** are core missions.
xa: Also outside the eight: **wind, nuclear, green hydrogen, biomass (SAMARTH)**.
NAPCC has **8 core National Missions**.

97.s: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship among NDCs, the National Adaptation Plan and State Action Plans on Climate Change?
o: SAPCCs replace the National Adaptation Plan and national missions.
NDCs are delivered only through international treaties and not through domestic plans.
NDCs are delivered through the National Adaptation Plan, national missions and SAPCCs.
The National Adaptation Plan applies only to urban local bodies.
97.x: NDC implementation is pursued through the National Adaptation Plan, national missions and State Action Plans on Climate Change.
97.tq: Test the relationship among national commitments and domestic implementation channels.
xs: NDCs are delivered through the **National Adaptation Plan**, **national missions** and **SAPCCs** — option **(3)**.
SAPCCs align with the NAPCC rather than replacing it.
xa: NAPCC = **domestic vehicle for NDCs**.
Adaptation spending rose from **3.7% of GDP (FY16)** to **5.6% (FY22)**.

97.s: The NAPCC Dashboard, launched in September 2026, is intended primarily to perform which function?
o: Replace the State Action Plans on Climate Change
97.x: The NAPCC Dashboard was launched in September 2026 to track the progress of the national climate missions.

97.s: The National Action Plan on Climate Change serves as India’s domestic vehicle for which international climate commitment?
97.x: The NAPCC is the domestic vehicle for implementing India’s Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs).
97.tq: Discriminate between climate commitments and instruments belonging to other environmental agreements.
xs: The NAPCC is the **domestic vehicle for NDCs** — **Nationally Determined Contributions** — option **(2)**.
NDCs are delivered through the **National Adaptation Plan**, **national missions** and **SAPCCs**.
xa: NAPCC covers **both mitigation and adaptation**.
Adaptation spending rose to **5.6% of GDP (FY22)**.

97.s:
Assertion (A): The Green India Mission is a climate change response mission.
Reason (R): It addresses climate change through adaptation and mitigation.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
97.x: Both are true: the Green India Mission is a climate mission because it tackles climate change through both adaptation and mitigation, by expanding forest cover. R explains A.
97.tq: Ask whether the method explains the label.
n: The Green India Mission responds to climate change through adaptation and mitigation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 13-16]
xs: Both **A and R are true**, and **R is the correct explanation of A** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Green India Mission** **responds** to **climate change** through **adaptation** and **mitigation**.
It does so by **protecting**, **restoring** and **enhancing forest cover**.
xa: GIM is one of the **eight NAPCC missions**.
**3 sub-missions**: forest quality, forest/tree cover and ecosystem restoration, incomes of forest-dependent people.
**CAG audit (Aug 2026)**: **91.87%** shortfall in quality improvement; **97.57%** in cover increase.

97.s: The National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency includes which of the following schemes?
97.x: The Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT) scheme is included in the National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency and is associated with the Ministry of Power and BEE.
97.tq: Use the distinctive scheme–mission association.
xs: The **NMEEE** includes the **PAT scheme** — **Perform, Achieve and Trade** — option **(4)**.
**SAMARTH** (biomass) is outside the eight; **AMRUT** and **Ujjwala** are typical non-mission distractors.
xa: NMEEE nodal: **Ministry of Power / BEE**.
Under PAT, units beating targets earn tradeable **Energy Saving Certificates**.

97.s:
Match List-I (NAPCC mission) with List-II (nodal ministry):
List-I
a. National Mission on Sustainable Habitat
b. National Mission for a Green India
c. National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture
d. National Water Mission
List-II
i. Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

Select the correct code:
97.x: NMSH is under MoHUA (a-ii), Green India Mission under MoEFCC (b-i), NMSA under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare (c-iv) and the National Water Mission under Jal Shakti (d-iii). Option A alone matches; B swaps every pair, C swaps GIM and NMSA, D swaps NMSH and NWM.
97.tq: Habitat-Housing, Green India-Environment, Agriculture-Agriculture, Water-Jal Shakti.
xs: The match is **a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii** — option **(1)**.

**NMSA** → **Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare**; **National Water Mission** → **Ministry of Jal Shakti**.

97.s:

1. The National Mission for Sustaining the Himalayan Ecosystem assesses Himalayan vulnerability across 12 thematic areas.
2. The National Mission on Strategic Knowledge for Climate Change supports Centres of Excellence, State Climate Change Centres and Global Technology Watch Groups.
3. Both missions have the Ministry of Jal Shakti as their nodal ministry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
97.x: Statement 1 is correct: NMSHE has 12 thematic areas. Statement 2 is correct: NMSKCC (4 thematic areas) builds S&T capacity through these institutions. Statement 3 is wrong: both are under the Department of Science and Technology. Hence 1 and 2 only.
97.tq: NMSHE 12 areas, NMSKCC 4 areas; both DST.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 is correct: **NMSHE** assesses Himalayan vulnerability in **12 thematic areas**.
Statement 2 is correct: **NMSKCC** supports **Centres of Excellence**, **State Climate Change Centres** and **Global Technology Watch Groups**.
Statement 3 is wrong: both are under **DST**, not Jal Shakti.
xa: NMSKCC has **4 thematic areas** and builds S&T capacity.
NMSKCC supports state- and district-level **vulnerability assessments** for SAPCCs.

97.s: The National Solar Mission was launched on 11 January 2010 with an objective of achieving what capacity by 2022?
97.x: The National Solar Mission was launched on 11 January 2010 and targeted 100 GW of solar capacity by 2022.

xs: The **National Solar Mission (JNNSM)**, launched **11 Jan 2010**, targeted **100 GW** by **2022** — option **(2)**.

97.s: Which one of the following is NOT a sub-mission of the Green India Mission?

Improvement of incomes of forest-dependent people

xs: **Promotion of thermal power generation** is not a GIM sub-mission — option **(2)**.

97.s:
Consider the following statements about NAPCC governance:
1. The PM's Council on Climate Change sets policy, while the Executive Committee on Climate Change under the Principal Secretary to the PM coordinates it.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
97.x: Both statements are correct as per the governance table: the PM's Council sets policy, the Executive Committee coordinates, and the MoEFCC Climate Change Division is the nodal unit for UNFCCC negotiations and NAPCC coordination. So 'Both 1 and 2'.
97.tq: Council = policy; Executive Committee = coordination; MoEFCC division = nodal unit.
xs: **Both statements** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
Statement 1: the **PM's Council on Climate Change** sets **policy**; the **Executive Committee on Climate Change**, under the **Principal Secretary to the PM**, **coordinates**.
Statement 2: the **MoEFCC Climate Change Division** is the **nodal unit** for **UNFCCC negotiations** and **NAPCC coordination**.
xa: NAPCC was **launched** on **30 June 2008** by PM **Dr Manmohan Singh**.

Tracking: **India Climate Change Knowledge Portal (2020)**, **NAPCC Dashboard**, **Net Zero Portal**.

97.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Water Mission:
1. Its goals include a public water database and a focus on over-exploited areas.
2. It aims to raise water-use efficiency by 30% through basin-level integrated water resources management.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
97.x: Statement 1 is correct: the five goals include a public water database, impact assessment, citizen/state action, focus on over-exploited areas and better water-use efficiency. Statement 2 is wrong: the target is a 20% increase in water-use efficiency, not 30%. Hence 1 only.
97.tq: NWM: +20% water-use efficiency.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 is correct: NWM goals include a **public water database** and **focus on over-exploited areas**.
Statement 2 is wrong: NWM aims to raise **water use efficiency by 20%**, not 30%.
xa: Other goals: **impact assessment** and **citizen/state action**; efficiency via basin-level **IWRM**.
NWM is under the **Ministry of Jal Shakti**, set up **30 June 2008**.
State Specific Action Plans get **₹50 lakh** for major States.

97.s: Under the Perform, Achieve and Trade mechanism, energy-intensive units that exceed their energy-saving targets receive:
o: Energy Saving Certificates that can be traded
Carbon tax rebates issued by State governments
97.x: PAT rewards industries that beat their energy-saving targets with tradable Energy Saving Certificates.
97.tq: Identify the market instrument generated by achievement of a performance target.
xs: Under **PAT**, units beating targets earn tradeable **Energy Saving Certificates** — option **(3)**.
PAT is a **market mechanism** under the **NMEEE**.
xa: NMEEE nodal: **Ministry of Power / BEE**.
PAT is aligned with **Mission LiFE**'s energy-efficiency theme.
NMEEE is one of the **8** core missions.

97.x: Statement 1 is correct: these are NMSA components, along with a Sub-Mission on Agroforestry. Statement 2 is correct: micro-irrigation gets up to 55% subsidy. Statement 3 is wrong: Soil Health Cards are issued free every two years. Hence 1 and 2 only.

xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 is correct: NMSA components are **Rainfed Area Development, On-Farm Water Management, Soil Health Management**.
Statement 2 is correct: up to **55%** subsidy for **micro-irrigation**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Soil Health Cards** are issued free **every two years**.
xa: **₹30,000/family** for Integrated Farming Systems.
NMSA also has a **Sub-Mission on Agroforestry**.

97.s: India's adaptation spending as a share of GDP rose from:
97.x: Adaptation spending rose from 3.7% of GDP (FY16) to 5.6% (FY22). The reversed option swaps the years, the 0.37/0.56 option misplaces the decimal, and 1.2/2.5 is incorrect.
97.tq: Adaptation spend: 3.7 → 5.6% of GDP.
xs: Adaptation spending rose from **3.7% of GDP (FY16)** to **5.6% (FY22)** — option **(1)**.
Option (3) reverses the years; option (4) misplaces the decimal.
xa: NAPCC is the **domestic vehicle for NDCs**.
**WRI**: a **ten-fold return** on adaptation investment.

97.s:
Consider the following statements about the Climate Change Action Programme (CCAP):
1. It is a 2014 scheme of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
2. It is the National Implementing Entity for the National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
97.x: Statement 1 is correct: CCAP (2014) is an MoEFCC scheme that builds assessment capacity, supports SAPCCs and strengthens the scientific base. Statement 2 is wrong: NABARD, not CCAP, is the National Implementing Entity for NAFCC. Hence 1 only.
97.tq: CCAP = MoEFCC 2014 capacity scheme; NAFCC NIE = NABARD.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 is correct: **CCAP** is a **2014 MoEFCC scheme** that builds assessment capacity and supports **SAPCCs**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **NABARD** is the National Implementing Entity for **NAFCC**.
xa: CCAP strengthens the **scientific and analytical base** on climate change.
NAFCC (**2015**) is a **central sector scheme** for State/UT adaptation projects.

97.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change (NAFCC):
1. It was set up in 2017 as a centrally sponsored scheme.
2. NABARD is its National Implementing Entity.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
97.x: Statement 1 is wrong: NAFCC was set up in 2015 as a central sector scheme to fund adaptation projects of States/UTs in vulnerable sectors (2017 is when the coal cess was folded into GST compensation cess). Statement 2 is correct: NABARD is the National Implementing Entity. Hence 2 only.
97.tq: NAFCC 2015, central sector, NABARD.
xs: Only statement **2** is correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is wrong: **NAFCC** was set up in **2015** as a **central sector scheme**.
Statement 2 is correct: **NABARD** is its **National Implementing Entity**.
xa: NAFCC funds adaptation projects of **States/UTs** in vulnerable sectors.
⚠ **2017** is when the coal cess was folded into the **GST compensation cess**.
NABARD is also the Adaptation Fund's National Implementing Entity.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
97.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: in 2017 the clean energy cess was folded into the GST compensation cess. So '1 only'.
97.tq: Coal cess -> NCEF (2010-11) -> GST compensation cess (2017).
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the **NCEF** was **created in 2010-11** from a **clean energy cess on coal** to fund clean-energy research and projects.
Statement 2 is wrong: in **2017** the cess was folded into the **GST compensation cess**.
xa: **NAFCC** (**2015**): funds State adaptation projects; **NABARD** is the **National Implementing Entity**.
**CCAP** (**2014**): MoEFCC scheme supporting **SAPCCs**.
⚠ NAFCC implementing entity = **NABARD**.

Consider the following statements:

97.x: All three statements are correct. The Economic Survey 2025–26 uses a nine-mission description by adding health, while the officially tested count of core missions remains eight.

97.s: The evolution of State Action Plans on Climate Change is best represented by which of the following?
o: From district-specific adaptation plans to broad mitigation plans
From broad mitigation plans during 2010–15 to district-specific, risk-based adaptation plans from 2020 onwards
From national mitigation plans to plans unrelated to local institutions
From risk-based plans during 2010–15 to purely sector-neutral plans after 2020
97.x: States have moved from broad mitigation-centric plans in 2010–15 towards district-specific, risk-based adaptation plans from 2020 onwards, linked with social schemes and local institutions.
97.tq: Use the time markers to identify the direction of policy evolution.
xs: SAPCCs moved from **mitigation-centric plans (2010-15)** to **district-specific, risk-based adaptation plans** from **2020** — option **(2)**.
Newer plans are **tied to social schemes and local institutions**.
xa: States prepare SAPCCs in line with the **NAPCC**.
**NMSKCC** supports **State Climate Change Centres** and vulnerability assessments.
SAPCCs are criticised as **weak on finance**.

xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 is correct: AP created an exclusive **Climate Change Cell** in **November 2022** (APPSC 2022 key).

97.x: The revised AP SAPCC covers 2025–30, includes eight energy-sector adaptation measures and is based on vulnerability to rising temperatures, variable rainfall and extreme events.
