Assertion (A): The key threat in a nuclear disaster is ionising radiation.
Reason (R): Ionising radiation includes alpha radiation, beta radiation, gamma radiation and neutrons.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
106.x: Both are true: ionising radiation is the main threat, and it includes alpha, beta, gamma and neutrons. Listing its forms does not explain why it is the threat, so R does not explain A.
106.tq: Ask whether a list explains a danger.
n: The key threat in a nuclear disaster is ionising radiation. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 19-22]
Ionising radiation includes alpha radiation, beta radiation, gamma radiation and neutrons. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 19-22]
xs: **Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A** — so option **(2)** is correct.
A: the **key threat** in a nuclear disaster is **ionising radiation**.
R lists its forms — **alpha**, **beta**, **gamma** and **neutrons** — which does not explain why it is the threat.
xa: **Long-term impacts**: **cancer**, **genetic damage**, contamination for **decades or centuries**.
**Iodine prophylaxis** (**potassium iodide** tablets) **protects** the **thyroid**.
**Radiological disasters** include **orphan-source incidents** and **dirty-bomb incidents**.

106.s: Which agency is responsible for forecasting heatwaves in India?
106.x: The IMD forecasts heatwaves. NDMA sets guidelines, and NDRF responds.
106.tq: Recall who forecasts heatwaves.
n: The India Meteorological Department is the nodal agency for forecasting heatwaves. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 70-72]
xs: The **India Meteorological Department** is the **nodal agency** for **forecasting heatwaves** — so option **(1)** is correct.
IMD gives **early warning** through **colour-coded alerts**.
**NDMA** issues guidelines; the **NDRF** is a response force — neither forecasts.
xa: Heatwave season: mainly **March to June**, **sometimes extends** to **July**.
Heatwave is now a **notified disaster** eligible for **SDRF** and **NDRF** assistance.
IMD is also the nodal agency for **cold-wave** forecasting.

106.s: Building embankments, planting mangroves and land-use zoning belong to which phase of the disaster management cycle?
106.x: Embankments, mangroves and zoning are pre-disaster mitigation measures. Response covers rescue and relief during or just after the event; recovery covers restoration and rebuilding after it.
106.tq: Mitigation = before; response = during; recovery = after.
xs: **Embankments, mangroves and zoning** are **pre-disaster** measures of **mitigation** — option **(3)**.
**Response** (during/after) covers **rescue and relief**.
**Recovery** (post-disaster) covers **restoration and rebuilding**.
xa: **DRR** works best when it **addresses underlying causes of vulnerability** (**APPSC 2024**).
Cyclone mitigation uses **mangroves (Coringa, Krishna)** and **shelter belts**.
Flood mitigation: **embankments, reservoir regulation, flood forecasting**.

106.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Earthquake-resistant buildings are structural mitigation measures in India.
II. Retrofitting is a structural mitigation measure in India.
III. Sea walls are structural mitigation measures in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: All three are structural mitigation: quake-resistant buildings, retrofitting and sea walls.
106.tq: Discriminate structural from non-structural mitigation.
n: Earthquake-resistant buildings are structural mitigation measures in India. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 30-32]
Retrofitting is a structural mitigation measure in India. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 30-32]
Sea walls are structural mitigation measures in India. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 30-32]
xs: **All three — I, II and III** — are structural measures — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Structural** mitigation = **physical** or **engineering constructions**: **earthquake-resistant buildings**, **retrofitting**, **sea walls**.
xa: Other structural examples: **embankments**, **dams**, **cyclone shelters**, **check dams**.
**Non-structural**: **building codes**, **Flood Plain Zoning**, **insurance**, **early warning systems**.
⚠ **Building codes** (**IS 1893**) are **non-structural**.

106.s:
Consider the following statements:

I. Earthquake-resistant design is a structural earthquake-mitigation measure.
II. IS 1893 is associated with earthquake-resistant design.
III. Building codes are structural earthquake-mitigation measures.
IV. Awareness is a non-structural earthquake-mitigation measure.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: I, II and IV are correct: quake-resistant design is structural, IS 1893 governs it, and awareness is non-structural. III is false because building codes are non-structural.
106.tq: Discriminate codes from construction.
n: Earthquake-resistant design is a structural earthquake-mitigation measure. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 30-32]
IS 1893 is associated with earthquake-resistant design. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 30-32]
Building codes are non-structural earthquake-mitigation measures. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 30-32]
Awareness is a non-structural earthquake-mitigation measure. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 30-32]
xs: **I, II and IV only** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
I: **earthquake-resistant** design is **structural**; II: **IS 1893** is the code tied to it.
III is wrong: **building codes** (IS 1893, **National Building Code**) are **non-structural**.
IV: **public awareness** is **non-structural**.
xa: Non-structural also covers **land-use planning**, **insurance**, **training**.
**Earthquake** mitigation: **seismic zoning**, **safe construction**.
**Retrofitting** and **sea walls** are structural.

106.s:
Match the heatwave-management measure with its type.

List-I
 a. Shade structures
 b. ORS distribution
 c. Adjusted working hours

106.s:
Consider the following statements regarding vulnerability:
1. Vulnerability denotes susceptibility to harm.
2. It may have physical, social, economic and environmental dimensions.
3. It is determined exclusively by the intensity of a hazard.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: Vulnerability is susceptibility to harm and may be physical, social, economic or environmental. It is not determined exclusively by hazard intensity.
106.tq: Find the statement that wrongly narrows a multidimensional concept through the word 'exclusively'.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **vulnerability** means **susceptibility** to harm.
Statement 2 correct: it has **physical, social, economic and environmental** dimensions.
Statement 3 wrong: vulnerability is a separate factor from the **hazard**; risk arises from their **interaction**.
xa: **Risk = Hazard x Vulnerability / Capacity**.
**Capacity** = strengths/resources to cope; **Resilience** = ability to resist, absorb and recover quickly.
**DRR** works best when it **addresses underlying causes of vulnerability** (**APPSC 2024**).

106.s:

2. Biological disasters — Epidemics and pest attacks
3. Emerging disasters — Cyber attacks and space weather
4. Man-made disasters — Chemical accidents and nuclear incidents
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
106.x: All four pairs match the classification: geological = earthquakes, volcanic eruptions; biological = epidemics, pest attacks; emerging = cyber attacks, space weather; man-made/industrial = chemical accidents, nuclear incidents. Hence 1, 2, 3 and 4.
106.tq: Match each example with its disaster category before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All four pairs are correctly matched — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Geological** = earthquakes, volcanic eruptions; **Biological** = epidemics, pest attacks.
**Emerging** = cyber attacks, space weather; **Man-made** = chemical accidents, nuclear incidents.
xa: Geological also includes **landslides** and **tsunamis**; climatological = **extreme temperatures, droughts**.
Emerging also includes **AI failures**.
**Fire from careless handling of gas cylinders** = **man-made disaster**.
⚠ **No man-made calamity is notified** for SDRF/NDRF.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about chemical-accident management in India:
1. Crisis Groups for chemical accidents are constituted only at the Central and State levels.
2. Chemical accidents are regulated under the MSIHC Rules, 1989 and the CAEPPR Rules, 1996.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: Statement 2 is correct: the MSIHC Rules 1989 and the CAEPPR Rules 1996 govern chemical accidents. Statement 1 is wrong: Crisis Groups exist at Central, State, District and Local levels. So '2 only'.
106.tq: Four tiers of Crisis Groups: Central, State, District, Local.
xs: Only **statement 2** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 2 is correct: chemical accidents fall under the **MSIHC Rules 1989** and **CAEPPR Rules 1996**.
Statement 1 is wrong: Crisis Groups exist at **Central/State/District/Local** levels.
xa: **Bhopal Gas Tragedy** gas = **methyl isocyanate (MIC)** — not chlorine, CO or ammonia.
It happened on the night of **2-3 December 1984** at **Union Carbide India Ltd**.
Bhopal is a **man-made** chemical leak.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about the Bhopal Gas Tragedy:
1. It occurred on the night of 2-3 December 1984.
2. The leak took place at the plant of Union Carbide India Ltd.
3. It is classified as a natural hazard.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the leak occurred on the night of 2-3 December 1984 at Union Carbide India Ltd, Bhopal. Statement 3 is wrong: it was a chemical leak, an anthropogenic (man-made) hazard. So every option with statement 3 is wrong.
106.tq: Bhopal: 2-3 Dec 1984, Union Carbide, man-made.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: it happened on the night of **2-3 December 1984**.
Statement 2 correct: the plant belonged to **Union Carbide India Ltd**, Bhopal.
Statement 3 wrong: it was a **chemical leak**, an **anthropogenic / man-made** hazard.
xa: Gas = **methyl isocyanate (MIC)** — not chlorine, CO or ammonia.
Chemical accident rules: **MSIHC Rules 1989** + **CAEPPR Rules 1996**.
**Man-made** disasters arise from **human activity, negligence or technological failure**.

106.s:
The mitigation of cyclones and storm surges may include which of the following?
1. IMD warnings
2. Cyclone shelters and evacuation
3. Shelter belts and mangroves
4. Seismic zoning as the primary measure
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
106.x: IMD warnings, shelters, evacuation, shelter belts and mangroves are cyclone-related measures. Seismic zoning is primarily an earthquake mitigation measure.
106.tq: Separate hazard-specific measures from a plausible but unrelated technical measure.
xs: **IMD warnings, cyclone shelters, evacuation, shelter belts and mangroves** are cyclone measures — option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
Statement 4 wrong: **seismic zoning** is an **earthquake** measure, with safe construction.
xa: Cyclone mangroves: **Coringa, Krishna**.
Tsunami: **INCOI** warning and **Tsunami Ready** villages.
Landslide: **hazard zonation mapping**, early warning.
AP has the **longest coastline on the east coast**.

106.s:
With reference to the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction, consider the following statements:
1. It covers the period 2015–2030.
2. It contains four priorities for action.
3. It contains seven global targets.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: The Sendai Framework covers 2015–2030 and contains four priorities and seven global targets.
106.tq: Combine the framework’s period with its two key numerical features.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Sendai** covers **2015-2030**, with **4 priorities** and **7 global targets**.
xa: Priorities: understanding risk; strengthening risk governance; investing in DRR; enhancing preparedness + **Build Back Better**.
Adopted at the **3rd UN WCDRR**; **succeeds Hyogo** (**2005-2015**).
⚠ Sendai = **4** priorities, **7** targets — do not swap them.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA):
1. It is chaired by the Union Home Minister.
2. It lays down policies and approves the National Plan.
3. It supports other countries in major disasters and lays down policy for NIDM.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: Statement 1 is wrong: NDMA is chaired by the Prime Minister. Statements 2 and 3 are correct functions of NDMA. Hence '2 and 3 only'; every other option includes the false statement 1.
106.tq: NDMA = PM; NPDRR = Home Minister.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 wrong: **NDMA** is **chaired by the PM**, not the Home Minister.
Statements 2, 3 correct: NDMA **lays down policies**, **approves the National Plan**, **supports other countries** and makes policy for **NIDM**.
xa: ⚠ **NPDRR** is the body chaired by the **Union Home Minister**.
NDMA also issues **guidelines to ministries/states**.
**APSDMA** is chaired by the **Chief Minister**.
**"Resilient India 2047"**: NDMA push for Ministry DM plans.

106.s: Which statement regarding the use of social media in disaster risk reduction is correct?
o: Social media has no role in community-based disaster management
Social media is a complete replacement for official warning systems
Social media can be used only after the recovery phase
Social media is a complementary tool and not a replacement for established systems
106.x: Social media can support communication and community engagement, but it is a complementary tool rather than a replacement for official disaster-management systems.
106.tq: Avoid absolute claims and identify the limited but useful complementary role.
xs: **Social media** is a **complementary** tool, **not a replacement** — option **(4)**.
So it neither replaces official systems nor lacks a role in community DRR.
xa: **SACHET**: NDMA's **Common Alerting Protocol** alert system (**C-DOT**).
**Aapda Mitra** trains community **first responders**.
**PRIs and ULBs** have a legal role under the **DM Act**.

106.s:
Match the following HADR operations with the countries assisted:

A. Maitri
B. Dost
C. Karuna
D. Sadbhav

1. Turkey and Syria
2. Nepal
3. Myanmar
4. Vietnam, Laos and Myanmar

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
106.x: Maitri assisted Nepal, Dost assisted Turkey and Syria, Karuna assisted Myanmar, and Sadbhav assisted Vietnam, Laos and Myanmar.
106.tq: Start with the distinctive multi-country pair and eliminate codes that swap neighbouring operations.
xs: The correct code is **A-2, B-1, C-3, D-4** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Maitri** went to **Nepal** (earthquake, **2015**); **Dost** went to **Turkey and Syria** (earthquake, **2023**).
**Karuna** went to **Myanmar** (Cyclone **Mocha**, **2023**); **Sadbhav** went to **Vietnam, Laos and Myanmar** (Typhoon **Yagi**, **2024**).
xa: **Operation Vanilla** helped **Madagascar** after Cyclone **Diane**, **2020**.
**Operation Brahma** helped **Myanmar** after the **2025** earthquake.
⚠ **Myanmar** appears in three operations: **Karuna** (cyclone), **Sadbhav** (typhoon) and **Brahma** (earthquake).
**NDMA** has the role of **supporting other countries** in major disasters.

106.s:
Assertion (A): NDMA gives special focus to disability-inclusive disaster risk reduction.
Reason (R): Persons with disabilities face greater risk and barriers in warning, evacuation and relief during disasters.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
106.x: Both are true and R explains A: because persons with disabilities face extra barriers in warning, evacuation and relief, NDMA focuses on disability-inclusive DRR, issuing guidelines on it in 2019.
106.tq: Check whether R gives the need that the policy in A responds to.
n: The NDMA focus area of disability-inclusive disaster risk reduction includes the NDMA Guidelines on Disability Inclusive Disaster Risk Reduction. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 68-70]
The NDMA Guidelines on Disability Inclusive Disaster Risk Reduction were issued in 2019. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 68-70]
xs: **Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A** — so option **(1)** is correct.
NDMA issued the **Guidelines on Disability Inclusive Disaster Risk Reduction** (**2019**).
**Persons with Disabilities (PwD)** are a **vulnerable group** facing extra barriers — hence the focus.
xa: **School safety** gives **special focus** to **children**.
**Gender mainstreaming** stresses **women's leadership** — part of the **PM's 10-Point Agenda**.
**Minimum standards of relief** carry **special provisions** for **vulnerable groups**.

106.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the priority focus areas of the Sendai Framework.

List-I
(a) Priority 1
(b) Priority 2
(c) Priority 3
(d) Priority 4

List-II
(i) Strengthening disaster risk governance
(ii) Enhancing disaster preparedness for effective response and to “Build Back Better”
(iii) Understanding disaster risk
(iv) Investing in disaster risk reduction for resilience
106.x: Priority 1 is understanding risk, 2 governance, 3 investing for resilience, and 4 preparedness and building back better. The answer is a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
106.tq: Recall the four Sendai priorities in order.
n: The first priority of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction is understanding disaster risk. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 61-63]
The second priority of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction is strengthening disaster risk governance. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 61-63]
The third priority of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction is investing in disaster risk reduction for resilience. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 61-63]

The fourth priority of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction is enhancing disaster preparedness for effective response and to “Build Back Better”. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 61-63]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Priority 1**: **understanding disaster risk**; **Priority 2**: **strengthening disaster risk governance**.
**Priority 3**: **investing in DRR for resilience**; **Priority 4**: **enhancing disaster preparedness** and "**Build Back Better**".
xa: Priority 1 covers **hazard**, **vulnerability**, **exposure**, **capacity**.
Priority 3 means **public** and **private investment** in **prevention and mitigation**.
Priority 4 covers **preparedness**, **recovery**, **rehabilitation**, **reconstruction**.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about the targets of the Sendai Framework:

I. Target C seeks to reduce direct economic loss in relation to global GDP by 2030.
II. Target E seeks to substantially increase the number of countries with national and local DRR strategies by 2030.
III. Target G seeks to substantially increase the availability of and access to multi-hazard early warning systems and disaster risk information by 2030.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: I and III are correct: Target C cuts economic loss relative to GDP by 2030, and Target G widens early warning by 2030. II is false because Target E's deadline was 2020, not 2030.
106.tq: Recall that Target E alone ends in 2020.
n: Target C of the Sendai Framework is to reduce direct economic loss in relation to global GDP by 2030. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 61-63]
Target E of the Sendai Framework is to substantially increase the number of countries with national DRR strategies by 2020. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 61-63]
Target E of the Sendai Framework is to substantially increase the number of countries with local DRR strategies by 2020. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 61-63]
Target G of the Sendai Framework is to substantially increase the availability of multi-hazard early warning systems by 2030. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 61-63]
Target G of the Sendai Framework is to substantially increase access to multi-hazard early warning systems by 2030. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 61-63]
Target G of the Sendai Framework is to substantially increase the availability of disaster risk information by 2030. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 61-63]
Target G of the Sendai Framework is to substantially increase access to disaster risk information by 2030. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 61-63]
xs: **I and III only** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
I is correct: **Target C** — reduce **direct economic loss** in relation to **global GDP** by **2030**.
II is wrong: **Target E** (national and local **DRR strategies**) had a deadline of **2020**, not 2030.
III is correct: **Target G** — **multi-hazard early warning systems** and **disaster risk information** by **2030**.
xa: **Target A**: reduce global **disaster mortality** by **2030**.
**Target F**: enhance **international cooperation** to **developing countries**.
⚠ Target E is the only target with a **2020** deadline.

106.s:
Consider the following statements regarding strengthening disaster risk governance:

I. It emphasizes laws.
II. It emphasizes institutions.
III. It emphasizes policies.
IV. It emphasizes coordination at all levels.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: All four are correct: strengthening risk governance stresses laws, institutions, policies and coordination at every level.
106.tq: Recall the governance priority.
n: Strengthening disaster risk governance emphasizes laws. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 61-63]
Strengthening disaster risk governance emphasizes institutions. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 61-63]
Strengthening disaster risk governance emphasizes policies. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 61-63]
Strengthening disaster risk governance emphasizes coordination at all levels. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 61-63]
xs: **All four — I, II, III and IV** — are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Strengthening disaster risk governance** (Priority 2) emphasises **laws**, **institutions**, **policies** and **coordination** at **all levels**.
xa: Priority 1 is **understanding disaster risk**.
Priority 3 is **investing in DRR for resilience**.
Guiding principle: **States** have the **primary role** in **reducing disaster risk**.

106.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the targets of the Sendai Framework.

List-I
(a) Target A
(b) Target B
(c) Target D: critical infrastructure
(d) Target D: basic services

List-II
(i) Substantially reduce the number of affected people globally by 2030
(ii) Substantially reduce disaster damage to critical infrastructure by 2030
(iii) Substantially reduce global disaster mortality by 2030
(iv) Substantially reduce disruption of basic services by 2030

Choose the correct answer using the code given below:
106.x: Target A cuts disaster deaths, Target B people affected, and Target D damage to critical infrastructure and disruption of basic services, all by 2030. The answer is a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv.
106.tq: Recall the Sendai targets by letter.
n: Target A of the Sendai Framework is to substantially reduce global disaster mortality by 2030. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 61-63]
Target B of the Sendai Framework is to substantially reduce the number of affected people globally by 2030. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 61-63]
Target D of the Sendai Framework is to substantially reduce disaster damage to critical infrastructure by 2030. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 61-63]
Target D of the Sendai Framework is to substantially reduce disruption of basic services by 2030. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 61-63]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Target A**: reduce global **disaster mortality**; **Target B**: reduce the **number of affected people**.
**Target D**: reduce **damage** to **critical infrastructure** and **disruption** of **basic services** — all by **2030**.
xa: **Target C**: reduce **direct economic loss** relative to **global GDP**.
**Target E**: more countries with **DRR strategies** by **2020**.
**Target G**: **multi-hazard early warning systems**.

106.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Build Back Better uses recovery as an opportunity to reduce future risk.
Statement B: The inclusive and people-centred principle gives special attention to vulnerable groups.

Which of the following is correct?
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
106.x: Both are true: 'build back better' uses recovery to reduce future risk, and the inclusive principle gives special attention to vulnerable groups.
106.tq: Recall the Sendai principles.
n: Build Back Better uses recovery as an opportunity to reduce future risk. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 61-63]
The inclusive and people-centred principle gives special attention to vulnerable groups. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 61-63]
xs: **Both statements are true** — so option **(1)** is correct.
A: **Build Back Better** uses **recovery** as an **opportunity** to **reduce future risk**.
B: the **inclusive and people-centred** principle gives **special attention** to **vulnerable groups**.
xa: **States** have the **primary role** in reducing disaster risk.
Sendai's **expected outcome**: a **substantial reduction** of **disaster risk** and **losses**.
Build Back Better is part of **Priority 4**.

106.s:
Consider the following statements:

I. Women who are pregnant, lactating, single or widowed, and transgender persons are listed as gender-based vulnerable groups.
II. Persons with Disabilities are listed under disability-based vulnerability.
III. Elderly people are listed under location-based vulnerability.
IV. People living in coastal areas, seismic Zone V, flood plains and hills are location-based vulnerable groups.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: I, II and IV are correct: gender-based, disability-based and location-based groups are listed as stated. III is false because the elderly are an age-based vulnerable group, not a location-based one.
106.tq: Match each group with the basis of its vulnerability.
n: Pregnant women are gender-based vulnerable groups in India. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 68-70]
Lactating women are gender-based vulnerable groups in India. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 68-70]
Single women are gender-based vulnerable groups in India. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 68-70]
Widows are gender-based vulnerable groups in India. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 68-70]
Transgender persons are gender-based vulnerable groups in India. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 68-70]
Persons with Disabilities are disability-based vulnerable groups in India. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 68-70]
Poor people are socio-economic vulnerable groups in India. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 68-70]
SC/ST communities are socio-economic vulnerable groups in India. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 68-70]
Informal sector workers are socio-economic vulnerable groups in India. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 68-70]
Homeless people are socio-economic vulnerable groups in India. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 68-70]
People living in high-risk zones are location-based vulnerable groups in India. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 68-70]
Coastal areas are high-risk zones for location-based vulnerability. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 68-70]
Seismic Zone V is a high-risk zone for location-based vulnerability. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 68-70]
Flood plains are high-risk zones for location-based vulnerability. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 68-70]
Hilly areas are high-risk zones for location-based vulnerability. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 68-70]
Migrants are vulnerable groups in India. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 68-70]
Refugees are vulnerable groups in India. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 68-70]
Remote tribal communities are vulnerable groups in India. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 68-70]
Women are gender-based vulnerable groups in India. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 68-70]
xs: **I, II and IV only** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
I is correct: by **gender** — **pregnant**, **lactating**, **single women**, **widows** and **transgender persons**.
II is correct: **Persons with Disabilities (PwD)** are the **disability** group.
III is wrong: **elderly people** are an **age**-based group; IV is correct: **coastal areas**, **Seismic Zone V**, **flood plains**, **hilly areas** are **location**-based.
xa: By **age**: **children** — especially **unaccompanied** children — and the elderly.
**Socio-economic**: **poor people**, **SC/ST communities**, **informal sector workers**, **homeless people**.
**Others**: **migrants**, **refugees**, **remote tribal communities**.

106.s: The overall coordination of disaster management at the Union level is undertaken through the disaster management division of the:
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
106.x: The disaster management division of the Ministry of Home Affairs undertakes overall coordination.
106.tq: Identify the responsible ministry rather than the operational force or technical ministry.
xs: **Overall coordination** is done by the DM division of the **Ministry of Home Affairs** — option **(2)**.
**Policy-making** and approving the **National Plan** rest with **NDMA**, chaired by the PM.
xa: **NPDRR** is chaired by the **Union Home Minister**.
**DG Fire Services, Civil Defence & Home Guards** is under **MHA**.
MHA added **heatwave and lightning** to notified disasters.

106.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority?
o: It is chaired by the Governor and manages only post-disaster compensation.
It is chaired by the Chief Minister and functions as the chief nodal agency for disaster management in the State.
It is chaired by the District Collector and controls the National Disaster Response Force.
It is headed by the Municipal Commissioner and operates only in municipal corporations.
106.x: APSDMA is chaired by the Chief Minister, serves as the State’s chief nodal agency, runs the State Emergency Operations Centre and supports early warning.
106.tq: Match the authority with its chairperson and operational responsibilities in a state-level scenario.
xs: **APSDMA** is **chaired by the Chief Minister** and is the **chief nodal agency** — option **(2)**.
It runs the **State Emergency Operations Centre** and **early warning** — not limited to compensation.
xa: Governed by **AP DM Rules 2007**.
**NDMA** is chaired by the **PM**; **NPDRR** by the **Union Home Minister**.
**NIDM southern campus**: **Kondapavuluru**, Krishna district.
AP SDMF/NDMF allotted = **Rs 521.17 crore**.

106.s: The National Platform for Disaster Risk Reduction (NPDRR) is chaired by the
106.x: NPDRR is a multi-stakeholder body chaired by the Union Home Minister.
106.tq: Identify the chairperson of the coordinating body rather than its implementing agencies.
xs: **NPDRR** is chaired by the **Union Home Minister** — option **(4)**.
⚠ The **Prime Minister** chairs **NDMA**, not NPDRR.
xa: NPDRR is a **multi-stakeholder** body.
**MHA** DM division: **overall coordination**.
**APSDMA**: chaired by the **Chief Minister**.

106.s: SACHET is best described as
o: an ISRO GIS database for all hazards
an NDMA alert system based on the Common Alerting Protocol and developed by C-DOT
a volunteer-training scheme run by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj
106.x: SACHET is NDMA's Common Alerting Protocol-based alert system, developed by C-DOT.
106.tq: Match the system with its authority, technical protocol and developer.
xs: **SACHET** is NDMA's **Common Alerting Protocol**-based alert system, developed by **C-DOT** — option **(3)**.
**Tsunami Ready** is the UNESCO-IOC programme; **NDEM** is ISRO's **GIS database**; **Aapda Mitra** trains volunteers.
xa: **NTRB**: set up by **MoES**, chaired by Director **INCOI**.
**ISRO** support: **DMS programme** + **NDEM**.
**Social media** is a **complementary**, not replacement, tool.

106.s: Which NDMA focus area gives special focus to children?
106.x: NDMA's School Safety programme focuses on children. Gender mainstreaming focuses on women.
106.tq: Match each NDMA focus area to its group.
n: School safety under the NDMA focus areas has a special focus on children. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 68-70]
xs: **School Safety** gives **special focus** to **children** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Gender mainstreaming** focuses on **women's leadership** and **participation**.
**Minimum standards of relief** cover **vulnerable groups**; **community-based DRR** includes the **most vulnerable** in **planning**.
xa: **Disability-inclusive DRR** guidelines came in **2019**.
**Aapda Mitra** trains **community volunteers** as **first responders**.
**Children** — especially **unaccompanied** children — are a vulnerable group by **age**.

106.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. NDMA was notified in 2006.
II. NDRF was raised in 2006.
III. Mock exercises and awareness campaigns are conducted regularly by NDMA, NIDM, NDRF and State authorities throughout the year.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: All three are correct: NDMA was notified in 2006, NDRF raised in 2006, and NDMA, NIDM, NDRF and the States hold drills and campaigns all year.
106.tq: Recall the 2006 milestones.
n: NDMA was notified in 2006. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 50-51]
The NDRF was raised in 2006. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 50-51]
NDMA, NIDM, NDRF and State authorities conduct mock exercises and awareness campaigns regularly throughout the year. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 50-51]
xs: **All three — I, II and III** — are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
**NDMA** was **notified** in **2006**; **NDRF** was **raised** in **2006**.
**NDMA, NIDM, NDRF** and **State authorities** hold **mock exercises** and **awareness campaigns** **regularly** through the **year**.
xa: **NDMA Formation Day** is around **September 26–27**.
**NDRF Raising Day** is **January 19**.
**World Humanitarian Day** (**August 19**) honours **humanitarian workers**.

106.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) National Institute of Disaster Management (NIDM)
(b) Aapda Mitra
(c) State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF)
(d) National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF)

List-II
(i) Scheme that trains community volunteers as first responders, including in search and rescue and first aid
(ii) Primary-level fund for immediate relief expenditure at the State level
(iii) Premier institute for capacity building, training and research in disaster management
(iv) Fund used for emergency response, relief and rehabilitation in severe calamities
106.x: NIDM is the premier training institute, Aapda Mitra trains community volunteers, the State fund gives immediate relief, and the National fund covers severe disasters. The answer is a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv.
106.tq: Match each body or fund to its role.
n: The State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) is the primary-level fund for immediate relief expenditure at the State level. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-4]
The National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) is used for emergency response, relief and rehabilitation in severe calamities. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-4]
The National Institute of Disaster Management (NIDM) is a premier institute for capacity building, training and research in disaster management. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-4]
Aapda Mitra is a scheme of the National Disaster Management Authority that trains community volunteers as first responders. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-4]
Aapda Mitra training includes search and rescue and first aid. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-4]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**NIDM**: **premier institute** for **capacity building, training and research**; **Aapda Mitra**: trains **community volunteers** as **first responders**.
**SDRF**: **primary-level** fund for **immediate relief** at **State level**; **NDRF** (fund): **severe calamities**.
xa: Aapda Mitra covers **search and rescue** and **first aid**.
**Notified disasters** eligible for SDRF/NDRF: **14 since Aug 2026** (earlier **12**).
⚠ **No man-made calamity is notified**.

106.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The National Crisis Management Committee is headed by the Cabinet Secretary.
The High Level Committee is chaired by the Union Home Minister.
The National Crisis Management Committee is chaired by the Union Home Secretary.
The National Executive Committee is chaired by the Union Home Secretary.
106.x: Option C is incorrect: the Cabinet Secretary heads the NCMC. The Union Home Secretary chairs the NEC, and the Home Minister the High Level Committee.
106.tq: Match each committee to its chair.
n: The Cabinet Secretary heads the National Crisis Management Committee (NCMC). [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 41-43]
The National Executive Committee is chaired by the Union Home Secretary. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 41-43]
The High Level Committee is chaired by the Union Home Minister. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 41-43]
xs: The incorrect statement is that the **NCMC** is **chaired** by the **Union Home Secretary** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **NCMC** is headed by the **Cabinet Secretary**.
The **NEC** is **chaired** by the **Union Home Secretary**; the **High Level Committee** by the **Union Home Minister**.
xa: The High Level Committee handles **financial approvals**.
The **NPDRR** is also chaired by the **Union Home Minister**.
The **NDMA** is **chaired** by the **Prime Minister**.

106.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The District Collector or District Magistrate has overall disaster management responsibility at the district level.
Statement B: The community is usually the first responder at the ground level.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
106.x: Both are true: the Collector/DM is in overall charge in the district, and the community is usually the first responder.
106.tq: Recall the district-level roles.
n: The Collector or District Magistrate is responsible for overall disaster management at the district level. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 41-43]
The community is usually the first responder at the ground level. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 41-43]
xs: **Both statements are true** — so option **(1)** is correct.
A: the **Collector** / **District Magistrate** has **overall responsibility** at the **district level**.
B: the **community** is usually the **first responder** at the **ground level**.
xa: **State Government**: **post-disaster relief** and **rehabilitation**.
**Union Government**: **physical** and **financial resources**, **early warning**, **coordination**.
The **DM Act** gives **PRIs and ULBs** a legal role.

106.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS)
(b) National Crisis Management Committee
(c) State Government
(d) State Crisis Management Committee

List-II
(i) Handles nuclear, biological and chemical emergencies
(ii) Coordinates and directs responses to national crises
(iii) Responsible for post-disaster relief and rehabilitation
(iv) Handles state-level crises and is chaired by the Chief Secretary
106.x: The CCS handles nuclear, biological and chemical emergencies, the NCMC directs national crisis response, the State handles relief and rehabilitation, and the State Crisis Committee handles State crises. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
106.tq: Match each body to its role.
n: The Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS) handles nuclear, biological and chemical emergencies. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 41-43]
The National Crisis Management Committee coordinates and directs responses to national crises. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 41-43]
The State Government is responsible for post-disaster relief. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 41-43]
The State Government is responsible for post-disaster rehabilitation. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 41-43]
The State Crisis Management Committee handles state-level crises. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 41-43]
The State Crisis Management Committee is chaired by the Chief Secretary. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 41-43]
xs: The correct match is **a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**CCS**: **nuclear, biological and chemical emergencies**; **NCMC**: **coordinates** and **directs** responses to **national crises**.
**State Government**: **post-disaster relief** and **rehabilitation**; **State Crisis Management Committee**: **state-level crises**, **chaired** by the **Chief Secretary**.
xa: The **NCMC** is headed by the **Cabinet Secretary**.
The **District Collector** has **overall** disaster management at district level.
The **community** is usually the **first responder**.

106.s:
Consider the following statements:

I. The Disaster Management Division strengthens Civil Defence.
II. The Disaster Management Division strengthens Home Guards.
III. The National Disaster Management Authority is under the administrative control of the Ministry of Home Affairs.
IV. The National Disaster Response Force is under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: All four are correct: the DM Division strengthens civil defence and home guards, and the NDMA and NDRF both come under the MHA.
106.tq: Recall the DM Division's role.
n: The Disaster Management Division strengthens Civil Defence. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 41-43]
The Disaster Management Division strengthens Home Guards. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 41-43]
The National Disaster Management Authority is under the administrative control of the Ministry of Home Affairs. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 41-43]
The National Disaster Response Force is under the Ministry of Home Affairs. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 41-43]
xs: **All four — I, II, III and IV** — are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
The DM Division **strengthens** **Fire Services**, **Civil Defence** and **Home Guards**.
The **NDMA** is under the MHA's **administrative control**; the **NDRF** is **under** the MHA, with **operational control** through the NDMA.
xa: **NIDM** is a **capacity-building** institute under the MHA.
The DM Division handles **administrative** and **budgetary** matters of NDMA, NDRF and NIDM.
The **NIDM southern campus** is at **Kondapavuluru**, **Krishna district, AP**.

106.s: The High Level Committee is concerned with which of the following?
o: Operation of the National Emergency Operations Centre
Coordination of international assistance and HADR operations
106.x: The High Level Committee, under the Union Home Minister, approves financial assistance from the national funds.
106.tq: Recall the HLC's role.
n: The High Level Committee deals with financial approvals. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 41-43]
xs: The **High Level Committee** is concerned with **financial approvals** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is **chaired** by the **Union Home Minister**.
The **National Emergency Operations Centre** and **HADR** coordination are DM Division roles; **relief and rehabilitation** is the **State Government**'s.
xa: The **NEC** is **chaired** by the **Union Home Secretary**.
The **NCMC** is headed by the **Cabinet Secretary**.
**SDRF** is the **primary-level** fund for **immediate relief** at State level.

106.s: Operation Vanilla was associated with humanitarian assistance to
o: Turkey and Syria after the 2023 earthquake
106.x: Operation Vanilla assisted Madagascar following Cyclone Diane in 2020.
106.tq: Link the operation name to the assisted country and disaster event.
xs: **Operation Vanilla** helped **Madagascar** after **Cyclone Diane, 2020** — option **(1)**.
**Karuna** = Myanmar (**Cyclone Mocha**, **2023**); **Maitri** = Nepal (earthquake, **2015**); **Dost** = Turkey, Syria (earthquake, **2023**).
xa: **Sadbhav**: Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar — **Typhoon Yagi**, **2024**.
**Brahma**: Myanmar — earthquake, **2025**.
**NDMA** also **supports other countries** in major disasters.

106.s: World Tsunami Awareness Day is observed on:
106.x: World Tsunami Awareness Day is 5 November. 13 October is the DRR day, 23 March Meteorological Day, and 19 August Humanitarian Day.
106.tq: Match each day to its date.
n: October 13 is observed as the International Day for Disaster Risk Reduction (IDDRR). [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 50-51]
November 5 is observed as World Tsunami Awareness Day. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 50-51]
World Tsunami Awareness Day raises awareness about tsunami risks and preparedness. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 50-51]
August 19 is observed as World Humanitarian Day. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 50-51]
March 23 is observed as World Meteorological Day. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 50-51]
World Tsunami Awareness Day focuses specifically on tsunami early warning and preparedness. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 50-51]
xs: **World Tsunami Awareness Day** is on **November 5** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**March 23** is **World Meteorological Day**; **August 19** is **World Humanitarian Day**; **October 13** is **IDDRR**.
xa: It is **declared** by the **UN** and observed **since 2015**.
It is inspired by **Japan's "Inamura-no-hi"**.
**UNESCO-IOC Tsunami Ready**: **24 Odisha villages** recognised; target **100 villages**.

106.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: International Day for Disaster Risk Reduction is observed on October 13.
World Meteorological Day is observed on March 23.
World Environment Day is observed on June 15.
World Humanitarian Day is observed on August 19.
106.x: Option C is incorrect: World Environment Day is 5 June, not 15 June. The other dates are right.
106.tq: Match each day to its date.
n: October 13 is observed as the International Day for Disaster Risk Reduction (IDDRR). [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 50-51]
August 19 is observed as World Humanitarian Day. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 50-51]
March 23 is observed as World Meteorological Day. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 50-51]
June 5 is observed as World Environment Day. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 50-51]
xs: The incorrect statement is "World Environment Day on **June 15**" — so option **(3)** is correct.
**World Environment Day** is on **June 5**.
The others are right: **IDDRR** on **October 13**; **World Meteorological Day** **March 23**; **World Humanitarian Day** **August 19**.
xa: **Earth Day** is **April 22**.
**NDRF Raising Day** is **January 19**.
**IDDRR** has been observed **since 1989**.

106.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Earth Day
(b) World Environment Day
(c) International Day for Disaster Risk Reduction
(d) World Meteorological Day

List-II
(i) Links environmental degradation with increased disaster risk
(ii) Core global disaster risk reduction awareness day
(iii) Observed on April 22; relevant through environmental protection and climate-related disaster risk
(iv) Declared by the World Meteorological Organization

Codes:
106.x: Earth Day (22 April) concerns environmental protection, World Environment Day links environmental damage with disaster risk, IDDRR is the main DRR day, and the WMO declared Meteorological Day. The answer is a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv.
106.tq: Match each day to its theme.
n: The World Meteorological Organization declared World Meteorological Day. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 50-51]
April 22 is observed as Earth Day. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 50-51]
Earth Day is relevant to disaster management through environmental protection and climate-related disaster risk. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 50-51]
World Environment Day links environmental degradation with increased disaster risk. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 50-51]
The International Day for Disaster Risk Reduction is the core global disaster risk reduction awareness day. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 50-51]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Earth Day**: **April 22**, **environmental protection** and **climate-related disaster risk**; **World Environment Day**: links **environmental degradation** with **increased disaster risk**.
**IDDRR**: the **core** global DRR **awareness day**; **World Meteorological Day**: **declared** by the **WMO**.
xa: **World Environment Day** is **June 5**.
**IDDRR** is on **October 13**, declared by the **UN**.
**World Meteorological Day** (**March 23**) stresses **weather, climate and water services** in DRR.

106.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Japan
(b) Nepal
(c) Turkey
(d) Myanmar

List-II
(i) Deployment in 2011
(ii) Deployment in 2015
(iii) Deployment in 2023 called Operation Dost
(iv) Deployment in 2025 after the Mandalay earthquake, under Operation Brahma
106.x: The NDRF went to Japan after the 2011 tsunami, Nepal after the 2015 earthquake, Turkey in 2023 under Operation Dost and Myanmar in 2025 under Operation Brahma. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
106.tq: Recall the year and operation name of each foreign deployment.
n: NDRF was deployed to Japan in 2011. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 37-39]
NDRF was deployed to Nepal in 2015. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 37-39]
NDRF was deployed to Turkey in 2023. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 37-39]
NDRF’s Turkey deployment was called Operation Dost. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 37-39]
NDRF was deployed to Myanmar. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 37-39]
xs: The correct match is **a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv** — so option **(1)** is correct.
NDRF went to **Japan** in **2011** and **Nepal** in **2015**.
**Turkey** in **2023** — **Operation Dost**; **Myanmar** — **Operation Brahma** (earthquake, **2025**).
xa: **Operation Vanilla**: **Madagascar** (Cyclone Diane, **2020**).
**Operation Karuna**: **Myanmar** (Cyclone Mocha, **2023**).
**Operation Sadbhav**: Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar (Typhoon Yagi, **2024**).

106.s: Tsunami mitigation and preparedness in India are associated with
o: IMD warnings and shelter belts only
INCOI warnings and Tsunami Ready villages
106.x: Tsunami warning information is associated with INCOI, while Tsunami Ready villages support local preparedness.
106.tq: Distinguish tsunami-specific institutions and preparedness measures from those for other hazards.
xs: Tsunami preparedness rests on **INCOI warnings** and **Tsunami Ready villages** — option **(4)**.
**IMD warnings and shelter belts** are cyclone measures; **embankments and reservoir regulation** are flood measures.
xa: **UNESCO-IOC Tsunami Ready:** **24 Odisha villages** recognised; target **100 villages**.
**NTRB** set up by **MoES**, chaired by Director **INCOI**.
Tsunamis are **geological** disasters.

106.s: The Tsunami Ready recognition programme associated with UNESCO-IOC has recognised how many villages in Odisha?
106.x: Twenty-four Odisha villages have been recognised under the UNESCO-IOC Tsunami Ready programme. The target is 100 villages.
106.tq: Distinguish the achieved number from the larger target number.
xs: **24 Odisha villages** are recognised under **UNESCO-IOC Tsunami Ready** — option **(3)**.
**100** is the **target**, not the number recognised.
xa: **NTRB** set up by **MoES**, chaired by Director **INCOI**.
Tsunami warning: **INCOI**.
**ISRO support:** **DMS programme** + **NDEM** (GIS database).

106.s: The southern campus of the National Institute of Disaster Management in Andhra Pradesh is located at:
106.x: The southern campus of NIDM was set up at Kondapavuluru in Krishna district, pursuant to the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014.
106.tq: Combine the institution, location and district to avoid nearby-place substitutions.
xs: The **NIDM southern campus** is at **Kondapavuluru**, **Krishna district** — option **(1)** (**APPSC 2024**).
It was set up under the **AP Reorganisation Act 2014**.
xa: **NDMA** lays down policy for **NIDM**.
**APSDMA** is chaired by the **Chief Minister**.
AP: **longest coastline on the east coast**.

106.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The vulnerable cyclone stretch in Andhra Pradesh is Ongole–Machilipatnam.
Planting lots of trees along coastal areas is a mitigation measure for cyclones.
The vulnerable cyclone stretch in Andhra Pradesh is Machilipatnam–Kakinada.
The maximum human-life loss in Andhra Pradesh occurred during the 1977 Cyclone.
106.x: Option C is incorrect: Andhra Pradesh's most cyclone-prone stretch is Ongole–Machilipatnam. The 1977 Diviseema cyclone caused the most deaths.
106.tq: Recall AP's cyclone-prone stretch.
n: Planting many trees along coastal areas is a mitigation measure for cyclones. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 30-32]
The vulnerable cyclone stretch in Andhra Pradesh extends from Ongole to Machilipatnam. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 30-32]
The maximum human-life loss in Andhra Pradesh occurred in the 1977 cyclone. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 30-32]
xs: The incorrect statement is that AP's vulnerable stretch is **Machilipatnam–Kakinada** — so option **(3)** is correct.
AP's **vulnerable cyclone stretch** is **Ongole** to **Machilipatnam**.
The rest hold: the **1977 cyclone** caused the **maximum human-life loss**; coastal **shelter belts** and **mangroves** are cyclone mitigation.
xa: Mangroves at **Coringa** and **Krishna** buffer storm surge.
**Cyclone shelters** and IMD warnings are other measures.
AP has the **longest** coastline on the **east coast**.

106.s: Which document provides key guidelines for heatwave management?
o: Heat Action Plans of States and Cities
NDMA Guidelines for Preparation of Action Plan – Prevention and Management of Heat Wave
IMD Colour-Coded Alert Guidelines for Heatwave Forecasting
106.x: NDMA's guidelines for heatwave action plans are the key document. States and cities use them to draw up their own heat action plans.
106.tq: Discriminate national guidelines from local plans.
n: The NDMA Guidelines for Preparation of Action Plan – Prevention and Management of Heat Wave provide key guidelines for heatwave management. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 70-72]
xs: The key document is the **NDMA Guidelines for Preparation of Action Plan – Prevention and Management of Heat Wave** — so option **(3)** is correct.
These **key guidelines** were **updated 2019**.
**Heat Action Plans** are prepared by **states** and **cities** using NDMA and IMD support.
xa: A **heatwave** = **abnormally high temperatures** **exceeding** the **normal maximum temperature** in **summer**.
**Cool roofs** = **reflective coatings** or **white painting** of **roofs**.
Notified disasters: **14 since Aug 2026** — **heatwave and lightning** added.

106.s: Heat Action Plans are prepared by which of the following with support from NDMA and IMD?
o: Only the National Disaster Management Authority
106.x: States and cities prepare heat action plans with help from NDMA and the IMD.
106.tq: Recall who prepares heat action plans.
n: Heat Action Plans are prepared by states and cities with support from NDMA and IMD. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 70-72]
xs: **Heat Action Plans** are **prepared** by **states** and **cities** — so option **(1)** is correct.
They get **support** from **NDMA** and **IMD**; neither body prepares them alone.
xa: Public awareness: **do's and don'ts**, **ORS distribution**, **cooling centres**.
Structural measures: **shade structures**, **drinking water points**.
NDMA heatwave guidelines were **updated 2019**.

106.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
 a. Nodal agency for forecasting
 b. Guidelines on Cold Wave and Frost
 c. Early warning system
 d. Agricultural measure

List-II
 i. Colour-coded alerts
 ii. Frost protection techniques for crops
 iii. India Meteorological Department
 iv. NDMA Guidelines, 2021
106.x: The IMD forecasts, NDMA issued the 2021 cold wave guidelines, early warning uses colour codes, and frost protection is the farm measure. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
106.tq: Match each item to its role.
n: The India Meteorological Department is the nodal agency for forecasting cold waves. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-74]
The NDMA Guidelines on Cold Wave and Frost were issued in 2021. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-74]
The IMD issues colour-coded cold-wave alerts. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-74]
Agricultural measures against cold waves include frost-protection techniques for crops. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-74]
Cold waves affect agriculture through crop damage due to frost. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-74]
The IMD cold-wave alert colours are Yellow, Orange and Red. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-74]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Nodal agency for forecasting**: **India Meteorological Department**; **Guidelines on Cold Wave and Frost**: **NDMA**, **2021**.
**Early warning**: **colour-coded** alerts; **agricultural measure**: **frost-protection techniques** for **crops**.
xa: IMD's cold-wave alerts are **Yellow**, **Orange** and **Red**.
Cold-wave season: **November to March**; peak **December to February**.
Protective measures: **warm clothing**, **night shelters**, **community kitchens**.

106.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Cold waves mainly occur in India from November to March.
Cold waves are notified disasters eligible for assistance under SDRF/NDRF.
The NDMA Guidelines on Cold Wave and Frost were issued in 2022.
The peak impact of cold waves is during December–February.
106.x: Option C is incorrect: NDMA's guidelines on cold waves and frost came in 2021, not 2022. Cold waves run from November to March, peaking December–February.
106.tq: Recall the cold wave guidelines year.
n: The main cold-wave season in India is November to March. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-74]
The peak impact of cold waves in India occurs during December to February. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-74]
The NDMA Guidelines on Cold Wave and Frost were issued in 2021. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-74]
A cold wave is a notified disaster eligible for assistance under the SDRF and NDRF. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-74]
xs: The incorrect statement is that the NDMA cold-wave guidelines were **issued in 2022** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **NDMA Guidelines on Cold Wave and Frost** were **issued 2021**.
The others are true: season **November to March**, **peak** **December to February**; a **notified disaster** under **SDRF** and **NDRF**.
xa: **Cold day**: maximum temperature departure of **–4.5°C to –6.4°C**.
**Severe cold day**: departure **less than –6.4°C**.
Power demand **increases** during cold waves.

106.s: A cold wave is best defined as:
o: A significant drop in minimum temperature below the normal climatological average during the winter season
A significant drop in maximum temperature below the normal climatological average during the summer season
A rise in minimum temperature above the normal climatological average during the winter season
A significant drop in rainfall below the normal climatological average during the winter season
106.x: A cold wave is a sharp drop in minimum temperature below normal in winter. The other options reverse the season or the direction.
106.tq: Recall the definition of a cold wave.
n: A cold wave is a significant drop in minimum temperature below the normal climatological average during the winter season. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-74]
xs: A **cold wave** is a **significant drop** in **minimum temperature** **below** the **normal climatological average** in **winter** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The other options wrongly use **maximum temperature**, a **rise**, or **rainfall**.
xa: Cold-wave impacts: **hypothermia**, **frostbite**, **respiratory diseases**.
Most vulnerable: **homeless people**, **elderly**, **children**, **outdoor workers**, **street vendors**.
**Crop damage** due to **frost**; it **affects livestock**.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about the NDMA guidelines on cold waves:

I. They focus on preparedness.
II. They focus on vulnerability mapping.
III. They focus on community awareness.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: All three are correct: NDMA's cold wave guidelines focus on preparedness, mapping vulnerability and community awareness.
106.tq: Recall the cold wave guidelines.
n: The NDMA guidelines focus on preparedness. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-74]
The NDMA guidelines focus on vulnerability mapping. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-74]
The NDMA guidelines focus on community awareness. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-74]
xs: **All three — I, II and III** — are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **NDMA Guidelines on Cold Wave and Frost** (**2021**) focus on **preparedness**, **vulnerability mapping** and **community awareness**.
xa: IMD issues **Yellow**, **Orange** and **Red** cold-wave alerts.
Cold wave is a **notified disaster** eligible under **SDRF** and **NDRF**.
**Medical preparedness** is a protective measure.

106.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Medical preparedness is included among protective measures against cold waves.
Statement B: Frost protection techniques for crops are identified as a general protective measure against cold waves.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
106.x: A is true and B is false: medical preparedness is a general protective measure, but frost protection for crops is listed separately as a farm measure.
106.tq: Discriminate general from farm measures.
n: Protective measures against cold waves include medical preparedness. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-74]
xs: **Statement A is true, Statement B is false** — so option **(3)** is correct.
A: **medical preparedness** is listed among **protective measures**, with **warm clothing**, **night shelters** and **community kitchens**.
B: **frost-protection techniques** for **crops** are listed separately as **agricultural measures**.
xa: Agriculture suffers **crop damage** from **frost** and livestock is affected.
Power demand **increases** during cold waves.
**Severe cold day** = maximum temperature departure **less than –6.4°C**.

106.s: Disaster risk reduction (DRR) works best when it:
o: Concentrates only on post-disaster relief distribution
Addresses the underlying causes of vulnerability
Relies only on rescue by national forces
Focuses solely on rebuilding damaged infrastructure
106.x: DRR is most effective when it tackles the underlying causes of vulnerability (APPSC 2024 key). Relief, rescue and rebuilding are response or recovery activities, not the core of risk reduction.
106.tq: DRR = fix root causes of vulnerability (APPSC 2024).
xs: **DRR** works best when it **addresses the underlying causes of vulnerability** — option **(2)** (**APPSC 2024** key).
**Relief** and **rescue** belong to the **response** phase; **rebuilding** belongs to **recovery** — not the core of risk reduction.
xa: **Mitigation** (pre-disaster): **embankments, mangroves, zoning**.
**Significance:** the **DM Act 2005** moved India from **relief → risk reduction**.
**Risk = Hazard x Vulnerability / Capacity**.

106.s: The gas that leaked in the Bhopal Gas Tragedy of 1984 was:
106.x: The Bhopal leak was of methyl isocyanate (MIC). Chlorine, carbon monoxide and ammonia are common distractors but were not the gas released at Bhopal.
106.tq: Bhopal = MIC, not chlorine/CO/ammonia.
xs: The Bhopal gas was **methyl isocyanate (MIC)** — option **(2)**.
It was **not chlorine, CO or ammonia** — these are the usual distractors.
xa: Date: night of **2-3 December 1984**.
Plant of **Union Carbide India Ltd**, Bhopal.
A chemical leak = **anthropogenic / man-made** hazard.
Chemical accident rules: **MSIHC Rules 1989** + **CAEPPR Rules 1996**.

106.s: Which of the following best describes cool roofs as a heatwave-management measure?
o: Shade structures over all public roads
Reflective coatings or white painting of roofs
106.x: Cool roofs use reflective coatings or white paint to keep buildings cooler.
106.tq: Recall what cool roofs are.
n: Cool roofs use reflective coatings or white painting of roofs. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 70-72]
xs: **Cool roofs** mean **reflective coatings** or **white painting** of **roofs** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Shade structures** are a separate **structural measure**; **cooling centres** are a **public awareness** measure.
**Adjusted working hours** is another listed measure, not a cool roof.
xa: **Heat Action Plans** are prepared by **states** and **cities**.
IMD issues **colour-coded alerts** for heatwaves.
Heatwave season runs mainly **March to June**.

106.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Floods can be worsened by deforestation.
Statement B: Landslides can be caused by unscientific construction.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
106.x: Both are true: deforestation worsens floods, and unscientific construction triggers landslides. These are socio-natural hazards, mixing nature and human action.
106.tq: Recall socio-natural hazards.
n: Floods can be worsened by deforestation. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 47-49]
Landslides can be caused by unscientific construction. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 47-49]
xs: **Both statements are true** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Floods** are **worsened** by **deforestation**; **landslides** are caused by **unscientific construction**.
These are **socio-natural hazards** — a **combination** of **natural and human factors**.
xa: **Technological** hazards include **dam failure**.
**Man-made** disasters arise from **human activity, negligence or technological failure**.
**Landslide** mitigation: **hazard zonation mapping**, early warning.

106.s: Which statement correctly describes Andhra Pradesh's coastline in the stated geographical context?
o: It is the longest coastline in India and lies on the west coast
It is the second-longest coastline in India and the shortest on the east coast
It has no significant exposure to coastal hazards
It is the third-longest coastline in India and the longest on the east coast
106.x: Andhra Pradesh now has the third-longest coastline in India and the longest on the east coast. 'Second-longest' is the older figure, AP is on the east (not west) coast, and its long coast makes it highly exposed to cyclones and storm surges.
106.tq: Handle comparative rankings carefully and avoid substituting an older figure for the stated current one.
xs: Andhra Pradesh has the **third-longest coastline in India** and the **longest on the east coast** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**"Second-longest"** is only the **older figure**, and AP lies on the **east coast**, not the west.
A long coast means high exposure: cyclone mitigation uses **cyclone shelters**, evacuation and **mangroves (Coringa, Krishna)**.
xa: The **Godavari floods of July 2026** tested **NDRF/SDRF** and early warning in AP.
**APSDMA** is chaired by the **Chief Minister** and runs the **State Emergency Operations Centre**.
The **NIDM southern campus** is at **Kondapavuluru**, **Krishna district**, under the **AP Reorganisation Act 2014**.

107.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Draft Public Health (Prevention, Control and Management of Epidemics, Bio-Terrorism and Disasters) Bill, 2017 has been enacted and has replaced the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897.
2. The Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897 provides the legal framework for biological disasters and was used during COVID-19.
3. The 2017 draft Bill dealt with epidemics, bio-terrorism and disasters.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the 2017 draft Bill was meant to replace the 1897 Act but was not enacted. Statement 2 is correct: the 1897 Act is the legal framework for biological disasters and was used in COVID-19. Statement 3 is correct: the draft Bill covered epidemics, bio-terrorism and disasters. Hence '2 and 3 only'.
107.tq: 1897 Act still in force; 2017 Bill never enacted.
xs: **Statements 2 and 3 only** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is wrong: the **2017** draft Bill was meant to replace the **1897** Act but was **not enacted**.
Statement 2 is correct: the **Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897** is the legal framework for **biological disasters**, used in **COVID-19**.
Statement 3 is correct: the draft Bill covered **epidemics, bio-terrorism and disasters**.
xa: The **2020 amendment** made violence against health workers **cognizable and non-bailable**.
Penalty: **3 months to 5 years** jail + **Rs 50,000 to Rs 2 lakh** fine.
Critics note the 1897 Act does not define "**dangerous epidemic disease**".

107.s: Under the Epidemic Diseases Act framework, which of the following is correctly matched?
107.x: Urgent cases must be reported within 24 hours, while routine cases must be reported within three days.
107.tq: Separate the shorter urgent-reporting period from the routine period.
xs: **Urgent cases** must be reported **within 24 hours** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Routine cases** are reported **within 3 days**, so options (2), (3) and (4) mix up the timelines.
xa: Example of notification: **20 states** made **human rabies** notifiable (Jan **2026**).
⚠ **24 hours** is also the IHR deadline to report a possible **PHEIC** to **WHO**.
The Act provides the legal framework for **biological disasters** and was used in **COVID-19**.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about the 2020 amendment to the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897:
1. It came as an ordinance in April 2020 and became an Act in September 2020.
2. It made violence against health workers cognizable and non-bailable.
3. It gave State Governments exclusive powers over inspection at ports of entry.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: Statement 1 is correct: ordinance in April, Act in September 2020. Statement 2 is correct: violence against health workers became cognizable and non-bailable. Statement 3 is wrong: the Centre, not the States, got powers over inspection at ports of entry. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
107.tq: 2020 amendment: protection of health workers + Centre's port powers.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the amendment came as an **ordinance in April** and became an **Act in September 2020**.
Statement 2 correct: violence against health workers became **cognizable and non-bailable**.
Statement 3 wrong: the **Centre**, not the States, got powers over **inspection at ports of entry**.
xa: Penalty for violence: **3 months to 5 years** jail + **Rs 50,000 to Rs 2 lakh** fine.
Grievous hurt: **6 months to 7 years** + **Rs 1-5 lakh** fine.
PM-ABHIM builds preparedness at **50 points of entry**.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC):
1. It was formerly the National Institute of Communicable Diseases (NICD).
2. It runs the Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme and sends Outbreak Investigation Teams.
3. The National Public Health Emergency Operations Centre is run by DGHS, not NCDC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: Statement 1 is correct: NCDC was formerly NICD. Statement 2 is correct: it runs IDSP and sends Outbreak Investigation Teams. Statement 3 is wrong: NCDC itself runs the National Public Health Emergency Operations Centre; DGHS is MoHFW's technical arm. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
107.tq: NCDC = surveillance + outbreak response + NPHEOC; DGHS = technical arm.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **NCDC** was formerly **NICD**.
Statement 2 correct: NCDC runs **IDSP** and sends **Outbreak Investigation Teams**.
Statement 3 wrong: **NCDC itself** runs the **National Public Health Emergency Operations Centre**; DGHS is only MoHFW's technical arm.
xa: **IDSP** began in **2004** under **NHM**, with a **Central Surveillance Unit** in Delhi.
Centre asked states to step up **IDSP** surveillance for **Ebola** (23 May **2026**).
AP's **zoonotic disease action plan** is being drawn up with **NCDC**, **US CDC** and **Jhpiego**.

107.s:
With reference to the institutional framework for health emergencies, consider the following statements:
1. NDMA is chaired by the Prime Minister.
2. State Disaster Management Authorities are chaired by Chief Ministers.
3. NDMA lays down guidelines and coordinates health emergencies under the Disaster Management Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: All three are correct: NDMA is chaired by the Prime Minister, SDMAs by the Chief Ministers, and NDMA lays down guidelines and coordinates health emergencies under the DM Act, 2005 (e.g. its Biological Disaster Management guidelines of 2008).
107.tq: Verify both the chairpersons and the statutory function before selecting the code.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
**NDMA** is chaired by the **PM**; **SDMAs** are chaired by **Chief Ministers**.
NDMA lays down **guidelines** and coordinates health emergencies under the **DM Act**.
xa: NDMA issued the **Biological Disaster Management guidelines** in **2008**.
The **March 2020** lockdown was ordered by **NDMA + MHA** under the **DM Act, 2005**.
**MoHFW** is still the **nodal ministry for epidemics**.

107.s:
Andhra Pradesh’s zoonotic disease action plan is being prepared under which approach and with which institutions?
1. One Health approach
2. NCDC, US CDC and Jhpiego
3. INSACOG, UNEP and WHO only
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: AP is preparing the plan under the One Health approach with NCDC, US CDC and Jhpiego. The third statement names institutions not given for this action plan.
107.tq: Spot the substituted institutional partners in the false statement.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
AP's plan is under the **One Health** approach, with **NCDC, US CDC and Jhpiego** (29 Jul **2026**).
Statement 3 is wrong: **INSACOG** is a genome-sequencing network, not a partner of this plan.
xa: About **60%** of infectious diseases and **75%** of emerging ones are zoonotic.
Other AP angles: the **Covid Pharma app** and **PM-ABHIM** units in **Vijayawada**.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about INSACOG:
1. Its full form is Indian SARS-CoV-2 Genomics Consortium.
2. It is a network of genome-sequencing laboratories.
3. It tracks SARS-CoV-2 variants.
4. It functions under the combined institutional framework of DBT, ICMR, CSIR and MoHFW.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: All four are correct: INSACOG (Indian SARS-CoV-2 Genomics Consortium), set up in December 2020, is a network of genome-sequencing labs under DBT, ICMR, CSIR and MoHFW that tracks SARS-CoV-2 variants.
107.tq: Confirm the full form, network function, purpose and sponsoring institutions together.
xs: All four statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4** is correct.
**INSACOG** = **Indian SARS-CoV-2 Genomics Consortium**, a **genome-sequencing lab network**.
It **tracks variants** and works under **DBT, ICMR, CSIR and MoHFW**.
xa: INSACOG was set up in **Dec 2020**.
**ICMR-NIV Pune** is the apex virology lab with **BSL-4** containment.
COVID testing reached **1,364 government + 1,753 private labs** by Jan **2022**.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about PM-ABHIM components:
1. 631 Critical Care Hospital Blocks are planned in districts with over 5 lakh people.
2. 744 Integrated Public Health Laboratories are planned, one in every district.
3. 3,389 Block Public Health Units are planned in every State of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: Statement 1 is correct: 631 CCBs in districts with over 5 lakh people. Statement 3 is wrong: the 3,389 BPHUs are in 11 high-focus states, not every State. Statement 2 is correct: 744 IPHLs, one per district. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
107.tq: IPHL 744 (every district); CCB 631 (>5 lakh); BPHU 3,389 (11 high-focus states).
xs: **Statements 1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **631** **Critical Care Hospital Blocks** in districts with **over 5 lakh** people.
Statement 2 is correct: **744** **Integrated Public Health Laboratories**, one in every district.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **3,389** Block Public Health Units are in **11 high-focus states**.
xa: PM-ABHIM also has **15 Health Emergency Operation Centres** + **50 BHISHM Cubes**.
Points of entry: preparedness at **50**.
AP got **10 Critical Care Blocks and 12 IPHLs** costing **Rs 250 crore**.

107.s:
Under the IHR (2005), Member States are required to:
1. Build core capacities for surveillance and response.
2. Report possible Public Health Emergencies of International Concern to WHO within 24 hours.
3. Designate a National IHR Focal Point.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: All three are obligations under the IHR (2005): building surveillance and response capacities, reporting possible PHEICs to WHO within 24 hours, and naming a National IHR Focal Point.
107.tq: Select the comprehensive option when all listed international obligations are supported.
xs: All three are IHR obligations — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
States must build **core capacities for surveillance and response**.
They must report possible **PHEICs** to WHO **within 24 hours** and name a **National IHR Focal Point**.
xa: IHR (2005) has been **in force since 2007**.
