⚠ **24 hours** is also the deadline for **urgent notifiable cases** under the **1897 Act**.
The **2024 amendments** added a **"pandemic emergency"** tier.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about the International Health Regulations (2005):
1. The 2024 amendments added a higher 'pandemic emergency' tier.
2. The May 2026 Ebola outbreak was declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern.
3. The May 2026 Ebola outbreak met the criteria for a pandemic emergency.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 2024 amendments added the pandemic-emergency tier. Statement 2 is correct: the May 2026 Ebola outbreak was a PHEIC. Statement 3 is wrong: it did not meet the pandemic-emergency criteria. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
107.tq: PHEIC is not automatically a pandemic emergency - the new tier is higher.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the **2024 amendments** added a higher **"pandemic emergency"** tier.
Statement 2 correct: the **May 2026 Ebola** outbreak was a **PHEIC**.
Statement 3 wrong: it **did not meet the pandemic-emergency criteria** (18 May **2026**).
xa: Centre asked states to step up **IDSP** surveillance for **Ebola** (23 May **2026**).
PHEICs must be reported to WHO **within 24 hours**.
The **WHO Pandemic Agreement** was adopted on **20 May 2025**.

107.s: Which of the following developments is associated with the BRICS New Delhi Declaration?
o: Adoption of the WHO Pandemic Agreement
Declaration of the May 2026 Ebola outbreak as a pandemic emergency
Creation of a sub-working group on an integrated early-warning system for infectious diseases
107.x: The BRICS New Delhi Declaration set up a sub-working group on an integrated early-warning system for infectious diseases.
107.tq: Match the international forum with its specific institutional outcome.
xs: The **BRICS New Delhi Declaration** created a **sub-working group on an integrated early-warning system for infectious diseases** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **WHO Pandemic Agreement** was adopted on **20 May 2025** by WHO, not BRICS.
The **Ebola** outbreak **did not meet** the pandemic-emergency criteria.
xa: Dated **13 Sep 2026** — the same day **CCBs and IPHLs** opened in AP.
Ebola advisory to states: **23 May 2026**.
**744 IPHLs** are a **PM-ABHIM** component.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about India's COVID-19 response:
1. The national lockdown of March 2020 was ordered under the Disaster Management Act, 2005.
2. The lockdown was ordered by NCDC and ICMR.
3. Empowered Groups of the Ministry of Home Affairs ran the pandemic response.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: Statement 1 is correct: the lockdown was under the DM Act, 2005. Statement 2 is wrong: it was ordered by NDMA and MHA, not NCDC and ICMR. Statement 3 is correct: MHA Empowered Groups ran the response. Hence '1 and 3 only'.
107.tq: Lockdown = DM Act via NDMA + MHA, not the 1897 Act.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the **March 2020 national lockdown** was ordered under the **DM Act, 2005**.
Statement 2 wrong: it was ordered by **NDMA + MHA**, not NCDC and ICMR.
Statement 3 correct: **MHA Empowered Groups** ran the pandemic response.
xa: **NDMA** is chaired by the **PM**; **SDMAs** by the **Chief Ministers**.
**MoHFW** remains the **nodal ministry for epidemics**.
The **MoHFW Disaster Management Cell** (Dec **2020**) is the nodal unit for pandemic planning.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Disaster Management Plan (NDMP):
1. Issued in 2016, it was India's first national disaster management plan.
2. It aligns with the Sendai Framework (2015-30), the SDGs and the Paris Agreement.
3. It deals only with post-disaster response and recovery.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 2016 NDMP was India's first. Statement 2 is correct: it aligns with Sendai, the SDGs and Paris. Statement 3 is wrong: it covers prevention, mitigation, preparedness, response and recovery. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
107.tq: NDMP 2016 covers the whole cycle, not just response.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the **NDMP (2016)** was **India's first** national plan.
Statement 2 correct: it aligns with **Sendai (2015-30)**, the **SDGs** and **Paris**.
Statement 3 wrong: it covers **prevention, mitigation, preparedness, response and recovery**.
xa: NDMA issued the **Biological Disaster Management guidelines** in **2008**.
The **DM Act 2005** is the law under which NDMA operates.
PYQ key: **vaccines before an outbreak** = **mitigation**.

107.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The WHO Pandemic Agreement was adopted on 20 May 2025.
2. The International Health Regulations (2005) are a non-binding WHO declaration.
3. The IHR (2005) have been in force since 2007.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: Statement 2 is wrong: the IHR (2005) are a legally binding WHO instrument. Statement 3 is correct: they came into force in 2007. Statement 1 is correct: the WHO Pandemic Agreement was adopted on 20 May 2025. Hence '1 and 3 only'.
107.tq: IHR: adopted 2005, in force 2007, legally binding.
xs: **Statements 1 and 3 only** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the **WHO Pandemic Agreement** was adopted on **20 May 2025**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the **IHR (2005)** are a **legally binding** WHO instrument.
Statement 3 is correct: the IHR have been **in force since 2007**.
xa: IHR: report possible **PHEICs** to WHO **within 24 hours**; name a **National IHR Focal Point**.
**2024 amendments** added a higher "**pandemic emergency**" tier.
⚠ **24 hours** = both urgent notifiable cases (1897 Act) and PHEIC report (IHR).

107.s: Which Ministry is the nodal ministry in India for the management of epidemics (biological disasters)?
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
107.x: MoHFW is the nodal ministry for epidemics (PYQ), with DGHS as its technical arm and NCDC as the surveillance agency. MHA coordinates disasters in general, while Science and Technology and Environment ministries are not nodal for epidemics.
107.tq: Epidemic nodal = MoHFW; general DM = MHA.
xs: **MoHFW** is the **nodal ministry for epidemics** (PYQ) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**MHA** coordinated the COVID lockdown with **NDMA** under the DM Act, but is not nodal for epidemics.
Within MoHFW, **DGHS** is the **technical arm** and **NCDC** the surveillance agency.
xa: The **MoHFW DM Cell** (Dec **2020**) is the nodal unit for pandemic planning.
Epidemics count as **biological disasters**.
The **Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897** is the legal framework for biological disasters.

107.s: Which laboratory is regarded as the apex virology laboratory in India and has BSL-4 containment?
107.x: ICMR-NIV Pune is the apex virology laboratory and has BSL-4 containment facilities.
107.tq: Match the apex laboratory with its location and containment level.
xs: **ICMR-NIV, Pune** is the apex virology lab with **BSL-4** containment — so option **(3)** is correct.
**INSACOG** is a genome-sequencing consortium, and a **State Surveillance Unit** is part of IDSP.
xa: **BSL-3 labs** are being added through **VRDLs** and **PM-ABHIM**.
**INSACOG** was set up in **Dec 2020** under **DBT, ICMR, CSIR, MoHFW**.
COVID testing: **1,364 government + 1,753 private labs** by Jan **2022**.

107.s: Distributing vaccines before the occurrence of an epidemic is classified under which phase of the disaster management cycle?
107.x: Pre-outbreak vaccine distribution reduces the potential impact of an epidemic and is therefore a mitigation measure.
107.tq: Classify the measure by asking whether it reduces impact before the event.
xs: **Distributing vaccines before an outbreak** is a **mitigation** measure (PYQ key) — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Preparedness** = surveillance, stockpiles, hospital readiness, mock drills.
**Response** = isolation, quarantine, contact tracing; **Recovery** = restoring services, rehabilitation.
xa: Other epidemic mitigation measures: **sanitation** and **vector control**.
Epidemics count as **biological disasters**.
⚠ Vaccines **before** an outbreak = mitigation; treatment **during** it = response.

107.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Mitigation — sanitation and vector control
2. Preparedness — hospital readiness and mock drills
3. Response — isolation, quarantine and contact tracing
4. Recovery — rehabilitation and economic relief
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
107.x: All four pairs correctly associate epidemic measures with the mitigation, preparedness, response and recovery phases respectively.
107.tq: Match each measure to the phase in which it is normally undertaken.
xs: All four pairs are correctly matched — so option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4** is correct.
**Mitigation**: sanitation, vector control; **Preparedness**: hospital readiness, mock drills.
**Response**: isolation, quarantine, contact tracing; **Recovery**: rehabilitation, economic relief.
xa: PYQ key: **distributing vaccines before an outbreak** = **mitigation**.
**Lockdown** and **treatment** also fall under the **response** phase.
The **NDMP (2016)** covers prevention, mitigation, preparedness, response and recovery.

107.s: BHISHM Cubes, deployed during Operation Sindoor, are associated with which programme?
o: PM Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM)
107.x: Under PM-ABHIM, MoHFW's DM Cell has 15 Health Emergency Operation Centres and 50 BHISHM Cubes, which were deployed during Operation Sindoor. NDRF, IDSP and Aapda Mitra are separate programmes.
107.tq: BHISHM Cubes (50) + HEOCs (15) = PM-ABHIM.
xs: **BHISHM Cubes** belong to **PM-ABHIM (PM Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission)** — so option **(3)** is correct.
PM-ABHIM provides **15 Health Emergency Operation Centres** + **50 BHISHM Cubes**, deployed during **Operation Sindoor**.
**IDSP** is a surveillance programme (**2004**), not the cubes' parent scheme.
xa: PM-ABHIM: **744 IPHLs**, one in every district.
PM-ABHIM: **631 Critical Care Hospital Blocks** in districts with over **5 lakh** people.
PM-ABHIM: preparedness at **50 points of entry**.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about disease surveillance in India:
1. The Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme (IDSP) was launched in 2004 under the National Health Mission.
2. IDSP works through a Central Surveillance Unit in Delhi along with State and District Surveillance Units.
3. The Integrated Health Information Platform (IHIP) was launched nationwide in 2018.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: Statement 1 is correct: IDSP began in 2004 under NHM. Statement 2 is correct: CSU in Delhi plus State and District units. Statement 3 is wrong: IHIP began in a few states in 2018 and went nationwide only from September 2021. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
107.tq: IHIP: 2018 pilot, nationwide Sep 2021.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **IDSP** was launched in **2004** under **NHM**.
Statement 2 correct: its units are a **Central Surveillance Unit** (Delhi) + State and District Surveillance Units.
Statement 3 wrong: **IHIP** began in a few states in **2018** and went **nationwide only from Sep 2021**.
xa: IDSP is implemented by **MoHFW** and run by **NCDC**.
The **IHIP** portal pools grassroots data in **real time**.
Centre asked states to step up IDSP surveillance for **Ebola** (May **2026**).

107.s: Which of the following correctly represents the three categories of reporting used in disease surveillance?
107.x: Surveillance data are reported through syndromic (S), presumptive (P) and laboratory-confirmed (L) categories.
107.tq: Expand the surveillance abbreviations and distinguish them from site categories.
xs: The three reporting categories are **Syndromic, Presumptive and Laboratory-confirmed** (S, P, L) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Sentinel and private sites** are additional data sources, not reporting categories.
xa: These feed **IDSP**, launched in **2004** under **NHM**.
The **IHIP** portal pools this grassroots data in **real time**.
IDSP units: **Central Surveillance Unit** (Delhi) + State and District units.

107.s: Approximately what proportions of infectious diseases and emerging infectious diseases, respectively, are zoonotic?
107.x: About 60% of infectious diseases and 75% of emerging infectious diseases are zoonotic.
107.tq: Preserve the order of the two percentages while comparing disease categories.
xs: About **60%** of infectious diseases and **75%** of emerging ones are **zoonotic** — so option **(4)** is correct.
This high zoonotic share is why the **One Health** approach links human, animal and environmental health.
xa: AP is drawing up a **zoonotic disease action plan** under **One Health** (Jul **2026**).
Partners: **NCDC**, **US CDC** and **Jhpiego**.
⚠ Do not reverse the pair: **60%** = all infectious, **75%** = emerging.

107.s:
Geospatial technology is useful in epidemic management for which of the following purposes?
1. Contact tracing
2. Mapping hotspots or containment zones
3. Real-time spatial planning of vaccine distribution
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: Geospatial technology supports contact tracing, hotspot and containment-zone mapping, and GIS-based real-time vaccine distribution planning.
107.tq: Check whether all three statements describe related applications of GIS.
xs: All three uses are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
**Geospatial technology** can **perform contact tracing** (PYQ statement I correct) and map **hotspots or containment zones**.
**Vaccine distribution** works best with **GIS real-time spatial mapping** (PYQ).
xa: **BBMP** ran a **COVID war room with GIS** (PYQ).
AP's **Covid Pharma app** (**25 Apr 2020**) tracked buyers of cough, cold and fever medicines.

107.s: The COVID war room supported by GIS was set up by which organisation?
107.x: The GIS-supported COVID war room was set up by the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP).
107.tq: Identify the local authority associated with the operational measure.
xs: The GIS-based **COVID war room** was set up by **Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP)** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**NCDC** runs IDSP; **ICMR-NIV Pune** is a BSL-4 lab; **MHA** coordinated the lockdown.
xa: **GIS real-time spatial mapping** works best for **vaccine distribution** (PYQ).
Geospatial technology can **perform contact tracing** and map **containment zones**.
AP's **Covid Pharma app** was launched on **25 Apr 2020**.

107.s: The Covid Pharma application launched in Andhra Pradesh on 25 April 2020 was used to track persons purchasing which medicines over the counter?
o: Medicines for cough, cold and fever
107.x: The AP Medical and Health Department launched Covid Pharma on 25 April 2020 to track people buying over-the-counter medicines for cough, cold and fever.
107.tq: Combine the app’s launch date, authority and precise purpose.
xs: **Covid Pharma** tracked people buying OTC **medicines for cough, cold and fever** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was launched on **25 Apr 2020** by AP's **Medical and Health Department** (PYQ).
xa: **BBMP** ran a **COVID war room with GIS** (PYQ).
Geospatial technology supports **contact tracing** and **hotspot mapping**.
Other AP angles: **zoonoses action plan** (Jul **2026**) and **PM-ABHIM** units in **Vijayawada**.

107.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897 is correct?
o: It was replaced by the 2017 draft Bill, which is already in force.
It has been criticised as colonial and for lacking a definition of dangerous epidemic disease and rights safeguards.
It applies only to non-infectious diseases.
It provides a detailed statutory definition of dangerous epidemic disease and comprehensive rights safeguards.
107.x: The 1897 Act is criticised as colonial and for lacking both a definition of dangerous epidemic disease and adequate rights safeguards.
107.tq: Find the option that accurately reflects the criticism rather than an exaggerated legal claim.
xs: The 1897 Act is criticised as **colonial**, **lacking a definition of "dangerous epidemic disease"** and **rights safeguards** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **2017 draft Bill** meant to replace it is **still pending**, not in force.
It is the framework for **biological disasters** (infectious epidemics), not non-infectious diseases.
xa: It was used during **COVID-19**.
**2020 amendment**: violence against health workers is **cognizable and non-bailable**.
Urgent cases reported **within 24 hours**; routine **within 3 days**.

108.s: Which one of the following branches is correctly matched with its broad field?
108.x: Red biotechnology concerns medicine, green agriculture, white industry and blue marine applications.
108.tq: Match colour coding with the sector it represents.
xs: **Red biotechnology** = **medical** applications — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Green** = agriculture, not marine; **White** = industrial, not medical diagnostics.
**Blue** = marine, not industrial enzymes.
xa: White biotech covers **enzymes, biofuels, bioplastics, precision fermentation** and green chemicals.

108.s:

108.x: Both are true: the genome is an organism's full genetic information, and a zygote's genome joins DNA from two gametes.

A genome is genetic information. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 63-66]

108.s:

n: The human genome contains approximately 3 billion DNA bases. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 63-66]
More than 99% of DNA bases are the same among humans. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 63-66]
A genome is roughly fixed for a line except for mutations. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 63-66]
A transcriptome can change with environmental conditions. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 63-66]
xs: **All four** statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **human genome** has about **3 billion DNA bases**; more than **99%** are the **same** among humans.
The genome is roughly **fixed** except for **mutations**; the **transcriptome** can **change** with **environmental conditions**.
xa: The transcriptome = **sum total** of **expressed mRNA molecules**.

108.s:
Assertion (A): microRNA can suppress or reduce the expression of a target gene.
Reason (R): Its typical action is post-transcriptional regulation.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
108.x: Both are true and R explains A: microRNA silences genes after transcription by blocking or breaking their mRNA.
108.tq: Check whether R is the mechanism of A.
n: microRNA typically acts through post-transcriptional regulation. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 73-75]
microRNA suppresses or reduces target gene expression. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 73-75]
microRNA regulates gene expression. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 73-75]
microRNA is conceptually linked to gene silencing. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 73-75]
xs: **Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**microRNA** is a **small non-coding RNA** that **suppresses** or **reduces** target gene expression.
It does so through **post-transcriptional regulation** — linked to **gene silencing**.
xa: **Victor Ambros and Gary Ruvkun** **identified** **microRNA**.
**mRNA** **carries** the **genetic message** for **protein production**.
**Transcriptome** = all **expressed mRNA molecules**.

108.s: Which of the following sets contains only ex-situ bioremediation techniques?
108.x: Landfarming, composting and biopiles require contaminated material to be treated outside its original location and are ex-situ techniques.
108.tq: Classify the techniques by whether the contaminated material remains at the site.
xs: **Landfarming, composting and biopiles** are all **ex-situ** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Bioventing, biosparging and bioaugmentation** are **in-situ** techniques.
Option (3) mixes ex-situ **slurry reactors** and landfarming with in-situ **biosparging**.
xa: Ex-situ = material **excavated/removed** and treated elsewhere in beds or reactors.
Ex-situ **bioreactors** (slurry, aqueous) are the **costliest** but **fastest**.
**Landfarming/biopiles** are low-cost ex-situ options.

108.s: A contaminated site is treated without excavating the polluted material, using a passive and relatively cheaper method. This approach is known as:
108.x: In-situ bioremediation treats contamination at its original site and is generally cheaper and more passive than ex-situ treatment.
108.tq: Apply the site-treatment condition first: treatment at the original location indicates in-situ remediation.
xs: Treatment at the site without excavation, cheap and passive, is **in-situ bioremediation** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Ex-situ** needs the material **excavated/removed**; **thermal remediation** is not biological; **biomagnification** is a food-chain process.
xa: In-situ = "**treats contaminated material directly at the site**" (APPSC-G2 **2025**).
In-situ techniques: **bioventing**, **biosparging**, **bioaugmentation**.
In-situ limits: **slow**, long treatment time; **metals/inorganics** complicate.

108.s:
Consider the following statements regarding in-situ and ex-situ bioremediation:
1. In-situ treatment is the most cost-efficient and relatively passive.
2. In-situ treatment is generally faster than treatment in ex-situ bioreactors.
3. Ex-situ treatment may face space needs, excavation, and mass-transfer and bioavailability problems.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
108.x: Statement 1 is correct: in-situ is the most cost-efficient and relatively passive. Statement 2 is wrong: in-situ is slow, while bioreactors are the fastest (optimised conditions, rapid kinetics). Statement 3 is correct: ex-situ limits include space, excavation, abiotic loss, mass-transfer and bioavailability problems. So A misses 3, C and D wrongly include 2; B is right.
108.tq: In-situ = cheap but slow; ex-situ bioreactors = fast but costly.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **in-situ** is the **most cost-efficient** and relatively **passive**.
Statement 2 wrong: in-situ is **slow**; ex-situ **bioreactors** are the **fastest** (rapid kinetics).
Statement 3 correct: ex-situ faces **space needs**, **excavation**, **mass-transfer and bioavailability** problems.
xa: Ex-situ also suffers **abiotic loss**.
Bioreactors have **high capital and operating cost** (costliest).
In-situ = "**treats contaminated material directly at the site**" (APPSC-G2 **2025**).

108.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Bioventing — injection of air below the water table
Biosparging — supply of air or nutrients through wells
Landfarming — treatment in a slurry bioreactor
108.x: Bioaugmentation adds specific pollutant-degrading microbes, so C is correct. A and B are swapped: bioventing supplies air/nutrients through wells to soil, while biosparging injects air below the water table. Landfarming is an ex-situ land-treatment method, distinct from slurry bioreactors.
108.tq: Match each technique with its defining operation before eliminating swapped descriptions.
xs: **Bioaugmentation** = **addition of selected microorganisms** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Options (1) and (2) are swapped: **bioventing** supplies air/nutrients through wells to soil; **biosparging** injects air **below the water table**.
**Landfarming** is ex-situ land treatment, different from **slurry bioreactors**.
xa: Oil spills → **bioaugmentation** (APPSC-G2 **2025**).
**Biostimulation** adds nutrients (**N, P**) and oxygen to boost **native** microbes.
⚠ Bioaugmentation **introduces** microbes; biostimulation **stimulates existing** ones.

108.s: Which one of the following is NOT an advantage of bioremediation?
o: It is usually cheaper than conventional clean-up methods
It invariably produces rapid results irrespective of pollutant and site conditions
In-situ treatment can cause little disruption at the contaminated site
It generally uses fewer chemicals and may avoid secondary pollution
108.x: Bioremediation is often slow, and its results vary with the pollutant, organism, site conditions and co-contaminants. The other three are recognised advantages.
108.tq: Identify the absolute claim that conflicts with the variable performance of biological treatment.
xs: **"Invariably rapid results"** is NOT an advantage — bioremediation is **slow** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Results **vary with pollutant, organism, site conditions and co-contaminants**.
**Cheaper**, **little site disruption** (in-situ) and **few chemicals / no secondary pollution** are real advantages.
xa: Bioremediation also **restores ecosystems**.
Conventional methods are **faster** but costly, with residues and emissions.
**Metals/inorganics** complicate bioremediation.

108.s:
With reference to bioremediation and conventional remediation, consider the following statements:
1. Bioremediation is generally slower than conventional remediation.
2. Bioremediation can be scalable and community-applied.
3. Conventional remediation is generally less dependent on site biology.
4. Bioremediation always has uniform reliability irrespective of pollutant, organism and site.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
108.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the reliability of bioremediation varies with the pollutant, organism, site and co-contaminants.
108.tq: Treat the absolute word ‘always’ as a warning and verify the stated limitations.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Bioremediation is **slow**; conventional is **faster**; bioremediation is **scalable, community-applied**.
Conventional is **less dependent on site biology**; statement 4 wrong — bioremediation's reliability **varies** with pollutant, organism, site, co-contaminants.
xa: Cost: bioremediation **low** ("fraction of the funds"); conventional **high**.
Side effects: bioremediation has **no secondary pollution**; conventional leaves **residues, emissions**.
Conventional = **thermal, chemical, excavation**.

108.s:

o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

n: The first MSCs were found in bone marrow. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 16-17]
Bone marrow is the discovery location of the first MSCs, not the name of a person. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 16-17]
xs: **Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A** — so option **(2)** is correct.
A: the **first MSCs** were **found** in **bone marrow** — a **discovery location**.
R (differentiation into bone, cartilage, fat) is a property of MSCs, not why they were found in bone marrow.
xa: ⚠ "Bone marrow" is **not** the **name** of a **person**.
**SRC** was the **first oncogene**, **discovered** in **1970**.
National Guidelines for **Stem Cell Research 2017** govern stem cells.

108.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Engineered Pseudomonas and algae — oil-spill treatment
2. PETase-producing bacteria — plastic degradation

4. Biofilters — microbe-laden beds for pollutants in air and gas streams
108.x: All four pairs are correct. Engineered Pseudomonas and algae can target oil spills, PETase-producing bacteria break down plastic, engineered microbes can produce PLA and PHA, and biofilters use microbe-laden beds to treat air or gas streams.
108.tq: Verify each tool by its product or environmental application; the comprehensive option is justified when all pairs align.
xs: All four pairs are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4** is correct.
Engineered **Pseudomonas and algae** → oil spills; **PETase**-producing bacteria → plastic.
**PLA, PHA** → bioplastics from engineered microbes; **biofilters** → microbe-laden beds for air and gas streams.

Waste-to-energy: **Gobar-Dhan** biogas; municipal waste to **CNG** in **Hyderabad and Pune**.
**2G ethanol** at **IOCL Panipat**; **E20** target **2025-26**.

108.s: Which one of the following statements regarding bioremediation is correct?
o: It can address oil spills, heavy metals, pesticides, solvents and organic pollutants.
It is restricted to soil and cannot be applied to water or air.
It always requires excavation of contaminated material.
108.x: Bioremediation can be applied to soil, water and air and may address oil spills, heavy metals, pesticides, solvents and other organic pollutants. It may be in-situ or ex-situ, and engineered microbes can be used.
108.tq: Test the scope of the process across media, pollutants and treatment conditions.
xs: Bioremediation can tackle **oil spills, heavy metals, pesticides, solvents and organic pollutants** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It works in **soil, water and air**, so (3) is wrong.
Microbes **can be genetically engineered**, and **in-situ** methods need no excavation — so (1) and (4) are wrong.
xa: **In-situ** techniques: **bioventing**, **biosparging**, **bioaugmentation**.
**Ex-situ**: landfarming, composting, biopiles, **bioreactors** (costliest, fastest).
Limitation: it is **slow** and pollutant-specific.

108.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Water hyacinth — phytoextraction of heavy metals
Eucalyptus along sewage ponds — arsenite degradation by bacteria
Ideonella sakaiensis — removal of arsenate from groundwater
Bacillus flexus — degradation of PET plastic
108.x: Water hyacinth is a standard example of phytoextraction, taking up heavy metals from water. Eucalyptus along sewage ponds transpires surplus wastewater (not arsenite degradation), Ideonella sakaiensis degrades PET plastic, and Bacillus flexus acts on arsenate, not PET.
108.tq: Use the pollutant-agent association and reject the options that swap biological agents.
xs: **Water hyacinth** = **phytoextraction of heavy metals** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Eucalyptus** along sewage ponds **transpires surplus wastewater**; it does not degrade arsenite.
**Ideonella sakaiensis** degrades **PET plastic**; **Bacillus flexus** acts on **arsenate**.
xa: Phytoextraction: contaminant stored in **roots and shoots**, then **harvested**.
**Acinetobacter junii** acts on **arsenite**.
Natural phytoremediators: **mangroves**, estuarine and wetland vegetation.

108.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with an application of bioremediation?
o: Oil spills — bioaugmentation with oil-degrading bacteria
Heavy metals — exclusive use of algal blooms
Sewage drains — burning of contaminated soil
108.x: Oil spills and oily sludge may be treated through bioaugmentation with oil-degrading bacteria. The other options describe harmful processes or unsuitable treatments.
108.tq: Match the pollutant with its biological treatment route and reject reversed ecological processes.
xs: **Oil spills** are treated by **bioaugmentation with oil-degrading bacteria** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Biomagnification** and **burning contaminated soil** are not bioremediation; heavy metals use **hyperaccumulator plants** and metal-absorbing microbes.
xa: **TERI** consortium was used at **Chennai port**.
**CPCB** handles bioremediation of oil-contaminated soils.
Sewage drains: **biostimulation**, aquatic plants, **constructed wetlands**.

108.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Technique)
a. Mycoremediation
b. Rhizofiltration
c. Biosparging
d. Rhizoremediation

List-II (Typical application)
i. Absorption or precipitation of contaminants from water by plant roots
ii. Injection of air under pressure below the water table
 iii. Use of fungi for treating organic pollutants
iv. Stimulation of microbes in the rhizosphere by plant roots

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
108.x: Mycoremediation uses fungi, rhizofiltration uses plant roots to remove contaminants from water, biosparging injects air below the water table, and rhizoremediation involves root–microbe interactions in the rhizosphere.
108.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes containing an incorrect technique–application match.
xs: The code is **a–iii, b–i, c–ii, d–iv** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Mycoremediation** = fungi for organic pollutants; **Rhizofiltration** = roots absorb/precipitate contaminants from water.
**Biosparging** = air injected **below the water table**; **Rhizoremediation** = roots stimulate rhizosphere microbes.
xa: Rhizofiltration targets **metals and radionuclides** in water.
⚠ **Bioventing** = soil; **Biosparging** = groundwater.
**Bioaugmentation** adds specific pollutant-degrading microbes.

108.s:
Consider the following statements regarding bioaugmentation and biostimulation:
1. Bioaugmentation introduces specific pollutant-degrading microbes into a contaminated site.
2. Biostimulation enhances the activity of existing microbes by supplying nutrients and oxygen.
3. Oilzapper is an example associated with bioaugmentation, whereas addition of nitrogen and phosphorus to polluted lakes is associated with biostimulation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
108.x: All three are correct: bioaugmentation introduces specific pollutant-degrading microbes (e.g. TERI's Oilzapper on oil spills), while biostimulation boosts existing microbes with nutrients and oxygen (e.g. adding N and P to polluted lakes and ponds).
108.tq: Use the meaning–example distinction to separate bioaugmentation from biostimulation.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
**Bioaugmentation introduces** specific pollutant-degrading microbes (native consortia or GE strains).
**Biostimulation stimulates existing** microbes with **nutrients and oxygen**.
**Oilzapper** on oil spills = bioaugmentation; **N and P** added to lakes = biostimulation.
xa: Oil spills → **bioaugmentation** (APPSC-G2 **2025**).
**Oilzapper** was developed by **TERI** (with Indian Oil).

108.s:
Match the micro-organism with the pollutant it is associated with in bioremediation:
a. Ideonella sakaiensis
b. Bacillus flexus
c. Acinetobacter junii
i. Arsenite
ii. PET plastic
iii. Arsenate
Select the correct answer:
108.x: Ideonella sakaiensis degrades PET plastic, Bacillus flexus acts on arsenate and Acinetobacter junii on arsenite. B gives Ideonella arsenate, C gives it arsenite, and D swaps the two arsenic bacteria.
108.tq: Ideonella = PET; flexus = arsenATE; junii = arseniTE.
xs: The code is **a-ii, b-iii, c-i** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Ideonella sakaiensis** → **PET plastic** (**2026**).
**Bacillus flexus** → **arsenate**; **Acinetobacter junii** → **arsenite**.
xa: ⚠ Do not swap the two arsenic bacteria: flexus = arsen**ate**, junii = arsen**ite**.
**PETase**-producing bacteria break down plastic.
Arsenic hyperaccumulator plant: **Pteris vittata** (Chinese brake fern).

108.s:
Consider the following statements about plants used in phytoremediation:
1. Sunflower can accumulate heavy metals, uranium and other radionuclides.
2. Water hyacinth can take up heavy metals and toxic materials from water.
3. Indian mustard is associated with the accumulation of lead, cadmium and selenium.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
108.x: All three are correct: sunflower accumulates heavy metals and uranium/other radionuclides, water hyacinth takes up heavy metals and toxic materials from water, and Indian mustard (Brassica juncea) accumulates lead, cadmium and selenium.
108.tq: Check each plant–contaminant association independently before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
**Sunflower**: heavy metals, **uranium** and other radionuclides; **Water hyacinth**: heavy metals and toxic materials in water.
**Indian mustard (Brassica juncea)**: **lead, cadmium, selenium**.
xa: **Pteris vittata** → **arsenic**; **Alyssum** → **nickel**.
**Thlaspi caerulescens** → **zinc, cadmium**.
Water hyacinth is the standard **phytoextraction** example.

108.s: Constructed wetlands are best described as systems in which:
o: Excavation removes contaminated soil for off-site disposal
Thermal treatment incinerates all sewage solids
Only chemical agents remove pollutants from groundwater
Plants and microbes break down and absorb pollutants
108.x: Constructed wetlands may be natural or engineered systems where plants and microbes break down and absorb pollutants, especially in sewage treatment.
108.tq: Identify the biological mechanism from the functions performed by plants and microbes.
xs: In **constructed wetlands**, **plants and microbes break down and absorb pollutants** — so option **(4)** is correct.
They are natural or engineered wetlands used in **sewage treatment** — not excavation, thermal or chemical methods.
xa: **Phytorid** (CSIR-NEERI): wastewater passes through a **planted gravel bed**.
Constructed wetlands are a **biological** method — counted as bioremediation.
Ponds use **water hyacinth** and **duckweed**.

108.s: Which of the following is included among the DBT biofuel targets?
o: Fuel from agricultural residue and municipal waste
108.x: The targets include fuels from agricultural residue and municipal waste, algal fuels, sustainable aviation fuel and integrated biorefineries.
108.tq: Prefer the option stated as a positive biotechnology application.
xs: DBT's biofuel targets include **fuel from agricultural residue and municipal waste** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The targets also list **algal fuels**, **SAF** and **integrated biorefineries** — so (1) and (3) contradict them.
xa: **2G ethanol** from crop residue at **IOCL Panipat**.
**E20 blending** target: **2025-26**.
Waste-to-energy: municipal waste to **CNG** in **Hyderabad and Pune**.

108.s: AMTZ refers to the:
o: Andhra Pradesh MedTech Zone located at Visakhapatnam
Agricultural Microbial Technology Zone located at Vijayawada
Advanced Medical Training Zone located at Amaravati
Andhra Pradesh Marine Technology Zone located at Kakinada
108.x: AMTZ is the Andhra Pradesh MedTech Zone located at Visakhapatnam.
108.tq: Discriminate between similar expansions and locations.
xs: **AMTZ** = **Andhra Pradesh MedTech Zone, Visakhapatnam** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is not located at Vijayawada, Amaravati or Kakinada.
xa: ⚠ Some notes say "**Amaravati Medtech Zone**" — the accepted form is Andhra Pradesh MedTech Zone.
Visakhapatnam was also chosen for a **marine biomaterials** research facility (Jan **2026**).
**IBDC** is at **RCB, Faridabad**.

108.s: Which of the following most appropriately describes bioremediation?
o: Thermal destruction of contaminated soil by incineration
Removal or degradation of pollutants by organisms or their enzymes
Physical excavation and permanent burial of contaminated material
Chemical conversion of all pollutants into radioactive substances
108.x: Bioremediation uses organisms such as bacteria, fungi, algae and plants, or their enzymes, to degrade or remove pollutants and restore a contaminated environment.
108.tq: Use the exact definition and distinguish biological treatment from thermal or physical treatment.
xs: **Bioremediation** is **removal or degradation of pollutants by organisms or their enzymes** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Incineration** is thermal, and **excavation/landfilling** physical — both are **not** bioremediation.
xa: APPSC-GS **2019**: "**Removal of pollutants from the biosphere by biological processes**".
Agents: **bacteria, fungi, algae and plants**; microbes can be genetically engineered.
Primary objective: **neutralising pollutants in contaminated soil and groundwater** (APPSC-G2 **2025**).
Nodal R&D body: **CSIR-NEERI** (Jun **2026**).

108.s: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes biomagnification from bioremediation?
o: Biomagnification is the rise of persistent toxins up a food chain, whereas bioremediation degrades or removes pollutants.
Bioremediation increases DDT concentration at successive trophic levels.
Biomagnification is a method of treating oil spills with bacteria.
Both terms refer to the biological removal of pollutants from soil.
108.x: Biomagnification is the increasing concentration of persistent toxins such as DDT or mercury along a food chain. Bioremediation is the biological degradation or removal of pollutants.
108.tq: Separate similar-looking biological terms by their direction of effect: pollutant increase versus pollutant removal.
xs: **Biomagnification** is the rise of persistent toxins up a food chain, while **bioremediation** degrades or removes pollutants — so option **(1)** is correct.
Biomagnification examples: **DDT**, **mercury** — it is a problem, not a treatment method.
xa: **Biofortification** = raising micronutrient content of crops.
**Eutrophication** = nutrient enrichment causing **algal blooms**; bioremediation can **control** it.
Oil spills are treated by **bioaugmentation**.

108.s: A municipal authority uses bacteria to break down organic waste. This activity is best classified as:
108.x: The biological breakdown of organic waste by bacteria is microbial degradation and therefore constitutes bioremediation.
108.tq: Identify the biological agent and process before distinguishing it from physical or thermal treatment.
xs: Breaking down organic waste with bacteria is **bioremediation** (APPSC-GS **2022**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ The distractors **desalination, fossilisation, incineration** are not biological clean-up.
xa: **Composting** organic waste and bacterial oil clean-up **are** bioremediation.
**SWM Rules 2026** mandate **biomining and bioremediation** of legacy dumpsites.
Only **60-70%** of waste is collected and **15-20%** processed.

108.s: Which one of the following is NOT an example of bioremediation?
o: Cleaning an oil spill with oil-degrading bacteria
Growing plants that absorb heavy metals from soil
108.x: Burning contaminated soil is thermal destruction, not a biological process, so it is not bioremediation (APPSC-G2 2025). Composting, bacterial oil clean-up and phytoremediation all use organisms to degrade or remove pollutants.
108.tq: Burning/incineration = thermal, never bioremediation.
xs: **Burning contaminated soil** is thermal destruction, so it is **NOT bioremediation** (APPSC-G2 **2025**) — option **(3)** is correct.
**Composting** and **bacterial oil clean-up** ARE bioremediation; plants absorbing heavy metals is **phytoremediation**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: "Which is NOT bioremediation?" = **burning contaminated soil**.
**Incineration** (thermal), **chemical treatment** and **desalination/excavation** (physical) are also not bioremediation.
APPSC-GS **2022**: breaking down organic waste with bacteria = **bioremediation**.
Agents: **bacteria, fungi, algae and plants**.

108.s:
With reference to Oilzapper and Oilivorous-S, consider the following statements:

2. Their development involved collaboration with Indian Oil.
3. They are used for degrading oily sludge and oil-contaminated sites.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
108.x: Oilzapper and Oilivorous-S are bacterial consortia developed by TERI with Indian Oil. They degrade oily sludge and oil-contaminated sites without leaving harmful residue.
108.tq: Test the complete profile of a named technology rather than relying only on its headline application.
xs: All four statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4** is correct.
**Oilzapper and Oilivorous-S** are bacterial consortia by **TERI** with **Indian Oil**.
They degrade **oily sludge** and oil-contaminated sites, leaving **no harmful residue**.
xa: **UPSC 2011**: Oilzapper = eco-friendly remediation of **oily sludge and oil spills**.
A TERI consortium was used at **Chennai port**.
⚠ **Oilzapper** = TERI; **Phytorid** = **CSIR-NEERI**.

108.s:
Match the Indian institution with the associated bioremediation product or role:

List-I (Institution)
a. TERI
b. CSIR-NEERI, Nagpur
c. CPCB
d. DBT-BIRAC

List-II (Product or role)
i. Funding biotechnology start-ups developing microbial kits for sewage plants and landfills
ii. Bioremediation of oil-contaminated soils
iii. Oilzapper and Oilivorous-S
aiv. Nodal bioremediation research and development, including heavy-metal removal from effluents

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
108.x: TERI is associated with Oilzapper and Oilivorous-S; CSIR-NEERI undertakes nodal bioremediation R&D; CPCB is associated with oil-contaminated soils; and DBT-BIRAC funds relevant biotechnology start-ups.
108.tq: Start with the distinctive TERI–Oilzapper pair and then match the institutional roles.
xs: The code is **a–iii, b–iv, c–ii, d–i** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**TERI** → **Oilzapper, Oilivorous-S**; **CSIR-NEERI, Nagpur** → nodal R&D and heavy-metal removal from effluents.
**CPCB** → oil-contaminated soils; **DBT-BIRAC** → funding startups with **microbial kits** for sewage plants and landfills.
xa: CSIR-NEERI also developed **Phytorid**.
BIRAC startup funding was noted in **Dec 2025**.
⚠ **Oilzapper** = TERI; **Phytorid** = CSIR-NEERI.

108.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Phytorid technology?
o: A chemical oxidation process developed by the US EPA
A constructed-wetland sewage-treatment technology developed by CSIR-NEERI
A thermal sewage-treatment system developed under SBM-U
An excavation-based technology developed by AMTZ
108.x: Phytorid is a constructed-wetland sewage-treatment technology developed by CSIR-NEERI.
108.tq: Link the technology with its developer and treatment category, avoiding swapped institutions.
xs: **Phytorid** is a **constructed-wetland sewage-treatment technology** by **CSIR-NEERI** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Wastewater passes through a **planted gravel bed**; it is not chemical, thermal or excavation-based.
xa: ⚠ **Phytorid** = CSIR-NEERI; **Oilzapper** = TERI.
CSIR-NEERI, Nagpur, is the **nodal bioremediation R&D** body.
**US EPA Superfund** guidelines are cited as the model for bioremediation.

108.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Visakhapatnam sewage-discharge issue:
1. The matter involved a Public Interest Litigation before the Andhra Pradesh High Court.
2. The stormwater drain passes through MVP Colony and Lawson’s Bay Colony.
3. The drain enters the sea at Pedda Jalaripeta.
4. The proposal favoured only large-scale pumping schemes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
108.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because immediate bioremediation and decentralised STPs were proposed as a lower-cost alternative to pumping schemes.
108.tq: Locate the single reversed policy claim among otherwise factual statements.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was an **AP High Court PIL** on sewage discharge (5 Jun **2026**); the drain runs through **MVP Colony and Lawson's Bay Colony** to **Pedda Jalaripeta**.
Statement 4 wrong: petitioner proposed **immediate bioremediation + decentralised STPs**, costing "a fraction" of pumping schemes.
xa: Petitioner: **Bollisetty Satyanarayana**.
Bioremediation cost: "**fraction of the funds**" of conventional methods.
Visakhapatnam was also chosen for a **marine biomaterials** research facility.

108.s:
Consider the following statements regarding SWM Rules 2026:
1. Annual auditing of landfills is mandatory.
2. All legacy dumpsites are to be mapped with biomining and bioremediation.
3. Landfills are intended for recyclable waste and energy-recoverable waste.
4. Environmental Compensation follows the ‘polluter pays’ principle.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
108.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is false because landfills are intended only for non-recyclable, non-energy-recoverable and inert waste.
108.tq: Find the reversed classification in the statement about what belongs in landfills.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 4** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Annual audit of landfills** is mandatory; legacy dumpsites are mapped with **biomining and bioremediation**.
Statement 3 wrong: landfills are only for **non-recyclable, non-energy-recoverable and inert** waste.
**Environmental Compensation** follows "**polluter pays**".
xa: Target: "**Lakshya Zero Dumpsites**" (**SBM-U 2.0**).
Only **60-70%** of waste collected; **15-20%** processed.

108.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Synthetic biology — current relevance in bioremediation discussions
2. Precision biotherapeutics — BioE3
3. Marine biomaterials research facility — Visakhapatnam
4. AMTZ — Vizag
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
108.x: All four associations are correct: synthetic biology is a current relevance area, precision biotherapeutics are linked with BioE3, Visakhapatnam was chosen for a marine biomaterials research facility, and AMTZ is associated with Vizag.
108.tq: Verify each association separately before selecting the all-inclusive code.
xs: All four pairs are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4** is correct.
**Synthetic biology** (Jun **2026**) is current; **precision biotherapeutics** sit under **BioE3** (Nov **2025**).
**Visakhapatnam** was chosen for a **marine biomaterials** facility (Jan **2026**); **AMTZ** is at Vizag.
xa: AMTZ = **Andhra Pradesh MedTech Zone**.
Vizag sewage-drain **PIL** and bioremediation proposal: 5 Jun **2026**.
DBT-BIRAC prioritises **Precision Biotherapeutics** under BioE3.

108.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: IgM is the primary antibody.
Statement B: IgM is the first antibody produced during an infection.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
108.x: Both are true: IgM is the primary antibody, the first made in a new infection.
108.tq: Recall IgM as the first antibody.
n: IgM is the primary antibody. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
IgM is the first antibody produced during an infection. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
xs: **Both statements are true** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**IgM** is the **primary antibody** — the **first** antibody made in an **infection**.
xa: **hCG** is the **placental hormone**.
**OAA** is the **organic product** in the **C4 pathway**.
**Edward Jenner** made the **smallpox vaccine**.

108.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Gregor Mendel conducted pea hybridisation experiments.
II. Triticale was the first man-made cereal.
III. Barney Clark was the recipient of an artificial heart.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
108.x: All three are correct: Mendel crossed peas, triticale was the first man-made cereal and Barney Clark received an artificial heart.
108.tq: Recall the biology firsts.
n: Gregor Mendel conducted pea hybridisation experiments. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
Triticale was the first man-made cereal. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
Barney Clark was the recipient of an artificial heart. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
xs: **All three — I, II and III** — are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
I: **Gregor Mendel** did **pea hybridisation experiments**.
II: **Triticale** is the **first man-made cereal crop**; III: **Barney Clark** received an **artificial heart**.
xa: **Christian Barnard** did the first **heart transplant** in **South Africa**.
**Jaya** is the **first dwarf rice variety** in India.
**hCG** is the **placental hormone** listed among firsts.

108.s: Who explained how the nucleotide sequence controls protein synthesis?
108.x: Khorana, Nirenberg and Holley cracked the genetic code, showing how nucleotide triplets specify amino acids (Nobel 1968). Watson and Crick gave the structure.
108.tq: Discriminate DNA structure from the genetic code.
n: Khorana, Nirenberg, and Holley explained how nucleotide sequences control protein synthesis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 21-24]
Khorana, Nirenberg, and Holley studied the genetic code. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 21-24]
Khorana, Nirenberg, and Holley worked in molecular biology. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 21-24]
xs: **Khorana, Nirenberg and Holley** explained how **nucleotide sequences** **control** **protein synthesis** — so option **(4)** is correct.
They worked out the **genetic code**.
**Miescher** **first isolated** DNA; **Watson, Crick and Wilkins** gave the **double helix**; **Kornberg** showed **DNA synthesis**.
xa: **Mendel** **laid** the **foundation** of **modern genetics**.
**Barbara McClintock** found **jumping genes**.
**Arber, Nathans and Smith** are linked to **restriction endonucleases**.

108.s:
Assertion (A): Mendel laid the foundation of modern genetics.
Reason (R): Mendel formulated the laws of inheritance and worked in genetics.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
108.x: Both are true and R explains A: Mendel's laws of inheritance from pea experiments are the foundation of modern genetics.
108.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: Mendel formulated the laws of inheritance. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 21-24]
Mendel worked in genetics. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 21-24]
Mendel laid the foundation of modern genetics. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 21-24]
xs: **Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Mendel** **formulated** the **laws of inheritance** in **genetics**.
Those laws **laid** the **foundation** of **modern genetics**.
xa: Mendel did the **first hybridization experiments** on **pea**.
**McClintock** (**genetics**) found **transposable elements**.
**Alec Jeffreys** (**genetics and forensics**) developed **DNA fingerprinting**.

108.s:
Consider the following statements:

Lukoskin was developed by DRDO and DIBER. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 18-19]
Amtooth was developed by DRDO. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 18-19]

xs: **All four — I, II, III and IV** — are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Saheli** contraceptive: **CDRI, Lucknow**; **Lukoskin**: **DRDO** and **DIBER**.
**Amtooth** and **Eczit**: **DRDO**.

**GM mustard (DMH-11)** by **Prof. Deepak Pental**'s team.
**Hybridoma technique** by **Georges Köhler** and **César Milstein**.

108.s: Marker-assisted selection is exemplified by the development of:
108.x: Sub1 flood-tolerant rice is given as an example of marker-assisted selection.

**R21** is a malaria vaccine, **Garima** a cloned buffalo, **Cervavac** an HPV vaccine.

Biofertilisers: **Rhizobium**, **Azotobacter**, **Azolla**, blue-green algae.

108.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The first polio vaccine was developed by Jonas Salk.
Covishield is associated with AstraZeneca and Oxford University.
Sputnik V was developed by Moderna, NIAID and BARDA.
The oral polio vaccine was developed by Albert Sabin.

n: The first polio vaccine was developed by Jonas Salk. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 18-19]
Covishield was developed by AstraZeneca and Oxford University. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 18-19]
Sputnik V was developed by the Gamaleya Research Institute. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 18-19]
The Moderna vaccine was developed by Moderna, NIAID, and BARDA. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 18-19]
The oral polio vaccine was developed by Albert Sabin. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 18-19]
xs: The incorrect statement is that **Sputnik V** was developed by **Moderna, NIAID and BARDA** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Sputnik V** came from the **Gamaleya Research Institute**; **Moderna, NIAID and BARDA** made the **Moderna** vaccine.
The rest are right: **Jonas Salk** (first polio vaccine), **Albert Sabin** (**oral polio vaccine**), **Covishield** (**AstraZeneca** and **Oxford University**).
xa: **Covaxin**: **Bharat Biotech** with **ICMR**.
**Cervavac** (qHPV) by the **Serum Institute of India** targets HPV / cervical cancer.
**ZyCoV-D** (**Zydus Cadila**) is the **first DNA vaccine**.

108.s: Which one of the following is NOT a component of Bio-RIDE?
o: National wildlife census and habitat mapping
108.x: Bio-RIDE has three components: R&D; industrial and entrepreneurship development; and bio-manufacturing and bio-foundry. Wildlife census is not one of them.
108.tq: Identify the unrelated component among a policy’s stated pillars.
xs: **National wildlife census** is not a **Bio-RIDE** component — so option **(3)** is correct.
Bio-RIDE's **3 components**: **R&D**, **Industrial/entrepreneurship development**, **Bio-manufacturing and bio-foundry**.
xa: Bio-RIDE merged **two DBT umbrella schemes**.
**BioE3** (**August 2024**) promotes high-performance biomanufacturing.
**BIRAC** is a DBT PSU.

108.s: The Dumpsite Remediation Accelerator is associated with which of the following?
o: Ministry of Jal Shakti under Namami Gange
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change under AMRUT 2.0
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs under SBM-U 2.0
108.x: The Dumpsite Remediation Accelerator is an initiative of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs under Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0.
108.tq: Use the ministry-and-scheme association to eliminate swapped-authority options.
xs: The **Dumpsite Remediation Accelerator** belongs to **MoHUA** under **SBM-U 2.0** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**BioE3** is a DBT policy, unrelated to dumpsites.
xa: Target: "**Lakshya Zero Dumpsites**".
It clears legacy dumpsites through **accelerated bioremediation** (Jun **2026**).
**SWM Rules 2026** mandate **biomining and bioremediation** of legacy dumpsites.

108.s: Which of the following statements regarding natural phytoremediators is correct?
o: Eucalyptus removes surplus wastewater mainly by injecting oxygen into groundwater.
Mangroves are used exclusively for thermal treatment of contaminated soil.
Mangroves, estuarine vegetation and wetland vegetation can act as natural phytoremediators, while Eucalyptus along sewage ponds transpires surplus wastewater.
Only desert shrubs can act as natural phytoremediators because wetland plants cannot absorb contaminants.
108.x: Mangroves, estuarine vegetation and wetland vegetation are natural phytoremediators. Eucalyptus planted along sewage ponds can transpire surplus wastewater.
108.tq: Combine the habitat clue with the plant process instead of confusing phytoremediation with air injection or thermal treatment.
xs: **Mangroves, estuarine and wetland vegetation** are natural phytoremediators, and **Eucalyptus** along sewage ponds **transpires surplus wastewater** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Eucalyptus works by **transpiration**, not oxygen injection; mangroves are not used for **thermal** treatment.
xa: Ponds use **water hyacinth** and **duckweed**.
**Constructed wetlands**: plants + microbes break down and absorb pollutants.
**Eucalyptus** is planted **along sewage ponds** for this purpose.

109.s: The primary goal of sustainable agriculture is to:
o: Replace all farm labour with mechanisation
Maximise yields through continuous use of chemical inputs
Produce food while protecting the environment and conserving resources for future generations
109.x: Sustainable agriculture seeks to produce food while protecting the environment and conserving resources for future generations.
109.tq: Identify the definition that combines production, environmental protection and intergenerational resource conservation.
xs: Sustainable agriculture aims to **produce food while protecting the environment and conserving resources for future generations** (PYQ) — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Monoculture** and continuous **chemical inputs** are listed as **harmful** practices, not goals.
xa: Sustainable practices: **crop rotation**, **organic farming**, mixed cropping, green manuring, **drip irrigation**, **IPM**.
Harmful practices: **excessive chemical fertilisers**, **overuse of pesticides**, **monoculture**, **over-irrigation**.
Shift: Green Revolution → "**evergreen revolution**" (ZBNF, organic farming, water conservation, IPM).

109.s: Which one of the following is NOT generally regarded as a harmful agricultural practice?
109.x: Integrated pest management is a sustainable practice. Excessive chemical fertiliser use, pesticide overuse and monoculture are listed as harmful practices.
109.tq: Find the one sustainable practice hidden among harmful practices.
xs: **Integrated pest management** is a **sustainable** practice — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Excessive chemical fertilisers**, **overuse of pesticides** and **monoculture** are the listed **harmful** practices.
xa: **Over-irrigation** is also harmful.
IPM keeps pests **below economic injury levels**; aim = **optimise, not maximise** control.
Other sustainable practices: **cover crops**, **reduced tillage**, **drip irrigation**.

109.s: The main advantage of organic farming as an eco-friendly agricultural technology is:
o: Reduced chemical input and improved soil health
Complete elimination of pests without any management
Lower labour requirement than every other system
109.x: Organic farming's main advantage is reduced chemical input and improved soil health (PYQ). It does not guarantee higher yields in all conditions (the trap), does not eliminate pests by itself, and is not necessarily less labour-intensive.
109.tq: Organic = less chemicals, better soil; not always more yield.
xs: Organic farming's main advantage is **reduced chemical input and improved soil health** (PYQ) — so option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ Trap: it does **NOT** give **higher yields in all conditions**.
xa: Organic farming is the PYQ answer for an **eco-friendly technology**.
Organic farming is **certified** and allows **approved organic inputs**.
Transition debate: **yield dip for 2-3 years** in natural farming.

109.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Bordeaux mixture contains CuSO₄ and Ca(OH)₂.
II. Fungicides are used for crop protection.
III. Fungicides are used in water tanks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
109.x: All three are correct: Bordeaux mixture is copper sulphate with lime, and fungicides protect crops and are used in water tanks.
109.tq: Recall the make-up of Bordeaux mixture.
n: Bordeaux mixture contains CuSO₄ and Ca(OH)₂. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]
Fungicides are used for crop protection. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]
Fungicides are used in water tanks. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** **I, II and III**.
**Bordeaux mixture** = **CuSO₄** + **Ca(OH)₂**.
**Fungicides** are used for **crop protection** and in **water tanks**.
xa: **Blue vitriol** is **CuSO₄**, also a fungicide.
**Chloropicrin** is a broad-spectrum fungicide, herbicide, insecticide and tear gas.
Pesticide residues **bioaccumulate** in the food chain.

109.s: The primary objective of Integrated Pest Management, as defined by the FAO, is to:
o: Replace all biological methods with resistant varieties
Maximise pest mortality through continuous chemical spraying
Keep pests below economic injury levels by optimising the use of suitable methods
Eliminate every pest from the agricultural ecosystem
109.x: IPM uses all suitable methods to keep pest populations below economic injury levels. Its aim is to optimise control, not maximise it.
109.tq: Distinguish the stated management objective from the extreme goal of total eradication.
xs: IPM (**FAO**) keeps pests **below economic injury levels** using all suitable methods — so option **(3)** is correct.
Its aim is to **optimise, not maximise** control, so continuous spraying and total elimination are wrong.
xa: Components: **resistant varieties**, **cultural**, **mechanical/physical**, **biological**, **chemical only when needed**.
Biological example: **green lacewing** vs **aphids**.
IPM is a **sustainable** practice (PYQ).

109.s:
Consider the following statements regarding components of Integrated Pest Management:
1. Resistant varieties form one component of IPM.
2. Crop rotation and changes in irrigation are cultural methods.
3. Traps and mulches are mechanical or physical methods.
4. Chemical control is used only when needed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: All four statements describe recognised IPM components: resistant varieties, cultural practices, mechanical or physical methods, and need-based chemical control.
109.tq: Check whether all listed methods fit the integrated, need-based character of IPM.
xs: All four statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4** is correct.
**Resistant varieties**; **cultural** = irrigation change, crop rotation.
**Mechanical/physical** = traps, mulches; **chemical only when needed**.
xa: **Biological** component: natural enemies (**green lacewing** vs aphids), **pheromone traps**.
IPM aim: **optimise, not maximise** control.
IPM keeps pests **below economic injury levels** (FAO).

109.s: Which one of the following biopesticides is correctly matched with its principal target?
109.x: NPV is a baculovirus-based biopesticide effective against Helicoverpa and Spodoptera caterpillars. Trichoderma targets soil-borne fungal diseases, neem has a wide insect range, and Beauveria bassiana attacks several insects.
109.tq: Use the source–target association and reject reversed biological targets.
xs: **NPV** (a **baculovirus**) targets **Helicoverpa** and **Spodoptera** caterpillars — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Trichoderma** targets **soil-borne fungal diseases** (wilt, root rot); **Bt** targets caterpillars/bollworms.
**Neem** acts on a **wide range of insects**; **Beauveria bassiana** attacks borers and whitefly.
xa: ⚠ **Bt** = bacterium; **Trichoderma**, **Beauveria** = fungi; **NPV** = virus.
Biopesticides are **biodegradable**, low-toxicity, short persistence.

109.s: Beauveria bassiana is best described as a:
o: Entomopathogenic fungus used against borers and whitefly
Plant extract used as an antifeedant
109.x: Beauveria bassiana is an entomopathogenic fungus effective against borers, whitefly and other insects.
109.tq: Distinguish closely related biopesticides by source and target.
xs: **Beauveria bassiana** is an **entomopathogenic fungus** used against **borers and whitefly** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **baculovirus** is **NPV**; the plant antifeedant is **neem**; the bacterium against bollworms is **Bt**.
xa: **Trichoderma** is also a fungus (antagonist) against **wilt, root rot**.
⚠ Fungi: **Trichoderma**, **Beauveria**; virus: **NPV**; bacterium: **Bt**.
Biopesticides are a **crucial IPM component**.

109.s: Carbosulfan was proposed for banning because it:
o: Fixes nitrogen but causes nitrate leaching
Improves soil microbial activity but reduces crop yield
Breaks down to highly toxic carbofuran and harms birds and aquatic life
Is a natural pesticide that attracts secondary pests
109.x: Carbosulfan breaks down into highly toxic carbofuran and is harmful to birds and aquatic life. The proposed ban was recommended by the Registration Committee under the Insecticides Act, 1968.
109.tq: Link the pesticide with its breakdown product and ecological harm.
xs: **Carbosulfan** breaks down to highly toxic **Carbofuran** and **harms birds and aquatic life** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The Centre proposed the ban (29 Aug **2026**) on the recommendation of the **Registration Committee under the Insecticides Act 1968**.
xa: ⚠ **Carbosulfan** (proposed ban) → breaks down to **Carbofuran**.
**Punjab** banned the sale of **glyphosate** in **2018**.
Indiscriminate use → **secondary pest outbreaks** and **pesticide resistance**.

109.s:
Consider the following pairs (organic input - feature):
1. Vermicompost - organic waste digested by earthworms
2. Farmyard manure - leguminous crops ploughed into the soil while green
3. Biochar - charcoal from pyrolysis of biomass; long-term carbon sequestration
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
109.x: Pair 3 is correct: biochar is pyrolysis charcoal giving long-term carbon sequestration and water/nutrient retention. Pair 1 is correct: vermicompost is earthworm-digested organic waste that restores soil microbes and organic carbon. Pair 2 is wrong: farmyard manure is dung, urine and litter of farm animals; legumes ploughed in green (sunn hemp, dhaincha) are green manure. Hence '1 and 3 only'.
109.tq: FYM = dung, urine, litter; green manure = legumes ploughed in green.
xs: Pairs **1** and **3** are correctly matched — so option **(1)** **1 and 3 only** is correct.
Pair 1 correct: **vermicompost** is organic waste digested by **earthworms**; it restores soil microbes and organic carbon.
Pair 3 correct: **biochar** is charcoal from **pyrolysis** of biomass, giving long-term **carbon sequestration**.
Pair 2 wrong: **farmyard manure** is dung, urine and litter of farm animals; legumes ploughed in green are **green manure**.
xa: Green manure crops: **sunn hemp** and **dhaincha** — they add nitrogen and organic matter.
**Compost**: decomposed crop residues; AP plans **1,500 MT/day** manure from **107 waste-processing centres**.
Farmyard manure gives **slow-release nutrients** and better soil structure.
Biochar also improves **water and nutrient retention**.

109.s: Which one of the following is an example of a biological component of Integrated Pest Management?
o: Use of a resistant seed variety only
Use of green lacewings against aphids
109.x: Green lacewings act as natural enemies of aphids and therefore represent a biological IPM method. Pheromone traps are also included among the listed IPM tools.
109.tq: Separate biological control from cultural and physical control methods.
xs: **Green lacewings against aphids** is a **biological** IPM method — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Resistant varieties** are a separate component; **irrigation change** is **cultural**; **mulches** are **mechanical/physical**.
xa: **Pheromone traps** are also listed under biological methods.
Biopesticides (**Bt**, **NPV**, **Trichoderma**) are a crucial IPM component.
Chemicals in IPM: **only when needed**.

109.s:
Assertion (A): Neem-coated urea improves nitrogen-use efficiency.
Reason (R): It slows the release of nitrogen.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
109.x: Both are true and R explains A: the neem coating slows the conversion and release of nitrogen, so less is lost and crops use more of it.
109.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: Neem-coated urea provides slow release. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
Neem-coated urea increases nitrogen-use efficiency. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
Neem-coated urea slows fertilizer release as an environmental solution. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
xs: **Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A** — option **(1)**.
**Neem-coated urea** gives **slow release** of nitrogen, which **increases nitrogen-use efficiency**.
xa: **Urea** promotes **vegetative growth** in **wheat** and most crops.
Neem-coated urea is listed as a **remedy** for agrochemical damage, along with **PM-PRANAM**.
Broadcasting granular fertiliser loses **50-70%** of applied nitrogen as ammonia or nitrate leaching.
Other solutions: **organic manure**, **vermicompost**, **biofertilizers**.

109.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Green manure is a cover crop grown and ploughed in while green or just after flowering.
Statement B: Legumes are among the main plants used as green manure.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
109.x: Both are true: green manure is a crop such as sesbania or clover ploughed in while green, and legumes are preferred because they fix nitrogen.
109.tq: Recall what green manure is.
n: Green manure is a cover crop grown and ploughed in while green or just after flowering. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
Legumes are the main plants used as green manure. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
Clover is a green-manure plant. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
Vetch is a green-manure plant. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
Sesbania is a green-manure plant. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
xs: **Both Statement A and Statement B are true** — option **(1)**.
A: **green manure** is a **cover crop** grown and **ploughed in** while green or just after flowering.
B: the main green-manure plants are **legumes** — **clover**, **vetch**, **sesbania**.
xa: Green manure adds **organic matter** and **humus**, and fixes nitrogen through **root nodules**.
Other green-manure crops: **sunn hemp** and **dhaincha**.
AP **Kharif 2026**: **Rs 62.20 crore** subsidy; **91,918 quintals** of green-manure seed.

109.s:
Assertion (A): Green manure improves soil structure and water retention.
Reason (R): Green manure adds organic matter and fixes atmospheric nitrogen through root nodules.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
109.x: Both are true and R explains A: green manure adds humus and fixes nitrogen in root nodules, which improves soil structure and water holding.
109.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: Green manure adds organic matter to soil. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
Green manure fixes atmospheric nitrogen through root nodules. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
Green manure improves soil structure. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
Green manure improves water retention. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
Green manure adds organic matter. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
Green manure contributes to nitrogen fixation. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
Green manure adds humus to soil. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
xs: **Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A** — option **(1)**.
Green manure adds **organic matter** and **humus** and **fixes atmospheric nitrogen** through **root nodules**.
This improves **soil structure**, **water retention** and **microbial activity**.
xa: Green manure is a **cover crop** ploughed in while **green** or just after **flowering**.
Main plants: **legumes** — **clover**, **vetch**, **sesbania**.
In AP, **sunn hemp** (**50,311** quintals) led Kharif 2026 green-manure seed supply.

109.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Urea
(b) Phosphatic fertilizers
(c) Potassic fertilizers
(d) DAP

List-II
(i) Balanced nitrogen and phosphorus supply
(ii) Vegetative growth and use for wheat and most crops
(iii) Improvement in quality
(iv) Root development, flowering and fruiting
109.x: Urea boosts vegetative growth, phosphatic fertilizers aid roots, flowering and fruiting, potassic fertilizers improve quality, and DAP gives balanced N and P, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
109.tq: Recall the role of each fertilizer type.
n: Urea promotes vegetative growth. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
Urea is used for wheat and most crops. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
Phosphatic fertilizers support root development. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
Phosphatic fertilizers support flowering. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
Phosphatic fertilizers support fruiting. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
Potassic fertilizers improve quality. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
DAP provides a balanced nitrogen and phosphorus supply. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i** — option **(2)**.
**Urea** — **vegetative growth** (wheat and most crops); **phosphatic** — **root development, flowering, fruiting**.
**Potassic** — **quality** (also disease resistance, drought tolerance); **DAP** — **balanced nitrogen and phosphorus** supply.
xa: Potassic fertilizers also give **disease resistance** and **drought tolerance**.
**Neem-coated urea**: **slow release**, higher nitrogen-use efficiency.
**Green manure** and **biofertilizers** improve **soil health** through organic matter.

109.s: Consider the following statements: I. Excess nitrogen fertilizers cause soil acidification. II. Excess nitrogen fertilizers cause nitrate leaching to groundwater. III. Excess nitrogen fertilizers cause eutrophication. Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: All three are correct: excess nitrogen acidifies soil, leaches nitrate into groundwater and runs off to cause eutrophication.
109.tq: Recall the effects of fertilizer overuse.
n: Excess nitrogen fertilizers cause soil acidification. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
Excess nitrogen fertilizers cause nitrate leaching to groundwater. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
Excess nitrogen fertilizers cause eutrophication. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(3)** **I, II and III**.
Excess **nitrogen fertilizers** cause **soil acidification**, **nitrate leaching** to **groundwater**, and **eutrophication**.
xa: Continuous chemical fertilizer use lowers **soil organic matter**, **microbial activity** and **nutrient density** in food.
Solutions: **organic manure**, **vermicompost**, **biofertilizers**, **neem-coated urea**.
Broadcasting granular fertiliser loses **50-70%** of applied nitrogen.
**PM-PRANAM**: states keep **50%** of saved fertiliser subsidy as grants.

109.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Continuous chemical fertilizer use causes a decline in soil organic matter.
II. Continuous chemical fertilizer use reduces microbial activity.
III. Continuous chemical fertilizer use lowers nutrient density in food.
IV. Continuous chemical fertilizer use increases soil organic matter.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
109.x: I, II and III are correct: continuous chemical fertilizer use depletes soil organic matter, reduces microbes and lowers nutrient density in food. IV contradicts I.
109.tq: Check for a statement that contradicts another.
n: Continuous chemical fertilizer use causes a decline in soil organic matter. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
Continuous chemical fertilizer use reduces microbial activity. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
Continuous chemical fertilizer use lowers nutrient density in food. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
xs: Statements **I, II and III** are correct — option **(4)** **I, II and III only**.
Continuous chemical fertilizer use causes **decline in soil organic matter**, **reduced microbial activity** and **lower nutrient density** in food.
Statement IV is wrong: it does **not increase** soil organic matter — it contradicts statement I.
xa: Excess nitrogen causes **soil acidification**, **nitrate leaching** and **eutrophication**.
**Vermicompost** restores soil microbes and organic carbon.
⚠ Organic farming's main advantage = **reduced chemical input and improved soil health**, NOT higher yields everywhere.

109.s:
With reference to sustainable agriculture, consider the following statements:
1. It may use synthetic inputs judiciously.
2. Integrated pest management and precision farming can be part of sustainable agriculture.
3. Sustainable agriculture is identical to organic farming because neither permits synthetic inputs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
