109.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Sustainable agriculture may use synthetic inputs judiciously, unlike the stricter approach generally associated with organic farming; statement 3 is false.
109.tq: Separate the broader concept of sustainable agriculture from the more restrictive organic-farming approach.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: sustainable agriculture may use synthetic inputs **judiciously**.
Statement 2 correct: **IPM**, **precision farming** and **conservation tillage** fit within it.
Statement 3 wrong: it is **not identical to organic farming**, which avoids synthetic inputs.
xa: Organic = **certified**, approved organic inputs; natural farming = **on-farm cow-based** inputs.
Organic farming's main advantage: **reduced chemical input and improved soil health**.

109.s:
Indiscriminate use of synthetic fertilisers and pesticides may result in:
1. Secondary pest outbreaks
2. Pesticide resistance
3. Ecosystem contamination
4. Soil and water contamination
Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: Indiscriminate agrochemical use can cause secondary pest outbreaks, pesticide resistance, ecosystem contamination and contamination of soil and water.
109.tq: Select the comprehensive environmental-impact option after checking each consequence.
xs: All four are effects of indiscriminate agrochemical use — so option **(3) 1, 2, 3 and 4** is correct.
It causes **secondary pest outbreaks**, **pesticide resistance** and **ecosystem contamination**.
Synthetic fertilisers and pesticides cause **soil and water contamination** (PYQ).
xa: Pesticide residues **bioaccumulate** in the food chain.
Broadcasting granular fertiliser loses **50-70%** of applied nitrogen.
Remedies: **neem-coated urea**, **PM-PRANAM**.

109.s: Under PM-PRANAM, States may retain what share of the fertiliser subsidy saved by reducing fertiliser use, in the form of grants?
109.x: PM-PRANAM allows States to retain 50 percent of the saved fertiliser subsidy as grants.
109.tq: Recall the exact percentage associated with the incentive mechanism.
xs: Under **PM-PRANAM**, states keep **50 percent** of the saved fertiliser subsidy as **grants** — so option **(3)** is correct.
PM-PRANAM is a remedy for fertiliser overuse, alongside **neem-coated urea**.
xa: Broadcasting fertiliser loses **50-70%** of nitrogen.
⚠ Do not confuse: **50%** = PM-PRANAM share; **50 farmers / 50 acres** = PKVY cluster.

109.s:
Which of the following characteristics make biopesticides an important component of Integrated Pest Management?
1. Biodegradability
2. Low toxicity
3. Short persistence
4. Permanent elimination of all pests
Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: Biopesticides are biodegradable, comparatively low in toxicity and short-lived in the environment. They are not intended to permanently eliminate all pests.
109.tq: Find the extreme and absolute statement among otherwise valid environmental characteristics.
xs: **Biodegradability, low toxicity and short persistence** make biopesticides crucial to IPM — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 4 wrong: IPM aims to keep pests **below economic injury levels**, not eliminate them.
xa: IPM aim = **optimise, not maximise** control.
Biopesticides: **Bt**, **Trichoderma**, **NPV**, **Neem**, **Beauveria bassiana**.
In IPM, **chemicals are used only when needed**.

109.s:
Consider the following statements about the Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY):
1. It was launched in 2015–16.
2. It was the first comprehensive Centrally Sponsored Scheme for organic farming.
3. It follows a cluster-based approach.
4. A standard cluster consists of 50 farmers covering 50 acres.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: PKVY was launched in 2015–16 as the first comprehensive Centrally Sponsored Scheme for organic farming. Its cluster approach specifies 50 farmers and 50 acres per cluster.
109.tq: Test the scheme through launch year, institutional character and cluster design.
xs: All four statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4** is correct.
**PKVY** was launched in **2015-16** as the **first comprehensive CSS** for organic farming.
It is **cluster-based**: **50 farmers / 50 acres**.
xa: Coverage: **15.08 lakh ha**, **25.38 lakh farmers** (to 31 Jul **2025**).
Portal: **jaivikkheti.in**.
⚠ **PKVY** = rest of India; **MOVCDNER** = North-East.

109.s: Which one of the following schemes is specifically associated with the development of organic value chains in the North-Eastern States?
109.x: MOVCDNER promotes organic value chains in the North-Eastern Region, whereas PKVY covers the rest of the country.
109.tq: Distinguish schemes by geographical scope and objective.
xs: **MOVCDNER** builds **organic value chains in the North-East** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**PKVY** covers the **rest** of India; **NPOP** and **PGS-India** are certification systems.
xa: MOVCDNER was launched in **2015-16**, the same year as PKVY.
**PGS-India** = farmer-group certification for the **domestic** market.
**NPOP** = **third-party** certification, mainly for **exports**.

109.s:
With reference to organic-farming certification in India, consider the following statements:
1. PGS-India uses participatory, farmer-group certification.
2. PGS-India is intended for the domestic market.
3. NPOP is based mainly on third-party certification.
4. NPOP is mainly associated with exports.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: PGS-India uses participatory farmer-group certification for the domestic market. NPOP relies mainly on third-party certification and is chiefly associated with exports.
109.tq: Compare the two certification systems across method and market.
xs: All four statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4** is correct.
**PGS-India** = participatory **farmer-group** certification for the **domestic market**.
**NPOP** = **third-party** certification, mainly for **exports**.
xa: NPOP dates from **2001**.
⚠ **PGS-India** = domestic, farmer groups; **NPOP** = third-party, exports.
Organic farming is **certified**; natural farming relies on **on-farm** inputs.

109.s:
Consider the following statements regarding NMNF:
1. It had trained 70,021 Krishi Sakhis by March 2026.
2. It involved 17,632 clusters.
3. Its reported coverage by March 2026 was 8.80 lakh hectares.
4. It had an outlay of Rs 897 crore in total.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Rs 897 crore was the States’ share, not the total NMNF outlay; the total was Rs 2,481 crore.
109.tq: Catch the component-share substitution in an otherwise accurate scheme profile.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
**70,021 Krishi Sakhis**, **17,632 clusters** and **8.80 lakh ha** coverage by March **2026**.
Statement 4 wrong: **Rs 897 crore** is only the **States' share**; total is **Rs 2,481 crore**.
xa: Centre's share: **Rs 1,584 crore**.
Coverage also reached **18.19 lakh farmers**.
**BPKP** also promotes natural farming.

109.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh Community-managed Natural Farming (APCNF):
1. It was formerly known as Zero Budget Natural Farming.
2. Jeevamrutham and ghanajeevamrutham are associated bio-inputs.
3. It covers more than seven lakh farmers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: All three statements are correct: APCNF was formerly ZBNF, uses jeevamrutham and ghanajeevamrutham, and covers over seven lakh farmers.
109.tq: Use the all-inclusive code only after verifying the programme’s name, inputs and coverage.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
**APCNF** was formerly **Zero Budget Natural Farming** and uses **jeevamrutham, ghanajeevamrutham**.
It covers **over 7 lakh farmers** (Feb **2026**).
xa: APCNF won the **Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity 2024**.
A **Kenyan delegation** praised it after visiting **Guntur** district farms (8 Jul **2026**).
**NTR district**: natural-farming model with **QR-based traceability**.

109.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the distinction between the first organic-farming milestone and the first comprehensive scheme?
o: PKVY was the first fully organic State, while Sikkim was the first certification scheme.
NPOP was the first fully organic State, while MOVCDNER was the first comprehensive scheme.
Sikkim was the first fully organic State, while PKVY was the first comprehensive organic-farming scheme.
PGS-India was the first fully organic State, while NMNF was launched as the first comprehensive scheme in 2015–16.
109.x: Sikkim holds the distinction of being the first fully organic State, whereas PKVY was the first comprehensive Centrally Sponsored Scheme for organic farming.
109.tq: Separate two different ‘first’ claims instead of treating them as the same milestone.
xs: **Sikkim** = first fully organic state; **PKVY** = first comprehensive organic-farming scheme — so option **(3)** is correct.
**NPOP** and **PGS-India** are certification systems; **MOVCDNER** is the North-East value-chain scheme; **NMNF** came in **2024**.
xa: Sikkim became fully organic in **2016**.
PKVY began in **2015-16** with **50 farmers / 50 acres** clusters.
PKVY portal: **jaivikkheti.in**.

109.s:
How many of the following are identified as insecticides?
I. DDT
II. BHC
III. 2,4-D
IV. Zinc phosphide
109.x: Two are insecticides: DDT and BHC. 2,4-D is a herbicide and zinc phosphide a rodenticide.
109.tq: Classify each pesticide by its target.
n: DDT is an insecticide. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]
BHC is an insecticide. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]
2,4-D is used as a herbicide. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]
2,4-D is a herbicide. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]
Zinc phosphide is a rodenticide. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]
xs: Only **two** — **DDT** and **BHC** — are insecticides, so option **(2)** **Only two** is correct.
**2,4-D** is a **herbicide** used against **broadleaf weeds**.
**Zinc phosphide** is a **rodenticide** (**rat poison**).
xa: Other insecticides: **allethrin**, **prallethrin** (mosquito repellents), **Sevin**, **Bt**.
**BHC** = **benzene hexachloride**.
Fungicides: **Bordeaux mixture**, **blue vitriol**, **chloropicrin**.

109.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Fungicide
(b) Herbicide
(c) Mosquito repellent—Allethrin
(d) Mosquito repellent—Prallethrin

List-II
(i) Bordeaux mixture
(ii) 2,4-D
(iii) Allethrin
(iv) Prallethrin
109.x: Bordeaux mixture is a fungicide, 2,4-D a herbicide, and allethrin and prallethrin are mosquito repellents, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
109.tq: Classify each pesticide by its target.
n: Bordeaux mixture is used as a fungicide. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]
2,4-D is used as a herbicide. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]
Allethrin is used as a mosquito repellent. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]
Prallethrin is used as a mosquito repellent. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]
Bordeaux mixture is a fungicide. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]
2,4-D is a herbicide. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]
xs: The correct match is **a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv** — option **(2)**.
**Bordeaux mixture** is a **fungicide**; **2,4-D** is a **herbicide** against broadleaf weeds.
**Allethrin** and **prallethrin** are **mosquito repellents** (insecticides).
xa: Bordeaux mixture = **CuSO₄** + **Ca(OH)₂**; **blue vitriol** = CuSO₄.
**Zinc phosphide** is a **rodenticide**.
**DDT** and **BHC** are insecticides.

109.s: The shift from the Green Revolution towards the ‘evergreen revolution’ is associated with which combination?
o: ZBNF, organic farming, water conservation and integrated pest management
Only genetically modified crops and mechanised harvesting
Monoculture, over-irrigation, pesticide intensification and soil mining
Expansion of chemical fertilisers without resource conservation
109.x: The evergreen revolution approach is associated with ZBNF, organic farming, water conservation and integrated pest management.
109.tq: Match the newer sustainability-oriented approach with its defining practices.
xs: The **"evergreen revolution"** shift rests on **ZBNF, organic farming, water conservation and IPM** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Monoculture**, **over-irrigation** and pesticide overuse are the **harmful** practices it moves away from.
xa: ZBNF was developed by **Subhash Palekar**.
First fully organic state: **Sikkim (2016)**.
First comprehensive CSS for organic farming: **PKVY** (**2015-16**).

109.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Permaculture is a third-party certification system for export-oriented organic produce.
2. Zero Budget Natural Farming was developed by Subhash Palekar.
3. The term 'permaculture' was coined by Bill Mollison and David Holmgren of Australia.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
109.x: Statement 2 is correct: Subhash Palekar developed ZBNF. Statement 3 is correct: Mollison and Holmgren coined 'permaculture'. Statement 1 is wrong: permaculture is site-specific design of ecological habitats and food systems; third-party export certification is NPOP. Hence '2 and 3 only'.
109.tq: Palekar = ZBNF; Mollison = permaculture; NPOP = export certification.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** **2 and 3 only** is correct.
Statement 1 wrong: **permaculture** is site-specific **design of ecological habitats and food systems**; third-party export certification is **NPOP**.
Statement 2 correct: **Subhash Palekar** developed **ZBNF**.
Statement 3 correct: **Bill Mollison** and **David Holmgren** (Australia) coined **permaculture**.
xa: ZBNF terms: **Jeevamrutha** (cow dung-urine microbial culture), **Beejamrutha** (seed treatment), **Achhadana** (mulching).
Organic farming is **certified**; natural farming uses **on-farm** cow-based inputs.
Natural farming cuts cultivation cost by **20-40%**.
⚠ **PGS-India** = domestic, farmer-group certification; **NPOP** = third-party, exports.

109.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with a natural-farming input or practice?
o: Jeevamrutha — cow dung and urine-based microbial culture
Beejamrutha — soil aeration through moisture regulation
109.x: Jeevamrutha is a microbial culture prepared from cow dung and urine. Beejamrutha is used for seed treatment, Achhadana denotes mulching, and Whapasa relates to soil aeration and moisture.
109.tq: Discriminate among similar-sounding natural-farming inputs by their functions.
xs: **Jeevamrutha** = **cow dung-urine microbial culture** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Beejamrutha** is **seed treatment**, not soil aeration.
**Achhadana** is **mulching**; **Whapasa** is **soil aeration/moisture** — options (3) and (4) are swapped.
xa: AP's APCNF bio-inputs: **jeevamrutham, ghanajeevamrutham**.
ZBNF originator: **Subhash Palekar**.
Natural farming cuts cultivation cost **20-40%**.

109.s: AP Community-managed Natural Farming received global recognition through the:
o: UNEP Champions of the Earth Award, 2024
109.x: APCNF received the Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity in 2024.
109.tq: Discriminate among similarly prestigious awards using the exact award-name and year pair.
xs: APCNF won the **Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity, 2024** — so option **(2)** is correct.
No World Food Prize, UNEP or Ramsar award is linked to APCNF.
xa: A **Kenyan delegation** praised APCNF as a **climate-resilient** model (8 Jul **2026**).
Guntur farms showed **20+** crop diversified plots and **trap crops** (marigold, castor).
AP is described as a **global pioneer** in natural farming.

109.s: Which of the following statements correctly reflects the reported economic and implementation aspects of natural farming?
o: It guarantees a market premium immediately after adoption.
It can reduce cultivation cost by 20–40%, while transition may involve knowledge-intensive practices.
It increases cultivation cost by 20–40% and requires no specialised knowledge.
It eliminates the possibility of yield decline during transition.
109.x: Natural farming was reported to reduce cultivation costs by 20–40%, but it is knowledge-intensive. Yield dips during the first two or three years and weak market premiums remain concerns.
109.tq: Balance a stated benefit against the documented transition constraints.
xs: Natural farming **cuts cultivation cost 20-40%**, but is **knowledge-intensive** — so option **(2)** is correct.
There is a **yield dip for 2-3 years** during transition, so (4) is wrong.
The **market premium** for natural produce is **weak**, so (1) is wrong.
xa: **ZBNF's scalability** is questioned.
Natural farming relies on **on-farm cow-based** inputs.
**NMNF** coverage: **8.80 lakh ha** by March **2026**.

109.s: The scalability of which agricultural approach has been questioned in policy and academic debates?
109.x: The scalability of Zero Budget Natural Farming has been questioned in debates concerning the wider adoption of natural farming.
109.tq: Link the debate to the specific approach rather than to a certification or monitoring scheme.
xs: The **scalability of ZBNF** is questioned — so option **(3)** is correct.
Other debates: **yield dip for 2-3 years**, **weak market premium** and **knowledge intensity**.
xa: ZBNF was developed by **Subhash Palekar**.
AP's **APCNF** (formerly ZBNF) covers **over 7 lakh farmers**.
**NPOP** and **PGS-India** are certification systems for organic produce.

109.s: Which statement best distinguishes organic farming from natural farming?
o: Organic farming excludes certification, whereas natural farming requires third-party export certification.
Natural farming permits only synthetic fertilisers, whereas organic farming uses only pesticides.
Organic farming is certified and permits approved organic inputs, whereas natural farming relies on on-farm cow-based inputs.
Both systems require exactly the same external inputs and certification procedure.
109.x: Organic farming involves certification and approved organic inputs. Natural farming emphasises on-farm, cow-based inputs and does not follow the same certification framework.
109.tq: Test the exact distinction between two commonly confused agricultural systems.
xs: **Organic** farming is **certified** and allows **approved organic inputs**; **natural** farming uses **on-farm cow-based inputs** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Neither system relies on synthetic fertilisers, and they do not share one certification procedure.
xa: Organic certification: **PGS-India** (domestic) and **NPOP** (exports).
Natural farming cuts cultivation cost **20-40%**.
**NMNF** (approved **25 Nov 2024**) promotes natural farming.

109.s:
Consider the following statements about chloropicrin:
I. It is a broad-spectrum fungicide.
II. It is a broad-spectrum herbicide.
III. It is a broad-spectrum insecticide.
IV. It is a broad-spectrum tear gas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
109.x: All four are correct: chloropicrin is a broad-spectrum fungicide, herbicide, insecticide and also a tear gas.
109.tq: Recall the uses of chloropicrin.
n: Chloropicrin is broad-spectrum. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]
Chloropicrin functions as a fungicide. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]
Chloropicrin functions as a herbicide. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]
Chloropicrin functions as an insecticide. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]
Chloropicrin functions as tear gas. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]
Chloropicrin is a fungicide. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]
xs: All four are correct — option **(2)** **I, II, III and IV**.
**Chloropicrin** is **broad-spectrum**: a **fungicide**, **herbicide**, **insecticide** and **tear gas**.
xa: Chloropicrin is listed among **fungicides** with **Bordeaux mixture** and **blue vitriol**.
**2,4-D** = herbicide; **zinc phosphide** = rodenticide.
Indiscriminate pesticide use causes **secondary pest outbreaks** and **pesticide resistance**.

110.s:
Arrange the following irrigation methods in descending order of approximate water-use efficiency:
A. Flood or furrow irrigation
B. Sprinkler irrigation
C. Drip irrigation
110.x: Drip irrigation has about 90% efficiency, sprinklers about 70–80%, and flood or furrow irrigation about 30–50%.
110.tq: Arrange the alternatives by comparing their stated efficiency ranges.
xs: Descending water-use efficiency is **Drip > Sprinkler > Flood/furrow**, i.e. **C, B, A** — so option **(2)** is correct.
xa: Drip is the PYQ answer for **water-scarce regions** (APPSC-G2 **2025**).
Drip's limitation: **higher initial investment**.
Sprinklers lose **more to wind and evaporation** than drip.

110.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes drip irrigation from sprinkler irrigation?
o: Drip irrigation applies water through nozzles as rainfall, whereas sprinkler irrigation uses emitters near roots.
Drip irrigation is suitable only for uneven terrain, whereas sprinkler irrigation is suitable only for level fields.
Drip irrigation applies water directly to the root zone through emitters, whereas sprinkler irrigation applies water under pressure through pipes and nozzles.
Both systems apply water only through underground channels without pressure.
110.x: Drip irrigation delivers water directly to the root zone through emitters on lateral pipes. Sprinkler irrigation distributes pressurised water through pipes and nozzles in the form of simulated rainfall.
110.tq: Use the application-method contrast to separate two closely related irrigation systems.
xs: **Drip** applies water **directly to the root zone through emitters**; **sprinkler** applies it **under pressure through pipes and nozzles** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Option (1) swaps the two; sprinklers **simulate rainfall**.
Sprinklers are **useful on uneven terrain**, so (2) is wrong.
xa: Drip emitters sit on **lateral pipes**.
Drip is **most efficient** (~**90%**), minimising evaporation and runoff.
Drip limitation: **higher initial investment**.

110.s:
With reference to drip and sprinkler irrigation, consider the following statements:
1. Drip irrigation generally has higher initial investment.
2. Sprinkler irrigation is useful on uneven terrain.
3. Sprinkler irrigation generally suffers greater wind and evaporation losses than drip irrigation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
110.x: All three statements are correct. Drip systems require relatively higher initial investment, while sprinklers are useful on uneven terrain but are more exposed to wind and evaporation losses.
110.tq: Check each comparison row separately, especially the limitation associated with each method.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
Drip has **higher initial investment**; sprinklers are **useful on uneven terrain**.
Sprinklers suffer **more loss to wind and evaporation** than drip.
xa: Efficiency: drip ~**90%**, sprinkler ~**70-80%**.
Both suit **water-scarce areas**.
Criticism: **high upfront cost** of drip.

110.s: The shift in agricultural policy from ‘more output’ to ‘more output at lower ecological cost’ is associated with which concept?
110.x: The policy emphasis on higher output with lower ecological cost is described as the Evergreen Revolution, associated with M.S. Swaminathan.
110.tq: Identify the exact policy concept from its defining contrast.
xs: The shift from "more output" to "**more output at lower ecological cost**" is the **Evergreen Revolution** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The concept is associated with **M.S. Swaminathan**.
xa: **APSES 2024-25** lists **precision farming, drones, IoT**, drip/sprinkler and **rainwater harvesting** as the way forward.
Criticism: **high upfront cost of drip**; irrigation **still skewed to rice**.
**SRI** cuts **seed, methane and electricity** use (UPSC **2022**).

110.s: Which of the following is identified as a criticism or continuing concern regarding resource-efficient irrigation and agriculture?
o: Drip irrigation has no initial cost and irrigation has shifted entirely away from rice
Drip irrigation has a high upfront cost and irrigation remains skewed towards rice
Solar pumps are prohibited in State irrigation plans
Precision agriculture cannot use sensors or data analytics
110.x: The stated concerns are the high upfront cost of drip irrigation and the continuing skew of irrigation towards rice.
110.tq: Select the option containing both recognised limitations without reversing the comparison.
xs: The concerns are **drip's high upfront cost** and irrigation **remaining skewed towards rice** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Assam** uses solar pumps in its irrigation plan, so (3) is false; AP uses **sensors + data analytics**, so (4) is false.
xa: Skew: **rice ~67%** irrigated vs **pulses ~26%**, millets **<15%**.
Drip's limitation is **higher initial investment**, despite ~**90%** efficiency.
Gross irrigated area: **55.8%** of GCA (**2022-23**).

110.s:
Consider the following statements about the advantages of fertigation:
1. Controlling the alkalinity of irrigation water is possible.
2. Efficient application of rock phosphate is possible.
3. Increased availability of nutrients to plants is possible.
4. Reduction in the leaching of chemical nutrients is possible.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
110.x: Fertigation lets alkalinity of irrigation water be controlled, makes more nutrients available and reduces leaching, so 1, 3 and 4 are correct (UPSC 2020). Efficient application of rock phosphate is NOT an advantage, which rules out every option containing statement 2.
110.tq: Fertigation trap: rock phosphate is not an advantage.
xs: Statements **1, 3 and 4** are correct (UPSC **2020**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
Fertigation allows **alkalinity control**, **more nutrients available** and **less leaching**.
⚠ Statement 2 wrong: **efficient application of rock phosphate** is NOT an advantage.
xa: Fertigation = fertiliser applied **through the irrigation water**.
**PDMC** promotes drip/sprinkler with fertigation.

110.s: Drone Shakti is associated with building the drone ecosystem through:
o: manufacturing and Remote Pilot Certificate training
110.x: Drone Shakti supports the drone ecosystem through manufacturing and training for Remote Pilot Certificates.
110.tq: Match the programme with its stated ecosystem-building functions.
xs: **Drone Shakti** builds the drone ecosystem through **manufacturing and Remote Pilot Certificate training** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Crop insurance is **PMFBY**; solar pumps belong to **PM-KUSUM**.
xa: Drones are regulated by **DGCA** (**Drone Rules 2021**).
Kisan drone uses: **crop assessment, soil health analysis, spraying**.
AP's **APDC** offers **drone-as-a-service**.

110.s: Direct-seeded rice differs from transplanted rice mainly because it involves:
110.x: Direct-seeded rice is planted without nursery raising or transplanting. It has also been promoted together with zero-till wheat under NICRA.
110.tq: Use the presence or absence of nursery and transplanting as the decisive distinction.
xs: **Direct-seeded rice** needs **no nursery or transplanting** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It is promoted with **zero-till wheat** under **NICRA**.
xa: **SRI** with alternate wetting and drying needs **less seed** and produces **less methane**.
Zero tillage also lets **paddy seed be planted directly** without a nursery (UPSC **2020**).
**Laser land levelling** saves irrigation water.

110.s:
Consider the following statements about the System of Rice Intensification (SRI) with alternate wetting and drying:
1. It reduces seed requirement.
2. It reduces methane production.
3. It reduces electricity consumption.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
110.x: All three are correct (UPSC 2022): SRI uses less seed, alternate wetting and drying cuts methane from flooded paddies, and less pumping saves electricity. Each other option leaves out a true statement.
110.tq: SRI: less seed, less methane, less power - all three.
xs: All three statements are correct (UPSC **2022**) — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
**SRI** with **alternate wetting and drying** uses **less seed**, gives **less methane** and uses **less electricity**.
xa: **Direct-seeded rice**: no nursery or transplanting.
Rice GHG emissions could fall **~10%** by mid-century with better practices.
**Sustainable Sugarcane Initiative** saves seed cane and water.

110.s: Variable-rate technology in agriculture refers to the practice of:
o: changing the crop variety every season without field data
applying the same quantity of inputs throughout a field
using only variable rainfall for crop production
applying inputs at varying rates within a field according to sensor or GIS maps
110.x: Variable-rate technology applies agricultural inputs at different rates within a field, based on sensor information or GIS maps.
110.tq: Distinguish precision-based variation from uniform field application.
xs: **Variable-rate technology** applies inputs **at varying rates within a field** per **sensor/GIS maps** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Applying the **same quantity** throughout a field is the opposite of VRT.
xa: **GPS, drones, AI, sensors** are the core of the "**Second Green Revolution**".
**Soil and Land Use Survey of India** maps soil from satellite data.
**Kisan e-Mitra**: AI chatbot for **PM-KISAN** queries.

110.s: GPS, drones, artificial intelligence and sensors are identified as core elements of which agricultural approach?
o: The Second Green Revolution and sustainable intensification
110.x: GPS, drones, AI and sensors form the technological core of the Second Green Revolution and sustainable intensification.
110.tq: Identify the exact conceptual grouping of related technologies.
xs: **GPS, drones, AI and sensors** are the core of the **Second Green Revolution** / **sustainable intensification** — so option **(3)** is correct.
They are precision tools, not organic certification or shifting cultivation.
xa: **Agritech startups** offer AI advisories, precision irrigation, crop-health monitoring.
**Kisan e-Mitra**: AI chatbot answering **PM-KISAN** queries in several languages.
The broader shift is the **Evergreen Revolution** (**M.S. Swaminathan**).

110.s: Component A of PM-KUSUM relates to
o: Installation of standalone off-grid solar pumps
Solarisation of existing grid-connected agricultural pumps
Decentralised grid-connected solar/renewable power plants on barren or fallow land
110.x: Component A of PM-KUSUM covers decentralised grid-connected solar/renewable plants on barren or fallow land. Standalone pumps and solarisation of grid-connected pumps are the other components.
110.tq: A = Acreage (barren land) power plants.
xs: **PM-KUSUM Component A** = **decentralised grid-connected solar/renewable power plants on barren or fallow land** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is about **power plants on unused land**, not rooftop solar on households.
xa: **Assam's** State Irrigation Plan uses **solar pumps**.
Micro-irrigation saves **water, labour, power and fertiliser**.
**PDMC** priority: **rainfed areas**, water-stressed districts, **critical groundwater blocks**.

110.s: Which of the following protected-cultivation practices grows crops in a controlled environment and can provide protection from weather, pests and diseases?
110.x: Protected cultivation in greenhouses, polytunnels or shade nets provides a controlled environment and protection from adverse weather, pests and diseases.
110.tq: Identify the common functional feature of protected-cultivation structures.
xs: **Greenhouse or polyhouse cultivation** is protected cultivation in a **controlled environment** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It protects crops from **weather, pests, disease** and allows **year-round** cropping.
xa: Protected cultivation also uses **polytunnels** and **shade nets**.
Typical crops: **tomatoes, cucumbers, flowers**.
AP's automation micro-irrigation covers **greenhouses and shade-net** crops.

110.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Vertical farming — crops are grown only in open fields
Hydroponics — roots hang in air and are misted
Aeroponics — roots grow in nutrient-rich water
Aquaponics — fish culture is combined with hydroponics and fish waste feeds plants
110.x: Aquaponics combines fish culture with hydroponics, with fish waste supplying nutrients to plants. Hydroponics uses nutrient-rich water, while aeroponics suspends roots in air and mists them.
110.tq: Find the swapped definitions among closely related soilless-farming techniques.
xs: **Aquaponics** = **fish culture + hydroponics**, with **fish waste feeding the plants** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Options (2) and (3) are swapped: **hydroponics** = roots in nutrient-rich water; **aeroponics** = roots in air, misted.
**Vertical farming** grows crops in **stacked layers indoors**, not open fields.
xa: Aquaponics fish: **tilapia or catfish**.
Hydroponics saves **water and space** — leafy greens, herbs.
Aeroponics uses **even less water** than hydroponics.

110.s: A farmer wants year-round crop production in a non-tropical or harsh setting by using stacked layers indoors under controlled conditions. Which technology is most appropriate?
110.x: Vertical farming grows crops in stacked indoor layers under controlled conditions and can provide year-round output even in non-tropical or harsh settings.
110.tq: Translate the production setting and structural clues into the appropriate technology.
xs: **Vertical farming** grows crops in **stacked layers indoors** for **year-round** output in harsh settings — so option **(3)** is correct.
It is **more efficient than land farming** (APPSC-GS **2021**).
**Zero tillage** and **direct-seeded rice** are field practices, not indoor systems.
xa: **Protected cultivation** (greenhouse, polytunnel) also gives year-round crops.
**Hydroponics** saves water and space.

110.s:
With reference to Per Drop More Crop (PDMC), consider the following statements:
1. It was launched in 2015–16.
2. It was part of PMKSY up to 2021–22.
3. From 2022–23, it has been implemented under RKVY.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
110.x: PDMC was launched in 2015–16, remained part of PMKSY until 2021–22, and has operated under RKVY since 2022–23.
110.tq: Use the timeline to verify each policy transition.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
**PDMC** was launched in **2015-16** and was part of **PMKSY** to **2021-22**.
From **2022-23** it is **implemented under RKVY**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes still call PDMC a **PMKSY component**.
Priority: **rainfed areas**, **water-stressed districts**, **critical groundwater blocks**.
PDMC: **102 lakh ha** and **₹24,789.16 crore** central assistance (**2015-16** to **2025-26**).

110.s:
Consider the following statements about the Micro Irrigation Fund (MIF):
1. It is a Rs 10,000 crore corpus with NABARD to help States mobilise resources.
2. It was operationalised in 2015-16 together with Per Drop More Crop.
3. Rs 5,000 crore was added to its initial Rs 5,000 crore for the 15th Finance Commission period.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
110.x: Statement 2 is wrong: MIF was operationalised in 2019-20 (PDMC began in 2015-16). Statement 1 is correct: a Rs 10,000 crore corpus with NABARD. Statement 3 is correct: set up with Rs 5,000 crore, another Rs 5,000 crore added for the 15th FC period. Hence '1 and 3 only'.
110.tq: MIF: NABARD, Rs 10,000 crore, operational 2019-20.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)** **1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **MIF** is a **₹10,000 crore** corpus with **NABARD** to help States mobilise resources.
Statement 2 wrong: MIF was **operationalised in 2019-20**; **Per Drop More Crop** began in **2015-16**.
Statement 3 correct: set up with **₹5,000 crore**; another **₹5,000 crore** added for the **15th Finance Commission** period.
xa: MIF progress: projects worth **₹4,709.06 crore** approved; **₹3,970.61 crore** disbursed.
**PDMC** was a PMKSY component till **2021-22**; from **2022-23** it runs under **RKVY**.
**NMSA**: up to **55%** subsidy for micro-irrigation, capped at **5 ha**.

110.s: Which of the following correctly describes the administrative character and nodal authority of PMKSY?
o: It is a State Sector Scheme with the State Revenue Department as nodal authority.
It is a Central Sector Scheme with the Union Finance Ministry as nodal authority.
It is a statutory scheme administered by NABARD.
It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme with the State Agriculture Department as nodal authority.
110.x: PMKSY is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, and the State Agriculture Department is the nodal authority.
110.tq: Apply the who-does-this-job test to distinguish scheme type from nodal department.
xs: **PMKSY** is a **Centrally Sponsored Scheme** with the **State Agriculture Department** as nodal authority — so option **(4)** is correct.
**NABARD** holds the **Micro Irrigation Fund**, but does not administer PMKSY.
xa: **PDMC** was part of PMKSY from **2015-16** to **2021-22**.
AP's micro-irrigation project runs **State-wide under PMKSY**.
PMKSY at **10 years** (Jul **2026**).

110.s: Under which scheme is the Andhra Pradesh Micro Irrigation Project implemented throughout the State with financial assistance?
110.x: The Andhra Pradesh Micro Irrigation Project is implemented State-wide under the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana with financial assistance.
110.tq: Identify the parent scheme associated with the State-level project.
xs: AP's micro-irrigation project runs State-wide under **Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**PMFBY** is crop insurance; **PM-KUSUM** concerns solar plants on barren land.
xa: AP ranked **1st** in micro-irrigation implementation (**2024-25**).
PMKSY is a **Centrally Sponsored Scheme**; State Agriculture Department is nodal.
APMIP reports **30-40% higher productivity** (**2025-26**).

110.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Andhra Pradesh Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25:
1. Drip and sprinkler irrigation are being implemented on a large scale.
2. Large-scale rainwater harvesting is being implemented.
3. Precision farming, drones and IoT are identified as key areas of focus.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
110.x: All three are correct: APSES 2024-25 records large-scale drip and sprinkler irrigation and rainwater harvesting, and names precision farming, drones and IoT as key areas of focus.
110.tq: Test a cluster of related policy priorities through an all-correct combination.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
**APSES 2024-25** records **drip and sprinkler** irrigation and **large-scale rainwater harvesting**.
It names **precision farming, drones and IoT** as key focus areas.
xa: AP ranked **1st** in micro-irrigation implementation (**2024-25**).
**Drone Corporation of AP** offers **drone-as-a-service**.
Policy shift = **Evergreen Revolution** (M.S. Swaminathan): more output at lower ecological cost.

110.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Mahalanobis National Crop Forecast Centre (2012) runs ISRO's crop forecasting under FASAL.
2. The KISAN project (Oct 2015) uses space technology to plan Crop Cutting Experiments under PM-KUSUM.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
110.x: Statement 1 is correct: MNCFC (2012) runs ISRO crop forecasting (FASAL) and monitors 29 double-risk districts. Statement 2 is wrong: KISAN plans Crop Cutting Experiments under PMFBY (crop insurance), not PM-KUSUM (solar pumps). Hence '1 only'.
110.tq: KISAN -> CCE -> PMFBY.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)** **1 only**.
Statement 1 correct: the **Mahalanobis National Crop Forecast Centre (2012)** runs ISRO crop forecasting under **FASAL**.
Statement 2 wrong: the **KISAN project (Oct 2015)** plans Crop Cutting Experiments under **PMFBY**, not PM-KUSUM.
xa: MNCFC does satellite monitoring of **29 double-risk districts**.
KISAN pilots: **Haryana**, **Karnataka**, **Maharashtra**, **MP**.
**Soil and Land Use Survey of India** maps soil resources from satellite data.
**Kisan e-Mitra** is an AI chatbot answering **PM-KISAN** queries.

110.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Drone Corporation of Andhra Pradesh?
o: A privately owned body providing only drone imports
A central regulatory authority under the Ministry of Civil Aviation
110.x: The Drone Corporation of Andhra Pradesh is State-owned and provides drone-as-a-service.
110.tq: Use ownership and function together to identify the correct institution.
xs: The **Drone Corporation of AP (APDC)** is **State-owned** and provides **drone-as-a-service** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **central regulator** is **DGCA**; the Farmers' Registry belongs to **AgriStack**.
xa: APDC extended **drone pesticide spraying** to **all 26 districts** (Jan **2026**).
**Kisan drones** save water **up to 30%**.
**Drone Shakti** builds the drone ecosystem.

110.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated use or benefit of Kisan drones?
o: Reduction of human exposure to chemicals
Elimination of the need for all irrigation water
110.x: Kisan drones are used for crop assessment, soil health analysis and spraying, and can reduce human exposure to chemicals. They do not eliminate the need for all irrigation water.
110.tq: Find the option that overstates the technology’s benefit.
xs: Kisan drones do **not** eliminate the need for all irrigation water — so option **(4)** is correct.
Their uses: **crop assessment**, **soil health analysis**, **spraying**; they cut **human exposure to chemicals**.
xa: They save water **up to 30%**.
Regulated by **DGCA** under **Drone Rules 2021**.
APDC drone spraying covers **all 26 districts**.

110.s: Which authority regulates agricultural drones under the Drone Rules, 2021?
o: Soil and Land Use Survey of India
110.x: Agricultural drones are regulated by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation under the Drone Rules, 2021.
110.tq: Apply the ‘who regulates this activity?’ institutional test.
xs: Drones are regulated by **DGCA** under the **Drone Rules 2021** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**ISRO** handles crop forecasting via satellites; **MNRE** runs **PM-KUSUM**.
xa: Drone categories: **nano, micro, small, medium, large**.
**Drone Shakti** supports **Remote Pilot Certificate** training.

110.s:
Consider the following statements about the Digital Agriculture Mission:
1. It was approved in September 2024.
2. It has an outlay of Rs 28,170 crore.
3. Its digital public infrastructure includes AgriStack, the Krishi Decision Support System and the Soil Fertility Profile.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
110.x: Statement 1 is correct: the mission was approved in September 2024. Statement 2 is wrong: the outlay is Rs 2,817 crore, not Rs 28,170 crore. Statement 3 is correct: AgriStack, Krishi DSS and Soil Fertility Profile are its DPI. So A misses 3, C and D wrongly include 2; B is right.
110.tq: Remember the outlay as Rs 2,817 crore - watch for an extra zero.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the **Digital Agriculture Mission** was approved in **September 2024**.
Statement 2 wrong: the outlay is **₹2,817 crore**, not Rs 28,170 crore.
Statement 3 correct: its DPI = **AgriStack, Krishi DSS, Soil Fertility Profile**.
xa: Roots: **NeGPA 2010-11**, updated **2020-21**.
State model: Karnataka **FRUITS** (**2020**).

110.s: AgriStack is best described as:
o: an Aadhaar-like digital public good built through a federated Centre-State approach
a satellite used for crop forecasting
a centralised crop insurance claim portal managed only by States
110.x: AgriStack is described as an Aadhaar-like digital public good developed through a federated Centre-State build.
110.tq: Combine the analogy with the governance model to identify the correct description.
xs: **AgriStack** is an "**Aadhaar-like**" **digital public good** with a **federated Centre-State** build — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is not a satellite (that is ISRO's crop forecasting) or a drone-licensing system (**DGCA**).
xa: Registries: **Farmers' Registry**, **geo-referenced village maps**, **Crop Sown Registry**.
Part of the **Digital Agriculture Mission** (**September 2024**, **₹2,817 crore**).
Karnataka's **FRUITS** (**2020**) is a unified farmer database.

110.s: Kisan e-Mitra is an AI chatbot that answers queries related to:
110.x: Kisan e-Mitra uses AI to answer PM-KISAN queries in several languages.
110.tq: Match the chatbot with its service domain and language feature.
xs: **Kisan e-Mitra** is an **AI chatbot** answering **PM-KISAN** queries **in several languages** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Drone pilot certification belongs to **Drone Shakti** (Remote Pilot Certificate training).
xa: **Agritech startups** offer AI advisories, precision irrigation, crop-health monitoring.
**GPS, drones, AI, sensors** = core of the "**Second Green Revolution**".
**KISAN project** (Oct **2015**) is a different thing: space tech for **PMFBY** crop-cutting experiments.

110.s: The gross irrigated area as a percentage of gross cropped area increased from approximately 41.7% in 2001-02 to:
110.x: The gross irrigated area increased from 41.7% in 2001-02 to 55.8% in 2022-23.
110.tq: Track both endpoints of a trend and avoid substituting an unsupported intermediate year.
xs: Gross irrigated area rose from **41.7% (2001-02)** to **55.8%** of GCA in **2022-23** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The other percentages and years do not match the reported figure.
xa: Skew: **rice ~67%** irrigated vs **pulses ~26%**, millets **<15%**.
Criticism: irrigation is **still skewed to rice**.
PDMC brought **102 lakh ha** under micro-irrigation (**2015-16** to **2025-26**).

110.s: Which areas receive priority under Per Drop More Crop?
o: Rainfed areas, water-stressed districts and critical groundwater blocks
Only command areas with assured canal irrigation
110.x: The priority areas are rainfed regions, water-stressed districts and critical groundwater blocks.
110.tq: Match the intervention’s resource-conservation objective with the areas facing water stress.
xs: PDMC prioritises **rainfed areas, water-stressed districts and critical groundwater blocks** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It is not limited to saline soils, peri-urban clusters or canal commands.
xa: PDMC was launched in **2015-16**; under **RKVY** from **2022-23**.
It brought **102 lakh ha** under micro-irrigation.
**NMSA** gives up to **55%** subsidy, capped at **5 ha**.

110.s: Which State ranked first in India in micro-irrigation implementation in 2024–25?
110.x: Andhra Pradesh ranked first in India in micro-irrigation implementation in 2024–25.
110.tq: Use the year-specific ranking rather than a general leading-state assumption.
xs: **Andhra Pradesh** ranked **1st** in India in micro-irrigation implementation in **2024-25** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Six AP districts** were in the national **top 10**, led by **Ananthapuramu**.
xa: AP's micro-irrigation is implemented State-wide under **PMKSY**.
APMIP reports **30-40% higher productivity**.
Automation-based micro-irrigation facility at **Governorpet, Vijayawada**.

110.s: Krishi Decision Support System integrates which combination of data?
o: Satellite, weather, soil and crop data
Only farmer identity and bank-account data
110.x: Krishi DSS joins satellite, weather, soil and crop data.
110.tq: Select the complete data combination rather than a partial description.
xs: **Krishi DSS** joins **satellite, weather, soil and crop data** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It supports **crop mapping**, **diversification** and **insurance claims**.
xa: It is aligned with the **National Geo-Spatial Policy**.
Krishi DSS is part of the **Digital Agriculture Mission** DPI with **AgriStack** and **Soil Fertility Profile**.
The mission was approved in **September 2024**.

110.s: Which irrigation technology is most suitable for water-scarce regions?
110.x: Drip irrigation applies water directly to the root zone, reaching about 90% efficiency and cutting evaporation and runoff, so it suits water-scarce areas (APPSC-G2 2025). Flood, furrow and basin irrigation are surface methods with only about 30-50% efficiency.
110.tq: Water-scarce = drip (~90% efficient).
xs: **Drip irrigation** suits **water-scarce regions** (APPSC-G2 **2025**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
Drip reaches ~**90%** efficiency; **flood/furrow** reaches only ~**30-50%**.
xa: Drip applies water **directly to the root zone**, minimising **evaporation and runoff**.
Micro-irrigation saves **water, labour, power and fertiliser**.
AP ranked **1st** in micro-irrigation implementation (**2024-25**).

110.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated feature of zero tillage?
o: Wheat can be sown without burning the previous crop residue.
It can contribute to soil carbon sequestration.
It necessarily requires complete removal of all crop residue before sowing.
Paddy seed can be planted directly without raising a nursery.
110.x: Zero tillage is associated with sowing wheat without burning previous residue, direct planting of paddy without a nursery, and soil carbon sequestration. Complete removal of residue is not a stated feature.
110.tq: Identify the extreme and reversed residue-management statement.
xs: Zero tillage does **not** require **complete removal of all crop residue** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Its stated features (UPSC **2020**, all three): wheat sown **without burning residue**, **paddy without nursery**, **soil carbon sequestration**.
xa: **Reduced/zero tillage + leaving crop residue** conserves water (UPSC **2017**).
**Direct-seeded rice** is promoted with **zero-till wheat** under **NICRA**.

110.s: Which practice is associated with conserving water in agriculture, whereas gypsum application before irrigation is NOT such a practice in the stated comparison?
o: Repeated deep ploughing after every irrigation
Reduced or zero tillage with crop residue left on the field
110.x: Reduced or zero tillage combined with leaving crop residue helps conserve water. Gypsum application before irrigation is not identified as the water-conserving practice in this comparison.
110.tq: Separate the positive resource-conservation practice from the deliberately inserted non-example.
xs: **Reduced or zero tillage with crop residue left on the field** conserves water (UPSC **2017**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Gypsum before irrigation** does NOT; flood irrigation and residue burning waste resources.
xa: **Laser land levelling** spreads water evenly and saves irrigation water.
Zero tillage also gives **soil carbon sequestration**.
Drip irrigation efficiency ~**90%**.

111.s:
Arrange the following steps of recombinant DNA technology in the correct sequence:
A. Formation of recombinant DNA by joining fragments with DNA ligase
B. Isolation of DNA
C. Insertion into a host cell
D. Cutting DNA at specific sites by restriction endonucleases
111.x: DNA is first isolated, then cut at specific sites, joined by DNA ligase to form recombinant DNA, and finally inserted into a host cell.
111.tq: Arrange the laboratory operations by identifying the necessary first cut and final host-insertion stages.
xs: The order is **B, D, A, C** — isolation → cutting → joining → insertion — so option **(1)** is correct.
Step 1: **isolation of DNA**; step 2: cutting by **restriction endonucleases**.
Step 4: rDNA formed by **DNA ligase**; step 5: insertion into a **host cell**.
xa: Step 3 (between cutting and joining): isolation and **amplification (PCR)** of the desired fragment.
Last steps: extracting the foreign gene product, then **downstream processing**.
Common host: **E. coli**.

111.s: ContactSeek is an AI tool associated with AlphaFold3 that is intended to:
111.x: ContactSeek uses AI with AlphaFold3 to help cut off-target edits, thereby improving the precision of gene editing.
111.tq: Match the named emerging tool with its specific biotechnology application.
xs: **ContactSeek** uses **AlphaFold3** to **cut off-target edits** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Bt toxin, **PCR** amplification and **T-DNA** transfer are unrelated tools.
xa: ContactSeek was reported on 27 Jul **2026**.
**Base editing** works **without double-strand breaks**.
**TnpB** (ICAR) is a smaller alternative to Cas9.

111.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: A restriction enzyme is also called a restriction endonuclease.
A restriction enzyme cuts DNA at or near specific recognition sites.
A restriction enzyme cuts DNA only at random locations.
A restriction enzyme cleaves DNA into fragments.
111.x: Option C is incorrect: restriction enzymes cut at specific recognition sequences, not at random. They are also called restriction endonucleases.
111.tq: Check each statement for the word "random".
n: A restriction enzyme is a restriction endonuclease. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #41 · pp 66-68]
A restriction enzyme cleaves DNA into fragments. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #41 · pp 66-68]
A restriction enzyme cuts DNA at or near specific recognition sites. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #41 · pp 66-68]
A restriction site is a recognition location for a restriction enzyme. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #41 · pp 66-68]
Restriction enzymes have a role in genetic engineering by cutting DNA. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #41 · pp 66-68]
xs: The incorrect statement is option **(3)**: restriction enzymes cut at **specific recognition sites**, **not at random**.
A **restriction enzyme** is also a **restriction endonuclease** and **cleaves DNA into fragments**.
xa: Restriction enzymes are popularly called **molecular scissors**.
**DNA ligase** = **molecular stitcher** / **molecular glue**.
In rDNA, cutting by restriction endonucleases is **step 2**; joining by ligase is **step 4**.

111.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
 a. DNA ligase
 b. PCR
 c. pBR322
 d. Plasmid

List-II
 i. Amplification of DNA
 ii. Small DNA molecule
 iii. Molecular stitcher
 iv. Early widely used E. coli cloning vector
111.x: DNA ligase is a molecular stitcher, PCR amplifies DNA, pBR322 was an early E. coli vector and a plasmid is a small DNA molecule, giving a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
111.tq: Recall the tools of genetic engineering.
n: DNA ligase is described as a molecular stitcher. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 68-71]
A plasmid is a small DNA molecule. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 68-71]
pBR322 was an early widely used Escherichia coli cloning vector. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 68-71]
The core purpose of PCR is amplification of DNA. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 68-71]
pBR322 is a classic vector. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 68-71]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii** — option **(4)**.
**DNA ligase** — **molecular stitcher**; **PCR** — **amplification of DNA**.
**pBR322** — **early widely used E. coli cloning vector**; **plasmid** — **small DNA molecule**.
xa: In pBR322, **p** = plasmid; **BR** = **Bolivar and Rodriguez**.
Other vectors: **BACs**, **YACs**.
PCR makes **many copies** of a selected DNA sequence.

111.s:
Consider the following statements:

I. Gene cloning involves copying or amplifying a desired gene or DNA fragment.
II. Whole-animal cloning involves cloning a complete organism.
III. In a bacterial cloning system, bacteria rapidly copy recombinant DNA.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
111.x: All three are correct: gene cloning copies a gene, whole-animal cloning copies an organism, and bacteria quickly copy recombinant DNA.
111.tq: Discriminate gene cloning from organism cloning.
n: Gene cloning is the copying of a desired gene or DNA fragment. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 68-71]
Gene cloning is the amplification of a desired gene or DNA fragment. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 68-71]
Bacteria in a bacterial cloning system rapidly copy recombinant DNA. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 68-71]
Whole-animal cloning produces a complete organism. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 68-71]
Bacteria act as factories to copy recombinant DNA. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 68-71]
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(2)** **I, II and III**.
**Gene cloning** copies or amplifies a desired gene; **whole-animal cloning** produces a **complete organism**.
In a **bacterial cloning system**, bacteria **rapidly copy** recombinant DNA.
xa: **Plasmid cloning** inserts a gene into a **plasmid vector**.
**Stem cells** can **differentiate** into other cell types.
Cloning is a **genetic** and **biotechnological technique**.

111.s:
Consider the following statements:

I. PCR is used for molecular and genetic analysis.
II. PCR is used for detection and diagnostic testing.
III. PCR is used in DNA-based research.
IV. PCR supports analysis of small quantities of DNA.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
111.x: All four are correct: PCR copies small amounts of DNA for analysis, diagnosis and research.
111.tq: Recall the uses of PCR.
n: PCR is used for molecular and genetic analysis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 68-71]
PCR is used for detection and diagnostic testing. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 68-71]
PCR is used in DNA-based research. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 68-71]
PCR supports analysis of small quantities of DNA. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 68-71]
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(2)** **I, II, III and IV**.
**PCR** is used for **molecular and genetic analysis**, **detection and diagnostic testing**, **DNA-based research**, and analysis of **small quantities** of DNA.
xa: PCR = **Polymerase Chain Reaction**; core purpose: **amplification** of DNA.
In rDNA, PCR amplifies the desired fragment (**step 3**).
**Genetic testing** identifies relevant variants in personalised medicine.

111.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I

a. Cells used in stem-cell-mediated gene transfer
b. Stem-cell laboratory procedure
c. Genetic-engineering step
d. Fate of modified stem cells

List-II

i. Desired gene inserted into stem cells
ii. Embryonic stem cells
iii. Isolated and grown in the laboratory
iv. Returned to an organism or embryonic system
111.x: Embryonic stem cells are used, grown in the lab, given the desired gene and returned to the organism or embryo, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv.
111.tq: Recall the steps of stem-cell gene transfer.
n: Embryonic stem cells are used in the described gene-transfer approach. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 68-71]
Stem cells can be isolated and grown in the laboratory. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 68-71]
Genetic engineering inserts a desired gene into stem cells. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 68-71]
Modified stem cells are returned to an organism or embryonic system. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 68-71]
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv** — option **(1)**.
**Embryonic stem cells** are used; they are **isolated and grown in the laboratory**.
A **desired gene is inserted**; the modified cells are **returned to an organism or embryonic system**.
xa: Key property of stem cells: ability to **differentiate** into other cell types.
**National Guidelines for Stem Cell Research, 2017** (ICMR-DBT).
Stem-cell sources: **embryonic**, adult, **umbilical cord blood**, **iPSC**.

111.s: In plant genetic engineering, Agrobacterium tumefaciens is commonly used because:
o: Its ribosomes replace the plant cell nucleus.
Its disarmed Ti plasmid transfers T-DNA into the plant nucleus.
It destroys all plant viruses without transferring DNA.
It produces human insulin directly in plant leaves.
111.x: Agrobacterium tumefaciens is called nature's genetic engineer because T-DNA from its disarmed Ti plasmid can carry the desired gene into the plant nucleus.
111.tq: Ask which biological mechanism explains the organism's use as a vector.
xs: **Agrobacterium tumefaciens** carries the gene in a **disarmed Ti plasmid**, and **T-DNA** takes it into the **plant nucleus** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is called "**nature's genetic engineer**"; it does not make insulin or replace the nucleus.
xa: Other vectors: **plasmids**, **BACs**, **YACs**.
First human hormone by rDNA: **insulin**.
Common bacterial host: **E. coli**.

111.s: Which of the following is a distinctive concern associated with gene-drive mosquitoes?
o: The released trait can be recalled easily by stopping pesticide application.
The trait may spread through wild populations and there is no simple recall mechanism.
The technology is incapable of affecting mosquito populations.
The trait remains confined to the laboratory by definition.
111.x: Gene drives may spread a trait through wild populations, potentially causing population collapse or producing malaria-resistant mosquitoes. Unlike pesticide use, there is no simple recall mechanism.
111.tq: Test the practical implication of an irreversible or difficult-to-recall intervention.
xs: A gene-drive trait **spreads through wild populations** with **no simple recall** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Unlike pesticides, it cannot be stopped by ceasing application (14 Jul **2026**).
xa: Inheritance: **over 90%** of offspring (normal **50%**).
Types: **population suppression** (sterile females) vs **population modification**.
Tanzania-led **"Transmission Zero"** project.

111.s: A soybean variety containing a Brazil-nut gene was not released commercially primarily because of concern regarding:
111.x: The Brazil-nut gene was intended to improve methionine content, but the resulting soybean raised allergy concerns and was therefore never released.
111.tq: Identify the risk that explains why a genetically modified product was withheld from release.
xs: The Brazil-nut-gene soybean was **never released** because of **allergenicity** — it triggered allergy in Brazil-nut-allergic people — option **(1)**.
The gene was added for **methionine**, so failure to produce methionine was not the issue.
xa: **Horizontal gene transfer**: genes moving between **unrelated organisms**.
**Antibiotic-resistance marker genes** raise fears of spreading resistance.
**Mon 863**: Monsanto's **pest-resistant maize** (against **corn rootworm**), in news over feeding-study safety.

111.s: Horizontal gene transfer in the biosafety context refers to:
o: Replacement of nuclear DNA by mitochondrial DNA in every cell
Movement of genes between unrelated organisms
Transmission of genes only from parent to offspring
Movement of pollen only within one flower
111.x: Horizontal gene transfer is the movement of genes between unrelated organisms. Antibiotic-resistance genes may potentially pass from environmental bacteria to human pathogens.
111.tq: Distinguish horizontal transfer from ordinary vertical inheritance.
xs: **Horizontal gene transfer** is the **movement of genes between unrelated organisms** — option **(2)** is correct.
Example: **antibiotic-resistance genes** can pass from soil/environment bacteria to **human pathogens**.
Parent-to-offspring transmission is vertical inheritance, not horizontal transfer.
xa: **Allergenicity**: **Brazil-nut** gene soybean caused allergy → **never released**.
**Mon 863** = GM **pest-resistant maize** (Monsanto; corn rootworm).
**Gene drives** spread a trait in a wild population — **over 90%** of offspring inherit it (normal **50%**).

111.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Agriculture
(b) Medicine
(c) Industry
(d) Research

List-II
(i) Microbial production of useful products
(ii) DNA/RNA/protein-based biochips in basic research
(iii) Improved and transgenic/GM crops
(iv) Drugs, vaccines, diagnostics and gene therapy
111.x: In agriculture biotech gives GM crops, in medicine drugs, vaccines and gene therapy, in industry microbial products and in research biochips, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
111.tq: Recall the fields of biotechnology.
n: Biotechnology is used in agriculture to produce improved crops. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 61-63]
Biotechnology is used in agriculture to produce transgenic or genetically modified crops. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 61-63]
Biotechnology is used in medicine to produce drugs. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 61-63]
Biotechnology is used in medicine to produce vaccines. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 61-63]
Biotechnology is used in medicine for diagnostics. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 61-63]
Biotechnology is used in medicine for gene therapy. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 61-63]
Biotechnology is used in industry for the microbial production of useful products. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 61-63]
DNA-based biochips are used in basic research. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 61-63]
RNA-based biochips are used in basic research. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 61-63]
Protein-based biochips are used in basic research. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 61-63]
Biotechnology produces transgenic organisms carrying introduced genes. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 61-63]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii** — option **(1)**.
**Agriculture** — improved and **transgenic/GM crops**; **Medicine** — **drugs, vaccines, diagnostics, gene therapy**.
**Industry** — **microbial production** of useful products; **Research** — DNA/RNA/protein **biochips**.
xa: Biochips are used in **drug discovery**.
**Human insulin** is made by **recombinant bacteria** carrying the human insulin gene.
**Genetic diagnostics** identify **genetic diseases**.

111.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. A desired DNA fragment or gene can be inserted into a plasmid to form a recombinant plasmid.
II. A recombinant plasmid can be introduced into a bacterium through transformation.
III. Rapid multiplication of bacteria helps produce large quantities of DNA or product.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
111.x: All three are correct: a gene is spliced into a plasmid, the plasmid enters bacteria by transformation, and fast bacterial growth makes much product.
111.tq: Recall the steps of gene cloning.
n: A recombinant plasmid contains a desired DNA fragment or gene inserted into a plasmid. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 61-63]
A recombinant plasmid is introduced into a bacterium through transformation. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 61-63]
Rapid multiplication of bacteria produces large quantities of DNA or product. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 61-63]
Bacteria multiply rapidly. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 61-63]
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(1)** **I, II and III**.
A desired gene inserted into a **plasmid** forms a **recombinant plasmid**.
It enters a **bacterium** through **transformation**; **bacteria multiply rapidly**, giving **large quantities** of DNA or product.
xa: **Gene cloning** amplifies or copies a desired gene.
rDNA steps begin with **isolation of DNA** and cutting by **restriction endonucleases**; rDNA is joined by **DNA ligase**.
First GMO: **1973**; first human hormone by rDNA: **insulin**.

111.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Genetic library
(b) Genetic diagnostics
(c) Biochips
(d) Gene cloning

List-II
(i) Drug discovery
(ii) Amplification or copying of a desired gene
(iii) Creation of a collection of genetic material
(iv) Identification of genetic diseases
111.x: A genetic library is a collection of genetic material, diagnostics identify genetic diseases, biochips aid drug discovery and gene cloning copies a gene, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
111.tq: Recall the tools of biotechnology.
n: Biotechnology in genetics includes the creation of genetic libraries. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 61-63]
Biotechnology is used in diagnosis through genetic diagnostics. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 61-63]
Biochips have applications in drug discovery. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 61-63]
Gene cloning amplifies or copies a desired gene. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 61-63]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii** — option **(2)**.
**Genetic library** — a collection of genetic material; **genetic diagnostics** — **identify genetic diseases**.
**Biochips** — **drug discovery**; **gene cloning** — **amplifies or copies** a desired gene.
xa: Biochips are **DNA-**, **RNA-** and **protein-based**, used in **basic research**.
Medicine uses: **drugs**, **vaccines**, **diagnostics**, **gene therapy**.
Industry: **microbial production** of useful products.

111.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I

a. Common form of a plasmid
b. Advantage conferred by some natural plasmid genes
c. Experimental plasmid
 d. Biotechnology functions of plasmids

List-II

i. Vector
 ii. Circular, double-stranded DNA
 iii. Clone, transfer and manipulate genes
 iv. Antibiotic resistance
111.x: Plasmids are usually circular double-stranded DNA, some genes give antibiotic resistance, lab plasmids serve as vectors and they are used to clone and move genes, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.
111.tq: Recall the features of plasmids.
n: A common plasmid form is circular, double-stranded DNA. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 68-71]
Natural plasmid genes may confer advantages such as antibiotic resistance. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 68-71]
Plasmids are used in biotechnology to clone genes. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 68-71]
Plasmids are used in biotechnology to transfer genes. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 68-71]
Plasmids are used in biotechnology to manipulate genes. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 68-71]
An experimental plasmid is a vector. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 68-71]
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii** — option **(4)**.
Plasmids are commonly **circular, double-stranded DNA**; some natural plasmid genes confer **antibiotic resistance**.
An **experimental plasmid** is a **vector**; in biotechnology plasmids **clone, transfer and manipulate genes**.
xa: A plasmid is a **small DNA molecule** separate from chromosomal DNA that **replicates independently**.
**pBR322**: early **E. coli** cloning vector — **p** = plasmid, **BR** = **Bolivar and Rodriguez**.
Plants: **Agrobacterium tumefaciens** with a disarmed **Ti plasmid**.

111.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) RNAi
(b) Core concept of RNAi
(c) Target of RNAi
(d) Effect of RNAi

List-II
(i) Reduces or prevents expression of the target gene
(ii) Gene expression
(iii) RNA interference
(iv) Gene silencing
111.x: RNAi means RNA interference, it works by gene silencing, targets gene expression and reduces or stops the target gene's expression, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
111.tq: Recall the facts about RNAi.
n: RNAi stands for RNA interference. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #41 · pp 66-68]
RNAi is based on gene silencing. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #41 · pp 66-68]
RNAi targets gene expression. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #41 · pp 66-68]
RNAi reduces or prevents the expression of the target gene. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #41 · pp 66-68]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i** — option **(1)**.
**RNAi** = **RNA interference**, based on **gene silencing**.
It targets **gene expression** and **reduces or prevents expression** of the target gene.
xa: **Restriction enzyme** cuts at **restriction sites** — "molecular scissors".
**DNA ligase** joins desired DNA with **vector DNA**.
**Plasmid** antibiotic-resistance genes are used **for selection**.

111.s:
Which one of the following represents the correct historical sequence?
A. First genetically modified organism
B. Marketing of human insulin as Humulin
C. Demonstration of CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing
D. Nobel Prize in Chemistry for CRISPR-related work
111.x: The first GMO dates to 1973, Humulin was marketed in 1982, CRISPR-Cas9 was demonstrated in 2012, and the Nobel Prize followed in 2020.
111.tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest and latest dated events before resolving the middle pair.
xs: The order is **A, B, C, D** — so option **(1)** is correct.
First GMO **1973** → **Humulin** marketed **1982** → CRISPR-Cas9 demonstrated **2012** → **Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2020**.
xa: First commercially sold GM food: **Flavr Savr tomato**, **1994**.
First transgenic cow: **Rosie (1997)**.
First GM crop in India: **Bt cotton**, **2002**.

111.s: The first human hormone produced using recombinant DNA technology was:
111.x: Insulin was the first human hormone produced by rDNA technology; human insulin was marketed in 1982 as Humulin. Growth hormone, thyroxine and oxytocin are not the answer to this 'first'.
111.tq: First rDNA hormone = insulin (Humulin 1982).
xs: The first human hormone made by rDNA was **insulin** (UKPSC **2024**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
Human insulin was marketed in **1982** as **Humulin**.
xa: Synthetic biology also makes **artemisinin** by microbes and **semaglutide** in baker's yeast.
First GMO: **1973**.
Recombinant vaccines: **Hepatitis B, HPV, COVID-19**.

111.s: Which one of the following statements regarding mutation breeding is correct?
o: It is necessarily a transgenic technique involving foreign genes.
It is a non-GMO approach, and 71 Trombay varieties have been associated with climate resilience.
It is restricted to the production of GM mosquitoes.
It was used only for developing AquAdvantage salmon.
111.x: Mutation breeding is a non-GMO approach. Seventy-one Trombay varieties are associated with climate resilience.
111.tq: Discriminate between non-GMO mutation breeding and transgenic engineering.
xs: **Mutation breeding** is **non-GMO**, and **71 Trombay varieties** have climate resilience — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is not transgenic; **AquAdvantage** salmon and **GM mosquitoes** are transgenic examples.
xa: Genome-edited **Pusa Rice DST1** also gives stress tolerance **without transgenes**.
ICAR released **524 varieties** in the year, incl. **79 stress-tolerant**.

111.s: The Flavr Savr tomato, developed by Calgene in the United States in 1994, was notable because it was the first commercially sold GM food and had which characteristic?
o: Resistance to the fruit and shoot borer
Delayed ripening and a longer shelf life
111.x: Flavr Savr was the first commercially sold genetically modified food. Its delayed ripening provided a longer shelf life.
111.tq: Combine the product's historical identity with its distinctive intended trait.
xs: **Flavr Savr** had **delayed ripening and a longer shelf life** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Beta-carotene** is Golden Rice; **fruit and shoot borer** resistance is Bt brinjal.
xa: It was made by **Calgene, USA**, in **1994** — the first commercially sold GM food.
First GMO: **1973**.
First transgenic cow: **Rosie (1997)**.

111.s:
Consider the following statements about CRISPR-Cas9:
1. It is derived from a natural defence of bacteria and archaea against viruses.
2. In this system, the guide RNA acts as the molecular scissors.
3. Jennifer Doudna and Emmanuelle Charpentier demonstrated it in 2012 and received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2020.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
111.x: Statement 1 is correct: CRISPR originated as a bacterial/archaeal anti-viral defence. Statement 2 is wrong: Cas9 is the molecular scissors; guide RNA is the navigator. Statement 3 is correct. So 1 and 3 only.
111.tq: Cas9 cuts, guide RNA guides.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: CRISPR is a natural **bacterial/archaeal defence** against viruses.
Statement 2 wrong: **Cas9 = molecular scissors**; **guide RNA = navigator**.
Statement 3 correct: **Doudna and Charpentier**, **2012**; **Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2020**.
xa: CRISPR is simpler, cheaper, more accurate than **ZFNs and TALENs**.
Personalised medicine built on genetic make-up = **CRISPR** (UKPSC **2025**).

111.s: Personalised medicine built on an individual's genetic make-up is most directly associated with which technology?
111.x: Personalised medicine built on genetic make-up is associated with CRISPR (UKPSC 2025 key). PCR only amplifies DNA, mutation breeding is a crop method, and V-GURT makes sterile seeds.
111.tq: Personalised medicine = CRISPR.
xs: Personalised medicine built on genetic make-up = **CRISPR gene editing** (UKPSC **2025**) — so option **(1)** is correct.
**V-GURT** (Terminator) makes **sterile seeds**; **mutation breeding** is a non-GMO crop method.
xa: **Genetic medicines** correct/compensate for faulty genes, carried by **engineered viruses and lipid nanoparticles**.
**Mitochondrial replacement therapy** = "**three-parent baby**".
Regulation: **CDSCO gene therapy rules 2023**.

111.s: Which of the following correctly represents a classic GMO application pathway?
111.x: The human insulin gene is put into bacteria, which then make insulin, the classic GMO application.
111.tq: Recall the recombinant insulin pathway.
n: A human insulin gene can be transferred to bacteria to produce insulin. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 71-73]
GMO applications produce desired traits or products. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 71-73]
xs: The classic GMO pathway is **human insulin gene → bacteria → insulin** — option **(3)**.
**Human insulin** is produced using **recombinant bacteria** carrying a transferred **human insulin gene**.
xa: **Insulin** was the **first human hormone by rDNA**; human insulin marketed **1982** (**Humulin**).
First GMO: **1973**.
First commercially sold GM food: **Flavr Savr tomato** (**1994**).

111.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) GMO
(b) Transgenic organism
(c) Purpose of a transgenic organism
(d) Transgenic crops

List-II
(i) Biotechnology or agricultural application
(ii) Organism carrying a foreign gene from another species
(iii) Desired characteristic or product
(iv) Broad term for any organism whose genome is altered by genetic engineering
111.x: GMO is the broad term for any organism with an engineered genome, a transgenic organism carries a foreign gene from another species, its purpose is a desired trait or product, and transgenic crops are an agricultural application, giving a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i.
111.tq: Recall the facts about transgenic organisms.
n: GMO is approximately synonymous with transgenic organism in the relevant context. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 71-73]
A transgenic organism is produced through genetic engineering. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 71-73]
The purpose of a transgenic organism is to produce a desired characteristic or product. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 71-73]
Transgenic crops are a biotechnology or agricultural application. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 71-73]
xs: The correct match is **a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i** — option **(4)**.
**GMO** — broad term for an organism with genome altered by genetic engineering; **transgenic organism** — carries a **foreign gene**.
Purpose of a transgenic organism — **desired characteristic or product**; **transgenic crops** — **agricultural application**.
xa: Human insulin: **human insulin gene** transferred to **bacteria**.
First transgenic cow: **Rosie (1997)**.
First GM crop in India: **Bt cotton (2002)**.

111.s: What is the full form of CRISPR?
o: Clustered Regularly Interspaced Small Palindromic Repeats
Clustered Repeatedly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats
Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats
Clustered Regularly Integrated Short Palindromic Repeats
111.x: CRISPR stands for Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats. The other options change one word.
111.tq: Check each word of the expansion.
n: CRISPR stands for Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #41 · pp 66-68]
xs: CRISPR = **Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats** — option **(3)**.
The other options change one word (**Small**, **Repeatedly**, **Integrated**).
xa: CRISPR originated as a **natural defence mechanism** of **bacteria and archaea**.
