114.tq: Check whether all three linked statements describe the same climate-health relationship.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4)** (**1, 2 and 3**).
1: more **heatwaves, floods, cyclones**; 2: **VBDs** like **malaria, dengue, JE**.
3: **3.6 billion+** people in highly climate-vulnerable areas.
xa: WHO projection: **~2.5 lakh** extra deaths a year (**2030-2050**).
**Dasra 'Under the Weather'** (Apr **2026**): **~40%** of districts at high risk.
Warming **expands the range** of dengue and malaria vectors.

114.s:
Which of the following is NOT identified as a cause or facilitating factor of antimicrobial resistance?
1. Overuse or misuse of antibiotics
2. Self-medication
3. Poor sanitation
4. Regulated and scientifically supervised veterinary drug use
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
114.x: Overuse or misuse, self-medication and poor sanitation contribute to AMR. Regulated and scientifically supervised veterinary drug use is not a cause; unregulated veterinary drug use is a concern.
114.tq: Find the carefully reversed statement in an otherwise familiar list of AMR causes.
xs: **Regulated, scientifically supervised veterinary drug use** is not a cause — it is **unregulated** veterinary drugs that drive AMR — option **(3)** (**4 only**).
Causes include **overuse/misuse** of antibiotics in humans and animals, **self-medication** and **poor sanitation**.
xa: Also **poor waste control** and **pharma effluents** → a **One Health** problem.
**National Action Plan on AMR (2017)**: One Health based.
**Biofilms** shield bacteria from antibiotics and immunity.

114.s:
Which of the following are listed as critical priority bacterial pathogens in the WHO Bacterial Priority Pathogens List, 2024?
1. Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii
2. Enterobacterales
3. Rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis
4. Wolbachia
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
114.x: The critical-priority group includes carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii, Enterobacterales and rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis. Wolbachia is not included in this list.
114.tq: Separate antimicrobial priority pathogens from an unrelated biological-control organism.
xs: The critical group of the **WHO Bacterial Priority Pathogens List (2024)** is **carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii**, **Enterobacterales** and **rifampicin-resistant TB** — option **(2)** (**1, 2 and 3 only**).
**Wolbachia** is not a pathogen list entry — it is a harmless bacterium used for **vector control**.
xa: **Biofilms**: bacterial communities in a **self-made slimy matrix** shielding them from antibiotics.
AMR causes: **overuse/misuse** of antibiotics, self-medication, **pharma effluents**.
**Nafithromycin ("Miqnaf")** — India's first indigenous **macrolide**.

114.s:
Consider the following statements about Mission Indradhanush:
1. It was launched in December 2014.
2. It aims at more than 90% full immunisation of children and pregnant women.
3. IMI 5.0 was designed mainly to reach adults above 60 years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
114.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Mission Indradhanush began in December 2014 with a target of >90% full immunisation of children and pregnant women. Statement 3 is wrong: IMI 5.0 reaches missed and dropped-out children, not the elderly. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses a true statement and the others include statement 3.
114.tq: Indradhanush = children + pregnant women; IMI targets missed/dropped-out children.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Mission Indradhanush** began in **Dec 2014** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(3)**.
Statement 2 is correct: target **>90% full immunisation** of children and pregnant women.
Statement 3 is wrong: **IMI 5.0** reaches **missed/dropped-out children**, not the elderly.
xa: **U-WIN**: digital portal registering every UIP vaccination.
AP adult **BCG** drive: **27.10 lakh** doses.

114.s:
With reference to the adult BCG drive in Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. It began on 16 May 2024.
2. It involved 27.10 lakh doses.
3. Andhra Pradesh was the leading State in India in this drive.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
114.x: The AP adult BCG drive began on 16 May 2024, administered 27.10 lakh doses and placed Andhra Pradesh first in India for this drive.
114.tq: Combine date, numerical scale and comparative rank in a single factual set.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4)** (**1, 2 and 3**).
AP's **adult BCG drive** began **16 May 2024**, gave **27.10 lakh** doses and made AP the **leader in India** (APSES **2024-25**).
xa: **Childhood TB** is one of the **UIP**'s **12** diseases.
TB is **air-borne**, targets the **lungs**.
**24-member State task force** on communicable diseases (**Jan 2026**).

114.s: Which of the following best describes India’s epidemiological transition as reflected in the reported health indicators?
o: Life expectancy increased, but non-communicable diseases account for more than 57% of deaths while communicable diseases persist.
Life expectancy remained unchanged and non-communicable diseases account for less than 10% of deaths.
Communicable diseases have disappeared because life expectancy increased.
Life expectancy declined while communicable diseases became the only major cause of death.
114.x: Life expectancy increased from 49.7 years in 1973 to 70.3 years in 2023, yet non-communicable diseases account for more than 57% of deaths and communicable diseases continue to persist, creating a double burden.
114.tq: Recognise the double burden by comparing improvements with continuing disease persistence.
xs: **Life expectancy rose**, but **NCDs** cause **>57%** of deaths while **communicable diseases persist** — option **(1)** is correct.
Life expectancy rose **49.7 (1973) → 70.3 (2023)** — so the "unchanged/declined" options are wrong.
xa: This is the **epidemiological transition/double burden** (ES **2025-26**).
Vector-borne and water-borne diseases still persist.
**DALY** (**YLL + YLD**) measures disease burden.

114.s:
Consider the following statements about antibiotics:
1. The term 'antibiotic' was coined by Alexander Fleming in 1942.
2. Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928 from Penicillium notatum.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
114.x: Statement 2 is correct: Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928 from Penicillium notatum. Statement 1 is wrong: the term 'antibiotic' was coined by Selman Waksman in 1942. So '2 only'.
114.tq: Fleming 1928 (penicillin); Waksman 1942 (the word 'antibiotic').
xs: Only statement **2** is correct — option **(1)** **2 only**.
Statement 1 wrong: the term **antibiotic** was coined by **Selman Waksman** in **1942**, not Fleming.
Statement 2 correct: **Alexander Fleming** discovered **penicillin** in **1928** from **Penicillium notatum**.
xa: Main antibiotic sources: **fungi** and **bacteria** — **Streptomyces** and **Bacillus**.
**Streptomycin** (from Streptomyces) is used against **tuberculosis**.
Antibiotics act against **bacteria only**; **chloramphenicol** is **broad-spectrum**.

114.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Hepatitis-B can spread through blood and body fluids.
Gonorrhoea is transmitted mainly through respiratory droplets.
Rabies can spread through a bite or scratch involving saliva.
Typhoid can spread through contaminated food and water.
114.x: Option B is incorrect: gonorrhoea is sexually transmitted, not spread by droplets. The hepatitis-B, rabies and typhoid routes are right.
114.tq: Recall the transmission route of each disease.
n: Hepatitis-B spreads through blood and body fluids. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Gonorrhoea spreads through sexual transmission. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Rabies is transmitted through bites or scratches. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Rabies transmission involves saliva. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Typhoid spreads through contaminated food or water. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
xs: The incorrect statement is option **(2)**: **gonorrhoea** spreads by **sexual transmission**, not respiratory droplets.
**Hepatitis-B** spreads via **blood and body fluids**; **rabies** via **bites or scratches** (saliva).
**Typhoid** spreads through **contaminated food or water**.
xa: Gonorrhoea is caused by **Neisseria gonorrhoeae** and affects **reproductive organs**.
Hepatitis B also spreads **mother to child** and affects the **liver**.
⚠ Hepatitis **B/C** = blood-borne, NOT water-borne.

114.s:
Consider the following statements about COVID-19:

I. COVID-19 is a viral disease.
II. Humans are the host of COVID-19.
III. COVID-19 is transmitted through respiratory and contact routes.
IV. COVID-19 affects the respiratory system.
V. COVID-19 can cause multi-organ complications.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: II, III, IV and V only
I, II, III, IV and V
I, II, III and IV only
114.x: All five are correct: COVID-19 is a human viral disease spread by droplets and contact, attacking the lungs and sometimes many organs.
114.tq: Recall the facts about COVID-19.
n: COVID-19 is a viral disease. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
COVID-19 has humans as hosts. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
COVID-19 spreads through respiratory transmission. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
COVID-19 spreads through contact. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
COVID-19 affects the respiratory system. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
COVID-19 can cause multi-organ complications. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
xs: All five statements are correct — option **(3)** **I, II, III, IV and V**.
**COVID-19** is viral (**SARS-CoV-2**), with **humans** as hosts, spread by **respiratory transmission** and **contact**.
It affects the **respiratory system** and can cause **multi-organ complications**.
xa: SARS-CoV-2 is a **coronavirus**.
The **Epidemic Diseases Act** (**1897**) was **amended in 2020** to protect health workers.
**Measles** also spreads by respiratory transmission and is **highly contagious**.

114.s:
How many of the following statements about measles are correct?
I. Measles is caused by measles virus.
II. Measles is a viral disease.
III. Humans are the host of measles.
IV. Measles is transmitted through respiratory routes.
V. Measles is highly contagious.
114.x: All five are correct: measles is a highly contagious human viral disease spread through the air.
114.tq: Recall the facts about measles.
n: Measles is caused by measles virus. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Measles is a viral disease. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Measles has humans as hosts. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Measles spreads through respiratory transmission. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Measles is highly contagious. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
xs: All five statements are correct — option **(4)** **All five**.
**Measles** is a viral disease (**measles virus**) with **humans** as hosts.
It spreads by **respiratory transmission** and is **highly contagious**.
xa: **Mumps** spreads through **saliva and nasal secretions**.
Measles is among the **UIP** diseases (**1985**).
**U-WIN** is the digital portal registering every UIP vaccination.

114.s: Which of the following statements about pneumonia is incorrect?
o: Humans are the host of pneumonia; it is infectious and affects the lungs.
Viral and fungal causes of pneumonia are also noted.
Pneumonia is mainly caused by bacteria, and Streptococcus pneumoniae is a main cause.
Pneumonia is mainly caused by fungi, although Streptococcus pneumoniae is a main cause.
114.x: Option D is incorrect: pneumonia is mainly bacterial, especially Streptococcus pneumoniae, though viruses and fungi can also cause it. It is an infectious lung disease.
114.tq: Check the main cause for a swapped word.
n: Pneumonia is mainly caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae and other organisms. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Pneumonia can have viral causes. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Pneumonia can have fungal causes. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Pneumonia has humans as hosts. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Pneumonia is infectious. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Pneumonia affects the lungs. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Pneumonia can have bacterial causes. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
xs: The incorrect statement is option **(4)**: pneumonia is **not mainly fungal**.
Pneumonia is mainly caused by **Streptococcus pneumoniae**; **bacterial**, **viral** or **fungal** causes are noted.
**Humans** are hosts; it is **infectious** and affects the **lungs**.
xa: **Atypical pneumonia** is caused by **Mycoplasma pneumoniae**.
**Pneumococcal pneumonia** and **Hib** are covered under **UIP**.
**Nafithromycin** ("**Miqnaf**") is India's first indigenous **macrolide**, for community-acquired bacterial pneumonia.

114.s:
Consider the following statements:

I. Humans are the host of diphtheria, and diphtheria is transmitted through respiratory routes.
II. Gonorrhoea is a bacterial disease, and humans are its host.
III. Syphilis is a bacterial disease and is transmitted sexually.
IV. Humans are the host of pertussis, and pertussis is transmitted through respiratory routes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
114.x: All four are correct: diphtheria and pertussis are human diseases spread through the air, and gonorrhoea and syphilis are sexually transmitted bacterial diseases.
114.tq: Recall the transmission of each disease.
n: Diphtheria has humans as hosts. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Diphtheria spreads through respiratory transmission. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Gonorrhoea is a bacterial disease. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Gonorrhoea has humans as hosts. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Syphilis is a bacterial disease. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Syphilis spreads through sexual transmission. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Pertussis has humans as hosts. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Pertussis spreads through respiratory transmission. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(2)** **I, II, III and IV**.
**Diphtheria** and **pertussis**: **humans** as hosts, **respiratory transmission**.
**Gonorrhoea** and **syphilis**: **bacterial** diseases of humans, **sexually transmitted**.
xa: Syphilis affects **genitals, rectum and mouth**.
Gonorrhoea affects **reproductive organs**.
**Diphtheria**, **pertussis** and **tetanus** are UIP diseases.

114.s:
Consider the following statements about tuberculosis:

I. Tuberculosis is a bacterial disease.
II. Humans are the host of tuberculosis.
III. Tuberculosis is transmitted through respiratory routes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
114.x: All three are correct: tuberculosis is a human bacterial disease spread through the air.
114.tq: Recall the facts about tuberculosis.
n: Tuberculosis is a bacterial disease. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Tuberculosis has humans as hosts. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Tuberculosis spreads through respiratory transmission. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(1)** **I, II and III**.
**Tuberculosis** is a **bacterial** disease (**Mycobacterium tuberculosis**) with **humans** as hosts.
It spreads by **respiratory transmission** (droplet nuclei).
xa: TB affects the **lungs**.
**Streptomycin** is used against **tuberculosis**.
⚠ **TB** = air-borne — a common odd-one-out in water-borne lists.

114.s:
Consider the following statements about fungal plant pathogens:
1. Ustilago causes smut diseases.
2. Puccinia causes smut of wheat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
114.x: Statement 1 is correct: Ustilago causes smut. Statement 2 is wrong: Puccinia causes rust of wheat, not smut. So '1 only'.
114.tq: Puccinia = rust; Ustilago = smut.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)** **1 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **Ustilago** causes **smut**.
Statement 2 wrong: **Puccinia** causes **rust of wheat**, not smut.
xa: Fungal pathogens cause **plant diseases**.
**White rust** affects **mustard** and crucifer areas.
**Ear cockle** of wheat: **Uttar Pradesh**, **Punjab**, **western Bihar**.

114.s:
Assertion (A): Biofilms can contribute to persistent or chronic infection.
Reason (R): The EPS matrix protects microbes and reduces antibiotic penetration or effect.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
114.x: Both are true and R explains A: the EPS matrix shields biofilm microbes and blocks antibiotics, so infections persist.
114.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: The EPS matrix protects microbes in a biofilm. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 124-126]
A biofilm reduces antibiotic penetration and effect. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 124-126]
A biofilm causes persistent or chronic infection. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 124-126]
xs: **Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A** — option **(1)**.
The **EPS matrix** protects microbes and **reduces antibiotic penetration and effect**.
So biofilms cause **persistent or chronic infection** that is **difficult to eradicate**.
xa: EPS = **extracellular polymeric substances**.
Biofilms form on **catheters**, **pipes**, **medical implants** and **human tissues**.
Biofilms give greater tolerance to **host defence** and **external stress**.

114.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Biofilms in the food industry are associated with spoilage and contamination.
Statement B: Biofilms are associated only with catheters and not with food-processing surfaces.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
114.x: Statement A is true: biofilms cause spoilage and contamination in food plants. Statement B is false because of "only"; biofilms also form on food-processing surfaces.
114.tq: Check each statement for the word "only".
n: Biofilms occur on catheters, pipes, implants, and food-processing surfaces. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 124-126]
Biofilms cause spoilage and contamination in the food industry. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 124-126]
xs: **Statement A is true, Statement B is false** — option **(3)**.
A: biofilms in the **food industry** cause **spoilage and contamination**.
B wrong: biofilms form not only on **catheters** but also on **food** and **food-processing surfaces**.
xa: Biofilms also occur on **pipes**, **implants** and **human tissues**.
A biofilm is a **microbial sessile community** adhering to a surface and to each other.
Biofilms **increase antibiotic resistance**.

114.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Biofilms are microbial communities embedded in a self-produced matrix.
II. The EPS matrix protects microbes.
III. Biofilms are associated with increased tolerance/resistance.
IV. Biofilms are associated with persistent/chronic infection.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
114.x: All four are correct: biofilms are microbial communities in a self-made EPS matrix that protects them, raises resistance and causes chronic infections.
114.tq: Recall the features of biofilms.
n: A biofilm is a microbial community embedded in a self-produced matrix. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 124-126]
The EPS matrix protects microbes in a biofilm. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 124-126]
A biofilm increases microbial tolerance and resistance. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 124-126]
A biofilm causes persistent or chronic infection. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 124-126]
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(3)** **I, II, III and IV**.
Biofilms are microbial communities in a **self-produced matrix**; the **EPS matrix** protects the microbes.
They show **increased tolerance/resistance** and cause **persistent/chronic infection**.
xa: EPS = **extracellular polymeric substances**.
In the food industry biofilms cause **spoilage and contamination**.
Resistance progression: **MDR → XDR → TDR**.

114.s:
How many of the following are locations or materials on which biofilms can form?

I. Medical implants
II. Human tissues
III. Food
IV. Food-processing surfaces
114.x: All four are correct: biofilms grow on medical implants, human tissues, food and food-processing surfaces.
114.tq: Recall where biofilms form.
n: Biofilms can form on medical implants. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 71-73]
Biofilms can occur on human tissues. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 71-73]
Biofilms can form in food. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 71-73]
Biofilms can form on food-processing surfaces. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 71-73]
xs: All four are biofilm sites — option **(4)** **All four**.
Biofilms form on **medical implants**, **human tissues**, **food** and **food-processing surfaces**.
xa: They also form on **catheters** and **pipes**.
In the food industry they cause **spoilage and contamination**.
The **EPS matrix** (**extracellular polymeric substances**) protects the microbes.

114.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Biofilms can exhibit antibiotic resistance.
II. Biofilms have greater tolerance to host defence.
III. Biofilms have greater tolerance to external stress.
IV. Bacterial drug resistance is graded in increasing severity as MDR, XDR and TDR.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
114.x: All four are correct: biofilms resist antibiotics and tolerate host defences and stress, and bacterial resistance is graded from multidrug (MDR) to extensively (XDR) to totally drug-resistant (TDR).
114.tq: Recall the features of biofilms.
n: Biofilms can exhibit antibiotic resistance. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 71-73]
Biofilms have greater tolerance to host defence. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 71-73]
Biofilms have greater tolerance to external stress. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 71-73]
The resistance progression mentioned for bacteria is MDR, XDR, and TDR. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 71-73]
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(1)** **I, II, III and IV**.
**Biofilms** show **antibiotic resistance** and greater tolerance to **host defence** and **external stress**.
Bacterial resistance progresses **MDR → XDR → TDR**.
xa: Biofilms cause **persistent or chronic infection**.
The **matrix** gives additional resistance or protection.
WHO **Bacterial Priority Pathogens List (2024)**: critical includes **rifampicin-resistant TB**.

114.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Antibiotic use in livestock can lead to resistant strains.
II. Repeated exposure can select resistant organisms.
III. Mutation can generate resistance.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
114.x: All three are correct: antibiotics in livestock, repeated exposure and mutation all contribute to resistance.
114.tq: Recall the causes of antibiotic resistance.
n: Antibiotic use in livestock causes resistant strains. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 124-126]
Repeated antibiotic exposure causes selection of resistant organisms. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 124-126]
Mutation can generate antibiotic resistance. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 124-126]
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(3)** **I, II and III**.
**Livestock use** → **resistant strains**; **repeated exposure** → **selection** of resistant organisms.
**Mutation** can **generate** antibiotic resistance.
xa: **Incorrect dose** → selection of resistant microbes.
**Overuse** → **selection pressure**.
**National Action Plan on AMR** (**2017**) is **One Health** based.

114.s:
Match the causes with their effects:

List-I (Cause)
a. Horizontal gene transfer
b. Mutation
c. Poor infection control
d. Incomplete course

List-II (Effect)
i. Spread of resistant organisms
ii. Can generate resistance
iii. Spread of resistance genes
iv. Resistant survivors multiply
114.x: Horizontal gene transfer spreads resistance genes, mutation creates resistance, poor infection control spreads resistant microbes and stopping a course early lets survivors multiply, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv.
114.tq: Recall the causes of antibiotic resistance.
n: An incomplete antibiotic course allows resistant survivors to multiply. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 124-126]
Horizontal gene transfer spreads resistance genes. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 124-126]
Mutation can generate antibiotic resistance. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 124-126]
Poor infection control spreads resistant organisms. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 124-126]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv** — option **(2)**.
**Horizontal gene transfer** — spreads **resistance genes**; **mutation** — can **generate** resistance.
**Poor infection control** — spreads **resistant organisms**; **incomplete course** — **resistant survivors multiply**.
xa: **Red Line campaign** (**2016**): red line on prescription-only antibiotic packs.
**Kerala KARSAP** (**2018**): first state AMR action plan.
**Nafithromycin** by **Wockhardt** — ⚠ **NOT Sun Pharma**.

114.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) GMO
(b) Transgenic organism
(c) Biofilm
(d) Matrix

List-II
(i) Extracellular polymeric substances
(ii) Microbial sessile community
(iii) Genetically Modified Organism
(iv) Organism into which a foreign gene has been introduced
114.x: GMO means genetically modified organism, a transgenic organism has a foreign gene, a biofilm is a sessile microbial community and its matrix is EPS, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
114.tq: Recall the definitions.
n: GMO stands for genetically modified organism. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 71-73]
A transgenic organism has a foreign gene introduced into it. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 71-73]
A biofilm is a microbial sessile community. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 71-73]
The biofilm matrix consists of extracellular polymeric substances. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 71-73]
A transgenic organism receives a gene from another organism. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 71-73]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i** — option **(4)**.
**GMO** — **Genetically Modified Organism**; **transgenic organism** — one into which a **foreign gene** is introduced.
**Biofilm** — **microbial sessile community**; **matrix** — **extracellular polymeric substances**.
xa: Biofilm cells **adhere** to a surface and to **each other**.
The EPS matrix **reduces antibiotic penetration**.
Biofilms form on **catheters**, **pipes**, **implants**.

114.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India's policy response to antimicrobial resistance:
1. The National Action Plan on AMR (2017) is based on the One Health approach.
2. Kerala's KARSAP (2018) was the first State-level AMR action plan.
3. The Red Line campaign (2016) places a red vertical line on the packs of all over-the-counter medicines.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
114.x: Statement 1 is correct: NAP-AMR (2017) is One Health based. Statement 2 is correct: Kerala's KARSAP (2018) was the first State AMR action plan. Statement 3 is wrong: the Red Line (2016) marks prescription-only antibiotics, not all over-the-counter medicines. So '1 and 2 only' is right; '1 only' misses KARSAP, and options with 3 include the false statement.
114.tq: Red Line = prescription-only antibiotics; NAP-AMR 2017, KARSAP 2018, Red Line 2016.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **National Action Plan on AMR (2017)** is **One Health** based — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Kerala's KARSAP (2018)** was the **first State AMR action plan**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **Red Line (2016)** marks **prescription-only antibiotics**, not all OTC medicines.
xa: **National One Health Mission** (**PM-STIAC**) tackles **AMR**, rabies, Nipah, avian influenza.
**National Institute of One Health**: **Nagpur**.
AMR causes include **self-medication** and unregulated veterinary drugs.

114.s: The National One Health Mission is associated with which of the following institutions or bodies?
114.x: The National One Health Mission is associated with PM-STIAC and provides institutional multisectoral coordination for One Health actions.
114.tq: Use institutional association to distinguish the mission from unrelated national bodies.
xs: The **National One Health Mission** comes under **PM-STIAC** — option **(3)** is correct.
It provides **institutional multisectoral coordination**; ECI, CPCB and ILO are unrelated.
xa: Used against **rabies**, **Nipah**, **avian influenza** and **AMR**.
**National Institute of One Health**: **Nagpur**.
AP's **State Action Plan on zoonotic diseases** (Jul **2026**) is under One Health.

114.s:
Consider the following statements about the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897:
1. It was enacted against the bubonic plague in Bombay.
2. It contains four sections.
3. It was amended in 2005 to protect health workers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
114.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Act was enacted against bubonic plague in Bombay. Statement 2 is correct: it has four sections. Statement 3 is wrong: the amendment protecting health workers came in 2020, not 2005. Hence '1 and 2 only'; every other option includes the false statement 3 or drops a true one.
114.tq: 1897 plague in Bombay, 4 sections, amended 2020 (COVID) for health workers.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **Epidemic Diseases Act 1897** was enacted against **bubonic plague** in **Bombay** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
Statement 2 is correct: it has **4 sections**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it was **amended in 2020** (not 2005) to protect health workers.
xa: **Plague**: rodents via **rat flea**; pathogen **Yersinia pestis**.
**IDSP (2004)**: disease surveillance under **MoHFW/NCDC**.
**NCDC** leads **surveillance and response**; IDSP now runs on the **IHIP** platform.

114.s: The Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP) was introduced in which year?
114.x: The Universal Immunisation Programme was introduced in 1985.
114.tq: Select the programme year from the sequence of major immunisation milestones.
xs: The **Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP)** began in **1985** — option **(2)** is correct.
It covers **12 diseases**.
xa: **Mission Indradhanush**: **Dec 2014**, **>90%** full immunisation target.
**U-WIN** registers every UIP vaccination.
UIP includes **JE** in **endemic districts**.

114.s: What is the principal function of the U-WIN digital portal?
o: Registering every vaccination provided under UIP
Monitoring only antimicrobial resistance in hospitals
Recording only adult BCG doses in Andhra Pradesh
114.x: U-WIN is a digital portal for registering every vaccination administered under the Universal Immunisation Programme.
114.tq: Match the digital platform with its exact record-keeping function.
xs: **U-WIN** is the digital portal **registering every UIP vaccination** — option **(2)** is correct.
It does not license manufacturers, monitor AMR or record only AP BCG doses.
xa: **Mission Indradhanush** (**Dec 2014**): **>90%** full immunisation.
**IDSP** surveillance now runs on the **IHIP** digital platform.

114.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
 a. Penicillium
 b. Streptomyces
 c. Bacillus
 d. Acetobacter

List-II
 i. Several antibiotics
 ii. Vinegar/acetic acid production
 iii. Penicillin
 iv. Streptomycin
114.x: Penicillium gives penicillin, Streptomyces streptomycin, Bacillus several antibiotics and Acetobacter vinegar, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
114.tq: Recall the source of each antibiotic.
n: Penicillium produces penicillin. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 122-124]
Acetobacter produces vinegar. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 122-124]
Acetobacter produces acetic acid. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 122-124]
Streptomyces produces streptomycin. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 122-124]
Bacillus produces several antibiotics. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 122-124]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii** — option **(1)**.
**Penicillium** — **penicillin**; **Streptomyces** — **streptomycin**.
**Bacillus** — **several antibiotics**; **Acetobacter** — vinegar/acetic acid production.
xa: **Streptomyces** and **Bacillus** are **important bacterial sources** of antibiotics.
Penicillin was discovered from **Penicillium notatum** in **1928**.
Streptomycin is used against **tuberculosis**.

114.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Antibiotic)
a. Penicillin
b. Streptomycin
c. Chloramphenicol
d. Griseofulvin

List-II (Key association)
i. Typhoid
ii. Tuberculosis
iii. First antibiotic, discovered by Alexander Fleming
iv. Fungal skin infections such as ringworm
114.x: Penicillin was the first antibiotic, discovered by Fleming in 1928; streptomycin was the first drug against tuberculosis; chloramphenicol is used for typhoid; griseofulvin treats ringworm, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv.
114.tq: Link each antibiotic to its landmark use.
n: Penicillin is associated with bacterial infections. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 124-126]
Streptomycin is associated with tuberculosis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 124-126]
Tetracycline is associated with bacterial infections. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 124-126]
Chloramphenicol is associated with typhoid. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 124-126]
Chloramphenicol is associated with bacterial infections. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 124-126]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv** — option **(4)**.
**Penicillin** — first antibiotic, by **Alexander Fleming**; **streptomycin** — **tuberculosis**.
**Chloramphenicol** — **typhoid**; **griseofulvin** — fungal skin infections such as **ringworm**.
xa: Fleming found penicillin in **1928** from **Penicillium notatum**.
Chloramphenicol is **broad-spectrum**.
**Ringworm** is caused by **dermatophytes**.

114.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Epidemic dropsy is caused by Argemone mexicana oil.
II. Argemone mexicana oil contains sanguinarine.
III. Argemone mexicana oil contains dihydrosanguinarine.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
114.x: All three are correct: epidemic dropsy comes from mustard oil adulterated with argemone oil, which contains sanguinarine and dihydrosanguinarine.
114.tq: Recall the cause of epidemic dropsy.
n: Epidemic dropsy is caused by Argemone mexicana oil. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 33-35]
Argemone mexicana oil contains sanguinarine. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 33-35]
Argemone mexicana oil contains dihydrosanguinarine. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 33-35]
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(2)** **I, II and III**.
**Epidemic dropsy** is caused by **Argemone mexicana oil**, which contains **sanguinarine** and **dihydrosanguinarine**.
xa: **Mushroom poisoning**: **Amanita**, with **α-amanitin**.
**Aflatoxin**: **Aspergillus flavus** and **Aspergillus parasiticus**.
**Ergotism**: **ergot alkaloids** of **Claviceps purpurea**.

114.s: The National Framework for Malaria Elimination (2016–2030) aims to achieve which of the following?
o: Elimination of all communicable diseases by 2030
114.x: The National Framework for Malaria Elimination covers the period 2016–2030 and aims at a malaria-free India by 2030.
114.tq: Match the programme period with its precise national target.
xs: The **National Framework for Malaria Elimination (2016-2030)** aims at a **malaria-free India by 2030** — option **(2)** is correct.
It targets malaria only, not dengue or all communicable diseases.
xa: Malaria is an NCVBDC elimination target alongside **LF** and **kala-azar**.
WHO malaria-free in South Asia: **Maldives (2015)**, **Sri Lanka (2016)**.
AP response: **IRS**, **LLINs**, source reduction.

114.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Nafithromycin:
1. It was launched on 20 November 2024.
2. It was launched by Dr Jitendra Singh.
3. It was developed by Wockhardt with BIRAC support.
4. It was developed by Sun Pharma.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
114.x: Nafithromycin was launched on 20 November 2024 by Dr Jitendra Singh and was developed by Wockhardt with BIRAC support. It was not developed by Sun Pharma.
114.tq: The wrong-company trap tests precise attribution of a product’s developer.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Nafithromycin was launched **20 Nov 2024** by **Dr. Jitendra Singh**, developed by **Wockhardt** with **BIRAC** support.
Statement 4 is wrong: ⚠ it is **NOT Sun Pharma**.
xa: Brand name **"Miqnaf"**; a **macrolide** for community-acquired bacterial pneumonia.
**National Action Plan on AMR**: **2017**.
**Kerala KARSAP (2018)**: first State AMR plan.

114.s: The 2026 rise in malaria cases in Andhra Pradesh was particularly concentrated in which districts or area?
114.x: The rise in malaria in 2026 was concentrated in Alluri Sitharama Raju, Polavaram and Vizianagaram districts.
114.tq: Use location-based elimination and avoid substituting other district groups.
xs: The **2026** malaria rise was concentrated in **ASR (Alluri Sitharama Raju), Polavaram and Vizianagaram** — option **(1)** is correct.
These are **tribal/agency** districts, not the coastal or Rayalaseema districts in other options.
xa: Free **LLINs** for **7.80 lakh** people (**Rs 19.25 crore**) in ASR and Parvathipuram-Manyam.
Response: **IRS**, **LLINs**, source reduction.

114.s: Which of the following correctly represents the reported 2026 burden of scrub typhus in Andhra Pradesh and its concentration?
o: 1,475 cases, rising in all coastal districts
941 cases, rising in ASR and Parvathipuram Manyam
52 cases, rising in ASR and Kurnool
146 cases, rising in Polavaram and Vizianagaram
114.x: Scrub typhus accounted for 941 cases and was rising in ASR and Parvathipuram Manyam districts.
114.tq: Match the disease burden figure with the correct geographical concentration.
xs: AP had **941** scrub typhus cases, **rising in ASR and Parvathipuram Manyam** — option **(2)** is correct.
xa: Scrub typhus vector: **chigger mite**; pathogen **Orientia tsutsugamushi**.
**High-level committees** were set up for scrub typhus.
**Agency districts** carry most of AP's scrub typhus.

114.s:
How many of the following statements about ergotism are correct?

I. Ergotism is associated with rye and cereals.
II. Ergotism can spread through ingestion.
III. Ergotism affects the nervous, vascular and endocrine systems.
114.x: All three are correct: ergotism comes from eating rye or grain infected by the ergot fungus, and it affects nerves, blood vessels and hormones.
114.tq: Recall the facts about ergotism.
n: Ergotism is associated with rye and cereals. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Ergotism can spread through ingestion. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Ergotism affects the nervous, vascular and endocrine systems. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(3)** **All three**.
**Ergotism** is linked to **rye and cereals**, spreads through **ingestion**, and affects the **nervous, vascular and endocrine systems**.
xa: It is caused by **ergot alkaloids** produced by **Claviceps purpurea**.
Ergotism is a **fungal intoxication**.
**Aflatoxin** comes from **Aspergillus flavus** and **Aspergillus parasiticus**.

114.s: Amoebiasis is primarily an infection of the:
o: Lymphatic system caused by filarial worms
Small intestine caused by Ascaris lumbricoides
Large intestine caused by Entamoeba histolytica
114.x: Amoebiasis affects the large intestine and is caused by Entamoeba histolytica.
114.tq: Discriminate between similar disease-organ and causative-organism combinations.
xs: **Amoebiasis** infects the **large intestine**, caused by **Entamoeba histolytica** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Ascaris lumbricoides** = **ascariasis** (small intestine); **filariasis** = lymphatic system; **Mycobacterium tuberculosis** = TB (lungs).
xa: **Dengue** targets **platelets** (APPSC **2023**).
**Malaria**: liver, then RBCs.
Water-borne **dysentery** pathogens: **rotavirus**, **E. coli**, **Shigella**.

114.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Ascaris lumbricoides
(b) Taenia solium
(c) Schistosomes
(d) Fasciola hepatica/gigantica

List-II
(i) Fascioliasis
(ii) Ascariasis
(iii) Schistosomiasis
(iv) Neurocysticercosis
114.x: Ascaris causes ascariasis, Taenia solium neurocysticercosis, schistosomes schistosomiasis and Fasciola fascioliasis, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
114.tq: Recall the worm behind each disease.
n: Ascaris lumbricoides causes ascariasis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 29-31]
Taenia solium causes neurocysticercosis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 29-31]
Schistosomes cause schistosomiasis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 29-31]
Fasciola hepatica/gigantica causes fascioliasis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 29-31]
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i** — option **(4)**.
**Ascaris lumbricoides** — **ascariasis**; **Taenia solium** — **neurocysticercosis**.
**Schistosomes** — **schistosomiasis**; **Fasciola hepatica/gigantica** — **fascioliasis**.
xa: Taenia solium also causes **taeniasis**; associated with **pork**.
Schistosomiasis affects **urinary tract and intestine**.
Fascioliasis affects **liver and bile ducts**.

114.s:
Consider the following statements about Taenia solium:
I. It has humans as hosts.
II. It is associated with pork.
III. It causes taeniasis.
IV. It causes neurocysticercosis.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
114.x: All four are correct: Taenia solium, the pork tapeworm, infects humans, causing taeniasis and, from its eggs, neurocysticercosis.
114.tq: Recall the facts about the pork tapeworm.
n: Taenia solium has humans as hosts. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 31-32]
Taenia solium is associated with pork. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 31-32]
Taenia solium causes taeniasis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 31-32]
Taenia solium causes neurocysticercosis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 31-32]
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)** **I, II, III and IV**.
**Taenia solium** has **humans** as hosts and is associated with **pork**.
It causes **taeniasis** and **neurocysticercosis**.
xa: Neurocysticercosis is caused by **Taenia solium eggs** via **contaminated food or water**.
It affects the **brain and central nervous system**.
**Fascioliasis** hosts are **ruminants** (cattle and sheep).

114.s: AIDS is caused by which of the following pathogens?
114.x: AIDS is caused by HIV, a retrovirus that destroys helper T cells. CHIKV, Zika and yellow fever viruses cause other diseases.
114.tq: Recall the virus behind each disease.
n: AIDS is caused by HIV. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
xs: AIDS is caused by **HIV** — option **(4)**.
**CHIKV** causes **chikungunya**; **Zika virus** causes **Zika**; **yellow fever virus** causes **yellow fever**.
xa: AIDS is a **retrovirus-related** disease that affects the **immune system**.
HIV spreads through **blood**, **sexual transmission** and **mother to child**.
**Hepatitis-B** (**HBV**) shares the same blood, sexual and mother-to-child routes.

114.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Diphtheria
(b) Gonorrhoea
(c) Syphilis
(d) Pertussis

List-II
i. Treponema pallidum
ii. Bordetella pertussis
iii. Neisseria gonorrhoeae
iv. Corynebacterium diphtheriae
114.x: Diphtheria is caused by Corynebacterium diphtheriae, gonorrhoea by Neisseria gonorrhoeae, syphilis by Treponema pallidum and pertussis by Bordetella pertussis, giving a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii.
114.tq: Recall the bacterium behind each disease.
n: Diphtheria is caused by Corynebacterium diphtheriae. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Gonorrhoea is caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Syphilis is caused by Treponema pallidum. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Pertussis is caused by Bordetella pertussis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
xs: The correct match is **a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii** — option **(4)**.
**Diphtheria** — **Corynebacterium diphtheriae**; **gonorrhoea** — **Neisseria gonorrhoeae**.
**Syphilis** — **Treponema pallidum**; **pertussis** — **Bordetella pertussis**.
xa: Diphtheria and pertussis spread by **respiratory transmission**.
Gonorrhoea and syphilis spread by **sexual transmission**.
Pertussis = **whooping cough**.

114.s: Which of the following effects is associated with tetanus?
114.x: Tetanus toxin causes jaw spasms (lockjaw). Whooping cough is pertussis, and reproductive-organ effects belong to gonorrhoea and syphilis.
114.tq: Recall the key symptom of tetanus.
n: Pertussis causes whooping cough. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Gonorrhoea affects the reproductive organs. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Syphilis affects the genitals, rectum and mouth. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Tetanus can cause jaw involvement. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
xs: **Jaw spasms** are associated with **tetanus** — option **(1)**.
Tetanus (**Clostridium tetani**) causes **muscle spasms** with **jaw involvement**.
**Whooping cough** is **pertussis**; **reproductive organs** — **gonorrhoea**; **genitals, rectum and mouth** — **syphilis**.
xa: Tetanus source: **soil**; it can follow a **contaminated wound**.
**Botulism** affects **nerves** and causes **paralysis**.
Tetanus is covered under **UIP**.

114.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
114.x: Option C is incorrect: Mycobacterium leprae causes leprosy; diphtheria is caused by Corynebacterium diphtheriae. The malaria and typhoid pairings are right.
114.tq: Recall the pathogen of each disease.
n: P. falciparum causes malignant malaria. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 29-31]
Salmonella typhi causes typhoid. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 29-31]
Mycobacterium leprae causes leprosy. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 29-31]
Corynebacterium diphtheriae causes diphtheria. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 29-31]
P. vivax causes recurring malaria. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 29-31]
Plasmodium causes malaria. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 29-31]
xs: The incorrect statement is option **(3)**: **Mycobacterium leprae** causes **leprosy**, not diphtheria.
**Diphtheria** is caused by **Corynebacterium diphtheriae**.
**P. falciparum** — **malignant malaria**; **P. vivax** — **recurring malaria**; **Salmonella typhi** — **typhoid**.
xa: P. falciparum is the **most lethal** — **cerebral malaria**.
P. vivax accounts for a **major share** of cases.
Leprosy affects **skin** and **peripheral nerves**.

114.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Aspergillus flavus produces aflatoxin.
II. Aspergillus parasiticus produces aflatoxin.
III. Mushroom poisoning is caused by Amanita.
IV. Amanita contains α-amanitin.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
114.x: All four are correct: Aspergillus flavus and A. parasiticus make aflatoxin, and Amanita mushrooms contain the deadly α-amanitin.
114.tq: Recall the fungal toxins.
n: Aspergillus flavus produces aflatoxin. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 33-35]
Aspergillus parasiticus produces aflatoxin. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 33-35]
Mushroom poisoning is caused by Amanita. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 33-35]
Amanita contains α-amanitin. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 33-35]
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(1)** **I, II, III and IV**.
**Aspergillus flavus** and **Aspergillus parasiticus** both **produce aflatoxin**.
**Mushroom poisoning** is caused by **Amanita**, which contains **α-amanitin**.
xa: **Epidemic dropsy**: **Argemone mexicana oil** (**sanguinarine**).
**Botulism**: **botulinum toxin** of **Clostridium botulinum**.
**Aspergillus** also causes **aspergillosis**.

114.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Antibiotics are mostly natural or semi-synthetic.
II. Some antibiotics are fully synthetic.
III. All antibiotics are obtained only from fungi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
114.x: I and II are correct: most antibiotics are natural or semi-synthetic, and some are fully synthetic. III is false because many come from bacteria, not only fungi.
114.tq: Check each statement for the words "all" and "only".
n: Antibiotics are mostly natural or semi-synthetic. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Some antibiotics are fully synthetic. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
xs: Statements **I and II** are correct — option **(1)** **I and II only**.
Antibiotics are **mostly natural or semi-synthetic**; **some are fully synthetic**.
Statement III wrong: main sources are **fungi and bacteria** — e.g. **Streptomyces** and **Bacillus**.
xa: **Penicillin** comes from **Penicillium**; **streptomycin** from **Streptomyces**.
**Fleming** discovered penicillin in **1928**; **Waksman** coined "antibiotic" in **1942**.
Resistance progression: **MDR → XDR → TDR**.

114.s: Which of the following antibiotics is broad-spectrum?
114.x: Chloramphenicol is a broad-spectrum antibiotic, acting on many Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. Penicillin G is narrow-spectrum, iodoform is an antiseptic and reserpine a tranquillizer.
114.tq: Discriminate broad-spectrum from narrow-spectrum antibiotics.
n: Chloramphenicol is broad-spectrum. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
xs: **Chloramphenicol** is the **broad-spectrum** antibiotic — option **(2)**.
Chloramphenicol is used against **typhoid** and other **bacterial infections**.
xa: **Penicillin** (from **Penicillium**) treats **bacterial infections**.
**Tetracycline** is used for **bacterial infections**.
Antibiotics act against **bacteria only**.

115.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The 'dual burden of malnutrition' means undernutrition coexisting with adult overweight and obesity.
2. DALY is the sum of years of life lost to premature death and years of healthy life gained through treatment.
3. The 'triple burden' of disease adds injuries to communicable and non-communicable diseases.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
115.x: Statement 3 is correct: triple burden = CDs + NCDs + injuries (road accidents, trauma). Statement 1 is correct: undernutrition plus adult overweight/obesity. Statement 2 is wrong: DALY = YLL (years of life lost) + YLD (years lived with disability). Hence '1 and 3 only'.
115.tq: DALY = YLL + YLD; triple burden adds injuries.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)** **1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **dual burden of malnutrition** = **undernutrition** + adult **overweight and obesity**.
Statement 2 wrong: **DALY** = **YLL** + **YLD** (years lived with disability), not years gained through treatment.
Statement 3 correct: **triple burden** adds **injuries** to CDs + NCDs.
xa: **Dual burden**: rising rates of both **infectious** and **non-communicable** diseases.
Omran stages: **Pestilence and Famine** → **Receding Pandemics** → **Degenerative and Man-Made Diseases**.
**NCDs cause 57%** of all deaths (ES 2025-26).

115.s: The India State-Level Disease Burden Initiative is associated with which combination of institutions and study?
o: ICMR, PHFI and IHME; Global Burden of Disease study
WHO, UNICEF and FAO; World Health Survey
NCDC, FSSAI and NITI Aayog; National Family Health Survey
ICMR, ISRO and DRDO; Census of India
115.x: The estimates are produced through the ICMR-PHFI-IHME India State-Level Disease Burden Initiative, which forms part of the Global Burden of Disease study.
115.tq: Match the institutional group with the named study rather than with a nearby health survey.
xs: Data come from the **ICMR-PHFI-IHME India State-Level Disease Burden Initiative**, part of the **Global Burden of Disease study** — option **(1)**.
WHO/UNICEF, NCDC/FSSAI/NITI and ISRO/DRDO are not its partners.
xa: **DALY** (**YLL + YLD**) is the burden metric.
**NFHS-5** gives overweight/obesity data.

115.s: The 'dual burden of disease' in India refers to:
o: Rising rates of both infectious and non-communicable diseases
Coexistence of undernutrition and obesity in the same household
High maternal mortality alongside high infant mortality
Simultaneous rise of injuries and mental illness
115.x: Dual burden (PYQ answer) means persistent communicable diseases such as TB, malaria and dengue coexisting with rising NCDs. Undernutrition with obesity is the dual burden of malnutrition; adding injuries gives the triple burden; the other option is not the term.
115.tq: Dual = CDs + NCDs; triple adds injuries.
xs: The **dual burden of disease** = **rising rates of both infectious and non-communicable diseases** (PYQ) — option **(1)** is correct.
Persistent CDs (**TB, malaria, dengue**, vector-borne) coexist with rising **NCDs**.
**Undernutrition + obesity** is the **dual burden of malnutrition**; adding **injuries** makes the **triple burden**.
xa: India's path: a **"linear shift"** from infectious diseases to NCDs.
Health systems must shift from **curative care to screening and prevention**.

115.s:
Arrange the following stages of epidemiological transition in the correct chronological order:
A. Age of Degenerative and Man-Made Diseases
B. Age of Pestilence and Famine
C. Age of Receding Pandemics
115.x: Omran's sequence proceeds from the Age of Pestilence and Famine to the Age of Receding Pandemics and then to the Age of Degenerative and Man-Made Diseases.
115.tq: Identify the initial high-infection stage and the final NCD-dominant stage, then place the intermediate stage.
xs: **Omran**'s order: **Pestilence and Famine → Receding Pandemics → Degenerative and Man-Made Diseases** (B, C, A) — option **(1)**.
Stage 1: deaths from infections and famine; stage 2: infections fall; stage 3: **NCDs dominate**.
xa: Receding Pandemics: improved **sanitation and vaccination**.
India's path: **"linear shift"** to NCDs.
**NCDs** now cause **57%** of deaths.

115.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Non-communicable diseases account for 57% of all deaths in India.
2. Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death in India.
3. The share of non-communicable diseases in deaths has declined from 61.8% in 2016 to 37.9% in 1990.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
115.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 reverses the trend: the recorded share was 37.9% in 1990 and 61.8% in 2016 in the cited study.
115.tq: Check the direction of the numerical trend before selecting the coded combination.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **NCDs cause 57% of all deaths** (ES **2025-26**) — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
Statement 2 is correct: **cardiovascular diseases** are India's leading cause.
Statement 3 reverses the trend: NCD share **rose** from **37.9% in 1990** to **61.8% in 2016** (Lancet study).
xa: World's single biggest killer: **ischaemic heart disease** (WHO).
Data: **ICMR-PHFI-IHME India State-Level Disease Burden Initiative**.
⚠ Older notes give NCD share as **">60%"**.

115.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the leading causes of death in India and in the world?
o: Tuberculosis leads in India, while dengue is the single biggest killer in the world.
Cardiovascular diseases lead in India, while ischaemic heart disease is the single biggest killer in the world.
Cancer leads in India, while cardiovascular disease is absent from the global ranking.
Injuries lead in India, while chronic respiratory disease is the single biggest global killer.
115.x: Cardiovascular diseases are the leading cause of death in India, while WHO estimates identify ischaemic heart disease as the world's single biggest killer.
115.tq: Keep the country-level and global-level comparisons separate before matching the two answers.
xs: **Cardiovascular diseases lead in India**, while **ischaemic heart disease** is the **world's single biggest killer** — option **(2)** is correct.
TB, cancer and injuries are not India's leading cause in the notes; dengue is not the global top killer.
xa: **NCDs** cause **57%** of deaths in India (ES **2025-26**).
"**Big four**" NCDs: **cardiovascular**, **cancers**, **chronic respiratory**, **diabetes**.
India's probability of dying from an NCD **rose** (**2001-2019**).

115.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India is undergoing a linear shift from infectious diseases to non-communicable diseases.
2. Life expectancy in India rose from 49.7 years in 1973 to 70.3 years in 2023.
3. Maternal mortality ratio has fallen by 86% since 1990.
4. Under-five mortality rate has fallen by 78% since 1990.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
115.x: All four statements correctly describe the epidemiological and mortality transition reported for India.
115.tq: Check each numerical and trend statement independently before selecting the complete combination.
xs: All four are correct — option **(4)** (**1, 2, 3 and 4**).
India shows a **"linear shift"** from infections to NCDs; life expectancy **49.7 (1973) → 70.3 (2023)**.
xa: **NCDs** cause **57%** of deaths.
**Cardiovascular diseases** lead in India.
Omran's third stage: **Degenerative and Man-Made Diseases**.

115.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Dengue — Aedes mosquito
2. Chikungunya — Aedes mosquito
3. Zika — Aedes mosquito
4. Japanese encephalitis — Culex mosquito
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
115.x: Dengue, chikungunya and Zika are carried by Aedes mosquitoes, whereas Japanese encephalitis is carried by Culex mosquitoes.
115.tq: Start with the repeated Aedes association and verify the contrasting Culex pair.
xs: All four pairs are correct — option **(4)** (**1, 2, 3 and 4**).
**Dengue, chikungunya and Zika** are spread by **Aedes**; **JE** by **Culex**.
xa: **Meningococcal meningitis** spreads by **respiratory droplets**, not mosquitoes.
AP **2025**: dengue **2,686** cases, **5** deaths; AES/JE **146** cases, **2** deaths.
**Malaria is NOT a lifestyle disease**.

115.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Bakery products are often rich in hydrogenated fats containing trans fats.
2. Excess intake of trans fats raises the risk of non-communicable diseases.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
115.x: Both statements are correct (PYQ): bakery products use hydrogenated fats containing trans fats, and excess trans fats raise NCD risk, which is why FSSAI caps trans fat at 2% in fats and oils. '1 only' and '2 only' each reject a true statement; 'Neither' rejects both.
115.tq: Trans fats: bakery + NCD risk, both true.
xs: Both are correct — option **(3)** (PYQ).
1: **Bakery products** are rich in **hydrogenated fats containing trans fats**.
2: Excess trans fats **raise the risk of NCDs**.
xa: **FSSAI** caps trans fat at **≤2%** in fats and oils.
Another PYQ: **sedentary lifestyle** + **energy-dense foods** → degenerative diseases (both correct).
**Eat Right India** promotes healthy eating.

115.s:
Which of the following are main risk factors for lifestyle (non-communicable) diseases?
1. Unhealthy diet
2. Physical inactivity
3. Tobacco use
4. Alcohol use
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
115.x: All four are main NCD risk factors (UPSC), along with urbanisation and ageing. Every other option leaves out at least one listed risk factor.
115.tq: NCD risks: diet, inactivity, tobacco, alcohol.
xs: All four — **unhealthy diet, physical inactivity, tobacco, alcohol** — are main NCD risk factors (UPSC) — option **(4)**.
Each other option leaves out at least one listed factor.
xa: Also **urbanisation** and **ageing**.
NFHS-5: **24%** women, **23%** men overweight/obese.
Uddanam survey: tobacco use **38.8%**, alcohol use **23.7%**.

115.s:
Consider the following statements regarding cancer notification in India:
1. Cancer is not nationally notifiable in India.
2. Seventeen States have made cancer a notifiable disease.
3. Telangana was the most recent State to make cancer notifiable.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
115.x: All three statements are correct: cancer is not nationally notifiable, 17 States have notified it, and Telangana was the most recent State to do so.
115.tq: Check each statement separately, especially the distinction between national and State-level notification.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4)** (**1, 2 and 3**).
Cancer is **not notifiable nationally**; **17 states** made it notifiable; **Telangana** was the **most recent** (**4 Jul 2026**).
xa: Registries cover only **10-16%** of people.
**UNGA** declaration adds **childhood cancer** as a new area.

115.s: Which one of the following is NOT a lifestyle disease?
115.x: Malaria is a communicable disease caused by Plasmodium and spread by mosquitoes, so it is not a lifestyle disease (PYQ). Diabetes, hypertension and obesity are lifestyle-related NCDs.
115.tq: Odd one out: malaria (pathogen-caused).
xs: **Malaria** is a communicable, pathogen-caused disease — **NOT a lifestyle disease** (PYQ) — option **(3)** is the answer.
**Diabetes**, **hypertension** and **obesity** are lifestyle NCDs.
xa: ICMR's malaria initiative: **MERA**.
Main NCD risk factors: diet, **physical inactivity**, **tobacco**, **alcohol**.
**Obesity**: excess energy intake + low physical activity.

115.s: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has capped trans fat in fats and oils at:
115.x: FSSAI has capped trans fat in fats and oils at 2%.
115.tq: Use the precise regulatory limit rather than the broader dietary-risk information.
xs: **FSSAI** caps **trans fat** at **≤2%** in fats and oils — option **(2)** is correct.
The cap targets trans fats because excess intake **raises NCD risk** (PYQ).
xa: **Bakery products** are rich in **hydrogenated fats** containing trans fats.
Programmes: **Eat Right India**, **Fit India** (**18 May 2026**).
The **UNGA declaration** seeks stronger regulation of **tobacco, trans fats** and **e-cigarettes**.

115.s:
The United Nations General Assembly declaration on non-communicable diseases and mental health includes which of the following newer areas or determinants?
1. Oral health and lung health
2. Childhood cancer
3. Air pollution and lead
4. Digital harms such as screen time
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
115.x: The declaration covers oral and lung health, childhood cancer, air pollution, lead and digital harms such as screen time. It also calls for stronger regulation of tobacco, trans fats and e-cigarettes.
115.tq: When all listed items belong to the stated expansion of scope, select the complete combination.
xs: All four are in the **UNGA declaration on NCDs and mental health** — option **(4)** (**1, 2, 3 and 4**).
New areas: **oral health, lung health, childhood cancer**; new determinants: **air pollution, lead**.
For the **first time**: **digital harms** (screen time).
xa: Targets for **2030**.
Stronger regulation of **tobacco, trans fats and e-cigarettes**.
**SDG 3**: cut premature NCD deaths by **one-third**.

115.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases (NP-NCD):
1. It was formerly known as NPCDCS.
2. It runs NCD clinics at district hospitals and Community Health Centres.
3. It screens everyone above 40 years of age.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
115.x: Statement 1 is correct: NP-NCD was formerly NPCDCS (2010). Statement 2 is correct: NCD clinics are run at district hospitals and CHCs. Statement 3 is wrong: screening covers everyone over 30, not 40. So '1 and 2 only'; '2 only' omits a true statement, and the options with 3 include the wrong age.
115.tq: NP-NCD: ex-NPCDCS, clinics at DH/CHC, screening 30+.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **NP-NCD** was **formerly NPCDCS** (**2010**) — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
Statement 2 is correct: it runs **NCD clinics at district hospitals and CHCs**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **everyone over 30** is screened, not 40.
xa: Funding **60:40** (**90:10** for NE and hilly states).
**Ayushman Arogya Mandirs** screen for hypertension, diabetes, cancers.
**SDG 3**: cut premature NCD deaths by **one-third**.

115.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the relevant SDG 3 health target?
o: Premature NCD deaths — reduce by one-half
Premature NCD deaths — reduce by one-third
115.x: SDG 3 includes the target of reducing premature deaths from non-communicable diseases by one-third. It also promotes mental health and seeks to halve road-traffic deaths.
115.tq: Discriminate between the different numerical targets under the same goal.
xs: **SDG 3**: cut **premature NCD deaths by one-third** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Road-traffic deaths** are to be **halved** (not cut by one-third); NCD deaths not halved; mental health is to be **promoted**.
xa: **Tele-MANAS**: **24x7** tele-mental-health support.
**Triple burden** includes **injuries** (road accidents).
**UNGA declaration** sets **2030** targets.

115.s: Tele-MANAS, available in all 36 States and Union Territories, provides:
o: Online registration of every UIP vaccination
115.x: Tele-MANAS gives round-the-clock tele-mental-health support across all 36 States and UTs. Vaccination registration is U-WIN; cancer screening and trauma surgery are not its role.
115.tq: Tele-MANAS = 24x7 mental-health helpline.
xs: **Tele-MANAS** gives **24x7 tele-mental-health support** in all **36** States/UTs (**12 Jun 2026**) — option **(1)** is correct.
Vaccination registration is **U-WIN**; cancer screening is at **Ayushman Arogya Mandirs**.
xa: **SDG 3** promotes **mental health**.
**UNGA declaration on NCDs and mental health**: first time **digital harms**.
**NP-NCD** runs NCD clinics at district hospitals and CHCs.

115.s: Excess saturated fat is associated with which of the following effects?
o: Night blindness due to vitamin A deficiency
Increase in blood lipids and cholesterol
115.x: Excess saturated fat raises blood lipids and cholesterol. Bleeding, night blindness and goitre are deficiency effects, not effects of excess fat.
115.tq: Discriminate saturated fat effects from trans fat effects.
n: Excess saturated fat increases blood lipids and cholesterol. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 45-46]
xs: Excess **saturated fat** causes an **increase in blood lipids and cholesterol** — option **(4)**.
The other options are deficiency effects, not effects of excess fat.
xa: Excess **trans fat** **increases LDL** — cardiovascular risk.
**FSSAI cap**: trans fat ≤ **2%** in fats and oils.
Saturated fatty acids: **palmitic** (butter, palm oil, meat), **stearic** (meat, cocoa butter).

115.s: Uddanam, located in which district of Andhra Pradesh, is associated with chronic kidney disease of unknown cause (CKDu)?
115.x: Uddanam is in Srikakulam district and is associated with CKDu. Palasa is the location of the kidney centre, while Mangalagiri is the location of AIIMS.
115.tq: Separate the geographical region from the nearby institutions associated with it.
xs: **Uddanam** is in **Srikakulam** district — known for **CKDu** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Vizianagaram** has the diabetic-foot clinic; **Mangalagiri** has AIIMS; **Palasa** has the kidney centre.
xa: Interim report: high kidney disease in **Kaviti mandal** (**13 Sep 2026**).
Samples tested for **pesticides/heavy metals** with **CSIR-IICT Hyderabad**.
**AIIMS Mangalagiri** runs CKDu screening camps.

115.s:
With reference to the investigation into chronic kidney disease of unknown cause (CKDu) in Uddanam, consider the following statements:
1. Soil, water, blood and urine samples are being tested for viruses and protozoa.
2. The testing is being done with CSIR-IICT, Hyderabad.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
115.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the samples are tested for pesticides and heavy metals, not viruses and protozoa. Statement 2 is correct: testing is with CSIR-IICT Hyderabad. So '2 only'; '1 only' and 'Both' accept the wrong statement, and 'Neither' rejects the true one.
115.tq: Uddanam CKDu: pesticides/heavy metals, CSIR-IICT Hyderabad.
xs: Statement 2 is correct: testing is with **CSIR-IICT Hyderabad** — so **2 only**, option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is wrong: soil, water, blood and urine are tested for **pesticides/heavy metals**, not viruses and protozoa.
xa: CKDu = **chronic kidney disease of unknown cause**.
High kidney disease in **Kaviti mandal**.
Among those covered: tobacco **38.8%**, alcohol **23.7%**.

115.s: Which institution conducts CKDu screening camps in the Uddanam region?
115.x: AIIMS Mangalagiri conducts screening camps for chronic kidney disease of unknown cause in the Uddanam region.
115.tq: Distinguish the institution conducting field screening from the laboratory involved in testing.
xs: **AIIMS Mangalagiri** runs **CKDu screening camps** — option **(3)** is correct.
**CSIR-IICT Hyderabad** tests samples; it does not run camps.
xa: Uddanam is in **Srikakulam**; hotspot **Kaviti mandal**.
**Palasa** kidney centre.
Interim report: **13 Sep 2026**.

115.s: The increasing importance of non-communicable diseases requires the health system to shift primarily from:
o: Hospital care to environmental sampling only
Curative care to screening and prevention
Prevention and screening to curative care
115.x: The growing NCD burden requires a shift from a predominantly curative approach towards screening and prevention.
115.tq: Apply the policy implication of changing disease patterns to the health-system approach.
xs: The NCD shift requires the health system to move **from curative care to screening and prevention** — option **(2)** is correct (UPSC).
Option (4) reverses the direction.
xa: **NP-NCD** screens everyone over **30**.
**Ayushman Arogya Mandirs** screen for hypertension, diabetes and cancers.

115.s: The Kidney Research Centre and Super Specialty Hospital associated with the Uddanam kidney disease issue is located at:
115.x: The Kidney Research Centre and Super Specialty Hospital is located at Palasa in Srikakulam district.
115.tq: Use the place-specific association instead of confusing the hospital with the screening institution.
xs: The kidney centre linked to **Uddanam** is at **Palasa, Srikakulam** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Mangalagiri** = AIIMS screening; **Kaviti** = CKDu hotspot mandal; **Vizianagaram** = diabetic-foot clinic.
xa: Uddanam CKDu: interim report **13 Sep 2026**.
Testing with **CSIR-IICT Hyderabad**.
AP's first **Diabetic Foot and Ulcer Clinic**: Vizianagaram (Jul **2026**).

115.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with Andhra Pradesh's NCD-care initiatives?
115.x: Vizianagaram hosts the diabetic-foot clinic. Palasa has the kidney centre, and Uddanam (including Kaviti) is known for CKDu.
115.tq: Vizianagaram feet, Palasa kidneys.
xs: **Vizianagaram — diabetic-foot clinic** is correct — option **(3)**.
**Palasa** has the **kidney centre**; **Kaviti/Uddanam** is known for **CKDu**, not a clinic or registry.
xa: Clinic opened Jul **2026** — AP's **first**.
**AIIMS Mangalagiri** runs CKDu screening camps.
**Diabetes** is among the **big four** NCDs.

115.s: Which one of the following sets consists entirely of the four major non-communicable disease groups?
o: Cardiovascular diseases, cancers, chronic respiratory diseases and diabetes
115.x: The four major NCD groups are cardiovascular diseases, cancers, chronic respiratory diseases and diabetes.
115.tq: Look for a set in which every item belongs to the same classification, not merely one or two items.
xs: The **"big four" NCDs**: **cardiovascular diseases, cancers, chronic respiratory diseases and diabetes** — option **(3)** is correct.
The other sets mix in communicable diseases like **malaria, typhoid, dengue, TB, cholera, chikungunya, Nipah**.
xa: **Cardiovascular diseases** lead in India.
Risk factors: unhealthy diet, **physical inactivity, tobacco, alcohol**.
**NP-NCD** screens everyone over **30**.

115.s: Meningococcal meningitis is primarily transmitted through:
o: Respiratory droplets from person to person
115.x: Meningococcal meningitis spreads from person to person through respiratory droplets. Vomiting and neck stiffness are among its symptoms.
115.tq: Separate a respiratory-droplet infection from mosquito-borne diseases by identifying the mode of transmission.
xs: **Meningococcal meningitis** spreads **person to person via respiratory droplets**, **not mosquitoes** — option **(3)** is correct.
Symptoms: **vomiting**, **neck stiffness**.
xa: **Aedes** spreads **dengue, chikungunya, Zika**; **Culex** spreads **JE**.
**H1N1** spike in **Aug 2026**.
ICMR wastewater surveillance: **5 to 50** cities.

115.s: Which one of the following statements regarding infectious disease surveillance in India is correct?
o: NCDC wastewater surveillance covers 10 cities and excludes antimicrobial resistance.
ICMR wastewater surveillance declined from 50 to 5 cities and tracks only one virus.
ICMR wastewater surveillance expanded from 5 to 50 cities and tracks 10 viruses, along with antimicrobial resistance.
The programme tracks only dengue and chikungunya and does not include avian influenza.
115.x: ICMR's wastewater surveillance expanded from 5 to 50 cities, tracks 10 viruses including avian influenza, and also monitors antimicrobial resistance.
115.tq: Check the direction of expansion, the number of cities and the scope of surveillance together.
xs: **ICMR wastewater surveillance** (**2026**) expanded **from 5 to 50 cities**, tracks **10 viruses** incl. **avian influenza**, plus **AMR** — option **(3)**.
It is ICMR's (not NCDC's), it **expanded** (not declined), and it includes **avian influenza**.
xa: **NCDC's PHEOC** activated (**13 Jan 2026**).
**India TB Research Consortium** and **MERA** are other ICMR initiatives.

115.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Linoleic acid
(b) Alpha-linolenic acid
(c) Palmitoleic acid
(d) Butyric acid

List-II
(i) Macadamia nuts
(ii) Butter
(iii) Linseed oil; omega-3
(iv) Peanut oil, chicken fat, olive oil
115.x: Linoleic acid is in peanut and olive oil, α-linolenic (omega-3) in linseed oil, palmitoleic acid in macadamia nuts and butyric acid in butter, giving a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii.
115.tq: Recall the source of each fatty acid.
n: Peanut oil is a source of linoleic acid. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 46-47]
Chicken fat is a source of linoleic acid. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 46-47]
Olive oil is a source of linoleic acid. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 46-47]
Linseed oil is a source of α-linolenic acid. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 46-47]
α-Linolenic acid is an omega-3 fatty acid. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 46-47]
Macadamia nuts are a source of palmitoleic acid. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 46-47]
Butter is a source of butyric acid. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 46-47]
xs: The correct match is **a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii** — option **(3)**.
**Linoleic acid** — **peanut oil, chicken fat, olive oil**; **α-linolenic acid** — **linseed oil** (**omega-3**).
**Palmitoleic acid** — **macadamia nuts**; **butyric acid** — **butter**.
xa: **Oleic acid**: **olive oil**, **canola oil**.
**Lauric acid**: **coconut oil**, palm-kernel oil, breast milk.
**Myristoleic acid**: **whale blubber**.

115.s:
How many of the following are correctly paired with the fatty acid they are known for?

I. Butter — Butyric acid
II. Coconut oil — Lauric acid
III. Linseed oil — Alpha-linolenic acid
IV. Macadamia nuts — Arachidonic acid
115.x: Three are correct: butter is known for butyric acid, coconut oil for lauric acid and linseed oil for alpha-linolenic acid. IV is wrong because macadamia nuts are known for palmitoleic acid; arachidonic acid comes from liver and brain.
115.tq: Recall the signature fatty acid of each food source.
n: Butter is a source of palmitic acid. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 46-47]
Palm oil is a source of palmitic acid. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 46-47]
Meat is a source of palmitic acid. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 46-47]
xs: **Three** pairs are correct — option **(3)** **Only three**.
Correct: **butter — butyric acid**, **coconut oil — lauric acid**, **linseed oil — alpha-linolenic acid**.
Pair IV wrong: **macadamia nuts** are known for **palmitoleic acid**; **arachidonic acid** is from **liver, brain, glandular organs**.
xa: **Palmitic acid**: **butter**, **palm oil**, **meat**.
**Stearic acid**: **meat**, **cocoa butter**.
**Linoleic acid**: **peanut oil**, chicken fat, olive oil.

116.s:
Which one of the following is correctly matched?

Term — Meaning
o: Pandemic — Spread across countries and continents
Endemic — Sudden severe outbreak in a region
Epizootic — Constant human disease at baseline level
116.x: A pandemic is an epidemic that spreads across countries and continents. Epizootic refers to an epidemic among animals, while endemic refers to constant baseline presence.
116.tq: Distinguish the four near-sounding terms by their geographical or host scope.
xs: **Pandemic — spread across countries and continents** is correct — option **(2)** (UPSC).
**Epidemic among animals** = **epizootic**; **sudden severe regional outbreak** = **epidemic**; **constant baseline presence** = **endemic**.
xa: H1N1 was declared a **pandemic** in **June 2009**.
COVID-19 pandemic declared **11 March 2020**.
⚠ **PHEIC** is not the same as a "pandemic emergency" (Ebola **2026**).

116.s: A sudden outbreak of a disease in a severe form in a particular region at a particular time is termed:
116.x: An epidemic is a sudden, severe outbreak in a region at a particular time. Endemic means constantly present at a baseline level; a pandemic is an epidemic spread across countries and continents; an epizootic is an epidemic among animals.
116.tq: Epidemic = sudden + regional; pandemic = cross-continent.
xs: A **sudden, severe outbreak in a region at a particular time** is an **epidemic** (PYQ) — option **(2)** is correct.
**Endemic** = constant baseline; **pandemic** = across countries and continents; **epizootic** = among animals.
xa: India example: **Chandipura**, **Gujarat 2024**.
**Plague**: **Surat**, Gujarat **1994**.
**Nipah**: **West Bengal**, **2** cases, Jan **2026**.

116.s: The first Indian outbreak of avian influenza was reported at Navapur in:
116.x: The first Indian outbreak of avian influenza was reported at Navapur in Maharashtra in 2006.
116.tq: Combine the first-outbreak location with the year and State.
xs: India's first **avian influenza** outbreak was at **Navapur, Maharashtra** in **2006** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Gujarat 1994** = Surat **plague**; **Kerala 2018** = **Nipah**.
xa: **H5N1** = avian influenza A.
**Chandipura**: Gujarat **2024**.
**Nipah**: West Bengal Jan **2026**.

116.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: COVID-19 was associated with Wuhan, China, in December 2019.
Nipah was associated with Kozhikode, Kerala.
Kala-azar is spread by the Anopheles mosquito.
Ebola was reported from Nzara, South Sudan, and Yambuku, DR Congo, in 1976.
116.x: Option C is incorrect: kala-azar (visceral leishmaniasis) is spread by the sandfly; Anopheles carries malaria. The COVID-19, Nipah and Ebola places are right.
116.tq: Match each disease with its correct vector or place of origin.
n: COVID-19 was reported in Wuhan, China, in December 2019. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 35-37]
Ebola was reported in Nzara, South Sudan, in 1976. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 35-37]
Ebola was reported in Yambuku, Democratic Republic of the Congo, in 1976. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 35-37]
Nipah was reported in Kozhikode, Kerala. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 35-37]
Kala-azar occurs in tropical areas. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 35-37]
Sleeping sickness occurs in tropical Africa. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 35-37]
xs: The incorrect statement is option **(3)**: **kala-azar** is spread by the **sandfly**, not the Anopheles mosquito.
**COVID-19** — **Wuhan**, **December 2019**; **Nipah** — **Kozhikode, Kerala**; **Ebola** — **Nzara** and **Yambuku**, **1976**.
xa: **Anopheles** transmits **malaria**.
