**Chandipura** (Gujarat **2024**) is also spread by **sandfly**.
**Nipah** in **West Bengal**: **2 cases**, **Jan 2026**.

116.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
116.x: COVID-19 was a pandemic, and Nipah had outbreaks in Kerala. 1976 outbreaks were Ebola, and 2011 eradication was rinderpest.
116.tq: Recall the facts about each outbreak.
n: COVID-19 is a pandemic. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 37-39]
Nipah had an outbreak in Kerala. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 37-39]
xs: **COVID-19—Pandemic; Nipah—outbreak in Kerala** is correctly matched — option **(3)**.
**Simultaneous outbreaks in 1976** belong to **Ebola**, not Nipah.
**Eradicated in 2011** refers to **rinderpest**, not Nipah.
xa: Nipah first identified in **1998**, **Malaysia**.
COVID-19 PHEIC: **30 Jan 2020**.
Ebola **2026** (**Bundibugyo virus**) was declared a **PHEIC** — ⚠ **not** a "pandemic emergency".

116.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Outbreak — Intermediate host
116.x: Civet cats were identified as the intermediate host associated with SARS. Dromedary camels are associated with MERS, while pangolins were suspected intermediate hosts for SARS-CoV-2.
116.tq: Discriminate between closely related outbreak-host associations.
xs: **SARS — civet cats** is correct — option **(1)**.
**MERS** = **dromedary camels** (not pangolins); **pangolins** = suspected host of **SARS-CoV-2**; Ebola reservoir = **fruit bats**.
xa: SARS-CoV-2's **natural reservoir** = **bats**.

116.s:
Which one of the following is correctly matched?

1. H1N1 — Influenza A subtype
2. H5N1 — Avian influenza A
3. MERS — 2012 outbreak
4. SARS — 2002–03 outbreak
116.x: All four associations are correct. H1N1 is an Influenza A subtype, H5N1 is avian influenza A, MERS is associated with 2012 and SARS with 2002–03.
116.tq: Check each outbreak against its virus type or period before selecting the complete combination.
xs: All four are correct — option **(4)** (**1, 2, 3 and 4**).
**H1N1** = Influenza A subtype; **H5N1** = avian influenza A.
xa: H1N1 first in **North America 2009**; **pandemic** declared **June 2009**.
MERS host: **dromedary camels**; SARS host: **civet cats**.
**H1N1** spike in India in **Aug 2026**.

116.s: Which one of the following combinations contains only diseases or outbreaks that were declared PHEICs before or during the COVID-19 period listed?
116.x: The listed earlier PHEICs included H1N1 in 2009, polio in 2014 and Zika in 2016. The listed PHEIC chronology also included Ebola in 2014 and 2019 and COVID-19 on 30 January 2020.
116.tq: Use chronology and exact PHEIC status to eliminate plausible but unsupported outbreaks.
xs: **H1N1 2009, polio 2014 and Zika 2016** were all PHEICs — option **(1)** is correct.
**SARS**, **MERS**, **Nipah**, **dengue**, **cholera** and **malaria** are not in the PHEIC list.
xa: Other PHEICs: **Ebola 2014 and 2019**; **COVID-19** (**30 Jan 2020**).
**Ebola (Bundibugyo)**: May **2026**.

116.s:
Which one of the following is correctly matched with a major outbreak in India?

1. Nipah — Kerala from 2018 onwards
2. Zika — Kerala, 2021
3. Chandipura — Gujarat, 2024
4. Plague — Surat, Gujarat, 1994
116.x: All four pairs are correct: Nipah has struck Kerala from 2018 onwards, Zika appeared in Kerala in 2021, Chandipura (sandfly-borne) broke out in Gujarat in 2024, and plague (Yersinia pestis) hit Surat, Gujarat, in 1994. Hence '1, 2, 3 and 4'.
116.tq: Check each disease-location-year association before accepting the complete combination.
xs: All four are correct — option **(4)** (**1, 2, 3 and 4**).
**Nipah – Kerala (2018 onwards)**; **Zika – Kerala 2021**.
**Chandipura – Gujarat 2024**; **plague – Surat, Gujarat 1994**.
xa: **Nipah**: also **West Bengal**, **2** cases, Jan **2026**.
**Avian influenza**: **Navapur, Maharashtra 2006**.
Plague: **Yersinia pestis** via **rat flea**; Zika via **Aedes**.

116.s: The causative organism of the plague outbreak reported in Surat in 1994 was:
116.x: The plague outbreak in Surat, Gujarat, in 1994 was associated with Yersinia pestis and transmission through rat fleas.
116.tq: Distinguish a bacterial causative organism from viral outbreak agents.
xs: The **Surat, Gujarat 1994** plague was caused by **Yersinia pestis**, spread by **rat flea** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Chandipura virus** = Gujarat **2024**; **Influenza A** = H1N1/H5N1; **Orthoebolavirus** = Ebola.
xa: First Indian **avian influenza**: **Navapur, Maharashtra 2006**.
**Zika** Kerala **2021**.
**Nipah** Kerala **2018** onwards.

116.s: SARS-CoV-2 was first identified in which place and month-year?
116.x: SARS-CoV-2 was first identified in Wuhan in Hubei province of China in December 2019.
116.tq: Combine location and time rather than selecting the correct place with a wrong date.
xs: **SARS-CoV-2** was first identified in **Wuhan, Hubei, China, December 2019** (UPSC) — option **(2)** is correct.
**March 2020** is when WHO declared the pandemic.
xa: **Natural reservoir** = **bats**; **pangolins** = suspected intermediate host.
India's first case: **Kerala, 30 Jan 2020**.
COVID-19 **PHEIC**: **30 Jan 2020**.

116.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Ebola disease was first identified in 1978.
Nipah disease was first identified in 1998 in Malaysia.
116.x: Option B is incorrect: Ebola was first identified in 1976 in Zaire and Sudan, not 1978. SARS (2002), Nipah (1998) and MERS (2012) are right.
116.tq: Recall the years diseases emerged.
n: SARS was first identified in 2002. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 19-20]
Ebola disease was first identified in 1976. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 19-20]
Nipah disease was first identified in 1998 in Malaysia. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 19-20]
MERS was first identified in 2012. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 19-20]
xs: The incorrect statement is option **(2)**: **Ebola** was first identified in **1976**, not 1978.
xa: Ebola 1976 sites: **Nzara, South Sudan** and **Yambuku, DR Congo**.
Nipah is named after **Sungai Nipah, Malaysia**; reported in **Kozhikode, Kerala**.
**COVID-19**: **December 2019**, **Wuhan, China**.
MERS host: **dromedary camels**.

116.s: Anopheles is identified by which characteristic?
116.x: Anopheles rests with its body at an angle to the surface, head down and tail up, unlike Culex, which rests parallel.
116.tq: Recall how Anopheles is told from Culex.
n: Anopheles is identified by its characteristic resting position. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 19-20]
xs: **Anopheles** is identified by its **characteristic resting position** — option **(2)**.
The notes name only the **resting position** as its identifying feature — not breeding, feeding or flying position.
xa: **Female Anopheles** transmits **malaria**.
**Culex** transmits **filariasis** and **Japanese encephalitis**.
**Aedes aegypti** transmits **dengue**, **yellow fever**, **chikungunya**, **Zika**.

116.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: An endemic disease is regularly found in a particular place or population.
A pandemic spreads across a large geographical region, multiple continents or worldwide.
The Ebola disease had simultaneous outbreaks in 2011.
An epidemic is a rapid or large occurrence in a population within a short period.
116.x: Option C is incorrect: Ebola's first simultaneous outbreaks were in 1976, not 2011. The definitions of endemic, pandemic and epidemic are right.
116.tq: Recall the dates of outbreaks.
n: An endemic disease is regularly found in a particular place or population. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 37-39]
An epidemic is a rapid or large occurrence of disease in a population within a short period. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 37-39]
A pandemic spreads across a large geographical region, multiple continents, or worldwide. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 37-39]
Ebola had simultaneous outbreaks in 1976. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 37-39]
xs: The incorrect statement is option **(3)**: **Ebola** had **simultaneous outbreaks** in **1976**, not 2011.
**Endemic** — regularly found in a particular place; **pandemic** — spreads across **multiple continents** or worldwide.
**Epidemic** — a **rapid or large occurrence** in a population within a **short period**.
xa: **Epizootic** = an epidemic-like occurrence among **animals**.
Example of a pandemic: **COVID-19**; of an epidemic: **Nipah** in **Kerala**.
WHO declared COVID-19 a pandemic on **11 March 2020**.

116.s: WHO declared COVID-19 a pandemic on:
116.x: WHO declared COVID-19 a pandemic on 11 March 2020. The date 30 January 2020 refers to the declaration of COVID-19 as a PHEIC.
116.tq: Discriminate between the PHEIC date and the later pandemic declaration date.
xs: WHO declared COVID-19 a **pandemic** on **11 March 2020** — option **(2)** is correct.
**30 Jan 2020** = COVID-19 **PHEIC** (and India's first case); **24 Feb 2022** = Lancet report; **16 Jan 2021** = vaccination start.
xa: **H1N1** pandemic: **June 2009**.
First identified: **Wuhan**, **December 2019**.
**Delta** second wave: **April-May 2021**.

116.s:
Arrange the following COVID-19 events in chronological order:
A. Omicron third wave in India
B. First COVID-19 case in Kerala
C. Delta second wave
D. Peak of the first wave
116.x: The first case in Kerala occurred on 30 January 2020, the first wave peaked in September 2020, the Delta second wave occurred in April–May 2021 and the Omicron third wave came in January 2022.
116.tq: Fix the first and last events, then place the two intervening waves by date.
xs: Order: **first case (Kerala, 30 Jan 2020) → first-wave peak (Sep 2020) → Delta wave (Apr-May 2021) → Omicron wave (Jan 2022)** — option **(1)** (B, D, C, A).
B (first case) comes first and A (**Omicron**, **third** wave) last; the **first-wave peak** (D) precedes the **Delta** second wave (C) — ruling out options **(2)**, **(3)** and **(4)**.
xa: Vaccination began **16 Jan 2021**.
WHO pandemic declaration: **11 March 2020**.
**200 crore** doses by **17 Jul 2022**.

116.s:
Consider the following statements about India's COVID-19 vaccination drive:
1. It began on 16 January 2021.
2. It was guided by NEGVAC.
3. It crossed 200 crore doses by 17 July 2021.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
116.x: Statement 1 is correct: vaccination began on 16 January 2021. Statement 2 is correct: it was guided by NEGVAC. Statement 3 is wrong: 200 crore doses were crossed by 17 July 2022, not 2021. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses NEGVAC, and the options with 3 have the wrong year.
116.tq: Start 16 Jan 2021 (NEGVAC); 200 crore by 17 Jul 2022.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: vaccination began **16 Jan 2021** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
Statement 2 is correct: it was guided by **NEGVAC**.

116.s: Which of the following statements regarding the 2026 Bundibugyo outbreak is NOT correct?
o: The fourth India-Africa Forum Summit was postponed.
It involved the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda.
It was officially declared a pandemic emergency.
It was declared a PHEIC in May 2026.
116.x: The outbreak was declared a PHEIC but not a pandemic emergency. It involved the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, and the fourth India-Africa Forum Summit was postponed.
116.tq: Find the single reversed or overstated institutional description.
xs: The **2026 Bundibugyo** outbreak was **not** declared a **pandemic emergency** — option **(3)** is the incorrect statement.
It was declared a **PHEIC** in **May 2026**, in **DR Congo (Ituri) and Uganda**, and the **4th India-Africa Forum Summit** was **postponed**.
xa: **Ebola** genus **Orthoebolavirus**; **Zaire** is the deadliest.
Earlier Ebola PHEICs: **2014** and **2019**.
**COVID-19** PHEIC: **30 Jan 2020**.

116.s: Which receptor enables SARS-CoV-2 to enter human cells?
116.x: SARS-CoV-2 enters cells through the ACE2 receptor.
116.tq: Identify the precise receptor instead of confusing it with a viral protein or immune-cell marker.
xs: SARS-CoV-2 enters cells via the **ACE2 receptor** — option **(2)** is correct.
**RBD** is the spike's receptor-binding domain — the basis of **Corbevax** — not the host receptor.
xa: Disease: **COVID-19** = Coronavirus Disease 2019.
Natural reservoir: **bats**; suspected intermediate host: **pangolins**.
First identified: **Wuhan**, **December 2019**.

116.s: Which COVID-19 variant was first found in India?
116.x: The Delta variant was first found in India. Alpha was associated with the United Kingdom, Beta with South Africa and Omicron with southern Africa.
116.tq: Test one distinctive variant-location association directly.
xs: The **Delta** variant was first found in **India** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Alpha** = **UK**; **Beta** = **South Africa**; **Omicron** = **Southern Africa**.
xa: **Gamma** = **Brazil**.
**Delta** drove India's **second wave** (**April-May 2021**).
**Omicron** third wave: **Jan 2022**.

116.s:
Which of the following formed part of India's COVID-19 strategy?

1. Test-track-treat-vaccinate
2. COVID-appropriate behaviour
3. A three-tier facility arrangement
4. MHA Empowered Groups
116.x: All four were components of India's COVID-19 response strategy: test-track-treat-vaccinate, COVID-appropriate behaviour, MHA Empowered Groups and a three-tier facility arrangement.
116.tq: Recognise the complete policy cluster and avoid excluding the administrative component.
xs: All four were part of India's strategy — option **(4)** (**1, 2, 3 and 4**).
**Test-track-treat-vaccinate** + **COVID-appropriate behaviour**.
**MHA Empowered Groups** and a **three-tier** facility arrangement.
xa: Labs: **1,364 government + 1,753 private** by **1 Jan 2022**.
Vaccination guided by **NEGVAC**, from **16 Jan 2021**.
**CoWIN**: booking, tracking, digital certificates.

116.s: The Lancet report released on 24 February 2022 estimated that approximately how many children in India lost a parent or caregiver?
116.x: The Lancet report of 24 February 2022 estimated that about 19 lakh children in India lost a parent or caregiver to COVID-19. The figure covers loss of a parent or caregiver, not only children who lost both parents.
116.tq: Use the approximate figure and distinguish it from other child-impact estimates.
xs: The **Lancet** (**24 Feb 2022**) estimated **about 19 lakh** children in India lost a **parent or caregiver** (PYQ) — option **(2)**.
The figure covers loss of a parent **or** caregiver, not only orphans.
xa: **PM CARES for Children (2021)**: children who lost both parents, surviving parent or guardian.
UNICEF-ILO: **8.9 million** more child labourers by end-**2022**.
Support under PM CARES at **23 years**.

116.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the lessons emerging from the COVID-19 pandemic:
1. One Health is associated with a Quadripartite approach.
2. Equitable access to vaccines is identified as an important lesson.
3. Pandemic preparedness can be separated entirely from animal and environmental health.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
116.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the One Health approach links human, animal and environmental health rather than separating them entirely.
116.tq: Find the statement with the extreme word 'entirely'; it reverses the integrated One Health approach.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **One Health** is linked to the **Quadripartite** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(3)**.
Statement 2 is correct: **equitable vaccine access** is a key lesson.
Statement 3 is wrong: One Health links human, animal and environmental health — they cannot be separated.
xa: **COVAX** (WHO, Gavi, CEPI) aimed at **equitable access**.
Gaps exposed: **oxygen supply**, **migrant crisis**, imported **reagents**.
SARS-CoV-2 reservoir **bats**, suspected host **pangolins** — a zoonotic link.

116.s:
Consider the following pairs (COVID-19 containment initiative - State):
1. Mo Jeeban - Odisha
2. Dharavi model - Kerala
3. Door-to-door fever surveys by village volunteers - Andhra Pradesh
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
116.x: Pair 1 is correct: Mo Jeeban was Odisha's initiative. Pair 2 is wrong: the Dharavi model ('chasing the virus') was in Mumbai, Maharashtra; Kerala's was Break the Chain. Pair 3 is correct: AP ran door-to-door fever surveys through village volunteers. So '1 and 3 only'.
116.tq: Mo Jeeban-Odisha, Dharavi-Mumbai, Bhilwara-Rajasthan, Break the Chain-Kerala, volunteer surveys-AP.
xs: Pair 1 is correct: **Mo Jeeban — Odisha** (PYQ) — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
Pair 2 is wrong: the **Dharavi model** ("chasing the virus") was **Mumbai, Maharashtra**; Kerala's was **Break the Chain**.
Pair 3 is correct: **AP** ran **door-to-door fever surveys** via village volunteers.
xa: **Bhilwara model** = **Rajasthan**.
AP added COVID treatment to **YSR Aarogyasri**.
AP's **Covid Pharma app** tracked OTC fever/cough medicine sales.

116.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Polio is caused by Poliovirus and is associated with the Salk vaccine.
Measles is caused by Measles virus and is associated with MMR.
Tetanus is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis and is associated with tetanus toxoid.
Rabies is caused by Rabies virus and is associated with the rabies vaccine.
116.x: Option C is incorrect: tetanus is caused by Clostridium tetani; Mycobacterium tuberculosis causes TB. The polio, measles and rabies facts are right.
116.tq: Recall the pathogen of each disease.
n: The polio vaccine is used against poliomyelitis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 131-133]
Poliomyelitis is caused by poliovirus. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 131-133]
Tuberculosis is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 131-133]
The rabies vaccine is used against rabies. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 131-133]
Rabies is caused by rabies virus. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 131-133]
The Salk vaccine is associated with polio. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 131-133]
Measles is caused by measles virus. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 131-133]
MMR is associated with measles. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 131-133]
Tetanus is caused by Clostridium tetani. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 131-133]
Tetanus toxoid is associated with tetanus. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 131-133]
xs: The incorrect statement is option **(3)**: **tetanus** is caused by **Clostridium tetani**, not Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
**Polio** — **Poliovirus**, **Salk vaccine**; **measles** — **Measles virus**, **MMR**; **rabies** — **rabies virus**, rabies vaccine.
xa: **Mycobacterium tuberculosis** causes **tuberculosis**; vaccine **BCG**.
**Tetanus toxoid** protects against tetanus.
**Louis Pasteur** is associated with the **rabies vaccine**.

116.s: Who is associated with cellular immunity and phagocytosis?
116.x: Élie Metchnikoff discovered phagocytosis and founded the idea of cellular immunity. Koch worked on TB and Pasteur on rabies.
116.tq: Recall the pioneers of immunology.
n: Elie Metchnikoff was associated with cellular immunity. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #71 · pp 133-135]
Elie Metchnikoff was associated with phagocytosis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #71 · pp 133-135]
Elie Metchnikoff was associated with immunology. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #71 · pp 133-135]
xs: **Elie Metchnikoff** is associated with **cellular immunity** and **phagocytosis** — option **(2)**.
**Robert Koch** — **tuberculosis**, **bacteriology**; **Louis Pasteur** — **rabies vaccine**; **Jonas Salk** — **polio vaccine**.
xa: **Karl Landsteiner** — **blood groups**.
**Edward Jenner** — **Father of Immunology**.
⚠ Koch is **not** the father of immunology.

117.s: Which one of the following is regarded as the first contact point in the primary healthcare tier?
117.x: The Sub Health Centre is the first contact point in the primary healthcare tier.
117.tq: Directly identify the facility associated with the stated function.
xs: The **Sub Health Centre** is the **first contact point** of the primary tier — option **(1)**.
The **PHC** is the referral unit for SHCs; the **CHC** (secondary tier) is the referral for PHCs; the **district hospital** is secondary tier.
xa: SHC norm: **5,000** people (plain) / **3,000** (hilly-tribal).
SHCs and PHCs were upgraded to **Health and Wellness Centres** from **2018**, now **Ayushman Arogya Mandirs**.
AAM-SHCs offer **106 drugs** and **14 diagnostics**.

117.s:
Consider the following statements about population norms for health facilities:
1. A Sub Health Centre covers 5,000 people in plain areas and 3,000 in hilly-tribal areas.
2. A Community Health Centre covers 1,20,000 people in plain areas and 80,000 in hilly-tribal areas.
3. An Urban PHC covers 25,000-30,000 people within a 10 km radius.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
117.x: Statement 1 is correct (SHC 5,000/3,000). Statement 2 is correct (CHC 1,20,000/80,000). Statement 3 is wrong: an Urban PHC covers 25,000-30,000 people within a 2-3 km radius, not 10 km. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses the CHC norm and the others include statement 3.
117.tq: SHC 5k/3k, PHC 30k/20k, CHC 1.2 lakh/80k; UPHC 25-30k within 2-3 km.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(4)**.
Statement 1 correct: **SHC** covers **5,000** (plain) / **3,000** (hilly-tribal).
Statement 2 correct: **CHC** covers **1,20,000** / **80,000**.
Statement 3 wrong: an **Urban PHC** covers **25,000-30,000** people within a **2-3 km** radius, not 10 km.
xa: **PHC** norm: **30,000** (plain) / **20,000** (hilly-tribal).
Norms are set by the **Indian Public Health Standards**; latest revision **IPHS 2022**.
The CHC is the **referral for PHCs**, with **OT and beds**.

117.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the primary healthcare tier:
1. The PHC functions as a referral centre for Sub Health Centres.
2. The population norm for a PHC is 30,000 in plain areas and 20,000 in hilly-tribal areas.
3. The PHC belongs to the secondary healthcare tier.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
117.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the PHC belongs to the primary tier.
117.tq: Find the statement that reverses the classification of a facility.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: the **PHC** is the **referral for SHCs**.
Statement 2 correct: PHC norm is **30,000** (plain) / **20,000** (hilly-tribal).
Statement 3 wrong: the PHC is in the **primary** tier; the **CHC** and district hospital form the secondary tier.
xa: India had **23,391 PHCs** as of Dec 2021 (PYQ key).
Some notes give **30,045 PHCs in 2019**, up from **725 in 1950-51** (including urban PHCs).
Kartar Singh (**1973**) had suggested **one PHC per 50,000** people.

117.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Platform)
A. Tele-MANAS
B. ONCONET
C. SeHAT

List-II (Primary focus)
1. Armed forces healthcare
2. Mental health
3. Cancer-centre connectivity

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
117.x: Tele-MANAS concerns mental health, ONCONET links cancer centres, and SeHAT serves the armed forces.
117.tq: Start with the sure platform-purpose pairs and eliminate inconsistent codes.
xs: The correct code is **A–2, B–3, C–1** — option **(1)**.
**Tele-MANAS** → **mental health**; **ONCONET** → **cancer-centre connectivity**; **SeHAT** → **armed forces**.
xa: ONCONET links **108 peripheral + 27 regional cancer centres**.
**eSanjeevani AAM** is hub-and-spoke; **eSanjeevani OPD** is patient-to-provider from home.
eSanjeevani developer: **C-DAC (Mohali)**.

117.s:
Consider the following statements about healthcare delivery in India:
1. The public health system is largely curative, with limited preventive and promotive care.
2. In cities, the private sector dominates secondary, tertiary and quaternary care.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
117.x: Statement 1 is correct: the public system is largely curative with limited preventive and promotive care (UPSC 2023 statement). Statement 2 is correct: the private sector dominates secondary, tertiary and quaternary care in cities. So 'Both'; '1 only' and '2 only' each reject a true statement, and 'Neither' rejects both.
117.tq: Public = curative-heavy; private = dominant in urban higher-tier care.
xs: **Both 1 and 2** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1 correct: the public system is **largely curative, with limited preventive and promotive care** (UPSC 2023).
Statement 2 correct: in cities the **private sector** dominates **secondary, tertiary and quaternary** care.
xa: Private sector: **over 60% of inpatient** and **about 70% of outpatient** care.
**NFHS-3**: private sector the main source for **70% of urban households**.
Average hospitalisation: **Rs 50,508** private vs **Rs 6,631** government.

117.s:
Arrange the following committees in chronological order of their reporting or recommendation period:
A. Shrivastava Committee
B. Bhore Committee
C. Kartar Singh Committee
D. Mudaliar Committee
117.x: The correct sequence is Bhore (1943–46), Mudaliar (1959–62), Kartar Singh (1973), and Shrivastava (1975).
117.tq: Fix the earliest and latest committees first, then arrange the middle two.
xs: The order is **B, D, C, A** — option **(1)**.
xa: Bhore: **three-tier PHC-based system**; integrated preventive and curative care.
Mudaliar: **consolidate PHCs** before expanding; strengthen district hospitals.
Kartar Singh: **multipurpose health workers**; Shrivastava: **village health guides** and **Referral Services Complex**.

117.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Committee)
a. Mudaliar Committee
b. Kartar Singh Committee
c. Shrivastava Committee
List-II (Recommendation)
i. Multipurpose health workers; one PHC per 50,000 people
ii. Community health volunteers or village health guides; Referral Services Complex
iii. Consolidate existing PHCs before expanding; strengthen district hospitals
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
117.x: Mudaliar (1959-62) asked to consolidate PHCs and strengthen district hospitals (iii); Kartar Singh (1973) recommended multipurpose workers and one PHC per 50,000 (i); Shrivastava (1975) recommended village health guides and a Referral Services Complex (ii). Only 'a-iii, b-i, c-ii' fits; the other codes swap at least two of these.
117.tq: Mudaliar = consolidate; Kartar Singh = multipurpose workers; Shrivastava = village health guides.
xs: The correct code is **a-iii, b-i, c-ii** — option **(1)**.
**Mudaliar** (**1959-62**) → **consolidate existing PHCs**, strengthen district hospitals (iii).
**Kartar Singh** (**1973**) → **multipurpose health workers**, **one PHC per 50,000** (i).
**Shrivastava** (**1975**) → **village health guides**, **Referral Services Complex** (ii).
xa: The earliest was the **Bhore Committee** (**1943-46**), appointed "to survey the state of public health".
Bhore recommended a **three-tier PHC-based system** with integrated preventive and curative care.
Current PHC norm: **30,000** (plain) / **20,000** (hilly-tribal).

117.s: The latest revision of the Indian Public Health Standards is:
117.x: IPHS 2022 is the latest revision stated for Indian Public Health Standards.
117.tq: Recall the latest revision year and avoid substituting a policy year.
xs: The latest revision of the Indian Public Health Standards is **IPHS 2022** — option **(3)**.
It sets norms for **SHC and HWC, PHC, CHC, sub-district and district hospitals**.
xa: AP's **UPHCs** were upgraded to **IPHS norms**: **92** are NQAS-certified.
**267** AP UPHCs scored above 70% for **Kayakalp**.

117.s:
Consider the following statements about Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (AAMs):
1. They were launched in 2018.
2. 1,50,000 Health and Wellness Centres were set up by December 2022 by upgrading SHCs and PHCs.
3. Fewer than 1 lakh AAMs are functioning in 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
117.x: Statement 1 is correct: launched in 2018. Statement 2 is correct: 1,50,000 HWCs by December 2022, later renamed AAMs. Statement 3 is wrong: more than 1.79 lakh AAMs are functioning in 2026. So '1 and 2 only'; the other options either omit a true statement or include statement 3.
117.tq: AAM: 2018 launch; 1.5 lakh by Dec 2022; 1.79 lakh+ now.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1 correct: launched in **2018**.
Statement 2 correct: **1,50,000** HWCs by **Dec 2022** by upgrading **SHCs and PHCs**, later renamed **Ayushman Arogya Mandirs**.
Statement 3 wrong: **more than 1.79 lakh** AAMs are functioning in **2026**.
xa: AAM-PHCs offer **172 drugs** and **63 diagnostics**; AAM-SHCs **106** and **14**.
Over **1.75 lakh AAMs** are linked to **eSanjeevani** (12 Jun 2026).
AP converted **10,032 sub-centres, 1,144 PHCs and 560 UPHCs** into AAMs (APSES 2024-25).

117.s: Under the Comprehensive Primary Health Care package at Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, NCD screening covers hypertension, diabetes and which cancers?
117.x: The CPHC package screens for hypertension, diabetes and the three common cancers: oral, breast and cervical. Lung, liver, stomach, blood, bone, skin, prostate, colon and pancreatic cancers are not part of the stated population-based screening.
117.tq: AAM cancer screening = oral, breast, cervical (the 'common three').
xs: NCD screening at AAMs covers **oral, breast and cervical cancer** besides hypertension and diabetes — option **(1)**.
The other cancer sets are not part of the CPHC NCD screening.
xa: CPHC also covers **mental health**, **ENT, eye, oral health**, **geriatric and palliative care**, **Yoga** and wellness.
**ONCONET** links **108** peripheral and **27** regional cancer centres.
AAM-PHCs: **172 drugs**, **63 diagnostics**.

117.s: Which of the following correctly describes human-resource challenges in rural healthcare?
o: The nurse ratio exceeds global norms and rural CHCs have no vacancies.
The nurse ratio is below global norms and specialist posts at rural CHCs have high vacancies.
Only urban CHCs face specialist vacancies.
Rural CHCs have surplus specialists and no nursing shortage.
117.x: The nurse ratio is below global norms, while specialist posts at rural CHCs have high vacancies.
117.tq: Identify the option that preserves both linked shortages.
xs: The **nurse ratio is below global norms** and **specialist posts at rural CHCs have high vacancies** — option **(2)**.
So the options claiming surplus specialists, no vacancies or urban-only vacancies are wrong.
xa: Doctor-population ratio about **1:834** vs **WHO norm 1:1000**, but doctors **cluster in cities**.
**Community workers** carry the heaviest workload.
"Urban concentration of doctors" is a listed criticism of India's health system.

117.s: eSanjeevani was developed by which organisation?
o: Indian Council of Medical Research, New Delhi
117.x: eSanjeevani was built by the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC), Mohali.
117.tq: Identify the correct technology agency rather than the health-sector organisation.
xs: **eSanjeevani** was developed by **C-DAC, Mohali** — option **(4)**.
ISRO, ICMR and NIC are not its developers.
xa: **eSanjeevani AAM**: provider-to-provider, **hub-and-spoke**; **eSanjeevani OPD**: patient-to-provider from home.
Network: **1,35,915 AAM spokes** + **17,893 hubs**.
Over **1.75 lakh AAMs** now linked (12 Jun 2026).

117.s: Which of the following correctly describes eSanjeevani AAM?
o: Teleconsultation exclusively for armed forces personnel
Patient-to-provider consultation from the patient's home
Mental-health counselling through a national helpline
Provider-to-provider consultation through a hub-and-spoke model
117.x: eSanjeevani AAM provides provider-to-provider teleconsultation through a hub-and-spoke model.
117.tq: Separate the two eSanjeevani variants by user relationship and service setting.
xs: **eSanjeevani AAM** is **provider-to-provider** teleconsultation through a **hub-and-spoke model** — option **(4)**.
**Patient-to-provider from home** is **eSanjeevani OPD**; armed-forces teleconsultation is **SeHAT**.
xa: Developer: **C-DAC (Mohali)**.
**1,35,915 AAM spokes** and **17,893 hubs**.
**ONCONET** links **108** peripheral and **27** regional cancer centres.

117.s:
Consider the following statements about India's doctor-population ratio:
1. The ratio for NMC-registered allopathic doctors is about 1:834.
2. The WHO norm it is compared with is 1:1000.
3. Real availability of doctors is higher than this ratio suggests because doctors are spread evenly across rural areas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
117.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: about 1:834 against the WHO norm of 1:1000. Statement 3 is wrong: real availability is lower, because doctors cluster in cities. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' omits the WHO norm and the options with 3 are wrong.
117.tq: 1:834 looks better than 1:1000, but urban clustering lowers real access.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: about **1:834** (NMC-registered allopathic doctors).
Statement 2 correct: compared with the **WHO norm of 1:1000**.
Statement 3 wrong: real availability is **lower**, because doctors **cluster in cities**.
xa: **Nurse** ratio is below global norms; **specialist vacancies** are high at rural CHCs.
**Community workers** carry the heaviest workload.
About **70%** of health infrastructure is urban, serving only **30%** of the population.

117.s: According to NFHS-3, the private sector was the main source of care for what proportion of urban households?
117.x: NFHS-3 reported that the private sector was the main source of care for 70% of urban households.
117.tq: Recall the survey-linked percentage without confusing it with other health-sector shares.
xs: **NFHS-3**: the private sector was the main source of care for **70% of urban households** — option **(3)** (PYQ).
In cities the private sector dominates **secondary, tertiary and quaternary** care.
xa: Private sector today: **over 60% of inpatient** and **about 70% of outpatient** care.
⚠ Don't confuse with the urban skew: **70%** of infrastructure in urban areas holding **30%** of population.
Average hospitalisation: **Rs 50,508** private vs **Rs 6,631** government.

117.s: Approximately what proportion of health infrastructure is located in urban areas, which contain what proportion of the population?
117.x: About 70% of health infrastructure is in urban areas, which contain only 30% of the population.
117.tq: Identify the reversed infrastructure-population distribution trap.
xs: About **70%** of health infrastructure is in **urban areas**, which hold only **30%** of the population — option **(4)**.
Option (1) reverses the figures.
xa: **Urban concentration of doctors** is a listed criticism; the doctor ratio is **1:834** vs WHO **1:1000**.
⚠ **NFHS-3**: private sector = main source for **70% of urban households** — a different 70%.
**Missing middle**: over **40 crore** people without cover.

117.s: According to the stated figures, the number of PHCs as of December 2021 was:
117.x: The stated December 2021 figure is 23,391 PHCs.
117.tq: Distinguish the dated count from the historical and alternative counts.
xs: India had **23,391 PHCs** as of **Dec 2021** — option **(3)** (PYQ key).
**725** was the count in **1950-51**; **30,045** is a **2019** figure that includes urban PHCs.
**11,086** is the number of **Sub Centres in AP**.
xa: PHC norm: **30,000** (plain) / **20,000** (hilly-tribal).
Urban PHCs cover **25,000-30,000** people within **2-3 km**.
AP has **1,293 rural** and **559 urban PHCs**.

117.s: The Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY), intended to establish AIIMS-like institutions and upgrade government medical colleges, was launched in which year?
117.x: PMSSY was launched in 2003. Its two major objectives are the establishment of AIIMS-like institutions and the upgradation of government medical colleges.
117.tq: Use the year-based numerical distinction among closely spaced options.
xs: **PMSSY** was launched in **2003** — option **(2)**.
It builds **AIIMS-like institutions** and **upgrades government medical colleges**.
xa: AP's AIIMS is **AIIMS Mangalagiri** — a telemedicine anchor with over **2,500 OPD** patients a day.
**PM-JAY**: **Rs 5 lakh per family per year** to **12 crore families**.
Dental colleges in **2024-25**: **319 BDS** and **281 MDS**.

117.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the AIIMS serving Andhra Pradesh?
117.x: AIIMS Mangalagiri is the AIIMS institution associated with Andhra Pradesh.
117.tq: Discriminate among nearby place-based institutional names.
xs: AP's AIIMS is **AIIMS Mangalagiri** — option **(4)**.
It is AP's **telemedicine anchor**, seeing **over 2,500 OPD** patients a day.
xa: AIIMS-like institutions come under **PMSSY (2003)**.
Other AP specialty centre: **Kidney Research Centre and Super Specialty Hospital, Palasa, Srikakulam**.
Greyfield super-specialty blocks: **Anantapur, Nellore and Eluru** (Feb 2026).

117.s: Under PM-JAY, the annual health cover provided per family is:
117.x: PM-JAY provides health cover of Rs 5 lakh per family per year.
117.tq: Recall the scheme amount by separating it from other plausible insurance figures.
xs: **PM-JAY** gives **Rs 5 lakh per family per year** — option **(4)**.
It covers **12 crore families**.
xa: Criticism: a **"missing middle"** of over **40 crore** people without cover.
Average hospitalisation: **Rs 50,508** private vs **Rs 6,631** government.
AP's **Sanjeevani** digital health programme issues **ABHA IDs**.

117.s: Which institution functions as the telemedicine anchor in Andhra Pradesh and has over 2,500 out-patients a day?
117.x: AIIMS Mangalagiri is the telemedicine anchor and has over 2,500 OPD patients a day.
117.tq: Match the institution with its distinctive service role and patient figure.
xs: **AIIMS Mangalagiri** is AP's **telemedicine anchor**, with over **2,500 OPD** patients a day — option **(4)**.
**Palasa** hosts the Kidney Research Centre; **Eluru** and **Nellore** are greyfield block sites.
xa: AIIMS-like institutions are built under **PMSSY (2003)**.
**eSanjeevani** (by **C-DAC Mohali**) is the national telemedicine platform.
AP's **Sanjeevani** programme integrates telemedicine with 104 and 108.

117.s: With reference to Andhra Pradesh's emergency and mobile health services, which statement is correct?
o: 104 is the emergency ambulance service and 108 is the advisory service.
104 is a specialty hospital network and 108 is a telemedicine platform.
108 is the emergency ambulance service, while 104 is the mobile medical unit and health advisory service.
Both 104 and 108 are emergency ambulance services.
117.x: The 108 service provides emergency ambulances, whereas 104 provides mobile medical units and health advisory services.
117.tq: Discriminate between two easily reversed service numbers.
xs: **108** is the **emergency ambulance** service; **104** is the **mobile medical unit and health advisory service** — option **(3)**.
Option (1) swaps them; neither is a specialty hospital network or telemedicine platform.
xa: AP's **Sanjeevani** programme (from **Aug 2026**) integrates **104, 108, e-Aushadhi** and telemedicine.
It also issues **ABHA IDs**.
AP angle also includes **Village Health Clinics**, **Palasa** and **AIIMS Mangalagiri**.

117.s: Which of the following is a feature of Andhra Pradesh's Sanjeevani digital health programme, rolled out from August 2026?
o: It provides only cancer treatment through ONCONET.
It replaces all village health clinics with AIIMS institutions.
It is restricted to armed forces personnel through SeHAT.
It issues ABHA IDs and integrates 104, 108, e-Aushadhi and telemedicine.
117.x: The programme issues ABHA IDs and integrates the 104 and 108 services, e-Aushadhi and telemedicine. The other options wrongly assign functions of separate platforms or make unsupported claims.
117.tq: Identify the option that combines the programme's stated functions without importing another platform's role.
xs: AP's **Sanjeevani** programme **issues ABHA IDs** and **integrates 104, 108, e-Aushadhi and telemedicine** — option **(4)**.
**ONCONET** is the cancer network and **SeHAT** the armed-forces platform — not Sanjeevani.
xa: It runs from **Aug 2026** (26 Jul 2026).
**108** = emergency ambulance; **104** = mobile medical unit + health advisory.
⚠ **eSanjeevani** (by **C-DAC Mohali**) is the national telemedicine platform, distinct from AP's Sanjeevani.

117.s: The Bhore Committee was appointed primarily to:
o: Survey the state of public health
117.x: The Bhore Committee was appointed to survey the state of public health.
117.tq: Match a committee with its stated mandate, not merely its broad sector.
xs: The **Bhore Committee** (Health Survey and Development) was appointed **"to survey the state of public health"** — option **(2)**.
**Multipurpose health workers** were the **Kartar Singh Committee's** (**1973**) idea; **village health guides** came from **Shrivastava** (**1975**).
**Consolidating existing PHCs** before expansion was the **Mudaliar Committee's** (**1959-62**) advice.
xa: The Bhore Committee worked in **1943-46**.
It recommended **integrated preventive and curative care** and a **three-tier PHC-based system**.
Kartar Singh also set the norm of **one PHC per 50,000** people.

117.s: The Kidney Research Centre and Super Specialty Hospital mentioned in relation to Andhra Pradesh is located at:
117.x: The Kidney Research Centre and Super Specialty Hospital is located at Palasa in Srikakulam.
117.tq: Use the location-specific hospital association.
xs: The **Kidney Research Centre and Super Specialty Hospital** is at **Palasa, Srikakulam** — option **(3)** (PYQ).
**Anantapur** and **Eluru** are greyfield super-specialty block sites; **Mangalagiri** has AIIMS.
xa: **AIIMS Mangalagiri** is the telemedicine anchor with over **2,500 OPD** patients a day.
Greyfield blocks: **Anantapur, Nellore and Eluru** (Feb 2026).
AP has **9 District Hospitals** and **54 Area Hospitals**.

117.s: Which of the following is identified as a major criticism or concern in India's healthcare system?
o: Excessive coverage of the missing middle and equal distribution of doctors
Low out-of-pocket expenditure and rural concentration of doctors
Absence of any public healthcare infrastructure and universal insurance coverage
High out-of-pocket expenditure, a missing middle of over 40 crore people without cover, and urban concentration of doctors
117.x: The stated concerns are high out-of-pocket expenditure, more than 40 crore people forming a 'missing middle' without cover, and the urban concentration of doctors.
117.tq: Reject options that reverse the direction of the stated healthcare problems.
xs: The criticisms are **high out-of-pocket expenditure**, a **missing middle** of over **40 crore** people without cover and **urban concentration of doctors** — option **(4)**.
The other options invert these (low OOPE, rural concentration, no public infrastructure).
xa: Older notes put **OOPE** at about **47-48%**.
**PM-JAY** covers **Rs 5 lakh per family per year** for **12 crore families**.
About **70%** of health infrastructure is urban, serving **30%** of the population.

118.s:
Consider the following statements regarding mortality indicators:
1. Neonatal Mortality Rate (NMR) counts deaths in the first 28 days of life per 1,000 live births.
2. Under-Five Mortality Rate (U5MR) is expressed per 1,00,000 live births.
3. Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) is expressed per 1,00,000 live births.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
118.x: Statement 1 is correct: NMR covers the first 28 days, per 1,000 live births. Statement 2 is wrong: U5MR, like IMR, uses a base of 1,000 live births. Statement 3 is correct: MMR alone uses 1,00,000 live births. Hence '1 and 3 only'; options with 2 are wrong and '1 only' misses 3.
118.tq: Only MMR uses the 1,00,000 base; IMR, NMR and U5MR all use 1,000.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **NMR** = deaths in the first **28 days** per **1,000** live births.
Statement 2 wrong: **U5MR** uses a base of **1,000** live births, like IMR.
Statement 3 correct: **MMR** is per **1,00,000 live births**.
xa: India's MMR: **97** (SRS 2018-20); AP's MMR: **45**.
U5MR: India **32**, AP **27** (SRS 2020); SDG target **< 25**.

118.s: According to the SRS 2023 figure cited for the latest estimates, India’s IMR was
118.x: The IMR was 25 according to SRS 2023, as cited in the Economic Survey 2025-26. The figures 28 and 35.2 refer to older or different sources.
118.tq: Match the latest year with the correct numerical value rather than using a stale estimate.
xs: India's IMR was **25** as per **SRS 2023** (ES 2025-26) — option **(2)**.
**28** is the stale **SRS 2020** figure; **35.2** is the **NFHS-5** survey value; **24** is **AP's** IMR (SRS 2020).
xa: IMR = infant deaths under 1 year per **1,000 live births**.
**Kerala** has the lowest IMR thanks to adequate basic health and education facilities.

118.s: As per SRS 2018-20, India's Maternal Mortality Ratio (maternal deaths per 1,00,000 live births) was:
118.x: India's MMR was 97 per 1,00,000 live births in SRS 2018-20. 25 is India's IMR (SRS 2023), which is per 1,000 live births; 45 is Andhra Pradesh's MMR; 130 is not the SRS 2018-20 figure.
118.tq: MMR 97 per lakh; IMR 25 per thousand: watch the base.
xs: India's **MMR** was **97** per 1,00,000 live births (**SRS 2018-20**) — option **(1)**.
**25** is India's **IMR** (SRS 2023, per 1,000 live births); **45** is **AP's MMR**.
xa: MMR is the only indicator here on a **1,00,000 live births** base.
**Telangana (2026)**: **MMR 43**.
AP beats national averages on IMR (**24**), MMR (**45**) and TFR (**1.5**) (APSES 2024-25).

118.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India’s IMR trend:
1. IMR was 40 in 2013.
2. IMR was 39 in 2014.
3. IMR was 37 in 2015.
4. IMR was 34 in 2016.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: The reported IMR values were 40, 39, 37 and 34 for 2013, 2014, 2015 and 2016 respectively.
118.tq: Check each year-value pair independently before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All four — **1, 2, 3 and 4** — are correct — option **(4)** (PYQ marked all four pairs correct).
xa: ⚠ The older **28 (SRS 2020)** figure is now stale.
Exam angle: year → IMR value matching, and per-1,000 vs per-1,00,000 base.

118.s:
Consider the following statements regarding SRS abridged life tables for 2016–20:
1. India’s male life expectancy was 68.6 years.
2. India’s female life expectancy was 71.4 years.
3. Andhra Pradesh’s male life expectancy was 69.1 years.
4. Andhra Pradesh’s female life expectancy was 72.2 years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: All four statements correctly state the SRS abridged life-table values for India and Andhra Pradesh during 2016–20.
118.tq: Verify each sex-state-value combination before selecting the complete code.
xs: All four — **1, 2, 3 and 4** — are correct — option **(4)**.
**India**: males **68.6**, females **71.4**; **AP**: males **69.1**, females **72.2** (SRS abridged life tables 2016-20, APSES 2024-25).
xa: Women live **~3 years** longer than men.
Life expectancy rose from **49.7 years (1973)** to **70.3 years (2023)**.
At Independence it was about **32 years**.

118.s: Which State is credited with having the lowest IMR owing to adequate basic health and education facilities?
118.x: Kerala has the lowest IMR, attributed to adequate basic health and education facilities.
118.tq: Use the state-specific association rather than confusing it with AP or Telangana figures.
xs: **Kerala** has the lowest IMR owing to **adequate basic health and education facilities** — option **(2)** (APPSC 2025 PYQ).
**Madhya Pradesh** is noted for high child wasting and underweight in NFHS-6.
xa: **Telangana (2026)**: **MMR 43, IMR 18, TFR 1.5**; **99.9%** institutional deliveries.
India's latest IMR: **25** (SRS 2023).

118.s: At the time of Independence, life expectancy in India was approximately
118.x: Life expectancy at Independence was approximately 32 years.
118.tq: Identify the historical baseline rather than a later SRS life-table value.
xs: Life expectancy at Independence was about **32 years** — option **(1)** (APPSC 2023 PYQ).
**49.7** was the **1973** level; **70.3** the **2023** level; **68.3** the older SRS 2011-15 figure.
xa: SRS 2016-20: India **68.6** (males), **71.4** (females).
Women live **~3 years** longer.

118.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, India's life expectancy rose from 49.7 years in 1973 to how many years in 2023?
118.x: Life expectancy rose from 49.7 years (1973) to 70.3 years (2023). 68.3 years is the older SRS 2011-15 figure; 72.2 years is AP's female life expectancy in SRS 2016-20; 32 years was the level at Independence.
118.tq: 32 at Independence, 49.7 in 1973, 70.3 in 2023.
xs: Life expectancy rose from **49.7 years (1973)** to **70.3 years (2023)** — option **(1)** (ES 2025-26).
**68.3** is the older **SRS 2011-15** figure; **72.2** is AP's **female** figure (2016-20); **32** was the level at Independence.
xa: SRS 2016-20: India males **68.6**, females **71.4**.
AP: males **69.1**, females **72.2**.
Women live **~3 years** longer.

118.s: Which one of the following pairs relating to Andhra Pradesh health indicators is correctly matched?
118.x: Andhra Pradesh has an MMR of 45 and an IMR of 24, both better than the corresponding national averages.
118.tq: Keep the two similarly abbreviated mortality indicators in their correct order.
xs: AP's **MMR — 45; IMR — 24** — option **(2)**.
Option (3) swaps them; **29.3%** is NFHS-6 stunting.
xa: AP beats national averages on IMR, MMR, **TFR (1.5)** and life expectancy (APSES 2024-25).
AP U5MR **27** vs India **32**; AP crude birth rate **15.7** vs **19.5**.

118.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (NFHS Round)
a. NFHS-1
b. NFHS-2
c. NFHS-3
d. NFHS-4

List-II (Year)
i. 2005-06
ii. 1992-93
iii. 2015-16
iv. 1998-99
118.x: NFHS-1 was conducted in 1992-93, NFHS-2 in 1998-99, NFHS-3 in 2005-06 and NFHS-4 in 2015-16.
118.tq: Start with the sure earliest and latest pairs, then complete the middle matches.
xs: The correct code is **a–ii, b–iv, c–i, d–iii** — option **(1)**.
xa: **NFHS-5**: **2019-21**; **NFHS-6**: scheduled **2023-24**, results released **2026**.
Conducted by **MoHFW**; nodal agency **IIPS, Mumbai**.
Exam angle: round → year matching.

118.s: NFHS is conducted under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, with which institution serving as the nodal agency?
o: Indian Council of Medical Research, Hyderabad
International Institute for Population Sciences, Mumbai
118.x: NFHS is conducted under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and the International Institute for Population Sciences (IIPS), Mumbai, is the nodal agency.
118.tq: Apply the institutional-authority trap by distinguishing the conducting ministry from the nodal agency.
xs: The nodal agency for NFHS is the **International Institute for Population Sciences (IIPS), Mumbai** — option **(2)**.
The survey is conducted under the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW)**.
xa: Rounds: NFHS-1 **1992-93** … NFHS-5 **2019-21**; NFHS-6 results released **2026**.
Coverage: maternal and child health, mortality, nutrition, immunisation, fertility, family planning, women's empowerment, sanitation and drinking water.
⚠ NFHS gives **no single overall "malnutrition %"**.

118.s: According to NFHS-5, which statement regarding sex ratio is correct?
o: The overall sex ratio was 1020; the rural ratio was 1,037 and the urban ratio was 985.
The overall sex ratio was 920, with the rural ratio lower than the urban ratio.
The overall sex ratio was 985; the rural ratio was 1,020 and the urban ratio was 1,037.
The overall sex ratio was 1,037, while both rural and urban ratios were below 1,000.
118.x: NFHS-5 reported an overall sex ratio of 1020, with 1,037 in rural areas and 985 in urban areas. The figure 920 refers to the child sex ratio mentioned separately.
118.tq: Avoid the confusable-pair trap between overall sex ratio and child sex ratio, and compare rural with urban values correctly.
xs: NFHS-5 sex ratio: **1020** overall; **rural 1,037**, **urban 985** — option **(1)**.
**920** is the **child sex ratio (CSR)** in NFHS-5, not the overall ratio.
xa: 1020 was the **first time more women than men**.
**Census 2011 CSR**: **918** final; older notes quote provisional **914**.
NFHS-5 was conducted in **2019-21**.

118.s:
Consider the following statements about State-level nutrition findings in NFHS-6:
1. Madhya Pradesh recorded high child wasting and underweight.
2. Meghalaya recorded a rise in stunting.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
118.x: Statement 1 is correct: Madhya Pradesh showed high child wasting and underweight. Statement 2 is wrong: Meghalaya showed a decline, not a rise, in stunting. Hence '1 only'.
118.tq: MP = the bad extreme; Meghalaya = the stunting success story.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: **Madhya Pradesh** had **high child wasting and underweight** in NFHS-6.
Statement 2 wrong: **Meghalaya** saw a **decline in stunting**, not a rise.
xa: NFHS-6: stunting fell to **29.3%**; underweight stuck at **31.8%**.
NFHS-6 + Vellore cohort study: thinness and overweight rise sharply between **ages 7 and 9**.
Rising **double burden** is a 2026 concern.

118.s:
According to the WHO classification, malnutrition in all its forms includes:
1. Undernutrition, including wasting, stunting and underweight.
2. Inadequate vitamins and minerals.
3. Overweight, obesity and diet-related non-communicable diseases.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: WHO’s broad definition includes undernutrition, micronutrient inadequacy, and overnutrition with diet-related non-communicable diseases.
118.tq: Recognise the comprehensive definition instead of treating malnutrition as undernutrition alone.
xs: All three — **1, 2 and 3** — form WHO's "malnutrition in all its forms" — option **(4)**.
**Undernutrition** (wasting, stunting, underweight) + **inadequate vitamins/minerals** + **overweight/obesity** and diet-related NCDs.
xa: **Double burden** = undernutrition + overnutrition together.
**Triple burden (SOFI 2025)** = undernutrition + micronutrient deficiency/anaemia + overweight.
NFHS reports stunting, wasting and underweight **separately**.

118.s:
Consider the following statements about malnutrition burdens:
1. SOFI 2025 describes a 'triple burden' made up of wasting, stunting and underweight.
2. The 'double burden' is undernutrition and overnutrition occurring together.
3. A Vellore cohort study found thinness and overweight rising sharply between ages 7 and 9.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
118.x: Statement 1 is wrong: SOFI 2025's triple burden is undernutrition + micronutrient deficiency/anaemia + overweight; wasting, stunting and underweight are all forms of undernutrition. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is correct: thinness and overweight rise sharply between ages 7 and 9. Hence '2 and 3 only'.
118.tq: Triple burden = under + micronutrient/anaemia + overweight.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — option **(3)** **2 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 wrong: **SOFI 2025** triple burden = **undernutrition** + **micronutrient deficiency/anaemia** + **overweight**.
Statement 2 correct: **double burden** = **undernutrition + overnutrition** together.
Statement 3 correct: the **Vellore cohort** found thinness and overweight rising sharply between **ages 7 and 9**.
xa: WHO: malnutrition in all its forms includes **undernutrition** (wasting, stunting, underweight).
SOFI 2025: India's wasting rate **18.7%** (**21 million** children) — world's highest.
⚠ NFHS gives **no single overall "malnutrition %"**.

118.s:
Consider the following statements about child-nutrition indicators:
1. Stunting is low height-for-age.
2. Wasting is low weight-for-age.
3. Underweight is low weight-for-age.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
118.x: Statement 1 is correct: stunting is low height-for-age (more than 2 SD below the WHO median). Statement 2 is wrong: wasting is low weight-for-height. Statement 3 is correct: underweight is low weight-for-age. Hence '1 and 3 only'.
118.tq: Stunting = height/age; wasting = weight/height; underweight = weight/age.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)** **1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **stunting** = low **height-for-age** (> **2 SD** below WHO median).
Statement 2 wrong: **wasting** = low **weight-for-height**.
Statement 3 correct: **underweight** = low **weight-for-age**.
xa: Wasting (NFHS-5): **19.3%**; severe wasting **5.2%** in NFHS-6.
Underweight barely moved: **32.1%** → **31.8%**.

118.s: Which of the following correctly presents the NFHS-5 and NFHS-6 figures for underweight children?
118.x: Underweight declined from 32.1% in NFHS-5 to 31.8% in NFHS-6. The 35.8% figure belongs to NFHS-4.
118.tq: Track both survey round and indicator before choosing the pair.
xs: Underweight: **32.1%** (NFHS-5) and **31.8%** (NFHS-6) — option **(2)**.
**35.5% / 29.3%** are **stunting**; **35.8%** is the **NFHS-4** underweight figure; **19.3%** is wasting and **5.2%** severe wasting.
xa: Underweight **barely moved** in NFHS-6.
NFHS-5: underweight highest among **STs (44.1%)** and **SCs (39.1%)**, higher in rural areas.
Underweight = low **weight-for-age**.

118.s: According to NFHS-5, anaemia affected approximately what proportions of children aged 6–59 months and women aged 15–49 years respectively?
118.x: NFHS-5 reported anaemia among 67.1% of children aged 6–59 months and 57.0% of women aged 15–49 years.
118.tq: Keep the age group and percentage in the same order as asked.
xs: NFHS-5 anaemia: **children 6-59 months 67.1%**, **women 15-49 57.0%** — option **(4)**.
**41%** is the share of women with **10+ years of schooling**, not anaemia.
xa: **Anemia Mukt Bharat** (2018) uses a **6x6x6** strategy.
Fortified rice carries **iron, folic acid, vitamin B12**.
AP's **Anna Amrutha Hastam** gives **iron and folic acid tablets** to pregnant and lactating women.

118.s: Underweight prevalence was highest among which of the following social groups according to NFHS-5?
o: Other Backward Classes, followed by Scheduled Tribes
Scheduled Tribes, followed by Scheduled Castes
Scheduled Castes, followed by Scheduled Tribes
Urban households, followed by rural households
118.x: Underweight was highest among Scheduled Tribes at 44.1%, followed by Scheduled Castes at 39.1%. It was also higher in rural areas.
118.tq: Rank the groups using the reported percentages rather than merely identifying both groups.
xs: Underweight was highest among **Scheduled Tribes (44.1%)**, followed by **Scheduled Castes (39.1%)** — option **(2)** (NFHS-5).
It was **higher in rural** areas, so option (4) is wrong.
xa: National underweight: **32.1%** (NFHS-5) → **31.8%** (NFHS-6).
NFHS-4 underweight: **35.8%**.
Underweight = low **weight-for-age**.

118.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with respect to NFHS-5 and NFHS-6 findings for children under five years?
118.x: Stunting fell from 35.5% in NFHS-5 to 29.3% in NFHS-6. Options A and D reverse the order of the underweight (32.1% → 31.8%) and severe-wasting (7.7% → 5.2%) figures, and the breastfeeding figures in C are not among the stated NFHS findings.
118.tq: Check the direction of change and reject reversed pairs.
xs: **Stunting: 35.5% and 29.3%** is correct — option **(2)**.
Option (1) reverses underweight (**32.1% → 31.8%**); option (4) reverses severe wasting (**7.7% → 5.2%**).
The breastfeeding figures in option (3) are not among the stated NFHS findings.
xa: Stunting = low **height-for-age**, > **2 SD** below WHO median.
Stunting fell **~17%** in NFHS-6.
**Meghalaya** saw a decline in stunting.

118.s:
Consider the following NFHS-5 figures linked to child nutrition:
1. About 41% of women had 10 or more years of schooling.
2. About 41% of women were married before the age of 18.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
118.x: Statement 1 is correct: 41% of women had 10+ years of schooling (NFHS-5). Statement 2 is wrong: the share married before 18 was 23.3%, not 41%. Hence '1 only'.
118.tq: 41% = schooling 10+ years; 23.3% = child marriage.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: **41%** of women had **10+ years of schooling** (NFHS-5).
Statement 2 wrong: **23.3%** were married before **18**, not 41%.
xa: Sanitation and drinking water are also tracked WASH factors.
Main driver of malnutrition: **poor dietary habits and food insecurity**.
Anaemia among women **15-49**: **57.0%**.

118.s:
Consider the following statements about POSHAN Abhiyaan:
1. It was launched in 2018 under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
2. It aims to reduce stunting, wasting, anaemia and low birth weight.
3. It works through convergence of ICDS, the National Health Mission and Swachh Bharat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
118.x: Statement 1 is wrong: POSHAN Abhiyaan (2018) is under the Ministry of Women and Child Development, not Health. Statement 2 is correct: it targets stunting, wasting, anaemia and low birth weight. Statement 3 is correct: it rests on convergence of ICDS, NHM and Swachh Bharat. Hence '2 and 3 only'.
118.tq: POSHAN Abhiyaan = National Nutrition Mission = WCD ministry, not MoHFW.
xs: Statements **2 and 3 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 wrong: **POSHAN Abhiyaan** (**2018**) is under the Ministry of **Women & Child Development**.
Statement 2 correct: it targets **stunting, wasting, anaemia and low birth weight**.
Statement 3 correct: **convergence of ICDS, NHM and Swachh Bharat**.
xa: It is also called the **National Nutrition Mission**.
The **8th Poshan Pakhwada** was held in **2026**.
**Anemia Mukt Bharat** was also launched in **2018**.

118.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the six services provided through Anganwadi Services?
118.x: The six services include supplementary nutrition, pre-school education, nutrition and health education, immunisation, health check-up and referral services. Old-age pension distribution is not one of them.
118.tq: Locate the option that does not belong to the programme’s fixed list of six services.
xs: **Old-age pension distribution** is not an Anganwadi service — option **(4)**.
The **six services**: **supplementary nutrition**, **pre-school education**, nutrition & health education, immunisation, health check-up and **referral**.
xa: Beneficiaries: children **6 months-6 years**, pregnant and lactating women.
**2.9 lakh** AWCs co-located with schools (3 Sep 2025).
**POSHAN Abhiyaan** converges ICDS with NHM and Swachh Bharat.

118.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Vitamin B3 deficiency
(b) Vitamin K deficiency
(c) Iron deficiency
(d) Iodine deficiency

List-II
(i) Pellagra
(ii) Bleeding
(iii) Anaemia
(iv) Goitre
118.x: Lack of B3 causes pellagra, vitamin K bleeding, iron anaemia and iodine goitre, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
118.tq: Recall the deficiency disease of each nutrient.
n: Vitamin B3 deficiency causes Pellagra. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 45-46]
Vitamin K deficiency causes bleeding. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 45-46]
Iron deficiency causes anaemia. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 45-46]
Iodine deficiency causes goitre. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 45-46]
xs: The correct match is **a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv** — option **(1)**.
**Vitamin B3** — **pellagra**; **vitamin K** — **bleeding**.
**Iron** — **anaemia**; **iodine** — **goitre**.
xa: **Vitamin B1** — **beri-beri**; **vitamin B12** — **pernicious anaemia**.
**Vitamin C** — **scurvy**; **vitamin D** — **rickets**.
**Protein** — **kwashiorkor**; **energy and protein** — **marasmus**.

118.s: Which of the following correctly describes the beneficiaries of Anganwadi Services under ICDS?
o: Only children below six months of age
Only elderly persons and persons with disabilities
Children aged six months to six years, and pregnant and lactating women
Only school-going children aged six to fourteen years
118.x: Anganwadi Services cover children from six months to six years and pregnant and lactating women.
118.tq: Distinguish the programme’s target groups from beneficiaries of school or social-security schemes.
xs: **Anganwadi Services (ICDS)** cover **children 6 months-6 years** and **pregnant and lactating women** — option **(3)**.
School meals for older children come under **PM POSHAN**.
xa: ICDS provides **six services**: supplementary nutrition, pre-school education, nutrition & health education, immunisation, health check-up, referral.
**2.9 lakh** AWCs are co-located with schools (guidelines **3 Sep 2025**).
AP's **Anna Amrutha Hastam** works through Anganwadis.

118.s: The 6x6x6 strategy is associated with which programme?
o: Rice fortification under the Public Distribution System
118.x: Anemia Mukt Bharat uses a 6x6x6 strategy consisting of six interventions, six target groups and six institutional mechanisms.
118.tq: Discriminate between similarly themed nutrition programmes by their signature strategy.
xs: The **6x6x6** strategy belongs to **Anemia Mukt Bharat** — option **(3)**.
It means **6 interventions, 6 target groups, 6 institutional mechanisms**.
xa: Anemia Mukt Bharat was launched in **2018**.
NFHS-5 anaemia: children **67.1%**, women **57.0%**.
Rice fortification with **iron, folic acid, vitamin B12** is a separate measure.

118.s: Fortified rice supplied through the Public Distribution System, ICDS and PM POSHAN is fortified with:
o: Calcium, vitamin C and vitamin D
Iron, folic acid and vitamin B12
Iodine, zinc and vitamin A only
118.x: The specified fortified rice contains iron, folic acid and vitamin B12 and is supplied through the PDS, ICDS and PM POSHAN.
118.tq: Match the intervention with its exact micronutrient combination and delivery channels.
xs: Fortified rice carries **iron, folic acid and vitamin B12** — option **(3)**.
It is supplied through **PDS, ICDS and PM POSHAN**.
xa: **Anemia Mukt Bharat** (2018) follows the **6x6x6** strategy.
AP's **Anna Amrutha Hastam** adds **iron and folic acid tablets** to meals.
NFHS-5 anaemia among children 6-59 months: **67.1%**.

118.s: Which Andhra Pradesh scheme provides a nutritious meal along with iron and folic acid tablets to pregnant and lactating women through Anganwadis?
118.x: Anna Amrutha Hastam provides a nutritious meal and iron-folic acid tablets to pregnant and lactating women through Anganwadis.
118.tq: Match the scheme name with its specific beneficiary and service.
xs: **Anna Amrutha Hastam** (AP) gives a **nutritious meal** plus **iron and folic acid tablets** to **pregnant and lactating women** via **Anganwadis** — option **(3)** (APPSC 2019 PYQ).
**PMSMA, LaQshya, JSSK** are other maternal services listed in APSES 2024-25.
xa: Its aim: cut **infant and maternal mortality**.
**JSY** had **1,76,966** beneficiaries (Apr-Dec 2024).
Other services: **PMMVY, SUMAN, MCP cards**.

118.s: Which statement best describes the reporting of malnutrition in the National Family Health Survey?
o: NFHS reports one single overall malnutrition percentage for the country.
NFHS reports only wasting and excludes stunting and underweight.
NFHS reports malnutrition only for urban children.
NFHS reports stunting, wasting and underweight separately rather than providing one single overall malnutrition percentage.
118.x: NFHS reports stunting, wasting and underweight as separate indicators; it does not provide one single overall ‘malnutrition percentage’.
118.tq: Distinguish separate indicators from an aggregated figure that the survey does not provide.
xs: NFHS reports **stunting, wasting and underweight separately**, not one single overall malnutrition percentage — option **(4)**.
⚠ This is a flagged trap: there is **no single overall "malnutrition %"** (17 Mar 2026).
xa: Stunting = low **height-for-age**; wasting = low **weight-for-height**; underweight = low **weight-for-age**.
NFHS-5: stunting **35.5%**, wasting **19.3%**, underweight **32.1%**.
NFHS-6: stunting **29.3%**, underweight **31.8%**.

118.s: Food insecurity and poverty may contribute to both undernutrition and overnutrition because they can lead to consumption of
o: Only locally produced fruits and vegetables
118.x: Food insecurity and poverty can produce undernutrition while also encouraging consumption of inexpensive energy-dense, nutrient-poor foods that contribute to overnutrition.
118.tq: Apply the cause-effect relationship to a realistic dietary situation.
xs: Food insecurity and poverty lead to **energy-dense but nutrient-poor foods** — option **(2)**.
This causes **both under- and overnutrition**, plus **anaemia** and **cognitive delays**.
xa: The main driver of malnutrition: **poor dietary habits and food insecurity** (APPSC 2025 key).
**Poor maternal nutrition** impairs the child's **brain development**.
**Double burden** = undernutrition + overnutrition.

118.s: Which one of the following is regarded as the main driver of malnutrition in India?
o: Poor dietary habits and food insecurity
118.x: Poor dietary habits and food insecurity are the main driver of malnutrition (APPSC 2025 key). Fortified rice is a remedy, not a cause; women's schooling improves child nutrition; overuse of supplements is not cited as a driver.
118.tq: Malnutrition driver = poor diet + food insecurity.
xs: **Poor dietary habits and food insecurity** are the main driver — option **(1)** (APPSC 2025 key).
**Fortified rice** is a remedy (iron, folic acid, vitamin B12); **women's schooling** is a protective factor.
xa: Food insecurity & poverty → **energy-dense, nutrient-poor food**, anaemia, cognitive delays.
**Poor maternal nutrition** impairs the child's brain development.
Child marriage: **23.3%** married before 18.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about India's National Health Accounts (NHA):
1. They are prepared by the National Health Accounts Technical Secretariat (NHATS) under NHSRC.
2. They use the System of Health Accounts (SHA) 2008 framework.
3. They were first published for the year 2013-14.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
119.x: Statement 1 is correct: NHATS under NHSRC (MoHFW) prepares the NHA. Statement 2 is wrong: the framework is SHA 2011 (with NHA Guidelines 2016), not SHA 2008. Statement 3 is correct: the first NHA was for 2013-14. Hence '1 and 3 only'.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: NHA is prepared by **NHATS under NHSRC** (MoHFW).
Statement 2 wrong: it uses **SHA 2011** (+ NHA Guidelines **2016**), not SHA 2008.
Statement 3 correct: first published for **2013-14**.
xa: The latest is the **10th edition** for **2022-23** (May 2026).
OOPE share of THE: **64.2%** → **43.4%**.

119.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the trend in the government share of Total Health Expenditure (THE) in India?
o: It remained unchanged at 43.7% during both periods.
119.x: The government share of THE rose to 43.7%, compared with 28.6% in 2013–14.
119.tq: Read the direction of change before comparing the two percentages.
xs: The government share of THE **increased** from **28.6%** in **2013-14** to **43.7%** — option **(2)**.
**39.4%** is the OOPE share during COVID, not the government share.
xa: OOPE share fell from **64.2%** to **43.4%**.
**Social security expenditure** share rose from **6%** to **9.9%**.

119.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to health expenditure indicators?

 a. SHA 2011 — Base used for National Health Accounts estimates
 b. Government health expenditure — Highest during the COVID-19 period
 c. Household out-of-pocket expenditure — Fell during COVID-19 to 39.4% of THE
 d. Government share in 2013–14 — 43.7%
119.x: Pairs a, b and c are correctly matched. Pair d is incorrect: the government share in 2013–14 was 28.6%, whereas 43.7% refers to the later estimate.
119.tq: Check each pair against the associated base year, period and percentage.
xs: Pairs **a, b and c only** are correct — option **(2)**.
a correct: NHA uses **SHA 2011** as its base.
b correct: GHE was highest during COVID — **1.84% of GDP (2021-22)**.
c correct: OOPE **fell** during COVID to **39.4%** of THE.
d wrong: the government share in **2013-14** was **28.6%**; **43.7%** is the **2022-23** figure.
xa: NHA is prepared by **NHATS under NHSRC**, first for **2013-14**.

119.s: Which of the following correctly represents the trend in OOPE as a share of Total Health Expenditure between 2013–14 and 2022–23?
119.x: OOPE declined from 64.2% of Total Health Expenditure in 2013–14 to 43.4% in 2022–23, although it remained about half of current health expenditure.
119.tq: Reject the reversed trend and distinguish total health expenditure from current health expenditure.
xs: Option (4) reverses it; **28.6%** is the 2013-14 government share.
xa: OOPE is still about **50% of current health expenditure** (NHA 2022-23).
⚠ During COVID OOPE **fell** to **39.4%** of THE.

119.s:
In August 2026, Praja Arogya Vedika sought which combination of measures from the Andhra Pradesh Health Minister?

1. Enactment of a Right to Health Act
2. Withdrawal of public-private partnerships in government medical colleges
3. Reduction of public spending on primary care
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Praja Arogya Vedika sought a Right to Health Act and withdrawal of PPPs in government medical colleges. It did not seek reduction of public spending on primary care.
119.tq: Separate the two stated demands from the reversed policy position in statement 3.
xs: **1 and 2 only** — option **(3)**.
**Praja Arogya Vedika** (**Aug 2026**) asked for a **Right to Health Act** and **withdrawal of PPP in government medical colleges**.
It did not seek reduced spending on primary care — the reform view wants **more**.
xa: AP Health & FW budget 2024-25 BE: **₹18,732 Cr**.
AP flagship scheme: **Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva**.
**70%** of AP households have health coverage (2026).

119.s: Government Health Expenditure reached what percentage of GDP during the COVID peak in 2021–22?
119.x: GHE reached 1.84% of GDP during the COVID peak in 2021–22.
119.tq: Distinguish the exceptional COVID-year peak from the regular annual figures.
xs: GHE reached **1.84% of GDP** in **2021-22**, the **COVID peak** — option **(3)**.
xa: ⚠ OOPE **fell**, not rose, during COVID — to **39.4%** of THE.
Centre + States spent about **1.3% of GDP** in **2019-20** (Economic Survey 2021-22).

119.s: Which of the following statements regarding the National Health Policy, 2017 target is correct?
o: It targeted GHE of 2.5% of GDP by 2022, with the Centre contributing 60%.
It targeted GHE of 1.5% of GDP by 2025, with the States contributing 40%.
It targeted GHE of 2.5% of GDP by 2025, with the Centre contributing 40% of public spending.
It targeted GHE of 3% of GDP by 2030, with no specified Centre share.
119.x: NHP 2017 targeted Government Health Expenditure of 2.5% of GDP by 2025, with the Centre’s share intended to be 40% of public spending. The target was missed.
119.tq: Match the target year, percentage and Centre-share provision precisely.
xs: **NHP 2017** targeted GHE of **2.5% of GDP by 2025**, with the **Centre's share 40%** of public spending — option **(3)**.
The target was **missed** (30 Jan 2026).
xa: The Centre now spends only **~0.29% of GDP**.
GHE stood at **1.43%** of GDP in **2022-23**.
NHA 2022-23 and the parliamentary panel on the **'missing middle'** both confirm the target is unmet.

119.s: The 15th Finance Commission recommended health grants of approximately what amount through local governments for the period 2021–2026?
119.x: The 15th Finance Commission recommended health grants amounting to ₹70,051 crore through local governments for 2021–2026.
119.tq: Use the exact figure and period to eliminate nearby numerical distractors.
xs: The **15th Finance Commission** gave **₹70,051 crore** of health grants through **local governments** for **2021-26** — option **(3)**.
The grants go to local bodies for primary-level and block-level health infrastructure.
xa: Components: **diagnostic infrastructure** for sub-centres/PHCs and **block public health units**.
Also **urban health and wellness centres**.
And **buildings for building-less SCs/PHCs/CHCs**.

119.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the health grants recommended by the 15th Finance Commission:
1. They are routed through local governments.
2. They include provision for buildings for building-less SCs, PHCs and CHCs.
3. They are intended only for urban health and wellness centres.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the grants cover several components, including rural and block-level infrastructure as well as urban health and wellness centres.
119.tq: Reject the restrictive word ‘only’ by checking the complete list of components.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: the grants are routed through **local governments**.
Statement 2 correct: they fund **buildings for building-less SCs/PHCs/CHCs**.
Statement 3 wrong: they also cover **diagnostic infrastructure** and **block public health units**, not only urban HWCs.
xa: ⚠ NHP 2017 target (**2.5%** of GDP by **2025**) was missed.

119.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority:
1. NPPA was established in 1997.
2. It fixes ceiling prices of scheduled drugs.
3. The scheduled drugs are those included in the National List of Essential Medicines.
4. Its price-control function operates under the Drugs Price Control Order, 2013.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: All four statements are correct. NPPA, established in 1997, fixes ceiling prices for scheduled NLEM drugs under the Drugs Price Control Order, 2013.
119.tq: Verify the institution, year, regulated category and legal instrument separately.
xs: All four — **1, 2, 3 and 4** — are correct — option **(4)**.
**NPPA (1997)** fixes **ceiling prices** of **scheduled (NLEM)** drugs under the **Drugs Price Control Order, 2013**.
xa: **Free Drugs Service Initiative (NHM)**: free generic medicines; **DVDMS** handles procurement/inventory.
**Clinical Establishments Act 2010** adopted in only ~**11 states** and **6 UTs**.
Medicines are part of the **over 50%** of OOPE not covered by insurance.

119.s: The Clinical Establishments Act, cited as a regulation gap for private healthcare in India, was enacted in which year and has been adopted by roughly how many States/UTs?
119.x: The Clinical Establishments Act, 2010 has been adopted in only about 11 States and 6 UTs, which is why private-sector regulation remains a gap. It is not universally adopted; 2013 is the year of the Drugs Price Control Order and 2017 that of the National Health Policy.
119.tq: Clinical Establishments Act 2010: only ~11 States + 6 UTs.
xs: The **Clinical Establishments Act 2010** is adopted in only about **11 states and 6 UTs** — option **(1)**.
That is why private-sector **regulation** remains a gap.
⚠ **2013** is the year of the **Drugs Price Control Order**; **2017** of the National Health Policy.
xa: **NPPA** was set up in **1997**.
Hospitalisation OOP rose sharply, especially in **private hospitals** (NSS 80th round).
Private childbirth costs **₹37,630** vs **₹2,299** public.

119.s: Which of the following components account for over 50% of OOPE because they are generally not covered by insurance?
o: Only inpatient surgery and intensive care
Ambulance services and health education alone
119.x: Outpatient care, diagnostics and medicines account for over half of OOPE because insurance commonly does not cover them.
119.tq: Apply the coverage gap to identify the major sources of household spending.
