xs: **Outpatient care, diagnostics and medicines** are **over 50%** of OOPE — option **(4)**.
They are the uncovered costs; inpatient care is what insurance mainly covers.
xa: Chronic NCDs keep households paying: **diabetes 11.4%**, **hypertension 35.5%** of adults.
Private outpatient medicine bills are about **6 times** those at **Jan Aushadhi**.
Fix suggested: more spending on **primary care** + **OPD cover**.

119.s: The term “missing middle” in the context of health financing refers to:
o: More than 40 crore Indians lacking financial protection
People covered simultaneously by both public and private insurance
The middle-income group receiving free medicines at public facilities
Households whose insurance claims are pending for less than one month
119.x: The “missing middle” refers to more than 40 crore Indians who lack adequate financial protection; NITI Aayog first flagged the term.
119.tq: Match the distinctive policy term with its precise population description.
xs: The **"missing middle"** = **40 crore+** Indians lacking **financial protection** — option **(1)**.
**NITI Aayog** first flagged the term; the parliamentary panel used it on **4 Sep 2026**.
xa: NSS 80th round: insurance covers **47.4%** rural and **44.3%** urban households.
Childbirth OOP: **₹37,630** private vs **₹2,299** public (over **16x**).
Government-financed insurance rose **2.5-fold** (**2017-18** to **2025**).

119.s: Which of the following is regarded as a criticism of insurance-led health financing models?
o: They provide universal outpatient coverage in all circumstances.
They increase coverage without necessarily increasing the availability of care.
They reduce coverage while automatically increasing the quality of care.
They eliminate the need for primary healthcare expenditure.
119.x: A stated criticism is that insurance-led models may expand coverage without a corresponding increase in actual care. Greater spending on primary care and outpatient care is suggested as part of the corrective approach.
119.tq: Distinguish nominal financial coverage from actual access to healthcare.
xs: Insurance-led models **increase coverage without increasing care** — option **(2)**.
The suggested fix is more spending on **primary care** plus **OPD cover**.
xa: Outpatient care, diagnostics and medicines = **over 50%** of OOPE, mostly uncovered.
Government-financed insurance grew **2.5-fold** but OOPE still ~**50%** of current health expenditure.
**Missing middle**: **40 crore+** lack protection.

119.s: Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva, formerly known as YSR Aarogyasri, is primarily intended to provide which of the following?
o: Subsidised insurance exclusively for private-sector employees
Free crop insurance to small farmers
Pension support to retired government employees
Cashless health assurance to economically vulnerable families in Andhra Pradesh
119.x: Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva, earlier YSR Aarogyasri, is Andhra Pradesh’s flagship cashless health assurance scheme for economically vulnerable families.
119.tq: Directly identify the purpose of the flagship state scheme.
xs: **Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva** (earlier **YSR Aarogyasri**) is AP's flagship **cashless health assurance** for **economically vulnerable families** — option **(4)**.
It is not an employee-only, crop-insurance or pension scheme.
xa: It runs **in convergence with PM-JAY** (portability, wider empanelment).
**Mar 2026**: **five more critical cardiovascular procedures** added.
AP Budget 2024-25 BE: **₹4,000 Cr** for the Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva Trust.
AP households covered by all schemes: **70%**.

119.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship between Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva and PM-JAY in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva is restricted to government hospitals under PM-JAY.
PM-JAY replaced Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva completely in Andhra Pradesh.
The two schemes operate without any institutional relationship.
Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva is implemented in convergence with PM-JAY, enabling portability and wider empanelment.
119.x: The Andhra Pradesh scheme is implemented in convergence with PM-JAY, particularly providing portability and wider hospital empanelment.
119.tq: Test the functional relationship between two similar health-assurance schemes.
xs: **Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva** is implemented **in convergence with PM-JAY**, giving **portability and wider empanelment** — option **(4)**.
PM-JAY did not replace it, and it is not restricted to government hospitals.
xa: **2,700 private hospitals** are registered; **540** speciality.
Coverage also includes the **Employee Health Scheme**, RSBY, ESIS and CGHS.

119.s: According to the Economic Survey 2021–22 context, Centre and States together spent approximately what percentage of GDP on health in 2019–20?
119.x: Centre and States together spent about 1.3% of GDP on health in 2019–20.
119.tq: Recall the approximate combined public-spending figure rather than the NHP target.
xs: Centre + States spent about **1.3% of GDP** on health in **2019-20** — option **(2)** (Economic Survey 2021-22).
**2.5%** is the **NHP 2017** target; **1.84%** was the **2021-22** COVID peak.
xa: On the new GDP base: **1.48%**.
The Centre's own spending is **~0.29% of GDP**.

119.s: DVDMS is associated with which function in the public medicine-supply system?
o: Setting the list of essential surgical procedures
119.x: DVDMS manages drug procurement and inventory under the Free Drugs Service Initiative.
119.tq: Match the digital system with its operational function.
xs: **DVDMS** manages **drug procurement and inventory** — option **(2)**.
It works under the **Free Drugs Service Initiative (NHM)**, which provides free generic medicines at public facilities.
xa: **NPPA (1997)** fixes ceiling prices of scheduled (**NLEM**) drugs.
NPPA acts under the **Drugs Price Control Order, 2013**.
Private pharmacies dominate over **Jan Aushadhi**, with bills about **6 times** higher.

120.s: Which of the following is the correct chronological order of India’s National Health Policies?
120.x: India’s National Health Policies were issued in 1983, 2002 and 2017, in that order.
120.tq: Arrange policy years from earliest to latest, checking the middle year carefully.
xs: First **National Health Policy 1983** → **NHP 2002** (more public spending + bigger private/NGO role) → **NHP 2017** (assurance-based).
xa: **India Newborn Action Plan**: **2014**.
**National Policy for Rare Diseases**: **2021**.
NHP 2017 target: public health spending **2.5% of GDP by 2025** — missed (**1.43%** in 2022-23).

120.s: Which of the following best characterises the approach of the National Health Policy, 2017?
o: A private-sector-only approach to emergency care
An assurance-based approach with comprehensive primary care
An insurance-only approach without public-sector services
A disease-specific approach limited to communicable diseases
120.x: NHP 2017 adopted an assurance-based approach and envisaged comprehensive primary care rather than an insurance-only or disease-specific model.
120.tq: Identify the official policy approach while rejecting extreme alternatives such as “only” and “private-sector-only.”
xs: **NHP 2017** took an **assurance-based approach** with **comprehensive primary care** — option **(2)**.
Its primary care package covers **NCDs, mental health, geriatric and palliative care** via **Health and Wellness Centres** — not communicable diseases alone.
xa: Public hospitals: **free drugs, diagnostics + emergency care**.
Targets: **TFR 2.1 by 2025**; life expectancy **67.5 → 70 by 2025**.
⚠ Spending target **2.5% of GDP by 2025** was missed.

120.s: The National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) and the National Urban Health Mission (NUHM), the two sub-missions of the National Health Mission, were launched in which years respectively?
120.x: NRHM was launched in 2005 to give rural India accessible, affordable, quality care, and NUHM followed in 2013; together they form NHM. 2002 and 2017 are National Health Policy years; '2013 and 2005' reverses the order; 2018 is the launch year of Ayushman Bharat and Anaemia Mukt Bharat.
120.tq: NRHM 2005 (rural first), NUHM 2013.
xs: **NRHM 2005** and **NUHM 2013** — option **(1)**.
**2002** and **2017** are National Health Policy years; option (3) reverses the order.
xa: NRHM was asked in **APPSC 2023** PYQ.
NRHM goal: **accessible, affordable, quality care** for rural India.
NHM funding: **60:40**; NE and Himalayan states **90:10**.

120.s: The Indian Research Fund Association, the predecessor of the Indian Council of Medical Research, was established in:
120.x: The Indian Research Fund Association was established in 1911 and was later renamed the ICMR in 1949.
120.tq: Distinguish the founding year from the later renaming year.
xs: The **Indian Research Fund Association (IRFA)** was set up in **1911** — option **(2)**.
It was renamed **ICMR** in **1949**; **1948** is the year **WHO** was founded.
xa: ICMR is among the world's **oldest medical research bodies**.
ICMR consortia: **MERA India** (malaria), **India TB Research Consortium**, **India Hypertension Control Initiative**.
The **Medical Device and Diagnostic Mission Secretariat** reduces import dependence.

120.s: Which of the following is NOT a disease consortium or initiative listed in connection with the ICMR?
120.x: MERA India, the India TB Research Consortium and the India Hypertension Control Initiative are listed ICMR-related initiatives; India Food Security Consortium is not.
120.tq: Find the invented-looking member by comparing every option with the named ICMR initiatives.
xs: **India Food Security Consortium** is not an ICMR consortium — option **(4)**.
**MERA India** (malaria), the **India TB Research Consortium** and the **India Hypertension Control Initiative** are ICMR consortia.
xa: Others: **Mission Delhi**, **India Cancer Research Consortium**, **Stroke Network**.
ICMR began in **1911** as IRFA; renamed **1949**.
**Medical Device and Diagnostic Mission Secretariat**: reduces import dependence.

120.s: Which statement best expresses the criticism that an insurance-led public health policy may face?
o: It eliminates the need for public hospitals.
It increases coverage but may not ensure access.
It increases access without increasing coverage.
120.x: The criticism is that insurance-led policies can expand coverage while failing to ensure actual access to health services.
120.tq: Distinguish the related but different concepts of coverage and access.
xs: An insurance-led public health policy **increases coverage but not access** — option **(3)** (24 Jun 2026).
Option (4) reverses the criticism.
xa: NHP 2017 was **assurance-based**, with comprehensive primary care.
Primary care meets **80-90%** of health needs.
⚠ The NHP 2017 spending target of **2.5% of GDP by 2025** was missed (**1.43%** in 2022-23).

120.s:
The National Health Policy, 2002, emphasised which of the following?
1. Increased public spending on health
2. A larger role for the private sector and NGOs
3. Exclusive provision of health services by the public sector
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
120.x: NHP 2002 called for increased public spending and a larger role for the private sector and NGOs. It did not advocate exclusive public-sector provision.
120.tq: Reject the absolute statement containing “exclusive” while retaining the two stated policy features.
xs: **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
**NHP 2002** called for **more public spending** and a **bigger private/NGO role**.
Statement 3 wrong: a bigger private/NGO role rules out exclusive public provision.
xa: The first National Health Policy came in **1983**.
**NHP 2017** adopted an **assurance-based** approach.
NHP 2017 promised **free drugs, diagnostics + emergency care** in public hospitals.

120.s:
Consider the following targets of the National Health Policy, 2017:
1. Public health spending of 2.5% of GDP by 2025.
2. Total fertility rate of 2.1 by 2025.
3. Life expectancy of 75 years by 2025.
4. Infant mortality rate of 28 by 2019.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
120.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct NHP 2017 targets (2.5% of GDP by 2025, TFR 2.1 by 2025, IMR 28 by 2019). Statement 3 is wrong: the life expectancy target was 70 years (from 67.5) by 2025. Hence '1, 2 and 4 only'.
120.tq: NHP 2017: 2.5% GDP, TFR 2.1, LE 70, IMR 28, MMR 100.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 4 only** — option **(2)**.
Correct: spending **2.5% of GDP by 2025**; **TFR 2.1 by 2025**; **IMR 28 by 2019**.
Statement 3 wrong: the life expectancy target was **67.5 → 70 by 2025**, not 75.
xa: MMR target: **100 by 2020**.
⚠ The spending target was **missed** — **1.43%** in **2022-23** (NHA).
NHP 2017 is **assurance-based**.

120.s:
Consider the following statements about Mission Indradhanush:
1. It was launched in December 2014 as a catch-up drive under the Universal Immunisation Programme.
2. It targets zero-dose and partly immunised children.
3. Its target is 100% full immunisation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
120.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: it is a December 2014 catch-up drive under UIP for zero-dose and partly immunised children. Statement 3 is wrong: the target is 90% full immunisation. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
120.tq: Indradhanush target = 90%, not 100%.
xs: **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **Mission Indradhanush** (**Dec 2014**) is a catch-up drive under the **Universal Immunisation Programme**.
Statement 2 correct: it reaches **zero-dose and partly immunised** children.
Statement 3 wrong: its target is **90% full immunisation**.
xa: **U-WIN** digitises maternal and child vaccination records.
**MR-1** at **9-12 months** is the correct PYQ pair.

120.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Fit India Movement (2019) aims to build fitness into daily life.
2. Swachh Bharat Abhiyan was launched in 2014 for sanitation and hygiene.
3. Eat Right India was launched by NITI Aayog.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
120.x: Statement 2 is correct: Swachh Bharat, 2014. Statement 1 is correct: Fit India, 2019. Statement 3 is wrong: Eat Right India (2018) is an FSSAI campaign; FSSAI was created under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
120.tq: Eat Right India = FSSAI (FSS Act 2006).
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** **1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **Fit India Movement** (**2019**) builds fitness into daily life.
Statement 2 correct: **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan** (**2014**) — sanitation and hygiene.
Statement 3 wrong: **Eat Right India** is an **FSSAI** campaign, not NITI Aayog.
xa: FSSAI was created under the **Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006**.
Eat Right India + Fit India together aim to **cut NCD deaths**.
**ICMR** began in **1911** as **IRFA**; renamed in **1949**.

120.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK) gives cash assistance to pregnant women for institutional delivery.
2. Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) gives cash assistance to pregnant women for institutional delivery and is 100% centrally sponsored.
3. JSSK entitles pregnant women to free ('zero expense') delivery and newborn care at public facilities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
120.x: Statement 2 is correct: JSY is cash assistance for institutional delivery, 100% centrally sponsored. Statement 1 is wrong: cash assistance is JSY; JSSK is a free-entitlement scheme. Statement 3 is correct: JSSK gives zero-expense delivery and newborn care. Hence '2 and 3 only'.
120.tq: JSY = cash; JSSK = free (zero expense) delivery.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)** **2 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 wrong: cash assistance for **institutional delivery** is **JSY**, not JSSK.
Statement 2 correct: **JSY** gives cash for institutional delivery and is **100% centrally sponsored**.
Statement 3 correct: **JSSK** gives free, "**zero expense**" delivery and newborn care.
xa: AP JSY: **1,76,966** beneficiaries (Apr-Dec **2024**).
**RKSK** covers adolescents **10-19 years**.
NHM funding: **60:40**; NE and Himalayan states **90:10**.

120.s: The usual Centre–State funding pattern under the National Health Mission is:
o: 60:40, with 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States
120.x: The normal funding pattern is 60:40 between the Centre and States, while North-Eastern and Himalayan States receive a 90:10 pattern.
120.tq: Compare the general funding ratio with the special ratio for specified regions.
xs: NHM funding: **Centre:State 60:40**, **90:10** for **NE and Himalayan states** — option **(3)**.
⚠ **JSY** is **100%** centrally sponsored.
xa: NRHM aims at **accessible, affordable, quality care** for rural India.
ASHAs + ANMs form the **backbone of rural care**.

120.s: Which of the following correctly matches an Ayushman Bharat pillar with its principal role?
o: Ayushman Arogya Mandir — comprehensive primary care
ABDM — construction of BSL-3 laboratories only
PM-ABHIM — cash assistance for institutional delivery
120.x: Ayushman Arogya Mandirs provide comprehensive primary care. PM-JAY is the hospitalisation assurance pillar, ABDM is the digital backbone, and PM-ABHIM strengthens health infrastructure.
120.tq: Match each pillar with its central role and reject cross-swapped functions.
xs: **Ayushman Arogya Mandir — comprehensive primary care** is correct — option **(1)**.
**ABDM** is the digital backbone; **PM-ABHIM** builds health infrastructure for pandemics; **JSY** gives cash for institutional delivery.
xa: AAMs were earlier **AB-HWCs**; **1.73 lakh+** converted (Sep 2026).
Primary care meets **80-90%** of health needs.
⚠ **Arogya Mitra** is a **PM-JAY** hospital facilitator.

120.s:
Consider the following statements about Ayushman Arogya Mandirs:
1. The target was 1,50,000 centres.
2. More than 1.73 lakh centres had been converted.
3. Primary care is expected to meet about 40-50% of health needs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
120.x: Statement 1 is correct: the target was 1,50,000 centres. Statement 2 is correct: 1.73 lakh+ had been converted (Sep 2026). Statement 3 is wrong: primary care meets 80-90% of health needs. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
120.tq: AAM: target 1.5 lakh, achieved 1.73 lakh+, primary care = 80-90% of needs.
xs: **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: target **1,50,000** centres.
Statement 2 correct: **1.73 lakh+** converted (LENSD Sep 2026).
Statement 3 wrong: primary care meets **80-90%** of health needs.
xa: AAM services: NCD screening (hypertension, diabetes, **oral/breast/cervix** cancers), mental health, ENT, eye, geriatric, palliative + trauma care.
Campaigns: **Ayushman Sabhas**, weekly **Ayushman Melas**, **Ayushman Gram**.
Telemedicine is available in **all AAMs in AP**.

120.s:
Which of the following statements about PM-ABHIM is correct?
1. It focuses on health infrastructure for pandemics.
2. It was launched on 25 October 2021 at Varanasi.
3. Its approved outlay was ₹64,180 crore for FY 2021–22 to FY 2025–26.
4. It includes critical care blocks, Integrated Public Health Laboratories and BSL-3 laboratories.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
120.x: All four statements are correct. PM-ABHIM strengthens pandemic-related health infrastructure through the stated investments and facilities.
120.tq: Combine launch details, financial outlay, purpose and infrastructure components in one coded question.
xs: All four — **1, 2, 3 and 4** — are correct — option **(4)**.
**PM-ABHIM** builds **health infrastructure for pandemics**; launched **25 Oct 2021** at **Varanasi**.
Outlay **₹64,180 crore** (FY **2021-22** to **2025-26**): **critical care blocks**, **IPHLs in all districts**, **BSL-3 labs**.
xa: In AP, **J.P. Nadda** inaugurated **10 Critical Care Blocks and 12 IPHLs** (**₹250 crore**) from **Vijayawada** (13 Sep 2026).
The other Ayushman Bharat pillars: **Ayushman Arogya Mandir** and **ABDM**.

120.s:
Consider the following statements about ABHA under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission:
1. ABHA is a 14-digit health ID.
2. ABHA accounts crossed 90 crore by June 2026.
3. ABHA is the ABDM registry of healthcare professionals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
120.x: Statement 1 is correct: ABHA is a 14-digit health ID. Statement 2 is correct: ABHA accounts crossed 90 crore (Jun 2026). Statement 3 is wrong: ABHA is the citizens' registry; professionals are in the Healthcare Professionals Registry (HPR). Hence '1 and 2 only'.
120.tq: Four ABDM registries: ABHA (citizens), HPR, HFR, Drug Registry.
xs: **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **ABHA** is a **14-digit** health ID.
Statement 2 correct: **90 crore+ ABHA accounts** (Jun 2026).
Statement 3 wrong: ABHA is the **citizens'** registry; professionals are in the **Healthcare Professionals Registry (HPR)**.
xa: Earlier (Aug 2025): **79.91 crore** accounts; **67.19 crore** linked records.
**NMC (Mar 2026)**: all medical colleges to link ABHA IDs for OPD/IPD/emergency patients.

120.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) is correct?
1. It was launched in September 2021.
2. It is implemented by the National Health Authority.
3. It seeks to create a consent-based and interoperable digital health ecosystem.
4. It is built on Digital Public Infrastructure.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
120.x: All four statements are correct. ABDM was launched in September 2021, is run by NHA, and builds a consent-based interoperable ecosystem on Digital Public Infrastructure.
120.tq: Combine date, implementing authority, design principle and technological foundation.
xs: All four — **1, 2, 3 and 4** — are correct — option **(4)**.
**ABDM** launched in **September 2021**, run by the **National Health Authority (NHA)**.
It aims at a **consent-based, interoperable** digital health ecosystem on **Digital Public Infrastructure**.
xa: Registries: **ABHA, HPR, HFR, Drug Registry**.
Gateways: **Health Information Consent Manager**, **UHI**, **NHCX**.
⚠ **Arogya Mitra is NOT part of ABDM** (APPSC 2025 PYQ).

120.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four principal registries of ABDM?
120.x: The four registries are ABHA, Healthcare Professionals Registry, Health Facility Registry and Drug Registry. Arogya Mitra is not an ABDM component.
120.tq: Use the ‘not part of the architecture’ trap to distinguish a familiar health term from an official registry.
xs: **Arogya Mitra registry** is not an ABDM registry — option **(1)**; Arogya Mitra is a **PM-JAY hospital facilitator** (APPSC 2025 PYQ).
The four registries: **ABHA**, **Healthcare Professionals Registry**, **Health Facility Registry** and **Drug Registry**.
xa: ABHA is a **14-digit** ID; **90 crore+** accounts (Jun 2026).
ABDM is run by the **National Health Authority**.
Gateways: **Consent Manager**, **UHI**, **NHCX**.

120.s: The March 2026 direction of the National Medical Commission required medical colleges to generate and link ABHA IDs for:
o: All OPD, IPD and emergency patients
120.x: The NMC directed medical colleges to generate and link ABHA IDs for all OPD, IPD and emergency patients, partly to detect fake patients during inspections.
120.tq: Identify the complete beneficiary category rather than narrowing the order to one department or scheme.
xs: **NMC (Mar 2026)** ordered medical colleges to generate and link **ABHA IDs** for **all OPD, IPD and emergency patients** — option **(2)**.
The aim: **weed out fake patients** during inspections.
xa: ABHA is a **14-digit** health ID; **90 crore+** accounts (Jun 2026).
Aug 2025: **79.91 crore** accounts, **67.19 crore** linked records.
AP's **Sanjeevani** gives an ABHA ID to every citizen.

120.s:
With reference to ASHA workers, consider the following statements:
1. ASHA stands for Accredited Social Health Activist.
2. ASHA functions as a link between households and the health system.
3. ASHA is a village-level community health worker.
4. ASHA and ANM are regarded as important components of rural healthcare delivery.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
120.x: All four statements are correct. ASHA means Accredited Social Health Activist, and ASHAs and ANMs play a crucial role in linking rural communities with healthcare services.
120.tq: Use the expansion, function, level of operation and institutional role as separate statement checks.
xs: All four — **1, 2, 3 and 4** — are correct — option **(4)**.
**ASHA = Accredited Social Health Activist**, a **village-level community health worker** linking households to the health system.
**ASHAs + ANMs** are the **backbone of rural care**.
xa: **Mobile Academy** is an audio course for ASHAs.
ASHAs came under **NRHM** (**2005**).

120.s:
Consider the following statements about the Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram (RKSK):
1. It covers adolescents aged 10-19 years.
2. It includes Adolescent Friendly Health Clinics, weekly iron folic acid supplementation and peer educators.
3. It sets up Integrated Public Health Laboratories in every district.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
120.x: Statement 1 is correct: RKSK covers adolescents of 10-19 years. Statement 2 is correct: AFHCs, WIFS and peer educators are its components. Statement 3 is wrong: Integrated Public Health Labs in all districts come under PM-ABHIM. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
120.tq: Labs and critical care blocks = PM-ABHIM, not RKSK.
xs: **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **RKSK** covers adolescents **10-19 years**.
Statement 2 correct: **Adolescent Friendly Health Clinics**, **Weekly Iron Folic Acid Supplementation**, **peer educators**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Integrated Public Health Labs in all districts** come under **PM-ABHIM**.
xa: RKSK also covers **menstrual hygiene**.
**Anaemia Mukt Bharat** (2018) follows the **6x6x6** strategy.

120.s:
Consider the following statements about Anaemia Mukt Bharat:
1. It was launched in 2014.
2. It includes IFA supplementation, deworming, and testing and treatment.
3. It follows the 6x6x6 strategy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
120.x: Statement 1 is wrong: Anaemia Mukt Bharat was launched in 2018. Statement 2 is correct: IFA supplementation, deworming and testing/treatment are among its interventions. Statement 3 is correct: it follows the 6x6x6 strategy. Hence '2 and 3 only'.
120.tq: Anaemia Mukt Bharat and POSHAN Abhiyaan are both 2018.
xs: **2 and 3 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 wrong: **Anaemia Mukt Bharat** was launched in **2018**.
Statement 2 correct: **IFA supplementation, deworming, testing and treatment**.
Statement 3 correct: it follows the **6x6x6** strategy.
xa: It also includes **fortified foods** and **behaviour change**.
RKSK's **Weekly Iron Folic Acid Supplementation** targets adolescents **10-19 years**.

120.s: Which one of the following sets of vaccines is administered at birth under the Universal Immunisation Programme?
o: BCG, OPV-0 and Hepatitis B birth dose
MR-2, DPT booster-1 and OPV booster
Td, DPT booster-2 and Rotavirus vaccine
120.x: The birth schedule includes BCG, OPV-0 and the birth dose of Hepatitis B.
120.tq: Start with the age column and eliminate vaccines belonging to later schedules.
xs: At birth: **BCG, OPV-0 and Hepatitis B birth dose** — option **(1)**.
**MR-1, JE-1, PCV booster** = **9-12 months**; **MR-2, DPT booster-1, OPV booster** = **16-24 months**; **Td** = **10 and 16 years**.
xa: **6, 10, 14 weeks**: OPV 1-3, Pentavalent 1-3, Rotavirus, fIPV; **PCV** at 6 and 14 weeks.
**DPT booster-2**: **5-6 years**.
Mission Indradhanush targets **90%** full immunisation.

120.s: Under the Universal Immunisation Programme schedule, which one of the following vaccine-age pairs is correctly matched?
120.x: MR-1 is given at 9-12 months (the correct PYQ pair). Td is given at 10 and 16 years, not 5-6 years; OPV-1 is given at 6 weeks, not 16-24 months (when the OPV booster is given); DPT booster-2 is given at 5-6 years, not 6 weeks.
120.tq: MR-1 at 9-12 months; Td at 10 and 16 years; DPT booster-2 at 5-6 years.
xs: **MR-1 — 9-12 months** is correct — option **(1)** (correct PYQ pair).
**Td** is at **10 and 16 years**, not 5-6 years.
**OPV-1** is at **6 weeks**; at **16-24 months** comes the **OPV booster**.
**DPT booster-2** is at **5-6 years**, not 6 weeks.
xa: At 9-12 months also: **JE-1** (endemic districts), **PCV booster**, **Vitamin A**.
**16-24 months**: **MR-2**, DPT booster-1, OPV booster, **JE-2**.

120.s: Which one of the following is the principal benefit of maintaining digital health records under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission?
o: They improve the sharing and use of patient information across providers
They replace the need for doctors at primary health centres
They make health insurance compulsory for every citizen
They allow hospitals to share records without the patient's consent
120.x: Digital records improve the sharing and use of patient information (APPSC 2023 PYQ answer). They support doctors rather than replace them; ABDM does not make insurance compulsory; and the ABDM ecosystem is consent-based, so sharing without consent is wrong.
120.tq: ABDM benefit = better sharing of records, always consent-based.
xs: Digital records **improve the sharing and use of patient information** — option **(1)** (APPSC 2023 PYQ answer).
ABDM is **consent-based**, so sharing without consent is wrong; it does not replace doctors or make insurance compulsory.
xa: ABHA is a **14-digit** health ID; **90 crore+** accounts.
ABDM is **interoperable** and built on **Digital Public Infrastructure**.
Telemedicine via **eSanjeevani** uses a Clinical Decision Support System.

120.s: World Health Day is observed on 7 April every year because on that date in 1948:
o: the World Health Organization was founded, with its headquarters at Geneva
the Alma-Ata Declaration on primary health care was adopted
the World Health Organization was founded, with its headquarters at New York
smallpox was declared eradicated by the World Health Assembly
120.x: WHO was founded on 7 April 1948 and is headquartered at Geneva, so World Health Day falls on 7 April. WHO's headquarters is not New York; the Alma-Ata Declaration and the eradication of smallpox are later events and not linked to 7 April 1948.
120.tq: WHO: Geneva, 7 April 1948 = World Health Day.
xs: **WHO** was founded on **7 April 1948**, headquartered at **Geneva** — option **(1)**.
Hence **World Health Day is 7 April**; WHO's headquarters is not New York.
xa: ⚠ **1949** is when IRFA was renamed **ICMR**.
ICMR's origin: **IRFA**, **1911**.
**One of the oldest** medical research bodies is ICMR.

120.s: The Sanjeevani digital health programme of Andhra Pradesh, commencing in August 2026, is primarily associated with which of the following?
o: Replacement of all public hospitals by private hospitals
Universal distribution of fortified food through fair-price shops
Free insurance cover of ₹5 lakh for every citizen
A digital health profile and ABHA ID for every citizen
120.x: Sanjeevani aims to create a digital health profile and ABHA ID for every citizen of Andhra Pradesh.
120.tq: Identify the defining feature of the programme rather than confusing it with an insurance scheme.
xs: AP's **Sanjeevani** (from **Aug 2026**) gives a **digital health profile and ABHA ID for every citizen** — option **(4)**.
It does not privatise hospitals, distribute food or give a fixed insurance cover.
xa: It links PHCs, hospitals, labs, **e-Aushadhi**, **108**, **104**, telemedicine + **AI assistance**.
The **Sanjeevani Citizen Wellness App** came in **Jul 2026**.
It makes AP an **ABDM-linked**, citizen-wide digital health state.

120.s: With reference to healthcare in Andhra Pradesh, which statement was marked valid in an APPSC 2024 question?
o: Telemedicine services are available in all Ayushman Arogya Mandirs in the State
Telemedicine is available only at AIIMS Mangalagiri
Ayushman Arogya Mandirs in the State provide no teleconsultation
Telemedicine is restricted to private hospitals empanelled under PM-JAY
120.x: Telemedicine is available in all Ayushman Arogya Mandirs in AP (APPSC 2024 statement marked valid). It is not confined to AIIMS Mangalagiri or to empanelled private hospitals, and AAMs do provide teleconsultation.
120.tq: AP: telemedicine at every AAM.
xs: **Telemedicine is available in all Ayushman Arogya Mandirs** in AP — option **(1)** (APPSC 2024 PYQ statement marked valid).
So telemedicine is not confined to one institution or to private hospitals, and AAMs do offer teleconsultation.
xa: **eSanjeevani** now has a **Clinical Decision Support System**.
AP's **Sanjeevani** programme (from **Aug 2026**) links telemedicine with PHCs, labs, **108** and **104**.
AAMs nationally: **1.73 lakh+** converted against a target of **1,50,000**.

120.s: The Eat Right India and Fit India campaigns together seek to reduce deaths due to:
120.x: Together, Eat Right India and Fit India aim to reduce deaths caused by non-communicable diseases through healthier diets and increased physical activity.
120.tq: Infer the common public-health outcome from the two campaigns’ complementary objectives.
xs: Eat Right India and Fit India together aim to cut **non-communicable disease (NCD)** deaths — option **(1)**.
Eat Right India promotes healthy diets; **Fit India** fights **sedentary lifestyles**.
xa: Fit India: **2019**; Eat Right India: **2018** (FSSAI).
**India Hypertension Control Initiative** is an ICMR consortium.
AAMs screen for NCDs such as **hypertension** and **diabetes**.

121.s:
Arrange the following milestones in chronological order:
A. Pulse Polio programme launched
B. India became free of smallpox
C. Last wild polio case in Howrah
D. WHO South-East Asia Region certified polio-free
121.x: India became free of smallpox in 1977, Pulse Polio was launched in 1995, the last wild polio case occurred in January 2011, and the region was certified polio-free in 2014.
121.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the middle events.
xs: The order is **B, A, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**Smallpox-free 1977** → **Pulse Polio 1995** → **last wild polio case, Howrah, Jan 2011** → **WHO SEAR polio-free 27 Mar 2014**.
xa: **Guinea worm** certified free: **2000**.
**Maternal and neonatal tetanus** eliminated: **2015**; **Yaws** declared free: **2016**.
Switch from trivalent to **bivalent OPV**: **Apr 2016**.

121.s:
Consider the following statements about polio milestones:
1. India's last wild polio case was reported from Howrah, West Bengal, in January 2011.
2. The WHO South-East Asia Region was certified polio-free on 27 March 2014.
3. India switched from trivalent to bivalent OPV in April 2014.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
121.x: Statement 1 is correct: last wild case, Howrah, January 2011. Statement 2 is correct: SEAR certified polio-free on 27 March 2014. Statement 3 is wrong: the tOPV-to-bOPV switch was in April 2016. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
121.tq: Polio: 1995 Pulse Polio, 2011 last case, 2014 certified, 2016 bOPV switch.
xs: **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: last wild polio case at **Howrah, WB**, **Jan 2011**.
Statement 2 correct: **WHO SEAR** certified polio-free on **27 Mar 2014**.
Statement 3 wrong: the switch to **bivalent OPV** was in **Apr 2016**.
xa: **Pulse Polio** was launched in **1995**.
**Yaws** was declared free in **2016**; **MNT** eliminated in **2015**.

121.s: The national target for tuberculosis elimination in India is:
121.x: India’s national target for TB elimination is 2025, five years ahead of the SDG target of 2030.
121.tq: Compare the national target with the later SDG target.
xs: India's national TB elimination target is **2025** — option **(2)**.
That is **five years ahead** of the SDG target of **2030**.
xa: Programme: **NTEP** — free diagnosis + treatment.
TB incidence fell **21%** and mortality **28%** (2015-2024).
⚠ **2030** is the target for **malaria**; **2027** for lymphatic filariasis; **2047** for sickle cell anaemia.

121.s: The National Framework for Malaria Elimination covers which period?
121.x: The National Framework for Malaria Elimination covers 2016–2030 and targets malaria elimination by 2030.
121.tq: Combine the official framework name with its exact period.
xs: The **National Framework for Malaria Elimination** covers **2016-2030** — option **(3)**.
It targets **malaria elimination by 2030**.
xa: Malaria cases fell **80%** during **2015-2023**.
**MERA India** = Malaria Elimination Research Alliance India, led by **ICMR**.
⚠ **2021-26** is **NACP Phase V**.

121.s: Which of the following is NOT a tool under the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme for malaria control?
121.x: IRS, LLINs, larvivorous fish, bio-larvicides and source reduction are listed malaria-control tools. Universal antibiotic prophylaxis is not one of them.
121.tq: Identify the non-vector-control measure among operational tools.
xs: **Universal antibiotic prophylaxis** is not an NVBDCP tool — option **(4)**.
NVBDCP tools: **IRS** (indoor residual spraying), **LLINs**, **larvivorous fish**, **bio-larvicides**, **source reduction**.
xa: NVBDCP elimination targets: **malaria, LF + kala-azar**.
NVBDCP handles outbreaks of **malaria, dengue, chikungunya** (PYQ key).
Malaria cases fell **80%** during **2015-2023**.

121.s: Under Sustainable Development Goal 3.4, the target for premature deaths from non-communicable diseases by 2030 is to:
121.x: SDG 3.4 calls for reducing premature mortality from non-communicable diseases by one-third through prevention and treatment by 2030.
121.tq: Focus on the exact target fraction and distinguish it from stronger but unsupported claims such as elimination.
xs: **SDG 3.4**: **reduce premature NCD deaths by one-third** by **2030** — option **(3)**.
It is a one-third cut, not halving, a quarter or complete elimination.
xa: ⚠ **SDG 3.3** is about ending **AIDS, TB, malaria and NTD** epidemics by 2030.
**NP-NCD** (earlier NPCDCS) links high-risk people to care.
AP screened **53.02 lakh** citizens under **NCD-CD 3.0**.

121.s: The national target of eliminating sickle-cell anaemia is set for:
121.x: India has set a target to eliminate sickle-cell anaemia by 2047 and to screen seven crore at-risk people.
121.tq: Separate the long-term disease mission year from 2025 and 2030 targets.
xs: India aims to **eliminate sickle cell anaemia by 2047** — option **(4)**.
It plans to **screen 7 crore** at-risk people (APPSC 2022 PYQ: A and R both true, R explains A).
xa: **Lymphatic filariasis**: **2027**; **malaria**: **2030**; **TB**: **2025**.
**Ayushman Gram** includes **sickle-cell screening**.

121.s:
Consider the following statements about lymphatic filariasis elimination in India:
1. India targets elimination by 2027, three years ahead of the SDG target.
2. The triple-drug IDA regimen uses Ivermectin, DEC and Azithromycin.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
121.x: Statement 1 is correct: the LF target is 2027, three years ahead of SDG 3.3. Statement 2 is wrong: IDA = Ivermectin, DEC and Albendazole. Hence '1 only'.
121.tq: IDA = I-D-A: Ivermectin, DEC, Albendazole.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: LF elimination by **2027**, **three years ahead** of **SDG 3.3**.
Statement 2 wrong: **IDA** = **Ivermectin, DEC and Albendazole**, not azithromycin.
xa: LF is eliminated through **MDA** with the triple-drug regimen.
LF is an **NVBDCP** elimination target with malaria and kala-azar.
Sickle cell anaemia target: **2047**.

121.s: The Sustainable Development Goal 3.3 seeks, by 2030, to:
o: Reduce premature NCD deaths by one-third only
Eliminate all forms of environmental pollution
Provide universal mental-health counselling through telemedicine
End epidemics of AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria and neglected tropical diseases
121.x: SDG 3.3 specifically seeks to end the epidemics of AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria and neglected tropical diseases by 2030.
121.tq: Distinguish SDG 3.3 from SDG 3.4, which concerns premature deaths from NCDs.
xs: **SDG 3.3** aims to **end the epidemics of AIDS, TB, malaria and NTDs** by **2030** — option **(4)**.
⚠ Cutting premature NCD deaths by **one-third** is **SDG 3.4**.
xa: India's TB target **2025** is five years ahead of the SDG target of 2030.
**Lymphatic filariasis** target **2027** is three years ahead of SDG 3.3.
Malaria elimination target: **2030** (framework **2016-2030**).

121.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: NP-NCD — Identification of high-risk persons and linkage to care
IDSP — Elimination of premature non-communicable disease deaths by one-third by 2030
IHCI — Reduction of hypertension-related heart attack, stroke and kidney-failure deaths
121.x: IDSP is concerned with outbreak surveillance. The target of reducing premature NCD deaths by one-third by 2030 belongs to SDG 3.4.
121.tq: Find the programme-target mismatch; the final option assigns an SDG target to an outbreak-surveillance programme.
xs: **IDSP — elimination of premature NCD deaths by one-third by 2030** is wrongly matched — option **(3)**.
**IDSP** (**2004**, under NHM) does **outbreak surveillance**; the one-third NCD target is **SDG 3.4**.
**Tele-MANAS** (24/7 tele-mental-health), **NP-NCD** (high-risk linkage) and **IHCI** (heart attack, stroke, kidney failure) are correct.
xa: Tele-MANAS was launched in **2022**.
NP-NCD was earlier called **NPCDCS**.
IHCI is run by **ICMR**.

121.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Ni-kshay is a digital portal for TB notification and tracking.
2. Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana gives nutritional DBT only to TB patients notified in the public sector.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
121.x: Statement 1 is correct: Ni-kshay is the digital TB notification and tracking portal. Statement 2 is wrong: Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana gives nutritional DBT to all notified TB patients, public and private. Hence '1 only'.
121.tq: Watch 'only' - the DBT covers public and private patients.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: **Ni-kshay** is the **digital TB portal** for notification and tracking.
Statement 2 wrong: **Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana** gives nutritional **DBT to all notified TB patients — public and private**.
xa: **Ni-kshay Mitras** adopt patients under the **PM TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan** (**Sept 2022**).
Dec 2025: **3.78 lakh+ Mitras**, **20 lakh+** patients, **45 lakh+** food baskets.

121.s: According to the India TB Report 2022, TB notifications in 2021 compared with 2020:
121.x: The India TB Report 2022 recorded a 19% rise in notifications in 2021 over 2020 (APPSC 2022 PYQ). 'Fell by 19%' reverses the direction; 53% is the 2015 treatment-coverage figure; 28% is the fall in TB mortality during 2015-2024.
121.tq: TB Report 2022: notifications up 19%.
xs: Notifications **rose by 19%** in 2021 over 2020 — option **(1)** (**India TB Report 2022**, APPSC 2022 PYQ).
**53%** is the 2015 treatment coverage; **28%** is the fall in TB mortality (2015-2024).
xa: TB incidence fell **21%** (2015-2024).
**Himachal Pradesh** screens all indoor hospital patients for TB (intensified case finding).
**Ni-kshay** is the digital notification portal.

121.s:
Consider the following statements about the National AIDS Control Programme (NACP):
1. It was launched in 1992.
2. It is led by NACO under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
3. NACP Phase V (2021-26) aims at a 50% cut in new infections and AIDS deaths.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
121.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: NACP began in 1992 and is led by NACO (MoHFW). Statement 3 is wrong: Phase V (2021-26) aims at an 80% cut in new infections and AIDS deaths. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
xs: **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **NACP** launched in **1992**.
Statement 2 correct: it is led by **NACO** (MoHFW).
Statement 3 wrong: **Phase V (2021-26)** aims at an **80% cut** in new infections and AIDS deaths.
xa: **HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017** bars discrimination.

121.s:
Consider the following statements regarding HIV-related services:
1. VCTC stands for Voluntary Counselling and Testing Centre.
2. Antiretroviral therapy is available free for life at ART centres.
3. ICTCs provide compulsory testing without counselling.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
121.x: VCTC means Voluntary Counselling and Testing Centre, and free lifelong ART is provided at ART centres. ICTC services are voluntary and include counselling, so statement 3 is false.
121.tq: Find the statement that reverses the voluntary nature of a service.
xs: **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **VCTC = Voluntary Counselling and Testing Centre**.
Statement 2 correct: **ART** is **free lifelong** at ART centres.
Statement 3 wrong: **ICTC = Integrated Counselling and Testing Centre**, offering **free voluntary** testing.
xa: **PEP** must be taken **within 72 hours**.
Other prevention tools: **Treatment as Prevention, Test and Treat, PrEP**, condoms.

121.s: The HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017 primarily seeks to prevent which of the following?
o: Discrimination against people living with HIV
121.x: The Act of 2017 bars discrimination against people living with HIV and provides a legal framework for their protection.
121.tq: Link the legislation with its principal legal protection.
xs: The **HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017** bars **discrimination against people living with HIV** — option **(2)**.
It does not restrict ART centres, medicines or voluntary testing.
xa: ⚠ **2017** also saw the **Mental Healthcare Act**.
India has **over 2.5 million** people living with HIV.
Free **lifelong ART** is given at ART centres.

121.s:
With reference to the UNAIDS 95-95-95 target adopted by India, consider the following statements:
1. 95% of people living with HIV should know their status.
2. 95% of those who know their status should be on treatment.
3. 95% of those on treatment should have a suppressed viral load.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
121.x: The three 95s refer respectively to knowledge of HIV status, treatment, and viral-load suppression among those treated.
121.tq: Read each repeated numerical target separately before selecting the code.
xs: All three — **1, 2 and 3** — are correct — option **(4)**.
**95-95-95** (UNAIDS, adopted by India): **95%** know their status; **95%** of them on treatment; **95%** of those treated with **suppressed viral load**.
xa: AP's minister called the national target **95-95-99** (**99%** viral suppression).
AP stands at **88% / 87% / 96.2%**; target **Dec 2026**.
AP launched the **Suraksha Dashboard** (13 Aug 2026).

121.s:
Consider the following statements about HIV/AIDS projects in India:
1. The Red Ribbon Express is an HIV/AIDS awareness train.
2. AVAHAN is a World Bank HIV prevention project.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
121.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Red Ribbon Express is an awareness train. Statement 2 is wrong: AVAHAN is the Gates Foundation's HIV prevention initiative, not a World Bank project. Hence '1 only'.
121.tq: AVAHAN = Gates Foundation.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: the **Red Ribbon Express** is an HIV/AIDS **awareness train**.
Statement 2 wrong: **AVAHAN** is a **Gates Foundation** HIV prevention project.
xa: NACO held the **'Suraksha Sankalp Karyashala'** district review at **Vijayawada** (Mar 2026).
NACP was launched in **1992**, led by **NACO**.
Prevention tools: **PEP within 72 hours**, PrEP, Test and Treat.

121.s: Which strain of HIV is dominant in India?
121.x: HIV-1 subtype C is the dominant strain in India. HIV-2, HIV-1 subtype B and HIV-1 subtype A are other HIV types or subtypes but are not the dominant strain in India.
121.tq: India's HIV = HIV-1 subtype C.
xs: The dominant strain in India is **HIV-1 subtype C** — option **(1)**.
So HIV-2 and the other HIV-1 subtypes listed are not India's dominant strain.
xa: India has **over 2.5 million** people living with HIV.
Highest burden: **Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka**.
Goal: end AIDS as a public health threat by **2030**.

121.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the 2026 Andhra Pradesh HIV target and reported three-part status?
121.x: Andhra Pradesh reported 88%, 87% and 96.2% across the three indicators, with a target for December 2026.
121.tq: Preserve the order of a multi-part numerical indicator.
xs: AP targets the HIV cascade by **Dec 2026**; option (4) jumbles the order.
xa: **95-95-95** is the UNAIDS target adopted by India.
AP's minister called the national target **95-95-99**.
AP launched the **Suraksha Dashboard** (13 Aug 2026).

121.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: RTS,S/AS01 (Mosquirix) was the first WHO-approved malaria vaccine.
BCG is a vaccine for tuberculosis.
A licensed vaccine against HIV/AIDS is in routine use.
R21/Matrix-M was developed through collaboration between the Oxford Jenner Institute and Serum Institute.
121.x: Option C is incorrect: no licensed vaccine against HIV/AIDS exists yet. Mosquirix was the first WHO-approved malaria vaccine, BCG prevents TB and R21 came from Oxford and Serum Institute.
121.tq: Recall which diseases have vaccines.
n: RTS,S/AS01 is the first WHO-approved malaria vaccine in the source. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 32-33]
BCG is a vaccine for tuberculosis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 32-33]
The source does not attribute a vaccine to AIDS. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 32-33]
R21/Matrix-M was developed through collaboration between the Oxford Jenner Institute and the Serum Institute. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 32-33]
RTS,S/AS01 is a malaria vaccine. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 32-33]
R21/Matrix-M is a malaria vaccine. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 32-33]
xs: The incorrect statement is option **(3)**: a licensed **HIV/AIDS** vaccine is **not** in routine use — the source attributes **no vaccine** to AIDS.
**RTS,S/AS01 (Mosquirix)** was the **first WHO-approved** malaria vaccine; **BCG** protects against **tuberculosis**.
**R21/Matrix-M** came from the **Oxford Jenner Institute** and **Serum Institute**.
xa: Mosquirix developer: **GSK**.
**Hepatitis B** has a vaccine.
**HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017** bars discrimination.

121.s: The India Hypertension Control Initiative, implemented with the involvement of ICMR, primarily seeks to reduce deaths due to:
o: Heart attack, stroke and kidney failure
121.x: The India Hypertension Control Initiative targets hypertension-related deaths from heart attack, stroke and kidney failure.
121.tq: Match the named initiative with its specific disease-outcome targets.
xs: The **India Hypertension Control Initiative (ICMR)** targets deaths from **heart attack, stroke and kidney failure** — option **(4)**.
Rabies, snake-bite and leptospirosis are separate programmes run in AP.
xa: **NP-NCD** finds high-risk people and links them to care.
**SDG 3.4**: cut premature NCD deaths by **one-third** by 2030.
⚠ **MERA India** is ICMR's malaria alliance.

121.s: Cervavac, announced in September 2022, is best described as:
o: India's first indigenous quadrivalent HPV vaccine against cervical cancer, made by the Serum Institute of India
India's first indigenous malaria vaccine, made by Bharat Biotech
An intranasal COVID-19 vaccine developed with ICMR-NIV
The world's first DNA vaccine approved for humans, made by Zydus
121.x: Cervavac is India's first indigenous quadrivalent HPV vaccine, made by the Serum Institute of India against cervical cancer (Sept 2022). The intranasal COVID vaccine is iNCOVACC; the first DNA vaccine is ZyCoV-D by Zydus; and Cervavac is not a malaria vaccine (R21 is the Oxford-SII malaria vaccine).
121.tq: Cervavac = HPV, quadrivalent, SII, cervical cancer.
xs: **Cervavac** is **India's first indigenous quadrivalent HPV vaccine** against **cervical cancer**, made by **Serum Institute of India** — option **(1)**.
It was announced in **Sept 2022** (two PYQs).
⚠ The malaria vaccine made by Serum Institute is **R21/Matrix-M**, developed by Oxford.
xa: **RTS,S/AS01 (Mosquirix)** is GSK's malaria vaccine.
AAMs screen for **oral, breast and cervical** cancers.

121.s:
Consider the following statements about TB outcomes in India during 2015-2024:
1. TB incidence fell by 21%.
2. TB mortality fell by 21%.
3. Treatment coverage rose from 53% to 92%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
121.x: Statement 1 is correct: incidence fell 21%. Statement 2 is wrong: mortality fell 28%, not 21%. Statement 3 is correct: treatment coverage rose from 53% (2015) to 92% (2024). Hence '1 and 3 only'.
121.tq: Incidence 21, mortality 28 - mortality fell more.
xs: **1 and 3 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: TB **incidence fell 21%** (2015-2024).
Statement 2 wrong: **mortality fell 28%**, not 21%.
Statement 3 correct: **treatment coverage 53% (2015) → 92% (2024)**.
xa: IYB gives coverage of **85%** in **2023**.
⚠ India TB Report 2022: notifications rose **19%** in 2021 over 2020.

121.s:
In Andhra Pradesh, which of the following programmes or health concerns are additionally covered under NP-NCD?
1. National Mental Health Programme
2. Elderly care
3. Iodine Deficiency Disorders
4. Tobacco control
5. Fluorosis and oral health

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
121.x: In Andhra Pradesh, the expanded NP-NCD coverage includes mental health, elderly care, iodine deficiency disorders, tobacco control, fluorosis and oral health.
121.tq: Use the list-completion method: check each item against the stated state-level coverage.
xs: All five — **1, 2, 3, 4 and 5** — are covered — option **(3)**.
AP's NP-NCD also covers **NMHP**, **elderly care**, **IDD**, **tobacco control**, **fluorosis + oral health**.
xa: AP's ANMs screen at home using the **ANM AP Health App**.
**NCD-CD 3.0**: universal screening from **14 Nov 2024** → **53.02 lakh** citizens screened (2024-25).
AP also runs **NTEP, NCVBDC, NPCBVI, NLEP** and rabies, leptospirosis, snake-bite programmes.

121.s:
Arrange the following mental-health programme developments in chronological order:
A. National Mental Health Programme was initiated
B. Mental Health Act was enacted
C. Mental Healthcare Act was enacted
D. Tele-MANAS was launched

Select the correct chronological sequence.
121.x: The National Mental Health Programme dates to 1982, the Mental Health Act to 1987, the Mental Healthcare Act to 2017 and Tele-MANAS to 2022.
121.tq: Anchor the sequence with the years 1982, 1987, 2017 and 2022.
xs: The order is **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**NMHP 1982** → **Mental Health Act 1987** → **Mental Healthcare Act 2017** → **Tele-MANAS 2022**.
xa: The 2017 Act **repealed** the 1987 Act.
It **decriminalised suicide** and gave a **right to access** government mental healthcare.
Prevalence of mental illness: about **1 in 7 Indians**.

121.s: Which of the following correctly represents the reported mental-health burden and treatment-resource situation in India?
o: About one in fourteen Indians is affected, the treatment gap is 48.5%, and there are 3 psychiatrists per lakh population.
About one in seven Indians is affected, the treatment gap is 14.5%, and there are 3 psychiatrists per lakh population.
About one in three Indians is affected, the treatment gap is 84.5%, and there are 30 psychiatrists per lakh population.
About one in seven Indians is affected, the treatment gap is 84.5%, and there are 0.3 psychiatrists per lakh population.
121.x: The reported figures are a burden of about one in seven Indians, an 84.5% treatment gap and 0.3 psychiatrists per lakh population.
121.tq: Check the three linked figures together; the distractors reverse or inflate the percentages and ratios.
xs: About **1 in 7 Indians** affected, **84.5%** treatment gap, **0.3 psychiatrists per lakh** — option **(4)**.
The other options distort these figures (14.5%, 3 or 30 per lakh).
xa: **DMHP** covers **90%+ districts**.
**Tele-MANAS** (**2022**) offers 24/7 support.
**1.73 lakh** AAMs include mental health services.

121.s:
Consider the following statements about the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017:
1. It gives a right to access mental healthcare from government services.
2. It decriminalised attempted suicide.
3. It removed all restrictions on electroconvulsive therapy (ECT).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
121.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Act gives a right to access government mental healthcare and decriminalised suicide. Statement 3 is wrong: the Act restricted ECT rather than removing restrictions. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses decriminalisation and the options with 3 are wrong.
121.tq: MHA 2017: right to access, suicide decriminalised, ECT restricted.
xs: **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: the **Mental Healthcare Act, 2017** gives a **right to access** government mental healthcare.
Statement 2 correct: it **decriminalised suicide**.
Statement 3 wrong: it **restricted ECT**.
xa: It repealed the **1987** Act.
**NMHP** dates to **1982**.

121.s: Which of the following sets consists only of countries certified malaria-free by WHO among the countries listed?
121.x: Sri Lanka, China and Timor-Leste are the three countries identified as WHO-certified malaria-free in this group.
121.tq: Use set comparison to eliminate a list containing an unlisted country.
xs: **Sri Lanka, China and Timor-Leste** are WHO-certified **malaria-free** — option **(1)**.
**Timor-Leste** is the most recent of the three (Jan 2026); **India** targets elimination only by **2030**.
xa: Only about **42%** of global malaria financing needs are met.
Malaria cases in India fell **80%** in **2015-2023**.
Vaccines: **RTS,S/AS01 (Mosquirix)** by GSK; **R21/Matrix-M** by Oxford, made by **Serum Institute**.

121.s: Which of the following States are identified as carrying the highest HIV burden among the listed States?
121.x: Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka are identified as carrying the highest HIV burden among the listed States.
121.tq: Recall the exact geographical grouping rather than a single State.
xs: The highest HIV burden is in **Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka** — option **(1)**.
India has **over 2.5 million** people living with HIV.
xa: Dominant strain in India: **HIV-1 subtype C**.
NACO's **'Suraksha Sankalp Karyashala'** district review was held in **Vijayawada**, Mar 2026.

121.s:
Consider the following statements regarding malaria epidemiology in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Malaria patterns are changing in tribal districts.
2. Malaria patterns are changing in non-tribal districts.
3. Sustained surveillance is therefore necessary.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
121.x: Malaria epidemiology is changing in both tribal and non-tribal districts of Andhra Pradesh, making continued surveillance necessary.
121.tq: Treat the geographical comparison as a two-part statement and connect it with the stated public-health response.
xs: All three — **1, 2 and 3** — are correct — option **(4)**.
Malaria epidemiology is **changing in AP's tribal and non-tribal districts**, so **surveillance must be sustained**.
xa: **IDSP** (**2004**, under NHM) does outbreak surveillance.
AP runs **NCVBDC** among its disease programmes.
National malaria elimination target: **2030**.

121.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. NVBDCP handles outbreaks of malaria, dengue and chikungunya.
2. NVBDCP provides free multidrug therapy for leprosy at PHCs.
3. The National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme (NVBDCP) targets elimination of malaria, lymphatic filariasis and kala-azar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
121.x: Statement 3 is correct: NVBDCP elimination targets are malaria, LF and kala-azar. Statement 2 is wrong: free MDT for leprosy at PHCs is under the National Leprosy Eradication Programme (NLEP), with the Sparsh campaign. Statement 1 is correct (PYQ key). Hence '1 and 3 only'.
121.tq: NVBDCP = vector-borne; NLEP = leprosy MDT.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(3)** **1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **NVBDCP** handles outbreaks of **malaria**, **dengue** and **chikungunya** (PYQ key).
Statement 2 wrong: free **MDT** for leprosy at PHCs is under **NLEP**, with the **Sparsh** campaign.
Statement 3 correct: NVBDCP elimination targets are **malaria**, **lymphatic filariasis** and **kala-azar**.
xa: Malaria elimination target: **2030**.
Lymphatic filariasis target: **2027**, using triple-drug **IDA**.
**Anti-Leprosy Day**: **30 January**.

121.s: Who developed the first polio vaccine?
121.x: Jonas Salk made the first (injected, inactivated) polio vaccine in 1955. Albert Sabin made the oral polio vaccine.
121.tq: Discriminate Salk (injected) from Sabin (oral).
n: Jonas Salk developed the first polio vaccine. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 32-33]
Albert Sabin developed the Oral Polio Vaccine. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 32-33]
xs: **Jonas Salk** developed the **first polio vaccine** — option **(2)**.
**Albert Sabin** developed the **Oral Polio Vaccine**; **Edward Jenner** — **smallpox vaccine**; **Louis Pasteur** — **rabies vaccine**.
xa: India switched from **trivalent** to **bivalent OPV** in **Apr 2016**.
WHO SEAR certified polio-free: **27 Mar 2014**.
**Pulse Polio** launched **1995**.

121.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Trivalent OPV covers polio types 1, 2 and 3.
II. Bivalent OPV covers polio types 1 and 3.
III. ZyCoV-D is a DNA-based COVID-19 vaccine.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
121.x: All three are correct: trivalent OPV covers polio types 1, 2 and 3, bivalent OPV types 1 and 3, and ZyCoV-D is India's DNA COVID vaccine.
121.tq: Recall the types of polio vaccine.
n: Trivalent OPV protects against poliovirus types 1, 2, and 3. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 32-33]
Bivalent OPV protects against poliovirus types 1 and 3. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 32-33]
ZyCoV-D is a DNA-based COVID-19 vaccine. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 32-33]
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** **I, II and III**.
**Trivalent OPV** covers types **1, 2 and 3**; **bivalent OPV** covers types **1 and 3**.
**ZyCoV-D** is a **DNA-based** COVID-19 vaccine.
xa: OPV was developed by **Albert Sabin**.
Switch to **bivalent OPV**: **Apr 2016**.
Last wild polio case: **Howrah, WB**, **Jan 2011**.

121.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Diphtheria is prevented with a toxoid vaccine.
Statement B: Hepatitis B has a vaccine.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
121.x: Both are true: diphtheria is prevented by a toxoid vaccine, and hepatitis B has a vaccine.
121.tq: Recall the vaccines.
n: Diphtheria is prevented with a toxoid vaccine. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 32-33]
Hepatitis B has a vaccine. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 32-33]
xs: **Both Statement A and Statement B are true** — option **(1)**.
A **toxoid vaccine** prevents **diphtheria**; **hepatitis B** has a vaccine.
xa: **DPT** covers **diphtheria**, **pertussis** and **tetanus**.
⚠ The source does **not** attribute a vaccine to **AIDS**.
**Cervavac** — India's first indigenous **quadrivalent HPV** vaccine (**Serum Institute of India**).
